+#### 3.x (proposed) Rework: shared-edge topological assembly instead of geometric sewing
+
+**Status: not started. Deliberately deferred and bound to the NURBS effort (see Future Enhancements). This section records the decision and its trigger so it is not rediscovered from scratch.**
+
+**The current design.** Stage 3.4 builds each face independently and stage 3.5 reconciles them with \`BRepBuilderAPI_Sewing\`, a *geometric* stitch that merges edges by proximity within a tolerance. Edges *are* created once as shared \`TopoDS_Edge\` objects (§3.1), but two things defeat that sharing by assembly time:
+- \`MakeFace\`/\`MakeWire\`/\`ShapeFix\` copy edges, so the "shared" edge in face A is no longer the identical object in face B.
+- The UV-bounds construction paths (full spheres, complete tori, full-revolution and — as of the cone-cap investigation — apex-cap cones) synthesize their *own* natural-bounds boundary edges that were never shared with a neighbour at all.
+
+So sewing is load-bearing, and the \`ReconEdge.pcurves: [_; 2]\` and \`BRepVertex.uv_coords\` fields (§3.0) that the original design earmarked for a both-sides-shared representation were never populated — the geometric sewing pass stands in for them. The face-construction + sewing block is ~2100 lines carrying ~150 pole/seam/apex/reorient/ShapeFix/degenerate special-cases.
+
+**Why this is the root of a whole class of fragility.** Every hard case in stage 3 — sphere pole caps, torus seams, cone apex caps, and the tangent-edge/corner-vertex *tolerance relaxations* (the "genuinely ambiguous junction rows") — is ultimately a symptom of trimming faces independently and matching them by geometric tolerance. \`cone_tangent_planes\` is the sharpest example: its two apex-cap cone faces are pie-slices-with-apex whose two boundary curves lie on the same iso-V line; the wire builder collapses them, and a pure UV-bounds cap gets the *area* right but only matches its neighbours along part of the boundary, so sewing leaves free edges → open shell. The problem spans segmentation → edge topology → trimming → sewing, which is exactly why patching any single layer only half-works.
+
+**The proposed design.** Build the B-rep topologically instead of geometrically:
+1. Build each edge once (shared \`TopoDS_Edge\` + shared vertices, with its 3D curve) — as today.
+2. For **both** adjacent faces of every edge, compute and attach the pcurve of that edge on that face's surface (populate \`ReconEdge.pcurves\`). Poles/seams are handled *only* here, in pcurve computation, uniformly for every periodic surface.
+3. Insert degenerate edges at UV poles (cone apex, sphere pole) and seam edges at periodic wraps, shared correctly, as first-class topology rather than per-surface fix-ups.
+4. Assemble each face and the shell directly with \`BRep_Builder\` from the shared edges — the shell is closed *by construction*. Drop \`BRepBuilderAPI_Sewing\`; it becomes at most a validation check.
+5. This makes construction lower-level and more controlled (avoid \`ShapeFix\`/\`MakeFace\` edge-copying that breaks sharing). The cone apex cap, sphere pole cap, and torus seam then all reduce to "attach the correct pcurve to the shared edge, plus a degenerate/seam edge" — one uniform mechanism instead of ~150 special-cases.
+
+**Why defer it.** 52/57 models pass; nothing is *blocked*. The only current beneficiary is one unusual model (\`cone_tangent_planes\`) that already writes valid-ish output with a volume warning. The full payoff arrives with **NURBS**: freeform patches have arbitrary trimmed boundaries and will stress this machinery hard, building NURBS on top of projection+sewing is building on sand, and NURBS is also what finally brings test coverage to validate a more general assembler (today it would be a more-general machine exercised only on the analytic surfaces the current code already handles). So the rework is the *foundation to lay when NURBS begins*, not a standalone task.
+
+**Trigger to pull it forward earlier.** If a model becomes *unfixable* without tighter topology — i.e. the tangent-edge/corner tolerance relaxations stop merely loosening tolerances and start letting a real model fail — do the rework then rather than adding relaxation #N.
+

Sewing is \`construct_shells\` (\`BRepBuilderAPI_Sewing\`); solids and void-merging are §3.6. +- \`MakeEdge\` on a periodic (circle) curve forces p1 < p2 and takes the forward arc V1→V2, so **vertex order selects which arc** — see the explicit first/last-parameter handling in \`create_occt_faces_all\` (the \`d0_start\`/\`d1_start\` block). # Prioritized by value toward the project goal (README: "analytic and freeform surfaces")

## 1. cone_tangent_planes: stage 3.4 conical apex-cap face construction
DONE at stage 2: all 3 cones detected (normal-line axis rescue for narrow arcs;
half-angle cap 85°); stage 3.3 computes 11/11 edge curves incl. plane-cone tangent
generator lines. The model completes and writes a STEP; the only symptom is a stage-3.6
volume WARNING (6617 mm³ vs 14676 mm³) — the surfaces are all correct (max face sample
distance 1.16e-6 mm), only the trimming of two cone faces is wrong.

Sharpened diagnosis (2026-07-07): faces 1 (cone ha 84.25°) and 3 (cone ha 73.04°) are
"pie-slice-with-apex" patches — the cone APEX is one of their boundary vertices, i.e. a
UV U-pole. Both of each face's two boundary edges lie at the SAME iso-V line (same
distance from the apex): e.g. face 1's edge 0 (junction with cone 0) and edge 4
(junction with plane 2, a plane perpendicular to the cone axis tangent to the cone)
both sit at V=11.35, U∈[4.76,7.34]. The generic wire builder (create_wire_based_periodic_
face, is_sphere=false) then collapses the wire: both edges project onto the same iso-V
arc, so the enclosed area is ~0 (face 3 came out 0.0001 mm²; face 1 mis-built to 130 mm²).

Two dead ends already explored:
- Pure UV-bounds "apex cap" (U=[0,2π], V=[0,V_arc], apex as degenerate V-pole, like the
  spherical pole path): gets the AREA right (403 / 163 mm²) but breaks sewing — the cap's
  boundary is OCCT-generated, not the shared edge objects, and it only geometrically

  mesh vertices scatter U across the full circle and a 148° wedge falsely reads as a 354°
  full revolution.

face 1) as the outer boundary — unwrapped to the correct arc so they don't stack on the
same U-range — (b) inserts a degenerate edge at the apex U-pole (the sphere pole-insertion
machinery in create_wire_based_periodic_face, currently gated behind is_sphere, generalized
to the cone apex), and (c) picks the correct V-side. Caution: existing code notes ShapeFix
segfaults on cones, so pole/degenerate handling for cones must be built without ShapeFix.
Low value (one unusual model, already emits valid-ish output) — but this is now a concrete,

440	### Stage 3: Surface Reconstruction
441	
442	Build OCCT B-Rep topology (faces, edges, vertices) from the selected surfaces. This is the most complex stage — surface intersections in 3D are numerically delicate, and small perturbations can cause large changes in intersection curves or cause them to disappear.
443	
444	**Core data structures:**
445	
446	A vector of \`FaceDescriptor\` structs, one per selected surface:
447	- \`selected_surface_idx: usize\` — Index into the selected surfaces from stage 2.6.
448	- \`surface: OwnedPtr<HandleGeomSurface>\` — Infinite OCCT surface, type-erased (created in 3.1).
449	- \`adjacent_faces: Vec<usize>\` — Indices of adjacent FaceDescriptors, ordered topologically around this face's boundary. A face may appear multiple times if it shares multiple edges with this face (e.g., a cylindrical face adjacent to itself via a seam edge).
450	- \`edge_indices: Vec<usize>\` — ReconEdge indices. \`edge_indices[i]\` is the edge between this face and \`adjacent_faces[i]\`.
451	- \`vertex_indices: Vec<usize>\` — BRepVertex indices at corners. \`vertex_indices[i]\` is the vertex between \`edge_indices[i]\` and \`edge_indices[(i+1) % N]\`.
452	- (TODO) \`occt_face: Option<TopoDS_Face>\` — Populated in 3.4.
453	
454	A vector of \`ReconEdge\` structs:
455	- \`face_indices: [usize; 2]\` — Indices of the two adjacent FaceDescriptors.
456	- \`vertex_indices: [usize; 2]\` — Indices of the two BRepVertices at each end. For closed-loop edges (no vertices), both are \`usize::MAX\`.
457	- \`curve_3d: Option<OwnedPtr<HandleGeomCurve>>\` — 3D intersection curve, trimmed to vertex endpoints (populated in 3.3).
458	- (TODO) \`pcurves: [Handle<Geom2d_Curve>; 2]\` — 2D parametric curve on each adjacent face's surface.
459	- \`tangent: bool\` — Whether the adjacent surfaces are tangent along this edge (detected in 3.2).
460	- \`mesh_boundary_vertices: Vec<usize>\` — Mesh vertex indices along this boundary, ordered along the boundary.
461	
462	A vector of \`BRepVertex\` structs:
463	- \`point: [f64; 3]\` — 3D position: the mesh vertex position, refined for sharp corners by cyclic projection onto the adjacent fitted surfaces (see stage 2.6 refitting notes).
464	- \`adjacent_faces: Vec<usize>\` — Indices of FaceDescriptors meeting at this vertex, in topological order.
465	- \`adjacent_edges: Vec<usize>\` — Indices of ReconEdges meeting at this vertex, in topological order.
466	- (TODO) \`uv_coords: Vec<(f64, f64)>\` — UV coordinates of this vertex on each adjacent face's surface.
467	- (TODO) \`tolerance: f64\` — Maximum deviation from any adjacent surface.
468	
469	#### 3.1 Create OCCT surface objects and build adjacency graph
470	
471	**Surface creation** (\`create_occt_surface\`):
472	- For each selected surface, create the corresponding infinite OCCT surface:
473	    - Planar → \`geom::Plane::new_pnt_dir\` with \`gp::Pnt\` at centroid and \`gp::Dir\` along normal. Wrapped via \`to_handle().to_handle_surface()\`.
474	    - Cylindrical → \`geom::CylindricalSurface::new_ax3_real\` with \`gp::Ax3\` from axis origin/direction and radius. Wrapped via \`to_handle().to_handle_surface()\`.
475	    - Spherical → \`geom::SphericalSurface::new_ax3_real\` with \`gp::Ax3\` from center and Z-axis direction. Wrapped via \`to_handle().to_handle_surface()\`.
476	    - Conical → \`geom::ConicalSurface::new_ax3_real2\` with \`gp::Ax3\` from apex/direction and half-angle + radius at reference height. Wrapped via \`to_handle().to_handle_surface()\`. The \`Ax3\` origin is at the cone apex, Z along axis.
477	    - Toroidal → \`geom::ToroidalSurface::new_ax3_real2\` with \`gp::Ax3\` from center/axis direction, major radius $R$, and minor radius $r$. Wrapped via \`to_handle().to_handle_surface()\`. The \`Ax3\` origin is at the torus center, Z along rotation axis.
478	    - (Future: BSpline → \`Geom_BSplineSurface\` via \`GeomAPI_PointsToBSplineSurface\`.)
479	
480	- For consistency with OCCT conventions: planes use gp_Ax3 with Z as normal; cylinders have Z along axis; spheres have poles at Z extremes; cones have Z along axis from apex; tori have Z along rotation axis. This affects pcurve computation in 3.3.
481	
482	
483	**Adjacency graph construction:**
484	1. Build face-to-surface map: for each mesh face, record which selected surface it belongs to (\`build_face_to_surface_map\`).
485	2. Collect boundary edges: walk all mesh edges; when an edge separates faces belonging to different surfaces, record it as an \`UndirectedEdge\` keyed by \`SurfacePair\` (\`collect_boundary_edges\`).
486	3. Chain boundary edges: for each surface pair, chain connected boundary edges into ordered vertex sequences (\`chain_boundary_edges\`). Each chain becomes a \`ReconEdge\` with the mesh boundary vertices in order.
487	4. Find corner vertices: mesh vertices where 3+ selected surfaces meet become \`BRepVertex\` entries (\`find_corner_vertices\`). Their 3D position is taken from the mesh vertex.
488	5. Assign vertex indices to edges: for each \`ReconEdge\`, check if its first/last mesh boundary vertex is a corner vertex and set \`vertex_indices\` accordingly (or \`usize::MAX\` for closed-loop edges).
489	6. Build face descriptors: for each selected surface, create a \`FaceDescriptor\` with the OCCT surface handle. Walk the boundary edges, ordering them topologically around the face boundary (\`walk_edges_around_face\`). This uses a rotation-order algorithm: at each vertex, pick the next edge that rotates counter-clockwise around the face. This populates \`adjacent_faces\`, \`edge_indices\`, and \`vertex_indices\` for each face.
490	7. Build vertex adjacency: for each \`BRepVertex\`, walk the edges meeting at that vertex in topological order, recording \`adjacent_faces\` and \`adjacent_edges\`.
491	8. Validate topology: check Euler's formula V-E+F=2 for genus-0 models.
492	
493	- With the \`--compare\` flag (runs after stage 3.2 tangency detection):
494	    - For each \`ReconEdge\`, sample the mesh boundary vertices along the edge. For each sample vertex, compute the distance to the nearest edge/vertex in the reference STEP file using \`BRepExtrema_DistShapeShape\`. Report an error if any sample exceeds the edge's tolerance: \`--vertex-tolerance\` for sharp edges, \`--surface-tolerance\` for tangent edges (an imprecise tessellation can place the region boundary one row off a tangent junction — still within chordal tolerance of both surfaces and harmless, since tangent junction curves are built from the fitted hypotheses, not from these vertices).
495	    - For each \`BRepVertex\`, compute the distance from the vertex's 3D position to the nearest vertex in the reference STEP file. Report an error if any exceeds \`--vertex-tolerance\`.
496	    - These checks validate that the adjacency graph's topological features (edges where surfaces meet, corners where 3+ surfaces meet) correspond to real features in the reference model.
497	
498	#### 3.2 Detect tangency relationships
499	For each ReconEdge, determine whether the two adjacent surfaces are tangent along the shared boundary. This matters because \`GeomAPI_IntSS\` can fail or produce degenerate results for tangent/near-tangent surfaces, requiring special handling in edge curve computation (3.3).
500	
501	**Detection algorithm (implemented):**
502	- For each ReconEdge, sample mesh boundary vertices along the shared boundary (every 5th vertex, minimum 3 samples, always including first and last).
503	- At each sample point, compute the outward-facing surface normal of both adjacent surfaces analytically:
504	    - Planar: the hypothesis normal (constant).
505	    - Cylindrical: normalized radial direction from axis to point, negated if concave.
506	    - Spherical: normalized direction from center to point, negated if concave.
507	    - Conical: radial direction from axis at the point's axial position, rotated by the cone's half-angle away from the axis, negated if concave. Specifically: for point $p$ with axial component $h = (p-A)\cdot\hat{a}$, the normal is the unit vector in the plane of (radial, axis) at angle $(90° - \theta)$ from radial.
508	    - Toroidal: direction from the nearest tube center point to the surface point, negated if concave. The tube center is $c = C + R \cdot \hat{r}$ where $\hat{r}$ is the radial unit vector from the torus axis to the point.
509	
510	- Compute the dot product of the two normals. If all sampled pairs agree within 2° (dot > cos(2°) ≈ 0.9994), mark the edge as tangent.
511	- Points too close to a cylinder axis or sphere center (degenerate) cause the edge to be marked non-tangent.
512	
513	**Decision: do not modify surfaces to enforce tangency.** Modifying analytic surfaces would change the geometry. Instead, tangent edges get special handling in edge curve computation (3.3): construct the edge curve directly rather than relying on surface-surface intersection.
514	
515	Tangent edges arise from fillets and blends: part_rounded_cube_10_r2 has 8 plane-cylinder tangent edges, and rounded_cube_10_r2 has 46 tangent edges (plane-cylinder + sphere-cylinder). Toroidal fillets produce tangent edges at both boundaries (torus-plane, torus-cylinder, torus-torus).
516	
517	
518	- With the \`--compare\` flag:
519	    - For each ReconEdge marked as tangent, verify that the corresponding edge in the reference STEP file is also tangent (i.e., the two adjacent STEP surfaces have matching normals along the STEP edge). Report a warning if tangency is detected in the mesh but not in the STEP reference, or vice versa.
520	    - This is a consistency check, not a geometry check — stage 3.1's --compare already validates that mesh edge boundary vertices lie on STEP edges. Stage 3.2 adds validation that the tangency classification itself is correct.
521	
522	#### 3.3 Create edge curves
523	For each ReconEdge, compute the 3D intersection curve between the two adjacent surfaces, trim it to the vertex endpoints, and store in \`edge.curve_3d\`.
524	
525	**Intersection computation (implemented):**
526	- For non-tangent edges: use \`GeomAPI_IntSS\` to compute intersection curves with tolerance \`vertex_tolerance_mm\`. IntSS may return multiple curves (e.g., a plane cutting through a torus); \`select_closest_curve()\` picks the one closest to the mesh boundary vertices by sampling up to 10 evenly-spaced boundary vertices, projecting each onto each candidate curve via \`GeomAPI_ProjectPointOnCurve\`, and summing distances.
527	- For tangent edges: construct the curve analytically rather than using \`GeomAPI_IntSS\` (which fails or produces degenerate results for tangent/near-tangent surfaces). Dispatches by surface pair type:
528	  - **Plane-cylinder**: \`Geom_Line\` parallel to the cylinder axis at the tangent point, computed from the cylinder axis, radius, and the plane normal component perpendicular to the axis.
529	  - **Cylinder-cylinder**: \`Geom_Line\` along the first cylinder's axis direction.
530	  - **Sphere-cylinder**: \`Geom_Circle\` (great circle arc on the sphere). Center and radius come from the sphere hypothesis. The circle plane normal is \`normalize(cross(v0 - center, v1 - center))\`. Arc selection samples mesh boundary vertices to determine forward vs. reverse arc on the periodic circle. Open arcs use this path for slight cones too (the circle is built from sphere geometry + endpoint vertices, so it is valid for near-cylindrical cones such as fillets fitted with a small half-angle).
531	  - **Sphere-cone (closed loop)**: the tangent circle is NOT a great circle (it sits at radius R·cos α, offset along the cone axis). Constructed as a \`Geom_Circle\` perpendicular to the cone axis, with axial position and radius averaged from the edge's mesh boundary vertices (\`compute_tangent_edge_curve_axis_circle_closed\`) — the same vertex-averaging approach as plane-torus.
532	  - **Plane-cone** (TODO): \`Geom_Line\` along the cone's generator at the tangent azimuth, from the tangent point toward (or away from) the apex.
533	  - **Cylinder-cone** (TODO): \`Geom_Circle\` at the axial position where the cone radius equals the cylinder radius (when coaxial), or \`IntSS\`-based (non-coaxial).
534	  - **Plane-torus**: \`Geom_Circle\` perpendicular to the torus axis. Circle center and radius computed from mesh boundary vertices projected onto the torus axis. Handles both closed loops and arcs.
535	  - **Cylinder-torus**: \`Geom_Circle\` computed by the vertex-averaging algorithm against *both* candidate axes — the torus axis (coaxial fillet junctions) and the cylinder axis (tube-continuation junctions, e.g. a straight pipe leaving a pipe-elbow torus, where the junction is a tube cross-section) — keeping whichever circle best fits the boundary vertices.
536	  - **Torus-torus**: \`Geom_Circle\` perpendicular to the torus axis. Same vertex-averaging algorithm.
537	  - **Sphere-torus** (TODO): \`Geom_Circle\` — analogous to sphere-cylinder but the junction is a circle on the sphere.
538	  - **Fallback**: Construct a line from the two vertex endpoints.
539	
540	  All tangent edges are trimmed to vertex endpoints using the same parameter projection as non-tangent edges. A \`validate_tangent_curve\` step checks that boundary vertices lie within \`surface_tolerance_mm\` of the constructed curve.
541	
542	**Trimming to vertex endpoints (implemented):**
543	- For each ReconVertex at an edge endpoint, project the vertex's 3D position onto the intersection curve using \`GeomAPI_ProjectPointOnCurve\` to get the curve parameter value.
544	- Trim the curve to the parameter range \`[t_start, t_end]\` using \`Geom_TrimmedCurve\`.
545	- For closed-loop edges (vertex_indices == usize::MAX), use the full intersection curve parameter range.
546	- **Partial arc reconstruction**: When \`IntSS\` returns a partial arc for a closed-loop edge (e.g., a semicircle when a sphere-plane intersection passes through the sphere's UV poles), reconstruct the full circle from 3 sampled points on the arc using the circumscribed circle formula. This fixes cases where the intersection plane contains the sphere axis, causing \`IntSS\` to split the circle into two separate arcs in UV space.
547	- For non-periodic curves, ensure \`t_start < t_end\` (swap if needed).
548	- The resulting \`TrimmedCurve\` is upcast to \`HandleGeomCurve\` via \`.to_handle().to_handle_curve()\` and stored in \`edge.curve_3d\`.
549	
550	**Pcurve computation (deferred to stage 3.4):**
551	- Pcurves will be derived when creating \`TopoDS_Edge\` objects.
552	- Options: analytic pcurves for simple cases (line on plane, circle on cylinder), or \`ShapeFix_Wire::FixEdgeCurves\` for general cases.
553	
554	**Seam edges (future):**
555	- A face adjacent to itself (e.g., a full cylinder wrapping around) requires a seam edge at a fixed U or V parameter. Create the seam as an iso-parametric curve on the surface.
556	- Conical faces: full-revolution cones require a seam edge along one generator line (iso-U curve from apex to base).
557	- Toroidal faces: full-revolution tori (360° around major axis) require a seam at one meridian (iso-U); full-tube tori (360° around minor circle) also need a seam at one parallel (iso-V). A complete torus needs both.
558	
559	
560	**Vertex position consistency (future):**
561	- OCCT requires all edges at a vertex to share the same \`TopoDS_Vertex\` (same 3D point). When edges computed independently disagree slightly about vertex position, use the averaged position from the ReconVertex and set the vertex tolerance to the maximum deviation.
562	
563	- With the \`--compare\` flag:
564	    - For each ReconEdge with a computed \`curve_3d\`, sample points along the trimmed curve (e.g., 10 evenly-spaced parameter values between start and end). For each sample point, compute the distance to the nearest edge in the reference STEP file using \`BRepExtrema_DistShapeShape\`. Report an error if any sample exceeds \`--vertex-tolerance\`.
565	    - Additionally, verify that the curve endpoints coincide with BRepVertex positions within \`--vertex-tolerance\`.
566	    - This validates that the computed intersection curves not only connect the right vertices but also follow the correct geometric path between them.
567	
568	#### 3.4 Create OCCT faces
569	For each ReconFace, construct a \`TopoDS_Face\` from the surface and bounding wires.
570	
571	**Algorithm (as implemented):**
572	
573	*Stage 1: Create TopoDS_Edge for each ReconEdge.*
574	- For each \`ReconEdge\`, create a \`BRepBuilderAPI_MakeEdge\` using the trimmed 3D curve and shared \`TopoDS_Vertex\` endpoints from stage 3.3. For periodic curves (circles from cylinder/sphere intersections), vertex order is matched to the curve parameterization direction: V1 corresponds to \`first_parameter()\` and V2 to \`last_parameter()\`. This is critical because \`MakeEdge\` strips \`TrimmedCurve\` wrappers and uses \`ElCLib::AdjustPeriodic\` on the base periodic curve, which always selects the forward (CCW) arc from V1 to V2.
575	- **Adaptive vertex tolerance**: Before each \`MakeEdge\`, the distance between each vertex position and its curve endpoint is computed. The OCCT vertex tolerance is updated to at least that distance (with 1% margin), accommodating imprecisely-fitted surface intersection curves that don't pass exactly through mesh vertex positions. This replaces the earlier fixed \`vertex_tolerance_mm\` approach.
576	
577	*Stage 2: Create OCCT faces.*
578	- **Planar faces** use wire-based construction:
579	  - Group the face's edges into wire loops based on \`BRepVertex\` connectivity. Edges sharing a vertex index are grouped together; closed-loop edges (vertex_indices both \`usize::MAX\`) each form a separate wire.
580	  - Build \`BRepBuilderAPI_MakeWire\` for each group by sequentially adding \`TopoDS_Edge\` objects.
581	  - Identify the outer wire as the group with the most edges (heuristic).
582	  - Create \`BRepBuilderAPI_MakeFace\` with the surface handle and outer wire, then add inner wires as holes.
583	
584	- **Cylindrical, spherical, conical, and toroidal faces** use three approaches:
585	
586	  - **Full revolution** (all boundary edges are closed loops): UV-bounds construction via \`MakeFace::new_handlegeomsurface_real5(surface, umin, umax, vmin, vmax, tol)\`. UV bounds are computed from edge projections using a circular gap algorithm that handles periodicity. This automatically creates seam edges for proper B-Rep topology.
587	  - **Spherical faces with closed-loop edges near poles** (e.g., pill/capsule hemispheres or dome hemispheres cut by a meridional plane): The boundary circles may pass through or near the sphere's UV singularities (poles at V=±π/2 where U is undefined). When any boundary circle passes within 45° of either pole (detected via \`ProjectPointOnCurve\` + chord-length formula), the sphere surface is recreated with its Z-axis aligned to a reorientation axis. The axis is determined from: (a) the adjacent cylinder's axis direction for tangent edges, or (b) the boundary circle's plane normal for non-tangent edges (computed from 3 sampled points on the curve). This is safe because for all-closed-loop boundaries, the reorientation axis is unique. The face's V bounds are computed by projecting samples of each boundary circle onto the oriented surface: for sphere-cylinder tangencies the junction is a great circle (V=0), but for sphere-cone tangencies it sits at a nonzero latitude, so fixed hemisphere bounds would misplace the boundary. With a single boundary circle, the face spans from that circle's latitude to the pole on the side occupied by the mesh (determined by projecting a mesh face centroid and checking the V-sign); with two, it spans between them.
588	  - **Spherical faces with pole vertices** (e.g., rounded cube corners where cylinders meet at a sphere pole): When a spherical face's UV bounds include V=±π/2, vertex U values at the pole are undefined (singularity). The \`compute_uv_bounds_from_edges\` function excludes pole U values (within 0.01 radians of ±π/2) from the circular gap algorithm to avoid corrupted U spans. The face is then constructed via UV-bounds \`MakeFace::new_handlegeomsurface_real5\`, producing a triangular-topology face (3 edges, 2 meridians + 1 parallel; pole collapsed to a vertex). These faces have a harmless BRepCheck edge failure (tolerance ~0) on the first edge, resolved by sewing.
589	  - **Partial revolution** (open edges with vertices): Wire-based construction with pre-set pcurves. Before building the wire, \`BRep_Builder::update_edge\` sets \`Geom2d_Line\` pcurves on each IntSS edge for the periodic surface, mapping the edge's 3D parameter range to (u(t), v(t)) in surface UV space. This ensures MakeFace selects the correct arc and shares edges with adjacent planar faces for sewing.
590	  - **Conical faces**: Same approaches as cylinder: full revolution via UV-bounds (with circular gap for U and cone apex V-extension), partial via wire+pcurves. The cone apex vertex is handled as a UV singularity (V extended to 0 for non-truncated cones). All test models pass: simple_cone, cone_cylinder, nosecone, block_with_conical_hole.
591	  - **Toroidal faces**: UV-bounds construction for complete torus patches. The torus UV space is doubly periodic: U ∈ [0,2π) around the major axis, V ∈ [0,2π) around the tube. Boundary edges are classified from per-edge projected samples: *iso-V* circles (fillet junctions: constant tube angle, spanning U) give a face full in U with V from the circular gap algorithm; *iso-U* circles (tube-continuation junctions, e.g. pipe elbows: constant major angle, spanning the full tube) give a face full in V with U from the circular gap algorithm over the edges' U positions, disambiguated by mesh centroid projections. Multiple sample points per edge curve (3 instead of 1) define the V window; mesh face centroid projections only *disambiguate* which of the two candidate arcs the face spans — they never extend the bounds (a cap triangle whose three vertices all lie on the plane-torus junction circle is legitimately absorbed by the torus hypothesis, but its centroid projects slightly past the tangent circle and would otherwise shift the face boundary off the junction, breaking sewing). Fillet patches typically span a small V arc (e.g., π/2 for a 90° fillet).
592	
593	  - Full spheres (no edges) use \`MakeFace::new_handlegeomsurface_real(surface, tolerance)\` with natural bounds.
594	
595	*Stage 3: Validate and compare.*
596	- Validate each face with \`BRepCheck_Analyzer\`. For invalid faces, run detailed \`BRepCheck_Face\` diagnostics (intersect_wires, classify_wires, orientation_of_wires, is_unorientable) and sub-shape analysis (edge tolerance, vertex checks). Faces where the only failure is edges with near-zero tolerance (< \`vertex_tolerance_mm\`) are treated as harmless (occurs on UV-bounds sphere pole faces, resolved by sewing) and not counted as failures.
597	- Wire orientation fix: after adding inner wires (holes) to a face, apply \`ShapeFix_Face::fix_orientation()\` to ensure inner wires are oriented opposite to the outer wire. This eliminates BRepCheck "bad orientation of sub-shape" warnings that previously appeared on all planar faces with holes.
598	- With \`--compare\`: for each face, sample a representative mesh face centroid from the surface's mesh faces and compute distance to the reference STEP shape using \`BRepExtrema_DistShapeShape\`. Report face count comparison. Error if max distance exceeds \`--surface-tolerance\`.
599	
600	#### 3.5 Construct shells
601	Group faces into shells using \`BRepBuilderAPI_Sewing\`.
602	
603	**Algorithm (as implemented):**
604	- Create a \`BRepBuilderAPI_Sewing\` instance with tolerance set to \`vertex_tolerance\`.
605	- Add all \`TopoDS_Face\` objects to the sewing operation.
606	- After \`Perform()\`, extract the sewed shape and iterate over its sub-shapes:
607	  - \`Shell\` sub-shapes are used directly.
608	  - Individual \`Face\` sub-shapes (e.g., a single-face model like \`simple_sphere\`) are wrapped in a new \`TopoDS_Shell\` via \`BRep_Builder\`.
609	  - \`Solid\`, \`Compound\`, and \`Compsolid\` sub-shapes are explored recursively for \`Shell\` children.
610	- Apply \`ShapeFix_Shell::Perform()\` (which calls \`ShapeFix_Face::Perform()\` on each face to re-add pcurves that sewing may have discarded, and \`FixFaceOrientation\` for edge consistency). Face orientation is NOT post-processed — \`FixFaceOrientation\` handles edge consistency and \`SolidFromShell\` (stage 3.6) handles global orientation via \`PerformInfinitePoint\`. Investigation showed that flipping individual face orientations breaks edge consistency and causes volume computation errors.
611	- Validate with \`ShapeAnalysis_Shell::CheckOrientedShells\` and report inconsistencies.
612	- Report sewing statistics: free edges, multiple edges, contiguous edges.
613	
614	- With the \`--compare\` flag:
615	    - Count shells in the reference STEP file by exploring for \`Shell\` sub-shapes.
616	    - Report an error if the sewing produced free edges (edges not shared by any pair of faces), as this indicates incomplete stitching.
617	    - Report shell count comparison and orientation check results.
618	
619	#### 3.6 Construct solids
620	Convert closed shells into \`TopoDS_Solid\` objects.
621	
622	**Algorithm:**
623	- For each shell, use \`ShapeFix_Solid::SolidFromShell\` which handles orientation automatically.
624	- Apply \`ShapeFix_Shape::Perform()\` for comprehensive face/wire/edge/shell/solid fixes.
625	- Call \`BRepLib::SameParameter\` with \`forced=false\` and tight tolerance (\`vertex_tolerance_mm\`) to ensure pcurve/3D curve agreement without corrupting already-correct pcurves. Using \`forced=true\` or a large tolerance (e.g. 1.0mm) recomputes all pcurves and can corrupt faces with closely-spaced tangent edges (e.g. sphere faces at sphere-cylinder junctions), causing BRepCheck self-intersection failures.
626	- Call \`BRepLib::UpdateTolerances\` and \`BRepLib::OrientClosedSolid\`.
627	- Validate with \`BRepCheck_Analyzer\`. Log warning if validation fails (may indicate upstream face issues from stage 3.4).
628	- Compute and report volume using \`BRepGProp::VolumeProperties\`.
629	- **Multi-shell solids (internal voids)**: after per-shell solids are built, \`merge_void_solids\` finds solids whose bounding box is contained in a strictly larger solid's box; each such void's shells are added to the container solid (\`BRep_Builder::Add\`), trying both shell orientations and keeping the one whose resulting volume equals container − Σ voids. The hollow_cube test model (tests/occt/, generated by \`gen-test-models\` since ccad cannot express enclosed voids) validates one solid of 7000 mm³ instead of two nested solids.
630	
631	- With the \`--compare\` flag:
632	    - Count solids in the reference STEP file.
633	    - Compute volumes of both constructed and reference solids. Match by sorted volume. Report warning if relative volume difference exceeds 1%. All current test models achieve volume agreement within ~1e-7 relative difference.
634	    - Compute \`BRepExtrema_DistShapeShape\` between each constructed solid and the reference STEP shape. Report error if distance exceeds \`--surface-tolerance\`. This is the tightest geometric accuracy check.
635	
636	#### 3.x (proposed) Rework: shared-edge topological assembly instead of geometric sewing
637	
638	**Status: not started. Deliberately deferred and bound to the NURBS effort (see Future Enhancements). This section records the decision and its trigger so it is not rediscovered from scratch.**
639	
640	**The current design.** Stage 3.4 builds each face independently and stage 3.5 reconciles them with \`BRepBuilderAPI_Sewing\`, a *geometric* stitch that merges edges by proximity within a tolerance. Edges *are* created once as shared \`TopoDS_Edge\` objects (§3.1), but two things defeat that sharing by assembly time:
641	- \`MakeFace\`/\`MakeWire\`/\`ShapeFix\` copy edges, so the "shared" edge in face A is no longer the identical object in face B.
642	- The UV-bounds construction paths (full spheres, complete tori, full-revolution and — as of the cone-cap investigation — apex-cap cones) synthesize their *own* natural-bounds boundary edges that were never shared with a neighbour at all.
643	
644	So sewing is load-bearing, and the \`ReconEdge.pcurves: [_; 2]\` and \`BRepVertex.uv_coords\` fields (§3.0) that the original design earmarked for a both-sides-shared representation were never populated — the geometric sewing pass stands in for them. The face-construction + sewing block is ~2100 lines carrying ~150 pole/seam/apex/reorient/ShapeFix/degenerate special-cases.
645	
646	**Why this is the root of a whole class of fragility.** Every hard case in stage 3 — sphere pole caps, torus seams, cone apex caps, and the tangent-edge/corner-vertex *tolerance relaxations* (the "genuinely ambiguous junction rows") — is ultimately a symptom of trimming faces independently and matching them by geometric tolerance. \`cone_tangent_planes\` is the sharpest example: its two apex-cap cone faces are pie-slices-with-apex whose two boundary curves lie on the same iso-V line; the wire builder collapses them, and a pure UV-bounds cap gets the *area* right but only matches its neighbours along part of the boundary, so sewing leaves free edges → open shell. The problem spans segmentation → edge topology → trimming → sewing, which is exactly why patching any single layer only half-works.
647	
648	**The proposed design.** Build the B-rep topologically instead of geometrically:
649	1. Build each edge once (shared \`TopoDS_Edge\` + shared vertices, with its 3D curve) — as today.
650	2. For **both** adjacent faces of every edge, compute and attach the pcurve of that edge on that face's surface (populate \`ReconEdge.pcurves\`). Poles/seams are handled *only* here, in pcurve computation, uniformly for every periodic surface.
651	3. Insert degenerate edges at UV poles (cone apex, sphere pole) and seam edges at periodic wraps, shared correctly, as first-class topology rather than per-surface fix-ups.
652	4. Assemble each face and the shell directly with \`BRep_Builder\` from the shared edges — the shell is closed *by construction*. Drop \`BRepBuilderAPI_Sewing\`; it becomes at most a validation check.
653	5. This makes construction lower-level and more controlled (avoid \`ShapeFix\`/\`MakeFace\` edge-copying that breaks sharing). The cone apex cap, sphere pole cap, and torus seam then all reduce to "attach the correct pcurve to the shared edge, plus a degenerate/seam edge" — one uniform mechanism instead of ~150 special-cases.
654	
655	**Why defer it.** 52/57 models pass; nothing is *blocked*. The only current beneficiary is one unusual model (\`cone_tangent_planes\`) that already writes valid-ish output with a volume warning. The full payoff arrives with **NURBS**: freeform patches have arbitrary trimmed boundaries and will stress this machinery hard, building NURBS on top of projection+sewing is building on sand, and NURBS is also what finally brings test coverage to validate a more general assembler (today it would be a more-general machine exercised only on the analytic surfaces the current code already handles). So the rework is the *foundation to lay when NURBS begins*, not a standalone task.
656	
657	**Trigger to pull it forward earlier.** If a model becomes *unfixable* without tighter topology — i.e. the tangent-edge/corner tolerance relaxations stop merely loosening tolerances and start letting a real model fail — do the rework then rather than adding relaxation #N.
658	
659	**Where the code lives (cold-start entry points).** All of stage 3 is in \`src/stage3.rs\` (~5800 lines); entry \`stage3()\`. The assembler is \`create_occt_faces_all\`: it builds one shared \`TopoDS_Vertex\` per \`BRepVertex\`, one shared \`TopoDS_Edge\` per \`ReconEdge\` (from \`ReconEdge.curve_3d\`, held in the \`topo_edges\` vec indexed by edge id — this is the sharing that later gets defeated), then dispatches each face to \`create_planar_face\` or \`create_periodic_face\`. \`create_periodic_face\` (cones/spheres/tori) chooses among: natural-bounds (\`MakeFace::new_handlegeomsurface_real\`, complete closed surfaces with no edges); UV-bounds (\`MakeFace::new_handlegeomsurface_real5\`, full-revolution / all-closed-loop / reoriented-sphere); and wire-based \`create_wire_based_periodic_face\` (partial revolution — projects each edge's 3D curve to pcurve points, sets the pcurve on the shared edge via \`BRep_Builder::update_edge_edge_...\`, builds a \`MakeWire\`, then \`MakeFace\`). Sewing is \`construct_shells\` (\`BRepBuilderAPI_Sewing\`); solids and void-merging are §3.6. The both-sides representation to populate is already declared but unused: \`ReconEdge.pcurves: [_; 2]\` and \`BRepVertex.uv_coords\` (§3.0 data structures).
660	
661	**Hard OCCT constraints (established empirically — do not relearn by crashing).**
662	- \`ShapeFix_*\` can **segfault on cone faces** (pcurve/edge-curve interaction); the wire path already skips ShapeFix for non-spheres for this reason. A shared-edge assembler that attaches pcurves directly and avoids \`ShapeFix\`/\`MakeFace\` edge-copying sidesteps this — but do not reintroduce ShapeFix on cone faces to "clean up" a wire.
663	- \`is_periodic\` in \`create_occt_faces_all\` **must include \`Conical(_)\`** or cone faces route to \`create_planar_face\` and segfault on a full-circle edge (LEARNINGS: "Conical faces need is_periodic treatment").
664	- \`MakeEdge\` on a periodic (circle) curve forces p1 < p2 and takes the forward arc V1→V2, so **vertex order selects which arc** — see the explicit first/last-parameter handling in \`create_occt_faces_all\` (the \`d0_start\`/\`d1_start\` block). This is the same complementary-arc trap that collapses the \`cone_tangent_planes\` apex caps.
665	- Thread-safety of the OCCT calls used here: LEARNINGS "OCCT Thread Safety" (BRepExtrema, MakeEdge/Face/Vertex/Sewing, ShapeFix_* are all safe; only STEP Reader/Writer need serializing).
666	
667	**Reproduce & validate the motivating case.**
668	- Repro: \`./target/release/brepper tests/onshape/cone_tangent_planes_medium.stl --compare tests/onshape/cone_tangent_planes.step -o tmp/x.step\` → completes (exit 0) but prints a stage-3.6 volume **WARNING** (6617 vs 14676 mm³) and three BRepCheck "face shape invalid" warnings.
669	- Inspect: \`--stage=3.4 -v\` prints each face's \`area=…\` (the two bad caps come out 0.0001 and a wrong 130 mm²) and which faces fail BRepCheck; \`--stage=3.1 -v\` lists each face's surface type + fitted parameters and every edge as \`faces [a,b] vertices [v0,v1]\`.
670	- Done = full suite green (\`cargo test --release\`, ~3 min) **and** \`cone_tangent_planes\` volume within 1% with no warning; regenerate \`tests/RESULTS.md\` via \`./scripts/run_test_table.sh\`.
671	- Directly relevant LEARNINGS entries to read first: the "Partial revolution … wire-based … pcurves" note, the two sphere-pole-vertex entries, the cone "extend V to the apex" entry, and "Conical faces need is_periodic treatment".
672

#!/bin/bash
# Run all STL test files through brepper and generate tests/RESULTS.md
# Usage: ./scripts/run_test_table.sh [<brepper_binary>]
# Default binary: ./target/release/brepper

set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

BREPPER="${1:-./target/release/brepper}"

if [ ! -x "$BREPPER" ]; then
    echo "Error: brepper binary not found at $BREPPER" >&2
    echo "Build with: cargo build --release" >&2
    exit 1
fi

OUTPUT="tests/RESULTS.md"

# Map STL file to its corresponding STEP file
find_step() {
    local stl="$1"
    local dir=$(dirname "$stl")
    local base=$(basename "$stl" .stl)

    # Strip .ascii suffix if present
    base="${base%.ascii}"

    # Try exact match first
    if [ -f "$dir/$base.step" ]; then
        echo "$dir/$base.step"
        return
    fi

    # Strip resolution suffixes (_coarse, _medium, _fine, _low, _high)
    local stripped=$(echo "$base" | sed -E 's/_(coarse|medium|fine|low|high)$//')
    if [ -f "$dir/$stripped.step" ]; then
        echo "$dir/$stripped.step"
        return
    fi

    echo ""
}

# Special flags for specific tests
get_extra_flags() {
    local stl="$1"
    case "$stl" in
        *rounded_cube_10_r2_coarse*)
            echo "--angular-tolerance 20"
            ;;
        *)
            echo ""
            ;;
    esac
}

# Count totals
total=0
pass_count=0
fail_count=0

`BRep_Builder` exposes everything needed (make_face/wire/shell/solid, add, degenerated, two-pcurve seam edges via the `handlegeom2dcurve2` variants). Before committing to the hardest path, let me check what the LEARNINGS already establish about edge sharing and sewing, since that determines how much I must hand-build.


## 🤖🔧 Assistant
<details>
<summary>Bash: Search LEARNINGS for sewing/edge-sharing facts</summary>

```bash
grep -n -i "sewing\|shared edge\|share.*edge\|copies edge\|copy.*edge\|MakeFace\|free edge\|seam" LEARNINGS.md | head -50
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>Tool Result</summary>

```
63:- All \`BRepBuilderAPI\` (MakeEdge, MakeFace, MakeVertex, Sewing) — only static helper functions
225:- **Planar faces**: Create \`TopoDS_Edge\` from trimmed curve using \`BRepBuilderAPI_MakeEdge::new_handlegeomcurve(curve)\`. Group edges into wire loops by \`BRepVertex\` vertex connectivity (union-find style). Build \`MakeWire\` from edges, \`MakeFace\` from surface + outer wire + hole wires.
227:  - **Full revolution** (all boundary edges are closed loops): Use UV-bounds construction via \`MakeFace::new_handlegeomsurface_real5(surface, umin, umax, vmin, vmax, tol)\`. This automatically creates seam edges needed for proper B-Rep topology. Circular gap algorithm computes correct u-bounds even when edges cross the 0/2π seam.
228:  - **Partial revolution** (open edges with vertices): Use wire-based construction WITH pre-set pcurves via \`BRep_Builder::update_edge\` before calling \`MakeFace\`. The pcurves (Geom2d_Line) map the edge's 3D parameter range to the surface's UV space. This ensures correct arc selection on the periodic surface and shares edges with adjacent planar faces for proper sewing.
229:- **Full spheres** (no edges): Use \`MakeFace::new_handlegeomsurface_real(surface, tolerance)\` which uses natural surface bounds.
233:- **Shared vertices**: Create \`TopoDS_Vertex\` objects from \`BRepVertex\` positions (\`MakeVertex::new_pnt(pt)\` then \`.vertex().to_owned()\`), then set vertex tolerance to \`vertex_tolerance_mm\` via \`BRep_Builder::update_vertex_vertex_real()\` (OCCT default tolerance ~1e-7 is too tight for mesh vertices). Use \`MakeEdge::new_handlegeomcurve_vertex2_real2(curve, &v1, &v2, fp, lp)\` with explicit parameter values to avoid OCCT's vertex-to-curve projection (which fails with \`Pointprojectionfailed\` when vertex is slightly off the curve). Parameters are always \`(first_parameter, last_parameter)\` since V1 is always ordered to be the vertex closest to the curve's start point.
234:- **Pcurves on periodic faces**: For partial-revolution periodic faces, pcurves must be pre-set on IntSS edges using \`BRep_Builder::update_edge_edge_handlegeom2dcurve_handlegeomsurface_location_real()\` BEFORE creating the MakeFace. Without pre-set pcurves, MakeFace may compute incorrect pcurves that select the wrong arc of the periodic surface.
237:- **Wire orientation fix for holes**: After adding inner wires (holes) to a \`MakeFace\`, apply \`shape_fix::Face::new_face(make_face.face())\` then \`.fix_orientation()\` to ensure inner wires are oriented opposite to the outer wire. Wrap the result back via \`MakeFace::new_face(&fixer.face())\`. Without this, OCCT's BRepCheck reports \`Badorientationofsubshape\` on every planar face with holes.
250:- \`BRepBuilderAPI_Sewing\`: Create with \`Sewing::new_real(tolerance)\` where tolerance = \`vertex_tolerance_mm\`. Add all faces via \`.add(face.as_shape())\`, then \`.perform(&ProgressRange::new())\`.
257:- Sewing statistics: \`.nb_free_edges()\`, \`.nb_multiple_edges()\`, \`.nb_contigous_edges()\` — note the OCCT typo "contigous" (not "contiguous").
278:- **Reorientation for all-closed-loop spheres (tangent and non-tangent)**: When a sphere face has all-closed-loop boundary edges and any boundary circle passes within 45° of a UV pole, the sphere surface is reoriented so the boundary circles become iso-V curves. The reorientation axis is determined from: (a) the adjacent cylinder's axis direction for tangent edges, or (b) the boundary circle's plane normal for non-tangent edges (e.g., dome hemispheres cut by a meridional plane). This generalizes the original tangent-only reorientation and fixes sewing failures for hemispheres where the flat face plane contains the sphere axis.
279:- **Failed alternatives**: (1) Wire-based split-at-poles with \`ShapeConstruct_ProjectCurveOnSurface\` produced correct face areas but wrong volume (cylinder only) due to BRepCheck edge/vertex consistency issues. (2) UV-bounds on the original sphere with mesh-centroid-derived U range produced 6 free edges because UV-bounds boundaries are iso-parametric meridian arcs, geometrically different from the tangent circles.
280:- **Sphere pole vertex faces** (open edges with vertices at poles, e.g., rounded cube corners where each octant has one vertex at a pole): When a spherical face has open edges with vertices, and the UV bounds include V=±π/2, the U value at the pole is undefined (singularity). This corrupts the circular gap algorithm for U bounds (producing ~205° span instead of ~90°), pcurves (diagonal instead of meridional), and face areas (negative). Fix: in \`compute_uv_bounds_from_edges\`, exclude U values from vertices/midpoints within 0.01 radians of a pole (V ≈ ±π/2). The face is constructed via UV-bounds \`MakeFace::new_handlegeomsurface_real5\`. OCCT creates a 3-edge face (2 meridians + 1 parallel at the non-pole boundary; the pole collapses to a vertex with no degenerate edge). BRepCheck reports a harmless edge failure on edge 0 with ~zero tolerance; this is suppressed in \`validate_faces\` since it's resolved by sewing.
281:- **BRep_Builder::degenerated(&edge, true)**: Sets the degenerate flag on an edge. \`BRep_Tool::degenerated(&edge)\` queries it. MakeFace UV-bounds on spheres near poles does NOT automatically mark pole edges as degenerate. The edges at the pole have finite 3D length (they are the meridian arcs, not zero-length pole edges).
282:- **BRepCheck_Analyzer::new_shape_bool(shape, false)**: \`GeomControls=false\` checks only topological info. However, UV-bounds sphere pole faces fail BOTH geometric and topological checks on edge 0 (~zero tolerance). The root cause is unclear but harmless — the final solid after sewing passes BRepCheck.
331:Cone and cylinder seeds use a "fan" topology: initial face fi, neighbor f1, and another face f2 that is a neighbor of fi but NOT an edge-wise neighbor of f1. This puts fi in between f1 and f2 for better angular coverage. Pairwise qualification checks normals of f1 and f2 against fi's normal (not against each other). When fi+f1+f2 yield only 5 unique vertices (insufficient for 6-DOF cone fitting), an optional f3 is added — a face adjacent to f2 that doesn't share an edge with fi or f1, giving at least 6 vertices.
347:\`create_wire_based_periodic_face\` deliberately skips \`ShapeFix_Wire\`/\`ShapeFix_Face\` for non-sphere periodic faces: on cones, ShapeFix crashes (not just errors) due to pcurve/edge-curve interactions. Spheres tolerate it. So cone face repair must be done without ShapeFix. This constrains the proposed stage-3 shared-edge rework (DEVELOPMENT_PLAN §3.x): attach pcurves to shared edges directly with \`BRep_Builder\` rather than routing cone faces through ShapeFix to "fix up" a wire.
388:Full (non-truncated) cones with a single boundary edge at the base produce zero V-range from \`compute_uv_bounds_from_edges\` (both V values project to the same edge height). This creates a degenerate face → BRepCheck failure → sewing failure. Fix: for conical surfaces with a single boundary edge, extend V to 0 (the apex) by sampling mesh face centroids to determine which side of the edge the face extends, then setting \`vmin = 0.0\`. This is analogous to sphere pole V-extension for hemispheres.
392:The \`is_concave\` check in \`create_periodic_face\` must handle \`SelectedSurface::Conical(idx)\` using \`!hypothesis.convex\`, not default to \`false\`. Concave cones (e.g., conical holes) need reversed normals during face construction so that sewing produces correctly oriented shells.
425:When convex and concave tori share edges (e.g., filleted_pipe: R=8.5 convex and R=7.5 concave), boundary vertices have incident faces from both torus patches. Seeds at these vertices mix faces from different tori, producing tube centers that scatter between two different major circles. A quality gate on the 3D circle fit RMS (reject if rms > 0.1 * minor_r) catches these mixed seeds early, before BFS expansion wastes time on a bad hypothesis.
474:- Sphere faces reoriented for pole handling must compute V bounds by projecting boundary-circle samples onto the oriented surface: fixed hemisphere bounds [0, π/2] assume a great-circle junction and misplace the boundary for cones (nosecone free edges 3 mm apart at sewing).
479:In \`compute_uv_bounds_from_edges\`, mesh face centroid projections must only *select* between the two candidate V windows delimited by the edge projections — never extend the window. A cap triangle whose three vertices all lie on the plane-torus junction circle is legitimately absorbed by the torus hypothesis, but its centroid projects ~2° past the tangent circle; including it in the window shifted the face boundary off the junction and produced sewing free edges (filleted_cylinder). This was also nondeterministic since only 3 arbitrary faces were sampled.
514:A complete donut selects one toroidal surface with NO boundary edges; like full spheres, the face is built with \`MakeFace::new_handlegeomsurface_real\` (natural [0,2π]×[0,2π] bounds), which creates both the U seam (around the major circle) and the V seam (around the tube) automatically. full_torus (tests/occt/, generated by gen-test-models via BRepPrimAPI_MakeTorus) passes stage 4.1 with volume matching to ~7e-9 relative.
```

<!-- msg_011CcoJvnMMuScwnsvRiNKdZ -->

I now have a complete understanding of the pipeline, data structures, OCCT bindings, and the exact fragility the rework targets. Let me lay out my plan and get started.

## Plan

The rework replaces geometric sewing with **topological assembly from shared edges**. My understanding of the current state (from LEARNINGS + code):
- Partial-revolution wire faces **already** share edges (via pre-set pcurves + MakeFace).
- Sewing is load-bearing only for the **UV-bounds / natural-bounds paths** (full-revolution cylinders/cones, spheres, tori) which synthesize their *own* boundary edges, and for pcurve reconciliation.

**Approach — one uniform mechanism:**
1. For **every** (edge, adjacent-face) pair, compute the pcurve via `GeomProjLib::Curve2d(curve_3d, surface)` (analytic for cone/cyl/sphere/torus/plane; numerical for future NURBS) and attach **both** pcurves to the single shared `TopoDS_Edge`. Populate `ReconEdge.pcurves`.
2. Build each face's wires **in UV** from those pcurves, inserting **seam edges** (periodic wraps) and **degenerate edges** (sphere poles, cone apex) as first-class shared topology — one code path for all periodic surfaces.
3. Assemble faces + shell directly with `BRep_Builder`; the shell is closed **by construction**. Consistent orientation via `ShapeFix_Shell::FixFaceOrientation` (proven safe on cones; no pcurve rebuild), then the existing `SolidFromShell`/`orient_closed_solid`.

**De-risking:** gate the new path behind a hidden `--topo-assembly` flag (default off) so `cargo test` stays green throughout. I'll drive the model zoo through the new path with a script, expand case-by-case (planar → cylinders → poles → tori → cone_tangent_planes), then flip the default and delete the old ~2100-line path + sewing.

Let me start with the config flag and the new module skeleton.

// ===========================================================================
// Topological shared-edge assembler (DEVELOPMENT_PLAN §3.x)
//
// Builds the B-rep shell directly from shared TopoDS_Edge objects with pcurves
// attached on BOTH adjacent faces, inserting seam/degenerate edges uniformly.
// The shell is closed by construction — no BRepBuilderAPI_Sewing. Enabled by
// --topo-assembly while it is brought to parity with the legacy path.
// ===========================================================================

/// Per-ReconEdge topology for the shared-edge assembler.
struct EdgeTopo {
    /// The single shared OCCT edge, referenced (with orientation) by both faces.
    edge: OwnedPtr<topo_ds::Edge>,
    /// BRepVertex index at the edge's forward (curve first-parameter) end, or MAX.
    fwd_v0: usize,
    /// BRepVertex index at the edge's forward (curve last-parameter) end, or MAX.
    fwd_v1: usize,
    /// True when the edge is a full closed loop (a circle with no corner vertices).
    closed_loop: bool,
}

/// Build the single shared TopoDS_Edge for a ReconEdge, reusing the proven
/// MakeEdge vertex-ordering logic from the legacy assembler.
fn build_shared_edge(
    ei: usize,
    edge: &ReconEdge,
    output: &Stage3Output,
    topo_vertices: &[OwnedPtr<topo_ds::Vertex>],
    builder: &b_rep::Builder,
    config: &Config,
) -> Result<EdgeTopo, Stage3Error> {
    let has_verts = edge.vertex_indices[0] != usize::MAX && edge.vertex_indices[1] != usize::MAX;
    match edge.curve_3d.as_ref() {
        None => {
            // No intersection curve — straight line between endpoints (fallback).
            if has_verts {
                let mut me = b_rep_builder_api::MakeEdge::new_vertex2(
                    &topo_vertices[edge.vertex_indices[0]],
                    &topo_vertices[edge.vertex_indices[1]],
                );
                if !me.is_done() {
                    return Err(Stage3Error::AdjacencyError(format!(
                        "topo: MakeEdge (straight-line fallback) failed for edge {ei}: {:?}",
                        me.error()
                    )));
                }
                Ok(EdgeTopo {
                    edge: me.edge().to_owned(),
                    fwd_v0: edge.vertex_indices[0],
                    fwd_v1: edge.vertex_indices[1],
                    closed_loop: false,
                })
            } else {
                Err(Stage3Error::AdjacencyError(format!(
                    "topo: edge {ei} has no curve and no vertex endpoints"
                )))
            }
        }
        Some(curve) => {
            if has_verts {
                // Order vertices so vi0 is closest to the curve's first parameter,
                // matching MakeEdge's AdjustPeriodic forward-arc selection.
                let c = curve.get();
                let p_start = c.value(c.first_parameter());
                let v0_pt = &output.vertices[edge.vertex_indices[0]].point;
                let v1_pt = &output.vertices[edge.vertex_indices[1]].point;
                let d0 = (v0_pt[0] - p_start.x()).powi(2)
                    + (v0_pt[1] - p_start.y()).powi(2)
                    + (v0_pt[2] - p_start.z()).powi(2);
                let d1 = (v1_pt[0] - p_start.x()).powi(2)
                    + (v1_pt[1] - p_start.y()).powi(2)
                    + (v1_pt[2] - p_start.z()).powi(2);
                let (vi0, vi1) = if d0 <= d1 {
                    (edge.vertex_indices[0], edge.vertex_indices[1])
                } else {
                    (edge.vertex_indices[1], edge.vertex_indices[0])
                };
                let fp = c.first_parameter();
                let lp = c.last_parameter();
                // Widen vertex tolerances to accommodate imprecise intersection curves.
                let p_fp = c.value(fp);
                let p_lp = c.value(lp);
                let a = &output.vertices[vi0].point;
                let b = &output.vertices[vi1].point;
                let da = ((a[0] - p_fp.x()).powi(2) + (a[1] - p_fp.y()).powi(2) + (a[2] - p_fp.z()).powi(2)).sqrt();
                let db = ((b[0] - p_lp.x()).powi(2) + (b[1] - p_lp.y()).powi(2) + (b[2] - p_lp.z()).powi(2)).sqrt();
                let min_tol = config.vertex_tolerance_mm;
                builder.update_vertex_vertex_real(&topo_vertices[vi0], da.max(min_tol) * 1.01);
                builder.update_vertex_vertex_real(&topo_vertices[vi1], db.max(min_tol) * 1.01);
                let me = b_rep_builder_api::MakeEdge::new_handlegeomcurve_vertex2_real2(
                    curve, &topo_vertices[vi0], &topo_vertices[vi1], fp, lp,
                );
                if !me.is_done() {
                    return Err(Stage3Error::AdjacencyError(format!(
                        "topo: MakeEdge failed for edge {ei}: {:?}", me.error()
                    )));
                }
                Ok(EdgeTopo { edge: me.edge().to_owned(), fwd_v0: vi0, fwd_v1: vi1, closed_loop: false })
            } else {
                // Closed-loop edge (full circle). Periodic seam handling for the
                // adjacent periodic face is added when that face is built.
                let me = b_rep_builder_api::MakeEdge::new_handlegeomcurve(curve);
                if !me.is_done() {
                    return Err(Stage3Error::AdjacencyError(format!(
                        "topo: MakeEdge (closed loop) failed for edge {ei}: {:?}", me.error()
                    )));
                }
                Ok(EdgeTopo { edge: me.edge().to_owned(), fwd_v0: usize::MAX, fwd_v1: usize::MAX, closed_loop: true })
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Order and orient a group of edges (connected by shared vertices) into a
/// single oriented cycle: a list of (edge_id, orientation). Closed-loop groups
/// (one full-circle edge) return that edge forward.
fn order_wire_edges(
    group: &[usize],
    edge_topos: &[EdgeTopo],
) -> Vec<(usize, top_abs::Orientation)> {
    use top_abs::Orientation::{Forward, Reversed};
    if group.len() == 1 {
        return vec![(group[0], Forward)];
    }
    let mut result: Vec<(usize, top_abs::Orientation)> = Vec::with_capacity(group.len());
    let mut used = vec![false; group.len()];
    used[0] = true;
    let e0 = &edge_topos[group[0]];
    result.push((group[0], Forward));
    let start_v = e0.fwd_v0;
    let mut cur_v = e0.fwd_v1;
    while cur_v != start_v {
        let mut found = false;
        for (idx, &ei) in group.iter().enumerate() {
            if used[idx] {
                continue;
            }
            let e = &edge_topos[ei];
            if e.fwd_v0 == cur_v {
                result.push((ei, Forward));
                cur_v = e.fwd_v1;
                used[idx] = true;
                found = true;
                break;
            } else if e.fwd_v1 == cur_v {
                result.push((ei, Reversed));
                cur_v = e.fwd_v0;
                used[idx] = true;
                found = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        if !found {
            break;
        }
    }
    result
}

/// Build a planar TopoDS_Face directly from shared edges via BRep_Builder.
fn build_planar_face_topo(
    fi: usize,
    output: &Stage3Output,
    edge_topos: &[EdgeTopo],
    builder: &b_rep::Builder,
    config: &Config,
) -> Result<OwnedPtr<topo_ds::Face>, Stage3Error> {
    let fd = &output.face_descriptors[fi];
    let groups = group_edges_into_wires(fd, &output.edges);
    if groups.is_empty() {
        return Err(Stage3Error::AdjacencyError(format!("topo: planar face {fi} has no edges")));
    }

    let mut face = topo_ds::Face::new();
    builder.make_face_face_handlegeomsurface_real(&mut face, &fd.surface, config.vertex_tolerance_mm);

    // Outer wire = the group with the most edges (heuristic, matches legacy).
    let outer_gi = groups.iter().enumerate().max_by_key(|(_, g)| g.len()).map(|(i, _)| i).unwrap();

    for (gi, group) in groups.iter().enumerate() {
        let ordered = order_wire_edges(group, edge_topos);
        let mut wire = topo_ds::Wire::new();
        builder.make_wire(&mut wire);
        for &(ei, orient) in &ordered {
            let oe = edge_topos[ei].edge.as_shape().oriented(orient);
            builder.add(wire.as_shape_mut(), &oe);
        }
        // Inner wires (holes) are added reversed relative to the outer wire.
        let wire_shape = if gi == outer_gi {
            wire.as_shape().to_owned()
        } else {
            wire.as_shape().oriented(top_abs::Orientation::Reversed)
        };
        builder.add(face.as_shape_mut(), &wire_shape);
    }
    Ok(face)
}

/// Assemble the B-rep shell(s) topologically from shared edges (stage 3.4 + 3.5).
fn assemble_topological(
    mut output: Stage3Output,
    config: &Config,
    _viz: Option<&crate::viz::VizSender>,
) -> Result<Stage3Output, Stage3Error> {
    let t = Instant::now();
    let builder = b_rep::Builder::new();
    let num_faces = output.face_descriptors.len();

    // Pass A: shared vertices.
    let topo_vertices: Vec<OwnedPtr<topo_ds::Vertex>> = output
        .vertices
        .iter()
        .map(|v| {
            let pt = gp::Pnt::new_real3(v.point[0], v.point[1], v.point[2]);
            let mut mv = b_rep_builder_api::MakeVertex::new_pnt(&pt);
            let vtx = mv.vertex().to_owned();
            builder.update_vertex_vertex_real(&vtx, config.vertex_tolerance_mm);
            vtx
        })
        .collect();

    // Pass B: shared edges.
    let mut edge_topos: Vec<EdgeTopo> = Vec::with_capacity(output.edges.len());
    for (ei, edge) in output.edges.iter().enumerate() {
        edge_topos.push(build_shared_edge(ei, edge, &output, &topo_vertices, &builder, config)?);
    }

    // Pass C: build each face from shared edges.
    let mut faces: Vec<OwnedPtr<topo_ds::Face>> = Vec::with_capacity(num_faces);
    for fi in 0..num_faces {
        let surface_type = &output.stage2.selected_surfaces[output.face_descriptors[fi].selected_surface_idx];
        let face = match surface_type {
            SelectedSurface::Planar(_) => {
                build_planar_face_topo(fi, &output, &edge_topos, &builder, config)?
            }
            _ => {
                return Err(Stage3Error::AdjacencyError(format!(
                    "topo: face {fi} surface type not yet supported by topological assembler"
                )));
            }
        };
        faces.push(face);
    }

    // Pass D: build the shell, fix orientation, verify closure.
    let mut shell = topo_ds::Shell::new();
    builder.make_shell(&mut shell);
    for f in &faces {
        builder.add(shell.as_shape_mut(), f.as_shape());
    }

    // Consistent face orientation via shared-edge propagation (no pcurve rebuild,
    // safe on cones — unlike ShapeFix_Shell::Perform).
    let mut fixer = shape_fix::Shell::new_shell(&shell);
    fixer.fix_face_orientation(&shell, true, false);
    let shell = fixer.shell();

    // Verify the shell is closed by construction.
    let mut sa = shape_analysis::Shell::new();
    sa.check_oriented_shells(shell.as_shape(), true, false);
    let has_free = sa.has_free_edges();

    let mut face_count = 0;
    let mut fe = top_exp::Explorer::new_shape_shapeenum2(
        shell.as_shape(), top_abs::ShapeEnum::Face, top_abs::ShapeEnum::Shape,
    );
    while fe.more() { face_count += 1; fe.next(); }

    if !config.quiet {
        eprintln!(
            "Stage 3.4-3.5 topo ({:.3}s): assembled 1 shell, {face_count} faces, free_edges={has_free}",
            t.elapsed().as_secs_f64(),
        );
    }
    if has_free {
        return Err(Stage3Error::AdjacencyError(
            "topo: shell has free edges (not closed by construction)".into(),
        ));
    }

    if config.compare_shape.is_some() {
        compare_shells_to_step(std::slice::from_ref(&shell), config)?;
    }

    output.shells = vec![shell];
    Ok(output)
}

pub fn stage3(config: &Config, input: Stage2Output, viz: Option<&crate::viz::VizSender>) -> Result<Stage3Output, Stage3Error> {

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Run every STL/STEP pair through the topological assembler (--topo-assembly)
# and report pass/fail. Non-bad models only. Usage: ./scripts/run_topo_zoo.sh [filter]
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
BREPPER=./target/release/brepper
FILTER="${1:-}"
mkdir -p tmp/topo
pass=0; fail=0; failed=()
find_step() {
    local stl="$1"; local dir base stripped
    dir=$(dirname "$stl"); base=$(basename "$stl" .stl); base="${base%.ascii}"
    [ -f "$dir/$base.step" ] && { echo "$dir/$base.step"; return; }
    stripped=$(echo "$base" | sed -E 's/_(coarse|medium|fine|low|high)$//')
    [ -f "$dir/$stripped.step" ] && { echo "$dir/$stripped.step"; return; }
    echo ""
}
extra_flags() { case "$1" in *rounded_cube_10_r2_coarse*) echo "--angular-tolerance 20";; *) echo "";; esac; }
for stl in $(find tests -name '*.stl' | grep -v '/bad/' | sort); do
    [ -n "$FILTER" ] && [[ "$stl" != *"$FILTER"* ]] && continue
    step=$(find_step "$stl"); [ -z "$step" ] && continue
    name=$(basename "$stl" .stl)
    out="tmp/topo/${name}.step"
    flags=$(extra_flags "$stl")
    log=$($BREPPER "$stl" --compare "$step" -o "$out" --topo-assembly $flags 2>&1)
    rc=$?
    # Treat a stage-3.6 volume WARNING or any compare error as failure.
    if [ $rc -eq 0 ] && ! echo "$log" | grep -qiE "WARNING.*volume|volume.*WARNING|free edges|free_edges=true"; then
        pass=$((pass+1)); # echo "  PASS $name"
    else
        fail=$((fail+1)); failed+=("$name")
        reason=$(echo "$log" | grep -iE "error|WARNING|free_edges=true|not yet supported|panic" | head -1 | cut -c1-90)
        printf "  FAIL %-45s %s\n" "$name" "$reason"
    fi
done
echo "-----"
echo "topo-assembly: $pass passed, $fail failed"
