1	## opencascade-sys API Patterns
2	
3	The Rust bindings mirror OCCT C++ closely but with automatic name transformations:
4	
5	### Module and Type Naming
6	- \`BRepBuilderAPI_MakeEdge\` → \`b_rep_builder_api::MakeEdge\`
7	- \`BRep_Tool\` → \`b_rep::Tool\`
8	- \`gp_Pnt\` → \`gp::Pnt\`
9	- \`TopExp_Explorer\` → \`top_exp::Explorer\`
10	- \`GeomAPI_ProjectPointOnSurf\` → \`geom_api::ProjectPointOnSurf\`
11	- \`STEPControl_Reader\` → \`step_control::Reader\`
12	- \`RWStl\` → \`rw_stl\` (free functions)
13	
14	### Constructors
15	Named \`::new_<compressed_param_types>()\`. For example:
16	\`\`\`rust
17	gp::Pnt::new_real3(x, y, z)           // gp_Pnt(double, double, double)
18	gp::Dir::new_real3(dx, dy, dz)
19	top_exp::Explorer::new_shape_shapeenum2(shape, from_type, avoid_type)
20	geom_api::ProjectPointOnSurf::new_pnt_handlegeomsurface_extalgo(pt, surf, algo)
21	\`\`\`
22	
23	### Ownership
24	- All objects are returned as \`OwnedPtr<T>\` which auto-derefs via \`Deref\`/\`DerefMut\`
25	- \`OwnedPtr<T>\` is essentially \`Box<T>\` for OCCT heap objects
26	
27	### Handles (OCCT \`Handle<T>\`)
28	- \`Type::to_handle(owned_ptr)\` consumes \`OwnedPtr<T>\` → \`OwnedPtr<HandleT>\`
29	- \`.get()\` dereferences a handle to access the underlying object
30	- Upcasting: \`.to_handle_surface()\`, \`.to_handle_curve()\`, etc.
31	- Downcasting: \`.downcast_to_plane()\` returns \`Option<OwnedPtr<HandleDerived>>\`
32	
33	### Enums
34	Typed Rust enums, not raw integers:
35	\`\`\`rust
36	top_abs::ShapeEnum::Face
37	extrema::ExtAlgo::Grad
38	\`\`\`
39	
40	### Shape Downcasting
41	\`topo_ds::face_shape\` is a safe function, but it panics if the shape is not a Face. Always guard with \`shape_type()\`:
42	\`\`\`rust
43	if shape_ref.shape_type() == top_abs::ShapeEnum::Face {
44	    let face = topo_ds::face_shape(shape_ref);  // &topo_ds::Shape → &topo_ds::Face
45	    ...
46	}
47	\`\`\`
48	
49	### Static Methods → Free Functions
50	OCCT utility classes (e.g., \`BRep_Tool\`) become module-level free functions or associated functions on the type.
51	
52	### OCCT Thread Safety
53	OCCT has process-global mutable state that is **not thread-safe**. Only STEP Reader/Writer operations are affected:
54	- \`STEPControl_Reader::new()\` / \`STEPControl_Writer::new()\` call \`STEPControl_Controller::Init()\` → \`XSAlgo::Init()\`, which writes to \`static Handle(XSAlgo_AlgoContainer) theContainer\` and calls many \`Interface_Static::Init()\` / \`SetIVal()\` on global settings. The init guard (\`static Standard_Boolean init\`) is a plain bool, not atomic.
55	- \`interface::Static::set_c_val()\` mutates global config.
56	- \`StepFile_Read.cxx\` has \`THE_GLOBAL_READ_MUTEX\` but it only covers data **processing** after lex/yacc parsing — the parsing calls \`Message::SendTrace()\` / \`Message::SendFail()\` which access the global \`Message_Messenger\` singleton without synchronization.
57	
58	The following APIs are **thread-safe** (verified in OCCT C++ source — no global mutable state):
59	- STL reading (\`RWStl\` — only \`const\` statics)
60	- \`Message_ProgressRange\` (no global state)
61	- \`BRepExtrema_DistShapeShape\` (no globals)
62	- \`GeomAPI_IntSS\`, \`ProjectPointOnCurve\`, \`ProjectPointOnSurf\` (no globals)
63	- All \`BRepBuilderAPI\` (MakeEdge, MakeFace, MakeVertex, Sewing) — only static helper functions
64	- \`ShapeFix_Shell\`, \`ShapeFix_Face\`, \`ShapeFix_Solid\` (no globals)
65	- \`BRepCheck\`, \`BRepGProp\`, \`BRepLib\` (no globals)
66	- All \`gp::*\`, \`geom::*\`, \`topo_ds::*\`, \`top_exp::*\` — value types / local objects
67	
68	Solution: \`step_control::StepReader\` and \`step_control::StepWriter\` wrappers in \`opencascade-sys\` hold a global \`STEP_MUTEX\` for their entire lifetime, serializing STEP I/O automatically. brepper's \`read_step_file()\` / \`write_step_file()\` use these wrappers. Tests run fully in parallel for all other OCCT operations.
69	
70	## Common API Recipes
71	
72	### Read an STL file → vertex positions
73	\`\`\`rust
74	use opencascade_sys::{rw_stl, message};
75	let progress = message::ProgressRange::new();
76	let tri_handle = rw_stl::read_file_charptr_progressrange_2(path, &progress);
77	let tri = tri_handle.get();  // &Poly_Triangulation
78	for i in 1..=tri.nb_nodes() {
79	    let pt = tri.node(i);  // OwnedPtr<gp::Pnt>
80	    let (x, y, z) = (pt.x(), pt.y(), pt.z());
81	}
82	\`\`\`
83	
84	### Read a STEP file → TopoDS_Shape
85	\`\`\`rust
86	// Thread-safe wrapper (serializes via StepReader's built-in mutex):
87	let shape = brepper::read_step_file(path).unwrap();
88	\`\`\`
89	
90	### Iterate faces of a shape
91	\`\`\`rust
92	use opencascade_sys::{top_exp, top_abs, topo_ds};
93	let mut explorer = top_exp::Explorer::new_shape_shapeenum2(
94	    &shape, top_abs::ShapeEnum::Face, top_abs::ShapeEnum::Shape,
95	);
96	while explorer.more() {
97	    let face = topo_ds::face_shape(explorer.value());
98	    // ... use face
99	    explorer.next();
100	}
101	\`\`\`
102	
103	### Project a point onto a surface (compute distance)
104	\`\`\`rust
105	use opencascade_sys::{b_rep, geom_api, extrema};
106	let surface = b_rep::Tool::surface_face(face);  // OwnedPtr<HandleGeomSurface>
107	let projector = geom_api::ProjectPointOnSurf::new_pnt_handlegeomsurface_extalgo(
108	    &point, &surface, extrema::ExtAlgo::Grad,
109	);
110	if projector.is_done() && projector.nb_points() > 0 {
111	    let dist = projector.lower_distance();
112	}
113	\`\`\`
114	
115	### Poly_Triangulation index convention
116	All node/triangle indices are **1-based** (OCCT convention).
117	
118	
119	### Bounded vs unbounded distance: BRepExtrema vs GeomAPI_ProjectPointOnSurf
120	\`GeomAPI_ProjectPointOnSurf\` projects onto the *infinite* underlying \`Geom_Surface\`, not the bounded face. Use \`BRepExtrema_DistShapeShape\` (via \`b_rep_extrema::DistShapeShape\`) instead to compute distance to bounded \`TopoDS_Face\` shapes. Create a \`BRepBuilderAPI_MakeVertex\` from the point, then compute \`DistShapeShape\` between the vertex shape and the target shape. This correctly reports nonzero distance for points that lie on an infinite surface extension but outside the bounded face.
121	
122	### Stage 2.1 planar hypothesis algorithm
123	- BFS region growing from seed faces using angular + vertex-distance tolerance.
124	- Angular threshold of \`1e-6\` (1 - cos ≈ 0.08°) prevents grouping faces with slightly different normals.
125	- Re-fitting via area-weighted normal averaging + vertex centroid for plane distance.
126	- For CAD meshes, vertices lie precisely on surfaces, so fit errors are typically 0 or near-epsilon.
127	- Coplanar but disconnected faces correctly get separate hypotheses (not a bug).
128	- The \`vertex_tolerance_mm\` config parameter controls the maximum vertex-to-plane distance for grouping.
129	
130	### CodeCAD (ccad) test model generation
131	- \`ccad build\` in \`tests/ccad/\` generates both STL and STEP files from Lua scripts.
132	- \`wedge(dx, dy, dz, ltx)\` requires \`ltx > 0\` (cannot be 0).
133	- Boolean operations like \`union()\` work with pre-translated shapes.
134	- Parts are registered in \`project.json\`; each entry needs a unique \`id\`.
135	- Available primitives: \`box()\`, \`cylinder(diameter, height)\`, \`sphere(diameter)\`, \`cone(d1, d2, height)\`, \`wedge()\`, \`hex_prism()\`.
136	- Boolean operations: \`union()\`, \`difference()\`, \`intersection()\`.
137	- Transformations: \`translate()\`, \`rotate_x/y/z()\`, \`scale()\`, \`center_xyz()\` etc.
138	- Construction: \`extrude(face, height)\`, \`revolve(profile, angle)\`.
139	- Edge ops: \`fillet_all(s, r)\`, \`chamfer_all(s, d)\`. Selective: \`edges(s):on_box_side("zmax"):collect()\` → \`fillet(s, edge_set, r)\`.
140	- ccad \`profile_xz\` only supports polylines (no arcs), so \`revolve()\` creates conical strip approximations, NOT true TOROIDAL_SURFACE. To create true toroidal surfaces in STEP via ccad, use fillet operations on circular edges (cylinder-plane junctions).
141	- Filleting straight edges on a box creates only CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE, not toroidal. A fully-filleted box (rounded_cube) has only cylindrical + spherical surfaces (no tori). Toroidal surfaces appear from fillets on curved (circular) edges.
142	- For pipe models: ensure fillet radius doesn't exceed half the annulus width (outer_r - inner_r), otherwise the mesh may have open edges from overlapping fillets.
143	- Cone-sphere tangency construction: for a cone with half-angle α (from axis). At a tangent circle of radius r on the cone, the tangent sphere has radius R = r / cos(α), and its center sits on the cone axis at distance r·tan(α) beyond the tangent circle in the apex direction. Using \`union(cone, sphere)\` in ccad produces an exact tangent junction in the STEP output.
144	- STEP files from ccad contain an embedded timestamp in the FILE_NAME header. \`generate_models.sh\` normalizes this to \`'2000-01-01T00:00:00'\` via sed to prevent gratuitous diffs on regeneration.
145	
146	### CAD tessellation quad-strip patterns
147	- Tessellated cylinders and spheres from CAD tools (CodeCAD/OCCT, Onshape) use quad-strip patterns where each quad facet splits into 2 coplanar triangles.
148	- Solution: stage 1.3 merges coplanar triangle pairs back into quads, so curved-surface facets become single faces with single-face planar hypotheses.
149	- This restores the clean "single-face = curved surface candidate" criterion for stages 2.2 and 2.3.
150	- Sphere poles are an exception: triangles in the polar fan pattern don't have coplanar neighbors and correctly remain as triangles.
151	
152	### Stage 2.2 cylindrical hypothesis algorithm
153	- Three-step fitting: (1) axis direction from smallest eigenvector of area-weighted normal covariance matrix M = Σ wᵢ nᵢ nᵢᵀ, (2) axis position and radius via 2D algebraic circle fit after projecting vertices perpendicular to axis, (3) Levenberg-Marquardt refinement of all 6 parameters [alpha, beta (tilt from initial axis), qx, qy, qz (axis point), radius]. LM uses \`levenberg-marquardt\` crate with \`nalgebra\` types. Residual per vertex: \`||cross(p - q, a)|| - r\`. Numerical Jacobian via central differences (eps=1e-8). This replaces a previous grid-search approach and an unsuccessful Newton-on-SSE attempt.
154	- **LM vs Newton on SSE**: Newton refinement of scalar SSE failed because the loss landscape is non-convex and can trap the optimizer. LM operates on the residual _vector_ with trust-region damping, which is fundamentally more robust. A 0.41° initial axis error from normal-covariance (on narrow-arc cylinders) converges to ~1e-5° error after LM.
155	- **Vertex-PCA axis candidate pitfall**: Using the largest eigenvector of vertex position covariance as an alternative axis candidate is dangerous. When vertices span a narrow arc, a degenerate small-radius cylinder can thread through the near-collinear projected points with extremely low SSE (e.g., r=0.5 with SSE=5e-15 vs correct r=5 with SSE=3e-12). The degenerate fit wins on SSE but is geometrically wrong. Solution: use only normal-covariance axis; LM converges from it reliably.
156	- **Critical: center the 2D projected coordinates before circle fitting.** Without centering, the normal equations matrix becomes catastrophically ill-conditioned when absolute vertex coordinates are large relative to the arc span (e.g., vertices at (15, 12.5) spanning 2.5° of a r=2mm cylinder). The sums-of-squares terms (sx2 ≈ 1350) dwarf the signal (radius ≈ 2), causing Cramer's rule to produce wildly wrong radii (e.g., 139mm instead of 2mm). Fix: subtract mean_x/mean_y before fitting, add back when converting 2D center to 3D. This is the standard numerical remedy for polynomial least-squares fitting.
157	- 3×3 symmetric eigenvalue computation uses depressed cubic (trigonometric solution with cos(θ/3)), plus null-space eigenvector via cross products of (M - λI) rows.
158	- Multi-seed evaluation with 3-face seeds: for each starting face fi, finds triples (fi, n1, n2) where n1 is a pairwise-qualified neighbor of fi, and n2 is a pairwise-qualified neighbor of n1 that is NOT a neighbor of fi. Runs a trial BFS for each triple using temporary data (no mesh mutation during trials), keeps the best trial (most total area).
159	- BFS seeds from triples of faces spanning more circumference. Pairwise qualification requires non-parallel normals (cross product > MIN_CROSS_THRESHOLD=0.01) and dihedral angle ≤ angular tolerance. No restrictions on multi-face planar faces.
160	- Angular coverage validation applied to each trial after BFS: requires 3+ angular clusters of face centroids around the cylinder circumference. Rejects bogus hypotheses where faces are clustered on one side. Early termination is disabled as future work.
161	- Centroid validation after BFS: each face centroid must be within surface_tolerance of the fitted cylinder. This rejects spurious fits from perpendicular planar faces that algebraically fit a cylinder.
162	- Minimum 3-face requirement: cylinder hypotheses must contain at least 3 faces. Any real cylindrical surface from a CAD tessellation will have at least 3 facets around its circumference. This eliminates spurious 2-face cylinder fits from locally adjacent faces on tori, cones, and spheres (e.g., cone went from 29 to 0 spurious fits, pipe_elbow from 252 to 51).
163	- Angular tolerance check: both seed pairs and BFS expansion candidates must have dihedral angle ≤ \`--angular-tolerance\` (default 25°). This prevents fitting cylinders to faces that meet at sharp angles (e.g., cube faces at 90°). CAD tessellators enforce a maximum angular tolerance between adjacent triangles on the same surface. (See the medium-resolution learnings at the end of this file for why the default is 25° rather than 17.5°.)
164	- Extracting cylinder parameters from STEP: \`b_rep_adaptor::Surface::cylinder()\` → \`gp::Cylinder\`, then \`.radius()\`, \`.axis().direction()\`, \`.axis().location()\`. Useful for test verification.
165	
166	### ccad box() coordinate system
167	- \`box(w, h, d)\` places the box in the positive octant: (0,0,0) to (w,h,d). It does NOT center at origin.
168	- To center a box, use \`translate(box(w,h,d), -w/2, -h/2, -d/2)\`.
169	- \`cylinder(diameter, height)\` is vertical (Z-axis), centered at the XY origin, extends from z=0 to z=height (NOT centered vertically). To make through-holes, translate cylinders vertically so they extend past both sides of the target body.
170	- \`sphere(diameter)\` is centered at the origin. To make hemispherical pockets or domes, use \`intersection()\` or \`difference()\` with a box.
171	
172	### Stage 2.3 spherical hypothesis algorithm
173	- Algebraic least-squares sphere fitting: expand |v-c|²=r² linearly into 4 unknowns (cx, cy, cz, k=r²-|c|²). Normal equations AᵀAx = Aᵀb solved via 4×4 Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting.
174	- Vertex-neighborhood seeding: for each mesh vertex, collect surrounding non-excluded faces (≥3), fit sphere from all their vertices. Naturally provides angular diversity for the 4-DOF sphere fit. Superior to pair-based seeding which failed on finely tessellated spheres.
175	- Multi-face planar faces excluded from seeding but absorb-able by BFS, same as cylindrical.
176	- Solid-angle coverage validation: area-weighted 3×3 covariance matrix of centroid-to-center unit direction vectors. Eigenvalues via depressed cubic (same as cylinder axis). Require λ_min/λ_max ≥ MIN_SPHERE_EIGENVALUE_RATIO (0.01). Rejects strip-like hypotheses from cylinder fillet growth.
177	- MAX_SPHERE_RADIUS_FACTOR = 1000.0 (was 10.0). With solid-angle coverage + surface-tolerance in BFS, radius limit only needs to prevent numerical precision issues.
178	- Centroid validation during BFS (not just post-BFS): each face centroid checked against surface_tolerance with 2x hard skip threshold.
179	- Minimum 4-face requirement: a sphere needs at least 4 non-coplanar points for a unique fit.
180	- All faces are candidates for BFS expansion (including those with cylindrical hypotheses and multi-face planar hypotheses). Only seeding excludes multi-face planar. Stage 2.6 resolves overlapping hypotheses.
181	- Torus faces locally fit spheres (e.g., pipe_elbow produces 36 sphere hypotheses). This is expected — stage 2.6 with torus hypothesis support will resolve it.
182	- Concave spheres (bowls/pockets) have normals pointing toward center — same convexity logic as cylinders.
183	- Angular tolerance check: same as cylindrical — seed faces and BFS neighbors must have dihedral angle ≤ \`--angular-tolerance\`. This fixed the spurious sphere detection on the 1mm manual cube.
184	
185	### Stage 2.6 surface selection
186	- Greedy area-based selection: iteratively selects the hypothesis with the largest total remaining mesh face area, assigns its unassigned faces, removes those faces from all other candidates, repeats.
187	- Multi-face planar, cylindrical, and spherical hypotheses are candidates. Single-face planar hypotheses are fallback for unclaimed faces.
188	- After selection, hypothesis face/vertex lists are updated in-place to reflect only the faces actually assigned.
189	- Replaced the old per-face priority rule (spherical > cylindrical > multi-face planar > single-face planar) which failed when bogus small-area hypotheses of a high-priority type beat correct large-area hypotheses of a lower-priority type.
190	- Sphere BFS along cylinder fillets is prevented by solid-angle coverage validation in stage 2.3. Vertex-based seeding also helps by providing better initial seeds.
191	- Compare tolerance uses \`surface_tolerance\` for all hypothesis types (stages 2.1-2.3 and 2.6 all use the same tolerance). Previously used \`vertex_tolerance\` which was too tight for centroid-to-surface distance checks.
192	
193	
194	### Stage 3.1 adjacency graph construction
195	- OCCT surface creation: \`geom::Plane::new_pnt_dir\`, \`geom::CylindricalSurface::new_ax3_real\`, \`geom::SphericalSurface::new_ax3_real\`. Type erasure via \`.to_handle().to_handle_surface()\` to get \`OwnedPtr<HandleGeomSurface>\`.
196	- Adjacency is determined from mesh edges: an edge between mesh faces assigned to different selected surfaces is a boundary edge.
197	- Boundary edges are grouped by \`SurfacePair\` (canonical ordering), then chained into ordered vertex sequences. Each chain becomes a \`ReconEdge\`.
198	- Corner vertices (where 3+ surfaces meet) become \`BRepVertex\` entries.
199	- Topological ordering of edges around each face uses rotation-order walk: at each vertex, pick the edge to the face that comes next in counter-clockwise order. For faces without vertices (closed loops like cylinder caps), all edges incident on that face are included.
200	- Bug encountered: closing vertex in topological walk was missing — after walking N edges around a face, the vertex connecting the last edge back to the first edge must be added separately.
201	- \`wedge(10, 10, 10, 5)\` in CodeCAD is a truncated wedge (8 vertices, 6 faces), NOT a triangular prism (6 vertices, 5 faces). The 4th parameter \`ltx\` is the top face X dimension.
202	- Euler formula V-E+F=2 is a good sanity check for genus-0 (no holes through the model) manifold solids. Models with through-holes have different Euler characteristics.
203	- Stage 3.1 --compare check: validates that (a) ReconEdge boundary mesh vertices lie within vertex_tolerance of STEP edges, and (b) BRepVertex positions lie within vertex_tolerance of STEP vertices. Uses \`topo_ds::Compound\` to build compounds of all STEP edges and vertices separately, then \`BRepExtrema_DistShapeShape\` against those compounds.
204	- Building a \`topo_ds::Compound\`: use \`topo_ds::Builder::new()\`, \`builder.make_compound(&mut compound)\`, then \`builder.add(compound.as_shape_mut(), shape)\`. Also available via \`b_rep::Builder\` which inherits from \`topo_ds::Builder\`.
205	- Shape downcasting: \`topo_ds::edge(shape)\`, \`topo_ds::vertex(shape)\`, \`topo_ds::face_shape(shape)\` etc. These panic on type mismatch — check \`shape.shape_type()\` first.
206	
207	### Stage 3.2 tangency detection
208	- Surface normals at boundary points can be computed analytically for planar/cylindrical/spherical surfaces without needing OCCT UV evaluation. Plane: constant normal. Cylinder: radial direction from axis (negate for concave). Sphere: direction from center (negate for concave).
209	- Tangency threshold of 2° (cos ≈ 0.9994) works well. Tangent edges arise from fillets (e.g., cylinder tangent to plane at a fillet edge). part_rounded_cube_10_r2 has 8 tangent edges (4 cylinders × 2 touching planes each).
210	
211	### Stage 3.3 edge curve computation
212	- \`GeomAPI_IntSS::new_handlegeomsurface2_real(S1, S2, Tol)\` computes surface-surface intersection curves. Returns 1-indexed curves via \`.nb_lines()\` and \`.line(i)\` which returns \`&HandleGeomCurve\`.
213	- When IntSS returns multiple curves, select the one closest to mesh boundary vertices by projecting sampled boundary points onto each curve via \`GeomAPI_ProjectPointOnCurve\` and picking minimum total distance.
214	- \`GeomAPI_ProjectPointOnCurve::new_pnt_handlegeomcurve(&pt, curve)\` projects a point onto a curve. \`.lower_distance_parameter()\` returns the parameter of the closest point.
215	- \`Geom_TrimmedCurve::new_handlegeomcurve_real2(curve, U1, U2)\` trims a curve to a parameter range. Convert to handle via \`Geom_TrimmedCurve::to_handle(owned).to_handle_curve()\`.
216	- For closed-loop edges (no vertex endpoints, e.g., full circle on a cylinder cap), use the curve's full parameter range \`[first_parameter, last_parameter]\`.
217	- \`ReconEdge.curve_3d\` stores \`Option<OwnedPtr<geom::HandleGeomCurve>>\`. \`OwnedPtr\` does not implement \`Debug\`, so \`ReconEdge\` needs a manual \`Debug\` impl.
218	- All current non-tangent edges compute 100% of edge curves successfully via IntSS (cube 12/12, cylinder 2/2, hemisphere 1/1, ball_on_cylinder 2/2, block_with_hole 15/15, pipe 4/4, spherical_pocket 13/13, chamfered_cube 48/48, part_rounded_cube 16/16).
219	- **Tangent edge curves**: \`GeomAPI_IntSS\` fails for tangent surfaces (returns no curves). Instead, construct tangent edge curves analytically. For plane-cylinder tangencies: compute the radial direction from the component of the plane normal perpendicular to the cylinder axis, find the tangent point at \`axis_origin + r * radial_unit\`, construct a \`Geom_Line\` through that point along the cylinder axis direction, and trim to the vertex endpoint parameters. Validate that boundary vertices lie within tolerance of the constructed curve.
220	- **Sphere-cylinder tangent edge curves**: The tangent curve between a sphere and a cylinder (at fillet corners) is a great circle arc on the sphere. Construct a \`Geom_Circle\` using the sphere's center and radius (NOT the cylinder's, which may be imprecisely fitted). The circle plane normal is \`normalize(cross(v0 - center, v1 - center))\` where v0, v1 are the endpoint vertex positions. This ensures the circle passes through both vertices to the sphere fit accuracy (~1e-6mm), independent of cylinder parameter quality. Use \`gp::Ax2::new_pnt_dir(&center_pnt, &normal_dir)\` → \`geom::Circle::new_ax2_real(&ax2, radius)\` → \`.to_handle().to_handle_curve()\`. For arc selection on the periodic circle, sample mesh boundary vertices to determine forward vs. reverse arc.
221	- **Closed-loop sphere-cylinder tangent edge curves** (no vertex endpoints, e.g. pill/capsule shapes): Construct a full \`Geom_Circle\` with the circle plane normal set to the cylinder axis direction and center at the sphere center. Use the full parameter range [0, 2π] as a \`TrimmedCurve\`.
222	- **Adaptive vertex tolerance for MakeEdge**: When surface fits are imprecise (e.g., cylinders fitted from limited mesh data), IntSS intersection curves may not pass exactly through mesh vertex positions. Before creating MakeEdge, compute the distance from each vertex to the curve at its assigned parameter, and update the OCCT vertex tolerance to at least that distance (with 1% margin). This replaces the fixed \`vertex_tolerance_mm\` (1e-5mm) with position-adaptive tolerances that accommodate surface fit imprecision.
223	
224	### Stage 3.4 face creation
225	- **Planar faces**: Create \`TopoDS_Edge\` from trimmed curve using \`BRepBuilderAPI_MakeEdge::new_handlegeomcurve(curve)\`. Group edges into wire loops by \`BRepVertex\` vertex connectivity (union-find style). Build \`MakeWire\` from edges, \`MakeFace\` from surface + outer wire + hole wires.
226	- **Periodic faces (cylinder/sphere) with edges**: Two approaches depending on the edge type:
227	  - **Full revolution** (all boundary edges are closed loops): Use UV-bounds construction via \`MakeFace::new_handlegeomsurface_real5(surface, umin, umax, vmin, vmax, tol)\`. This automatically creates seam edges needed for proper B-Rep topology. Circular gap algorithm computes correct u-bounds even when edges cross the 0/2π seam.
228	  - **Partial revolution** (open edges with vertices): Use wire-based construction WITH pre-set pcurves via \`BRep_Builder::update_edge\` before calling \`MakeFace\`. The pcurves (Geom2d_Line) map the edge's 3D parameter range to the surface's UV space. This ensures correct arc selection on the periodic surface and shares edges with adjacent planar faces for proper sewing.
229	- **Full spheres** (no edges): Use \`MakeFace::new_handlegeomsurface_real(surface, tolerance)\` which uses natural surface bounds.
230	- \`MakeEdge::edge()\` takes \`&mut self\`, not \`&self\`. Need \`&mut\` references when accessing edges.
231	- \`BRepCheck_Analyzer::new_shape_bool(shape, true)\` validates faces. \`.is_valid()\` returns bool.
232	- The base \`geom::Surface\` type does NOT have \`bounds()\` or \`first_u_parameter()\` etc. in the Rust bindings. These are available on specific subtypes (CylindricalSurface, SphericalSurface, Plane, etc.). For UV bounds, compute them from geometry (mesh vertices, hypothesis parameters) rather than trying to query the surface.
233	- **Shared vertices**: Create \`TopoDS_Vertex\` objects from \`BRepVertex\` positions (\`MakeVertex::new_pnt(pt)\` then \`.vertex().to_owned()\`), then set vertex tolerance to \`vertex_tolerance_mm\` via \`BRep_Builder::update_vertex_vertex_real()\` (OCCT default tolerance ~1e-7 is too tight for mesh vertices). Use \`MakeEdge::new_handlegeomcurve_vertex2_real2(curve, &v1, &v2, fp, lp)\` with explicit parameter values to avoid OCCT's vertex-to-curve projection (which fails with \`Pointprojectionfailed\` when vertex is slightly off the curve). Parameters are always \`(first_parameter, last_parameter)\` since V1 is always ordered to be the vertex closest to the curve's start point.
234	- **Pcurves on periodic faces**: For partial-revolution periodic faces, pcurves must be pre-set on IntSS edges using \`BRep_Builder::update_edge_edge_handlegeom2dcurve_handlegeomsurface_location_real()\` BEFORE creating the MakeFace. Without pre-set pcurves, MakeFace may compute incorrect pcurves that select the wrong arc of the periodic surface.
235	- **CRITICAL: MakeEdge vertex order for periodic curves**: \`BRepBuilderAPI_MakeEdge\` strips \`TrimmedCurve\` wrappers and uses the base curve. For periodic curves (circles), \`ElCLib::AdjustPeriodic\` forces p1 < p2, always selecting the forward (CCW) arc from V1 to V2. If V1/V2 are in the wrong order relative to the curve parameterization, MakeEdge creates an edge spanning the complementary arc (e.g., 270° instead of 90°). Fix: when creating MakeEdge, ensure V1 is closest to the curve's \`first_parameter()\` point and V2 to the \`last_parameter()\` point.
236	- **BRepCheck_Face diagnostics**: \`b_rep_check::Face::new_face(face)\` creates a face checker. Call \`.minimum()\` first to compute all checks, then query \`.intersect_wires(false)\`, \`.classify_wires(false)\`, \`.orientation_of_wires(false)\` (each returns \`b_rep_check::Status\`), and \`.is_unorientable()\` (bool).
237	- **Wire orientation fix for holes**: After adding inner wires (holes) to a \`MakeFace\`, apply \`shape_fix::Face::new_face(make_face.face())\` then \`.fix_orientation()\` to ensure inner wires are oriented opposite to the outer wire. Wrap the result back via \`MakeFace::new_face(&fixer.face())\`. Without this, OCCT's BRepCheck reports \`Badorientationofsubshape\` on every planar face with holes.
238	- **Torus doubly-periodic V-bounds**: The torus surface is periodic in both U (major revolution) and V (minor/tube revolution), with V ∈ [0, 2π]. When computing face UV bounds, simple min/max of projected V values fails for faces crossing the V=0/2π boundary (e.g., a quarter-tube fillet from V=3π/2 to V=2π gets expanded to V=[0, 3π/2], covering 3/4 of the tube). Fix: use the circular gap algorithm (same as for U-bounds on partial revolution faces) to correctly identify the smallest arc containing all projected V values. Also sample 3 points per edge curve (not just midpoint) and add mesh face centroid projections for disambiguation.
239	- **Plane-cone and cylinder-cone junctions are never tangent**: At a plane-cone junction (plane ⊥ axis at base), the normals differ by the cone half-angle. At a cylinder-cone junction (coaxial), the cone normal has an axial tilt of sin(half_angle) that the cylinder normal lacks. For any real cone (half-angle > 2°), these exceed the tangency threshold. No test model has cone tangent edges; all cone models pass via the non-tangent IntSS path.
240	
241	
242	### Stage 3.3 edge curve computation: tricky cases
243	- **IntSS degenerate curves for plane-through-cylinder-axis**: When a plane passes through a cylinder's axis, \`GeomAPI_IntSS\` returns 4 degenerate curves with extreme parameter ranges (~-846M to -846M+47k), none containing the model's actual z-range. \`ProjectPointOnCurve\` fails on 3 of 4 curves. Fallback: validate IntSS curve by projecting boundary vertices — if distance exceeds 1mm, construct a \`Geom_Line\` from the two vertex positions instead.
244	- **\`is_periodic()\` returns false for IntSS circles**: Circle curves from cylinder×plane⊥axis intersections have \`is_periodic()=false\` despite being full circles with \`first_param=0, last_param=2π\`. Detect by checking \`(last_param - first_param - 2π).abs() < 1e-6\` instead.
245	- **Closed curve arc selection**: When a curve has param span ≈ 2π (full circle), the default parameter range may select the wrong arc (e.g., 270° instead of 90°). Fix: sample mesh boundary vertices, count which ones lie on the direct vs. complementary arc, and pick the arc with more support.
246	- **Centroid-based curve selection**: When IntSS returns multiple curves, selecting the one closest to a centroid computed from boundary vertices is more robust than sequential \`ProjectPointOnCurve\` calls, which can fail on degenerate curves.
247	- **IntSS partial arcs for sphere-plane through poles**: When a sphere-plane intersection circle passes through the sphere's UV poles (i.e., the plane contains the sphere axis), \`GeomAPI_IntSS\` returns TWO semicircular arcs instead of one full circle. This happens because in UV space, the circle maps to two disconnected meridional lines (U=0 and U=π), which IntSS treats as separate intersection curves. Fix: for closed-loop edges, detect when the curve span < 2π and reconstruct the full circle from 3 sampled points using the circumscribed circle formula (circumcenter from 3 non-collinear points).
248	
249	### Stage 3.5 shell construction
250	- \`BRepBuilderAPI_Sewing\`: Create with \`Sewing::new_real(tolerance)\` where tolerance = \`vertex_tolerance_mm\`. Add all faces via \`.add(face.as_shape())\`, then \`.perform(&ProgressRange::new())\`.
251	- The sewed shape can contain mixed types: \`Shell\` (most common), \`Face\` (single-face models like \`simple_sphere\`), \`Solid\`, \`Compound\`, \`Compsolid\`. Iterate sub-shapes by type to extract all shells.
252	- For \`Face\` results, wrap in a \`TopoDS_Shell\` manually: \`topo_ds::Builder::new()\`, \`.make_shell(&mut shell)\`, \`.add(shell.as_shape_mut(), face.as_shape())\`.
253	- \`ShapeAnalysis_Shell::check_oriented_shells(shape, false, false)\` returns \`true\` when BAD edges are found (orientation problems), not when the shell is valid. The return value is inverted from what you might expect.
254	- \`ShapeFix_Shell::new_shell(shell)\`, then \`.fix_face_orientation(shell, false, false)\`, \`.perform(&ProgressRange::new())\`, \`.shell()\` returns the fixed shell.
255	- \`top_abs::ShapeEnum::Compsolid\` (not \`CompSolid\`) — watch the capitalization.
256	- \`topo_ds::shell_shape(shape)\` downcasts \`&Shape\` to \`&Shell\` reference; Shell implements \`CppCopyable\`/\`ToOwned\` so you can \`.to_owned()\` to get \`OwnedPtr<Shell>\`.
257	- Sewing statistics: \`.nb_free_edges()\`, \`.nb_multiple_edges()\`, \`.nb_contigous_edges()\` — note the OCCT typo "contigous" (not "contiguous").
258	
259	### Stage 3.6 solid construction
260	- \`shape_fix::Solid::new()\`, then \`.solid_from_shell(shell)\` creates an \`OwnedPtr<topo_ds::Solid>\` with automatic orientation handling.
261	- \`topo_ds::solid(shape)\` downcasts \`&Shape\` to \`&Solid\`; \`Solid\` is \`CppCopyable\`/\`ToOwned\`.
262	- \`b_rep_g_prop::volume_properties_shape_gprops_bool3(shape, &mut gprops, only_closed, skip_shared, use_triangulation)\` computes volume. \`gprops.mass()\` returns the signed volume.
263	- Volume was historically wrong for models with periodic faces (cylinders/spheres) due to pcurve and vertex ordering issues. These are now resolved — all test models produce volumes matching STEP references to within ~1e-7 relative difference.
264	- Face orientation is handled correctly by the combination of \`ShapeFix_Shell::Perform()\` (edge consistency + pcurve repair) and \`ShapeFix_Solid::SolidFromShell()\` (global orientation via \`BRepClass3d_SolidClassifier::PerformInfinitePoint\`). Do NOT post-process individual face orientations — flipping individual faces breaks edge consistency, which causes both \`BRepGProp::VolumeProperties\` and \`SolidFromShell\` to give wrong results. This was extensively tested: 6/8 models produce perfect volume without any post-processing, vs. various failures when individual faces were flipped.
265	- \`b_rep_check::Analyzer::new_shape_bool(shape, true)\` + \`.is_valid()\` validates a solid.
266	
267	### Stage 4.1 STEP output
268	- \`step_control::Writer::new()\` creates a writer. \`writer.transfer_shape_stepmodeltype_bool_progressrange(shape, mode, compgraph, &progress)\` transfers shapes. \`writer.write(path)\` writes the file.
269	- \`step_control::StepModelType::Asis\` preserves the exact geometry (no conversion to manifold/faceted form).
270	- \`if_select::ReturnStatus::Retdone\` indicates success for both transfer and write.
271	- \`interface::Static::set_c_val(name, val)\` sets STEP header metadata. Key parameters: \`"write.step.schema"\` (e.g., "AP214"), \`"write.step.product.name"\`.
272	- OCCT prints transfer statistics to stdout during \`transfer_shape\`, which cannot be suppressed via the Rust API. This is cosmetic noise in tests.
273	- For compare validation, re-read the written STEP via \`step_control::Reader\` to validate the full round-trip (write + read), not just the in-memory shapes.
274	
275	### Sphere UV pole singularity handling
276	- Sphere surfaces have UV singularities at poles (V=±π/2) where U is undefined. When a sphere's boundary circle passes through or near a pole, UV-bounds construction fails: the projected pcurve degenerates, producing edges with zero-area faces or incorrect topology.
277	- **Angular proximity detection**: Use \`ProjectPointOnCurve\` to find the closest point on the boundary circle to each pole, then compute angular distance via chord-length formula: \`cos(angle) = 1 - dist²/(2R²)\`. The 45° threshold avoids both false positives and numerical issues near the exact pole.
278	- **Reorientation for all-closed-loop spheres (tangent and non-tangent)**: When a sphere face has all-closed-loop boundary edges and any boundary circle passes within 45° of a UV pole, the sphere surface is reoriented so the boundary circles become iso-V curves. The reorientation axis is determined from: (a) the adjacent cylinder's axis direction for tangent edges, or (b) the boundary circle's plane normal for non-tangent edges (e.g., dome hemispheres cut by a meridional plane). This generalizes the original tangent-only reorientation and fixes sewing failures for hemispheres where the flat face plane contains the sphere axis.
279	- **Failed alternatives**: (1) Wire-based split-at-poles with \`ShapeConstruct_ProjectCurveOnSurface\` produced correct face areas but wrong volume (cylinder only) due to BRepCheck edge/vertex consistency issues. (2) UV-bounds on the original sphere with mesh-centroid-derived U range produced 6 free edges because UV-bounds boundaries are iso-parametric meridian arcs, geometrically different from the tangent circles.
280	- **Sphere pole vertex faces** (open edges with vertices at poles, e.g., rounded cube corners where each octant has one vertex at a pole): When a spherical face has open edges with vertices, and the UV bounds include V=±π/2, the U value at the pole is undefined (singularity). This corrupts the circular gap algorithm for U bounds (producing ~205° span instead of ~90°), pcurves (diagonal instead of meridional), and face areas (negative). Fix: in \`compute_uv_bounds_from_edges\`, exclude U values from vertices/midpoints within 0.01 radians of a pole (V ≈ ±π/2). The face is constructed via UV-bounds \`MakeFace::new_handlegeomsurface_real5\`. OCCT creates a 3-edge face (2 meridians + 1 parallel at the non-pole boundary; the pole collapses to a vertex with no degenerate edge). BRepCheck reports a harmless edge failure on edge 0 with ~zero tolerance; this is suppressed in \`validate_faces\` since it's resolved by sewing.
281	- **BRep_Builder::degenerated(&edge, true)**: Sets the degenerate flag on an edge. \`BRep_Tool::degenerated(&edge)\` queries it. MakeFace UV-bounds on spheres near poles does NOT automatically mark pole edges as degenerate. The edges at the pole have finite 3D length (they are the meridian arcs, not zero-length pole edges).
282	- **BRepCheck_Analyzer::new_shape_bool(shape, false)**: \`GeomControls=false\` checks only topological info. However, UV-bounds sphere pole faces fail BOTH geometric and topological checks on edge 0 (~zero tolerance). The root cause is unclear but harmless — the final solid after sewing passes BRepCheck.
283	- **Pcurve parameter sharing**: OCCT stores pcurves with the same parameterization as the 3D edge curve — use \`c2d.value(t)\` with the same parameter \`t\` from the 3D curve. Do NOT linearly remap parameters between curve parameter range and pcurve parameter range. Getting this wrong produces huge apparent deviations (multiple mm) that are diagnostic artifacts, not real errors.
284	- **Great circle arc fallback for sphere edges**: When \`compute_edge_curve\` finds a large gap (>0.3mm) and one surface is a sphere, constructing a great circle arc on the sphere between the two vertices produces a better edge curve than a straight line. Uses \`geom::Circle\` with proper normal (calculated from sphere center and edge vertices) and \`select_arc_parameters\` to trim. This fixed BRepCheck wire self-intersection failures on sphere faces.
285	
286	## Cylinder-Sphere Boundary: BFS Fragmentation
287	
288	### face_area bug (fixed)
289	The \`face_area\` function in stage 2 only computed area from \`vertex_indices[0..2]\` — correct for triangles but wrong for quads (\`vertex_count == 4\`) created by stage 1.3 coplanar fusion. For quads, the second triangle (v0, v2, v3) was ignored, computing roughly half the correct area. Fix: check \`vertex_count\` and add the second triangle's area when it's 4.
290	
291	### Cylinder fragmentation mechanism (empirically verified)
292	On rounded_cube_10_r2_fine, one of the 12 quarter-cylinder edges is fragmented into 6 small hypotheses (22+12+9+5+5+34 faces) instead of one 36-face hypothesis. Investigation found:
293	
294	1. **Fragment faces are NOT sphere faces.** All 108 faces within vertex tolerance of the ideal cylinder have \`sph_hyp=-1\` (no sphere hypothesis) and \`max_cyl_err < 2e-6\` against the precise ideal cylinder axis.
295	
296	2. **Fragmentation is caused by barrier faces.** At 3-4 locations along the cylinder strip, individual faces get \`cyl_hyp=-1\` (no valid seed partner). These faces cannot grow through committed neighbors or form valid seed pairs (cross product < MIN_CROSS_THRESHOLD with cylinder-side neighbors, sphere-side neighbors already committed by bogus equatorial hypotheses). Each barrier splits the BFS growth region.
297	
298	3. **Bogus equatorial hypotheses contribute indirectly.** They commit sphere faces that are mesh neighbors of boundary cylinder faces. When BFS reaches a barrier face, its sphere-side neighbors are already committed, and its cylinder-side neighbors have nearly parallel normals. No valid seed → \`cyl_hyp=-1\` → barrier.
299	
300	4. **The high vtx_err_max (~1.58e-4) in fragment hypotheses is misleading.** It's computed against the fragment's own poorly-fitted cylinder (fitted from a small portion of the full cylinder). Against the ideal cylinder, all face errors are < 2e-6.
301	
302	5. **Coordinate precision matters.** Using truncated sphere center coordinates (4 decimal places: 21.1219 instead of 21.1218879546) shifts the ideal cylinder axis enough to make all face errors appear ~1e-5, obscuring the true ~1e-6 errors. Always use full f64 precision for distance measurements.
303	
304	### Axis drift theory: disproven
305	Hypothesis: BFS refitting gradually rotates the cylinder axis when sphere faces are added, causing "drift." Empirical testing across rounded_cube_10_r2_{coarse,fine,medium} and pill_coarse showed **zero significant axis drift** on any successful/committed cylinder hypothesis. All axis_dot(seed, refit) values were ≥ 0.999999996. Drift only occurred on tiny (3-4 face) hypotheses already rejected by existing validation (min face count, angular coverage). The axis stability check described in some versions of the development plan would not have solved the actual problem.
306	
307	
308	### Interactive visualization (viz.rs) architecture
309	- \`three_d::Window::render_loop(self, callback)\` consumes \`self\` — the render loop must own the Window and run on the main thread.
310	- Channel-based architecture: main thread owns the render loop, pipeline runs in a background thread communicating via \`mpsc::sync_channel(0)\` for synchronous handoff.
311	- \`VizSender\` (pipeline side) calls \`show_and_wait()\` which blocks until the user presses Space/Shift+Space/Q.
312	- \`VizReceiver\` (render side) receives overlays and sends back \`VizAction\` responses.
313	- Closures inside \`render_loop\` must be \`'static\` — extract helper logic to free functions rather than using closures that capture outer scope references.
314	- Config has \`OwnedPtr<Shape>\` which is not Clone — must move Config into the pipeline thread closure, not clone it.
315	- \`VizOverlay\` supports multiple overlay types: \`FaceHighlight\` (mesh face coloring), \`EdgeHighlight\` (mesh edge coloring), \`CylinderOverlay\`/\`SphereOverlay\` (analytic geometry), \`LineOverlay\` (polyline segments with optional \`no_depth_test\`), \`ShapeMeshOverlay\` (tessellated OCCT shapes with edges).
316	- \`tessellate_shape()\` tessellates a \`TopoDS_Shape\` via \`BRepMesh_IncrementalMesh\` for viz display. \`sample_curve_for_viz()\` samples a \`HandleGeomCurve\` into polyline segment pairs.
317	- **three-d borrow conflict with egui**: \`frame_input.screen()\` returns a \`RenderTarget\` that holds an immutable borrow on \`frame_input\`. \`gui.update()\` needs \`&mut frame_input.events\`. Solve by scoping \`screen\` in a block \`{ let screen = frame_input.screen(); ... }\` so it drops before \`gui.update()\` is called.
318	- **Depth buffer readback for face label occlusion is unreliable**: The depth buffer read with \`DEPTH_COMPONENT\`/\`FLOAT\` appeared to work partially but many back-facing labels were still visible, likely due to precision issues with the wide near/far plane ratio (0.001×extent to 100×extent), polygon-offset interference, and tolerance calibration. **Use face-normal culling instead**: compute \`dot(face_normal, camera_pos - centroid)\` — if ≤ 0 the face is back-facing and the label should be hidden. This is simpler, has no GPU readback, and works correctly for solid models.
319	- **Sync-channel deadlock with click-to-skip**: The viz uses \`mpsc::sync_channel(0)\` (rendezvous). The render loop only calls \`try_recv()\` on the overlay channel when \`!waiting_for_input\`. If a click sends \`SkipToSeed\` but does NOT set \`waiting_for_input = false\`, the BFS can never deliver the next overlay (its \`overlay_tx.send()\` blocks waiting for the render loop's \`try_recv()\`, which never fires). Always set \`waiting_for_input = false\` immediately after sending any \`VizAction\`. Also guard the send with \`if waiting_for_input\` to avoid sending on a sync channel when BFS is not blocked in \`recv()\`, which would also deadlock.
320	- **Hover wireframe rebuild**: Rebuild \`WireframeRenderer\` (GPU buffer allocation) only when the hovered face changes, not every frame. Cache \`hover_face: Option<usize>\` and compare before rebuilding.
321	- **three-d \`MouseMotion\` fires for all mouse movement**, including button-free hover (\`button: None\`). Track \`mouse_pos\` from the \`position\` field of \`MouseMotion\` events. \`MousePress\`/\`MouseRelease\` also carry \`position\` for click detection.
322	- **Click vs drag detection**: Record \`mouse_down_pos\` on \`MousePress\`, compare with \`MouseRelease\` position. If \`dx² + dy² < 25\` (5px radius), it's a click; otherwise a drag. This prevents orbiting from triggering face picks.
323	
324	
325	### BRepLib::SameParameter corrupts pcurves on closely-spaced edges
326	Calling \`BRepLib::SameParameter(shape, 1.0, true)\` with a large tolerance (1.0mm) and \`forced=true\` recomputes all pcurves, which can corrupt pcurves on faces with closely-spaced edges (e.g., sphere faces at sphere-cylinder tangent junctions). This manifests as BRepCheck_Wire self-intersection failures. The fix is to use \`forced=false\` (skip edges already flagged as SameParameter) and a tight tolerance (\`vertex_tolerance_mm\`, typically 1e-5). This allows edges that were correctly constructed to keep their pcurves while only fixing genuinely misaligned ones.
327	
328	
329	### Cone/cylinder seed face selection: fan topology with optional f3
330	
331	Cone and cylinder seeds use a "fan" topology: initial face fi, neighbor f1, and another face f2 that is a neighbor of fi but NOT an edge-wise neighbor of f1. This puts fi in between f1 and f2 for better angular coverage. Pairwise qualification checks normals of f1 and f2 against fi's normal (not against each other). When fi+f1+f2 yield only 5 unique vertices (insufficient for 6-DOF cone fitting), an optional f3 is added — a face adjacent to f2 that doesn't share an edge with fi or f1, giving at least 6 vertices.
332	
333	### Conical surface detection: apex-vertex seeding
334	
335	Triple-seed (3 adjacent faces) fails for cones because apex-adjacent faces share the apex vertex and only span ~12° of the cone base — this gives a biased centroid, tilted axis, and wrong half-angle (~2° instead of true ~20°). Instead, use **apex-vertex seeding**: identify vertices with many incident non-coplanar-normal faces (eigenval/trace ratio < 0.3 from normal covariance), then use ALL faces incident to each apex vertex as the seed set. This gives robust axis estimation.
336	
337	### Cone axis orientation must be explicit
338	
339	The normal covariance eigenvector gives an unsigned axis direction. The cone distance formula \`d = r·cos(θ) - h·sin(θ)\` requires h > 0 (vertices on the apex-to-base side). If the axis happens to point the wrong way, h is negative for base vertices and the distance formula produces huge false errors (~14mm instead of ~0). Fix: after profile fitting, check if the sum of all h values is negative and flip the axis if so, then re-fit the profile.
340	
341	### Conical faces need \`is_periodic\` treatment
342	
343	In stage 3, conical faces are periodic (full-revolution) like cylindrical and spherical faces. The \`is_periodic\` check must include \`SelectedSurface::Conical(_)\` or conical faces will go through \`create_planar_face\` instead of \`create_periodic_face\`, causing segfaults when a full-circle edge is encountered.
344	
345	### \`ShapeFix_*\` can segfault on cone faces
346	
347	\`create_wire_based_periodic_face\` deliberately skips \`ShapeFix_Wire\`/\`ShapeFix_Face\` for non-sphere periodic faces: on cones, ShapeFix crashes (not just errors) due to pcurve/edge-curve interactions. Spheres tolerate it. So cone face repair must be done without ShapeFix. This constrains the proposed stage-3 shared-edge rework (DEVELOPMENT_PLAN §3.x): attach pcurves to shared edges directly with \`BRep_Builder\` rather than routing cone faces through ShapeFix to "fix up" a wire.
348	
349	### OCCT cone convention: origin at apex, zero ref_radius
350	
351	\`geom::ConicalSurface::new_ax3_real2(&ax3, half_angle, ref_radius)\` — for brepper's cones, set origin at the apex and ref_radius=0. The Ax3 origin is the apex point, Z-direction points from apex toward the base.
352	
353	### False positive cone detection on spherical/cylindrical patches
354	
355	Sphere and cylinder patches can be approximately fitted as cones because locally any smooth surface looks conical. Key discriminators:
356	1. **Half-angle bounds**: ha < 2° → cylindrical, ha > 85° → planar. Reject both.
357	2. **Apex distance**: If apex is > 10× mesh bounding-box diagonal from mesh center, the fit is degenerate (distant apex = near-cylindrical).
358	3. **Normal-axis consistency** (restored after a brief removal): on a cone, |n·axis| = sin(half_angle) is constant for all facet normals — tessellation coarseness rotates facet normals *around* the axis, preserving the dot product exactly. Applied twice: per-face during BFS expansion (deviation > 0.05 rejects, keeping doomed trials small) and post-BFS as a variance check (> 0.0005 rejects). Removing it let stage 2.2 tile torus fillets with bogus conical hypotheses, which starved torus seeding (stage 2.5 seeds exclude conical-committed faces) and broke torus detection entirely.
359	4. **What these checks cannot catch**: a *single row* of quads (two rings of vertices) lies EXACTLY on some cone; a *band of azimuthal strips* on a shallow cone lies almost exactly on a tilted cylinder (any 3 plane normals are coplanar-ish). Such spurious hypotheses are geometrically legitimate and unavoidable at the hypothesis level; they are removed by area-based selection plus the post-selection absorption pass (see below). Tests must therefore assert on *selected* surfaces (stage 2.6), never raw hypothesis counts.
360	
361	### Pointed cone fitting: fixed-apex LM
362	
363	For pointed cones (all faces share a single apex vertex), the general 7-parameter cone LM (apex_x, apex_y, apex_z, axis_alpha, axis_beta, half_angle, unused) is underdetermined — the apex has zero residual regardless of parameters, so the LM Jacobian rows for apex vertices are near-zero, causing poor convergence. Solution: use a fixed-apex 3-parameter LM (axis_alpha, axis_beta, half_angle) that only optimizes axis direction and half-angle while keeping the apex pinned at the shared vertex position.
364	
365	### LM recentering and patience for cone/cylinder fits
366	
367	Both cone and cylinder LM refinement **recenter** all vertex positions around their centroid before optimization, then shift fitted parameters (apex, axis origin) back afterward. This improves numerical stability when vertex coordinates are large relative to the surface feature size. LM patience is set to 500 (up from default ~100) to ensure convergence well below vertex tolerance. \`seed_vtol_multiplier\` is 1.0 for cones/cylinders since CAD mesh vertices lie precisely on the surface.
368
