```
370	
371	After \`select_surfaces\` assigns faces to hypotheses, unselected hypotheses should be removed from the hypothesis vectors in \`Stage2Output\` (planes, cylinders, spheres, cones, tori). This requires remapping \`SelectedSurface\` indices to match the compacted vectors. Benefits: downstream code (stage 3) can index directly into hypothesis vectors without gaps; \`Stage2Output\` accurately represents only the surfaces used for reconstruction.
372	4. **Error_max after final re-fit**: BFS may accept faces within tolerance during expansion, but the final re-fit can shift parameters — must verify \`error_max ≤ surface_tol\` after the final fit.
373	- Stage 3 viz (3.3/3.4/3.5/3.6): stage 3.3 uses \`FaceHighlight\` for surface context and \`LineOverlay\` for edge curves; stage 3.4 uses \`ShapeMeshOverlay\` for OCCT faces; stages 3.5/3.6 use \`ShapeMeshOverlay\` for shells/solids.
374	
375	### Cone BFS angular tolerance
376	
377	Tessellated cones with N circumferential divisions have inter-strip dihedral angles ≈ 360°/N. For N=20 (typical), that's ~18°, near the historical default \`angular_tol\` of 17.5°. The cone BFS uses \`angular_tol * 2.0\` for the *growth* dihedral check because vertex-to-surface distance is the primary discriminator for cones (not angular similarity). Without this relaxation, BFS captures only ~127/167 cone facets, and the remaining strips become spurious small planar hypotheses that corrupt surface selection. Note the seed-pair qualification uses the *raw* \`angular_tol\`, which is why the default was later raised to 25° (see the medium-resolution learnings at end of file).
378	
379	### Conical stage performance: spheres first, cylinder-first fitting, bounded LM patience
380	
381	- **Spherical detection (2.3) executes before conical (2.2)**: every band of quad rows on a tessellated sphere lies exactly on some cone/cylinder, so the conical BFS used to tile fine spheres with hundreds of band hypotheses (pill_fine: 456 bogus hypotheses, 45 s). Sphere detection is cheap and its solid-angle coverage acceptance rejects band fits on cylinders/cones/tori, so spheres are committed first and conical *seeding* skips sphere-committed faces (BFS expansion may still absorb them, so tangent junctions work). This dropped pill_fine stage 2.2 to 0.002 s. The old warning about spurious sphere hypotheses on cone faces (block_with_conical_hole) is obsolete — the solid-angle acceptance now rejects those, and block_with_conical_hole detects its cone with 0 sphere hypotheses.
382	- **Cylinder-first fitting**: \`fit_surface\` runs the cheap 4-DOF cylinder fit first and skips the expensive cone LM when the cylinder fit is already exact (max vertex error ≤ 1e-6 mm) — a cone could at best tie, and ties select the cylinder.
383	- **LM patience 150** (was 500): good fits converge and exit early regardless; the patience budget was only being burned by doomed fits on sphere/torus patches. Fillet models run ~3× faster in stage 2.2 with identical selected surfaces.
384	- **Early half-angle rejection**: after the initial cone fit but before seed tolerance check and BFS, reject cones with half-angle outside [2°, 85°].
385	
386	### Cone apex UV bounds extension
387	
388	Full (non-truncated) cones with a single boundary edge at the base produce zero V-range from \`compute_uv_bounds_from_edges\` (both V values project to the same edge height). This creates a degenerate face → BRepCheck failure → sewing failure. Fix: for conical surfaces with a single boundary edge, extend V to 0 (the apex) by sampling mesh face centroids to determine which side of the edge the face extends, then setting \`vmin = 0.0\`. This is analogous to sphere pole V-extension for hemispheres.
389	
390	### Cone concave flag in face creation
391	
392	The \`is_concave\` check in \`create_periodic_face\` must handle \`SelectedSurface::Conical(idx)\` using \`!hypothesis.convex\`, not default to \`false\`. Concave cones (e.g., conical holes) need reversed normals during face construction so that sewing produces correctly oriented shells.
393	
394	### Torus fitting: medial axis / tube center method
395	
396	The torus fitting algorithm: (1) estimate minor radius r from normal-line intersections of sampled face pairs using **25th percentile** (not median — see below), (2) compute tube centers k_i = p_i + r*n_i (trying both signs, keeping best circle-fit RMS), (3) fit 3D circle to tube centers using PCA for axis + 2D algebraic circle fit for R, (4) refine all 7 parameters [alpha, beta, cx, cy, cz, R, r] via Levenberg-Marquardt (patience=500, threshold=7). For better normal estimates, vertex normals are averaged across all incident seed faces rather than using a single face normal. Vertex iteration is sorted for determinism (HashSet ordering varies between runs).
397	
398	\`fit_torus\` tries **both** the tube center method and \`fit_torus_sor\`, keeping whichever achieves lower maximum vertex-to-torus distance. The SOR method estimates the axis from normal covariance smallest eigenvector, projects vertices to (h,r) coords, fits a shifted circle for R and r.
399	
400	### Minor radius estimation: 25th percentile, not median
401	
402	Normal-line intersections between adjacent faces on a torus produce a **mix** of tube curvature ($\approx r$, from edges running along the tube) and azimuthal curvature ($\approx R - r$ for concave, $\approx R + r$ for convex, from edges running along the major circle). The tube-curvature estimates are the **smallest** values. Using the median picks a value contaminated by azimuthal curvature ($\approx 6$ instead of the true $r = 1.5$ for the filleted_pipe inner fillet). The 25th percentile consistently selects the correct tube-curvature cluster. This was the key fix for detecting the z=28.5 inner concave fillet (R=7.5, r=1.5).
403	
404	### Torus seeding: face-based 1-ring neighborhoods
405	
406	Component-based seeding fails for tori because connected components typically contain cylinder body faces and fillet faces mixed together (e.g., a 383-face component). Face-based seeding works: for each uncommitted candidate face, build a seed consisting of that face plus all faces sharing at least one vertex (the 1-ring vertex neighborhood). Only uncommitted faces are included. Seeds with <7 faces or <9 vertices are skipped. BFS naturally skips faces already committed to a toroidal hypothesis, so later seeds avoid already-identified regions. This is simpler and more robust than vertex-neighborhood seeding with post-merge: every toroidal face gets a chance to anchor a hypothesis without needing merge to combine overlapping seeds.
407	
408	### Generic BFS abstraction (bfs.rs)
409	
410	The \`SurfaceType\` trait in \`bfs.rs\` unifies BFS region growing across all 5 surface types. Key design decisions:
411	- Associated types \`Fit\` (surface parameters) and \`Hypothesis\` (hypothesis struct) avoid trait objects.
412	- \`generate_seeds()\` returns \`Vec<Seed>\` — each type has its own seeding strategy (face-pair for plane/cylinder, vertex-neighborhood for sphere, apex-vertex for cone, 1-ring for torus).
413	- \`fit_surface()\` takes face/vertex lists and returns \`Option<Fit>\` — type-specific fitting logic.
414	- \`vertex_distance()\` computes point-to-surface distance for BFS expansion.
415	- \`acceptance_test()\` validates after BFS (angular coverage, min face count, etc.).
416	- \`seed_vtol_multiplier()\` and \`angular_tol_multiplier()\` allow per-type tolerance overrides (defaults 1.0).
417	- **Performance regression**: The generic BFS is ~3× slower than per-type BFS because it generates more seeds (it tries all seeds from \`generate_seeds()\` instead of early-terminating). The per-type code had hand-tuned seed iteration with domain-specific early exit.
418	
419	### Multi-axis LM rescue for small torus patches
420	
421	Small torus patches (~15° of the major circle) often defeat geometric axis estimation because there is insufficient angular coverage for reliable PCA or normal covariance analysis. When the initial geometric fit fails vertex_tolerance, a multi-axis Levenberg–Marquardt rescue tries 5 axis candidates: the geometric estimate, the normal covariance smallest eigenvector, and the three coordinate axes. For each axis, vertices are projected to a 2D plane perpendicular to the axis, a 2D algebraic circle (Kasa method, 3×3 system) estimates center and major radius, and LM refines from there. The best result across all candidates is kept if it achieves vertex_tolerance.
422	
423	### Torus quality gate on circle-fit RMS
424	
425	When convex and concave tori share edges (e.g., filleted_pipe: R=8.5 convex and R=7.5 concave), boundary vertices have incident faces from both torus patches. Seeds at these vertices mix faces from different tori, producing tube centers that scatter between two different major circles. A quality gate on the 3D circle fit RMS (reject if rms > 0.1 * minor_r) catches these mixed seeds early, before BFS expansion wastes time on a bad hypothesis.
426	
427	### Pipe elbow torus tessellation
428	
429	The onshape pipe_elbow model's torus surface is tessellated into many narrow strips whose normals span < 180° locally. Stage 2.5 torus fitting doesn't fire because the normal distribution looks locally cylindrical (not toroidal). Stage 2.6 selects 290 cylindrical patches that individually pass \`--compare\`. This is expected behavior for coarsely tessellated, low-curvature tori where the mesh facets don't exhibit the characteristic toroidal normal pattern (band pattern in Gaussian map). Future improvement: unified SOR framework fitting could detect this by comparing cylinder vs torus profile fits in (h,r) space.
430	### HashSet iteration order causes flaky results — fitting functions take sorted slices
431	
432	When fitting code iterates over a \`HashSet<usize>\` of vertex indices, the iteration order varies between runs (Rust's default hasher uses per-process random keys). Since floating-point addition is non-associative, different orders produce slightly different fitted parameters — enough to flip marginal hypotheses (simple_cone failed 1 run in 3). All \`fit_*\` functions now take \`vertex_set: &[usize]\` (sorted, deduplicated by the caller in \`fit_surface\`) instead of \`&HashSet<usize>\`; never reintroduce unordered iteration in anything that feeds a fit.
433	
434	### Wide-angle cone: axis estimation uses both eigenvectors
435	
436	For a cone with half-angle ha, face normals make angle (90°−ha) with the axis. The covariance eigenvalue along the axis is proportional to sin²(ha), while the radial eigenvalues are proportional to cos²(ha)/2. For ha > ~35°, the axis corresponds to the **largest** eigenvector, not the smallest. The current \`compute_truncated_cone_axis\` tries both smallest and largest eigenvectors of the normal covariance matrix, plus mean-direction from centroid, keeping whichever gives the lowest fitting error.
437	
438	
439	The \`Geom_ToroidalSurface\` binding was present in opencascade-sys all along (\`geom::ToroidalSurface::new_ax3_real2\`), but workspace-scoped search tools (grep_search, file_search, semantic_search, and Explore agent searches) cannot find content in \`../opencascade-rs/\` because it's outside the workspace root. Use terminal \`grep\` to search files outside the workspace. Don't assume a binding is missing just because workspace search tools return no results.
440	
441	### BFS verbosity levels and viz_level
442	
443	Verbosity in \`generate_hypotheses()\` (in \`bfs.rs\`) uses consistent indentation — no \`[prefix]\` tags:
444	- Level 1: stage summary output (in \`stage2/mod.rs\`)
445	- Level 2: per-hypothesis detail
446	- Level 3: per-committed-hypothesis progress/stats (2s interval profiling reports, seed/fit counts)
447	- Level 4: per-seed-attempt details (seed accepted/rejected with error values, fit descriptions)
448	- Level 5: per-BFS-face exploration (each face accepted/rejected/skipped with error values)
449	
450	Viz pause granularity in BFS is controlled by \`BfsConfig.viz_level\` (set from \`Config.viz_stages_level\` → \`--viz-stages-level\` CLI flag):
451	- Level 1: pause only at committed hypotheses and stage 2.6 selections (default, least intrusive)
452	- Level 2: also pause after each accepted seed, before BFS expansion
453	- Level 3: also pause after each individual BFS face acceptance
454	
455	Both \`verbosity\` and \`viz_level\` are fields in \`BfsConfig\` (defined in \`src/stage2/bfs.rs\`) and set in \`stage2/mod.rs\` when building \`BfsConfig\` from \`Config\`.
456	
457	### Post-selection absorption of redundant surfaces (stage 2.6)
458	
459	\`absorb_redundant_surfaces\` merges a selected surface S into an adjacent larger surface T when ALL of S's vertices lie within tolerance of T's geometry AND all of S's face centroids lie within surface tolerance of T. Two cases:
460	- Spurious sub-fits (a cylinder band on a shallow cone): tolerance 10× vertex tolerance — the overlap is exact.
461	- Tangent-junction bridge facets (≤ 2 faces): tolerance = surface tolerance. A facet spanning a tangent junction (e.g. cone-sphere on the nosecone) has vertices on both sides; its chordal deviation from either surface is ~d²/2R, far above vertex tolerance but below surface tolerance. Without absorption these become orphan single-face planar surfaces with fake edges that break stage 3.1 compare.
462	
463	**The centroid check is essential**: a flat end cap triangulated as a fan from a *boundary* vertex has ALL its vertices on the boundary circle — which lies exactly on the adjacent cone/cylinder — so a vertex-only test absorbs the entire cap into the cone (simple_cone collapsed to 1 surface). Cap face *centroids* are well off the cone, so the centroid test rejects the merge.
464	
465	**Limits**: absorbing bridge facets into a curved surface shifts the reconstructed mesh boundary between two tangent surfaces by one facet at those azimuths; on rounded_cube_10_r2_coarse at an out-of-spec angular tolerance (17.5° vs the required 20°) this produced invalid faces. Models must be run within their tessellation's angular tolerance (rounded_cube coarse tests pass --angular-tolerance=20 per tests/RESULTS.md).
466	
467	### Flat annuli and cylinder bands lie exactly on degenerate torus families
468	
469	Two coaxial circles at the same axial position (a flat annulus boundary) lie on a one-parameter FAMILY of tori (any tube offset works), so torus LM can fit an annulus exactly with an arbitrary tube radius, and its faces can span a nonzero *positional* tube arc on a large-tube member of the family. The minor-circle coverage acceptance therefore measures tube span from face NORMALS (ψ = atan2(n·â, n·r̂), span ≥ 0.3 rad): annuli and cylinder bands have all-parallel normals (span ≈ 0) and are rejected, while real fillets span their tube arc (90° typically). This fixed filleted_pipe, where bogus tori were stealing the annulus faces from the real planes.
470	
471	### Sphere-cone tangent junctions
472	
473	- The tangent circle between a sphere and a cone is NOT a great circle: it sits at radius R·cos α, offset along the cone axis. \`compute_tangent_edge_curve_axis_circle_closed\` builds it as a circle perpendicular to the cone axis with axial position and radius averaged from the edge's mesh boundary vertices.
474	- Sphere faces reoriented for pole handling must compute V bounds by projecting boundary-circle samples onto the oriented surface: fixed hemisphere bounds [0, π/2] assume a great-circle junction and misplace the boundary for cones (nosecone free edges 3 mm apart at sewing).
475	- Facets *bridging* the tangent junction (2 vertices on each side) cannot be absorbed by either surface at vertex tolerance (chordal deviation d²/2R ≈ 0.09 mm for d = 1.5 mm rows, R = 12.5 mm) — they are handled by the absorption pass above.
476	
477	### Torus face V-bounds: centroids disambiguate, never extend
478	
479	In \`compute_uv_bounds_from_edges\`, mesh face centroid projections must only *select* between the two candidate V windows delimited by the edge projections — never extend the window. A cap triangle whose three vertices all lie on the plane-torus junction circle is legitimately absorbed by the torus hypothesis, but its centroid projects ~2° past the tangent circle; including it in the window shifted the face boundary off the junction and produced sewing free edges (filleted_cylinder). This was also nondeterministic since only 3 arbitrary faces were sampled.
480	
481	### OCCT detailed BRepCheck diagnostics can throw
482	
483	\`BRepCheck_Face\`/\`BRepCheck_Edge\` diagnostics on invalid faces can throw \`Standard_NullObject\` (edges without geometry), which the bindings surface as a Rust panic. \`validate_faces\` wraps the detailed diagnostics in \`catch_unwind\` and treats a diagnostic failure as an ordinary invalid face rather than aborting the pipeline.
484	
485	### Pipe elbows: strip-merge torus seeding and iso-U boundaries
486	
487	- A coarsely tessellated torus (pipe elbow) is tiled by narrow cylinder strips in stage 2.2 — each strip's 1-ring neighborhood spans too little major-arc curvature for a torus fit. Strip-merge seeding: for conical-committed faces, seed from a 3-ring edge neighborhood when it spans ≥ 2 distinct conical hypotheses (a plain cylinder is 1 hypothesis → skipped cheaply). Three adjacent strips give a reliable 7-DOF torus fit; BFS then grows over the whole elbow and area-based selection discards the strips. pipe_elbow_10 medium/fine now pass the full pipeline; the deduced torus matches STEP exactly (R=10, r=5).
488	- Elbow junction circles are iso-U on the torus (tube cross-sections, perpendicular to the CYLINDER axis), unlike fillet junctions which are iso-V (perpendicular to the TORUS axis). Both the tangent-circle construction (try both axes, keep the better vertex fit) and the UV-bounds computation (classify per-edge sample spreads; iso-U boundaries → face full in V, U from gap algorithm + centroid disambiguation) must handle both configurations.
489	
490	### Tangent-edge boundary vertices need chordal tolerance in stage 3.1 compare
491	
492	Onshape's fine tessellation does not always place a precise vertex ring on tangent junction circles (vertex positions can be ~1e-4 off the ideal surfaces near corners), so the mesh region boundary between two tangent surfaces can sit one row off the junction — one row of sagitta (row²/2R ≈ 7.6e-3 mm on rounded_cube fine) from the STEP edge. This is harmless: tangent junction curves are constructed from the fitted hypotheses, not from boundary vertices. The stage 3.1 compare therefore runs after tangency detection (3.2) and checks tangent-edge boundary vertices against --surface-tolerance while sharp edges keep --vertex-tolerance. Whether this fired at all used to depend on nondeterministic boundary composition and every-Nth sampling.
493	
494	### Internal voids (multi-shell solids)
495	
496	- Stage 1.2: a closed shell with negative signed volume is a legitimate internal void (normals point out of the material, into the cavity) when its bounding box is contained in a closed positive shell's box; counted in \`voids_within_solids\`. Otherwise negative volume still means inverted winding.
497	- Stage 3.6: \`merge_void_solids\` merges solids whose bbox is contained in a strictly larger solid by adding the void's shells to the container (\`BRep_Builder::Add\`), trying both shell orientations and keeping the one whose volume equals container − Σ voids. hollow_cube (tests/occt/) validates 1 solid at exactly 7000 mm³.
498	- Test models with enclosed voids cannot be made in ccad (and the installed ccad currently segfaults on \`ccad build\` even for the pre-existing project); \`gen-test-models\` (src/bin/gen_test_models.rs) builds them via OCCT MakeBox + BRepAlgoAPI_Cut and writes both STL (StlAPI_Writer after BRepMesh_IncrementalMesh) and STEP. Run via scripts/generate_occt_models.sh (normalizes STEP timestamps).
499	
500	### Narrow-arc cones: normal-line axis rescue
501	
502	The primary cone axis estimates (normal covariance smallest eigenvector, normal-difference crosses) degenerate when a seed's normals are nearly parallel — side cone patches of a transition piece spanning a few tessellation columns produced 136/138 seed fit failures on cone_tangent_planes. Cone surface normal lines all pass through the axis, so closest-approach midpoints of normal-line pairs trace the axis: fit a 3D line through them (centroid + dominant scatter eigenvector), then the (h,r) profile line for apex/half-angle, then LM. Implemented as \`fit_cone_normal_line_rescue\`, tried when the primary fit is missing or above 1e-4 mm.
503	
504	### Cone acceptance half-angle cap raised to 85°
505	
506	Real CAD cones close to flat exist (cone_tangent_planes has an 84.25° cone). The old 80° cap guarded against near-tangent bogus cones on sphere polar caps, which is now prevented upstream (spherical detection runs before conical; sphere-committed faces don't seed cones).
507	
508	### Plane-cone tangent lines are generators, not axis-parallel lines
509	
510	\`compute_tangent_edge_curve_line\` originally assumed plane-CYLINDER geometry: direction = cylinder axis, point at radius_at_apex from the axis. For a true cone the tangent line is a GENERATOR (tilted from the axis by the half-angle), and radius_at_apex = 0 collapses the analytic point onto the axis — the constructed line ran through the apex, 11 mm off. The two endpoint vertices lie exactly on the generator, so cones use the vertex-to-vertex line directly.
511	
512	### Complete tori use natural-bounds face construction
513	
514	A complete donut selects one toroidal surface with NO boundary edges; like full spheres, the face is built with \`MakeFace::new_handlegeomsurface_real\` (natural [0,2π]×[0,2π] bounds), which creates both the U seam (around the major circle) and the V seam (around the tube) automatically. full_torus (tests/occt/, generated by gen-test-models via BRepPrimAPI_MakeTorus) passes stage 4.1 with volume matching to ~7e-9 relative.
515	
516	### Curvature-guided seeding (stages 1+2) and toroidal-before-conical ordering
517	
518	- \`compute_seed_scores\` (stage2/mod.rs) builds two per-face signals once per mesh: a diffused curvature-difference score for ORDERING (BFS start faces ascending — interior faces of uniform regions first) and a raw-score junction mask for GATHERING EXCLUSION (pass 1 only; pass 2 lifts the filter so all-junction surfaces still seed). Curvature summary per face = max over edges of dihedral/centroid-distance; the junction criterion is LOCAL relative change (score > 50% of local curvature magnitude) — a mesh-global threshold fails because sharp creases dominate the max and tangent junctions (the primary target, G1-continuous but G2-discontinuous) fall under any fraction of it.
519	- With clean interior seeds available, TOROIDAL detection (2.5) moved before CONICAL (2.2), completing the ordering principle: spheres → tori → cones/cylinders, most-constrained surfaces first. Any adjacent pair of quad rows on a torus tube lies exactly on some cone, so cones previously tiled fillets with 2-ring bands before the torus stage ran. Cylinders resist bogus torus fits cheaply (tube centers collapse onto the axis; the (h,r) profile is a constant-r line). Conical seeding skips torus-committed faces like sphere-committed ones.
520	- Toroidal seed gathering uses hop-expansion (up to 3 hops, target ≥16 faces) instead of a fixed 1-ring: small fillets (r=0.5 tubes, 2-3 rows) have little interior after junction exclusion across the tube but extend far along the fillet axis.
521	- Raw-hypothesis stage-2 compare failures are now warnings; the hard gate is the post-selection compare. Spurious pre-selection hypotheses are expected by design.
522	- Results: filleted_pipe stage 2.2 5.2 s → 0.06 s with exactly the right selection (its STEP has 4 tori — the previous "6 tori" selection was over-segmented); stepped_block stage 2.2 3 s → 0.4 s with planar count matching STEP exactly (17); filleted_cylinder 2.2+2.5 ≈ 0.03 s total.
523	
524	### Boundary refinement and corner vertex refinement (plan §2.6 refitting)
525	
526	- \`refine_boundary_assignments\` (stage 2.6, after absorption): region-boundary faces move to an adjacent selected surface that fits their vertices ≥2× better; iterated to a fixpoint. Fixes row-off region boundaries that shifted reconstructed corners (stepped_block fine's corner vertex went from 0.07 mm off to exact). Only membership changes — geometry is not re-fitted.
527	- \`refine_corner_vertices\` (stage 3, after tangency detection): SHARP corner vertices are refined by cyclic projection onto adjacent fitted surfaces. Must skip corners adjacent to tangent edges: tangent pairs meet along a curve, not a point, and cyclic projection slides along it (drifted 0.57 mm before the restriction). Guard: revert if the move exceeds 2× surface tolerance.
528	- Torus tangent ARC construction now tries both candidate axes (torus + adjacent cone/cylinder/other-torus axis) like the closed-loop variant, picking the circle that best fits the boundary vertices. A wrong axis projects both endpoint vertices to the same circle parameter → zero-span arc → MakeEdge "Differentpointsonclosedcurve".
529	- The tangent-edge/vertex compare relaxations must stay: with refinement, most models pass at tight tolerance, but genuinely ambiguous junction rows remain (a face whose vertices sit on both tangent surfaces equally is not movable by any best-fit rule), e.g. one edge on stepped_block fine at 0.044 mm.
530	
531	### Medium-resolution tessellation: coverage floor, cylinder-only gating, and the default angular tolerance
532	
533	stepped_block_toroidal_fillets MEDIUM (2.3K triangles) went from one undetected corner-blend torus (fails stage 3.1 at 0.35 mm) to full stage-4.1 pass via three coupled changes. The root cause is that Onshape's "medium" preset tessellates by chordal deviation, so a small feature gets very few segments regardless of the angular preset — an r=0.5 fillet becomes four rows across each 90° tube arc, with ~24° dihedral steps between rows.
534	
535	- **BFS final re-fit keeps the better of two fits, not always the fresh one.** The end-of-trial \`S::fit_surface\` from scratch can converge to a *worse* local minimum than the fit maintained incrementally during BFS growth, even when every trial vertex is within 1e-5 of the incremental fit (observed: the full-ring R=3.5 pocket-rim fillet torus refit to 0.87 mm and was rejected). \`current_fit\` is a valid fallback by construction (it satisfied the vertex tolerance for every accepted face), so adopt the from-scratch fit only when it lowers the trial's max vertex error. This alone recovered the 18th torus.
536	- **Angular-coverage floor for coarse tessellation, gated to cylinders AND to well-spanned arcs.** The \`angular_coverage_valid\` span/3 second-gap rule rejects legitimate coarse fillets (four rows across 90° = 24° gaps > span/3 = 23°). Added a \`max_gap\` floor = \`angular_tol * angular_tol_multiplier\` (capped at span/2). Two gates keep it from admitting bogus bands:
537	  - *Cylinders only* (\`half_angle < 1e-4\`): a true cone's coarse-coverage lookalike is a 6-face ~50° half-angle patch fitted to a corner sphere-blend, which *must* stay rejected or it wins selection over the correct sphere (regressed rounded_cube_medium 48→40 tangent edges before the gate). Straight-edge fillets are cylinders, so gating loses nothing.
538	  - *Span ≥ 45° only*: without this, the floor floods a smooth truncated cone with spurious narrow cylinder bands — a thin slice of a shallow cone fits a cylinder within tolerance and is locally almost cylindrical (low n·axis variance, so the aggregate-normal check doesn't catch it). Instrumenting \`angular_coverage_valid\` showed the discriminator cleanly: the legit stepped_block corner fillet spans ~69°, every spurious nosecone_truncated band spans ≤14°. Without the span gate the floor regressed nosecone_truncated_medium (was passing) from 4 selected surfaces to 27 (over-segmented). 45° sits well above the bands and below any genuine coarse quarter/half-round.
539	- **Default --angular-tolerance raised 17.5° → 25°.** Conical seed-pair qualification (\`conical_pairwise_qualified\`) uses the *raw* (unmultiplied) angular tolerance, so the 24.1° fillet-row pairs were rejected below 25° and the four corner edge-fillet cylinders never seeded (33 vs 37 cylinders at 20° vs 25°). rounded_cube_10_r2_coarse's explicit \`--angular-tolerance=20\` still works; the selection for rounded_cube_medium is byte-identical at 17.5/20/25 (its fillet steps are finer). Verified no model regresses at the higher default (full suite green).
```
</details>

```
2940	fn group_edges_into_wires(fd: &FaceDescriptor, edges: &[ReconEdge]) -> Vec<Vec<usize>> {
2941	    if fd.edge_indices.is_empty() {
2942	        return Vec::new();
2943	    }
2944	
2945	    let mut groups: Vec<Vec<usize>> = Vec::new();
2946	    // Map from BRepVertex index to which group it belongs to
2947	    let mut vertex_group: HashMap<usize, usize> = HashMap::new();
2948	
2949	    for &ei in &fd.edge_indices {
2950	        let edge = &edges[ei];
2951	        let [v0, v1] = edge.vertex_indices;
2952	
2953	        if v0 == usize::MAX && v1 == usize::MAX {
2954	            // Closed loop — its own wire
2955	            groups.push(vec![ei]);
2956	            continue;
2957	        }
2958	
2959	        // Find existing group for v0 or v1
2960	        let g0 = if v0 != usize::MAX {
2961	            vertex_group.get(&v0).copied()
2962	        } else {
2963	            None
2964	        };
2965	        let g1 = if v1 != usize::MAX {

2969	        };

2981	            }
2982	            (Some(gi), None) => {
2983	                groups[gi].push(ei);
2984	                if v1 != usize::MAX {
2985	                    vertex_group.insert(v1, gi);
2986	                }
2987	            }
2988	            (None, Some(gi)) => {
2989	                groups[gi].push(ei);

2992	                }
2993	            }

2995	                groups[g0i].push(ei);

2997	            (Some(g0i), Some(g1i)) => {
```

```
349	fn create_occt_surface(
350	    surface: &SelectedSurface,
351	    output: &Stage2Output,
352	) -> OwnedPtr<geom::HandleGeomSurface> {
353	    match surface {
354	        SelectedSurface::Planar(idx) => {
355	            let hyp = &output.planar_hypotheses[*idx];
356	            let origin = gp::Pnt::new_real3(
357	                hyp.normal[0] * hyp.distance,
358	                hyp.normal[1] * hyp.distance,
359	                hyp.normal[2] * hyp.distance,
360	            );
361	            let normal = gp::Dir::new_real3(hyp.normal[0], hyp.normal[1], hyp.normal[2]);
362	            let plane = geom::Plane::new_pnt_dir(&origin, &normal);
363	            geom::Plane::to_handle(plane).to_handle_surface()
364	        }
365	        SelectedSurface::Conical(idx) => {
366	            let hyp = &output.conical_hypotheses[*idx];
367	            let dir = gp::Dir::new_real3(
368	                hyp.axis_direction[0],
369	                hyp.axis_direction[1],
370	                hyp.axis_direction[2],
371	            );
372	            if hyp.is_cylinder() {
373	                let origin = gp::Pnt::new_real3(hyp.apex[0], hyp.apex[1], hyp.apex[2]);
374	                let ax3 = gp::Ax3::new_pnt_dir(&origin, &dir);
375	                let cyl = geom::CylindricalSurface::new_ax3_real(&ax3, hyp.radius_at_apex);
376	                geom::CylindricalSurface::to_handle(cyl).to_handle_surface()
377	            } else {
378	                let origin = gp::Pnt::new_real3(hyp.apex[0], hyp.apex[1], hyp.apex[2]);
379	                let ax3 = gp::Ax3::new_pnt_dir(&origin, &dir);
380	                let cone = geom::ConicalSurface::new_ax3_real2(&ax3, hyp.half_angle, 0.0);
381	                geom::ConicalSurface::to_handle(cone).to_handle_surface()
382	            }
383	        }
384	        SelectedSurface::Spherical(idx) => {
385	            let hyp = &output.spherical_hypotheses[*idx];
386	            let origin = gp::Pnt::new_real3(hyp.center[0], hyp.center[1], hyp.center[2]);
387	            // Sphere axis direction is arbitrary; use Z-up
388	            let dir = gp::Dir::new_real3(0.0, 0.0, 1.0);
389	            let ax3 = gp::Ax3::new_pnt_dir(&origin, &dir);
390	            let sphere = geom::SphericalSurface::new_ax3_real(&ax3, hyp.radius);
391	            geom::SphericalSurface::to_handle(sphere).to_handle_surface()
392	        }
393	        SelectedSurface::Toroidal(idx) => {
394	            let hyp = &output.toroidal_hypotheses[*idx];
395	            let origin = gp::Pnt::new_real3(hyp.center[0], hyp.center[1], hyp.center[2]);
396	            let dir = gp::Dir::new_real3(
397	                hyp.axis_direction[0],
398	                hyp.axis_direction[1],
399	                hyp.axis_direction[2],
400	            );
401	            let ax3 = gp::Ax3::new_pnt_dir(&origin, &dir);
402	            let torus = geom::ToroidalSurface::new_ax3_real2(
403	                &ax3,
404	                hyp.major_radius,
405	                hyp.minor_radius,
406	            );
407	            geom::ToroidalSurface::to_handle(torus).to_handle_surface()
408	        }
409	    }
410	}

412	/// Get the faces belonging to a selected surface.
413	fn surface_faces<'a>(surface: &SelectedSurface, output: &'a Stage2Output) -> &'a [usize] {
414	    match surface {
415	        SelectedSurface::Planar(idx) => &output.planar_hypotheses[*idx].faces,
416	        SelectedSurface::Conical(idx) => &output.conical_hypotheses[*idx].faces,
417	        SelectedSurface::Spherical(idx) => &output.spherical_hypotheses[*idx].faces,
418	        SelectedSurface::Toroidal(idx) => &output.toroidal_hypotheses[*idx].faces,
419	    }
420	}
```

```
gp_Circ ElSLib::SphereUIso(const gp_Ax3& Pos, const Standard_Real Radius, const Standard_Real U)
{
  gp_Vec  dx = Pos.XDirection();
  gp_Vec  dy = Pos.YDirection();
  gp_Dir  dz = Pos.Direction();
  gp_Dir  cx = cos(U) * dx + sin(U) * dy;
  gp_Ax2  axes(Pos.Location(), cx.Crossed(dz), cx);
  gp_Circ Circ(axes, Radius);
  return Circ;
}
gp_Lin ElSLib::ConeUIso(const gp_Ax3&       Pos,
                        const Standard_Real Radius,
                        const Standard_Real SAngle,
                        const Standard_Real U)
{
  gp_Pnt P;
  gp_Vec DU, DV;
  ConeD1(U, 0, Pos, Radius, SAngle, P, DU, DV);
  gp_Lin L(P, DV);
  return L;
}
```

```
gp_Circ ElSLib::TorusUIso(const gp_Ax3&       Pos,
                          const Standard_Real MajorRadius,
                          const Standard_Real MinorRadius,
                          const Standard_Real U)
{
  gp_Vec dx = Pos.XDirection();
  gp_Vec dy = Pos.YDirection();
  gp_Dir dz = Pos.Direction();
  gp_Dir cx = cos(U) * dx + sin(U) * dy;
  gp_Ax2 axes(Pos.Location(), cx.Crossed(dz), cx);
  gp_Vec Ve = cx;
  Ve *= MajorRadius;
  axes.Translate(Ve);
  gp_Circ Circ(axes, MinorRadius);
  return Circ;
}
gp_Circ ElSLib::TorusVIso(const gp_Ax3&       Pos,
                          const Standard_Real MajorRadius,
                          const Standard_Real MinorRadius,
                          const Standard_Real V)
{
  gp_Ax3 axes = Pos.Ax2();
  gp_Vec Ve(Pos.Direction());
  Ve.Multiply(MinorRadius * sin(V));
  axes.Translate(Ve);
  Standard_Real R = MajorRadius + MinorRadius * cos(V);
  if (R < 0)
  {
    axes.XReverse();
    axes.YReverse();
    R = -R;
  }
  gp_Circ Circ(axes.Ax2(), R);
  return Circ;
}
gp_Lin ElSLib::CylinderUIso(const gp_Ax3& Pos, const Standard_Real Radius, const Standard_Real U)
{
  gp_Pnt P;
  gp_Vec DU, DV;
  CylinderD1(U, 0., Pos, Radius, P, DU, DV);
  gp_Lin L(P, DV);
  return L;
}
```

```
// ===========================================================================
// Stage 3.4: shared-edge topological assembly (DEVELOPMENT_PLAN §3.x)
//
// Every ReconEdge is exactly one TopoDS_Edge, shared by both adjacent faces.
// For each (edge, face) incidence a pcurve is computed from analytic UV
// coordinates and attached to the shared edge. UV poles (sphere pole, cone
// apex) become degenerate edges and periodic wraps become seam edges —
// first-class topology built by one uniform mechanism for every surface
// type. Faces and shells are assembled directly with BRep_Builder from the
// shared edges, so shells are closed by construction and
// BRepBuilderAPI_Sewing is not used for construction (stage 3.5 validates).
// ===========================================================================

/// Analytic parameterization chart of a face's surface. Mirrors the gp_Ax3
/// frame of the corresponding Geom surface, so UVs computed here agree
/// exactly with OCCT's parameterization of that surface.
struct SurfaceChart {
    origin: [f64; 3],
    x: [f64; 3],
    y: [f64; 3],
    z: [f64; 3],
    kind: ChartKind,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
enum ChartKind {
    Plane,
    Cylinder { radius: f64 },
    /// OCCT convention: apex at origin (reference radius 0), V is the slant
    /// distance from the apex along a generator. The apex is the V=0 pole.
    Cone { half_angle: f64 },
    /// V is latitude; poles at V = ±π/2.
    Sphere { radius: f64 },
    /// U around the main axis, V around the tube; doubly periodic.
    Torus { major_radius: f64, minor_radius: f64 },
}

const TWO_PI: f64 = 2.0 * std::f64::consts::PI;

fn dot3(a: &[f64; 3], b: &[f64; 3]) -> f64 {
    a[0] * b[0] + a[1] * b[1] + a[2] * b[2]
}

impl SurfaceChart {
    fn u_periodic(&self) -> bool {
        !matches!(self.kind, ChartKind::Plane)
    }

    fn v_periodic(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self.kind, ChartKind::Torus { .. })
    }

    /// Analytic (u, v) of a 3D point on (or near) the surface, plus the
    /// point's distance from the chart's U-degeneracy locus (pole): U is
    /// meaningless when that distance is ~0. u is reduced to [0, 2π) for
    /// periodic charts; v is reduced to [0, 2π) for the torus.
    fn point_uv(&self, p: &[f64; 3]) -> (f64, f64, f64) {
        let d = [p[0] - self.origin[0], p[1] - self.origin[1], p[2] - self.origin[2]];
        let dx = dot3(&d, &self.x);
        let dy = dot3(&d, &self.y);
        let dz = dot3(&d, &self.z);
        match self.kind {
            ChartKind::Plane => (dx, dy, f64::INFINITY),
            ChartKind::Cylinder { radius: _ } => {
                let rad = (dx * dx + dy * dy).sqrt();
                (dy.atan2(dx).rem_euclid(TWO_PI), dz, rad)
            }
            ChartKind::Cone { half_angle } => {
                let rad = (dx * dx + dy * dy).sqrt();
                (dy.atan2(dx).rem_euclid(TWO_PI), dz / half_angle.cos(), rad)
            }
            ChartKind::Sphere { radius } => {
                let rad = (dx * dx + dy * dy).sqrt();
                let v = (dz / radius).clamp(-1.0, 1.0).asin();
                (dy.atan2(dx).rem_euclid(TWO_PI), v, rad)
            }
            ChartKind::Torus { major_radius, minor_radius: _ } => {
                let rad = (dx * dx + dy * dy).sqrt();
                let v = dz.atan2(rad - major_radius).rem_euclid(TWO_PI);
                (dy.atan2(dx).rem_euclid(TWO_PI), v, rad)
            }
        }
    }

    /// Evaluate the surface at (u, v). Used for pcurve deviation checks.
    fn point_at(&self, u: f64, v: f64) -> [f64; 3] {
        let (cu, su) = (u.cos(), u.sin());
        let (rad, h) = match self.kind {
            ChartKind::Plane => {
                return [
                    self.origin[0] + u * self.x[0] + v * self.y[0],
                    self.origin[1] + u * self.x[1] + v * self.y[1],
                    self.origin[2] + u * self.x[2] + v * self.y[2],
                ];
            }
            ChartKind::Cylinder { radius } => (radius, v),
            ChartKind::Cone { half_angle } => (v * half_angle.sin(), v * half_angle.cos()),
            ChartKind::Sphere { radius } => (radius * v.cos(), radius * v.sin()),
            ChartKind::Torus { major_radius, minor_radius } => {
                (major_radius + minor_radius * v.cos(), minor_radius * v.sin())
            }
        };
        [
            self.origin[0] + rad * (cu * self.x[0] + su * self.y[0]) + h * self.z[0],
            self.origin[1] + rad * (cu * self.x[1] + su * self.y[1]) + h * self.z[1],
            self.origin[2] + rad * (cu * self.x[2] + su * self.y[2]) + h * self.z[2],
        ]
    }

    /// The V parameter and 3D position of this chart's pole on the given
    /// side (sign of V), if the surface has one there. Cones have a single
    /// pole (the apex, V=0); spheres have poles at V=±π/2.
    fn pole(&self, positive_v_side: bool) -> Option<(f64, [f64; 3])> {
        match self.kind {
            ChartKind::Cone { .. } => {
                // The apex (V=0) bounds the face from below only: our cone
                // axes point from apex toward the mesh, so faces live at V>0.
                if positive_v_side {
                    None
                } else {
                    Some((0.0, self.origin))
                }
            }
            ChartKind::Sphere { radius } => {
                let sign = if positive_v_side { 1.0 } else { -1.0 };
                let v = sign * std::f64::consts::FRAC_PI_2;
                Some((
                    v,
                    [
                        self.origin[0] + sign * radius * self.z[0],
                        self.origin[1] + sign * radius * self.z[1],
                        self.origin[2] + sign * radius * self.z[2],
                    ],
                ))
            }
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

/// Build the analytic chart for a face, together with a replacement OCCT
/// surface when the chart requires one (spheres are re-axised).
///
/// The sphere axis is a pure gauge choice — nothing in the B-rep depends on
/// it — so we point it at the mesh region's mean direction from the center.
/// This guarantees the region's boundary stays away from the UV poles: the
/// poles land either strictly inside the region (a polar cap, handled by a
/// degenerate pole edge) or strictly outside it. That one choice replaces
/// all of the old pole-proximity special cases.
fn build_face_chart(
    fd: &FaceDescriptor,
    stage2: &Stage2Output,
) -> (SurfaceChart, Option<OwnedPtr<geom::HandleGeomSurface>>) {
    let surface = &stage2.selected_surfaces[fd.selected_surface_idx];
    let ax3_frame = |origin: [f64; 3], dir: [f64; 3]| -> ([f64; 3], [f64; 3], [f64; 3]) {
        let o = gp::Pnt::new_real3(origin[0], origin[1], origin[2]);
        let d = gp::Dir::new_real3(dir[0], dir[1], dir[2]);
        let ax3 = gp::Ax3::new_pnt_dir(&o, &d);
        let x = ax3.x_direction();
        let y = ax3.y_direction();
        let z = ax3.direction();
        (
            [x.x(), x.y(), x.z()],
            [y.x(), y.y(), y.z()],
            [z.x(), z.y(), z.z()],
        )
    };
    match surface {
        SelectedSurface::Planar(idx) => {
            let hyp = &stage2.planar_hypotheses[*idx];
            let origin = [
                hyp.normal[0] * hyp.distance,
                hyp.normal[1] * hyp.distance,
                hyp.normal[2] * hyp.distance,
            ];
            let (x, y, z) = ax3_frame(origin, hyp.normal);
            (SurfaceChart { origin, x, y, z, kind: ChartKind::Plane }, None)
        }
        SelectedSurface::Conical(idx) => {
            let hyp = &stage2.conical_hypotheses[*idx];
            let (x, y, z) = ax3_frame(hyp.apex, hyp.axis_direction);
            let kind = if hyp.is_cylinder() {
                ChartKind::Cylinder { radius: hyp.radius_at_apex }
            } else {
                ChartKind::Cone { half_angle: hyp.half_angle }
            };
            (SurfaceChart { origin: hyp.apex, x, y, z, kind }, None)
        }
        SelectedSurface::Spherical(idx) => {
            let hyp = &stage2.spherical_hypotheses[*idx];
            // Mean direction of the region's mesh face centroids from the
            // sphere center (deterministic: hyp.faces order is stable).
            let mut mean = [0.0_f64; 3];
            for &mfi in &hyp.faces {
                let c = compute_mesh_face_centroid(mfi, &stage2.mesh);
                let d = [c[0] - hyp.center[0], c[1] - hyp.center[1], c[2] - hyp.center[2]];
                let len = dot3(&d, &d).sqrt();
                if len > 1e-12 {
                    mean[0] += d[0] / len;
                    mean[1] += d[1] / len;
                    mean[2] += d[2] / len;
                }
            }
            let len = dot3(&mean, &mean).sqrt();
            let axis = if len > 1e-9 {
                [mean[0] / len, mean[1] / len, mean[2] / len]
            } else {
                [0.0, 0.0, 1.0] // full sphere: any axis works
            };
            let (x, y, z) = ax3_frame(hyp.center, axis);
            let origin = gp::Pnt::new_real3(hyp.center[0], hyp.center[1], hyp.center[2]);
            let dir = gp::Dir::new_real3(axis[0], axis[1], axis[2]);
            let ax3 = gp::Ax3::new_pnt_dir(&origin, &dir);
            let sphere = geom::SphericalSurface::new_ax3_real(&ax3, hyp.radius);
            let handle = geom::SphericalSurface::to_handle(sphere).to_handle_surface();
            (
                SurfaceChart {
                    origin: hyp.center,
                    x,
                    y,
                    z,
                    kind: ChartKind::Sphere { radius: hyp.radius },
                },
                Some(handle),
            )
        }
        SelectedSurface::Toroidal(idx) => {
            let hyp = &stage2.toroidal_hypotheses[*idx];
            let (x, y, z) = ax3_frame(hyp.center, hyp.axis_direction);
            (
                SurfaceChart {
                    origin: hyp.center,
                    x,
                    y,
                    z,
                    kind: ChartKind::Torus {
                        major_radius: hyp.major_radius,
                        minor_radius: hyp.minor_radius,
                    },
                },
                None,
            )
        }
    }
}

/// UV samples of one edge on one face's chart: ascending edge parameter,
/// U (and V for tori) branch-continuous within the edge, and pole-degenerate
/// U values backfilled from the nearest well-defined sample.
struct EdgeUv {
    ts: Vec<f64>,
    us: Vec<f64>,
    vs: Vec<f64>,
    /// Whether the first/last sample sits at a U pole (U meaningless there).
    start_at_pole: bool,
    end_at_pole: bool,
}

impl EdgeUv {
    fn first_uv(&self) -> (f64, f64) {
        (self.us[0], self.vs[0])
    }
    fn last_uv(&self) -> (f64, f64) {
        (*self.us.last().unwrap(), *self.vs.last().unwrap())
    }
}

/// Sample an edge's stored 3D curve over its stored parameter range and map
/// the points through the chart. Returns None for edges without a 3D curve.
fn sample_edge_uv(
    edge: &topo_ds::Edge,
    chart: &SurfaceChart,
    n: usize,
    pole_eps: f64,
) -> Option<EdgeUv> {
    let mut first = 0.0;
    let mut last = 0.0;
    let curve = b_rep::Tool::curve_edge_real2(edge, &mut first, &mut last);
    if curve.is_null() {
        return None;
    }
    let c = curve.get();
    let mut ts = Vec::with_capacity(n);
    let mut raw: Vec<(f64, f64, f64)> = Vec::with_capacity(n); // (u, v, radial)
    for i in 0..n {
        let t = first + (last - first) * (i as f64) / ((n - 1) as f64);
        let pt = c.value(t);
        let (u, v, rad) = chart.point_uv(&[pt.x(), pt.y(), pt.z()]);
        ts.push(t);
        raw.push((u, v, rad));
    }
    // Backfill pole-degenerate U values and unwrap U (and torus V) so the
    // samples are branch-continuous along the edge.
    let good = |i: usize| raw[i].2 >= pole_eps;
    let first_good = (0..raw.len()).find(|&i| good(i))?;
    let mut us = vec![0.0; raw.len()];
    let mut vs = vec![0.0; raw.len()];
    let mut prev_u = raw[first_good].0;
    for i in 0..raw.len() {
        let u = if good(i) {
            let mut u = raw[i].0;
            u -= TWO_PI * ((u - prev_u) / TWO_PI).round();
            prev_u = u;
            u
        } else {
            prev_u
        };
        us[i] = u;
    }
    // Leading pole samples take the first good sample's (unwrapped) U.
    for i in 0..first_good {
        us[i] = us[first_good];
    }
    let mut prev_v = raw[0].1;
    for i in 0..raw.len() {
        let mut v = raw[i].1;
        if chart.v_periodic() {
            v -= TWO_PI * ((v - prev_v) / TWO_PI).round();
        }
        prev_v = v;
        vs[i] = v;
    }
    let start_at_pole = !good(0);
    let end_at_pole = !good(raw.len() - 1);
    Some(EdgeUv { ts, us, vs, start_at_pole, end_at_pole })
}

/// One edge occurrence in a face boundary loop, in traversal order.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
struct LoopItem {
    /// ReconEdge index.
    ei: usize,
    /// True when the loop traverses the edge in increasing parameter.
    forward: bool,
}

/// A face boundary loop with branch-aligned UV data.
struct BoundaryLoop {
    items: Vec<LoopItem>,
    /// Per item: (u_offset, v_offset) — multiples of 2π added to the edge's
    /// canonical samples to make the loop branch-continuous.
    offsets: Vec<(f64, f64)>,
    /// Net winding around the periodic directions (±1 wraps, 0 plain).
    winding_u: i32,
    winding_v: i32,
    /// U jumps across poles between item j and item j+1 (cyclic): the loop
    /// passes through a pole vertex there and needs a degenerate edge.
    pole_gaps: Vec<PoleGap>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
struct PoleGap {
    /// The gap follows this item index (cyclic).
    after_item: usize,
    u_from: f64,
    u_to: f64,
    /// True when the pole is on the positive-V side of the chart.
    positive_v_side: bool,
}

/// Order the edges of one vertex-connectivity group into a traversal cycle.
fn order_loop(
    group: &[usize],
    edge_vertices: &[[usize; 2]],
) -> Result<Vec<LoopItem>, Stage3Error> {
    if group.len() == 1 {
        return Ok(vec![LoopItem { ei: group[0], forward: true }]);
    }
    let mut items = Vec::with_capacity(group.len());
    let mut used = vec![false; group.len()];
    items.push(LoopItem { ei: group[0], forward: true });
    used[0] = true;
    let start_v = edge_vertices[group[0]][0];
    let mut cur_v = edge_vertices[group[0]][1];
    while items.len() < group.len() {
        let mut advanced = false;
        for (gi, &ei) in group.iter().enumerate() {
            if used[gi] {
                continue;
            }
            let [v0, v1] = edge_vertices[ei];
            if v0 == cur_v {
                items.push(LoopItem { ei, forward: true });
                cur_v = v1;
            } else if v1 == cur_v {
                items.push(LoopItem { ei, forward: false });
                cur_v = v0;
            } else {
                continue;
            }
            used[gi] = true;
            advanced = true;
            break;
        }
        if !advanced {
            return Err(Stage3Error::AdjacencyError(format!(
                "boundary loop is not vertex-connected (edges {group:?})"
            )));
        }
    }
    if cur_v != start_v {
        return Err(Stage3Error::AdjacencyError(format!(
            "boundary loop does not close (edges {group:?})"
        )));
    }
    Ok(items)
}

/// Branch-align a walked loop: choose per-item 2π offsets so consecutive
/// item endpoints agree in UV, detect pole gaps, and compute the winding.
fn align_loop(
    items: Vec<LoopItem>,
    samples: &HashMap<usize, EdgeUv>,
    chart: &SurfaceChart,
) -> Result<BoundaryLoop, Stage3Error> {
    let n = items.len();
    let mut offsets = vec![(0.0, 0.0); n];
    let mut pole_gaps: Vec<PoleGap> = Vec::new();

    // Traversal-order endpoints of item i with its offset applied.
    let ends = |item: &LoopItem, off: (f64, f64)| -> ((f64, f64), (f64, f64), bool, bool) {
        let s = &samples[&item.ei];
        let (a, b) = (s.first_uv(), s.last_uv());
        let (start, end, sp, ep) = if item.forward {
            (a, b, s.start_at_pole, s.end_at_pole)
        } else {
            (b, a, s.end_at_pole, s.start_at_pole)
        };
        (
            (start.0 + off.0, start.1 + off.1),
            (end.0 + off.0, end.1 + off.1),
            sp,
            ep,
        )
    };

    for i in 1..n {
        let (_, prev_end, _, prev_end_pole) = ends(&items[i - 1], offsets[i - 1]);
        let (cur_start, _, cur_start_pole, _) = ends(&items[i], (0.0, 0.0));
        let mut du = 0.0;
        let mut dv = 0.0;
        if chart.u_periodic() {
            du = TWO_PI * ((prev_end.0 - cur_start.0) / TWO_PI).round();
        }
        if chart.v_periodic() {
            dv = TWO_PI * ((prev_end.1 - cur_start.1) / TWO_PI).round();
        }
        offsets[i] = (du, dv);
        if prev_end_pole && cur_start_pole {
            // The junction vertex is a pole: U legitimately jumps there.
            let (cs, _, _, _) = ends(&items[i], offsets[i]);
            if (cs.0 - prev_end.0).abs() > 1e-6 {
                pole_gaps.push(PoleGap {
                    after_item: i - 1,
                    u_from: prev_end.0,
                    u_to: cs.0,
                    positive_v_side: prev_end.1 > 0.0,
                });
            }
        }
    }

    // Winding: net change over the full cycle, including the closing junction.
    let (first_start, _, first_start_pole, _) = ends(&items[0], offsets[0]);
    let (_, last_end, _, last_end_pole) = ends(&items[n - 1], offsets[n - 1]);
    let mut wu = 0i32;
    let mut wv = 0i32;
    if chart.u_periodic() {
        if last_end_pole && first_start_pole {
            if (last_end.0 - first_start.0).abs() > 1e-6 {
                pole_gaps.push(PoleGap {
                    after_item: n - 1,
                    u_from: last_end.0,
                    u_to: first_start.0,
                    positive_v_side: last_end.1 > 0.0,
                });
            }
        } else {
            wu = ((last_end.0 - first_start.0) / TWO_PI).round() as i32;
        }
    }
    if chart.v_periodic() {
        wv = ((last_end.1 - first_start.1) / TWO_PI).round() as i32;
    }
    Ok(BoundaryLoop { items, offsets, winding_u: wu, winding_v: wv, pole_gaps })
}
```

```
/// Which periodic direction (if any) a face's boundary wraps all the way
/// around, requiring a seam edge.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
enum WrapKind {
    None,
    U,
    V,
}

/// How the seam endpoint on a winding boundary loop is realized.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
enum AnchorSource {
    /// An existing shared BRepVertex (index into Stage3Output.vertices).
    Vertex(usize),
    /// A closed-loop edge re-ranged to start at the seam; the anchor vertex
    /// lives in AssemblyCtx.closed_anchors under this edge id.
    ClosedEdge(usize),
}

/// Per-face seam plan: one anchor per winding boundary loop, in the face's
/// deterministic loop-scan order.
struct WrapPlan {
    kind: WrapKind,
    anchors: Vec<AnchorSource>,
}

/// Shared assembly state for stage 3.4.
struct AssemblyCtx {
    topo_vertices: Vec<OwnedPtr<topo_ds::Vertex>>,
    topo_edges: Vec<OwnedPtr<topo_ds::Edge>>,
    /// BRepVertex ids [start, end] of each edge in stored-curve direction
    /// (both usize::MAX for closed-loop edges).
    edge_vertices: Vec<[usize; 2]>,
    /// Seam-anchor vertices added to re-ranged closed-loop edges.
    closed_anchors: HashMap<usize, OwnedPtr<topo_ds::Vertex>>,
}

/// Pole-detection radius: below this distance from the chart's degeneracy
/// locus, a sample's U coordinate is treated as meaningless.
fn pole_radius_eps(config: &Config) -> f64 {
    (10.0 * config.vertex_tolerance_mm).max(1e-6)
}

/// Number of samples per edge for UV analysis and pcurve interpolation.
const PCURVE_BASE_SAMPLES: usize = 33;

/// Scan of one face's boundary in UV: chart, per-edge samples, aligned
/// loops, and the wrap classification.
struct FaceScan {
    chart: SurfaceChart,
    surface_override: Option<OwnedPtr<geom::HandleGeomSurface>>,
    samples: HashMap<usize, EdgeUv>,
    loops: Vec<BoundaryLoop>,
    wrap: WrapKind,
}

fn scan_face(
    fi: usize,
    output: &Stage3Output,
    ctx: &AssemblyCtx,
    config: &Config,
) -> Result<FaceScan, Stage3Error> {
    let fd = &output.face_descriptors[fi];
    let (chart, surface_override) = build_face_chart(fd, &output.stage2);
    let pole_eps = pole_radius_eps(config);

    let mut samples = HashMap::new();
    for &ei in &fd.edge_indices {
        let uv = sample_edge_uv(&ctx.topo_edges[ei], &chart, PCURVE_BASE_SAMPLES, pole_eps)
            .ok_or_else(|| {
                Stage3Error::AdjacencyError(format!(
                    "face {fi}: edge {ei} has no stored 3D curve to project"
                ))
            })?;
        samples.insert(ei, uv);
    }

    let groups = group_edges_into_wires(fd, &output.edges);
    let mut loops = Vec::with_capacity(groups.len());
    for group in &groups {
        let items = order_loop(group, &ctx.edge_vertices)?;
        loops.push(align_loop(items, &samples, &chart)?);
    }

    let mut wrap = WrapKind::None;
    for lp in &loops {
        if lp.winding_u != 0 && lp.winding_v != 0 {
            return Err(Stage3Error::AdjacencyError(format!(
                "face {fi}: boundary loop winds both U and V (unsupported)"
            )));
        }
        if lp.winding_u != 0 {
            if wrap == WrapKind::V {
                return Err(Stage3Error::AdjacencyError(format!(
                    "face {fi}: boundary loops wind both U and V (unsupported)"
                )));
            }
            wrap = WrapKind::U;
        }
        if lp.winding_v != 0 {
            if wrap == WrapKind::U {
                return Err(Stage3Error::AdjacencyError(format!(
                    "face {fi}: boundary loops wind both U and V (unsupported)"
                )));
            }
            wrap = WrapKind::V;
        }
    }
    let n_winding = loops
        .iter()
        .filter(|l| l.winding_u != 0 || l.winding_v != 0)
        .count();
    if n_winding > 2 {
        return Err(Stage3Error::AdjacencyError(format!(
            "face {fi}: {n_winding} winding boundary loops (at most 2 supported)"
        )));
    }
    Ok(FaceScan { chart, surface_override, samples, loops, wrap })
}

/// The wrap-direction coordinate of a 3D point on a face's chart (U for
/// U-wrapped faces, V for V-wrapped), reduced mod 2π.
fn wrap_coord(chart: &SurfaceChart, kind: WrapKind, p: &[f64; 3]) -> f64 {
    let (u, v, _) = chart.point_uv(p);
    match kind {
        WrapKind::V => v.rem_euclid(TWO_PI),
        _ => u,
    }
}

/// Congruence distance of two angles mod 2π.
fn angle_dist(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    let d = (a - b).rem_euclid(TWO_PI);
    d.min(TWO_PI - d)
}

/// Choose seam anchors for every wrapped face, mutating closed-loop edges:
/// each re-anchored closed edge is rebuilt to start at its anchor point and
/// gains the anchor vertex at both ends. Because the anchor vertex is part
/// of the shared edge, every face using that edge sees the same anchor —
/// consistency across faces is forced by the sharing, not by tolerances.
fn plan_seam_anchors(
    output: &Stage3Output,
    scans: &[Option<FaceScan>],
    ctx: &mut AssemblyCtx,
    config: &Config,
) -> Result<HashMap<usize, WrapPlan>, Stage3Error> {
    // Committed anchor parameter per closed-loop edge.
    let mut anchor_t: HashMap<usize, f64> = HashMap::new();
    let mut plans: HashMap<usize, WrapPlan> = HashMap::new();

    // The anchor point of a winding loop, if already determined.
    let anchor_point = |src: &AnchorSource, anchor_t: &HashMap<usize, f64>| -> Option<[f64; 3]> {
        match src {
            AnchorSource::Vertex(vid) => Some(output.vertices[*vid].point),
            AnchorSource::ClosedEdge(ei) => anchor_t.get(ei).map(|&t| {
                let mut f = 0.0;
                let mut l = 0.0;
                let curve = b_rep::Tool::curve_edge_real2(&ctx.topo_edges[*ei], &mut f, &mut l);
                let p = curve.get().value(t);
                [p.x(), p.y(), p.z()]
            }),
        }
    };

    // A winding loop's natural anchor source: a real vertex when the loop
    // has one (lowest id for determinism), else its single closed edge.
    let loop_anchor_source = |lp: &BoundaryLoop| -> Result<AnchorSource, Stage3Error> {
        let mut best: Option<usize> = None;
        for item in &lp.items {
            for &vid in &ctx.edge_vertices[item.ei] {
                if vid != usize::MAX && best.is_none_or(|b| vid < b) {
                    best = Some(vid);
                }
            }
        }
        if let Some(vid) = best {
            return Ok(AnchorSource::Vertex(vid));
        }
        if lp.items.len() == 1 {
            return Ok(AnchorSource::ClosedEdge(lp.items[0].ei));
        }
        Err(Stage3Error::AdjacencyError(
            "winding boundary loop has multiple edges but no vertices".into(),
        ))
    };

    // Find the parameter on a closed edge where the wrap coordinate equals
    // `target` (mod 2π), by bisection on the branch-continuous samples.
    let solve_anchor_t = |ei: usize,
                          uv: &EdgeUv,
                          chart: &SurfaceChart,
                          kind: WrapKind,
                          target: f64|
     -> Result<f64, Stage3Error> {
        let coords = match kind {
            WrapKind::V => &uv.vs,
            _ => &uv.us,
        };
        // Lift target into the samples' branch range.
        let (lo, hi) = (coords[0].min(*coords.last().unwrap()), coords[0].max(*coords.last().unwrap()));
        let mut tgt = target;
        while tgt < lo {
            tgt += TWO_PI;
        }
        while tgt > hi {
            tgt -= TWO_PI;
        }
        if tgt < lo - 1e-9 {
            return Err(Stage3Error::AdjacencyError(format!(
                "edge {ei}: seam azimuth not reachable on closed loop"
            )));
        }
        let k = (0..coords.len() - 1)
            .find(|&i| (coords[i] - tgt) * (coords[i + 1] - tgt) <= 0.0)
            .ok_or_else(|| {
                Stage3Error::AdjacencyError(format!(
                    "edge {ei}: seam azimuth not bracketed on closed loop"
                ))
            })?;
        let mut f = 0.0;
        let mut l = 0.0;
        let curve = b_rep::Tool::curve_edge_real2(&ctx.topo_edges[ei], &mut f, &mut l);
        let c = curve.get();
        let (mut ta, mut tb) = (uv.ts[k], uv.ts[k + 1]);
        let (mut ca, _cb) = (coords[k], coords[k + 1]);
        for _ in 0..60 {
            let tm = 0.5 * (ta + tb);
            let pt = c.value(tm);
            let raw = wrap_coord(chart, kind, &[pt.x(), pt.y(), pt.z()]);
            // Lift onto the local branch near ca.
            let cm = raw - TWO_PI * ((raw - ca) / TWO_PI).round();
            if (cm - tgt) * (ca - tgt) <= 0.0 {
                tb = tm;
            } else {
                ta = tm;
                ca = cm;
            }
        }
        Ok(0.5 * (ta + tb))
    };

    // Fixpoint: plan faces that already have a determined anchor first, so
    // chains of wrapped faces adopt a single consistent seam azimuth.
    let wrapped: Vec<usize> = scans
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .filter(|(_, s)| s.as_ref().is_some_and(|s| s.wrap != WrapKind::None))
        .map(|(fi, _)| fi)
        .collect();
    let mut pending: Vec<usize> = wrapped.clone();
    while !pending.is_empty() {
        let mut planned_one = false;
        // Two rounds: first faces with a determined anchor, then (if none
        // progressed) force the lowest-index pending face with defaults.
        for force in [false, true] {
            let mut i = 0;
            while i < pending.len() {
                let fi = pending[i];
                let scan = scans[fi].as_ref().unwrap();
                let winding: Vec<&BoundaryLoop> = scan
                    .loops
                    .iter()
                    .filter(|l| l.winding_u != 0 || l.winding_v != 0)
                    .collect();
                let sources: Vec<AnchorSource> = winding
                    .iter()
                    .map(|lp| loop_anchor_source(lp))
                    .collect::<Result<_, _>>()?;
                let det: Vec<Option<[f64; 3]>> =
                    sources.iter().map(|s| anchor_point(s, &anchor_t)).collect();
                if !force && det.iter().all(|d| d.is_none()) {
                    i += 1;
                    continue;
                }
                // Seam azimuth from the first determined anchor, or commit
                // the first loop's default anchor.
                let seam_c = if let Some(p) = det.iter().flatten().next() {
                    wrap_coord(&scan.chart, scan.wrap, p)
                } else {
                    match sources[0] {
                        AnchorSource::ClosedEdge(ei) => {
                            let uv = &scan.samples[&ei];
                            anchor_t.insert(ei, uv.ts[0]);
                            match scan.wrap {
                                WrapKind::V => uv.vs[0].rem_euclid(TWO_PI),
                                _ => uv.us[0].rem_euclid(TWO_PI),
                            }
                        }
                        AnchorSource::Vertex(_) => unreachable!("vertex anchors are always determined"),
                    }
                };
                for (li, lp) in winding.iter().enumerate() {
                    match det[li] {
                        Some(p) => {
                            let c = wrap_coord(&scan.chart, scan.wrap, &p);
                            if angle_dist(c, seam_c) > 0.01 {
                                return Err(Stage3Error::AdjacencyError(format!(
                                    "face {fi}: winding loops have incompatible seam anchors \
                                     ({c:.4} vs {seam_c:.4} rad); edge splitting not implemented"
                                )));
                            }
                        }
                        None => {
                            let AnchorSource::ClosedEdge(ei) = sources[li] else {
                                unreachable!("vertex anchors are always determined")
                            };
                            let t = solve_anchor_t(ei, &scan.samples[&ei], &scan.chart, scan.wrap, seam_c)?;
                            anchor_t.insert(ei, t);
                        }
                    }
                }
                plans.insert(fi, WrapPlan { kind: scan.wrap, anchors: sources });
                pending.remove(i);
                planned_one = true;
                if force {
                    break; // re-enter the determined-anchor round
                }
            }
            if planned_one {
                break;
            }
        }
        if !planned_one {
            break;
        }
    }

    // Apply the committed anchors: rebuild each re-anchored closed edge so
    // its range starts at the anchor and the anchor vertex is at both ends.
    let builder = b_rep::Builder::new();
    let mut anchor_edges: Vec<(usize, f64)> = anchor_t.into_iter().collect();
    anchor_edges.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.cmp(&b.0));
    for (ei, t) in anchor_edges {
        let mut f = 0.0;
        let mut l = 0.0;
        let curve = b_rep::Tool::curve_edge_real2(&ctx.topo_edges[ei], &mut f, &mut l);
        let period = l - f;
        let t = if !curve.get().is_periodic() && (t - f).abs() > 1e-12 {
            if !config.quiet {
                eprintln!(
                    "  Warning: edge {ei}: closed curve is not periodic; keeping its \
                     existing start as the seam anchor"
                );
            }
            f
        } else {
            t
        };
        let p = curve.get().value(t);
        let mut mv = b_rep_builder_api::MakeVertex::new_pnt(&p);
        let vtx = mv.vertex().to_owned();
        builder.update_vertex_vertex_real(&vtx, config.vertex_tolerance_mm);
        let make_edge = b_rep_builder_api::MakeEdge::new_handlegeomcurve_vertex2_real2(
            &curve, &vtx, &vtx, t, t + period,
        );
        if !make_edge.is_done() {
            return Err(Stage3Error::AdjacencyError(format!(
                "MakeEdge failed while re-anchoring closed edge {ei}: {:?}",
                make_edge.error(),
            )));
        }
        let mut make_edge = make_edge;
        ctx.topo_edges[ei] = make_edge.edge().to_owned();
        ctx.closed_anchors.insert(ei, vtx);
    }

    Ok(plans)
}

/// Circular window over values mod 2π: the arc complementary to the largest
/// gap between consecutive values, flipped to its complement when a majority
/// of `interior` values (mod 2π) fall outside it. Returns (lo, hi) with
/// lo ∈ [0, 2π) and lo ≤ hi ≤ lo + 2π.
fn circular_window(values: &[f64], interior: &[f64]) -> (f64, f64) {
    let mut sorted: Vec<f64> = values.iter().map(|v| v.rem_euclid(TWO_PI)).collect();
    sorted.sort_by(|a, b| a.partial_cmp(b).unwrap());
    sorted.dedup_by(|a, b| (*a - *b).abs() < 1e-10);
    if sorted.is_empty() {
        return (0.0, TWO_PI);
    }
    if sorted.len() == 1 {
        return (sorted[0], sorted[0]);
    }
    let mut max_gap = 0.0_f64;
    let mut gap_end = 0;
    for i in 0..sorted.len() {
        let next = (i + 1) % sorted.len();
        let gap = if next > i {
            sorted[next] - sorted[i]
        } else {
            sorted[next] + TWO_PI - sorted[i]
        };
        if gap > max_gap {
            max_gap = gap;
            gap_end = next;
        }
    }
    let gap_start = if gap_end == 0 { sorted.len() - 1 } else { gap_end - 1 };
    let lo = sorted[gap_end];
    let mut hi = sorted[gap_start];
    if hi < lo {
        hi += TWO_PI;
    }
    if !interior.is_empty() {
        let tol = 0.1;
        let inside = |x: f64| -> bool {
            let xx = lo + (x - lo).rem_euclid(TWO_PI);
            xx <= hi + tol || xx >= lo + TWO_PI - tol
        };
        let n_in = interior.iter().filter(|&&x| inside(x)).count();
        if 2 * n_in < interior.len() {
            let new_lo = hi.rem_euclid(TWO_PI);
            let mut new_hi = lo.rem_euclid(TWO_PI);
            if new_hi < new_lo {
                new_hi += TWO_PI;
            }
            return (new_lo, new_hi);
        }
    }
    (lo, hi)
}

/// Winding number of a closed polygon around a point (crossing count).
fn winding_number(poly: &[(f64, f64)], p: (f64, f64)) -> i32 {
    let mut w = 0i32;
    for i in 0..poly.len() {
        let a = poly[i];
        let b = poly[(i + 1) % poly.len()];
        if a.1 <= p.1 {
            if b.1 > p.1 && cross_z(a, b, p) > 0.0 {
                w += 1;
            }
        } else if b.1 <= p.1 && cross_z(a, b, p) < 0.0 {
            w -= 1;
        }
    }
    w
}

fn cross_z(a: (f64, f64), b: (f64, f64), p: (f64, f64)) -> f64 {
```
