```
/// Create OCCT faces for all face descriptors (stage 3.4 main entry).
///
/// Shared-edge topological assembly: one TopoDS_Vertex per BRepVertex, one
/// TopoDS_Edge per ReconEdge, pcurves attached to the shared edges for both
/// adjacent faces, seam and degenerate edges as first-class topology, and
/// faces built directly with BRep_Builder (see DEVELOPMENT_PLAN §3.x).
fn create_occt_faces_all(
    mut output: Stage3Output,
    config: &Config,
    viz: Option<&crate::viz::VizSender>,
) -> Result<Stage3Output, Stage3Error> {
    let t = Instant::now();
    let num_faces = output.face_descriptors.len();

    // 1. Create shared TopoDS_Vertex for each BRepVertex.
    // Set tolerance to vertex_tolerance_mm so that mesh vertex positions
    // (which may deviate slightly from fitted analytical surfaces) are accepted
    // by MakeEdge when projecting vertices onto edge curves.
    let builder = b_rep::Builder::new();
    let topo_vertices: Vec<OwnedPtr<topo_ds::Vertex>> = output
        .vertices
        .iter()
        .map(|v| {
            let pt = gp::Pnt::new_real3(v.point[0], v.point[1], v.point[2]);
            let mut mv = b_rep_builder_api::MakeVertex::new_pnt(&pt);
            let vtx = mv.vertex().to_owned();
            builder.update_vertex_vertex_real(&vtx, config.vertex_tolerance_mm);
            vtx
        })
        .collect();

    // 2. Create one shared TopoDS_Edge per ReconEdge.
    let mut topo_edges: Vec<OwnedPtr<topo_ds::Edge>> = Vec::with_capacity(output.edges.len());
    // BRepVertex ids at each edge's curve start/end (stored-curve direction).
    let mut edge_vertices: Vec<[usize; 2]> = Vec::with_capacity(output.edges.len());
    for (ei, edge) in output.edges.iter().enumerate() {
        let curve = match edge.curve_3d.as_ref() {
            Some(c) => c,
            None => {
                // No intersection curve — create a straight-line edge between endpoints
                if edge.vertex_indices[0] != usize::MAX && edge.vertex_indices[1] != usize::MAX {
                    let mut make_edge = b_rep_builder_api::MakeEdge::new_vertex2(
                        &topo_vertices[edge.vertex_indices[0]],
                        &topo_vertices[edge.vertex_indices[1]],
                    );
                    if !make_edge.is_done() {
                        return Err(Stage3Error::AdjacencyError(format!(
                            "Edge {ei}: straight-line fallback failed ({:?}), faces [{}, {}]",
                            make_edge.error(),
                            edge.face_indices[0],
                            edge.face_indices[1]
                        )));
                    }
                    if !config.quiet {
                        eprintln!(
                            "  Edge {ei}: using straight-line fallback (no intersection curve)"
                        );
                    }
                    topo_edges.push(make_edge.edge().to_owned());
                    edge_vertices.push([edge.vertex_indices[0], edge.vertex_indices[1]]);
                } else {
                    return Err(Stage3Error::AdjacencyError(format!(
                        "Edge {ei}: no curve and no vertex endpoints"
                    )));
                }
                continue;
            }
        };
        let (mut make_edge, verts) = if edge.vertex_indices[0] != usize::MAX
            && edge.vertex_indices[1] != usize::MAX
        {
            // Both endpoints have shared vertices — create edge with explicit vertex topology.
            // For periodic curves (circles), MakeEdge strips the TrimmedCurve and uses
            // AdjustPeriodic which forces p1 < p2, always taking the forward arc from V1
            // to V2. We must ensure V1 corresponds to the curve's first_parameter and V2
            // to last_parameter, otherwise MakeEdge will select the complementary arc.
            let c = curve.get();
            let p_start = c.value(c.first_parameter());
            let v0_pt = &output.vertices[edge.vertex_indices[0]].point;
            let v1_pt = &output.vertices[edge.vertex_indices[1]].point;
            let d0_start = (v0_pt[0] - p_start.x()).powi(2)
                + (v0_pt[1] - p_start.y()).powi(2)
                + (v0_pt[2] - p_start.z()).powi(2);
            let d1_start = (v1_pt[0] - p_start.x()).powi(2)
                + (v1_pt[1] - p_start.y()).powi(2)
                + (v1_pt[2] - p_start.z()).powi(2);
            let (vi0, vi1) = if d0_start <= d1_start {
                (edge.vertex_indices[0], edge.vertex_indices[1])
            } else {
                (edge.vertex_indices[1], edge.vertex_indices[0])
            };
            // Use explicit parameter values to avoid OCCT's vertex-to-curve projection,
            // which can fail when vertex tolerance exceeds default precision.
            // vi0 is always the vertex closest to the curve start, vi1 closest to end,
            // so parameters are always (first_parameter, last_parameter).
            let fp = c.first_parameter();
            let lp = c.last_parameter();

            // Update vertex tolerances to accommodate curve-vertex distance.
            // Imprecisely-fitted surfaces produce intersection curves that may not
            // pass exactly through mesh vertex positions.
            let p_fp = c.value(fp);
            let p_lp = c.value(lp);
            let v0_pt = &output.vertices[vi0].point;
            let v1_pt = &output.vertices[vi1].point;
            let d0 = ((v0_pt[0] - p_fp.x()).powi(2)
                + (v0_pt[1] - p_fp.y()).powi(2)
                + (v0_pt[2] - p_fp.z()).powi(2))
            .sqrt();
            let d1 = ((v1_pt[0] - p_lp.x()).powi(2)
                + (v1_pt[1] - p_lp.y()).powi(2)
                + (v1_pt[2] - p_lp.z()).powi(2))
            .sqrt();
            let min_tol = config.vertex_tolerance_mm;
            let tol0 = d0.max(min_tol) * 1.01; // 1% margin
            let tol1 = d1.max(min_tol) * 1.01;
            builder.update_vertex_vertex_real(&topo_vertices[vi0], tol0);
            builder.update_vertex_vertex_real(&topo_vertices[vi1], tol1);

            (
                b_rep_builder_api::MakeEdge::new_handlegeomcurve_vertex2_real2(
                    curve,
                    &topo_vertices[vi0],
                    &topo_vertices[vi1],
                    fp,
                    lp,
                ),
                [vi0, vi1],
            )
        } else {
            // Closed-loop edge (no vertex endpoints) — create without vertices
            (
                b_rep_builder_api::MakeEdge::new_handlegeomcurve(curve),
                [usize::MAX, usize::MAX],
            )
        };
        if !make_edge.is_done() {
            return Err(Stage3Error::AdjacencyError(format!(
                "MakeEdge failed for edge {ei}: {:?}",
                make_edge.error(),
            )));
        }
        topo_edges.push(make_edge.edge().to_owned());
        edge_vertices.push(verts);
    }

    let mut ctx = AssemblyCtx {
        topo_vertices,
        topo_edges,
        edge_vertices,
        closed_anchors: HashMap::new(),
    };

    // 3. Scan every face's boundary in UV, then choose seam anchors for the
    // wrapped faces (re-anchoring closed-loop edges so seam endpoints are
    // shared vertices of the shared edges).
    let mut scans: Vec<Option<FaceScan>> = Vec::with_capacity(num_faces);
    for fi in 0..num_faces {
        if output.face_descriptors[fi].edge_indices.is_empty() {
            scans.push(None);
        } else {
            scans.push(Some(scan_face(fi, &output, &ctx, config)?));
        }
    }
    let plans = plan_seam_anchors(&output, &scans, &mut ctx, config)?;
    drop(scans); // re-anchoring invalidated closed-edge samples

    // 4. Assemble each face from the shared edges.
    let mut faces: Vec<OwnedPtr<topo_ds::Face>> = Vec::with_capacity(num_faces);
    let mut concave_faces: Vec<bool> = vec![false; num_faces];
    let mut all_edge_pcurves: Vec<(usize, usize, OwnedPtr<geom2d::HandleGeom2dCurve>)> =
        Vec::new();
    let mut all_vertex_uvs: Vec<Vec<(usize, (f64, f64))>> = vec![Vec::new(); num_faces];

    for fi in 0..num_faces {
        let fd = &output.face_descriptors[fi];
        let surface_type = &output.stage2.selected_surfaces[fd.selected_surface_idx];
        let stype = match surface_type {
            SelectedSurface::Planar(_) => "planar",
            SelectedSurface::Conical(i) => {
                if output.stage2.conical_hypotheses[*i].is_cylinder() {
                    "cylindrical"
                } else {
                    "conical"
                }
            }
            SelectedSurface::Spherical(_) => "spherical",
            SelectedSurface::Toroidal(_) => "toroidal",
        };

        let (face, is_concave) = if fd.edge_indices.is_empty() {
            // Complete closed surface with no boundary (full sphere or
            // torus): natural bounds. OCCT creates the seam and degenerate
            // edges itself; there are no shared edges to preserve.
            let mut make_face = b_rep_builder_api::MakeFace::new_handlegeomsurface_real(
                &fd.surface,
                config.vertex_tolerance_mm,
            );
            if !make_face.is_done() {
                return Err(Stage3Error::AdjacencyError(format!(
                    "MakeFace failed for complete closed face {fi}: {:?}",
                    make_face.error(),
                )));
            }
            let concave = match surface_type {
                SelectedSurface::Spherical(idx) => {
                    !output.stage2.spherical_hypotheses[*idx].convex
                }
                SelectedSurface::Toroidal(idx) => {
                    !output.stage2.toroidal_hypotheses[*idx].convex
                }
                _ => false,
            };
            (make_face.face().to_owned(), concave)
        } else {
            let assembled = assemble_face(fi, &output, &ctx, &plans, config)?;
            all_edge_pcurves.extend(assembled.edge_pcurves);
            all_vertex_uvs[fi] = assembled.vertex_uvs;
            (assembled.face, assembled.concave)
        };
        concave_faces[fi] = is_concave;

        if config.verbose {
            eprintln!(
                "  Face {fi}: {stype} — created successfully ({} edges)",
                fd.edge_indices.len(),
            );
        }

        if let Some(viz_sender) = viz {
            let mut overlay = crate::viz::VizOverlay::new();
            // Tessellate the OCCT face and show it translucent
            overlay.shape_meshes.push(crate::viz::tessellate_shape(
                face.as_shape(), [0.3, 0.8, 0.3, 0.4], [0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0], 0.1, 0.5,
            ));
            // Show edge curves in bright green
            for &edge_idx in &output.face_descriptors[fi].edge_indices {
                if let Some(curve) = output.edges[edge_idx].curve_3d.as_ref() {
                    overlay.lines.push(crate::viz::LineOverlay {
                        positions: crate::viz::sample_curve_for_viz(curve, 64),
                        color: [0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0],
                        no_depth_test: true,
                    });
                }
            }
            overlay.status_text = format!(
                "Stage 3.4: Face {fi}/{num_faces}: {stype} ({} edges)",
                output.face_descriptors[fi].edge_indices.len(),
            );
            let centroid = viz_selected_surface_centroid(fi, &output.face_descriptors, &output.stage2);
            overlay.focus_point = Some([centroid[0] as f32, centroid[1] as f32, centroid[2] as f32]);
            overlay.focus_normal = Some(viz_surface_normal_at_point(
                fi, centroid, &output.face_descriptors, &output.stage2,
            ));
            viz_sender.show_and_wait(overlay);
        }

        faces.push(face);
    }

    // Record the computed pcurves and vertex UVs in the stage-3 topology.
    for (ei, side, pcurve) in all_edge_pcurves {
        output.edges[ei].pcurves[side] = Some(pcurve);
    }
    for (vi, vertex) in output.vertices.iter_mut().enumerate() {
        vertex.uv_coords = vertex
            .adjacent_faces
            .iter()
            .map(|&fi| {
                all_vertex_uvs[fi]
                    .iter()
                    .find(|(vid, _)| *vid == vi)
                    .map(|(_, uv)| *uv)
                    .unwrap_or((f64::NAN, f64::NAN))
            })
            .collect();
    }

    if !config.quiet {
        eprintln!(
            "Stage 3.4 ({:.3}s): Created {}/{} OCCT faces",
            t.elapsed().as_secs_f64(),
            faces.len(),
            num_faces,
        );
    }

    output.faces = faces;
    output.concave_faces = concave_faces;

    // 5. Validate faces
    validate_faces(&output, config)?;

    // 6. Compare against reference STEP if --compare
    if config.compare_shape.is_some() {
        compare_faces_to_step(&output, config)?;
        compare_surface_orientations_to_step(&output, config);
    }

    Ok(output)
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Stage 3.5: Construct shells
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

```
/// Shared-edge topological assembly: one TopoDS_Vertex per BRepVertex, one
/// TopoDS_Edge per ReconEdge, pcurves attached to the shared edges for both
/// adjacent faces, seam and degenerate edges as first-class topology, and
/// faces built directly with BRep_Builder (see DEVELOPMENT_PLAN §3.x).
fn create_occt_faces_all(
    mut output: Stage3Output,
    config: &Config,
    viz: Option<&crate::viz::VizSender>,
) -> Result<Stage3Output, Stage3Error> {
    let t = Instant::now();
    let num_faces = output.face_descriptors.len();

    // 1. Create shared TopoDS_Vertex for each BRepVertex.
    // Set tolerance to vertex_tolerance_mm so that mesh vertex positions
    // (which may deviate slightly from fitted analytical surfaces) are accepted
    // by MakeEdge when projecting vertices onto edge curves.
    let builder = b_rep::Builder::new();
    let topo_vertices: Vec<OwnedPtr<topo_ds::Vertex>> = output
        .vertices
        .iter()
        .map(|v| {
            let pt = gp::Pnt::new_real3(v.point[0], v.point[1], v.point[2]);
            let mut mv = b_rep_builder_api::MakeVertex::new_pnt(&pt);
            let vtx = mv.vertex().to_owned();
            builder.update_vertex_vertex_real(&vtx, config.vertex_tolerance_mm);
            vtx
        })
        .collect();

    let mut topo_edges: Vec<OwnedPtr<topo_ds::Edge>> = Vec::with_capacity(output.edges.len());
    // BRepVertex ids at each edge's curve start/end (stored-curve direction).
    let mut edge_vertices: Vec<[usize; 2]> = Vec::with_capacity(output.edges.len());
    for (ei, edge) in output.edges.iter().enumerate() {
        let curve = match edge.curve_3d.as_ref() {
            Some(c) => c,
            None => {
                // No intersection curve — create a straight-line edge between endpoints
                if edge.vertex_indices[0] != usize::MAX && edge.vertex_indices[1] != usize::MAX {
                    let mut make_edge = b_rep_builder_api::MakeEdge::new_vertex2(
                        &topo_vertices[edge.vertex_indices[0]],
                        &topo_vertices[edge.vertex_indices[1]],
                    );
                    if !make_edge.is_done() {
                        return Err(Stage3Error::AdjacencyError(format!(
                            "Edge {ei}: straight-line fallback failed ({:?}), faces [{}, {}]",
                            make_edge.error(),
                            edge.face_indices[0],
                            edge.face_indices[1]
                        )));
                    }
                    if !config.quiet {
                        eprintln!(
                            "  Edge {ei}: using straight-line fallback (no intersection curve)"
                        );
                    }
                    topo_edges.push(make_edge.edge().to_owned());
                    edge_vertices.push([edge.vertex_indices[0], edge.vertex_indices[1]]);
                } else {
                    return Err(Stage3Error::AdjacencyError(format!(
                        "Edge {ei}: no curve and no vertex endpoints"
                    )));
                }
                continue;
            }
        };
        let (mut make_edge, verts) = if edge.vertex_indices[0] != usize::MAX
            && edge.vertex_indices[1] != usize::MAX
        {
            // Both endpoints have shared vertices — create edge with explicit vertex topology.
            // For periodic curves (circles), MakeEdge strips the TrimmedCurve and uses
            // AdjustPeriodic which forces p1 < p2, always taking the forward arc from V1
            // to V2. We must ensure V1 corresponds to the curve's first_parameter and V2
            // to last_parameter, otherwise MakeEdge will select the complementary arc.
            let c = curve.get();
            let p_start = c.value(c.first_parameter());
            let v0_pt = &output.vertices[edge.vertex_indices[0]].point;
            let v1_pt = &output.vertices[edge.vertex_indices[1]].point;
            let d0_start = (v0_pt[0] - p_start.x()).powi(2)
                + (v0_pt[1] - p_start.y()).powi(2)
                + (v0_pt[2] - p_start.z()).powi(2);
            let d1_start = (v1_pt[0] - p_start.x()).powi(2)
                + (v1_pt[1] - p_start.y()).powi(2)
                + (v1_pt[2] - p_start.z()).powi(2);
            let (vi0, vi1) = if d0_start <= d1_start {
                (edge.vertex_indices[0], edge.vertex_indices[1])
            } else {
                (edge.vertex_indices[1], edge.vertex_indices[0])
            };
            // Use explicit parameter values to avoid OCCT's vertex-to-curve projection,
            // which can fail when vertex tolerance exceeds default precision.
            // vi0 is always the vertex closest to the curve start, vi1 closest to end,
            // so parameters are always (first_parameter, last_parameter).
            let fp = c.first_parameter();
            let lp = c.last_parameter();

            // Update vertex tolerances to accommodate curve-vertex distance.
            // Imprecisely-fitted surfaces produce intersection curves that may not
            // pass exactly through mesh vertex positions.
            let p_fp = c.value(fp);
            let p_lp = c.value(lp);
            let v0_pt = &output.vertices[vi0].point;
            let v1_pt = &output.vertices[vi1].point;
            let d0 = ((v0_pt[0] - p_fp.x()).powi(2)
                + (v0_pt[1] - p_fp.y()).powi(2)
                + (v0_pt[2] - p_fp.z()).powi(2))
            .sqrt();
            let d1 = ((v1_pt[0] - p_lp.x()).powi(2)
                + (v1_pt[1] - p_lp.y()).powi(2)
                + (v1_pt[2] - p_lp.z()).powi(2))
            .sqrt();
            let min_tol = config.vertex_tolerance_mm;
            let tol0 = d0.max(min_tol) * 1.01; // 1% margin
            let tol1 = d1.max(min_tol) * 1.01;
            builder.update_vertex_vertex_real(&topo_vertices[vi0], tol0);
            builder.update_vertex_vertex_real(&topo_vertices[vi1], tol1);

            (
                b_rep_builder_api::MakeEdge::new_handlegeomcurve_vertex2_real2(
                    curve,
                    &topo_vertices[vi0],
                    &topo_vertices[vi1],
                    fp,
                    lp,
                ),
                [vi0, vi1],
            )
        } else {
            // Closed-loop edge (no vertex endpoints) — create without vertices
            (
                b_rep_builder_api::MakeEdge::new_handlegeomcurve(curve),
                [usize::MAX, usize::MAX],
            )
        };
        if !make_edge.is_done() {
            return Err(Stage3Error::AdjacencyError(format!(
                "MakeEdge failed for edge {ei}: {:?}",
                make_edge.error(),
            )));
        }
        topo_edges.push(make_edge.edge().to_owned());
        edge_vertices.push(verts);
    }

    let mut ctx = AssemblyCtx {
        topo_vertices,
        topo_edges,
        edge_vertices,
        closed_anchors: HashMap::new(),
    };

    // 3. Scan every face's boundary in UV, then choose seam anchors for the
    // wrapped faces (re-anchoring closed-loop edges so seam endpoints are
    // shared vertices of the shared edges).
    let mut scans: Vec<Option<FaceScan>> = Vec::with_capacity(num_faces);
    for fi in 0..num_faces {
        if output.face_descriptors[fi].edge_indices.is_empty() {
            scans.push(None);
        } else {
            scans.push(Some(scan_face(fi, &output, &ctx, config)?));
        }
    }
    let plans = plan_seam_anchors(&output, &scans, &mut ctx, config)?;
    drop(scans); // re-anchoring invalidated closed-edge samples

    // 4. Assemble each face from the shared edges.
    let mut faces: Vec<OwnedPtr<topo_ds::Face>> = Vec::with_capacity(num_faces);
    let mut concave_faces: Vec<bool> = vec![false; num_faces];
    let mut all_edge_pcurves: Vec<(usize, usize, OwnedPtr<geom2d::HandleGeom2dCurve>)> =
        Vec::new();
    let mut all_vertex_uvs: Vec<Vec<(usize, (f64, f64))>> = vec![Vec::new(); num_faces];

    for fi in 0..num_faces {
        let fd = &output.face_descriptors[fi];
        let surface_type = &output.stage2.selected_surfaces[fd.selected_surface_idx];
        let stype = match surface_type {
            SelectedSurface::Planar(_) => "planar",
            SelectedSurface::Conical(i) => {
                if output.stage2.conical_hypotheses[*i].is_cylinder() {
                    "cylindrical"
                } else {
                    "conical"
                }
            }
            SelectedSurface::Spherical(_) => "spherical",
            SelectedSurface::Toroidal(_) => "toroidal",
        };

        let (face, is_concave) = if fd.edge_indices.is_empty() {
            // Complete closed surface with no boundary (full sphere or
            // torus): natural bounds. OCCT creates the seam and degenerate
            // edges itself; there are no shared edges to preserve.
            let mut make_face = b_rep_builder_api::MakeFace::new_handlegeomsurface_real(
                &fd.surface,
                config.vertex_tolerance_mm,
            );
            if !make_face.is_done() {
                return Err(Stage3Error::AdjacencyError(format!(
                    "MakeFace failed for complete closed face {fi}: {:?}",
                    make_face.error(),
                )));
            }
            let concave = match surface_type {
                SelectedSurface::Spherical(idx) => {
                    !output.stage2.spherical_hypotheses[*idx].convex
                }
                SelectedSurface::Toroidal(idx) => {
                    !output.stage2.toroidal_hypotheses[*idx].convex
                }
                _ => false,
            };
            (make_face.face().to_owned(), concave)
        } else {
            let assembled = assemble_face(fi, &output, &ctx, &plans, config)?;
            all_edge_pcurves.extend(assembled.edge_pcurves);
            all_vertex_uvs[fi] = assembled.vertex_uvs;
            (assembled.face, assembled.concave)
        };
        concave_faces[fi] = is_concave;

        if config.verbose {
            eprintln!(
                "  Face {fi}: {stype} — created successfully ({} edges)",
                fd.edge_indices.len(),
            );
        }

        if let Some(viz_sender) = viz {
            let mut overlay = crate::viz::VizOverlay::new();
            // Tessellate the OCCT face and show it translucent
            overlay.shape_meshes.push(crate::viz::tessellate_shape(
                face.as_shape(), [0.3, 0.8, 0.3, 0.4], [0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0], 0.1, 0.5,
            ));
            // Show edge curves in bright green
            for &edge_idx in &output.face_descriptors[fi].edge_indices {
                if let Some(curve) = output.edges[edge_idx].curve_3d.as_ref() {
                    overlay.lines.push(crate::viz::LineOverlay {
                        positions: crate::viz::sample_curve_for_viz(curve, 64),
                        color: [0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0],
                        no_depth_test: true,
                    });
                }
            }
            overlay.status_text = format!(
                "Stage 3.4: Face {fi}/{num_faces}: {stype} ({} edges)",
                output.face_descriptors[fi].edge_indices.len(),
            );
            let centroid = viz_selected_surface_centroid(fi, &output.face_descriptors, &output.stage2);
            overlay.focus_point = Some([centroid[0] as f32, centroid[1] as f32, centroid[2] as f32]);
            overlay.focus_normal = Some(viz_surface_normal_at_point(
                fi, centroid, &output.face_descriptors, &output.stage2,
            ));
            viz_sender.show_and_wait(overlay);
        }

        faces.push(face);
    }

    // Record the computed pcurves and vertex UVs in the stage-3 topology.
    for (ei, side, pcurve) in all_edge_pcurves {
        output.edges[ei].pcurves[side] = Some(pcurve);
    }
    for (vi, vertex) in output.vertices.iter_mut().enumerate() {
        vertex.uv_coords = vertex
            .adjacent_faces
            .iter()
            .map(|&fi| {
                all_vertex_uvs[fi]
                    .iter()
                    .find(|(vid, _)| *vid == vi)
                    .map(|(_, uv)| *uv)
                    .unwrap_or((f64::NAN, f64::NAN))
            })
            .collect();
    }

    if !config.quiet {
        eprintln!(
            "Stage 3.4 ({:.3}s): Created {}/{} OCCT faces",
            t.elapsed().as_secs_f64(),
            faces.len(),
            num_faces,
        );
    }

    output.faces = faces;
    output.concave_faces = concave_faces;

    // 5. Validate faces
    validate_faces(&output, config)?;

    // 6. Compare against reference STEP if --compare
    if config.compare_shape.is_some() {
        compare_faces_to_step(&output, config)?;
        compare_surface_orientations_to_step(&output, config);
    }

    Ok(output)
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Stage 3.5: Construct shells
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

```
/// Stitch OCCT faces into shells using BRepBuilderAPI_Sewing.
///
/// Takes all faces created in stage 3.4 and passes them to BRepBuilderAPI_Sewing,
/// which merges shared edges and produces one or more TopoDS_Shell objects.
fn construct_shells(
    mut output: Stage3Output,
    config: &Config,
    viz: Option<&crate::viz::VizSender>,
) -> Result<Stage3Output, Stage3Error> {
    let t = Instant::now();
    let num_faces = output.make_faces.len();
    if num_faces == 0 {
        return Err(Stage3Error::AdjacencyError("no faces to sew into shells".into()));
    }

    // Create sewing operator
    let sewing_tol = config.vertex_tolerance_mm;
    let mut sewing = b_rep_builder_api::Sewing::new_real(sewing_tol);

    // Add all faces to the sewing operator.
    for mf in output.make_faces.iter() {
        sewing.add(mf.face().as_shape());
    }

    // Perform sewing
    let progress = message::ProgressRange::new();
    sewing.perform(&progress);

    let sewn = sewing.sewed_shape();
    let sewn_type = sewn.shape_type();

    if config.verbose {
        eprintln!("  Sewing result shape type: {:?}", sewn_type);
        let n_free = sewing.nb_free_edges();
        let n_multi = sewing.nb_multiple_edges();
        let n_contig = sewing.nb_contigous_edges();
        eprintln!("  Sewing stats: {n_free} free edges, {n_multi} multiple edges, {n_contig} contiguous edges");
        for i in 1..=n_free {
            let free_edge = sewing.free_edge(i);
            let mut edge_explorer = top_exp::Explorer::new_shape_shapeenum2(
                free_edge.as_shape(), top_abs::ShapeEnum::Vertex, top_abs::ShapeEnum::Shape,
            );
            let mut pts: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
            while edge_explorer.more() {
                let vtx = topo_ds::vertex(edge_explorer.value());
                let pt = b_rep::Tool::pnt(vtx);
                pts.push(format!("({:.4},{:.4},{:.4})", pt.x(), pt.y(), pt.z()));
                edge_explorer.next();
            }
            eprintln!("    Free edge {i}: vertices {}", pts.join(" -> "));
        }
    }

    // Extract shells from the sewing result.
    // The result can be a Shell (single), a Solid, or a Compound containing shells.
    let mut shells: Vec<OwnedPtr<topo_ds::Shell>> = Vec::new();

    match sewn_type {
        top_abs::ShapeEnum::Shell => {
            // Single shell result — copy it
            let shell = topo_ds::shell_shape(sewn);
            shells.push(shell.to_owned());
        }
        top_abs::ShapeEnum::Face => {
            // Single face — wrap it in a shell (e.g., a full sphere with no edges)
            let mut shell = topo_ds::Shell::new();
            let builder = topo_ds::Builder::new();
            builder.make_shell(&mut shell);
            builder.add(shell.as_shape_mut(), sewn);
            shells.push(shell);
        }
        top_abs::ShapeEnum::Solid => {
            // Sewing produced a solid directly — extract shells from it
            let mut shell_explorer = top_exp::Explorer::new_shape_shapeenum2(
                sewn,
                top_abs::ShapeEnum::Shell,
                top_abs::ShapeEnum::Shape,
            );
            while shell_explorer.more() {
                let shell = topo_ds::shell_shape(shell_explorer.value());
                shells.push(shell.to_owned());
                shell_explorer.next();
            }
        }
        top_abs::ShapeEnum::Compound | top_abs::ShapeEnum::Compsolid => {
            // Multiple shells — iterate to find them; also check for loose faces
            let mut shell_explorer = top_exp::Explorer::new_shape_shapeenum2(
                sewn,
                top_abs::ShapeEnum::Shell,
                top_abs::ShapeEnum::Shape,
            );
            while shell_explorer.more() {
                let shell = topo_ds::shell_shape(shell_explorer.value());
                shells.push(shell.to_owned());
                shell_explorer.next();
            }

        _ => {

                "unexpected sewing result shape type: {:?}",

            )));
        }

    // re-adding pcurves that sewing may have discarded when merging edges.
    let progress2 = message::ProgressRange::new();
    for shell in shells.iter_mut() {
        let mut fixer = shape_fix::Shell::new_shell(shell);
        fixer.perform(&progress2);
        *shell = fixer.shell();
    }

    // Fix face orientations in each shell.
    // ShapeFix_Shell::FixFaceOrientation uses BFS to propagate consistent
    // face orientations through shared edges.
    for shell in shells.iter_mut() {
        let mut fixer = shape_fix::Shell::new_shell(shell);
        fixer.fix_face_orientation(shell, true, false);

    // Validate shells using ShapeAnalysis_Shell

    // false if the shell is correctly oriented.
    let mut total_faces_in_shells = 0;
    for (si, shell) in shells.iter().enumerate() {
        let mut sa = shape_analysis::Shell::new();
        let has_bad_edges = sa.check_oriented_shells(shell.as_shape(), true, false);

        // Count faces in this shell
        let mut face_count = 0;
        let mut face_explorer = top_exp::Explorer::new_shape_shapeenum2(
            shell.as_shape(),
            top_abs::ShapeEnum::Face,

        );
        while face_explorer.more() {

            face_explorer.next();

        total_faces_in_shells += face_count;

            eprintln!(
                "  Shell {si}: {face_count} faces, bad_edges={has_bad_edges}, free_edges={has_free}"
            );
        }

        if has_bad_edges {
            eprintln!("  Warning: shell {si} has orientation inconsistencies after fixing");
        }
    }
```

```
/// Assemble OCCT faces into shells directly from the shared-edge topology.
///
/// Faces already share their TopoDS_Edge objects (stage 3.4), so a shell is
/// closed by construction: group faces into connected components over the
/// ReconEdge adjacency and add each face to its component's shell with the
/// orientation given by its hypothesis convexity. BRepBuilderAPI_Sewing is
/// no longer used; ShapeAnalysis_Shell remains as validation.
fn construct_shells(
    mut output: Stage3Output,
    config: &Config,
    viz: Option<&crate::viz::VizSender>,
) -> Result<Stage3Output, Stage3Error> {
    let t = Instant::now();
    let num_faces = output.faces.len();
    if num_faces == 0 {
        return Err(Stage3Error::AdjacencyError("no faces to assemble into shells".into()));
    }

    // Connected components of faces over the shared-edge adjacency.
    let mut component: Vec<usize> = vec![usize::MAX; num_faces];
    let mut n_components = 0;
    for start in 0..num_faces {
        if component[start] != usize::MAX {
            continue;
        }
        let comp = n_components;
        n_components += 1;
        let mut queue = vec![start];
        component[start] = comp;
        while let Some(fi) = queue.pop() {
            for &ei in &output.face_descriptors[fi].edge_indices {
                for &nfi in &output.edges[ei].face_indices {
                    if component[nfi] == usize::MAX {
                        component[nfi] = comp;
                        queue.push(nfi);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // Build one shell per component. A face whose natural surface normal
    // points into the material (concave) is added Reversed, so the shell is
    // consistently oriented outward by construction (mesh normals point
    // outward by the stage-1 validation).
    let builder = b_rep::Builder::new();
    let mut shells: Vec<OwnedPtr<topo_ds::Shell>> = Vec::new();
    for comp in 0..n_components {
        let mut shell = topo_ds::Shell::new();
        builder.make_shell(&mut shell);
        let mut face_count = 0;
        for fi in 0..num_faces {
            if component[fi] != comp {
                continue;
            }
            let orient = if output.concave_faces[fi] {
                top_abs::Orientation::Reversed
            } else {
                top_abs::Orientation::Forward
            };
            let oriented = output.faces[fi].as_shape().oriented(orient);
            builder.add(shell.as_shape_mut(), &oriented);
            face_count += 1;
        }
        shell.as_shape_mut().closed_bool(true);
        if config.verbose {
            eprintln!("  Shell {comp}: assembled from {face_count} faces");
        }
        shells.push(shell);
    }

    // Validate shells using ShapeAnalysis_Shell
    // Note: check_oriented_shells returns true if bad edges are FOUND,
    // false if the shell is correctly oriented.
    let mut total_faces_in_shells = 0;
    for (si, shell) in shells.iter().enumerate() {
        let mut sa = shape_analysis::Shell::new();
        let has_bad_edges = sa.check_oriented_shells(shell.as_shape(), true, false);

        // Count faces in this shell
        let mut face_count = 0;
        let mut face_explorer = top_exp::Explorer::new_shape_shapeenum2(
            shell.as_shape(),
            top_abs::ShapeEnum::Face,
            top_abs::ShapeEnum::Shape,
        );
        while face_explorer.more() {
            face_count += 1;
            face_explorer.next();
        }
        total_faces_in_shells += face_count;

        if config.verbose {
            let has_free = sa.has_free_edges();
            eprintln!(
                "  Shell {si}: {face_count} faces, bad_edges={has_bad_edges}, free_edges={has_free}"
            );
        }

        if has_bad_edges {
            eprintln!("  Warning: shell {si} has orientation inconsistencies");
        }
    }
```

```
    // junction within chordal tolerance, so the trimmed curve must pass

    // parameterization, or a straight-line stand-in for a curved junction —

    // chain-supported arc. The chain is the one representation available

/// Maximum distance from a spread of the edge's mesh boundary vertices to
/// the (trimmed) curve.
fn boundary_chain_deviation(
    curve: &geom::HandleGeomCurve,
    mesh_boundary_vertices: &[usize],
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
) -> f64 {
    let n = mesh_boundary_vertices.len();
    let step = (n / 9).max(1);
    let mut dev = 0.0_f64;
    for i in (0..n).step_by(step).chain([n - 1]) {
        let v = &mesh.vertices[mesh_boundary_vertices[i]];
        let pt = gp::Pnt::new_real3(v.x, v.y, v.z);
        let proj = geom_api::ProjectPointOnCurve::new_pnt_handlegeomcurve(&pt, curve);
        if proj.nb_points() == 0 {
            // No projection: measure against the endpoints instead.
            let c = curve.get();
            let (p, q) = (c.value(c.first_parameter()), c.value(c.last_parameter()));
            let dp = ((v.x - p.x()).powi(2) + (v.y - p.y()).powi(2) + (v.z - p.z()).powi(2)).sqrt();
            let dq = ((v.x - q.x()).powi(2) + (v.y - q.y()).powi(2) + (v.z - q.z()).powi(2)).sqrt();
            dev = dev.max(dp.min(dq));
        } else {
            dev = dev.max(proj.lower_distance());
        }
    }
    dev
}

/// Validate an edge curve against the mesh boundary chain; on failure, try
/// the circle through three spread chain vertices (falling back to the
/// original curve when the chain is straight or the repair doesn't help).
fn repair_edge_curve_from_boundary(
    curve: OwnedPtr<geom::HandleGeomCurve>,
    edge: &ReconEdge,
    vertices: &[BRepVertex],
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    config: &Config,
    fi0: usize,
    fi1: usize,
) -> OwnedPtr<geom::HandleGeomCurve> {
    if edge.mesh_boundary_vertices.len() < 3 {
        return curve;
    }
    let tol = config.surface_tolerance_mm;
    let dev = boundary_chain_deviation(&curve, &edge.mesh_boundary_vertices, mesh);
    if dev <= tol {
        return curve;
    }

    // Fit the circle through three spread chain vertices.
    let chain = &edge.mesh_boundary_vertices;
    let pnt_at = |i: usize| {
        let v = &mesh.vertices[chain[i]];
        gp::Pnt::new_real3(v.x, v.y, v.z)
    };
    let (p0, p1, p2) = (pnt_at(0), pnt_at(chain.len() / 2), pnt_at(chain.len() - 1));
    let Some(circle) = reconstruct_full_circle(&p0, &p1, &p2) else {
        if !config.quiet {
            eprintln!(
                "  Warning: edge (f{fi0},f{fi1}) curve is {dev:.3} mm from its mesh \
                 boundary chain and the chain is straight — keeping the curve"
            );
        }
        return curve;
    };

    // Trim to the endpoint vertices with a chain-supported arc, or keep the
    // full circle for closed-loop edges.
    let repaired: Option<OwnedPtr<geom::HandleGeomCurve>> = if edge.vertex_indices[0] != usize::MAX
        && edge.vertex_indices[1] != usize::MAX
    {
        let v0 = &vertices[edge.vertex_indices[0]];
        let v1 = &vertices[edge.vertex_indices[1]];
        match (
            project_point_on_curve(&v0.point, &circle),
            project_point_on_curve(&v1.point, &circle),
        ) {
            (Ok(t0), Ok(t1)) => {
                let (t_lo, t_hi) =
                    select_arc_parameters(t0, t1, &edge.mesh_boundary_vertices, &circle, mesh);
                let arc = geom::TrimmedCurve::new_handlegeomcurve_real2(&circle, t_lo, t_hi);
                Some(geom::TrimmedCurve::to_handle(arc).to_handle_curve())
            }
            _ => None,
        }
    } else {
        Some(circle)
    };

    match repaired {
        Some(repaired) => {
            let new_dev =
                boundary_chain_deviation(&repaired, &edge.mesh_boundary_vertices, mesh);
            if new_dev < dev {
                if !config.quiet {
                    eprintln!(
                        "  Edge (f{fi0},f{fi1}): curve was {dev:.3} mm from its mesh boundary \
                         chain; repaired with the chain's circle ({new_dev:.2e} mm)"
                    );
                }
                if new_dev > tol && !config.quiet {
                    eprintln!(
                        "  Warning: edge (f{fi0},f{fi1}) repaired curve still {new_dev:.3} mm \
                         from its mesh boundary chain"
                    );
                }
                repaired
            } else {
                curve
            }
        }
        None => curve,
    }
}
```

```
/// Dump a face's wire/edge structure for debugging: per edge occurrence its
/// orientation, flags, 3D range, pcurve endpoints on this face's surface,
/// and vertices with parameters.
fn debug_dump_face(face: &topo_ds::Face) {
    let surface = b_rep::Tool::surface_face(face);
    let identity_loc = top_loc::Location::new();
    let mut wire_exp = top_exp::Explorer::new_shape_shapeenum2(
        face.as_shape(),
        top_abs::ShapeEnum::Wire,
        top_abs::ShapeEnum::Shape,
    );
    let mut wi = 0;
    while wire_exp.more() {
        let wire = topo_ds::wire_shape(wire_exp.value());
        eprintln!("    wire {wi} (orient {:?}):", wire.as_shape().orientation());
        let mut we = b_rep_tools::WireExplorer::new_wire_face(wire, face);
        while we.more() {
            let edge = we.current();
            let orient = edge.as_shape().orientation();
            let degen = b_rep::Tool::degenerated(edge);
            let tol = b_rep::Tool::tolerance_edge(edge);
            let mut f = 0.0;
            let mut l = 0.0;
            b_rep::Tool::range_edge_real2(edge, &mut f, &mut l);
            let mut pf = 0.0;
            let mut pl = 0.0;
            let c2d = b_rep::Tool::curve_on_surface_edge_handlegeomsurface_location_real2_boolptr(
                edge, &surface, &identity_loc, &mut pf, &mut pl, None,
            );
            let pdesc = if c2d.is_null() {
                "NO PCURVE".to_string()
            } else {
                let c = c2d.get();
                let a = c.value(pf);
                let b = c.value(pl);
                format!(
                    "pcurve ({:.4},{:.4})->({:.4},{:.4})",
                    a.x(),
                    a.y(),
                    b.x(),
                    b.y()
                )
            };
            eprintln!(
                "      edge {orient:?} degen={degen} range=[{f:.4},{l:.4}] tol={tol:.2e} {pdesc}"
            );
            let mut vexp = top_exp::Explorer::new_shape_shapeenum2(
                edge.as_shape(),
                top_abs::ShapeEnum::Vertex,
                top_abs::ShapeEnum::Shape,
            );
            while vexp.more() {
                let v = topo_ds::vertex(vexp.value());
                let p = b_rep::Tool::pnt(v);
                let t = b_rep::Tool::parameter_vertex_edge(v, edge);
                eprintln!(
                    "        vertex {:?} t={t:.4} at ({:.4},{:.4},{:.4}) tol={:.2e}",
                    v.as_shape().orientation(),
                    p.x(),
                    p.y(),
                    p.z(),
                    b_rep::Tool::tolerance_vertex(v),
                );
                vexp.next();
            }
            we.next();
        }
        wi += 1;
        wire_exp.next();
    }
}
```

```
//! Debug utility: dump the seam-edge pcurve convention of an OCCT-built
//! cylinder face (BRepPrimAPI_MakeCylinder ground truth), to mirror it in
//! stage 3.4's shared-edge assembler.

use opencascade_sys::{b_rep, b_rep_prim_api, b_rep_tools, top_abs, top_exp, top_loc, topo_ds};

fn main() {
    let mut mk = b_rep_prim_api::MakeCylinder::new_real2(5.0, 10.0);
    let shape = mk.shape();
    let mut fexp = top_exp::Explorer::new_shape_shapeenum2(
        shape,
        top_abs::ShapeEnum::Face,
        top_abs::ShapeEnum::Shape,
    );
    let mut fi = 0;
    while fexp.more() {
        let face = topo_ds::face_shape(fexp.value());
        let surface = b_rep::Tool::surface_face(face);
        println!("face {fi} (orient {:?}):", face.as_shape().orientation());
        let identity_loc = top_loc::Location::new();
        let mut wexp = top_exp::Explorer::new_shape_shapeenum2(
            face.as_shape(),
            top_abs::ShapeEnum::Wire,
            top_abs::ShapeEnum::Shape,
        );
        while wexp.more() {
            let wire = topo_ds::wire(wexp.value());
            let mut we = b_rep_tools::WireExplorer::new_wire_face(wire, face);
            while we.more() {
                let edge = we.current();
                let orient = edge.as_shape().orientation();
                let mut pf = 0.0;
                let mut pl = 0.0;
                // Query pcurve for the edge oriented as it occurs in the wire.
                let oriented_shape = edge.as_shape().oriented(orient);
                let oriented_edge = topo_ds::edge(&oriented_shape);
                let c2d = b_rep::Tool::curve_on_surface_edge_handlegeomsurface_location_real2_boolptr(
                    oriented_edge, &surface, &identity_loc, &mut pf, &mut pl, None,
                );
                let degen = b_rep::Tool::degenerated(edge);
                if c2d.is_null() {
                    println!("  edge {orient:?} degen={degen}: NO PCURVE");
                } else {
                    let c = c2d.get();
                    let a = c.value(pf);
                    let b = c.value(pl);
                    println!(
                        "  edge {orient:?} degen={degen}: pcurve ({:.4},{:.4})->({:.4},{:.4})",
                        a.x(),
                        a.y(),
                        b.x(),
                        b.y()
                    );
                }
                we.next();
            }
            wexp.next();
        }
        fi += 1;
        fexp.next();
    }
}

```
```
/// How to build one edge's pcurve on a face's chart.
#[derive(Default, Clone, Copy)]
struct PcurveSpec {
    /// Pins the U branch: resampled arrays are shifted by whole periods to
    /// match the first sample of the planning-time scan.
    basis_first_u: f64,
    /// Branch/window offsets applied after basis pinning.
    u_off: f64,
    v_off: f64,
    /// Pin every sample's U (or V) exactly — for seam edges, which lie
    /// exactly on an isoline at a window border.
    force_u: Option<f64>,
    force_v: Option<f64>,
    /// Snap the first/last sample (in stored-curve direction) to the shared
    /// vertex's analytic UV, so consecutive pcurves in a wire meet exactly
    /// at their common vertex even when the vertex is slightly off this
    /// face's fitted surface.
    snap_start: Option<(f64, f64)>,
    snap_end: Option<(f64, f64)>,
}

/// Interpolate a pcurve through analytically-computed UV samples of an
/// edge's stored curve, densifying until the pcurve reproduces the 3D curve
/// within a target deviation. Returns (pcurve, max observed deviation).
///
/// The pcurve is parameterized exactly like the edge's stored curve, so
/// SameParameter holds by construction (within the returned deviation).
fn build_pcurve(
    edge: &topo_ds::Edge,
    chart: &SurfaceChart,
    spec: &PcurveSpec,
    config: &Config,
) -> Result<(OwnedPtr<geom2d::HandleGeom2dCurve>, f64), Stage3Error> {
    let pole_eps = pole_radius_eps(config);
    let dev_target = (config.vertex_tolerance_mm * 0.1).max(1e-7);
    let mut f = 0.0;
    let mut l = 0.0;
    let curve = b_rep::Tool::curve_edge_real2(edge, &mut f, &mut l);
    let c = curve.get();

    let mut best: Option<(OwnedPtr<geom2d::HandleGeom2dCurve>, f64)> = None;
    let mut n = PCURVE_BASE_SAMPLES;
    loop {
        let mut uv = sample_edge_uv(edge, chart, n, pole_eps).ok_or_else(|| {
            Stage3Error::AdjacencyError("edge lost its 3D curve during assembly".into())
        })?;
        // Pin the branch to the basis used during face planning.
        let shift = TWO_PI * ((spec.basis_first_u - uv.us[0]) / TWO_PI).round();
        for u in uv.us.iter_mut() {
            *u += shift + spec.u_off;
        }
        for v in uv.vs.iter_mut() {
            *v += spec.v_off;
        }
        if let Some(exact_u) = spec.force_u {
            for u in uv.us.iter_mut() {
                *u = exact_u;
            }
        }
        if let Some(exact_v) = spec.force_v {
            for v in uv.vs.iter_mut() {
                *v = exact_v;
            }
        }
        // Snap endpoints to their shared vertex UVs (branch-lifted).
        let mut snap = |i: usize, target: (f64, f64), uv: &mut EdgeUv| {
            let tu = target.0 + TWO_PI * ((uv.us[i] - target.0) / TWO_PI).round();
            let tv = if chart.v_periodic() {
                target.1 + TWO_PI * ((uv.vs[i] - target.1) / TWO_PI).round()
            } else {
                target.1
            };
            uv.us[i] = tu;
            uv.vs[i] = tv;
        };
        if let Some(t) = spec.snap_start {
            if !uv.start_at_pole {
                snap(0, t, &mut uv);
            }
        }
        if let Some(t) = spec.snap_end {
            if !uv.end_at_pole {
                let last = uv.us.len() - 1;
                snap(last, t, &mut uv);
            }
        }
```

```
        // Deviation of the pcurve (mapped through the chart) from the 3D
        // curve, at the interpolation samples and their midpoints. Endpoints
        // matter: OCCT's in-context BRepCheck validates pcurve/curve
        // agreement over the whole range against the edge tolerance, and a
        // vertex slightly off this face's fitted surface shows up exactly at
        // the (possibly vertex-snapped) pcurve ends.
        let pc = pcurve.get();
        let mut dev = 0.0_f64;
        {
            let mut check = |t: f64| {
                let p2 = pc.value(t);
                let p3 = chart.point_at(p2.x(), p2.y());
                let q = c.value(t);
                let d = ((p3[0] - q.x()).powi(2)
                    + (p3[1] - q.y()).powi(2)
                    + (p3[2] - q.z()).powi(2))
                .sqrt();
                dev = dev.max(d);
            };
            for i in 0..uv.ts.len() {
                check(uv.ts[i]);
                if i + 1 < uv.ts.len() {
                    check(0.5 * (uv.ts[i] + uv.ts[i + 1]));
                }
            }
        }
```

```
        // Densify until the target is met, but stop when the deviation has
        // plateaued (e.g. the 3D curve is off this fitted surface by its
        // fit residual, which no pcurve can represent away).
        let plateaued = best.as_ref().is_some_and(|(_, bd)| dev > 0.7 * bd);
        let better = best.as_ref().is_none_or(|(_, bd)| dev < *bd);
        if better {
            best = Some((pcurve, dev));
        }
        if dev <= dev_target || n >= 257 || plateaued {
            break;
        }
        n = n * 2 - 1;
    }
    Ok(best.unwrap())
```

```markdown
#### 3.4 Create OCCT faces
For each ReconFace, construct a `TopoDS_Face` from the surface and bounding wires.

**Algorithm (as implemented):**

*Stage 1: Create TopoDS_Edge for each ReconEdge.*
- For each `ReconEdge`, create a `BRepBuilderAPI_MakeEdge` using the trimmed 3D curve and shared `TopoDS_Vertex` endpoints from stage 3.3. For periodic curves (circles from cylinder/sphere intersections), vertex order is matched to the curve parameterization direction: V1 corresponds to `first_parameter()` and V2 to `last_parameter()`. This is critical because `MakeEdge` strips `TrimmedCurve` wrappers and uses `ElCLib::AdjustPeriodic` on the base periodic curve, which always selects the forward (CCW) arc from V1 to V2.
- **Adaptive vertex tolerance**: Before each `MakeEdge`, the distance between each vertex position and its curve endpoint is computed. The OCCT vertex tolerance is updated to at least that distance (with 1% margin), accommodating imprecisely-fitted surface intersection curves that don't pass exactly through mesh vertex positions. This replaces the earlier fixed `vertex_tolerance_mm` approach.

*Stage 2: Create OCCT faces.*
- **Planar faces** use wire-based construction:
  - Group the face's edges into wire loops based on `BRepVertex` connectivity. Edges sharing a vertex index are grouped together; closed-loop edges (vertex_indices both `usize::MAX`) each form a separate wire.
  - Build `BRepBuilderAPI_MakeWire` for each group by sequentially adding `TopoDS_Edge` objects.
  - Identify the outer wire as the group with the most edges (heuristic).
  - Create `BRepBuilderAPI_MakeFace` with the surface handle and outer wire, then add inner wires as holes.

- **Cylindrical, spherical, conical, and toroidal faces** use three approaches:

  - **Full revolution** (all boundary edges are closed loops): UV-bounds construction via `MakeFace::new_handlegeomsurface_real5(surface, umin, umax, vmin, vmax, tol)`. UV bounds are computed from edge projections using a circular gap algorithm that handles periodicity. This automatically creates seam edges for proper B-Rep topology.
  - **Spherical faces with closed-loop edges near poles** (e.g., pill/capsule hemispheres or dome hemispheres cut by a meridional plane): The boundary circles may pass through or near the sphere's UV singularities (poles at V=±π/2 where U is undefined). When any boundary circle passes within 45° of either pole (detected via `ProjectPointOnCurve` + chord-length formula), the sphere surface is recreated with its Z-axis aligned to a reorientation axis. The axis is determined from: (a) the adjacent cylinder's axis direction for tangent edges, or (b) the boundary circle's plane normal for non-tangent edges (computed from 3 sampled points on the curve). This is safe because for all-closed-loop boundaries, the reorientation axis is unique. The face's V bounds are computed by projecting samples of each boundary circle onto the oriented surface: for sphere-cylinder tangencies the junction is a great circle (V=0), but for sphere-cone tangencies it sits at a nonzero latitude, so fixed hemisphere bounds would misplace the boundary. With a single boundary circle, the face spans from that circle's latitude to the pole on the side occupied by the mesh (determined by projecting a mesh face centroid and checking the V-sign); with two, it spans between them.
  - **Spherical faces with pole vertices** (e.g., rounded cube corners where cylinders meet at a sphere pole): When a spherical face's UV bounds include V=±π/2, vertex U values at the pole are undefined (singularity). The `compute_uv_bounds_from_edges` function excludes pole U values (within 0.01 radians of ±π/2) from the circular gap algorithm to avoid corrupted U spans. The face is then constructed via UV-bounds `MakeFace::new_handlegeomsurface_real5`, producing a triangular-topology face (3 edges, 2 meridians + 1 parallel; pole collapsed to a vertex). These faces have a harmless BRepCheck edge failure (tolerance ~0) on the first edge, resolved by sewing.
  - **Partial revolution** (open edges with vertices): Wire-based construction with pre-set pcurves. Before building the wire, `BRep_Builder::update_edge` sets `Geom2d_Line` pcurves on each IntSS edge for the periodic surface, mapping the edge's 3D parameter range to (u(t), v(t)) in surface UV space. This ensures MakeFace selects the correct arc and shares edges with adjacent planar faces for sewing.
  - **Conical faces**: Same approaches as cylinder: full revolution via UV-bounds (with circular gap for U and cone apex V-extension), partial via wire+pcurves. The cone apex vertex is handled as a UV singularity (V extended to 0 for non-truncated cones). All test models pass: simple_cone, cone_cylinder, nosecone, block_with_conical_hole.
  - **Toroidal faces**: UV-bounds construction for complete torus patches. The torus UV space is doubly periodic: U ∈ [0,2π) around the major axis, V ∈ [0,2π) around the tube. Boundary edges are classified from per-edge projected samples: *iso-V* circles (fillet junctions: constant tube angle, spanning U) give a face full in U with V from the circular gap algorithm; *iso-U* circles (tube-continuation junctions, e.g. pipe elbows: constant major angle, spanning the full tube) give a face full in V with U from the circular gap algorithm over the edges' U positions, disambiguated by mesh centroid projections. Multiple sample points per edge curve (3 instead of 1) define the V window; mesh face centroid projections only *disambiguate* which of the two candidate arcs the face spans — they never extend the bounds (a cap triangle whose three vertices all lie on the plane-torus junction circle is legitimately absorbed by the torus hypothesis, but its centroid projects slightly past the tangent circle and would otherwise shift the face boundary off the junction, breaking sewing). Fillet patches typically span a small V arc (e.g., π/2 for a 90° fillet).

  - Full spheres (no edges) use `MakeFace::new_handlegeomsurface_real(surface, tolerance)` with natural bounds.

*Stage 3: Validate and compare.*
- Validate each face with `BRepCheck_Analyzer`. For invalid faces, run detailed `BRepCheck_Face` diagnostics (intersect_wires, classify_wires, orientation_of_wires, is_unorientable) and sub-shape analysis (edge tolerance, vertex checks). Faces where the only failure is edges with near-zero tolerance (< `vertex_tolerance_mm`) are treated as harmless (occurs on UV-bounds sphere pole faces, resolved by sewing) and not counted as failures.
- Wire orientation fix: after adding inner wires (holes) to a face, apply `ShapeFix_Face::fix_orientation()` to ensure inner wires are oriented opposite to the outer wire. This eliminates BRepCheck "bad orientation of sub-shape" warnings that previously appeared on all planar faces with holes.
- With `--compare`: for each face, sample a representative mesh face centroid from the surface's mesh faces and compute distance to the reference STEP shape using `BRepExtrema_DistShapeShape`. Report face count comparison. Error if max distance exceeds `--surface-tolerance`.

#### 3.5 Construct shells
Group faces into shells using `BRepBuilderAPI_Sewing`.

**Algorithm (as implemented):**
- Create a `BRepBuilderAPI_Sewing` instance with tolerance set to `vertex_tolerance`.
- Add all `TopoDS_Face` objects to the sewing operation.
- After `Perform()`, extract the sewed shape and iterate over its sub-shapes:
  - `Shell` sub-shapes are used directly.
  - Individual `Face` sub-shapes (e.g., a single-face model like `simple_sphere`) are wrapped in a new `TopoDS_Shell` via `BRep_Builder`.
  - `Solid`, `Compound`, and `Compsolid` sub-shapes are explored recursively for `Shell` children.
- Apply `ShapeFix_Shell::Perform()` (which calls `ShapeFix_Face::Perform()` on each face to re-add pcurves that sewing may have discarded, and `FixFaceOrientation` for edge consistency). Face orientation is NOT post-processed — `FixFaceOrientation` handles edge consistency and `SolidFromShell` (stage 3.6) handles global orientation via `PerformInfinitePoint`. Investigation showed that flipping individual face orientations breaks edge consistency and causes volume computation errors.
- Validate with `ShapeAnalysis_Shell::CheckOrientedShells` and report inconsistencies.
- Report sewing statistics: free edges, multiple edges, contiguous edges.

- With the `--compare` flag:
    - Count shells in the reference STEP file by exploring for `Shell` sub-shapes.
    - Report an error if the sewing produced free edges (edges not shared by any pair of faces), as this indicates incomplete stitching.
    - Report shell count comparison and orientation check results.
```

**After:**
```markdown
#### 3.4 Create OCCT faces
For each ReconFace, construct a `TopoDS_Face` from the surface and the shared edges — **shared-edge topological assembly** (the §3.x rework, implemented). Every ReconEdge is exactly one `TopoDS_Edge` used by both adjacent faces; each face attaches its own pcurve to the shared edge and assembles its wires and the face directly with `BRep_Builder`. `MakeWire`/`MakeFace`-from-wire/`ShapeFix` (which copy edges and would break the sharing) are not used; the one uniform mechanism below covers planes, cylinders, cones, spheres, and tori alike, and is the intended foundation for NURBS faces.

**Algorithm (as implemented):**

*Step 1: Shared vertices and edges.*
- One `TopoDS_Vertex` per `BRepVertex` (tolerance `vertex_tolerance_mm`).
- One `TopoDS_Edge` per `ReconEdge` via `BRepBuilderAPI_MakeEdge` from the trimmed 3D curve with explicit parameters. For periodic curves (circles), vertex order is matched to the curve parameterization direction: V1 corresponds to `first_parameter()` and V2 to `last_parameter()`. This is critical because `MakeEdge` strips `TrimmedCurve` wrappers and uses `ElCLib::AdjustPeriodic` on the base periodic curve, which always selects the forward (CCW) arc from V1 to V2.
- **Adaptive vertex tolerance**: before each `MakeEdge`, each vertex's distance to its curve endpoint is computed and the OCCT vertex tolerance raised to cover it (1% margin) — intersection curves of imprecisely-fitted surfaces don't pass exactly through mesh vertex positions.

*Step 2: Per-face UV analysis (`scan_face`).*
- Each face gets an analytic **chart** (`SurfaceChart`) mirroring the gp_Ax3 frame of its OCCT surface, with closed-form point→(U,V) and (U,V)→point maps for all five surface types (a future NURBS chart can substitute `ShapeAnalysis_Surface::ValueOfUV`). All UV work — sampling, windows, orientation tests — is analytic; `GeomAPI_ProjectPointOnSurf` is no longer used in face construction.
- **Sphere gauge choice**: a sphere's axis is a free gauge, so it is pointed at the mesh region's mean centroid direction from the center. The region's boundary then never passes near a UV pole: poles land strictly inside the region (a polar cap — handled by a degenerate pole edge) or strictly outside. This one choice replaces all of the old pole-proximity reorientation and pole-vertex special cases.
- Each boundary edge's stored curve (read back from the `TopoDS_Edge`, so `MakeEdge` parameter adjustments are respected) is sampled to branch-continuous UV arrays; U values within `pole_radius_eps` of a chart pole are backfilled from the nearest well-defined sample.
- Boundary edges are grouped into loops by `BRepVertex` connectivity and each loop is **branch-aligned**: consecutive edges' UV endpoints are matched by whole-period shifts. The loop's net **winding** around each periodic direction classifies the face: a loop with winding ±1 wraps the surface. U-jumps across pole junctions (a boundary loop passing through a cone apex or sphere pole vertex) are recorded as pole gaps rather than winding.

*Step 3: Seam planning (`plan_seam_anchors`).*
- A face whose boundary winds a periodic direction needs a **seam edge**; its endpoints must be vertices of the winding loops. Anchors: an existing `BRepVertex` on the loop when there is one; otherwise the (single) closed-loop edge is rebuilt to start at the seam azimuth and gains an anchor vertex at both ends. Because the anchor vertex becomes part of the *shared* edge, every face using that edge sees the same anchor — cross-face consistency is forced by sharing, not by tolerances. Faces are planned in waves so chains of wrapped faces (e.g. plane–cylinder–torus stacks) adopt one consistent seam azimuth; a face whose winding loops carry incompatible pre-determined anchors is a hard error (edge splitting is the recorded future extension).

*Step 4: Per-face assembly (`assemble_face`).*
- **Window**: wrapped faces span `[c, c+2π]` in the wrap direction, bordered by the seam at the anchor coordinate; other periodic directions use the circular-gap window over boundary samples with mesh-centroid majority disambiguation (`circular_window`). Winding loops are rotated to start at their anchor and oriented for a counterclockwise composite; plain loops are lifted into the window.
- **Seam edge**: 3D curve = `Geom_Surface::u_iso`/`v_iso` at the seam coordinate (parameterized exactly by the other coordinate, for every surface type), trimmed between the two anchors (or anchor and pole), built with `MakeEdge` + explicit parameters. It carries **two pcurves** (`BRep_Builder::update_edge` two-pcurve variant): PC1 for its FORWARD occurrence at the window's high border, PC2 for REVERSED at the low border (OCCT resolves FORWARD→PCurve1; verified against a `BRepPrimAPI_MakeCylinder` seam).
- **Degenerate pole edges**: at a cone apex or sphere pole the UV boundary closes across the pole with a degenerate edge — no 3D curve, `degenerated` flag, a constant-V pcurve line spanning the U gap, the pole vertex at both ends. Used both for wrapped pole caps (apex/pole interior to the face) and for pole gaps inside ordinary loops (boundary through an apex vertex). This is the *only* pole mechanism; it is identical for cones and spheres.
- **Pcurves** (`build_pcurve`): for every (edge, face) incidence, UV samples of the edge's stored curve are interpolated (`Geom2dAPI_Interpolate`) with the curve's own parameters, so SameParameter holds by construction. Endpoint samples snap to the shared vertex's analytic UV (branch-lifted), making wires closed in 2D at their vertices even when a mesh vertex sits slightly off this face's fitted surface. Seam pcurves pin the wrap coordinate to the window borders exactly. Sampling densifies (33→257) until the pcurve reproduces the 3D curve within `vertex_tolerance/10` or the deviation plateaus (a 3D curve off the fitted surface by its fit residual cannot be represented away); the achieved deviation, measured at samples *and* midpoints *including endpoints*, sets the edge tolerance (OCCT's in-context BRepCheck validates pcurve/curve agreement over the whole range against it). The pcurves are recorded in `ReconEdge.pcurves` and vertex UVs in `BRepVertex.uv_coords`.
- **Wires and orientation**: the composite wire of a wrapped face is emitted in counterclockwise window order (e.g. bottom loop +U, seam up, top loop −U, seam down). Plain loops are oriented by the mesh ground truth: the loop that winds around interior mesh-centroid UV points is the outer wire (counterclockwise); loops containing no interior points are holes (clockwise). Wires are `BRep_Builder`-built from the shared edges with per-occurrence orientations; the face is `BRep_Builder::make_face` + wires + `natural_restriction(false)`.
- **Faces with no boundary edges** (full sphere, complete torus) use `MakeFace` natural bounds — OCCT generates their seam/degenerate edges and there are no shared edges to preserve.
- A face is flagged **concave** when its hypothesis is concave: its natural surface normal points into the material, so stage 3.5 adds it to the shell REVERSED.

*Step 5: Validate and compare.*
- Validate each face with `BRepCheck_Analyzer`; invalid faces get detailed `BRepCheck_Face` diagnostics plus a structural dump (wire order, orientations, pcurve endpoints, vertex parameters) under `-v`. Note `BRepCheck_Analyzer::IsValid(face)` reflects subshape statuses *in the face's context* (e.g. `InvalidCurveOnSurface`), which is why the edge tolerance accounting above matters.
- With `--compare`: for each face, sample a representative mesh face centroid and compute distance to the reference STEP shape using `BRepExtrema_DistShapeShape`. Report face count comparison. Error if max distance exceeds `--surface-tolerance`.

#### 3.5 Construct shells
Assemble faces into shells directly from the shared-edge topology. Faces already share their `TopoDS_Edge` objects, so shells are **closed by construction** — `BRepBuilderAPI_Sewing` is no longer used, and `ShapeAnalysis_Shell` remains as validation only.

**Algorithm (as implemented):**
- Group faces into connected components over the ReconEdge adjacency (multi-solid models produce one shell per component, e.g. hollow_cube's outer and void shells).
- For each component, `BRep_Builder::make_shell` and add every face — FORWARD for convex/planar faces, REVERSED for concave ones — then set the shell's closed flag. Orientation is consistent outward by construction because mesh normals point outward (stage 1 validation) and the hypothesis convexity flags encode each surface's relation to the material.
- Validate with `ShapeAnalysis_Shell::CheckOrientedShells` (free edges, orientation inconsistencies) and report.

- With the `--compare` flag:
    - Count shells in the reference STEP file by exploring for `Shell` sub-shapes.
    - Report an error if any shell has free edges (an edge used by only one face), which would indicate broken shared-edge topology.
    - Report shell count comparison and orientation check results.
```

```
/// Merge redundant/orphan selected surfaces into larger adjacent ones.
///
/// Two situations produce selected surfaces that duplicate a neighbor's
/// geometry rather than describing a real model feature:
///
/// 1. **Spurious sub-fits**: a narrow band of faces on a cone/sphere can fit
///    an "exact" cylinder (e.g. 3 azimuthal strips of a shallow cone have
///    nearly coplanar normals) and get committed before the real surface's
///    BFS reaches those faces. All of the band's vertices lie exactly on the
///    real surface.
/// 2. **Tangent-junction bridge facets**: a mesh facet spanning a tangent
///    junction (e.g. cone–sphere) has vertices on both sides and can't be
///    absorbed by either surface at vertex tolerance; it becomes an orphan
///    single-face planar surface. Its chordal deviation from either surface
///    is bounded by the tessellation's surface tolerance.
///
/// Both create fake edges/vertices that break stage 3 reconstruction. This
/// pass merges a surface S into an adjacent, larger-area surface T when all
/// of S's vertices lie within tolerance of T's geometry: a tight tolerance
/// (10× vertex tolerance) for multi-face S (case 1: exact overlap), and the
/// looser surface tolerance for S with ≤ 2 faces (case 2: chordal sag).

/// "Surface refitting"). BFS greedily absorbs border faces that fit within
/// tolerance but belong more naturally to the adjacent surface — e.g. a face
/// one row past a fillet junction absorbed by the plane. The misassignment
/// shifts the mesh region boundary by a row, which shifts reconstructed edge
/// boundary vertices and corner vertices off the true feature curves.
```
