## Rewrite Roadmap

The jump from the BFS pipeline to partition-then-classify is immediate — no
compatibility flag, no parallel pipelines. The test suite will be red in the
interim; models are re-enabled as they pass, easiest first. Suggested order:

1. **Stage 2.1 + 2.2** (edge classifier, region extraction): new
   `src/stage2/edges.rs` + `src/stage2/regions.rs`. Wire viz (edge-class
   overlay — this is finally the producer for the never-populated
   `EdgeHighlight` overlay noted in TODO.md) and the report-only partition
   diagnostics. Calibrate `J` and `κ_floor` across the corpus by inspecting
   partitions against reference STEP face structure *before* any fitting
   exists.
2. **Stage 2.3 analytic ladder**: new `src/stage2/classify.rs` calling the
   existing fitters (`planar.rs`, `cylindrical.rs`, `conical.rs`,
   `spherical.rs`, `toroidal.rs` keep their fitting/validation functions;
   their seeding/BFS entry points go). Terminal per-facet-plane fallback
   from day one, so every model produces output immediately.
3. **Stage 2.4 repair**: `src/stage2/repair.rs` — merge, split (reusing the
   2.1 classifier with a threshold parameter), and boundary relabel (port of
   `refine_boundary_assignments`). Connectivity re-split + the three hard
   invariants.
4. **Freeform rung rewiring**: `bspline.rs` keeps parameterization → grid →
   fit → validate; its gathering front end is deleted; hook it behind the
   2.4 split-probe protocol.
5. **Deletion pass**: `bfs.rs` (generation loop, seed machinery, masks,
   acceptance tests), greedy selection, `absorb_redundant_surfaces`, the
   `MeshFace` hypothesis fields, `--skip-stage`. Update SURFACE_FITTING.md's
   seeding/BFS/acceptance sections with pointers to Abandoned Approaches.
6. **Test migration**: stage-2 integration tests re-target region counts and
   classification results (end-state expectations — cube = 6 planar,
   block_with_hole = 6 planar + 1 cylindrical, etc. — are unchanged);
   re-enable corpus models in roughly this order: pure-planar ccad models →
   analytic primitives → fillet/tangent models (pill, rounded cubes,
   stepped_block_toroidal) → nurbs suite → nosecone/nosecone_truncated →
   pipe_elbow → 3DBenchy.

Expected wins to verify along the way: pipe_elbow's torus recovered without
strip-merge seeding; nosecone with no absorb pass; stepped_block's
single-rectangle walls as real planar regions; stage-2 runtime on large
models collapsing (each region fit O(1) times — no more tiling large spheres
with thousands of band trials; full stage 2 on 3DBenchy was ~15 min under
BFS vs ~3 s planar-only).

---

## Abandoned Approaches

Retired with the 2026-07-17 stage-2 redesign. Recorded here because each
worked well enough to ship models, and some may be worth resurrecting as
*diagnostics* — but all of them existed to compensate for fit-driven greedy
segmentation, and the compensations kept multiplying (that treadmill is why
the architecture changed). Do not re-add one without identifying which
design principle it would compensate for.

**Per-type BFS hypothesis generation** (the `SurfaceType` trait framework in
`bfs.rs`: per-face seeding, trial BFS growth with refit-on-near-miss
(`REFIT_SKIP_MULTIPLIER` band), best-trial-by-area commit). The core defect
was *commit-during-generation*: the first hypothesis of a type to claim a
face owned it, so an accidental sub-region fit committed early fragmented
the real surface — a 6-face r=12.4992 cylinder band on the nosecone's
r=12.5 sphere; a 31-face split fragment of nosecone_truncated's real cone
that left a fake corner vertex 80.6 mm off the model until a later pass
rejoined it. Fit-driven growth also *invited* accidental fits (every
quad-row band on a sphere lies exactly on some cone and some torus) and paid
for them at scale. What survives: the fitting math and LM refinement
(SURFACE_FITTING.md), whole-region refit-validate retry, and the convexity
logic (as 2.3's orientation-coherence check).

**Stage execution ordering** (planar → spherical → toroidal → conical →
selection, "most-constrained first"). Existed purely so the conical stage
would not tile spheres and torus tubes with exactly-fitting narrow band
hypotheses, starving the later stages' seeding. With per-region
classification there is no cross-type competition to referee.

**Curvature-guided seed ordering, junction mask, and the large_sphere
mask.** The curvature-difference score (κ = θ/d, neighbor difference,
local-relative 50% threshold) was computed per *face* and used only to order
seeds and exclude junction faces from seed neighborhoods; the large_sphere
mask kept torus seeding off sphere interiors (measured 2026-07-15: without
it, bogus-but-valid torus tilings cost 120–358× in stage-2 runtime —
pill_fine 1.2 s → 429 s). The curvature math is *promoted*, not abandoned:
it is now the 2.1 edge classifier (extended to a signed two-sided
descriptor). The ordering and masking roles are moot — there are no seeds.

**Seed topologies** (conical 3-face fan with optional f3 for 6-vertex
coverage; spherical 1-ring vertex neighborhood; toroidal 1-ring +
3-hop-expansion targeting ≥16 faces; strip-merge torus seeds, already
deleted 2026-07-15 as unreachable). All existed because fits from tiny face
sets are ill-conditioned and had to be grown carefully. Region-level fits
see all faces at once; the conditioning problem is gone (pipe_elbow's torus
is the emblematic case).

**Global acceptance tests**: cylinder/cone angular coverage (second-largest
gap ≤ span/3, plus the coarse-fillet `max_gap` floor gated to cylinders
already spanning ≥45°), sphere solid-angle coverage (eigenvalue ratio
λ3/λ1 of the centroid-direction covariance), torus minor-circle coverage
from face normals (tube span ≥ 0.3 rad), and normal-axis consistency
(per-face |n·axis| deviation ≤ 0.05 during BFS; aggregate variance ≤ 0.0005
at acceptance). Every one is a detector for "this hypothesis is an
accidental sub-region fit on a different surface type" — a class of
hypothesis the new pipeline never constructs, because fits only see maximal
regions and a cone cannot validate an entire sphere. Their rationale
documentation (angular-cluster reasoning, the medium-resolution-fillet gap
analysis) remains valuable context if tiny-region ambiguity ever needs a
diagnostic.

**Greedy area-based surface selection** (old stage 2.6): resolved
overlapping hypotheses (a face could hold one hypothesis per type) largest
total-area first. Obsolete: the partition is disjoint by construction, so
there is nothing to select between. It was also the connectivity-invariant
violator — it kept only a winner's *still-unassigned remnant* with no
connectivity recheck, which is how 3DBenchy face 5841 reached stage 3.4
claiming three disconnected mesh regions (the ≥3-winding-loop abort).

**Redundant-surface absorption** (old stage 2.8, `absorb_redundant_surfaces`):
merged a selected surface into an adjacent larger one under a *tight* rule
(10× vertex tolerance) and a *loose* rule (`--surface-tolerance`, ≤2-face
orphans). The tight rule's targets — spurious sub-fits and split fragments —
cannot form under per-region classification; its sound criterion lives on as
the 2.4 merge. The loose rule was condemned by measurement before the
redesign: its motivating "tangent-junction bridge facet" story was tested
and found false (tessellators emit seam edges even at tangencies), its only
corpus firings absorbed *real* narrow planar faces 0.12–0.27 mm off, and in
planar-only 3DBenchy it introduced up to 0.4 mm of chordal slop (794
BRepCheck face failures, 1% volume loss).

**Per-face multi-hypothesis bookkeeping** (`planar_hypothesis`,
`conical_hypothesis`, `spherical_hypothesis`, `toroidal_hypothesis` fields
on `MeshFace`, with `UNDEDUCED`/`NO_HYPOTHESIS` sentinels). Existed to let
overlapping hypotheses coexist until selection. Replaced by the single
`face_region` map in `Stage2Output`.

**NURBS region gathering** (old stage 2.7 steps 1–3): connected-component
gathering of single-face planar *selections* over smooth edges, absorption
of ≤16-face analytic selections (freeform surfaces bait the analytic
detectors locally — accidental coplanar strips, cylinder ribbons on
saddles), the two protective guards, and the tangent-plane merge of
wholly-smooth-boundary planar neighbors. All of it reconstructed "the
freeform region" from the wreckage of analytic over-detection; the partition
now hands the freeform rung an intact region directly, and exactly-planar
margins of freeform surfaces land in the same region by curvature
continuity.

**Boundary refinement is NOT abandoned** — `refine_boundary_assignments`
(old stage 2.9) is promoted into the 2.4 repair loop unchanged in
mechanism, upgraded in role. Corner vertex refinement likewise survives in
stage 3.

## Visualization (`--viz-stages`)

The `--viz-stages` flag enables interactive 3D visualization for debugging pipeline stages. The companion `--viz-stages-level` flag (default 1) controls pause granularity.

Supported stages after the rewrite:
- **2.1**: edge classification — BOUNDARY edges drawn via `EdgeHighlight`
  overlays (sharp vs curvature-jump color-coded), faces shaded by curvature
  descriptor. (This wires up the previously never-populated `EdgeHighlight`
  overlay type.)
- **2.2**: regions — faces colored by region id.
- **2.3**: per-region classification — level 1 pauses at each classified
  region (fit overlay + parameters via the existing `viz_overlays` /
  `viz_fit_description` per-surface-type functions); level 2 pauses at each
  attempted rung.
- **2.4**: repair — level 1 pauses after the loop converges; level 2 pauses
  at each merge/split/relabel operation.
- **3.3** (edge curves), **3.4** (faces), **3.5** (shells), **3.6** (solids)
  — unchanged.

### Architecture

The visualization uses a two-thread architecture with synchronous channel communication:

1. **Main thread**: Owns the window, drives the three-d render loop, and displays overlays.
2. **Pipeline thread**: Runs the brepper pipeline (stages 1–4) in the background.

- `VizSender::show_and_wait(overlay)` sends a `VizOverlay` to the render thread and blocks.
- The render thread displays face highlights, edge highlights, translucent geometry overlays (cylinders, cones, spheres, tori), status text, and optionally moves the camera.
- The user presses **Space** (NextStep), **Shift+Space** (skip to next region/operation), or **Q** (Quit); clicking a face skips ahead to that face's region.

### Key types (in `src/viz.rs`)

- `VizSender` / `VizReceiver`: Channel endpoints. Created by `viz_channel()`.
- `VizOverlay`: A display frame containing face highlights, edge highlights, cylinder/cone/sphere/torus overlays, line overlays, shape meshes, status text, and optional camera focus.
- `VizAction`: The user's response — `NextStep`, `NextSeed`, `SkipToSeed(face_index)`, or `Quit`.
- `FaceHighlight`, `EdgeHighlight`, `CylinderOverlay`, `ConeOverlay`, `SphereOverlay`, `TorusOverlay`, `LineOverlay`, `ShapeMeshOverlay`: Overlay primitives.

The render window (powered by three-d with egui overlay) provides camera controls (orbit/pan/zoom-at-cursor), face-number labels with occlusion (`N`), hover info with ray-cast picking, click-to-skip, and a help overlay (`?`).

Debug verbosity (`--verbose`) uses consistent indentation:
- **Level 1**: Stage summaries (region counts, classification counts, timing).
- **Level 2**: Per-region details (classification result, fit parameters, repair operations).
- **Level 3**: Per-rung fit attempts with error values; repair-loop round summaries.
- **Level 4**: Per-face evidence (curvature descriptors, relabel decisions).

---

## Source Code Organization

Each stage is a function taking a config reference and consuming the
previous stage's output structure:

- main:
  - let config = parse flags, load --compare STEP file
  - out1 = stage1(config)?           # ConnectedMesh
  - out2 = stage2(config, out1)?     # Stage2Output: regions + selected surfaces
  - out3 = stage3(config, out2)?     # Stage3Output: B-Rep topology
  - stage4(config, out3)?            # writes STEP file

Stage 2 module layout (target):

- `src/stage2/mod.rs` — orchestration, `Stage2Output` (`face_region`,
  `regions`, `EdgeClassification`, typed hypothesis vectors,
  `SelectedSurface`), shared helpers.
- `src/stage2/edges.rs` — 2.1 curvature field + edge classifier
  (threshold-parameterized so 2.4's split repair can reuse it).
- `src/stage2/regions.rs` — 2.2 union-find extraction, boundary loops.
- `src/stage2/classify.rs` — 2.3 ladder, subsample/validate/refit driver.
- `src/stage2/repair.rs` — 2.4 merge/split/relabel, invariants.
- `src/stage2/{planar,cylindrical,conical,spherical,toroidal}.rs` — fitting
  + validation for each surface type (seeding/BFS entry points deleted).
- `src/stage2/bspline.rs` — freeform rung (parameterize/resample/fit/
  validate; gathering deleted).
- `src/stage2/bfs.rs` — deleted with the BFS pipeline.

Data-structure linking uses indices into vectors throughout (stable, easily
debuggable, serialization-friendly; no lifetime complexity).

---

## Testing Strategy

The main testing strategy is to process a set of example stl/step pairs, and use the --compare flag to ensure that the pipeline is working correctly for each.

1. **Unit Tests**: Individual components (readers, fitters, edge classifier, region extraction, repair operations)
2. **Integration Tests**: Full pipeline on known geometries
3. **Regression Tests**: Compare output STEP to reference
4. **Validation**: Round-trip test (STEP → mesh → STEP)

Stage-2 integration tests assert:
- Edge classification / partition sanity per model (with `--compare`: region
  boundary edges near reference edges; region interiors mapping to
  consistent reference surfaces).
- Region classification end states — the same expectations the old suite
  pinned (cube = 6 planar; block_with_hole = 6 planar + 1 cylindrical;
  pipe = 2 planar + 2 cylindrical; ball_on_cylinder = 1 planar +
  1 cylindrical + 1 spherical; hemisphere = 1 planar + 1 spherical;
  cone_15x20 = 1 planar + 1 conical; etc.), plus fitted-parameter agreement
  with the reference STEP (axis, radius, center) for analytic models.
- Repair-loop behavior on the models that motivated it (coarse cones
  re-merged; capsule junction found; stepped_block narrow walls kept as
  real planar regions).

**Migration reality**: the suite is red during the rewrite (see Rewrite
Roadmap step 6). Re-enable per model; a model stays disabled with a comment
naming its blocker rather than being nerfed with loosened gates.

### Test Cases

See [tests/RESULTS.md](tests/RESULTS.md) for the full test results table.
Generated by: `./scripts/run_test_table.sh [path/to/brepper]`

## Performance Targets

| Mesh Size | Target Time |
|-----------|-------------|
| < 10K triangles | < 5 seconds |
| 10K - 100K triangles | < 30 seconds |
| 100K - 1M triangles | < 5 minutes |

The partition-then-classify design should land large models well inside
these targets: stage 2 does O(E) edge classification, O(N α(N)) extraction,
and one fit-and-validate per region — no per-seed redundancy and no
accidental-fit trials (under BFS, full stage 2 on 3DBenchy's 196k faces ran
~15 minutes; the planar-only path that skips hypothesis generation ran ~3 s,
which is the cost floor the new architecture approaches plus per-region
fitting).

- [ ] Support for OBJ, PLY input formats
- [ ] IGES export option
- [ ] Hole detection and filling
- [ ] Feature recognition (holes, pockets, bosses)
- [ ] Richer curvature estimators for 2.1: per-vertex principal curvatures (Rusinkiewicz) would give full curvature tensors instead of the per-edge samples, sharpening the two-sided descriptor on irregular triangulations.
- [ ] Quadric pre-classification: fit a 10-coefficient quadric via SVD as a fast O(N) pre-rung — its eigenvalue pattern classifies plane/sphere/cylinder/cone directly and could order or prune the 2.3 ladder for large regions.
- [ ] Adaptive tessellation handling: `κ_floor` and the curvature descriptors assume locally comparable facet sizes; meshes with strong adaptive refinement may need area-weighted or multi-ring curvature estimates.
- [ ] Repair mode for assumption violations beyond stage 1.2's current repairs (e.g. boundary crack stitching — see TODO.md).

This inverted-loop design is a genuinely strong alternative — it's the best incremental redesign of the old pipeline I can construct, and under the exactness assumption its core decision rule is actually *sound*, not heuristic. Here's my honest assessment of how it would behave.

## Why the core rule works

The load-bearing property is what you might call the sub-region lemma: an accidental fit (the 6-face cylinder band on the nosecone sphere, a torus through a band of sphere quads) is by definition supported only on a *subset* of a true region, while the true surface fitted from an interior seed expands — with vertex tolerance as the arbiter — to the *entire* region. So when both compete on the same seed, the true surface always covers at least as much area, and largest-area-wins picks it. The old pipeline compared hypotheses born from *different* seeds at *different* times, which is why commit order mattered and fragmentation happened. Comparing all types on the *same* seed makes the comparison fair, and:

- **Fragmentation dies.** The nosecone_truncated 31-face split fragment can't form: expansion is allowed through claimed faces, so the interior-seeded cone covers the whole cone in one trial regardless of what committed earlier.
- **Stage ordering dies.** Per-seed competition replaces the planar→spherical→toroidal→conical sequencing and its exclusion rules.
- **The tiling pathology dies too.** The 429-second pill_fine case came from *thousands* of seeds each growing a bogus torus band on the sphere. Here, the sphere's interior seed runs one torus expansion (one band), one cone expansion (one band), loses them to the sphere, and the whole region leaves the seed pool. Cost per region ≈ 5 bounded expansions. The large_sphere mask becomes unnecessary without any masking.
- **Cross-region leakage is bounded.** My first instinct was that a fitted surface could span two regions (the tangent cone of a sphere *is* the real adjacent cone), but vertex tolerance at 5e-5 limits overlap to faces whose vertices genuinely lie on both surfaces — the single junction row. Two distinct analytic surfaces agreeing to 5e-5 over an extended 2D patch would be near-identical. So the shared-face semantics maps exactly onto the real ambiguity, which is elegant.

One more real advantage over the partition approach: **boundary placement never depends on discrete curvature estimates.** The capsule's equal-radius sphere↔cylinder junction, which forces my 2.1 design into a two-sided curvature descriptor with calibrated thresholds (J, κ_floor), is handled here by exact vertex distances — the fit itself finds the boundary. Curvature ordering is only used to pick seeds, where an error costs efficiency, not correctness. That's a graceful degradation the partition approach doesn't have; its miscalibrations must be caught and repaired explicitly.

## Where it falls short of the documented plan

**1. Small-seed fit conditioning is unsolved — and it's what pipe_elbow actually needs.** The inversion changes *when* types compete but not *what the fitter sees*: still a 1-ring or 3-face fan. On the pipe elbow's strip tessellation, a 1-ring torus fit is ill-conditioned (no major-arc coverage), so the torus expansion fails at every seed, the cylinder wins a strip, and the elbow decomposes into cylinder strips again — the exact failure that spawned strip-merge seeding. Fixing it inside this design means re-adding escalation machinery (e.g. "when growth stalls, refit the stalled frontier with a higher-DOF type using the already-grown support" — a model-promotion variant your spec doesn't include but would need). Partition-first fits the whole elbow tube at once; conditioning is solved structurally.

**2. Freeform stays a second-class afterthought.** NURBS can't participate in the per-seed competition (you can't fit a B-spline patch from a 1-ring; parameterization needs a bounded region). So on a freeform surface, the winner at each seed is the largest *accidental analytic* patch — the 12-face cylinder ribbons on the saddle, the accidental coplanar strips — and you're back to gathering leftovers and absorbing ≤16-face analytic confetti afterward, with the guards that entails. Partition-first hands the freeform fitter an intact region.

**3. The heuristic surface shrinks a lot but doesn't collapse.** You still need: overlap resolution into a strict partition for stage 3 (per-face best-fit among claimants — essentially the 2.9 rule — plus the connected-component re-split, since resolution can still disconnect a remnant; face 5841's family is about *selection stripping faces*, and any design with overlaps keeps a small version of that step); degeneracy guards and a DOF tiebreak (on a plane region, a near-infinite-radius cylinder and sphere *tie* the plane on area — "largest" alone is ill-defined without simplest-on-ties, plus the existing max-radius/half-angle guards); a crisp definition of "already has a good hypothesis" for seed suppression; and the curvature ordering itself, which remains load-bearing for keeping first-commit quality high.

**4. Cost is ~5 expansions per region.** Much better than the old pathologies, likely somewhat worse than partition-first's one-classification-per-region with fits that mostly succeed on the first or second rung. Not a deciding factor.

## Bottom line

I'd rank it clearly above the old pipeline and honestly competitive with partition-first — the two converge more than they first appear: your inversion effectively *discovers* regions by fit growth with the fit as classifier, where partition-first *extracts* regions from edge signals and then classifies. The trade is: the inversion buys exact, calibration-free boundaries at tangent junctions and a much smaller code delta, at the price of keeping small-seed conditioning heuristics and leaving freeform as leftover-gathering. Partition-first buys whole-region fit conditioning and first-class freeform, at the price of a calibrated edge classifier whose mistakes must be explicitly repaired.

If the 2.1 curvature calibration turns out to be the weak link in practice (coarse fillets, f32 quantization noise), this inversion is exactly the design I'd retreat to — and it's compatible with keeping most of the new plan's skeleton (the repair loop, invariants, and per-region refit all apply to its output unchanged). It would be worth a short "Contingency: seed-first multi-type competition" note in the plan's Abandoned Approaches-adjacent territory — not abandoned, just not chosen — so the option and its rationale don't get lost. Want me to add that?

8	
9	/// Stage identifier as (major, minor). Minor=0 means run all sub-stages of that major stage.
10	/// Examples: (1, 2) = stage 1.2, (2, 0) = all of stage 2, (4, 1) = full pipeline.
11	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
12	pub struct Stage(pub u8, pub u8);
13	
14	impl Stage {
15	    /// The final sub-stage for each major stage.
16	    fn last_minor(major: u8) -> u8 {
17	        match major {
18	            1 => 3,
19	            2 => 9,
20	            3 => 6,
21	            4 => 1,
22	            _ => 0,
23	        }
24	    }
25	
26	    /// Normalize: if minor is 0, expand to last sub-stage of that major.
27	    pub fn normalized(self) -> (u8, u8) {
28	        if self.1 == 0 {
29	            (self.0, Self::last_minor(self.0))
30	        } else {
31	            (self.0, self.1)
32	        }
33	    }
34	
35	    /// Returns true if the pipeline should run at least through the given stage.
36	    pub fn at_least(&self, major: u8, minor: u8) -> bool {
37	        let (sm, ss) = self.normalized();
38	        (sm, ss) >= (major, minor)
39	    }
40	}
41	
42	impl Default for Stage {
43	    fn default() -> Self {
44	        Stage(4, 1)
45	    }
46	}
47	
48	fn parse_stage(s: &str) -> Result<Stage, String> {
49	    if let Some((major_s, minor_s)) = s.split_once('.') {
50	        let major: u8 = major_s.parse().map_err(|_| format!("invalid stage: {s}"))?;
51	        let minor: u8 = minor_s.parse().map_err(|_| format!("invalid stage: {s}"))?;
52	        if !(1..=4).contains(&major) || !(1..=Stage::last_minor(major)).contains(&minor) {
53	            return Err(format!("invalid stage: {s} (valid: 1.1–4.1)"));
54	        }
55	        Ok(Stage(major, minor))
56	    } else {
57	        let major: u8 = s.parse().map_err(|_| format!("invalid stage: {s}"))?;
58	        if !(1..=4).contains(&major) {
59	            return Err(format!("invalid stage: {s} (valid: 1–4)"));
60	        }
61	        Ok(Stage(major, 0))
62	    }
63	}
64	
65	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
66	// Units
67	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
68	
69	/// Length units for STL/STEP files.
70	#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, ValueEnum)]
71	pub enum Units {
72	    /// Millimeters
73	    #[default]
74	    Mm,
75	    /// Centimeters
76	    Cm,
77	    /// Meters
78	    M,
79	    /// Inches
80	    In,
81	    /// Feet
82	    Ft,
83	    /// Micrometers
84	    Um,
85	}
86	
87	impl Units {
88	    /// Conversion factor: 1 of this unit = N millimeters.
89	    pub fn to_mm(self) -> f64 {
90	        match self {
91	            Units::Mm => 1.0,
92	            Units::Cm => 10.0,
93	            Units::M => 1000.0,
94	            Units::In => 25.4,
95	            Units::Ft => 304.8,
96	            Units::Um => 0.001,
97	        }
98	    }
99	}
100	
101	
102	impl Display for Units {
103	    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
104	        match self {
105	            Units::Mm => write!(f, "mm"),
106	            Units::Cm => write!(f, "cm"),
107	            Units::M => write!(f, "m"),
108	            Units::In => write!(f, "in"),
109	            Units::Ft => write!(f, "ft"),
110	            Units::Um => write!(f, "μm"),
111	        }
112	    }
113	}

119	/// brepper — Convert STL mesh to STEP with fitted analytic and freeform surfaces.
120	#[derive(Parser, Debug)]
121	#[command(name = "brepper", version, about)]
122	struct CliArgs {
123	    /// Input STL file (binary or ASCII).
124	    pub input_stl: String,
125	
126	    /// Output STEP file.
127	    #[arg(short = 'o', long = "output")]
128	    pub output_step: Option<String>,
129	
130	    /// Units used by the STL file.
131	    #[arg(long, default_value = "mm", value_enum)]
132	    pub stl_units: Units,
133	
134	    /// Units to use in exported STEP file.
135	    #[arg(long, default_value = "mm", value_enum)]
136	    pub step_units: Units,
137	
138	    /// STEP file to compare against at each stage.
139	    #[arg(long = "compare")]
140	    pub compare_step: Option<String>,
141	
142	    /// Fitting tolerance for vertex-to-surface distance, in STL units.
143	    #[arg(long, default_value = "5e-5")]
144	    pub vertex_tolerance: f64,
145	
146	    /// Tolerance for surface-to-triangle-face offset, in STL units.
147	    #[arg(long, default_value = "0.4")]
148	    pub surface_tolerance: f64,
149	
150	    /// Max dihedral angle between adjacent triangles on same surface, in
151	    /// degrees. Medium-resolution CAD exports step small-radius fillets up
152	    /// to ~24° between rows (Onshape "medium" enforces chordal deviation, so
153	    /// small features get few segments regardless of the angular preset);
154	    /// the default must admit those.
155	    #[arg(long, default_value = "25")]
156	    pub angular_tolerance: f64,
157	
158	    /// Increment verbosity by 1 per flag (-v = 1, -vv = 2, -vvv = 3).
159	    #[arg(short = 'v', action = ArgAction::Count)]
160	    pub verbose_short: u8,
161	
162	    /// Set verbosity to an explicit level:
163	    /// --verbose=1 (stage summaries),
164	    /// --verbose=2 (per-hypothesis details),
165	    /// --verbose=3 (per-committed-hypothesis seed/count info, stats, profiles),
166	    /// --verbose=4 (per-seed-attempt details),
167	    /// --verbose=5 (per-BFS-face exploration details).
168	    /// Bare --verbose sets level 1.
169	    #[arg(long = "verbose", value_name = "LEVEL", default_missing_value = "1", num_args = 0..=1)]
170	    pub verbose_level: Option<u8>,
171	
172	    /// Suppress non-error output.
173	    #[arg(short = 'q', long)]
174	    pub quiet: bool,
175	
176	    /// Fail on degenerate mesh faces instead of repairing them.
177	    #[arg(long)]
178	    pub strict_mesh: bool,
179	
180	    /// Enable debug output and intermediate files.
181	    #[arg(long)]
182	    pub debug: bool,
183	
184	    /// Stop after this stage (e.g. "2.2" or "2"). Default: run all stages.
185	    #[arg(long, value_parser = parse_stage)]
186	    pub stage: Option<Stage>,
187	
188	    /// Comma-separated list of sub-stages to skip entirely (e.g.
189	    /// "2.2,2.3,2.5,2.7" disables conical, spherical, toroidal, and NURBS
190	    /// recognition, leaving every mesh face to fall back to a planar
191	    /// hypothesis). Unlike --stage, which stops the pipeline early, skipped
192	    /// stages simply do nothing and the rest of the pipeline (selection,
193	    /// stage 3, stage 4) still runs through to output. Honored sub-stages:
194	    /// 2.2 (conical), 2.3 (spherical), 2.5 (toroidal), 2.7 (NURBS),
195	    /// 2.8 (redundant-surface absorption), 2.9 (boundary refinement).
196	    #[arg(long = "skip-stage", value_parser = parse_stage, value_delimiter = ',')]
197	    pub skip_stages: Option<Vec<Stage>>,

201	    pub viz_stages: Option<Vec<Stage>>,

206	    /// 3 = also pause at each BFS face acceptance.
207	    #[arg(long = "viz-stages-level", default_value = "1")]
208	    pub viz_stages_level: u8,
209	}

238	    pub verbosity: u8,

267	            .field("vertex_tolerance_mm", &self.vertex_tolerance_mm)
268	            .field("surface_tolerance_mm", &self.surface_tolerance_mm)

283	impl Config {
284	    fn from_cli(args: CliArgs) -> Self {
285	        let scale = args.stl_units.to_mm();
286	        Self {
287	            input_stl: args.input_stl,
288	            output_step: args.output_step,
289	            stl_units: args.stl_units,
290	            step_units: args.step_units,
291	            compare_step: args.compare_step,
292	            compare_shape: None,
293	            compare_face_count: 0,
294	            vertex_tolerance_mm: args.vertex_tolerance * scale,
295	            surface_tolerance_mm: args.surface_tolerance * scale,
296	            angular_tolerance_rad: args.angular_tolerance.to_radians(),
297	            verbosity: args.verbose_level.unwrap_or(0).max(args.verbose_short),
298	            verbose: args.verbose_level.unwrap_or(0).max(args.verbose_short) >= 1,
299	            quiet: args.quiet,
300	            strict_mesh: args.strict_mesh,
301	            debug: args.debug,
302	            stage: args.stage.unwrap_or_default(),
303	            skip_stages: args.skip_stages.unwrap_or_default(),
304	            viz_stages: args.viz_stages.unwrap_or_default(),
305	            viz_stages_level: args.viz_stages_level,
306	        }
307	    }
308	
309	    /// Check if a specific stage should be visualized.
310	    pub fn viz_active(&self, major: u8, minor: u8) -> bool {
311	        self.viz_stages.iter().any(|s| {
312	            let (sm, ss) = s.normalized();
313	            sm == major && ss == minor
314	        })
315	    }
316	
317	    /// Check if a specific sub-stage was named in --skip-stage. Matches the
318	    /// exact (major, minor) pair as parsed — unlike \`viz_active\`/\`at_least\`,
319	    /// a bare major (minor 0) is not expanded, since the recognition
320	    /// sub-stages this is meant for (2.2, 2.3, 2.5, 2.7) always need an
321	    /// explicit minor.
322	    pub fn skip_stage(&self, major: u8, minor: u8) -> bool {
323	        self.skip_stages.iter().any(|s| s.0 == major && s.1 == minor)
324	    }
325	
326	    /// If --compare was specified, load the STEP file shape for bounded distance comparison.
327	    pub fn load_compare_step(&mut self) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
328	        let step_path = match &self.compare_step {
329	            Some(p) => p.clone(),
330	            None => return Ok(()),
331	        };
332	
333	        let step_shape = crate::read_step_file(&step_path)
334	            .map_err(|e| -> Box<dyn std::error::Error> { e.into() })?;
335	
336	        // Count faces for validation and status output
337	        let mut face_count = 0_usize;
338	        let mut explorer = top_exp::Explorer::new_shape_shapeenum2(
339	            &step_shape,
340	            top_abs::ShapeEnum::Face,
341	            top_abs::ShapeEnum::Shape,
342	        );
343	        while explorer.more() {
344	            face_count += 1;
345	            explorer.next();
346	        }
347	
348	        if face_count == 0 {
349	            return Err(format!("STEP file {step_path} contains no faces").into());
350	        }
351	
352	        if !self.quiet {
353	            eprintln!("Loaded {} faces from comparison STEP file", face_count);
354	        }
355	
356	        self.compare_face_count = face_count;
357	        self.compare_shape = Some(step_shape);
358	
359	        Ok(())
360	    }
361	}
362	/// Parse command-line arguments and return a resolved Config.
363	pub fn parse_config() -> Config {
364	    Config::from_cli(CliArgs::parse())
365	}
366	
367	/// Parse from an explicit argument iterator (for testing or embedding).
368	pub fn parse_config_from<I, T>(args: I) -> Result<Config, clap::Error>
369	where
370	    I: IntoIterator<Item = T>,
371	    T: Into<std::ffi::OsString> + Clone,
372	{
373	    CliArgs::try_parse_from(args).map(Config::from_cli)
374	}

55	/// Lower bound on cross product magnitude |n₁ × n₂| for a valid cylinder/sphere
56	/// seed pair. Since |n₁ × n₂| = sin(θ) for unit normals, this corresponds to a
57	/// minimum dihedral angle of arcsin(0.01) ≈ 0.57° (~0.6°). Seed pairs closer
58	/// than this are too nearly parallel for numerically stable axis estimation
59	/// (cylinders) or sphere fitting (spheres). Together with \`angular_tol\` (the
60	/// upper bound, typically 17.5°), this defines the valid seed-pair window
61	/// [~0.6°, angular_tol].
62	pub(crate) const MIN_CROSS_THRESHOLD: f64 = 0.01;
63	
64	/// Fast-reject multiplier for BFS vertex-distance checks. When a candidate face
65	/// has a vertex farther than \`REFIT_SKIP_MULTIPLIER × vertex_tol\` from the
66	/// current fitted surface, the distance is too large for a re-fit to absorb and
67	/// the face is rejected immediately without attempting re-fitting.
68	/// Set to 10.0 to allow aggressive refitting — the refit itself validates all
69	/// faces, so the only cost of a high multiplier is more refit attempts.
70	pub(crate) const REFIT_SKIP_MULTIPLIER: f64 = 10.0;
71	
72	/// Minimum number of mesh faces required to accept a cylindrical hypothesis.
73	/// Any real CAD tessellation of a cylinder produces at least 3 facets around
74	/// the circumference; this rejects spurious 2-face fits (e.g. adjacent torus
75	/// facets that locally approximate a cylinder).
76	pub(crate) const MIN_CYLINDER_FACES: usize = 3;
77	
78	/// Minimum number of mesh faces required to accept a spherical hypothesis.
79	/// Sphere fitting has 4 degrees of freedom (cx, cy, cz, r), so at least 4
80	/// non-degenerate faces are needed for a well-determined fit. This also rejects
81	/// spurious fits from small patches that are consistent with many surface types.
82	pub(crate) const MIN_SPHERE_FACES: usize = 4;
83	
84	/// Minimum number of mesh faces required to accept a conical hypothesis.
85	/// A cone has 5 degrees of freedom (apex xyz, axis direction 2, half-angle),
86	/// so at least 6 faces are needed for a well-determined and robust fit.
87	pub(crate) const MIN_CONE_FACES: usize = 6;
88	
89	/// Minimum number of mesh faces required to accept a toroidal hypothesis.
90	/// A torus has 7 degrees of freedom (center xyz, axis direction 2, R, r),
91	/// so at least 7 faces are needed for a well-determined fit.
92	pub(crate) const MIN_TORUS_FACES: usize = 7;
93	
94	/// Maximum sphere radius as a multiple of the mesh bounding-box diagonal.
95	/// With solid-angle coverage validation and surface-tolerance validation during

97	/// growth. A large value serves as a numerical guardrail against degenerate fits.

1737	fn compute_seed_scores(mesh: &ConnectedMesh) -> (Vec<f64>, Vec<bool>) {
1738	    let n = mesh.faces.len();
1739	    let centroids: Vec<[f64; 3]> = mesh
1740	        .faces
1741	        .iter()
1742	        .map(|f| face_centroid(f, &mesh.vertices))
1743	        .collect();
1744	
1745	    // Step 1: per-face curvature summary.
1746	    let mut summary = vec![0.0_f64; n];
1747	    for fi in 0..n {
1748	        let Some(n1) = mesh.faces[fi].normal else { continue };
1749	        let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
1750	        for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
1751	            if ni < 0 {
1752	                continue;
1753	            }
1754	            let ni = ni as usize;
1755	            let Some(n2) = mesh.faces[ni].normal else { continue };
1756	            let d = dot3(&n1, &n2).clamp(-1.0, 1.0);
1757	            let theta = d.acos();
1758	            let dx = centroids[ni][0] - centroids[fi][0];
1759	            let dy = centroids[ni][1] - centroids[fi][1];
1760	            let dz = centroids[ni][2] - centroids[fi][2];
1761	            let dist = (dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz).sqrt();
1762	            if dist > 1e-12 {
1763	                summary[fi] = summary[fi].max(theta / dist);
1764	            }
1765	        }
1766	    }
1767	
1768	    // Step 2: raw score = max |summary difference| vs neighbors.
1769	    let mut score = vec![0.0_f64; n];
1770	    for fi in 0..n {
1771	        let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
1772	        for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
1773	            if ni >= 0 {
1774	                score[fi] = score[fi].max((summary[fi] - summary[ni as usize]).abs());
1775	            }
1776	        }
1777	    }
1778	
1779	    // Junction mask from the RAW score, before diffusion smears it. The
1780	    // criterion is LOCAL relative change: flag a face when its curvature
1781	    // changes by a large fraction of the local curvature magnitude. A
1782	    // mesh-global threshold fails here — sharp creases (κ jumps of several
1783	    // 1/mm) dominate the maximum and tangent fillet junctions (jumps of
1784	    // 1/r_fillet) fall under any fraction of it, yet tangent junctions are
1785	    // the primary target. Locally, a plane→fillet transition changes
1786	    // curvature by ~100% of the fillet curvature; interior faces of any
1787	    // uniform surface change by only tessellation noise.
1788	    let junction: Vec<bool> = (0..n)
1789	        .map(|fi| {
1790	            let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
1791	            let mut local_scale = summary[fi];
1792	            for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
1793	                if ni >= 0 {
1794	                    local_scale = local_scale.max(summary[ni as usize]);
1795	                }
1796	            }
1797	            local_scale > 1e-12 && score[fi] > 0.5 * local_scale
1798	        })
1799	        .collect();
1800	
1801	    // Step 3: diffusion (Jacobi — deterministic).
1802	    for _pass in 0..3 {
1803	        let mut next = vec![0.0_f64; n];
1804	        for fi in 0..n {
1805	            let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
1806	            let mut sum = 0.0_f64;
1807	            let mut count = 0_usize;
1808	            for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
1809	                if ni >= 0 {
1810	                    sum += score[ni as usize];
1811	                    count += 1;
1812	                }
1813	            }
1814	            next[fi] = if count > 0 {
1815	                0.5 * score[fi] + 0.5 * (sum / count as f64)
1816	            } else {
1817	                score[fi]
1818	            };
1819	        }
1820	        score = next;
1821	    }
1822	
1823	    (score, junction)
1824	}

<!-- msg_011Cd8FN89XyozyDkvNg8ojT -->

"The pipe-elbow strip problem" is this repo's canonical example of a correct surface that fit-driven growth can't discover because **no small seed neighborhood contains enough geometry to constrain the fit** — even though the surface fits the data perfectly.

**The setup.** `onshape_pipe_elbow` is a bent pipe: two straight cylindrical sections joined by a bend, and the bend is a torus patch (a circle swept along a 90° arc). CAD tessellators mesh swept surfaces anisotropically: the bend arrives as a stack of narrow quad **strips**, each strip a full ring around the tube (the minor circle, well sampled) but only one tessellation step along the sweep (the major arc, barely sampled). Real exporters do this for all swept/ruled surfaces — it's why the `tests/nurbs/` extrusion models deliberately ship as strip meshes too.

**Why local seeds fail.** A torus has 7 DOF, and the parameters that distinguish it from a cylinder — major radius R and axis — are only observable from how the tube *curves along the sweep*. A 1-ring seed sits essentially inside one strip: it spans maybe a degree of major arc. Over that span, the torus deviates from its osculating cylinder/cone by far less than vertex tolerance (the old plan noted "any adjacent pair of quad rows on a torus tube lies exactly on some cone"). So from any local seed:

- the **torus fit is ill-conditioned** — R and the axis are unconstrained by the data, the fit either fails or lands on garbage that doesn't validate; and
- the **cylinder fit succeeds** — the strip genuinely lies within tolerance of a cylinder.

BFS then grows the cylinder along the strip and *stalls at the strip boundary*: the next strip's vertices are off this strip's cylinder by more than vertex tolerance (the tube has visibly turned by then). Result: one hypothesis per strip. The model passed `--compare` with **290 cylindrical selections and 0 toroidal** — every strip individually within tolerance of the reference, which is why the old plan carried it as an accepted "nerfed" outcome for a while.

**The historical fixes** were all ways of manufacturing a bigger seed: first **strip-merge seeding** (commit 9555c8c) — when a 3-ring neighborhood spanned ≥2 distinct cylinder hypotheses, use it as a torus seed, because several strips together *do* span enough major arc to condition the fit — and later the hop-expanding direct toroidal seeds (up to 3 hops, targeting ≥16 faces) plus the toroidal-before-conical reordering, after which strip-merge became unreachable and was deleted (5691ea5). Note what these are: hand-tuned answers to "how big must a seed be to see the major curvature?", with the answer depending on tessellation density — i.e., exactly the kind of heuristic the redesign is trying to eliminate.

**Why I keep citing it in the architecture comparison:**

- The **seed-first inversion** (the contingency) doesn't fix it, because it changes *when* surface types compete but not *what the fitter sees*. From any elbow seed, the torus rung is still fed a 1-ring, still ill-conditioned, still loses; the cylinder rung wins its strip; the elbow decomposes into strips again. Rescuing it inside that design means re-adding escalation machinery ("when growth stalls, refit the stalled frontier at higher DOF using everything grown so far") — workable, but it's the strip-merge idea reborn.
- **Partition-then-classify** dissolves it structurally. The bend's interior edges are all smooth — dihedral steps are small, and the curvature descriptor varies *continuously* along the tube, so no curvature-jump boundary fires inside the bend. The whole bend is one region, and the ladder's torus rung fits it with vertices spanning the full 90° of major arc: R, axis, and r are all well-conditioned on the first try, with no seeding heuristics at all. The fit support is the maximal region rather than whatever a local neighborhood happens to sample — which is the general cure for anisotropic tessellation, not just for this model.

One adjacent caveat worth keeping in mind (distinct from the strip problem): the elbow's *junctions* — where the bend meets the straight pipes — are tangent tube-continuations, and their curvature jump is `σ_min`: 0 on the cylinder vs ~1/(R±r) on the torus, against a local scale of 1/r. That ratio is r/(R∓r), which for a typical elbow geometry hovers right around the J=0.5 threshold — so pipe_elbow is likely to be a calibration-interesting model for edge classification too, with the split repair as the backstop if the jump lands under threshold. The strips themselves, though, stop being a problem the moment the fit sees the whole region.

What you're describing is the classical "nested model family" trick: fit with the more general model, parameterized so the degenerate case is a *regular interior point* of the parameter space, and let the data pull it off the degenerate limit as support accumulates. The circle-fitting literature does exactly this for lines (Pratt/Taubin parameterize circles by curvature k so a line is just k=0, not r=∞). For your case: parameterize the torus by a point on the tube spine, spine direction, tube radius r, spine *curvature* k = 1/R, and a bending-plane azimuth — at k=0 that's exactly a cylinder, and k is a well-behaved LM parameter with no infinity anywhere. The growth story becomes: fit starts at k≈0 on one strip, expansion reaches the next strip, the refit including it makes k identifiable, LM discovers the bend, and the surface sweeps around the elbow. One fitter, no discrete "promote" event, no seed-size heuristics.

Three implementation realities to go with it:

1. **The fast-reject multiplier is the actual blocker, not the fitter.** The reason cylinder BFS stalls today isn't just that the cylinder can't bend — it's that the neighbor strip's vertices sit ~R·Δφ²/2 off the current fit, which for elbow-scale geometry is hundreds to thousands of times vertex tolerance, far outside the 10× refit window. So `REFIT_SKIP_MULTIPLIER` gating must change for the general model — e.g. attempt refits for candidates within *surface* tolerance (chordal) of the current fit, or batch-refit per stalled frontier rather than per face. That's where the performance tuning would live, since refits over the whole region are the expensive operation.

2. **The underdetermined phase needs regularization.** While support is one strip, k is unidentifiable — LM will wander unless you bias it toward k=0 (ridge toward the degenerate model, relaxed as support grows). Fiddly but standard. Note the exactness assumption protects against the scarier failure: extra flexibility can't help the model absorb faces from a genuinely different surface, because within-vertex-tolerance is still the acceptance bar, and two distinct true surfaces agreeing to 5e-5 over an extended patch would be near-identical. Flexibility only expands which *true* shapes you can represent — which is the point.

3. **Torus-only generalization doesn't finish the job.** A torus-that-can't-become-a-sphere has the dual problem: on a sphere, the bent-tube model locks onto a latitude band, closes the ring, and stalls — spheres get tiled by torus bands, the old pathology in new clothes. The logical endpoint of your idea is growing with a model family that contains *all* the primitives as degenerate cases — which is exactly the "Unified SOR framework" already sketched in SURFACE_FITTING.md's algorithm reference (spine + profile: plane/cylinder/cone/sphere/torus as profile-curve special cases; the Dupin cyclide family is the mathematically complete version of this). Then classification becomes model *reduction* at the end — collapse k≈0 to cylinder, collapse to sphere when the spine degenerates — rather than a ladder of separate fitters. Freeform remains outside any such family, so the B-spline path stays a separate mechanism regardless.

Where this lands in the architecture decision: it's the missing piece that repairs the seed-first contingency's worst weakness. Seed-first + degenerate-limit growth model handles the elbow, sphere bands, and coarse fillets without seed-topology heuristics — which makes the contingency genuinely competitive rather than a downgrade. Partition-first doesn't need it, because fitting the maximal region gives you full-arc support up front and the five simple fitters stay simple; narrow-region degeneracy there is handled discretely (simplest-fit-first, merge repair). So I'd file your idea as: **the upgrade that belongs inside the contingency** (and the fallback tool if some future model class defeats edge classification), not a reason to change the primary plan.

docs: rewrite DEVELOPMENT_PLAN — stage 2 becomes partition-then-classify

Full redesign of the stage-2 architecture on paper (no code change; the
tree still runs the BFS pipeline until the Rewrite Roadmap lands). The
fit-driven BFS hypothesis pipeline had accumulated heuristics-on-heuristics
— stage ordering, seeding masks, coverage acceptance tests, greedy
selection, absorb, refinement — each compensating for greedy commitment
and accidental sub-region exact fits. The new design attacks both causes
directly:

- Design Principles: exactness makes validation decisive; tessellators
  emit seam edges along B-rep boundaries even at tangencies (verified on
  the nosecone 2026-07-17), so the true segmentation is a partition of
  the face graph whose boundaries are mesh edges; fit only maximal
  regions so accidental sub-region fits are never hypothesized; repair by
  validation, locally; invariants (coverage, connectivity, per-region
  validity, determinism) enforced by assertion.
- New stage 2: 2.1 fit-free edge classification (sharp dihedral OR
  signed two-sided curvature-jump descriptor sigma_max/sigma_min, local-
  relative J=0.5 + noise floor; two-sided catches the capsule's equal-
  radius sphere/cylinder tangency via sigma_min), 2.2 connected-region
  extraction, 2.3 classification ladder in ascending DOF (plane, sphere,
  cylinder, cone, torus, freeform — first fit validating all vertices at
  vertex tolerance wins; per-facet planes are the terminal fallback, so
  planar-only mode becomes --surface-types=planar with no absorb slop),
  2.4 repair loop (merge = the tight absorb rule reborn at vertex
  tolerance; split = re-run 2.1 at lowered thresholds inside failing
  regions, preferring all-analytic splits before freeform; boundary
  relabel = old 2.9 promoted, with connectivity re-split), 2.5 unchanged
  SelectedSurface output for stage 3.
- Stages 1/3/4 carry over as as-built docs with cross-references fixed;
  the old 2.7 NURBS fitting machinery survives intact as the freeform
  rung (its region-gathering front end is superseded by the partition).
- Abandoned Approaches section: per-type BFS generation, stage ordering,
  seed ordering/junction/large_sphere masks, seed topologies, the four
  coverage/consistency acceptance tests, greedy area selection, absorb
  (tight rule's targets cannot form; loose rule already condemned by
  measurement), per-face multi-hypothesis fields, NURBS gathering — each
  with the measured evidence for why it existed and why it is now
  structurally unnecessary.
- Contingency section (considered, not chosen): seed-first multi-type
  competition — invert the old loops, all surface types compete from the
  same seed, largest-area-with-DOF-tiebreak wins; sound via the
  sub-region lemma but keeps small-seed conditioning and freeform

  growth model — parameterize the torus by spine curvature k=1/R so k=0

docs: rewrite DEVELOPMENT_PLAN — stage 2 becomes partition-then-classify

Full redesign of the stage-2 architecture on paper (no code change; the
tree still runs the BFS pipeline until the Rewrite Roadmap lands). The
fit-driven BFS hypothesis pipeline had accumulated heuristics-on-heuristics
— stage ordering, seeding masks, coverage acceptance tests, greedy
selection, absorb, refinement — each compensating for greedy commitment
and accidental sub-region exact fits. The new design attacks both causes
directly:

- Design Principles: exactness makes validation decisive; tessellators
  emit seam edges along B-rep boundaries even at tangencies (verified on
  the nosecone 2026-07-17), so the true segmentation is a partition of
  the face graph whose boundaries are mesh edges; fit only maximal
  regions so accidental sub-region fits are never hypothesized; repair by
  validation, locally; invariants (coverage, connectivity, per-region
  validity, determinism) enforced by assertion.
- New stage 2: 2.1 fit-free edge classification (sharp dihedral OR
  signed two-sided curvature-jump descriptor sigma_max/sigma_min, local-
  relative J=0.5 + noise floor; two-sided catches the capsule's equal-
  radius sphere/cylinder tangency via sigma_min), 2.2 connected-region
  extraction, 2.3 classification ladder in ascending DOF (plane, sphere,
  cylinder, cone, torus, freeform — first fit validating all vertices at
  vertex tolerance wins; per-facet planes are the terminal fallback, so
  planar-only mode becomes --surface-types=planar with no absorb slop),
  2.4 repair loop (merge = the tight absorb rule reborn at vertex
  tolerance; split = re-run 2.1 at lowered thresholds inside failing
  regions, preferring all-analytic splits before freeform; boundary
  relabel = old 2.9 promoted, with connectivity re-split), 2.5 unchanged
  SelectedSurface output for stage 3.
- Stages 1/3/4 carry over as as-built docs with cross-references fixed;
  the old 2.7 NURBS fitting machinery survives intact as the freeform
  rung (its region-gathering front end is superseded by the partition).
- Abandoned Approaches section: per-type BFS generation, stage ordering,
  seed ordering/junction/large_sphere masks, seed topologies, the four
  coverage/consistency acceptance tests, greedy area selection, absorb
  (tight rule's targets cannot form; loose rule already condemned by
  measurement), per-face multi-hypothesis fields, NURBS gathering — each
  with the measured evidence for why it existed and why it is now
  structurally unnecessary.
- Contingency section (considered, not chosen): seed-first multi-type
  competition — invert the old loops, all surface types compete from the
  same seed, largest-area-with-DOF-tiebreak wins; sound via the
  sub-region lemma but keeps small-seed conditioning and freeform
  problems. Its required upgrade if ever adopted: the degenerate-limit
  growth model — parameterize the torus by spine curvature k=1/R so k=0
  IS the cylinder (Pratt/Taubin-style), grow at k~0 with ridge
  regularization until the data identifies the bend; notes that the 10x
  REFIT_SKIP_MULTIPLIER window is the real pipe-elbow strip blocker and
  that a torus-only generalization would re-tile spheres with bands (the
  endpoint is the full SOR/Dupin-cyclide family with classification as
  model reduction).
- Rewrite Roadmap: one-shot transition — no reconciliation of old and new
  stage numbers; when 2.1/2.2 land the new numbering owns --stage and
  --viz-stages and the old BFS pipeline is nerfed in place (disconnected
  from stage2(), deleted in a later pass); suite red until 2.3-2.5 land,
  models re-enabled easiest first. Step 1 records the verified viz plan:
  boundary edges as class-colored LineOverlay segments, regions as
  per-region FaceHighlight with a deterministic palette; EdgeHighlight is
  NOT the right primitive (outlines whole faces) and stays TODO.md's
  delete candidate. Step 1's threshold calibration is the decision gate
  for falling back to the contingency.

//! Stage 2.1: fit-free edge classification.
//!
//! Labels every manifold mesh edge INTERIOR or BOUNDARY using two fit-free
//! signals (DEVELOPMENT_PLAN §2.1): a sharp dihedral angle, or a jump in the
//! per-face two-sided discrete-curvature descriptor (σ_max, σ_min) across
//! the edge. The true segmentation's boundaries are a subset of mesh edges
//! (tessellators emit seam edges along B-rep face boundaries, even at
//! tangencies), so this classification IS the segmentation; stage 2.2
//! extracts its connected regions and stage 2.4 (future) repairs mistakes.
//!
//! The curvature-jump rule runs iteratively: descriptors are computed over a
//! face's NON-boundary edges only, then edges are (re)classified, until the
//! classification is stable. The iteration exists to kill "ghost"
//! boundaries: the plane face bordering a tangent fillet inherits the
//! junction edge's transition curvature into its descriptor, which on round
//! one makes it differ from its plane neighbors one row in. Once the
//! junction edge is classified boundary it leaves the descriptor, the
//! plane face's descriptor returns to ≈0, and the ghost un-fires (the
//! junction edge itself keeps firing — the fillet side's descriptor is
//! supported by its interior cross-tube edges).

use super::{dot3, face_centroid};
use crate::stage1::ConnectedMesh;

/// Local-relative curvature-jump threshold J (DEVELOPMENT_PLAN §2.1): an
/// edge is a boundary when the descriptor jump exceeds this fraction of the
/// local curvature magnitude. Carried over from the junction-mask finding:
/// thresholds relative to a mesh-global maximum fail because sharp creases
/// dominate it while tangent junctions fall below any global fraction.
pub const JUMP_RATIO: f64 = 0.5;

/// Noise-floor coefficient: κ_floor = FLOOR_COEFF · vertex_tolerance / d²
/// per edge (centroid distance d). Vertex position noise ε perturbs the
/// dihedral by ~ε/d and the discrete curvature by ~ε/d²; the floor keeps
/// exact-coplanar plane interiors (κ ≡ 0 ± noise) from ever firing the
/// relative test. Calibration constant — revisit against the corpus.
pub const FLOOR_COEFF: f64 = 4.0;

/// Cap on classify/re-descriptor rounds. Convergence is typically 2–3
/// rounds (fire junctions, ghosts un-fire); the cap guards oscillation.
pub const MAX_ROUNDS: usize = 10;

/// Classification of one manifold mesh edge.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub enum EdgeClass {
    /// Both faces on the same surface region.
    #[default]
    Interior,
    /// Dihedral angle exceeds the angular tolerance — a hard feature edge.
    Sharp,
    /// G1-smooth but G2-discontinuous — a tangent junction found by the
    /// curvature-jump rule.
    Jump,
}

/// Stage 2.1 output: per-half-edge classes plus the curvature evidence,
/// kept for the 2.4 split repair (re-run at lowered thresholds), for
/// `--compare` diagnostics, and for viz.
///
/// All per-edge arrays are indexed `[face][slot]`, parallel to
/// `MeshFace.neighbors`: slot `e` is the edge from `vertex_indices[e]` to
/// `vertex_indices[(e+1) % vertex_count]`. Values are mirrored — the two
/// half-edges of a manifold edge always carry identical class/κ (computed
/// from symmetric formulas, not copied).
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct EdgeClassification {
    /// Class per half-edge. Slots without a manifold neighbor stay Interior
    /// (they never participate in region unions anyway).
    pub class: Vec<[EdgeClass; 4]>,
    /// Signed discrete normal curvature κ = ±θ/d per half-edge (positive
    /// convex, negative concave); NaN where no manifold neighbor.
    pub kappa: Vec<[f64; 4]>,
    /// Final per-face curvature descriptor: max signed κ over the face's
    /// non-boundary manifold edges (0.0 when it has none).
    pub sigma_max: Vec<f64>,
    /// Final per-face descriptor minimum (see `sigma_max`).
    pub sigma_min: Vec<f64>,
    /// Rounds until the jump classification stabilized (or MAX_ROUNDS).
    pub rounds: usize,
    /// Undirected manifold-edge counts by final class.
    pub sharp_count: usize,
    pub jump_count: usize,
    pub interior_count: usize,
}

impl EdgeClassification {
    /// Is the manifold edge across `faces[fi]`'s slot `e` a region boundary?
    pub fn is_boundary(&self, fi: usize, e: usize) -> bool {
        self.class[fi][e] != EdgeClass::Interior
    }
}

/// Classify every manifold mesh edge (stage 2.1). Deterministic, O(E) per
/// round with a small bounded round count.
pub fn classify_edges(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    vertex_tolerance: f64,
    angular_tolerance: f64,
) -> EdgeClassification {
    let n = mesh.faces.len();
    let centroids: Vec<[f64; 3]> = mesh
        .faces
        .iter()
        .map(|f| face_centroid(f, &mesh.vertices))
        .collect();

    // Per half-edge: signed κ, sharpness, and the noise floor. Each side is
    // computed independently from symmetric formulas, so mirrored slots get
    // identical values without explicit pairing.
    let mut kappa = vec![[f64::NAN; 4]; n];
    let mut sharp = vec![[false; 4]; n];
    let mut floor = vec![[f64::INFINITY; 4]; n];
    for fi in 0..n {
        let Some(n1) = mesh.faces[fi].normal else { continue };
        let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
        for e in 0..vc {
            let ni = mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[e];
            if ni < 0 {
                continue;
            }
            let ni = ni as usize;
            let Some(n2) = mesh.faces[ni].normal else { continue };
            let theta = dot3(&n1, &n2).clamp(-1.0, 1.0).acos();
            let dx = centroids[ni][0] - centroids[fi][0];
            let dy = centroids[ni][1] - centroids[fi][1];
            let dz = centroids[ni][2] - centroids[fi][2];
            let d = (dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz).sqrt();
            if d <= 1e-12 {
                continue;
            }
            // Sign: convex (+) when the neighbor's centroid lies below this
            // face's plane. Symmetric — for a convex edge each centroid is
            // below the other face's plane.
            let below = n1[0] * dx + n1[1] * dy + n1[2] * dz <= 0.0;
            kappa[fi][e] = if below { theta / d } else { -theta / d };
            sharp[fi][e] = theta > angular_tolerance;
            floor[fi][e] = FLOOR_COEFF * vertex_tolerance / (d * d);
        }
    }

    // Iterate: descriptors over non-boundary edges → (re)classify jumps.
    let mut jump = vec![[false; 4]; n];
    let mut sigma_max = vec![0.0_f64; n];
    let mut sigma_min = vec![0.0_f64; n];
    let mut rounds = 0;
    for _round in 0..MAX_ROUNDS {
        rounds += 1;
        for fi in 0..n {
            let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
            let mut smax = f64::NEG_INFINITY;
            let mut smin = f64::INFINITY;
            for e in 0..vc {
                let k = kappa[fi][e];
                if k.is_finite() && !sharp[fi][e] && !jump[fi][e] {
                    smax = smax.max(k);
                    smin = smin.min(k);
                }
            }
            if smax == f64::NEG_INFINITY {
                smax = 0.0;
                smin = 0.0;
            }
            sigma_max[fi] = smax;
            sigma_min[fi] = smin;
        }

        let mut changed = false;
        let mut new_jump = vec![[false; 4]; n];
        for fi in 0..n {
            let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
            for e in 0..vc {
                if !kappa[fi][e].is_finite() || sharp[fi][e] {
                    continue;
                }
                let ni = mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[e] as usize;
                let jmp = (sigma_max[fi] - sigma_max[ni])
                    .abs()
                    .max((sigma_min[fi] - sigma_min[ni]).abs());
                let scale = sigma_max[fi]
                    .abs()
                    .max(sigma_min[fi].abs())
                    .max(sigma_max[ni].abs())
                    .max(sigma_min[ni].abs());
                let fire = jmp > JUMP_RATIO * scale && jmp > floor[fi][e];
                new_jump[fi][e] = fire;
                if fire != jump[fi][e] {
                    changed = true;
                }
            }
        }
        jump = new_jump;
        if !changed {
            break;
        }
    }

    // Final classes + undirected counts.
    let mut class = vec![[EdgeClass::Interior; 4]; n];
    let (mut sharp_count, mut jump_count, mut interior_count) = (0, 0, 0);
    for fi in 0..n {
        let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
        for e in 0..vc {
            let ni = mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[e];
            if ni < 0 || !kappa[fi][e].is_finite() {
                continue;
            }
            class[fi][e] = if sharp[fi][e] {
                EdgeClass::Sharp
            } else if jump[fi][e] {
                EdgeClass::Jump
            } else {
                EdgeClass::Interior
            };
            if fi < ni as usize {
                match class[fi][e] {
                    EdgeClass::Sharp => sharp_count += 1,
                    EdgeClass::Jump => jump_count += 1,
                    EdgeClass::Interior => interior_count += 1,
                }
            }
        }
    }

    EdgeClassification {
        class,
        kappa,
        sigma_max,
        sigma_min,
        rounds,
        sharp_count,
        jump_count,
        interior_count,
    }
}

//! Stage 2.2: region extraction — connected components of the face graph
//! over INTERIOR edges (union-find). Regions are maximal, mesh-connected by
//! construction, and every face belongs to exactly one region (a single
//! facet is a valid region — the terminal per-facet-plane fallback of the
//! classification ladder depends on that). Region numbering is
//! deterministic: regions are ordered by their smallest member face index.

use super::edges::EdgeClassification;
use crate::stage1::ConnectedMesh;

/// One region of the partition: a maximal set of faces connected across
/// INTERIOR edges.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct Region {
    /// Member mesh face indices, ascending.
    pub faces: Vec<usize>,
    /// Member mesh vertex indices (union of face vertices), sorted, deduped.
    pub vertices: Vec<usize>,
}

fn find(parent: &mut [usize], mut x: usize) -> usize {
    while parent[x] != x {
        parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]; // path halving
        x = parent[x];
    }
    x
}

/// Extract regions from the edge classification. Returns
/// `(face_region, regions)` where `face_region[fi]` is the region id of
/// face `fi`.
pub fn extract_regions(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    edge_classes: &EdgeClassification,
) -> (Vec<usize>, Vec<Region>) {
    let n = mesh.faces.len();
    let mut parent: Vec<usize> = (0..n).collect();

    for fi in 0..n {
        let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
        for e in 0..vc {
            let ni = mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[e];
            if ni >= 0 && !edge_classes.is_boundary(fi, e) {
                let ra = find(&mut parent, fi);
                let rb = find(&mut parent, ni as usize);
                if ra != rb {
                    // Union by smaller root index keeps numbering stable.
                    parent[ra.max(rb)] = ra.min(rb);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    let mut face_region = vec![usize::MAX; n];
    let mut region_of_root = vec![usize::MAX; n];
    let mut regions: Vec<Region> = Vec::new();
    for fi in 0..n {
        let root = find(&mut parent, fi);
        let id = if region_of_root[root] == usize::MAX {
            regions.push(Region::default());
            region_of_root[root] = regions.len() - 1;
            regions.len() - 1
        } else {
            region_of_root[root]
        };
        face_region[fi] = id;
        regions[id].faces.push(fi);
    }

    for region in &mut regions {
        let mut vertices: Vec<usize> = region
            .faces
            .iter()
            .flat_map(|&fi| {
                let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
                mesh.faces[fi].vertex_indices[..vc].iter().copied()
            })
            .collect();
        vertices.sort_unstable();
        vertices.dedup();
        region.vertices = vertices;
    }

    (face_region, regions)
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Stage 2 entry: partition-then-classify (rewrite frontier = 2.2)

pub fn stage2(
    config: &Config,
    mesh: ConnectedMesh,
    viz: Option<&crate::viz::VizSender>,
) -> Result<Stage2Output, Stage2Error> {
    // --- Stage 2.1: edge classification (fit-free) ---
    let t = Instant::now();
    let edge_classes = edges::classify_edges(
        &mesh,
        config.vertex_tolerance_mm,
        config.angular_tolerance_rad,
    );
    if config.verbosity >= 1 {
        let total =
            edge_classes.sharp_count + edge_classes.jump_count + edge_classes.interior_count;
        eprintln!(
            "Stage 2.1 ({:.3}s): Edge classification: {} manifold edges — {} sharp, {} curvature-jump, {} interior ({} round{})",
            t.elapsed().as_secs_f64(),
            total,
            edge_classes.sharp_count,
            edge_classes.jump_count,
            edge_classes.interior_count,
            edge_classes.rounds,
            if edge_classes.rounds == 1 { "" } else { "s" },
        );
    }
    let mut segmentation = Segmentation {
        edge_classes,
        face_region: Vec::new(),
        regions: Vec::new(),
    };
    if config.viz_active(2, 1) {
        if let Some(vs) = viz {
            let overlay = segmentation_edges_overlay(&mesh, &segmentation.edge_classes);
            if matches!(vs.show_and_wait(overlay), VizAction::Quit) {
                return Ok(segmentation_only_output(mesh, segmentation));
            }
        }
    }
    if !config.stage.at_least(2, 2) {
        return Ok(segmentation_only_output(mesh, segmentation));
    }

    // --- Stage 2.2: region extraction ---
    let t = Instant::now();
    let (face_region, region_list) =
        regions::extract_regions(&mesh, &segmentation.edge_classes);
    if config.verbosity >= 1 {
        let single = region_list.iter().filter(|r| r.faces.len() == 1).count();
        let largest = region_list.iter().map(|r| r.faces.len()).max().unwrap_or(0);
        eprintln!(
            "Stage 2.2 ({:.3}s): Region extraction: {} regions over {} faces ({} single-face, largest {} faces)",
            t.elapsed().as_secs_f64(),
            region_list.len(),
            mesh.faces.len(),
            single,
            largest,
        );
        if config.verbosity >= 2 {
            for (i, r) in region_list.iter().enumerate() {
                if r.faces.len() > 1 {
                    eprintln!(
                        "  Region {}: {} faces, {} vertices (first face {})",
                        i,
                        r.faces.len(),
                        r.vertices.len(),
                        r.faces[0],
                    );
                }
            }
        }
    }
    segmentation.face_region = face_region;
    segmentation.regions = region_list;
    if config.viz_active(2, 2) {
        if let Some(vs) = viz {
            let overlay = segmentation_regions_overlay(&mesh, &segmentation);
            if matches!(vs.show_and_wait(overlay), VizAction::Quit) {
                return Ok(segmentation_only_output(mesh, segmentation));
            }
        }
    }

    // --- Rewrite frontier: 2.3 classification / 2.4 repair / 2.5 selection ---
    if config.stage.at_least(2, 3) && !config.quiet {
        eprintln!(
            "Stage 2.3+: not yet implemented (partition-then-classify rewrite in progress) — stopping after stage 2.2"
        );
    }
    Ok(segmentation_only_output(mesh, segmentation))
}

/// Stage2Output for the current rewrite frontier: segmentation only, no
/// hypotheses or selected surfaces (stages 3/4 are unreachable until the
/// classification ladder lands).
fn segmentation_only_output(mesh: ConnectedMesh, segmentation: Segmentation) -> Stage2Output {
    Stage2Output {
        mesh,
        planar_hypotheses: Vec::new(),
        conical_hypotheses: Vec::new(),
        spherical_hypotheses: Vec::new(),
        toroidal_hypotheses: Vec::new(),
        bspline_hypotheses: Vec::new(),
        selected_surfaces: Vec::new(),
        segmentation,
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Segmentation viz (--viz-stages=2.1 / 2.2)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

const SHARP_EDGE_COLOR: [f32; 4] = [0.9, 0.1, 0.1, 1.0];
const JUMP_EDGE_COLOR: [f32; 4] = [1.0, 0.6, 0.0, 1.0];

/// Boundary-edge line segments for viz, one segment per undirected boundary
/// edge, offset slightly along the adjacent faces' average normal so they
/// sit visibly on top of the rendered mesh instead of z-fighting it.
/// Returns (sharp_positions, jump_positions) as [p0, p1, p0, p1, ...] pairs.
fn boundary_line_positions(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    ec: &EdgeClassification,
) -> (Vec<[f32; 3]>, Vec<[f32; 3]>) {
    let mut min = [f64::INFINITY; 3];
    let mut max = [f64::NEG_INFINITY; 3];
    for v in &mesh.vertices {
        for (k, c) in [v.x, v.y, v.z].into_iter().enumerate() {
            min[k] = min[k].min(c);
            max[k] = max[k].max(c);
        }
    }
    let diag = ((max[0] - min[0]).powi(2)
        + (max[1] - min[1]).powi(2)
        + (max[2] - min[2]).powi(2))
    .sqrt();
    let offset = if diag.is_finite() { diag * 5e-4 } else { 0.0 };

    let mut sharp = Vec::new();
    let mut jump = Vec::new();
    for fi in 0..mesh.faces.len() {
        let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
        for e in 0..vc {
            let ni = mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[e];
            if ni < fi as i32 {
                continue; // open edge, or emitted from the other side
            }
            let class = ec.class[fi][e];
            if class == EdgeClass::Interior {
                continue;
            }
            let n1 = mesh.faces[fi].normal.unwrap_or([0.0; 3]);
            let n2 = mesh.faces[ni as usize].normal.unwrap_or(n1);
            let mut nn = [n1[0] + n2[0], n1[1] + n2[1], n1[2] + n2[2]];
            let len = (nn[0] * nn[0] + nn[1] * nn[1] + nn[2] * nn[2]).sqrt();
            if len > 1e-12 {
                for c in &mut nn {
                    *c /= len;
                }
            } else {
                nn = [0.0; 3];
            }
            let va = &mesh.vertices[mesh.faces[fi].vertex_indices[e]];
            let vb = &mesh.vertices[mesh.faces[fi].vertex_indices[(e + 1) % vc]];
            let pa = [
                (va.x + nn[0] * offset) as f32,
                (va.y + nn[1] * offset) as f32,
                (va.z + nn[2] * offset) as f32,
            ];
            let pb = [
                (vb.x + nn[0] * offset) as f32,
                (vb.y + nn[1] * offset) as f32,
                (vb.z + nn[2] * offset) as f32,
            ];
            let out = if class == EdgeClass::Sharp {
                &mut sharp
            } else {
                &mut jump
            };
            out.push(pa);
            out.push(pb);
        }
    }
    (sharp, jump)
}

fn push_boundary_lines(overlay: &mut viz::VizOverlay, mesh: &ConnectedMesh, ec: &EdgeClassification) {
    let (sharp, jump) = boundary_line_positions(mesh, ec);
    if !sharp.is_empty() {
        overlay.lines.push(viz::LineOverlay {
            positions: sharp,
            color: SHARP_EDGE_COLOR,
            no_depth_test: false,
        });
    }
    if !jump.is_empty() {
        overlay.lines.push(viz::LineOverlay {
            positions: jump,
            color: JUMP_EDGE_COLOR,
            no_depth_test: false,
        });
    }
}

fn segmentation_edges_overlay(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, ec: &EdgeClassification) -> viz::VizOverlay {
    let mut overlay = viz::VizOverlay::new();
    overlay.status_text = format!(
        "Stage 2.1: edge classification — {} sharp (red), {} curvature-jump (orange), {} interior [space=continue, q=quit]",
        ec.sharp_count, ec.jump_count, ec.interior_count,
    );
    push_boundary_lines(&mut overlay, mesh, ec);
    overlay
}

/// Deterministic distinct color for region `i`: golden-ratio hue stepping.
fn region_color(i: usize) -> [f32; 4] {
    let h = (i as f64 * 0.618_033_988_749_895).fract() * 6.0;
    let sector = (h.floor() as i32).rem_euclid(6);
    let f = h - h.floor();
    let (s, v) = (0.55, 0.9);
    let p = v * (1.0 - s);
    let q = v * (1.0 - s * f);
    let t = v * (1.0 - s * (1.0 - f));
    let (r, g, b) = match sector {
        0 => (v, t, p),
        1 => (q, v, p),
        2 => (p, v, t),
        3 => (p, q, v),
        4 => (t, p, v),
        _ => (v, p, q),
    };
    [r as f32, g as f32, b as f32, 1.0]
}

fn segmentation_regions_overlay(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, seg: &Segmentation) -> viz::VizOverlay {
    let mut overlay = viz::VizOverlay::new();
    let single = seg.regions.iter().filter(|r| r.faces.len() == 1).count();
    let largest = seg.regions.iter().map(|r| r.faces.len()).max().unwrap_or(0);
    overlay.status_text = format!(
        "Stage 2.2: {} regions ({} single-face, largest {} faces) — boundaries: sharp red / jump orange [space=continue, q=quit]",
        seg.regions.len(),
        single,
        largest,
    );
    overlay.face_highlights = seg
        .regions
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(i, r)| viz::FaceHighlight {
            face_indices: r.faces.clone(),
            color: region_color(i),
        })
        .collect();
    push_boundary_lines(&mut overlay, mesh, &seg.edge_classes);
    overlay
}
