**Before:**
```markdown
#### 2.4 Repair loop

Runs after initial classification; fixes the two 2.1 failure modes
(over-segmentation and missed seams) plus row-level boundary error, by
validation-driven local operations. Iterate the three operations in a
deterministic order (by region index; smallest region first for merges) to a
fixpoint, bounded rounds.

**Merge** — repairs over-segmentation (coarse-cone banding; any residual
same-surface fragmentation): merge region S into an adjacent larger region T
when every vertex of S lies within `--vertex-tolerance` of T's fitted
surface and every centroid of S within `--surface-tolerance`; refit the
union, revalidate, keep only if valid. This is the abandoned absorb pass's
*tight* rule reborn with a principled criterion (vertex tolerance, at which
"on the same surface" is decisive — never the chordal slop of the abandoned
loose rule, which put absorbed facets up to 0.4mm off their claimed plane
and caused 794 BRepCheck failures on planar-only 3DBenchy). It also folds in
chord-degenerate narrow strips (a single-facet-wide band of a coarse
cylinder validates rung-1 as its own facet plane, but its vertices lie
exactly on the neighbor cylinder, so merge claims it).

**Split** — repairs missed seams (a region that fails every rung is
presumed to be several surfaces): re-run the 2.1 curvature-jump classifier
on the region's internal edges at progressively lower thresholds (J/2, J/4,
…) until the region separates; classify the components. Acceptance
preference, in order:
1. A split whose components ALL classify analytically → accept (this is how
   a fillet↔cylinder junction with similar radii — below the global J — is
   recovered).
2. Otherwise, try the freeform rung on the *whole* region (a genuine
   freeform surface has no internal jump structure worth splitting on; this
   ordering also prevents a smooth-but-merged analytic pair from
   reconstructing as one plausible-but-wrong freeform patch that would erase
   a reference edge).
3. Otherwise accept the best split and recurse on its components. Terminal
   case: a single facet always classifies as a plane, so this ladder cannot
   fail to terminate — the worst case degrades to per-facet planes (exactly
   the planar-only mode that runs 3DBenchy end-to-end), never to a
   conversion failure.

**Boundary relabel** — repairs ±1-row boundary error (the 2.1 classifier and
tessellation can place a tangent boundary one facet row off the true
junction, which would shift stage 3's reconstructed boundary vertices off
the feature curves): walk faces with a neighbor in a different region;
compute the face's max vertex distance to its own surface and to each
adjacent region's surface; move the face when an adjacent surface fits at
least **2× better** (margin prevents oscillation for true junction faces,
whose vertices lie on both surfaces equally). Iterate to a fixpoint (≤ 10
rounds; boundaries only move locally), then rebuild affected regions'
vertex lists. Region *geometry* is not refitted — the fits were validated
against the region interior; only the membership map changes. This is the
previous architecture's `refine_boundary_assignments` promoted from a
fix-up pass to a core mechanism. After relabeling, re-split any region that
became disconnected (each fragment keeps the shared fitted geometry as its
own region — connectivity is the invariant; identical geometry on two
non-adjacent regions is legal).

**Post-2.4 invariants (hard assertions before stage 3):**
- Every mesh face belongs to exactly one region (total coverage).
- Every region is mesh-connected.
- Every region's surface validates the region's own vertices/centroids.
```

**After:**
```markdown
#### 2.4 Resolution & repair

Turns 2.3's claims into a strict, connected, validated partition. All
operations are fit-validated and deterministic (fixed iteration order —
by region/hypothesis index, smallest region first for merges — bounded
rounds).

**Claim resolution** — the boundary placement at tangent junctions: faces
claimed by multiple hypotheses (junction rows) go to the claimant whose
surface fits their vertices best, requiring a **2× margin** to prefer a
different side than the larger claimant (a true junction face fits both
sides equally — the margin prevents arbitrary flapping; residual ties
break to the larger claimant, then lower hypothesis index). Exact vertex
distances, no curvature involved.

**Boundary relabel** (±1-row polish; port of the old
`refine_boundary_assignments`): after resolution, walk region-boundary
faces; move a face when an adjacent region's surface fits its vertices at
least 2× better; iterate to a fixpoint (≤ 10 rounds; boundaries only move
locally), then rebuild affected regions' vertex lists. Region *geometry*
is not refitted — only the membership map changes.

**Merge**: absorb region S into an adjacent larger region T when every
vertex of S lies within `--vertex-tolerance` of T's fitted surface and
every centroid of S within `--surface-tolerance`; refit the union,
revalidate, keep only if valid. Eats junction-circle singletons (faces
whose vertices sit ON a tangent seam — genuinely ambiguous, claimable by
either side), chord-degenerate slivers (a single-facet-wide band of a
coarse cylinder validates as its own facet plane, but its vertices lie
exactly on the neighbor cylinder), and residual same-surface fragments.
This is the abandoned absorb pass's *tight* rule reborn with a principled
criterion — vertex tolerance, at which "on the same surface" is decisive;
never the chordal slop of the abandoned loose rule (0.4mm slop, 794
BRepCheck failures on planar-only 3DBenchy). B-spline surfaces are never
merge TARGETS for faces outside their fitted region: a fit vouches only
for its data (the island-dissolution guard in 2.3(e) is the fit-validated
way into a freeform patch).

**Connectivity re-split + invariants** (hard assertions before stage 3):
resolution and relabeling can disconnect a region — re-split into
mesh-connected components (identical fitted geometry on two non-adjacent
regions is legal). Then assert: every mesh face belongs to exactly one
region (total coverage); every region is mesh-connected; every region's
surface validates the region's own vertices/centroids.

(The old standalone "split repair" is gone: under-segmentation cannot
survive 2.3 — competition decomposes within smooth regions — and a region
nothing explains degrades to per-facet planes via 2.3(e). There is no
mechanism left that re-runs a curvature classifier at lowered thresholds;
that mechanism died with the classifier.)
```

### Resolution (2026-07-20): pivot decided

The "build 2.3/2.4 next as the make-or-break test" recommendation above
was overtaken by evidence. Direct measurement with `dump_regions` on the
corpus:

- **nosecone_medium**: the sphere is ONE clean 644-face region reading
  σ = (0.080, 0.080) = 1/12.5 — and the cone is **129 fragments whose
  descriptors show a clean gradient**: (0.00, 0.00) at the wide base →
  (0.02, 0) mid-cone → (0.08, 0) near the tip. The estimator measures
  correctly — κ_max = 1/ρ(h) genuinely varies along a cone — and a
  threshold on first differences of curvature fires on real gradients. A
  false-positive *class*, not a bug.
- The same statistic must stay blind at 0.35 to those gradient steps
  while firing at 0.33 for pipe_elbow's genuine torus↔cylinder junction:

```markdown
## Contingency: Seed-First Multi-Type Competition

Not abandoned — considered (2026-07-17) and not chosen. This is the fallback
design if stage 2.1's curvature-jump calibration proves unreliable in
practice (coarse fillets, f32 quantization noise defeating `J`/`κ_floor`
tuning). Recorded so the option and its rationale don't get lost.

**The design**: keep fit-driven BFS growth, but invert the old pipeline's
loops. Iterate over seed faces in curvature-score order (interior faces
first — the existing seed-ordering heuristics); skip faces already claimed
by a committed hypothesis. For each seed, run *every* surface type's
fit-and-expand from that same seed, and commit the hypothesis with the
largest supported area (with a simplest-DOF tiebreak). Expansion may grow
through already-claimed faces — junction faces whose vertices genuinely lie
on two surfaces end up claimed by both — but claimed faces never seed. After
all faces are claimed, resolve overlaps into a strict partition (per-face
best-fit among claimants, the boundary-relabel rule) and re-split any
disconnected remnant.

**Why it is sound, not heuristic** (under the exactness assumption): an
accidental fit is by definition supported on a *sub-region* — the true
surface fitted from an interior seed expands, with vertex tolerance as the
arbiter, to the entire region, so when all types compete on the *same* seed,
largest-area-wins selects the true surface. The old pipeline compared
hypotheses born from different seeds at different times, which is why commit
order mattered. Cross-region leakage is bounded: two distinct analytic
surfaces agreeing to vertex tolerance over an extended patch would be
near-identical, so overlap is confined to genuine junction rows.

**What it fixes without any masks or ordering**: fragmentation (an
interior-seeded surface covers its whole region regardless of prior
commits), stage ordering (per-seed competition replaces it), and the
accidental-fit tiling cost (each region pays ~5 bounded expansions once,
not per-face — the large_sphere pathology disappears without masking). Its
distinctive strength over partition-then-classify: **boundary placement
never depends on discrete curvature estimates** — the fit itself finds the
boundary from exact vertex distances (the capsule's equal-radius
sphere↔cylinder junction needs no two-sided descriptor here), and curvature
ordering errors cost only efficiency, never correctness.

**Why it was not chosen**:
1. Small-seed fit conditioning is unsolved — fits still start from 1-rings/
   fans, so the pipe-elbow torus (strip tessellation; a 1-ring spans no
   major arc) again decomposes into cylinder strips. The degenerate-limit
   growth model below repairs this, at the cost of the machinery it
   describes. Partition-first instead fits the whole region at once and
   needs none of it.
2. Freeform stays second-class: a B-spline patch cannot compete from a seed
   (parameterization needs a bounded region), so freeform surfaces get
   tiled by their largest accidental analytic patches and the old
   leftover-gathering + confetti-absorption heuristics return. (The
   degenerate-limit model does not help here — no analytic family contains
   B-splines.)
3. The residual heuristic surface is larger: overlap resolution + remnant
   re-split, degeneracy guards and the DOF tiebreak (on a plane region a
   near-infinite-radius cylinder *ties* the plane on area), a "good enough
   to suppress seeding" definition, and load-bearing seed ordering.

**Required upgrade if adopted — degenerate-limit growth model** (identified
2026-07-17): grow with a model family whose degenerate cases are *regular
interior points* of the parameter space, so the fit explores as the simpler
surface until the data pulls it off the limit. Concretely for the strip
problem: parameterize the torus by a point on the tube spine, spine
direction, tube radius `r`, spine **curvature** `k = 1/R`, and a
bending-plane azimuth — `k = 0` *is* the cylinder, with no infinity
anywhere (the Pratt/Taubin curvature parameterization that circle fitters
use to make lines a regular case). Growth starts at `k ≈ 0` on one strip;
the refit that admits the neighboring strip makes `k` identifiable and LM
discovers the bend — no seed-size machinery, no discrete promotion event.
Three consequences to design for:
- *The refit trigger, not the fitter, is the actual blocker.* A neighboring
  strip sits ~`R·Δφ²/2` off the current fit — hundreds to thousands of
  times vertex tolerance, far outside the `REFIT_SKIP_MULTIPLIER` (10×)
  window that gates refit attempts today. The general model needs refits
  triggered by *chordal* (surface-tolerance) proximity, or batched per
  stalled frontier; this is where the performance cost concentrates, since
  refits run LM over the whole grown region.
- *The underdetermined phase needs regularization.* While support spans one
  strip, `k` is unidentifiable; ridge the fit toward `k = 0` and relax the
  bias as support grows. The exactness assumption bounds the
  over-flexibility risk: added flexibility cannot absorb faces of a
  genuinely different surface, because within-vertex-tolerance remains the
  acceptance bar and two distinct surfaces agreeing to that tolerance over
  an extended patch would be near-identical.
- *A torus-only generalization re-creates the dual pathology*: a bent-tube
  model that cannot degenerate further locks onto a sphere's latitude band,
  closes the ring, and stalls — spheres get tiled by torus bands again. The
  logical endpoint is growing with a family containing **all** the analytic
  primitives as degenerate cases — the Unified SOR framework of
  SURFACE_FITTING.md (Dupin cyclides are the mathematically complete
  version) — after which classification becomes model *reduction* (collapse
  `k ≈ 0` to cylinder, a degenerate spine to sphere) instead of a ladder of
  fitters. Freeform stays outside any such family.

If adopted, the 2.4 repair loop, the post-stage-2 invariants, and the 2.5
output contract apply to its results unchanged — only 2.1–2.3 would be
replaced by the seed-competition driver (plus the degenerate-limit growth
model above).

---

## Abandoned Approaches

Retired with the 2026-07-17 stage-2 redesign. Recorded here because each
worked well enough to ship models, and some may be worth resurrecting as
*diagnostics* — but all of them existed to compensate for fit-driven greedy
segmentation, and the compensations kept multiplying (that treadmill is why
the architecture changed). Do not re-add one without identifying which
design principle it would compensate for.
```

Retired with the 2026-07-17 stage-2 redesign and the 2026-07-20 fit-driven

junctions from local curvature-descriptor differences, without fitting.
Five estimator variants (per-edge κ = θ/d → neighbor-normal tensor →

rejection) each fixed one corpus class and broke another. Terminal
evidence (measurements in the Stage-2 Retrospective's Resolution): the
decision statistic — a threshold on local differences of principal
curvatures — cannot separate real curvature *gradients* on one surface

threshold exists, and the hysteresis fixpoint oscillated to its round cap
on every fragmenting model. What survives: the sharp-dihedral rule
(exact, load-bearing in §2.1(a)) and the anchored osculating-jet
estimator itself — an accurate interior-curvature field, demoted to the
§2.1(b) prior whose errors can only cost time (Design Principle #4). Do
not resurrect a fit-free junction detector without a statistic that
provably separates gradients from jumps on staggered tessellations.

the recovery that works is fit validation at vertex tolerance — curvature
is reliable only where dihedral angles already decide (sharp edges) or in
roles where errors cost time instead of correctness (the prior).

## Abandoned Approaches

Retired with the 2026-07-17 stage-2 redesign and the 2026-07-20 fit-driven
pivot. Recorded here because each worked well enough to ship models — but
each existed to compensate for a structural defect elsewhere, and the
compensations kept multiplying (that treadmill is why the architecture
changed, twice). Do not re-add one without identifying which design
principle it would compensate for.

**Fit-free curvature-jump edge classification** (built 2026-07-18/19,
retired 2026-07-20): the attempt to detect tangent (G1-smooth,
G2-discontinuous) junctions from local curvature-descriptor differences,
without fitting. Five estimator variants (per-edge κ = θ/d →
neighbor-normal tensor → jet with outlier rejection → re-weighted jet →
anchored jet without rejection) each fixed one corpus class and broke
another. Terminal evidence (measurements in the Stage-2 Retrospective's
Resolution): the decision statistic — a threshold on local differences of
principal curvatures — cannot separate real curvature *gradients* on one
surface (a cone's κ_max = 1/ρ(h); gradient steps read > 0.35 and
shattered nosecone's cone into 129 fragments while its sphere stayed one
clean 644-face region) from real *junctions* between surfaces with
similar curvatures (pipe_elbow's torus↔cylinder junction reads 0.33,
missed). The classes overlap, so no threshold exists, and the hysteresis
fixpoint oscillated to its round cap on every fragmenting model. What
survives: the sharp-dihedral rule (exact, load-bearing in §2.1(a)) and
the anchored osculating-jet estimator itself — an accurate
interior-curvature field, demoted to the §2.1(b) prior whose errors can
only cost time (Design Principle #4). Do not resurrect a fit-free
junction detector without a statistic that provably separates gradients
from jumps on staggered tessellations.
```
</details>

## Visualization (\`--viz-stages\`)

The \`--viz-stages\` flag enables interactive 3D visualization for debugging pipeline stages. The companion \`--viz-stages-level\` flag (default 1) controls pause granularity.

Supported stages after the rewrite:
- **2.1**: edge classification — BOUNDARY edges drawn as \`LineOverlay\`

  color palette, boundary \`LineOverlay\` retained for context.

## Testing Strategy

The main testing strategy is to process a set of example stl/step pairs, and use the --compare flag to ensure that the pipeline is working correctly for each.

1. **Unit Tests**: Individual components (readers, fitters, edge classifier, region extraction, repair operations)
2. **Integration Tests**: Full pipeline on known geometries
3. **Regression Tests**: Compare output STEP to reference
4. **Validation**: Round-trip test (STEP → mesh → STEP)

Stage-2 integration tests assert:
- Edge classification / partition sanity per model (with \`--compare\`: region
  boundary edges near reference edges; region interiors mapping to
  consistent reference surfaces).
- Region classification end states — the same expectations the old suite
  pinned (cube = 6 planar; block_with_hole = 6 planar + 1 cylindrical;
  pipe = 2 planar + 2 cylindrical; ball_on_cylinder = 1 planar +
  1 cylindrical + 1 spherical; hemisphere = 1 planar + 1 spherical;
  cone_15x20 = 1 planar + 1 conical; etc.), plus fitted-parameter agreement
  with the reference STEP (axis, radius, center) for analytic models.
- Repair-loop behavior on the models that motivated it (coarse cones
  re-merged; capsule junction found; stepped_block narrow walls kept as
  real planar regions).

**Migration reality**: the suite is red during the rewrite (see Rewrite
Roadmap step 6). Re-enable per model; a model stays disabled with a comment
naming its blocker rather than being nerfed with loosened gates.

### Test Cases

See [tests/RESULTS.md](tests/RESULTS.md) for the full test results table.
Generated by: \`./scripts/run_test_table.sh [path/to/brepper]\`

  design principle: curvature allocates effort — seed order, rung

  bands — and never decides membership or boundaries; vertex-tolerance

77	    Spherical(SphericalHypothesis),
78	}
79	
80	impl CompeteHyp {
81	    fn faces(&self) -> &[usize] {
82	        match self {
83	            CompeteHyp::Planar(h) => &h.faces,
84	            CompeteHyp::Conical(h) => &h.faces,
85	            CompeteHyp::Spherical(h) => &h.faces,
86	        }
87	    }
88	    fn set_faces(&mut self, faces: Vec<usize>, verts: Vec<usize>) {
89	        match self {
90	            CompeteHyp::Planar(h) => {
91	                h.faces = faces;
92	                h.vertices = verts;
93	            }
94	            CompeteHyp::Conical(h) => {
95	                h.faces = faces;
96	                h.vertices = verts;
97	            }
98	            CompeteHyp::Spherical(h) => {
99	                h.faces = faces;
100	                h.vertices = verts;
101	            }
102	        }
103	    }
104	}

106	/// Decompose a tangent-chain region. Returns the committed analytic
107	/// hypotheses (a strict partition after claim resolution) plus the leftover
108	/// faces no hypothesis explained.
109	pub(super) fn compete_region(
110	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
111	    region: &Region,
112	    jet: &[JetField],
113	    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
114	    config: &Config,
115	) -> (Vec<CompeteHyp>, Vec<usize>) {
116	    let n = mesh.faces.len();
117	    let debug = config.verbosity >= 3 || std::env::var("BREPPER_DEBUG_COMPETE").is_ok();
118	    let mut in_region = vec![false; n];
119	    for &fi in &region.faces {
120	        in_region[fi] = true;
121	    }
122	
123	    // Region curvature scale: a face reads "flat" when its principal
124	    // curvature radius exceeds a couple of region diameters.
125	    let extent = region_extent(mesh, region);
126	    let flat_eps = if extent > 0.0 { 1.0 / (2.0 * extent) } else { 1e-6 };
127	
128	    // Seed order: jet-interior-first (ascending curvature mismatch with
129	    // region neighbors), ties by face index for determinism.
130	    let mut seeds = region.faces.clone();
131	    let score: Vec<f64> = (0..n)
132	        .map(|fi| {
133	            if !in_region[fi] {
134	                return f64::INFINITY;
135	            }
136	            neighbor_jet_mismatch(mesh, fi, jet, &in_region)
137	        })
138	        .collect();
139	    seeds.sort_by(|&a, &b| {
140	        score[a]
141	            .partial_cmp(&score[b])
142	            .unwrap()
143	            .then_with(|| a.cmp(&b))
144	    });
145	
146	    let mut claimed = vec![false; n]; // out of the seed pool once claimed
147	    let mut committed: Vec<CompeteHyp> = Vec::new();
148	    let mut claim_lists: Vec<Vec<usize>> = vec![Vec::new(); n]; // face -> committed idxs
149	
150	    for &seed in &seeds {
151	        if claimed[seed] {
152	            continue;
153	        }
154	        let jf = jet[seed];
155	        let a1 = jf.k1.abs();
156	        let a2 = jf.k2.abs();
157	
158	        // Grow the jet-pruned candidate types; keep the largest validated
159	        // area (simplest-DOF tiebreak).
160	        let mut best: Option<(CompeteHyp, f64, u8)> = None; // (hyp, area, dof)
161	        let consider = |hyp_area: Option<(CompeteHyp, f64)>, dof: u8, best: &mut Option<(CompeteHyp, f64, u8)>| {
162	            if let Some((h, area)) = hyp_area {
163	                let better = match best {
164	                    None => true,
165	                    Some((_, ba, bd)) => area > *ba + 1e-9 || ((area - *ba).abs() <= 1e-9 && dof < *bd),
166	                };
167	                if better {
168	                    *best = Some((h, area, dof));
169	                }
170	            }
171	        };
172	
173	        // Plane is always a candidate (cheap; catches misread flats).
174	        let plane = grow::<PlanarSurface>(mesh, &in_region, seed, jet, centroids, config, 1);
175	        let mut cone_area = None;
176	        let mut sphere_area = None;
177	        if a1 >= flat_eps {
178	            // Curved: a developable (cylinder/cone) is always plausible.
179	            let cone = grow::<ConicalSurface>(mesh, &in_region, seed, jet, centroids, config, MIN_CYLINDER_FACES);
180	            cone_area = cone.as_ref().map(|(_, a, f)| (*a, f.len()));
181	            consider(cone.map(|(h, a, _)| (CompeteHyp::Conical(h), a)), 2, &mut best);
182	            // Curved in both directions → also try a sphere.
183	            if a2 >= 0.3 * a1 {
184	                let sphere = grow::<SphericalSurface>(mesh, &in_region, seed, jet, centroids, config, MIN_SPHERE_FACES);
185	                sphere_area = sphere.as_ref().map(|(_, a, f)| (*a, f.len()));
186	                consider(sphere.map(|(h, a, _)| (CompeteHyp::Spherical(h), a)), 1, &mut best);
187	            }
188	        }
189	        let plane_area = plane.as_ref().map(|(_, a, f)| (*a, f.len()));
190	        consider(plane.map(|(h, a, _)| (CompeteHyp::Planar(h), a)), 0, &mut best);
191	
192	        if debug && best.is_none() {
193	            eprintln!(
194	                "    compete: seed {seed} jet=({:.3},{:.3}) class {:?} → NO GROWTH (plane {plane_area:?} cone {cone_area:?} sphere {sphere_area:?})",
195	                jf.k1, jf.k2, curvature_class(jf),
196	            );
197	        }
198	
199	        match best {
200	            Some((hyp, area, dof)) => {
201	                if debug {
202	                    let kind = match hyp {
203	                        CompeteHyp::Planar(_) => "plane",
204	                        CompeteHyp::Conical(ref h) => if h.is_cylinder() { "cyl" } else { "cone" },
205	                        CompeteHyp::Spherical(_) => "sphere",
206	                    };
207	                    eprintln!(
208	                        "    compete: seed {seed} → {kind} ({} faces, area {area:.2}, dof {dof})",
209	                        hyp.faces().len()
210	                    );
211	                }
212	                let idx = committed.len();
213	                for &f in hyp.faces() {
214	                    claimed[f] = true;
215	                    claim_lists[f].push(idx);
216	                }
217	                committed.push(hyp);
218	            }
219	            None => {
220	                // The seed grows nothing analytic; drop it from the pool so
221	                // the loop terminates. It becomes a leftover.
222	                claimed[seed] = true;
223	            }
224	        }
225	    }
226	
227	    resolve_claims(mesh, &region.faces, &mut committed, &claim_lists)
228	}
229	
230	/// Resolve multi-claimed faces to their best-fitting claimant (2× margin to
231	/// leave the larger claimant), rebuild each hypothesis's face/vertex lists,
232	/// drop hypotheses that lost all faces, and collect unclaimed leftovers.
233	fn resolve_claims(
234	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
235	    region_faces: &[usize],
236	    committed: &mut Vec<CompeteHyp>,
237	    claim_lists: &[Vec<usize>],
238	) -> (Vec<CompeteHyp>, Vec<usize>) {
239	    let hyp_area: Vec<f64> = committed
240	        .iter()
241	        .map(|h| h.faces().iter().map(|&fi| face_area(&mesh.faces[fi], &mesh.vertices)).sum())
242	        .collect();
243	
244	    let mut assigned: Vec<Vec<usize>> = vec![Vec::new(); committed.len()];
245	    let mut leftovers: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
246	
247	    for &fi in region_faces {
248	        let claimants = &claim_lists[fi];
249	        if claimants.is_empty() {
250	            leftovers.push(fi);
251	            continue;
252	        }
253	        if claimants.len() == 1 {
254	            assigned[claimants[0]].push(fi);
255	            continue;
256	        }
257	        // Best (smallest max-vertex-distance) claimant; the larger-area
258	        // claimant wins ties and only loses by a 2× margin (a true junction
259	        // face fits both sides equally — the margin prevents flapping).
260	        let dist = |ci: usize| max_vertex_dist(mesh, &committed[ci], fi);
261	        let mut order: Vec<usize> = claimants.clone();
262	        order.sort_by(|&a, &b| {
263	            hyp_area[b]
264	                .partial_cmp(&hyp_area[a])
265	                .unwrap()
266	                .then_with(|| a.cmp(&b))
267	        });
268	        let incumbent = order[0]; // largest area
269	        let mut winner = incumbent;
270	        let mut winner_d = dist(incumbent);
271	        for &ci in &order[1..] {
272	            let d = dist(ci);
273	            if d * 2.0 < winner_d {
274	                winner = ci;
275	                winner_d = d;
276	            }
277	        }
278	        assigned[winner].push(fi);
279	    }
280	
281	    let mut out = Vec::new();
282	    for (ci, mut hyp) in committed.drain(..).enumerate() {
283	        let faces = std::mem::take(&mut assigned[ci]);
284	        if faces.is_empty() {
285	            continue;
286	        }
287	        let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &faces);
288	        hyp.set_faces(faces, verts);
289	        out.push(hyp);
290	    }
291	    (out, leftovers)
292	}
293	
294	/// Grow a hypothesis of type \`S\` from \`seed\`: condition an initial fit on a
295	/// jet-similar seed patch, then flood-accept every region face the fit
296	/// validates and refit on the grown support, to a fixpoint. Returns the
297	/// hypothesis, its validated area, and its face list.
298	fn grow<S: SurfaceType>(
299	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
300	    in_region: &[bool],
301	    seed: usize,
302	    jet: &[JetField],
303	    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
304	    config: &Config,
305	    min_faces: usize,
306	) -> Option<(S::Hypothesis, f64, Vec<usize>)> {
307	    let vtol = config.vertex_tolerance_mm * GROW_VTOL_FACTOR;
308	    let stol = config.surface_tolerance_mm;
309	
310	    let mut accepted = seed_patch(mesh, in_region, seed, jet);
311	    let mut prev = 0usize;
312	    for round in 0..MAX_GROW_ROUNDS {
313	        let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &accepted);
314	        let mut fit = S::fit_surface(mesh, &accepted, &verts, config.verbosity)?;
315	        S::determine_convexity(mesh, &accepted, &mut fit);
316	        let comp = flood::<S>(mesh, in_region, seed, &fit, centroids, vtol, stol);
317	        if comp.is_empty() {
318	            return None; // the seed does not lie on its own fit — reject
319	        }
320	        if comp.len() == accepted.len() && round > 0 {
321	            accepted = comp;
322	            break;
323	        }
324	        if comp.len() == prev {
325	            // Oscillating between two sizes — stop at the larger.
326	            if comp.len() >= accepted.len() {
327	                accepted = comp;
328	            }
329	            break;
330	        }
331	        prev = accepted.len();
332	        accepted = comp;
333	    }
334	
335	    // Final fit + validated flood.
336	    let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &accepted);
337	    let mut fit = S::fit_surface(mesh, &accepted, &verts, config.verbosity)?;
338	    S::determine_convexity(mesh, &accepted, &mut fit);
339	    let faces = flood::<S>(mesh, in_region, seed, &fit, centroids, vtol, stol);
340	    if faces.len() < min_faces {
341	        return None;
342	    }
343	    let area: f64 = faces.iter().map(|&fi| face_area(&mesh.faces[fi], &mesh.vertices)).sum();
344	    let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &faces);
345	    let hyp = S::make_hypothesis(mesh, faces.clone(), verts, &fit);
346	    Some((hyp, area, faces))
347	}
348	
349	/// Connected region-faces reachable from \`seed\` that all validate \`fit\`
350	/// (vertex tolerance + centroid tolerance + orientation coherence).
351	fn flood<S: SurfaceType>(
352	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
353	    in_region: &[bool],
354	    seed: usize,
355	    fit: &S::Fit,
356	    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
357	    vtol: f64,
358	    stol: f64,
359	) -> Vec<usize> {
360	    if !face_validates::<S>(mesh, seed, fit, centroids, vtol, stol) {
361	        return Vec::new();
362	    }
363	    let mut seen: HashSet<usize> = HashSet::new();
364	    seen.insert(seed);
365	    let mut out = Vec::new();
366	    let mut stack = vec![seed];
367	    while let Some(fi) = stack.pop() {
368	        out.push(fi);
369	        let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
370	        for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
371	            if ni < 0 {
372	                continue;
373	            }
374	            let ni = ni as usize;
375	            if in_region[ni]
376	                && !seen.contains(&ni)
377	                && face_validates::<S>(mesh, ni, fit, centroids, vtol, stol)
378	            {
379	                seen.insert(ni);
380	                stack.push(ni);
381	            }
382	        }
383	    }
384	    out.sort_unstable();
385	    out
386	}
387	
388	/// Does face \`fi\` validate \`fit\` (all vertices ≤ vtol, centroid ≤ stol,
389	/// orientation coherent)?
390	fn face_validates<S: SurfaceType>(
391	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
392	    fi: usize,
393	    fit: &S::Fit,
394	    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
395	    vtol: f64,
396	    stol: f64,
397	) -> bool {
398	    if !S::convexity_check(fit, mesh, fi) {
399	        return false;
400	    }
401	    let face = &mesh.faces[fi];
402	    let vc = face.vertex_count as usize;
403	    for &vi in &face.vertex_indices[..vc] {
404	        let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
405	        if S::vertex_distance(fit, &[v.x, v.y, v.z]) > vtol {
406	            return false;
407	        }
408	    }
409	    S::centroid_distance(fit, &centroids[fi]) <= stol
410	}
411	
412	/// A small jet-similar patch around \`seed\` (same curvature class, magnitude
413	/// within 2×), capped, for a well-conditioned initial fit.
414	fn seed_patch(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, in_region: &[bool], seed: usize, jet: &[JetField]) -> Vec<usize> {
415	    let seed_class = curvature_class(jet[seed]);
416	    let seed_mag = jet[seed].k1.abs().max(jet[seed].k2.abs());
417	    let mut seen: HashSet<usize> = HashSet::new();
418	    seen.insert(seed);
419	    let mut out = vec![seed];
420	    // Depth-limited BFS (frontier by ring).
421	    let mut frontier = vec![seed];
422	    for _depth in 0..MAX_PATCH_DEPTH {
423	        if out.len() >= SEED_PATCH_CAP {
424	            break;
425	        }
426	        let mut next = Vec::new();
427	        for &fi in &frontier {
428	            let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
429	            for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
430	                if ni < 0 {
431	                    continue;
432	                }
433	                let ni = ni as usize;
434	                if !in_region[ni] || seen.contains(&ni) {
435	                    continue;
436	                }
437	                if curvature_class(jet[ni]) != seed_class {
438	                    continue;
439	                }
440	                let mag = jet[ni].k1.abs().max(jet[ni].k2.abs());
441	                if seed_mag > 1e-9 && (mag > 1.5 * seed_mag || mag < 0.667 * seed_mag) {
442	                    continue;
443	                }
444	                seen.insert(ni);
445	                out.push(ni);
446	                next.push(ni);
447	                if out.len() >= SEED_PATCH_CAP {
448	                    break;
449	                }
450	            }
451	        }
452	        frontier = next;
453	    }
454	    out.sort_unstable();
455	    out
456	}
457	
458	#[derive(PartialEq, Eq, Clone, Copy, Debug)]
459	enum CurvClass {
460	    Flat,
461	    Developable,
462	    Spherelike,
463	}
464	
465	fn curvature_class(jf: JetField) -> CurvClass {
466	    let a1 = jf.k1.abs();
467	    let a2 = jf.k2.abs();
468	    // Absolute floor is generous; only used to cluster the seed patch.
469	    if a1 < 1e-4 {
470	        CurvClass::Flat
471	    } else if a2 >= 0.4 * a1 {
472	        CurvClass::Spherelike
473	    } else {
474	        CurvClass::Developable
475	    }
476	}
477	
478	/// Curvature mismatch of a face vs its region neighbors (low = interior).
479	fn neighbor_jet_mismatch(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, fi: usize, jet: &[JetField], in_region: &[bool]) -> f64 {
480	    let jf = jet[fi];
481	    let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
482	    let mut worst = 0.0_f64;
483	    for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
484	        if ni < 0 {
485	            continue;
486	        }
487	        let ni = ni as usize;
488	        if !in_region[ni] {
489	            continue;
490	        }
491	        let jn = jet[ni];
492	        let d = (jf.k1 - jn.k1).abs() + (jf.k2 - jn.k2).abs();
493	        worst = worst.max(d);
494	    }
495	    worst
496	}
497	
498	/// Max distance from face \`fi\`'s vertices to a committed hypothesis.
499	fn max_vertex_dist(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, hyp: &CompeteHyp, fi: usize) -> f64 {
500	    let face = &mesh.faces[fi];
501	    let vc = face.vertex_count as usize;
502	    face.vertex_indices[..vc]
503	        .iter()
504	        .map(|&vi| {
505	            let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
506	            let p = [v.x, v.y, v.z];
507	            match hyp {
508	                CompeteHyp::Planar(h) => {
509	                    (h.normal[0] * p[0] + h.normal[1] * p[1] + h.normal[2] * p[2] - h.distance).abs()
510	                }
511	                CompeteHyp::Conical(h) => {
512	                    if h.is_cylinder() {
513	                        super::cylindrical::vertex_to_cylinder_distance(
514	                            v, &h.apex, &h.axis_direction, h.radius_at_apex,
515	                        )
516	                        .abs()
517	                    } else {
518	                        super::conical::vertex_to_cone_distance(v, &h.apex, &h.axis_direction, h.half_angle)
519	                            .abs()
520	                    }
521	                }
522	                CompeteHyp::Spherical(h) => {
523	                    super::spherical::vertex_to_sphere_distance(v, &h.center, h.radius).abs()
524	                }
525	            }
526	        })
527	        .fold(0.0_f64, f64::max)
528	}
529	
530	/// Sorted, deduplicated vertex indices of a face set.
531	fn vertices_of(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, faces: &[usize]) -> Vec<usize> {
532	    let mut v: Vec<usize> = faces
533	        .iter()
534	        .flat_map(|&fi| {
535	            let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
536	            mesh.faces[fi].vertex_indices[..vc].iter().copied()
537	        })
538	        .collect();
539	    v.sort_unstable();
540	    v.dedup();
541	    v
542	}
543	
544	/// Largest bounding-box dimension of a region's vertices.
545	fn region_extent(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, region: &Region) -> f64 {
546	    let mut min = [f64::INFINITY; 3];
547	    let mut max = [f64::NEG_INFINITY; 3];
548	    for &vi in &region.vertices {
549	        let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
550	        for (k, c) in [v.x, v.y, v.z].into_iter().enumerate() {
551	            min[k] = min[k].min(c);
552	            max[k] = max[k].max(c);
553	        }
554	    }
555	    (max[0] - min[0]).max(max[1] - min[1]).max(max[2] - min[2])
556	}

1	//! Stage 2.3(a): the whole-region DOF ladder.
2	//!
3	//! Try to explain each smooth region (stage 2.2) with ONE surface, ascending
4	//! degrees of freedom; the first fit that validates wins. Simplest-first
5	//! resolves degeneracy (any plane also lies on an infinite-radius cylinder; a
6	//! single facet is exactly a plane) without coverage heuristics.
7	//!
8	//! | Rung | Surface  | DOF |
9	//! |------|----------|-----|
10	//! | 1    | Plane    | 3   |
11	//! | 2    | Sphere   | 4   |
12	//! | 3    | Conical  | 5/6 | (cylinder-or-cone; the fitter prefers cylinder)
13	//! | 4    | Torus    | 7   |
14	//!
15	//! The conical rung fits a cylinder first and only falls to a cone when the
16	//! cylinder does not validate (\`ConicalSurface::fit_surface\`), so it covers
17	//! both the 5-DOF cylinder and 6-DOF cone cases in DOF order.
18	//!
19	//! **Validation decides all geometry** (Design Principle #1): every claimed
20	//! vertex within \`--vertex-tolerance\`, every claimed face centroid within
21	//! \`--surface-tolerance\`, and orientation coherence (every face normal
22	//! agrees in sign with the surface normal at its centroid — the per-type
23	//! \`convexity_check\`, which also fixes the hypothesis \`convex\` flag). The
24	//! fitters apply their own numeric-validity guards (cone half-angle bounds,
25	//! torus \`0 < r ≤ R\`, sphere radius cap) and return \`None\` outside them.
26	//!
27	//! A region the ladder cannot explain with one surface is a tangent chain
28	//! (pill capsule, rounded-cube shell, pipe-elbow tube). Decomposing those is
29	//! stage 2.3(b) scoped competition (not yet implemented). Until then such a
30	//! region **terminally degrades to per-facet planes** — total coverage can
31	//! never fail, and a single triangle is exactly a plane.

126	/// Run the whole-region ladder over every smooth region; regions the ladder
127	/// cannot explain go to scoped competition (2.3(b)), and whatever competition
128	/// leaves unclaimed degrades to per-facet planes.
129	pub(super) fn classify_regions(
130	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
131	    regions: &[Region],
132	    jet: &[JetField],
133	    config: &Config,
134	) -> Classification {
135	    let centroids: Vec<[f64; 3]> = mesh
136	        .faces
137	        .iter()
138	        .map(|f| face_centroid(f, &mesh.vertices))
139	        .collect();
140	
141	    let mut cls = Classification::new();
142	    let mut ladder_wins = [0usize; 4]; // plane, sphere, conical, torus
143	    let mut competed_regions = 0usize;
144	    let mut competed_surfaces = 0usize;
145	    let mut facet_faces = 0usize;
146	    for region in regions {
147	        if classify_one_region(mesh, region, &centroids, config, &mut cls, &mut ladder_wins) {
148	            continue;
149	        }
150	        // The ladder cannot explain this region — scoped competition.
151	        competed_regions += 1;
152	        let (hyps, leftovers) = compete::compete_region(mesh, region, jet, &centroids, config);
153	
154	        // A whole undecomposed sub-surface left as per-facet planes (e.g. a
155	        // coarse fillet competition cannot fit) reconstructs to invalid wires
156	        // where it abuts a committed analytic surface — worse than a clean
157	        // polyhedron. When the largest leftover blob is more than a junction
158	        // sliver, discard competition and per-facet the whole region; a clean
159	        // polyhedron is the safe fallback until freeform fitting (2.3(e))
160	        // gives those blobs a principled home. (Healthy competition leaves
161	        // only tiny scattered slivers at junctions.)
162	        if largest_component(mesh, &leftovers) > LEFTOVER_BLOB_MAX {
163	            for &fi in &region.faces {
164	                cls.push_planar(facet_plane(mesh, fi));
165	            }
166	            facet_faces += region.faces.len();
167	            continue;
168	        }
169	
170	        competed_surfaces += hyps.len();
171	        for hyp in hyps {
172	            cls.push_compete(hyp);
173	        }
174	        // Whatever competition left unclaimed → per-facet planes (total
175	        // coverage can never fail; a single triangle is exactly a plane).
176	        facet_faces += leftovers.len();
177	        for fi in leftovers {
178	            cls.push_planar(facet_plane(mesh, fi));
179	        }
180	    }
181	
182	    if config.verbosity >= 1 {
183	        eprintln!(
184	            "  ladder: {} plane, {} sphere, {} cyl/cone, {} torus; competition: {} region(s) → {} surfaces + {} per-facet",
185	            ladder_wins[0], ladder_wins[1], ladder_wins[2], ladder_wins[3],
186	            competed_regions, competed_surfaces, facet_faces,
187	        );
188	    }
189	    cls
190	}

192	/// Try the DOF ladder on one region; commit the first surface that validates.
193	/// Returns true on a committed surface, false if the region fell through
194	/// (caller applies the per-facet fallback).
195	fn classify_one_region(
196	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
197	    region: &Region,
198	    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
199	    config: &Config,
200	    cls: &mut Classification,
201	    wins: &mut [usize; 4],
202	) -> bool {
203	    let faces = &region.faces;
204	    let verts = &region.vertices;
205	
206	    if let Some(hyp) = fit_validate::<PlanarSurface>(mesh, faces, verts, centroids, config) {
207	        cls.push_planar(hyp);
208	        wins[0] += 1;
209	        return true;
210	    }
211	    if let Some(hyp) = fit_validate::<SphericalSurface>(mesh, faces, verts, centroids, config) {
212	        cls.push_spherical(hyp);
213	        wins[1] += 1;
214	        return true;
215	    }
216	    if let Some(hyp) = fit_validate::<ConicalSurface>(mesh, faces, verts, centroids, config) {
217	        cls.push_conical(hyp);
218	        wins[2] += 1;
219	        return true;
220	    }
221	    if let Some(hyp) = fit_validate::<ToroidalSurface>(mesh, faces, verts, centroids, config) {
222	        cls.push_toroidal(hyp);
223	        wins[3] += 1;
224	        return true;
225	    }
226	    false
227	}

229	/// Fit surface type \`S\` to a region and validate it against the whole region.
230	/// Large regions fit on a stride subsample, refit-augmented with the worst
231	/// validation offenders on a near-miss. Returns the committed hypothesis, or
232	/// \`None\` if \`S\` cannot explain the region within tolerance.
233	///
234	/// Also the stage-2.4 merge revalidation entry point (\`repair.rs\`): refit a
235	/// candidate union and confirm it validates end to end before committing.
236	pub(super) fn fit_validate<S: SurfaceType>(
237	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
238	    region_faces: &[usize],
239	    region_verts: &[usize],
240	    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
241	    config: &Config,
242	) -> Option<S::Hypothesis> {
243	    let vtol = config.vertex_tolerance_mm;
244	    let stol = config.surface_tolerance_mm;
245	
246	    // Initial fit set: the whole region, or a deterministic stride subsample
247	    // when the region is large.
248	    let mut fit_faces: Vec<usize> = if region_faces.len() > MAX_FIT_FACES {
249	        let stride = region_faces.len().div_ceil(MAX_FIT_FACES);
250	        region_faces.iter().copied().step_by(stride).collect()
251	    } else {
252	        region_faces.to_vec()
253	    };
254	
255	    for _round in 0..=MAX_REFIT {
256	        let fit_verts = vertices_of(mesh, &fit_faces);
257	        let mut fit = S::fit_surface(mesh, &fit_faces, &fit_verts, config.verbosity)?;
258	        S::determine_convexity(mesh, region_faces, &mut fit);
259	
260	        // Validate every region face; collect near-miss offenders for a refit.
261	        let mut offenders: Vec<(f64, usize)> = Vec::new();
262	        for &fi in region_faces {
263	            // Orientation coherence: a face whose normal disagrees with the
264	            // fitted surface's convexity means the region is not one clean
265	            // surface of type S — no refit rescues that.
266	            if !S::convexity_check(&fit, mesh, fi) {
267	                return None;
268	            }
269	            let face = &mesh.faces[fi];
270	            let vc = face.vertex_count as usize;
271	            let mut excess = 0.0_f64;
272	            for &vi in &face.vertex_indices[..vc] {
273	                let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
274	                let d = S::vertex_distance(&fit, &[v.x, v.y, v.z]);
275	                if d > vtol {
276	                    excess = excess.max(d - vtol);
277	                }
278	            }
279	            let cd = S::centroid_distance(&fit, &centroids[fi]);
280	            if cd > stol {
281	                excess = excess.max(cd - stol);
282	            }
283	            if excess > 0.0 {
284	                offenders.push((excess, fi));
285	            }
286	        }
287	
288	        if offenders.is_empty() {
289	            return Some(S::make_hypothesis(
290	                mesh,
291	                region_faces.to_vec(),
292	                region_verts.to_vec(),
293	                &fit,
294	            ));
295	        }
296	
297	        // Near-miss handling: if the worst offender is far out, the region is
298	        // decisively not this surface. Otherwise fold the worst offenders
299	        // into the fit set and refit (bounded rounds).
300	        offenders.sort_by(|a, b| {
301	            b.0.partial_cmp(&a.0)
302	                .unwrap()
303	                .then_with(|| a.1.cmp(&b.1))
304	        });
305	        if offenders[0].0 > REFIT_GIVE_UP * stol {
306	            return None;
307	        }
308	        let before = fit_faces.len();
309	        let existing: HashSet<usize> = fit_faces.iter().copied().collect();
310	        for &(_, fi) in offenders.iter().take(REFIT_ADD) {
311	            if !existing.contains(&fi) {
312	                fit_faces.push(fi);
313	            }
314	        }
315	        fit_faces.sort_unstable();
316	        fit_faces.dedup();
317	        if fit_faces.len() == before {
318	            // No new faces to learn from — cannot improve.
319	            return None;
320	        }
321	    }
322	    None
323	}
324	
325	/// Size of the largest mesh-connected component within a face set.
326	fn largest_component(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, faces: &[usize]) -> usize {
327	    let member: HashSet<usize> = faces.iter().copied().collect();
328	    let mut seen: HashSet<usize> = HashSet::new();
329	    let mut largest = 0usize;
330	    for &start in faces {
331	        if seen.contains(&start) {
332	            continue;
333	        }
334	        let mut size = 0usize;
335	        let mut stack = vec![start];
336	        seen.insert(start);
337	        while let Some(fi) = stack.pop() {
338	            size += 1;
339	            let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
340	            for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
341	                if ni >= 0 {
342	                    let ni = ni as usize;
343	                    if member.contains(&ni) && seen.insert(ni) {
344	                        stack.push(ni);
345	                    }
346	                }
347	            }
348	        }
349	        largest = largest.max(size);
350	    }
351	    largest
352	}
353	
354	/// Sorted, deduplicated vertex indices of a face set.
355	fn vertices_of(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, faces: &[usize]) -> Vec<usize> {
356	    let mut v: Vec<usize> = faces
357	        .iter()
358	        .flat_map(|&fi| {
359	            let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
360	            mesh.faces[fi].vertex_indices[..vc].iter().copied()
361	        })
362	        .collect();
363	    v.sort_unstable();
364	    v.dedup();
365	    v
366	}
367	
368	/// A single-face planar hypothesis (the terminal per-facet fallback).
369	fn facet_plane(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, fi: usize) -> PlanarHypothesis {
370	    let face = &mesh.faces[fi];
371	    let vc = face.vertex_count as usize;
372	    let vertices: Vec<usize> = face.vertex_indices[..vc].to_vec();
373	    let vertex_set: HashSet<usize> = vertices.iter().copied().collect();
374	    let (normal, distance) = fit_plane(&[fi], &vertex_set, &mesh.faces, &mesh.vertices);
375	    let mut error_max = f64::NEG_INFINITY;
376	    let mut error_min = f64::INFINITY;
377	    let mut error_abs_sum = 0.0_f64;
378	    for &vi in &vertices {
379	        let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
380	        let d = normal[0] * v.x + normal[1] * v.y + normal[2] * v.z - distance;
381	        error_max = error_max.max(d);
382	        error_min = error_min.min(d);
383	        error_abs_sum += d.abs();
384	    }
385	    PlanarHypothesis {
386	        normal,
387	        distance,
388	        faces: vec![fi],
389	        vertices,
390	        error_max,
391	        error_min,
392	        error_abs_sum,
393	    }
394	}
395	
```

2. **Bend promotion as the user suggested** — after a cylinder candidate grows, examine its frontier. The key insight that makes this *better* than jet-class seeding: the cylinder fit itself locates the tangency (frontier faces failed cylinder validation), so "frontier + off-cylinder neighbors" is a guaranteed pure-bend patch that cannot straddle the junction the way a jet-similar patch can (the step-4 cone↔cylinder straddle problem, which recurs here since bend and straight tube share κ1). The promoted torus is just another candidate at the same seed — no special commit logic.

/// Grow a hypothesis of type `S` from `seed`: condition an initial fit on a
/// jet-similar seed patch, then flood-accept every region face the fit
/// validates and refit on the grown support, to a fixpoint. Returns the
/// hypothesis, its validated area, and its face list.
fn grow<S: SurfaceType>(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    in_region: &[bool],
    seed: usize,
    jet: &[JetField],
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    config: &Config,
    min_faces: usize,
) -> Option<(S::Hypothesis, f64, Vec<usize>)> {
    let vtol = config.vertex_tolerance_mm * GROW_VTOL_FACTOR;
    let stol = config.surface_tolerance_mm;

    let mut accepted = seed_patch(mesh, in_region, seed, jet);
    let mut prev = 0usize;
    for round in 0..MAX_GROW_ROUNDS {
        let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &accepted);
        let mut fit = S::fit_surface(mesh, &accepted, &verts, config.verbosity)?;
        S::determine_convexity(mesh, &accepted, &mut fit);
        let comp = flood::<S>(mesh, in_region, seed, &fit, centroids, vtol, stol);
        if comp.is_empty() {
            return None; // the seed does not lie on its own fit — reject
        }
        if comp.len() == accepted.len() && round > 0 {
            accepted = comp;
            break;
        }
        if comp.len() == prev {
            // Oscillating between two sizes — stop at the larger.
            if comp.len() >= accepted.len() {
                accepted = comp;
            }
            break;
        }
        prev = accepted.len();
        accepted = comp;
    }

    // Final fit + validated flood.
    let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &accepted);
    let mut fit = S::fit_surface(mesh, &accepted, &verts, config.verbosity)?;
    S::determine_convexity(mesh, &accepted, &mut fit);
    let faces = flood::<S>(mesh, in_region, seed, &fit, centroids, vtol, stol);
    if faces.len() < min_faces {
        return None;
    }
    let area: f64 = faces.iter().map(|&fi| face_area(&mesh.faces[fi], &mesh.vertices)).sum();
    let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &faces);
    let hyp = S::make_hypothesis(mesh, faces.clone(), verts, &fit);
    Some((hyp, area, faces))
}
```

**After:**
```
/// Grow a hypothesis of type `S` from `seed`: condition an initial fit on a
/// jet-similar seed patch, then flood-accept every region face the fit
/// validates and refit on the grown support, to a fixpoint. Returns the
/// hypothesis, its validated area, and its face list.
fn grow<S: SurfaceType>(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    in_region: &[bool],
    seed: usize,
    jet: &[JetField],
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    config: &Config,
    min_faces: usize,
) -> Option<(S::Hypothesis, f64, Vec<usize>)> {
    let patch = seed_patch(mesh, in_region, seed, jet);
    grow_from::<S>(mesh, in_region, seed, patch, centroids, config, min_faces)
}

/// The grow loop proper, from an explicit initial fit patch and flood start:
/// fit the patch, flood-accept every region face the fit validates, refit on
/// the grown support, to a fixpoint. Returns the hypothesis, its validated
/// area, and its face list.
fn grow_from<S: SurfaceType>(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    in_region: &[bool],
    start: usize,
    initial: Vec<usize>,
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    config: &Config,
    min_faces: usize,
) -> Option<(S::Hypothesis, f64, Vec<usize>)> {
    let vtol = config.vertex_tolerance_mm * GROW_VTOL_FACTOR;
    let stol = config.surface_tolerance_mm;

    let mut accepted = initial;
    let mut prev = 0usize;
    for round in 0..MAX_GROW_ROUNDS {
        let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &accepted);
        let mut fit = S::fit_surface(mesh, &accepted, &verts, config.verbosity)?;
        S::determine_convexity(mesh, &accepted, &mut fit);
        let comp = flood::<S>(mesh, in_region, start, &fit, centroids, vtol, stol);
        if comp.is_empty() {
            return None; // the start face does not lie on its own fit — reject
        }
        if comp.len() == accepted.len() && round > 0 {
            accepted = comp;
            break;
        }
        if comp.len() == prev {
            // Oscillating between two sizes — stop at the larger.
            if comp.len() >= accepted.len() {
                accepted = comp;
            }
            break;
        }
        prev = accepted.len();
        accepted = comp;
    }

    // Final fit + validated flood.
    let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &accepted);
    let mut fit = S::fit_surface(mesh, &accepted, &verts, config.verbosity)?;
    S::determine_convexity(mesh, &accepted, &mut fit);
    let faces = flood::<S>(mesh, in_region, start, &fit, centroids, vtol, stol);
    if faces.len() < min_faces {
        return None;
    }
    let area: f64 = faces.iter().map(|&fi| face_area(&mesh.faces[fi], &mesh.vertices)).sum();
    let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &faces);
    let hyp = S::make_hypothesis(mesh, faces.clone(), verts, &fit);
    Some((hyp, area, faces))
}

/// Grow a toroidal candidate from an initial fit patch, trying flood starts
/// in order until one grows. Rejects degenerate giant-major-radius fits: a
/// short segment of straight cylinder fits a torus with an absurdly distant
/// axis (observed R ≈ 1500–3600 mm on ~100 mm models under the old BFS), and
/// a legitimate torus's major radius cannot exceed the mesh extent — the
/// same guard as the ladder's acceptance test.
fn torus_candidate(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    in_region: &[bool],
    initial: &[usize],
    starts: &[usize],
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    config: &Config,
) -> Option<(ToroidalHypothesis, f64, Vec<usize>)> {
    let bb_diag = bounding_box_diagonal(&mesh.vertices);
    for &start in starts.iter().take(MAX_TORUS_STARTS) {
        if let Some((hyp, area, faces)) = grow_from::<ToroidalSurface>(
            mesh,
            in_region,
            start,
            initial.to_vec(),
            centroids,
            config,
            MIN_TORUS_FACES,
        ) {
            if hyp.major_radius <= bb_diag {
                return Some((hyp, area, faces));
            }
        }
    }
    None
}

/// Stage 2.3(c) bent-tube promotion. A cylinder flood that stalled against
/// region faces whose jet continues the tube — κ1 ≈ the tube's 1/r, |κ2|
/// well below κ1 (the same tube swinging around a bend, not a cap plane's
/// (0,0) or an end sphere's (κ,κ)) — is the developable prefix of a bent
/// tube. Fit a torus to the pure-bend patch just past the stall line
/// (frontier faces plus their off-cylinder tube-jet neighbours) and grow it;
/// the result competes on validated area like any other candidate.
///
/// The cylinder fit itself locates the tangency — frontier faces failed
/// cylinder validation — so unlike a jet-class seed patch (which cannot tell
/// bend from straight tube: both read the same κ1) this patch cannot
/// straddle the junction.
fn promote_bend(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    in_region: &[bool],
    cyl: &ConicalHypothesis,
    cyl_faces: &[usize],
    jet: &[JetField],
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    config: &Config,
) -> Option<(ToroidalHypothesis, f64, Vec<usize>)> {
    if cyl.radius_at_apex <= 0.0 {
        return None;
    }
    let k_tube = 1.0 / cyl.radius_at_apex;
    let grow_vtol = config.vertex_tolerance_mm * GROW_VTOL_FACTOR;

    // Max vertex distance to the stalled cylinder — the "past the tangency"
    // test (frontier faces failed the flood at exactly this tolerance).
    let off_cyl_dist = |fi: usize| -> f64 {
        let face = &mesh.faces[fi];
        let vc = face.vertex_count as usize;
        face.vertex_indices[..vc]
            .iter()
            .map(|&vi| {
                super::cylindrical::vertex_to_cylinder_distance(
                    &mesh.vertices[vi],
                    &cyl.apex,
                    &cyl.axis_direction,
                    cyl.radius_at_apex,
                )
                .abs()
            })
            .fold(0.0_f64, f64::max)
    };
    // Tube-continuation jet signature. The κ2 bound is generous: a bend's
    // inner (saddle) side reads |κ2| = 1/(R−r), which approaches κ1 = 1/r
    // only for very tight bends; junction rows have contaminated jets and
    // are excluded from the fit patch either way (the flood claims them).
    let tube_jet = |fi: usize| -> bool {
        let a1 = jet[fi].k1.abs();
        a1 >= 0.5 * k_tube && a1 <= 2.0 * k_tube && jet[fi].k2.abs() <= 0.8 * a1
    };

    // Frontier: in-region neighbours of the cylinder support that are past
    // the tangency and continue the tube.
    let mut seen: HashSet<usize> = cyl_faces.iter().copied().collect();
    let mut frontier: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
    for &fi in cyl_faces {
        let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
        for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
            if ni < 0 {
                continue;
            }
            let ni = ni as usize;
            if !in_region[ni] || !seen.insert(ni) {
                continue;
            }
            if off_cyl_dist(ni) > grow_vtol && tube_jet(ni) {
                frontier.push(ni);
            }
        }
    }
    if frontier.is_empty() {
        return None; // finished a straight pipe (or stalled at a cap/sphere)
    }
    frontier.sort_unstable();

    // Pure-bend fit patch: depth-limited multi-source BFS from the frontier
    // through off-cylinder tube-jet faces. (Neighbours examined and rejected
    // above stay excluded — junction rows with contaminated jets would only
    // pollute the fit.)
    let mut patch: Vec<usize> = frontier.clone();
    let mut ring = frontier.clone();
    for _depth in 0..BEND_PATCH_DEPTH {
        if patch.len() >= BEND_PATCH_CAP {
            break;
        }
        let mut next: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
        for &fi in &ring {
            let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
            for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
                if ni < 0 {
                    continue;
                }
                let ni = ni as usize;
                if !in_region[ni] || seen.contains(&ni) {
                    continue;
                }
                if off_cyl_dist(ni) <= grow_vtol || !tube_jet(ni) {
                    continue;
                }
                seen.insert(ni);
                patch.push(ni);
                next.push(ni);
                if patch.len() >= BEND_PATCH_CAP {
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        if next.is_empty() {
            break;
        }
        ring = next;
    }
    patch.sort_unstable();

    // Flood starts: deepest-off-cylinder first — the faces most surely
    // interior to the bend (frontier faces sit on the junction row and may
    // not validate the torus fit themselves).
    let mut starts = patch.clone();
    starts.sort_by(|&a, &b| {
        off_cyl_dist(b)
            .partial_cmp(&off_cyl_dist(a))
            .unwrap()
            .then_with(|| a.cmp(&b))
    });

    torus_candidate(mesh, in_region, &patch, &starts, centroids, config)
}

# Instructions for LLM Coding Assistants

This file contains guidelines for AI/LLM coding assistants working on this project. Read ALL of AGENTS.md - no just the first 100 lines.

The shell is zsh. Use zsh quoting conventions. "echo ===" will fail, and globs in flags must be quoted.

### Commit Checklist (MANDATORY — verify before every commit)

- \`cargo clippy\` emits no warnings.
- Build passes with no errors or warnings.

## Project Layout

This is a Rust project. Key locations:

- \`README.md\` - Program usage. Read it.
- \`DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md\` - Development plan. Read it.
- \`Cargo.toml\` — Rust project manifest
- \`src/\` — Rust source files
  - \`bin/brepper.rs\` — the main program
  - \`bin/step_measure_tolerance.rs\` — utility to measure distances from STL to correpsonding STEP
  - \`bin/viewer.rs\` — GUI to visualize STL or STEP files
- \`scripts/\` — shell scripts for batch operations over test data
  - \`step_distance_table.sh\` - runs \`step_measure_tolerance\` over all STL/STEP pairs and summarizes statistics
- \`tests/\` — STL and STEP test file pairs
  - \`manual/\` — handcrafted simple models
  - \`onshape/\` — models exported from Onshape
  - \`ccad/generated/\` — models generated via CodeCAD

### OCCT / opencascade-rs

The project uses the \`opencascade-sys\` crate (auto-generated Rust FFI bindings to OpenCASCADE Technology) via a path dependency. MANDATORY: All useful C++ OCCT APIs should be available in the binding - if you want to use one that doesn't seem to be bound, complain loudly about it AND STOP.

\`\`\`
../opencascade-rs/crates/opencascade-sys   ← Rust FFI bindings (8700+ types)
../opencascade-rs/crates/opencascade-sys/PORTING.md  ← Naming conventions & usage patterns
../opencascade-rs/crates/opencascade-sys/generated/  ← All generated .rs modules
../opencascade-rs/crates/occt-sys/OCCT/src/  ← OCCT C++ source (for reading docs/headers)
../opencascade-rs/crates/occt-sys/OCCT/dox/  ← OCCT C++ documentation
\`\`\`

The \`builtin\` feature (default) compiles OCCT from source — first build takes ~8 minutes. Subsequent builds are fast.

## Commit Messages

All commit messages must include:

1. **A clear description** of the changes made
2. **The AI agent/model** used to generate the changes (e.g., "Claude Sonnet 4 (Anthropic, 2025)")
3. **The user prompts** that led to the changes

Format:
\`\`\`
<descriptive commit title>

<detailed description of changes>

---
Generated with assistance from <model name> (<provider>, <year>)
```

2. **Bent-tube promotion** (`promote_bend`): a grown cylinder's frontier is

   a torus is fitted to the pure-bend patch past the stall line (frontier +
   off-cylinder tube-jet neighbours, depth ≤ 4, cap 64; flood starts
   deepest-off-cylinder first, ≤ 4 tries). Key: the cylinder fit locates the
   tangency, so the patch can't straddle it (jet class can't tell bend from
   straight — same κ1). Result competes as a normal candidate (dof 3).
3. Guard: reject torus fits with `major_radius > bbox diagonal` (straight
   segments fit absurdly distant tori). `grow` split into `grow`+`grow_from`.

Smoke: pipe_elbow_10_medium → 2 planes + 2 cyl + 1 torus, 1 valid solid, 0
leftovers (the acceptance shape, first run — but --compare NOT run).
`stage2_competition` (2 tests) green. Nothing else verified.

## What to test

- `pipe_elbow_10_medium` + `_fine` with `--compare` vs
  tests/onshape/pipe_elbow_10.step (volume gate, BRepCheck).
- stepped_block_toroidal_*, cone_cylinder (concave fillet, jet k2<0),
  filleted_cylinder/pipe/hole_block, rounded_cube_* (esp. coarse — blob
  fallback interaction), pill.
- Full suites vs baseline: stage2 130 / stage3 99 / stage4 27, lib 90, seg
  14. Torus models previously fell back to valid per-facet → no regression
  pressure, a clean bar. Add stage2_competition tests for the new wins.

## Likely failure points (ranked)

- **κ2 gates (0.8, two places)**: inner-bend saddle reads |κ2| =
  1/(R−r) → up to κ1·r/(R−r); tight bends (R−r small) get excluded from
  direct seeding AND the bend patch. Loosen/rethink if inner-bend faces are
  missing from claims.
- **Direct-candidate seed_patch straddle**: for fillet tori tangent to
  cones/cylinders, the jet-similar patch (class Developable, same κ1) can
  straddle → contaminated fit → NO GROWTH → blob fallback per-facets the
  region (pre-step-5 behaviour, not a regression, but no win). Fix would be
  a cone-side promotion or patch tightening.
- **Coarse meshes**: GROW_VTOL_FACTOR=30 may reject coarse bend rows
  (rounded_cube_coarse precedent) → leftover blob → per-facet fallback.
- **Genuine strip sweeps**: the bend of pipe_elbow is gridded, but a
  strip-only tessellated sweep will defeat `fit_torus` (needs both
  curvature directions in the patch) → that is the trigger to implement the
  plan's k=1/R degenerate-limit model (§2.3(c)), not to tune thresholds.
- **Sphere-band tori**: if a bogus torus ever beats a sphere, competition
  lacks toroidal.rs's `angular_coverage_valid`/`minor_circle_coverage_valid`
  (only the bbox-R guard is applied) — wire those in rather than masking.
- **Convexity**: TorusFit convex comes from the first accepted face; flood
  rejects opposite-convexity faces. Pipe exterior is uniformly convex around
  the tube; watch concave fillets.
- **Runtime**: every curved non-sphere-like seed now runs an LM torus fit
  (+ up to 4 refits per promotion). If large models crawl, gate harder.

Debug: `BREPPER_DEBUG_COMPETE=1` logs per-commit, NO-GROWTH (now with torus
area), seed jets.

```

**What I built, and where I diverged from the kickoff:** Taking your point that the goal is general toroid recognition, I skipped the kickoff's stall-detection heuristic and medial-spine/`k=1/R` machinery entirely (they remain contingency in the plan) and instead made the torus a first-class citizen of the existing competition in [compete.rs](src/stage2/compete.rs):

1. **Direct toroidal candidate** — every curved seed with |κ2| < 0.8|κ1| also grows a `ToroidalSurface` candidate alongside plane/cone/sphere. This recognizes fillet tori and bends anywhere, including next to cones, with no "stalled cylinder" precondition. Sphere-like seeds are skipped because sphere quad-row bands lie near tori (the old BFS pathology).
2. **Bend promotion, per your framing** — after a cylinder candidate grows, its frontier is scanned for tube-continuation jet (κ1 ≈ 1/r, |κ2| ≤ 0.8κ1 — excludes cap planes and end spheres). A torus is then fitted to the *pure-bend patch just past the stall line*. The insight that makes this better than jet seeding: the cylinder fit itself locates the tangency, so this patch cannot straddle the junction — jet class fundamentally can't tell bend from straight tube since both read the same κ1 (the step-4 straddle problem reborn). The promoted torus is just another candidate; largest-validated-area still decides, so no special commit logic.
3. Degenerate guard: torus fits with R > bbox diagonal are rejected (a straight segment fits an absurdly distant torus), mirroring the ladder's acceptance test.

## The pipe_elbow_10_fine note
I investigated deeper, and **your suspicion is correct — it's a real geometry-representation issue, not a serialization bug.** The evidence:

- `_fine` and `_medium` produce **identical** analytic surfaces (torus R=10/r=5, two r=5 cylinders, planes) and **identical** STEP entity counts. The only difference is the numeric B-spline pcurve data, fit from the 4×-denser mesh.
- Both build a **valid, closed, correctly-measured in-memory solid** (BRepCheck clean, `orient_closed_solid` true, BRepGProp volume 3589.976, distance-to-reference 0).
- `_medium` round-trips through STEP faithfully (3589.87); `_fine` collapses to 3087 (14% low).

Since OCCT preserves valid solids through its *own* writer→reader, a volume change on round-trip means the written face bounds are ambiguous enough that the reader normalizes them to a face bounding a *different* region. The suspect is the toroidal face: it's **V-periodic** (the tube wraps 360°, so there's a `SEAM_CURVE` along the outer equator over the trimmed 90° major arc), and its boundary pcurves are degree-3 B-splines fit to mesh chains. In-memory `BRepGProp` tolerates the pcurve/seam inconsistency (it integrates 3D curves); the STEP reader doesn't. `occt_full_torus` (complete donut) round-trips fine, so it's specific to a *partial* periodic-torus face at fine tessellation.

I recorded this as an Active item in [TODO.md](TODO.md) with reproduction steps and pointers to the likely stage-3 seam/pcurve code, and noted it's not a suite regression (pipe_elbow_10_fine is untracked).

```
//! Debug probe: read a STEP file and report per-face surface type, area, and
//! UV bounds, plus total surface area and volume. Used to diagnose which face
//! of a re-imported solid collapses on STEP round-trip (pipe_elbow_fine).
//!
//! TEMPORARY debugging tool — delete after the pipe_elbow_fine investigation.

use opencascade_sys::{
    b_rep_adaptor, b_rep_g_prop, b_rep_tools, g_prop, geom_abs, message, step_control, top_abs,
    top_exp, topo_ds,
};
use std::env;
use std::process;

fn main() {
    let args: Vec<String> = env::args().collect();
    if args.len() < 2 {
        eprintln!("Usage: {} <input.step>", args[0]);
        process::exit(1);
    }
    let path = &args[1];

    let mut reader = step_control::StepReader::new();
    let status = reader.read_file_charptr(path);
    if status != opencascade_sys::if_select::ReturnStatus::Retdone {
        eprintln!("Failed to read STEP {path}: {status:?}");
        process::exit(1);
    }
    let progress = message::ProgressRange::new();
    reader.transfer_roots(&progress);
    let shape = reader.one_shape();
    drop(reader);

    let type_name = |t: geom_abs::SurfaceType| -> &'static str {
        match t {
            geom_abs::SurfaceType::Plane => "plane",
            geom_abs::SurfaceType::Cylinder => "cylinder",
            geom_abs::SurfaceType::Cone => "cone",
            geom_abs::SurfaceType::Sphere => "sphere",
            geom_abs::SurfaceType::Torus => "torus",
            geom_abs::SurfaceType::Bsplinesurface => "bspline",
            _ => "other",
        }
    };

    let mut explorer =
        top_exp::Explorer::new_shape_shapeenum2(&shape, top_abs::ShapeEnum::Face, top_abs::ShapeEnum::Shape);
    let mut idx = 0;
    while explorer.more() {
        let face_shape = explorer.value();
        let face = topo_ds::face_shape(face_shape);
        let adaptor = b_rep_adaptor::Surface::new_face(face);
        let stype = adaptor.get_type();

        let (mut umin, mut umax, mut vmin, mut vmax) = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0);
        b_rep_tools::uv_bounds_face_real4(face, &mut umin, &mut umax, &mut vmin, &mut vmax);

        let mut props = g_prop::GProps::new();
        b_rep_g_prop::surface_properties_shape_gprops_bool2(face_shape, &mut props, false, false);
        let area = props.mass();

        let orient = face_shape.orientation();
        println!(
            "face {idx}: {:8} area={:10.4}  U=[{:.5},{:.5}] V=[{:.5},{:.5}]  orient={:?}",
            type_name(stype), area, umin, umax, vmin, vmax, orient,
        );
        idx += 1;
        explorer.next();
    }

    let mut area_props = g_prop::GProps::new();
    b_rep_g_prop::surface_properties_shape_gprops_bool2(&shape, &mut area_props, false, false);
    let mut vol_props = g_prop::GProps::new();
    b_rep_g_prop::volume_properties_shape_gprops_bool3(&shape, &mut vol_props, false, false, false);
    println!(
        "TOTAL: {idx} faces, area={:.4}, volume={:.4}",
        area_props.mass(),
        vol_props.mass()
    );
}

```

        ("edge", top_abs::ShapeEnum::Edge),
    ] {

        let mut c = 0;
        while e.more() {
            c += 1;
            e.next();
        }
        counts.insert(label, c);
    }
    let analyzer = b_rep_check::Analyzer::new_shape_bool3(&shape, true, false, false);
    println!(

        area_props.mass(),
        vol_props.mass()
    );
    println!(
        "TOPOLOGY: {} solid(s), {} shell(s), {} face(s), {} edge(s); BRepCheck valid={}",
        counts["solid"], counts["shell"], counts["face"], counts["edge"], analyzer.is_valid(),
    );
}

/// Relative-volume tolerance for the STEP round-trip self-check. Matches the
/// `--compare` volume gate; a divergence above this means the written STEP
/// does not faithfully represent the in-memory solid.
const STEP_ROUNDTRIP_VOLUME_TOL: f64 = 0.01;

/// Re-read the just-written STEP and verify it. The **round-trip self-check**
/// always runs: OCCT re-expresses every pcurve as a B-spline on STEP export,
/// and on some meshes a periodic-face pcurve degenerates (observed on
/// `pipe_elbow_10_fine`: an end-cap plane's boundary collapsed to a point),
/// producing a re-import that is still topologically valid and closed but
/// bounds a different volume. The in-memory solid passes every geometric and
/// topological BRepCheck, so **only a round-trip catches this** — hence we
/// compare the re-imported volume against the in-memory volume measured before
/// the write. When `--compare` is set, the reference comparison reuses the
/// same re-read shape.
fn verify_output(
    output_path: &str,
    in_memory_volume: f64,
    config: &Config,
) -> Result<(), Stage4Error> {
    let comparing = config.compare_shape.is_some();

    let output_shape = match crate::read_step_file(output_path) {
        Ok(shape) => shape,
        Err(e) => {
            // With --compare an unreadable output is a hard error (the round
            // trip could not be validated); without it (e.g. -o /dev/null)
            // there is simply nothing to self-check.
            if comparing {
                eprintln!("  Compare 4.1: ERROR failed to re-read written STEP file {output_path}: {e}");
                return Err(Stage4Error::Compare(Stage4CompareError::RoundTrip {
                    path: output_path.to_string(),
                    error: e,
                }));
            }
            return Ok(());
        }
    };

    let output_vol = compute_volume(&output_shape);

    // Round-trip self-check (no reference needed).
    if in_memory_volume > 0.0 {
        let self_diff = (output_vol - in_memory_volume).abs() / in_memory_volume;
        if self_diff > STEP_ROUNDTRIP_VOLUME_TOL {
            eprintln!(
                "  Stage 4.1 WARNING: written STEP volume {output_vol:.6} mm\u{00b3} differs from \
                 the in-memory solid ({in_memory_volume:.6} mm\u{00b3}) by {self_diff:.2e} — the \
                 STEP file does not faithfully represent the computed geometry (a periodic-face \
                 pcurve likely degenerated on export). The in-memory solid is valid; the written \
                 file is not."
            );
        } else if !config.quiet {
            eprintln!("  Stage 4.1: STEP round-trip volume check OK (rel diff {self_diff:.2e})");
        }
    }

    // Reference comparison (--compare).
    if comparing {
        compare_output_to_step(&output_shape, output_vol, config)?;
    }
    Ok(())
}
```
</details>

  entity count yet round-trips faithfully (3589.87 mm³); the ONLY difference
  is the numeric B-spline pcurve/edge data, which is fit from the (4×
  denser) mesh vertex chains. **This is a real geometry-representation
  inconsistency, not a text-serialization bug**: OCCT preserves valid solids
  through its own writer→reader, so a volume change on round-trip means the
  written face bounds are ambiguous enough that the reader normalizes them
  to a face bounding a *different* region. The suspect is the toroidal face:
  it is V-periodic (the tube wraps 360°, so there is a `SEAM_CURVE` along the
  outer equator spanning the 90° major arc, U∈[0,π/2]) and its boundary
  pcurves are degree-3 B-splines fit to mesh chains; a pcurve that is
  slightly off the seam, or wraps it inconsistently, lets the re-import build
  the face on the wrong side of the seam. In-memory `BRepGProp` tolerates it
  (integrates 3D curves / triangulation); the STEP reader does not.
  Reproduce: `brepper tests/onshape/pipe_elbow_10_fine.stl -o out.step
  --compare tests/onshape/pipe_elbow_10.step -v` (watch the Stage-3.6 vs
  4.1 volumes diverge). `occt_full_torus` (complete donut, both seams)
  round-trips fine, and `pipe_elbow_10_medium` passes, so this is specific to
  a *partial* (trimmed-U) periodic-torus face at fine tessellation.
  `pipe_elbow_10_fine` is NOT a tracked test, so this is not a suite
  regression — but it will block any future fine-torus `--compare` test.
  Likely lives in the stage-3 periodic-face seam/pcurve construction (cf. the
  periodic-band / seam-anchor notes: `build_pcurve`, seam re-anchoring in
  stage3.rs).
```

  (`pipe_elbow_10_fine`; found + diagnosed 2026-07-21 during step-5 debug).

  builds a fully valid in-memory solid; the *written* STEP re-reads 14% low
  (3087 vs 3590 mm³) → fails `--compare` at stage 4.1. `pipe_elbow_10_medium`

    and BOTH pass geometric AND topological `BRepCheck_Analyzer`. There is
    no in-memory defect to find.
  - **The corruption is entirely in OCCT's STEP export.** OCCT re-expresses
    every pcurve as a B-spline on write (the file has 20 `B_SPLINE_CURVE`s,
    only 3 exact `CIRCLE`s). For the fine mesh this conversion produces a
    DEGENERATE pcurve for one end-cap plane: on re-import that face's UV

    while its 3D area stays ~78.5. The re-imported solid is STILL

    carry a sub-micron parametric seam offset — torus `V=[-3.5e-6, 2π-3.5e-6]`
    and a cylinder `U=[-1e-5, 2π-1e-5]`, versus medium's exact `[0, 2π]`.
