    positioned vertex chains) is invisible to `BRepCheck` but appears to be
    what tips OCCT's pcurve→B-spline export into the degenerate case for the
    adjacent end-cap. The fix probably lives in stage-3 pcurve/seam
    construction (`build_pcurve`, seam re-anchoring): snap periodic-face
    parameter domains to exactly `[0, 2π]` and/or attach exact-circle
    pcurves (not B-splines) for circular edges so OCCT does not resample.
  Reproduce: `brepper tests/onshape/pipe_elbow_10_fine.stl -o out.step -v`

Everything is clean and committed. Here's the summary of the investigation and what I built.

## What the pipe_elbow_fine issue actually is

The user's hint was key: the geometry *should* be identical to medium, so differences are diagnostic. I built a probe that reads the written STEP back per-face (type + area + UV bounds + BRepCheck) and instrumented stage 4 to dump the in-memory faces before writing. The result **revised my earlier "real geometry inconsistency" read**:

- **The deduced geometry is correct and identical-quality for both meshes.** In memory, every face of both medium and fine has clean exact pcurve bounds — both end-cap planes are exactly `dU=dV=10` (a radius-5 disk), the torus is `U∈[0,π/2] V∈[0,2π]`, the volume is 3589.98mm³, and **both pass geometric *and* topological BRepCheck**. There is no in-memory defect.
- **The corruption is entirely in OCCT's STEP export.** OCCT re-expresses every pcurve as a B-spline on write (the file has 20 B-spline curves, only 3 exact circles). For the fine mesh, that conversion **degenerates one end-cap plane's pcurve** — on re-import the face's UV domain collapses to a point (`U=[59.14681,59.14681]`) while its 3D area stays ~78.5. The re-imported solid is still topologically valid and closed, but BRepGProp's volume integral uses the collapsed pcurve domain and loses one end-cap's worth → 3087 vs 3590 (14%).
- **Likely trigger** (a fix lead, not fixed here): fine's periodic faces carry a sub-micron seam offset (torus `V=[-3.5e-6, 2π-3.5e-6]` vs medium's exact `[0,2π]`), invisible to BRepCheck but apparently enough to tip OCCT's export into the degenerate case. The fix probably belongs in stage-3 pcurve/seam construction (snap periodic domains to `[0,2π]`, or attach exact-circle pcurves for circular edges so OCCT doesn't resample).

## Can it be recognized before shipping a bad STEP?

Not by any in-memory check — the in-memory solid is pristine by every geometric *and* topological measure, so BRepCheck/volume/UV-bounds all pass. **The only reliable detector is a round-trip.** So I added an unconditional **STEP round-trip self-check** in [stage4.rs](src/stage4.rs): measure the in-memory solid volume before the write, re-read the written STEP once, and warn if the re-imported volume differs by >1%. It:
- Cleanly separates good from bad (medium 3e-5 → silent OK; fine 0.14 → a prominent `Stage 4.1 WARNING` naming the likely pcurve degeneracy).
- Has **no false positives** across the corpus (all passing models ≤2.1e-3; freeform B-splines round-trip at ~1e-14).
- Requires **no reference STEP** (works on any output), and the `--compare` path now reuses the same single re-read, with its error behavior unchanged.

## State
- Full diagnosis + fix lead recorded in [TODO.md](TODO.md).
- Throwaway probe removed; temporary debug scaffolding removed.
- Clippy clean (with and without `--tests`); stage3 99/7, stage4 28/8, competition 3/3, lib 90 — all unchanged, no regressions.
- Folded into the step-5-debug commit `31da32a` (title updated to mention the self-check). Working tree clean.

One note on scope: you asked to detect it "before the STEP round-trip phase," but the investigation showed the bug *is* the round-trip and nothing in-memory reveals it — so the self-check detects it at output time (before brepper returns), which serves the underlying goal of not silently shipping a STEP that misrepresents the computed solid. If you'd prefer this gated behind a flag (it does add one STEP re-read per run, which matters for very large models like 3DBenchy), that's a quick change.

/// Re-read the just-written STEP and verify it. The **round-trip self-check**
/// always runs: OCCT re-expresses every pcurve as a B-spline on STEP export,
/// and on some meshes a periodic-face pcurve degenerates (observed on
/// `pipe_elbow_10_fine`: an end-cap plane's boundary collapsed to a point),
/// producing a re-import that is still topologically valid and closed but
/// bounds a different volume. The in-memory solid passes every geometric and
/// topological BRepCheck, so **only a round-trip catches this** — hence we
/// compare the re-imported volume against the in-memory volume measured before
/// the write. When `--compare` is set, the reference comparison reuses the
/// same re-read shape.
fn verify_output(
    output_path: &str,
    in_memory_volume: f64,
    config: &Config,
) -> Result<(), Stage4Error> {
    let comparing = config.compare_shape.is_some();

    let output_shape = match crate::read_step_file(output_path) {
        Ok(shape) => shape,
        Err(e) => {
            // With --compare an unreadable output is a hard error (the round
            // trip could not be validated); without it (e.g. -o /dev/null)
            // there is simply nothing to self-check.
            if comparing {
                eprintln!("  Compare 4.1: ERROR failed to re-read written STEP file {output_path}: {e}");
                return Err(Stage4Error::Compare(Stage4CompareError::RoundTrip {
                    path: output_path.to_string(),
                    error: e,
                }));
            }
            return Ok(());
        }
    };

    let output_vol = compute_volume(&output_shape);

    // Round-trip self-check (no reference needed).
    if in_memory_volume > 0.0 {
        let self_diff = (output_vol - in_memory_volume).abs() / in_memory_volume;
        if self_diff > STEP_ROUNDTRIP_VOLUME_TOL {
            eprintln!(
                "  Stage 4.1 WARNING: written STEP volume {output_vol:.6} mm\u{00b3} differs from \
                 the in-memory solid ({in_memory_volume:.6} mm\u{00b3}) by {self_diff:.2e} — the \
                 STEP file does not faithfully represent the computed geometry (a periodic-face \
                 pcurve likely degenerated on export). The in-memory solid is valid; the written \
                 file is not."
            );
        } else if !config.quiet {
            eprintln!("  Stage 4.1: STEP round-trip volume check OK (rel diff {self_diff:.2e})");
        }
    }

    // Reference comparison (--compare).
    if comparing {
        compare_output_to_step(&output_shape, output_vol, config)?;
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

```
/// Re-read the just-written STEP and verify it against the reference
/// (`--compare` only). One re-read feeds two checks:
///
///  1. **Round-trip self-check** — the re-imported volume vs the in-memory
///     solid volume measured before the write. OCCT re-expresses every pcurve
///     as a B-spline on STEP export, and on some meshes a periodic-face pcurve
///     degenerates (observed on `pipe_elbow_10_fine`: an end-cap plane's
///     boundary collapsed to a point), producing a re-import that is still
///     topologically valid and closed but bounds a different volume. The
///     in-memory solid passes every geometric and topological BRepCheck, so
///     **only a round-trip catches this** — the reference comparison alone
///     cannot tell "the geometry was wrong" from "a correct solid was
///     corrupted on export", which is what this self-check disambiguates.
///  2. **Reference comparison** — volume and distance vs the `--compare` STEP.
fn verify_output(
    output_path: &str,
    in_memory_volume: f64,
    config: &Config,
) -> Result<(), Stage4Error> {
    // An unreadable output (including -o /dev/null) means the round trip could
    // not be validated, which fails --compare.
    let output_shape = match crate::read_step_file(output_path) {
        Ok(shape) => shape,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("  Compare 4.1: ERROR failed to re-read written STEP file {output_path}: {e}");
            return Err(Stage4Error::Compare(Stage4CompareError::RoundTrip {
                path: output_path.to_string(),
                error: e,
            }));
        }
    };

    let output_vol = compute_volume(&output_shape);

    // 1. Round-trip self-check (against the in-memory solid, no reference).
    if in_memory_volume > 0.0 {
        let self_diff = (output_vol - in_memory_volume).abs() / in_memory_volume;
        if self_diff > STEP_ROUNDTRIP_VOLUME_TOL {
            eprintln!(
                "  Stage 4.1 WARNING: written STEP volume {output_vol:.6} mm\u{00b3} differs from \
                 the in-memory solid ({in_memory_volume:.6} mm\u{00b3}) by {self_diff:.2e} — the \
                 STEP file does not faithfully represent the computed geometry (a periodic-face \
                 pcurve likely degenerated on export). The in-memory solid is valid; the written \
                 file is not."
            );
        } else if !config.quiet {
            eprintln!("  Stage 4.1: STEP round-trip volume check OK (rel diff {self_diff:.2e})");
        }
    }

    // 2. Reference comparison.
    compare_output_to_step(&output_shape, output_vol, config)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

Based on the web search results, I found relevant information about OCCT's handling of STEP export with toroidal surfaces and related issues:

## Key Findings

**Degenerate Toroidal Surface Issue:**
In STEP export, an inner void can get transformed into a degenerate toroid, causing the void to only cut out a ~0.7mm thick shell of a sphere rather than cutting out its entire volume.

**Pcurve Handling:**
OCCT controls pcurve export through write.surfacecurve.mode, and OCCT converts all trimmed_curve entities to Geom2d_BSplineCurve during import. Pcurves from a STEP file are translated if present and read.surfacecurve.mode is 0; for each edge method ShapeFix_Edge::FixSameParameter() is called, and if the resulting tolerance is greater than the maximum value between 1.0 and 2*Value of basis precision, then the pcurve is recomputed.

**Periodic Surface Handling:**
OCCT's shape healing can split toroidal, cylindrical, conical, and spherical surfaces so that each resulting segment covers not more than a defined number of degrees.

The search results indicate these are known issues in OCCT's STEP translator related to how degenerate and periodic surfaces are exported and imported, though the specific round-trip bug you're referencing may require additional technical documentation or issue tracker details.

**No — I'd made it unconditional** (it re-read the output STEP on every run). ## OCCT version

brepper bundles **OCCT 7.9.3** (via `opencascade-rs`'s `occt-sys`, pinned to the `V7_9_3` tag). The current upstream release is now **8.0.0** (May 2026) / 8.0.0_p1 (June 2026) — so brepper is one major version behind.

## Is it a known OCCT bug, and is it fixed?

**Yes, this looks like a known OCCT bug with a matching fix already released in 8.0.0** — which brepper doesn't have yet. The OCCT 8.0.0 release notes list a fix that maps almost exactly onto our reproduction:

- **"partial torus creation handles inverted V range"** — our case is precisely a *partial* torus (the 90° bend) whose fine-mesh V-range came out slightly negative (`V=[-3.5e-6, 2π-3.5e-6]`), i.e. an inverted/offset V range.
- Plus **"periodic BSpline curve bounding works with the corrected tolerance"** and **"unstable PCurve processing… addressed during shape healing"** — both in the pcurve area where our end-cap pcurve degenerated.

The broader class (STEP export turning geometry into a degenerate toroid → volume error on re-import) also shows up in OCCT forum reports, so this isn't unique to us.

I recorded two concrete next steps in the TODO note (and commit `867f28a`):
1. **Bump the bundled OCCT to 8.0.0** and recheck — may fix it with no brepper change (not yet confirmed against this exact repro, so verify).
2. **Cheaper workaround to try first, no OCCT bump:** export without pcurves (`write.surfacecurve.mode=0`, `read.surfacecurve.mode=3`) and let the reader rebuild 2D pcurves from our *exact* 3D curves — sidestepping the bad B-spline pcurve conversion entirely. Needs a binding to `Interface_Static::SetIVal` before the STEP write.

## 🤖 Assistant
<!-- msg_011CdFip6AsJp5VAa9V54wnc -->

Short answer: **8.0.0_p1.**

A `_p1` patch release in OCCT is a hotfix on top of the same API/ABI as 8.0.0 — no migration cost over 8.0.0, just additional stabilization fixes. The release description for it was explicitly *"a hot patch on top of 8.0.0"* consolidating fixes (Gordon surface rework, BRepGraph stabilization, thread-safe numeric parsing, modeling crash/hang fixes), with the C++17 baseline and API unchanged from 8.0.0.

So there's no reason to pin the plain 8.0.0 tag when a strictly-newer, API-compatible patch of the same release exists. The only situations where you'd prefer plain `V8_0_0`:

- **Reproducibility of an existing pin** — not your case; you're moving off 7.9.3.
- **A regression introduced by the patch** — none reported that I saw, but worth a quick corpus run after the bump either way (you'd do that regardless of which tag).

One caveat on the whole plan: the upgrade is a change to the vendored OCCT in the sibling `opencascade-rs` repo (`crates/occt-sys/OCCT` is pinned to the `V7_9_3` tag), and its FFI bindings (`opencascade-sys`) are generated against that source. A 7.9.3 → 8.0.0 jump crosses a **major** version, so expect some binding/API churn (renamed/removed symbols, signature changes) — this is more involved than repointing a submodule, which is why I'd still **try the `write.surfacecurve.mode=0` workaround first**: it's a one-line `Interface_Static::SetIVal` in brepper and confirms whether the pcurve-export path is really the culprit before you take on a major OCCT bump.

If you do bump, go straight to `V8_0_0_p1`.

    // Omitting pcurves makes the reader rebuild them from our exact 3D edge
    // curves, sidestepping the bad conversion. (STEP write.surfacecurve.mode.)
    interface::Static::set_i_val("write.surfacecurve.mode", 0);

Here's the outcome.

## Is `Interface_Static::SetIVal` available?

**Yes.** The safe wrapper is `opencascade_sys::interface::Static::set_i_val(name: &str, val: i32) -> bool` (wrapping `Interface_Static::SetIVal` via the `Interface_Static_set_i_val` FFI), alongside `set_c_val`/`set_r_val` and the getters `i_val`/`c_val`/`r_val`. `write_step_file` already uses `set_c_val` for the schema, so the pattern was ready to go.

## Did mode = 0 work?

**No — I tried it and it doesn't fix the issue**, so I reverted it. The evidence is actually quite illuminating:

- Setting `write.surfacecurve.mode = 0` **did** take effect — the written STEP dropped from 20 B-spline pcurves + seam/surface curves to **zero pcurves**, leaving only the (exact) 3D edge curves.
- But the re-imported volume was **still 3087 mm³** (14% low). Adding `read.surfacecurve.mode = 3` (3D-preferred) didn't change it either.

That's a meaningful result: it **relocates the bug**. The degeneracy is *not* in the writer's pcurve→B-spline conversion, as I'd hypothesized — OCCT **rebuilds the pcurve from the 3D curve on read**, and *that reconstruction also degenerates* for this partial-torus periodic face. So the bug lives in OCCT 7.9.3's pcurve computation for the partial torus, hit on **both** the write and read paths. No `surfacecurve.mode` setting can route around it.

## Bottom line

The `surfacecurve.mode` lever is a dead end; the real fix is the **OCCT 8.0.0_p1 upgrade** (whose "partial torus creation handles inverted V range" fix matches this repro directly). I've recorded the failed workaround in the TODO note so the next session doesn't retry it, and noted that `interface::Static::set_i_val` is available if some future attempt needs it.

Working tree is clean; both experimental changes reverted (`lib.rs` back to its committed state). The only lasting change this turn is the corrected TODO note, folded into the step-5-debug commit. clippy clean.

One note: I amended the commit to correct the note, since the previously-committed version suggested the mode=0 workaround as promising — leaving that in would have misled the next session. If you'd rather I hadn't amended for a docs-only correction, say so and I'll adjust.

I've recorded the failed workaround in the TODO note so the next session doesn't retry it, and noted that \`interface::Static::set_i_val\` is available if some future attempt needs it.

Working tree is clean; both experimental changes reverted (\`lib.rs\` back to its committed state). The only lasting change this turn is the corrected TODO note, folded into the step-5-debug commit. clippy clean.

One note: I amended the commit to correct the note, since the previously-committed version suggested the mode=0 workaround as promising — leaving that in would have misled the next session. If you'd rather I hadn't amended for a docs-only correction, say so and I'll adjust.

    Upgrade to OCCT 8.0.0; pivot collections to canonical NCollection names; expand coverage
    
    Upgrades the vendored OCCT to V8_0_0_p1 and reworks the binding generator to
    match OCCT 8.0's API, which now uses the canonical \`NCollection_*<T>\` templates
    directly and deprecated the old \`TColgp_*\`/\`TColStd_*\`/\`TopTools_*\` aliases.
    
    Binding generator:
    - Exclude deprecated 8.0 backward-compat alias headers automatically
      (\`exclude_deprecated_headers\`), so bindings target canonical NCollection types.
    - Auto-discover NCollection instantiations from referenced template spellings and
      generate them under canonical \`n_collection::\` names with full method sets,
      including collections of primitive scalars and \`HArray1\`/\`HSequence\` handle
      collections (\`to_handle\`, \`get\`/\`get_mut\`).
    - Handle types use the \`Handle_<C++name>\` scheme (e.g. \`Handle_Geom_Curve\`).
    - Auto-register handle-able \`NCollection_H*<T>\` instantiations (they inherit
      \`Standard_Transient\`), so \`Handle(NCollection_HArray1<T>)\` parameters resolve.
      Skipped symbols drop from ~1,680 to ~720.
    - Collection iterators implement the standard \`Iterator\` trait (usable in \`for\`
      loops and adapters, via a blanket \`Iterator for OwnedPtr<I: Iterator>\`).
    - Shorten collection overload-suffix tokens (\`imap_shape\`, \`arr1_pnt\`, \`harr1_pnt\`,
      … — dropping the hasher argument) for readable overloaded method names.
    - Fix the opencascade-sys compile breakages surfaced by 8.0: non-allocatable-class
      handling, the Rust-2024 \`gen\` keyword, the private \`BRepGraphInc_BitFlags::BlockType\`
      typedef, and the unbuilt TKDraw toolkit.
    
    High-level crate, examples, and tests:
    - Port \`opencascade\` and all in-repo examples to the canonical names and new idioms.
...

//! Build script for opencascade-sys
//!
//! This script:
//! 1. Uses pre-generated code from the \`generated/\` directory
//! 2. Compiles wrappers.cpp with cc
//!
//! To regenerate the bindings, run:
//!   DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/lib cargo run -p opencascade-binding-generator -- \
//!     -I target/OCCT/include \
//!     -o crates/opencascade-sys/generated \
//!     $(cat crates/opencascade-sys/headers.txt | grep -v '^#' | grep -v '^$' | sed 's|^|target/OCCT/include/|')

use std::io::Write;
use std::path::PathBuf;

fn main() {
    let manifest_dir = PathBuf::from(std::env::var("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR").expect("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR not set"));
    let gen_dir = manifest_dir.join("generated");

    let target = std::env::var("TARGET").expect("No TARGET environment variable defined");
    let is_windows = target.to_lowercase().contains("windows");
    let is_windows_gnu = target.to_lowercase().contains("windows-gnu");

    // Detect OCCT installation
    let occt_config = OcctConfig::detect();

    println!("cargo:rustc-link-search=native={}", occt_config.library_dir.to_str().unwrap());
    if is_windows {
        println!("cargo:rustc-link-lib=dylib=user32");
    }

    // Find generated wrappers*.cpp files (may be split by toolkit)
    let mut wrapper_cpp_files: Vec<PathBuf> = std::fs::read_dir(&gen_dir)
        .expect("Failed to read generated/ directory")
        .filter_map(|entry| {
            let path = entry.ok()?.path();
            if path.extension().map_or(false, |e| e == "cpp")
                && path.file_stem().map_or(false, |s| s.to_string_lossy().starts_with("wrappers"))
            {
                Some(path)
            } else {
                None
            }
        })
        .collect();
    wrapper_cpp_files.sort();
    if wrapper_cpp_files.is_empty() {
        panic!("No generated wrappers*.cpp files found in {}. Run the binding generator first.", gen_dir.display());
    }

    // Derive OCCT libraries to link from generated wrapper file names.
    // Each wrappers_TK<name>.cpp corresponds to an OCCT library named TK<name>.
    let lib_type = if occt_config.is_dynamic { "dylib" } else { "static" };
    for cpp_file in &wrapper_cpp_files {
        if let Some(stem) = cpp_file.file_stem().and_then(|s| s.to_str()) {
            if let Some(lib_name) = stem.strip_prefix("wrappers_") {
                if lib_name.starts_with("TK") {
                    println!("cargo:rustc-link-lib={lib_type}={lib_name}");
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // Find manual wrapper .cpp files
    let manual_dir = manifest_dir.join("manual");
    let manual_cpp_files: Vec<PathBuf> = if manual_dir.exists() {
        std::fs::read_dir(&manual_dir)
            .expect("Failed to read manual/ directory")
            .filter_map(|entry| {
                let path = entry.ok()?.path();
                if path.extension().map_or(false, |e| e == "cpp") {
                    Some(path)
                } else {
                    None
                }
            })
            .collect()
    } else {
        Vec::new()
    };

    // Combine all per-toolkit wrappers into a single compilation unit.
    // This reduces total CPU time by avoiding redundant OCCT header parsing
    // across 50 separate files.
    let out_dir = PathBuf::from(std::env::var("OUT_DIR").expect("OUT_DIR not set"));
    let combined_cpp = out_dir.join("wrappers_combined.cpp");
    {
        let mut f = std::fs::File::create(&combined_cpp)
            .expect("Failed to create combined wrapper file");
        writeln!(f, "// Auto-generated: combines all per-toolkit wrappers into one TU").unwrap();
        for cpp_file in &wrapper_cpp_files {
            let abs = std::fs::canonicalize(cpp_file)
                .unwrap_or_else(|_| cpp_file.clone());
            writeln!(f, "#include \"{}\"", abs.display()).unwrap();
        }
    }

    // Build with cc
    let mut build = cc::Build::new();
    build.file(&combined_cpp);
    for cpp_file in &manual_cpp_files {
        build.file(cpp_file);
    }

    if is_windows_gnu {
        build.define("OCC_CONVERT_SIGNALS", "TRUE");
    }

    build
        .cpp(true)
        .flag_if_supported("-std=c++17")
        // Generated wrappers use extern "C" functions that return C++ reference types
        // (e.g. const TopoDS_Shape&). This is technically incompatible with C linkage
        // but works fine for Rust FFI where both sides agree on calling convention.
        .flag_if_supported("-Wno-unused-function")
        .flag_if_supported("-Wno-deprecated-declarations")
        .flag_if_supported("-Wno-return-type-c-linkage")
        // OCCT classes math_FunctionSample, Poly_MakeLoops, Poly_MakeLoops2D,
        // and Poly_MakeLoops3D have virtual functions but non-virtual destructors.
        // Our generated destructors always delete through the concrete type pointer
        // (e.g. delete static_cast<Poly_MakeLoops3D*>(ptr)), never through a base
        // pointer, so the non-virtual destructor is safe. OwnedPtr<T> ensures the
        // static type always matches the dynamic type.
        .flag_if_supported("-Wno-delete-non-abstract-non-virtual-dtor")
        .flag_if_supported("-Wno-delete-abstract-non-virtual-dtor")
        .define("_USE_MATH_DEFINES", "TRUE")
        .include(&gen_dir)
        .debug(false);

    // Treat the OCCT include directory as a system header path so the compiler
    // suppresses warnings from third-party OCCT code (e.g. sprintf deprecation).
    // MSVC does not support -isystem; on GCC/Clang it is standard.
    if target.contains("msvc") {
        build.include(&occt_config.include_dir);
        if let Some(ref bi) = occt_config.build_include_dir {
            build.include(bi);
        }
    } else {
        build.flag("-isystem");
        build.flag(occt_config.include_dir.to_str().unwrap());
        if let Some(bi) = &occt_config.build_include_dir {
            build.flag("-isystem");
            build.flag(bi.to_str().unwrap());
        }
    }

    build.compile("opencascade_sys_wrapper");

    println!("cargo:rustc-link-lib=static=opencascade_sys_wrapper");

    // Rerun if generated or manual files change
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=generated");
    for cpp_file in &wrapper_cpp_files {
        println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", cpp_file.display());
    }
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=manual");
    for cpp_file in &manual_cpp_files {
        println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", cpp_file.display());
    }
}

struct OcctConfig {
    include_dir: PathBuf,
    /// Optional build-time include directory containing generated \`.pxx\` headers
    /// that are not part of the installed public headers.
    build_include_dir: Option<PathBuf>,
    library_dir: PathBuf,
    is_dynamic: bool,
}

impl OcctConfig {
    /// Find OpenCASCADE library using cmake
    fn detect() -> Self {
        println!("cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=DEP_OCCT_ROOT");

        // Add path to builtin OCCT
        #[cfg(feature = "builtin")]
        {
            let builtin_occt_path = occt_sys::occt_path();

            // Skip building if OCCT appears to be already installed
            // Check for a key library file to determine if build is needed
            let marker_lib = builtin_occt_path.join("lib").join("libTKernel.a");
            if !marker_lib.exists() {
                occt_sys::build_occt();
            }
            // SAFETY: This build script is single-threaded, so there are no
            // concurrent reads of the environment variable.
            unsafe { std::env::set_var("DEP_OCCT_ROOT", builtin_occt_path.as_os_str()) };

            // With builtin feature, skip cmake detection and use built OCCT directly
            // Prefer include/ (installed headers, complete set) over build/include
            let include_dir = if builtin_occt_path.join("include").exists() {
                builtin_occt_path.join("include")
            } else if builtin_occt_path.join("build").join("include").exists() {
                builtin_occt_path.join("build").join("include")
            } else {
                panic!("Builtin OCCT include directory not found at {:?}", builtin_occt_path);
            };

            let library_dir = if builtin_occt_path.join("lib").exists() {
                builtin_occt_path.join("lib")
            } else if builtin_occt_path.join("build").join("lib").exists() {
                builtin_occt_path.join("build").join("lib")
            } else {
                panic!("Builtin OCCT library directory not found at {:?}", builtin_occt_path);
            };

                        let build_include_dir = {
                let p = builtin_occt_path.join("build").join("include");
                if p.exists() { Some(p) } else { None }
            };
            return Self {
                include_dir,
                build_include_dir,
                library_dir,
                is_dynamic: false  // Built OCCT is static
            };
        }

        // Non-builtin: use cmake detection
        #[cfg(not(feature = "builtin"))]
        {
            /// Minimum compatible version of OpenCASCADE library (major, minor)
            const OCCT_VERSION: (u8, u8) = (7, 8);

            let dst =
                std::panic::catch_unwind(|| cmake::Config::new("OCCT").register_dep("occt").build());
            let dst = dst.expect("Pre-installed OpenCASCADE library not found. You can use \`builtin\` feature if you do not want to install OCCT libraries system-wide.");

            let cfg = std::fs::read_to_string(dst.join("share").join("occ_info.txt"))
                .expect("Something went wrong when detecting OpenCASCADE library.");

            let mut version_major: Option<u8> = None;
            let mut version_minor: Option<u8> = None;
            let mut include_dir: Option<PathBuf> = None;
            let mut library_dir: Option<PathBuf> = None;
            let mut is_dynamic: bool = false;

            for line in cfg.lines() {
                if let Some((var, val)) = line.split_once('=') {
                    match var {
                        "VERSION_MAJOR" => version_major = val.parse().ok(),
                        "VERSION_MINOR" => version_minor = val.parse().ok(),
                        "INCLUDE_DIR" => include_dir = val.parse().ok(),
                        "LIBRARY_DIR" => library_dir = val.parse().ok(),
                        "BUILD_SHARED_LIBS" => is_dynamic = val == "ON",
                        _ => (),
                    }
                }
            }

            if let (Some(version_major), Some(version_minor), Some(include_dir), Some(library_dir)) =
                (version_major, version_minor, include_dir, library_dir)
            {
                if version_major != OCCT_VERSION.0 || version_minor < OCCT_VERSION.1 {
                    panic!("Pre-installed OpenCASCADE library found but version is not met (found {}.{} but {}.{} required). Please provide required version or use \`builtin\` feature.",
                           version_major, version_minor, OCCT_VERSION.0, OCCT_VERSION.1);
                }

                Self { include_dir, build_include_dir: None, library_dir, is_dynamic }
            } else {
                panic!("OpenCASCADE library found but something wrong with config.");
            }
        }
    }
}

use std::{
    env::var,
    path::{Path, PathBuf},
};

const LIB_DIR: &str = "lib";
const INCLUDE_DIR: &str = "include";

/// Get the path to the OCCT library installation directory to be
/// used in build scripts.
///
/// Only valid during build (\`cargo clean\` removes these files).
pub fn occt_path() -> PathBuf {
    // moves the output into target/TARGET/OCCT
    // this way its less likely to be rebuilt without a cargo clean
    Path::new(&var("OUT_DIR").expect("missing OUT_DIR")).join("../../../../OCCT")
}

/// Build the OCCT library.
pub fn build_occt() {
    cmake::Config::new(Path::new(env!("OCCT_SRC_DIR")))
        .define("BUILD_LIBRARY_TYPE", "Static")
        .define("BUILD_MODULE_ApplicationFramework", "FALSE")
        .define("BUILD_MODULE_Draw", "FALSE")
        .define("BUILD_MODULE_Visualization", "FALSE")
        .define("USE_D3D", "FALSE")
        .define("USE_DRACO", "FALSE")
        .define("USE_EIGEN", "FALSE")
        .define("USE_FFMPEG", "FALSE")
        .define("USE_FREEIMAGE", "FALSE")

```
use std::{
    env::var,
    path::{Path, PathBuf},
};

const LIB_DIR: &str = "lib";
const INCLUDE_DIR: &str = "include";

/// Name of the stamp file (written under [`occt_path`]) recording which OCCT
/// source revision the built artifacts correspond to. See [`occt_source_stamp`].
const STAMP_FILE: &str = ".occt-src-stamp";

/// Get the path to the OCCT library installation directory to be
/// used in build scripts.
///
/// Only valid during build (`cargo clean` removes these files).
pub fn occt_path() -> PathBuf {
    // moves the output into target/TARGET/OCCT
    // this way its less likely to be rebuilt without a cargo clean
    Path::new(&var("OUT_DIR").expect("missing OUT_DIR")).join("../../../../OCCT")
}

/// A short identifier for the OCCT source the current bindings target.
///
/// This is the checked-out commit of the vendored OCCT submodule. It is written
/// into a stamp file after a successful build (see [`build_occt`]) and compared
/// on subsequent builds so that bumping the submodule (e.g. a version upgrade)
/// invalidates a stale prebuilt tree instead of being silently reused. Falls
/// back to the empty string if git is unavailable, which degrades to the old
/// "marker file exists" behaviour.
pub fn occt_source_stamp() -> String {
    let src = env!("OCCT_SRC_DIR");
    std::process::Command::new("git")
        .args(["-C", src, "rev-parse", "HEAD"])
        .output()
        .ok()
        .filter(|out| out.status.success())
        .map(|out| String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout).trim().to_string())
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

/// Whether the prebuilt OCCT under [`occt_path`] is present and matches the
/// current source revision, so a rebuild can be skipped.
pub fn occt_is_up_to_date() -> bool {
    let path = occt_path();
    let marker_lib = path.join(LIB_DIR).join("libTKernel.a");
    if !marker_lib.exists() {
        return false;
    }
    match std::fs::read_to_string(path.join(STAMP_FILE)) {
        Ok(stamp) => stamp.trim() == occt_source_stamp(),
        // Marker present but no stamp: an older or externally-produced build we
        // can't verify — rebuild to be safe.
        Err(_) => false,
    }
}
```

/// Exact cubic B-spline curve in the XZ plane (y=0) from poles at
/// x = x0 + i*d, z from \`zs\`.
fn profile_bspline_curve(x0: f64, d: f64, zs: &[f64]) -> OwnedPtr<geom::Handle_Geom_BSplineCurve> {
    let n = zs.len();
    let mut poles = n_collection::Array1_gp_Pnt::new_int2(1, n as i32);
    for (i, z) in zs.iter().enumerate() {
        let p = gp::Pnt::new_real3(x0 + i as f64 * d, 0.0, *z);
        poles.set_value(i as i32 + 1, &p);
    }
    let (knots, mults) = clamped_cubic_knots(n);
    let curve = geom::BSplineCurve::new_array1ofpnt_array1ofreal_array1ofinteger_int(
        &poles, &knots, &mults, 3,
    );
    geom::BSplineCurve::to_handle(curve)
}

pub fn stage2(
    config: &Config,
    mesh: ConnectedMesh,
    viz: Option<&crate::viz::VizSender>,
) -> Result<Stage2Output, Stage2Error> {
    // --- Stage 2.1(a): sharp-edge classification (fit-free) ---
    let t = Instant::now();
    let edge_classes = edges::classify_edges(&mesh, config.angular_tolerance_rad);
    if config.verbosity >= 1 {
        let total = edge_classes.sharp_count + edge_classes.interior_count;
        eprintln!(
            "Stage 2.1(a) ({:.3}s): Sharp-edge classification: {} manifold edges — {} sharp, {} interior",
            t.elapsed().as_secs_f64(),
            total,
            edge_classes.sharp_count,
            edge_classes.interior_count,
        );
    }
    // --- Stage 2.1(b): osculating-jet curvature prior ---
    let t = Instant::now();
    let jet = edges::compute_jet_field(&mesh, &edge_classes);
    if config.verbosity >= 1 {
        eprintln!(
            "Stage 2.1(b) ({:.3}s): Jet curvature prior: {} faces summarized",
            t.elapsed().as_secs_f64(),
            jet.len(),
        );
    }
    let mut segmentation = Segmentation {
        edge_classes,
        jet,
        face_region: Vec::new(),
        regions: Vec::new(),
    };
    if config.viz_active(2, 1) {
        if let Some(vs) = viz {
            let overlay = segmentation_edges_overlay(&mesh, &segmentation.edge_classes);
            if matches!(vs.show_and_wait(overlay), VizAction::Quit) {
                return Ok(segmentation_only_output(mesh, segmentation));
            }
        }
    }
    if !config.stage.at_least(2, 2) {
        return Ok(segmentation_only_output(mesh, segmentation));
    }

    // --- Stage 2.2: region extraction ---
    let t = Instant::now();
    let (face_region, region_list) =
        regions::extract_regions(&mesh, &segmentation.edge_classes);
    if config.verbosity >= 1 {
        let single = region_list.iter().filter(|r| r.faces.len() == 1).count();
        let largest = region_list.iter().map(|r| r.faces.len()).max().unwrap_or(0);
        eprintln!(
            "Stage 2.2 ({:.3}s): Region extraction: {} regions over {} faces ({} single-face, largest {} faces)",
            t.elapsed().as_secs_f64(),
            region_list.len(),
            mesh.faces.len(),
            single,
            largest,
        );
        if config.verbosity >= 2 {
            for (i, r) in region_list.iter().enumerate() {
                if r.faces.len() > 1 {
                    eprintln!(
                        "  Region {}: {} faces, {} vertices (first face {})",
                        i,
                        r.faces.len(),
                        r.vertices.len(),
                        r.faces[0],
                    );
                }
            }
        }
    }
    segmentation.face_region = face_region;
    segmentation.regions = region_list;
    if config.viz_active(2, 2) {
        if let Some(vs) = viz {
            let overlay = segmentation_regions_overlay(&mesh, &segmentation);
            if matches!(vs.show_and_wait(overlay), VizAction::Quit) {
                return Ok(segmentation_only_output(mesh, segmentation));
            }
        }
    }

    if !config.stage.at_least(2, 3) {
        return Ok(segmentation_only_output(mesh, segmentation));
    }

    // --- Stage 2.3: per-region surface discovery (ladder + competition) ---
    let t = Instant::now();
    let mut cls = classify::classify_regions(&mesh, &segmentation.regions, &segmentation.jet, config);
    if config.verbosity >= 1 {
        eprintln!(
            "Stage 2.3 ({:.3}s): Region classification: {} surfaces ({} planar, {} cyl/cone, {} spherical, {} toroidal)",
            t.elapsed().as_secs_f64(),
            cls.selected.len(),
            cls.planar.len(),
            cls.conical.len(),
            cls.spherical.len(),
            cls.toroidal.len(),
        );
    }

    // --- Stage 2.4: resolution & repair (relabel, merge, re-split) ---
    if config.stage.at_least(2, 4) {
        let t = Instant::now();
        let stats = repair::repair(&mesh, &mut cls, config);
        if config.verbosity >= 1 {
            eprintln!(
                "Stage 2.4 ({:.3}s): Repair: {} relabeled, {} merged, {} re-split → {} surfaces",
                t.elapsed().as_secs_f64(),
                stats.relabeled,
                stats.merged,
                stats.split,
                cls.selected.len(),
            );
        }
    }

occt-sys: rebuild builtin OCCT when the source revision changes

The builtin OCCT build gated only on "does libTKernel.a exist?", so bumping
the vendored submodule (e.g. the 8.0 upgrade) silently reused a stale prebuilt
tree in each consumer's target/OCCT until a manual `rm -rf`. It surfaced as
`BRepGraph_ItemId.hxx file not found` when freshly generated 8.0 wrappers were
compiled against stale 7.9.3 headers.

Record the submodule's checked-out commit in a `.occt-src-stamp` file after
each successful build, and skip rebuilding only when the marker library is
present AND the stamp matches the current source (`occt_is_up_to_date`). A
marker present without a matching stamp is treated as stale and rebuilt.
Degrades to the old marker-only behaviour when git is unavailable.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

Done. Here's the summary.

## What happened

**1. Why the build was broken.** brepper keeps its *own* builtin OCCT under `brepper/target/OCCT` (separate from opencascade-rs's), and the build gated only on "does `libTKernel.a` exist?" — so your submodule bump to 8.0 was silently ignored and the freshly-generated 8.0 wrappers were compiled against stale 7.9.3 headers → `BRepGraph_ItemId.hxx not found`. You didn't skip a step; the build system had no invalidation edge for a source-revision change.

**2. Fixed the invalidation (opencascade-rs, commit `a9bf1bf` on `rust-2024`).** `occt-sys` now writes a `.occt-src-stamp` (the submodule's checked-out SHA) after each build and rebuilds when it mismatches (`occt_is_up_to_date`), instead of the marker-only check. Per your instruction, `brepper/target/OCCT` is now a **symlink** to `../opencascade-rs/target/OCCT` (its fresh 8.0 build) with a matching stamp — sharing one build rather than duplicating the ~15-min compile.

**3. Ported brepper to the 8.0 API (commit `4b20904` on `experiment-fable`).** 5 files: `t_colgp::/t_col_std::` collection types → `n_collection::`, `HandleGeom*` → `geom::Handle_Geom_*`, and shortened ctor/method names. A recurring trap: rustc's fuzzy "similar name" suggestions kept pointing at the wrong *rational* BSpline overloads — I verified each arg list and used the correct non-rational ones.

**4. Tests: zero regressions.** Results match the documented pre-upgrade baseline *exactly* — lib 90, stage1 83, stage2_segmentation 14, stage2_competition all green, stage2_integration 132/53 (stale pre-rewrite suite), stage3 99/7, stage4 28/8, same failing set. All remaining failures are pre-existing and documented (stale BFS-era tests, coarse-mesh blob fallback, ccad geometry mismatch).

**5. The STEP round-trip issue is FIXED.** pipe_elbow_10_fine's written STEP now reads back at the correct volume 3589.9 mm³ (round-trip rel diff 7.6e-9) and passes `--compare` end-to-end — it was a 14% loss (3087 mm³) under 7.9.3. OCCT 8.0.0_p1's partial-torus fix resolved it with no brepper code change, exactly as hypothesized.

One incidental note worth flagging: OCCT 8.0's STEP reader now *loads* the 4 ccad reference STEPs that gave "Reterror" under 7.9.3. Those tests still fail, but now at a stage-3 geometry compare (~3.95 mm edge distance) — a pre-existing reconstruction mismatch that was previously masked by the load failure, not a regression.

Memory updated (project-state + step-5-debug + index). The only uncommitted items are your untracked `tests/downloaded/` STL/STEP files, which I left alone.

Surviving boundary-vertex stations keep their exact pinned positions; new substations land only inside long segments, where a long boundary chord means the mesh itself is flat and mid-segment samples lie on the true surface. Good question to push on — the answer is **no**, nothing in the automated suite runs on it.

- **No test loads `tests/downloaded/3DBenchy.stl` or `.step`.** The only place the file path appears is a manual repro command in `TODO.md:135` (`./target/release/brepper tests/downloaded/3DBenchy.stl -o /tmp/benchy.step`). The `#[test]` functions in `stage3.rs` that mention "3DBenchy" are regression tests that **inline the minimal failing geometry** (e.g. `bounded_bspline_trim_parameters_stay_in_domain` builds a small hardcoded point array reproducing the crash shape) — they don't read the 11 MB file. That's deliberate: full stage 2 on 3DBenchy's ~196k faces ran ~15 min under the old pipeline, far too slow for the suite.

- So 3DBenchy is a **committed manual-corpus asset**: used for hand-run debugging and as the historical origin of many regression comments, but not exercised by `cargo test`.

That reframes your untracked files: `OrcaCube v2` and `xyz-cube-test-20mm` are the same *kind* of thing 3DBenchy is — manual corpus models, not test inputs. So "commit them like 3DBenchy" would mean committing them purely as manual-run assets, not because any test needs them (none does, and `xyz-cube` is only referenced conceptually in comments).

Given that, the real question is whether you want ~3.2 MB of manual-only models in the repo history. Options:
1. **Commit** them to `tests/downloaded/` as manual corpus (matches 3DBenchy precedent).
2. **Leave untracked** (they stay local; fine if they're scratch).
3. **Gitignore** `tests/downloaded/` for un-referenced downloads while keeping the two 3DBenchy files tracked — though that's a bit inconsistent.

I'd lean toward (1) only if you actually reach for these in manual runs the way you do 3DBenchy; otherwise (2). Which do you want?

2020	/// Boundary-edge line segments for viz, one segment per undirected sharp
2021	/// edge, offset slightly along the adjacent faces' average normal so they
2022	/// sit visibly on top of the rendered mesh instead of z-fighting it.
2023	/// Returns positions as [p0, p1, p0, p1, ...] pairs.
2024	fn boundary_line_positions(
2025	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
2026	    ec: &EdgeClassification,
2027	) -> Vec<[f32; 3]> {
2028	    let mut min = [f64::INFINITY; 3];
2029	    let mut max = [f64::NEG_INFINITY; 3];
2030	    for v in &mesh.vertices {
2031	        for (k, c) in [v.x, v.y, v.z].into_iter().enumerate() {
2032	            min[k] = min[k].min(c);
2033	            max[k] = max[k].max(c);
2034	        }
2035	    }
2036	    let diag = ((max[0] - min[0]).powi(2)
2037	        + (max[1] - min[1]).powi(2)
2038	        + (max[2] - min[2]).powi(2))
2039	    .sqrt();
2040	    let offset = if diag.is_finite() { diag * 5e-4 } else { 0.0 };
2041	
2042	    let mut sharp = Vec::new();
2043	    for fi in 0..mesh.faces.len() {
2044	        let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
2045	        for e in 0..vc {
2046	            let ni = mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[e];
2047	            if ni < fi as i32 {
2048	                continue; // open edge, or emitted from the other side
2049	            }
2050	            if ec.class[fi][e] != EdgeClass::Sharp {
2051	                continue;
2052	            }
2053	            let n1 = mesh.faces[fi].normal.unwrap_or([0.0; 3]);
2054	            let n2 = mesh.faces[ni as usize].normal.unwrap_or(n1);
2055	            let mut nn = [n1[0] + n2[0], n1[1] + n2[1], n1[2] + n2[2]];
2056	            let len = (nn[0] * nn[0] + nn[1] * nn[1] + nn[2] * nn[2]).sqrt();
2057	            if len > 1e-12 {
2058	                for c in &mut nn {
2059	                    *c /= len;
2060	                }
2061	            } else {
2062	                nn = [0.0; 3];
2063	            }
2064	            let va = &mesh.vertices[mesh.faces[fi].vertex_indices[e]];
2065	            let vb = &mesh.vertices[mesh.faces[fi].vertex_indices[(e + 1) % vc]];
2066	            let pa = [
2067	                (va.x + nn[0] * offset) as f32,
2068	                (va.y + nn[1] * offset) as f32,
2069	                (va.z + nn[2] * offset) as f32,
2070	            ];
2071	            let pb = [
2072	                (vb.x + nn[0] * offset) as f32,
2073	                (vb.y + nn[1] * offset) as f32,
2074	                (vb.z + nn[2] * offset) as f32,
2075	            ];
2076	            sharp.push(pa);
2077	            sharp.push(pb);
2078	        }
2079	    }
2080	    sharp
2081	}
2082	
2083	fn push_boundary_lines(overlay: &mut viz::VizOverlay, mesh: &ConnectedMesh, ec: &EdgeClassification) {
2084	    let sharp = boundary_line_positions(mesh, ec);

2086	        overlay.lines.push(viz::LineOverlay {
2087	            positions: sharp,
2088	            color: SHARP_EDGE_COLOR,
2089	            no_depth_test: false,
2090	        });
2091	    }
2092	}

2098	        ec.sharp_count, ec.interior_count,

2104	/// Deterministic distinct color for region \`i\`: golden-ratio hue stepping.
2105	fn region_color(i: usize) -> [f32; 4] {
2106	    let h = (i as f64 * 0.618_033_988_749_895).fract() * 6.0;
2107	    let sector = (h.floor() as i32).rem_euclid(6);
2108	    let f = h - h.floor();
2109	    let (s, v) = (0.55, 0.9);
2110	    let p = v * (1.0 - s);
2111	    let q = v * (1.0 - s * f);
2112	    let t = v * (1.0 - s * (1.0 - f));
2113	    let (r, g, b) = match sector {
2114	        0 => (v, t, p),
2115	        1 => (q, v, p),
2116	        2 => (p, v, t),
2117	        3 => (p, q, v),
2118	        4 => (t, p, v),
2119	        _ => (v, p, q),
2120	    };
2121	    [r as f32, g as f32, b as f32, 1.0]
2122	}

2127	    let largest = seg.regions.iter().map(|r| r.faces.len()).max().unwrap_or(0);
2128	    overlay.status_text = format!(
2129	        "Stage 2.2: {} regions ({} single-face, largest {} faces) — sharp boundaries in red [space=continue, q=quit]",
2130	        seg.regions.len(),
2131	        single,
2132	        largest,
2133	    );
2134	    overlay.face_highlights = seg
2135	        .regions
2136	        .iter()
2137	        .enumerate()
2138	        .map(|(i, r)| viz::FaceHighlight {
2139	            face_indices: r.faces.clone(),
2140	            color: region_color(i),
2141	        })
2142	        .collect();

230	/// Fit surface type \`S\` to a region and validate it against the whole region.
231	/// Large regions fit on a stride subsample, refit-augmented with the worst
232	/// validation offenders on a near-miss. Returns the committed hypothesis, or
233	/// \`None\` if \`S\` cannot explain the region within tolerance.
234	///
235	/// Also the stage-2.4 merge revalidation entry point (\`repair.rs\`): refit a
236	/// candidate union and confirm it validates end to end before committing.
237	pub(super) fn fit_validate<S: SurfaceType>(
238	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
239	    region_faces: &[usize],
240	    region_verts: &[usize],
241	    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
242	    config: &Config,
243	) -> Option<S::Hypothesis> {
244	    let vtol = config.vertex_tolerance_mm;
245	    let stol = config.surface_tolerance_mm;
246	
247	    // Initial fit set: the whole region, or a deterministic stride subsample
248	    // when the region is large.
249	    let mut fit_faces: Vec<usize> = if region_faces.len() > MAX_FIT_FACES {
250	        let stride = region_faces.len().div_ceil(MAX_FIT_FACES);
251	        region_faces.iter().copied().step_by(stride).collect()
252	    } else {
253	        region_faces.to_vec()
254	    };
255	
256	    for _round in 0..=MAX_REFIT {
257	        let fit_verts = vertices_of(mesh, &fit_faces);
258	        let mut fit = S::fit_surface(mesh, &fit_faces, &fit_verts, config.verbosity)?;
259	        S::determine_convexity(mesh, region_faces, &mut fit);
260	
261	        // Validate every region face; collect near-miss offenders for a refit.
262	        let mut offenders: Vec<(f64, usize)> = Vec::new();
263	        for &fi in region_faces {
264	            // Orientation coherence: a face whose normal disagrees with the
265	            // fitted surface's convexity means the region is not one clean
266	            // surface of type S — no refit rescues that.
267	            if !S::convexity_check(&fit, mesh, fi) {
268	                return None;
269	            }
270	            let face = &mesh.faces[fi];
271	            let vc = face.vertex_count as usize;
272	            let mut excess = 0.0_f64;
273	            for &vi in &face.vertex_indices[..vc] {
274	                let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
275	                let d = S::vertex_distance(&fit, &[v.x, v.y, v.z]);
276	                if d > vtol {
277	                    excess = excess.max(d - vtol);
278	                }
279	            }
280	            let cd = S::centroid_distance(&fit, &centroids[fi]);
281	            if cd > stol {
282	                excess = excess.max(cd - stol);
283	            }
284	            if excess > 0.0 {
285	                offenders.push((excess, fi));
286	            }
287	        }
288	
289	        if offenders.is_empty() {
290	            return Some(S::make_hypothesis(
291	                mesh,
292	                region_faces.to_vec(),
293	                region_verts.to_vec(),
294	                &fit,
295	            ));
296	        }
297	
298	        // Near-miss handling: if the worst offender is far out, the region is
299	        // decisively not this surface. Otherwise fold the worst offenders
300	        // into the fit set and refit (bounded rounds).
301	        offenders.sort_by(|a, b| {
302	            b.0.partial_cmp(&a.0)
303	                .unwrap()
304	                .then_with(|| a.1.cmp(&b.1))
305	        });
306	        if offenders[0].0 > REFIT_GIVE_UP * stol {
307	            return None;
308	        }
309	        let before = fit_faces.len();
310	        let existing: HashSet<usize> = fit_faces.iter().copied().collect();
311	        for &(_, fi) in offenders.iter().take(REFIT_ADD) {
312	            if !existing.contains(&fi) {
313	                fit_faces.push(fi);
314	            }
315	        }
316	        fit_faces.sort_unstable();
317	        fit_faces.dedup();
318	        if fit_faces.len() == before {
319	            // No new faces to learn from — cannot improve.
320	            return None;
321	        }
322	    }
323	    None
324	}
325	
326	/// Size of the largest mesh-connected component within a face set.
327	fn largest_component(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, faces: &[usize]) -> usize {
328	    let member: HashSet<usize> = faces.iter().copied().collect();
329	    let mut seen: HashSet<usize> = HashSet::new();
330	    let mut largest = 0usize;
331	    for &start in faces {
332	        if seen.contains(&start) {
333	            continue;
334	        }
335	        let mut size = 0usize;
336	        let mut stack = vec![start];
337	        seen.insert(start);
338	        while let Some(fi) = stack.pop() {
339	            size += 1;
340	            let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
341	            for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
342	                if ni >= 0 {
343	                    let ni = ni as usize;
344	                    if member.contains(&ni) && seen.insert(ni) {
345	                        stack.push(ni);
346	                    }
347	                }
348	            }
349	        }
350	        largest = largest.max(size);
351	    }
352	    largest
353	}

355	/// Sorted, deduplicated vertex indices of a face set.
356	fn vertices_of(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, faces: &[usize]) -> Vec<usize> {
357	    let mut v: Vec<usize> = faces
358	        .iter()
359	        .flat_map(|&fi| {
360	            let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
361	            mesh.faces[fi].vertex_indices[..vc].iter().copied()
362	        })
363	        .collect();
364	    v.sort_unstable();
365	    v.dedup();
366	    v
367	}

369	/// A single-face planar hypothesis (the terminal per-facet fallback).
370	fn facet_plane(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, fi: usize) -> PlanarHypothesis {
371	    let face = &mesh.faces[fi];
372	    let vc = face.vertex_count as usize;
373	    let vertices: Vec<usize> = face.vertex_indices[..vc].to_vec();
374	    let vertex_set: HashSet<usize> = vertices.iter().copied().collect();
375	    let (normal, distance) = fit_plane(&[fi], &vertex_set, &mesh.faces, &mesh.vertices);
376	    let mut error_max = f64::NEG_INFINITY;
377	    let mut error_min = f64::INFINITY;
378	    let mut error_abs_sum = 0.0_f64;
379	    for &vi in &vertices {
380	        let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
381	        let d = normal[0] * v.x + normal[1] * v.y + normal[2] * v.z - distance;
382	        error_max = error_max.max(d);
383	        error_min = error_min.min(d);
384	        error_abs_sum += d.abs();
385	    }
386	    PlanarHypothesis {
387	        normal,
388	        distance,
389	        faces: vec![fi],

524	
525	**Algorithm (\`deduce_bspline_surfaces\`, per component):**
526	1. Components planar to fitting exactness (10× vertex tolerance,
527	   NaN-guarded: the area-weighted normal of a closed region cancels to
528	   zero) become a multi-face planar hypothesis instead — a plane is
529	   preferable to a B-spline that overfits noise. Components below 4 faces
530	   are not fitted (they degrade to per-facet planes).
531	2. **Parameterize** the region onto the unit square: outer boundary loop pinned by cumulative chord length, 4 corners chosen where the adjacent *outside* region changes (arc-length-quartile fallback when the boundary offers ≠ 4 transitions), interior and hole-loop vertices solved with Floater mean-value weights by Gauss–Seidel (convergence enforced — an unconverged map voids Floater's bijectivity guarantee). Quads are split along the v0–v2 diagonal for weighting and sampling. **Closed bands** (a second boundary loop of extent ≥ half the largest — a small hole floats freely, a comparable second loop means the region wraps, e.g. the wall of a closed prism) are first **seam-cut** into a disk along a shortest vertex path between the two loops (\`cut_region_seam\`): the path follows FACE perimeter edges only (a path along a quad's split diagonal would tear that quad across the cut), its vertices are duplicated, right-side triangle fans switch to the clones, and the boundary re-chains into one loop whose two cut copies carry a \`CUT_OUTSIDE\` id — corner detection then lands the 4 corners exactly at the cut endpoints. The clones keep their originals' positions, so the two parameter-extreme grid columns of the around-the-band axis carry identical data (the periodic fit drops the closing one; the clamped fallback fit keeps both and closes exactly through the shared column).
532	3. **Resample a grid** through the flattened triangulation (uniform-bin point location; numeric misses near corner slivers are clamped to the nearest triangle within one bin — feeding them to the hole membrane extrapolates garbage). Grid stations per axis are the boundary vertices' own pinned positions (stations *between* the vertices of a coarse profile sample chord interiors and pin the fit to the chordal prism — a 1.7% volume deficit on the arch, the mesh's own chordal error), subdivided up to an interior-density target of ~1.5·√(region vertices) (a flat margin tessellates coarsely: hill_with_hole has 8-vertex sides on a 946-vertex region). Station spacing is **conditioned in 3D-arc measure** (\`axis_stations\`): chord-length-parametrized C2 interpolation amplifies data noise by roughly the square of the adjacent knot-spacing ratio, so a boundary mixing fine facets with one long straight chord (the xyz-cube letter walls: a 21× jump) turned a 0.02 mm-flat ribbon into control points 150 mm off the part while passing through every grid node exactly. Near-coincident stations (< 0.25× the median arc gap — the near-singular end of the same conditioning problem) are merged, and segments are subdivided to a fixpoint where no piece exceeds 2× either neighbor segment's pieces, uniformly in arc rather than UV (the Floater map compresses high-curvature areas). Surviving boundary-vertex stations keep their exact pinned positions; new substations land only inside long segments, where a long boundary chord means the mesh itself is flat and mid-segment samples lie on the true surface. Genuine hole interiors are filled with a Laplacian membrane so the fitter sees smooth data. The grid is flipped if needed so d1u×d1v matches the mesh's outward normals: B-spline faces are always \`concave = false\`.
533	4. **Fit**: \`GeomAPI_PointsToBSplineSurface::Interpolate\` (chord-length, C2 cubic) first — the grid is sampled from an exact-on-surface mesh, and OCCT's least-squares approximator reports \`IsDone\` while overshooting its \`Tol3D\` by millimeters near strongly curved patch boundaries. The approximator (tol = surface/8, then surface/2) remains as fallback, and grid density retries at caps 121/181/241. **Closed bands fit periodically**: \`Interpolate(…, thePeriodic=true)\` with the around-the-band axis as the array's FIRST index (transposed when that axis is v; the outward-orientation flip then reverses the second index and accounts for the transpose's normal negation) and the closing station omitted — OCCT appends the wrap-around copy of the first row itself and calls \`SetUPeriodic()\`. The periodic path is interpolation-only (the approximator binding carries no periodic flag). The resulting closure is C1, not C2 (position and D1 match across the wrap to ~1e-14; D2 jumps — measured), which nothing downstream requires. The fitted around-axis knots are then rescaled to exactly [0, 2π] via \`SetUKnots\` — an exact affine reparameterization (~1e-15 drift, measured) — because stage 3.4's wrapped-face machinery hard-codes that period. The U=0 iso is then exactly the cut path (chord-length parameters start at the first supplied row), a free seam gauge.
534	5. **Validate**: first a **control-point bound check** — every pole must lie within the grid data's bounding box inflated by half its diagonal. An ill-conditioned fit passes through every grid node exactly yet swings wildly between them, and the vertex/centroid validation below samples at data points, making it structurally blind to inter-node excursions; the surface lies in the convex hull of its poles, so poles near the data bound the whole surface near the data (the xyz-cube blow-up put poles 22 diagonals out; legit fits, including periodic bands, stay well inside the margin). Then every region vertex and face centroid within \`--surface-tolerance\` of the fit, each projection seeded from the vertex's own parameterization value (sequential seeding breaks at mesh row wraps, and neither \`NextValueOfUV\` nor \`ValueOfUV\` recovers reliably on many-knot surfaces). On failure at every grid density, the region returns to the 2.4 fallback ladder.
535	6. **Closed-band result**: the periodic fit produces ONE \`BSplineHypothesis\` with \`u_periodic = true\`, reconstructed by stage 3 as one wrapped face with a real seam edge — the form CAD kernels (and the references) write. If the periodic fit fails validation at every grid density, the band retries with the clamped fit and is **seam-split** (\`split_cut_hypothesis\`) into two \`SelectedSurface::BSpline\` halves sharing the fitted surface object; their two cut edges are plain edges that a reference model does not have, so the stage 3.1 edge compare will (correctly) flag them — the fallback trades compare-exactness for robustness and is currently exercised by no model.
536	
537	The \`BSplineHypothesis\` owns the fitted \`Geom_BSplineSurface\` (stage 3 reuses the same object via fresh handles) plus a cached, seed-rechecking \`ShapeAnalysis_Surface\` projector used by the 2.4 repair operations, \`--compare\`, and stage-3 charts/normals/projections. Stage-3 charts of B-spline faces also carry a parameter-space \`home\` anchor (the projection of the region's mean face centroid): a projection landing on a coincident-boundary curve of a seam-split band (the fallback) is ambiguous between the two parameter extremes (Newton, the gap re-check, and \`ValueOfUV\` all cannot tell — both branches are exact), and the branch nearer the face's own interior wins. On a periodic (u_periodic) chart the U-arm of that resolution is replaced by principal-value reduction to [0, 2π) — the same contract as the analytic periodic charts — and the whole wrapped-face machinery (edge-sample branch unwrap, winding classification, seam planning/anchoring, pcurve shifts) applies verbatim. There is no compare exemption: the stage 3.1 edge/vertex compare is fully armed for every edge, including the seam (a real feature both the reconstruction and the reference have).
538	
539	**Periodic-band junctions (stage 3.3)**: the band's two cap junctions are closed-loop edges (no vertices) and must carry PERIODIC curves — seam planning re-anchors a closed edge with \`MakeEdge\` over [t, t+period] at a solved seam azimuth, which a closed-but-non-periodic curve refuses. Two mechanisms deliver that (both were needed on elliptical_cylinder): (a) an IntSS curve that comes back closed-but-non-periodic (observed type: \`Geom_TrimmedCurve\`, exact to ~1e-14) is converted via \`GeomConvert::CurveToBSplineCurve\` + \`SetPeriodic\` (exact, measured); (b) an IntSS curve that comes back as a genuine partial arc falls to the boundary-chain repair, whose closed-chain arm interpolates a periodic C2 B-spline through the chain vertices (\`GeomAPI_Interpolate\` with the periodic flag, closing point not repeated — ~4e-15 chain deviation observed). Partial-arc detection for closed loops keys on the ENDPOINT GAP, not the parameter span: a closed B-spline junction arrives over an arbitrary range (observed [0,1]), and the old span≠2π test replaced the true junction with a bogus circle (14.8 mm off, 12% volume error).
540	
541	**Periodic closed-band conventions (probed 2026-07-15, \`tmp/probe_periodic.rs\`; confirmed in \`GeomAPI_PointsToBSplineSurface.cxx\`)**: periodic along U = the array's FIRST index; supply each row once (OCCT appends the wrap-around copy of row 1 itself; a duplicated closing row would make the system singular); the result already has \`SetUPeriodic()\` applied. The around-the-band axis is NOT always U in the Floater square (elliptical_cylinder's cut copies land as the u-extreme sides, making v the around axis): \`cut_around_axis\` detects it from the \`CUT_OUTSIDE\` loop entries, and \`fit_grid\` transposes the array so the surface's U is always the around axis — \`BSplineHypothesis.u_periodic\` is a single flag, no per-axis plumbing. The stage-3.4 wrapped-face machinery (branch unwrap in \`sample_edge_uv\`, winding classification, \`align_loop\` offsets, pcurve shifts, seam handling — \`grep TWO_PI src/stage3.rs\`) hard-codes the 2π period; \`SetUKnots\` rescales the fitted knots exactly, after which it all applies verbatim once the chart reports \`u_periodic()\`. Debug probes: \`BREPPER_DEBUG_EDGE_UV=1\` prints every chart projection during edge sampling; \`--stage=3.4 -v\` prints per-edge pcurve deviations + UV endpoints per face; the \`-vvv\` fit-residual-vs-own-grid probe separates fit error from sampler/projection error.

543	**Implementation notes (from the stage-3 rework, 2026-07-08; all implemented — kept for reference):**
544	- *The chart contract.* A chart provides \`point_uv(p) → (u, v, pole_radius)\` and \`point_at(u, v)\`, plus \`u_periodic()\`/\`v_periodic()\`. For a B-spline chart: \`pole_radius\` is ∞ (like the plane chart — fitted height-field patches have no UV degeneracies), and **both periodic flags must be false for open patches** (\`u_periodic()\` is true only for the periodic closed-band fit). Every mod-2π unwrap/branch-lift in stage 3.4 is gated on those flags; reducing non-periodic parameter coordinates mod 2π silently corrupts them (a real bug on plane charts once, masked for months — see LEARNINGS). With both flags false, the whole seam/winding/degenerate-pole machinery self-disables and B-spline faces take the plain-loop path end to end.
545	- *The chart must wrap the exact \`Handle(Geom_BSplineSurface)\` stored in \`FaceDescriptor.surface\`* — never a reconstruction. Use one \`ShapeAnalysis_Surface\` per face: \`new_handlegeomsurface\` + \`value_of_uv(&mut self, pnt, precision)\` — note \`&mut\` (it caches internally). For sampling along an edge curve, prefer \`next_value_of_uv(prev_uv, pnt, preci, maxpreci)\`. Validate each solution with \`gap()\` and fall back to a fresh \`value_of_uv\` when the gap exceeds tolerance.

Choosing the convention at fit time is one line; recovering it later is a per-face heuristic.
548	- *Edge curves lean on the boundary chain.* \`GeomAPI_IntSS\` is flakier against B-spline surfaces than between quadrics, and tangent-classified junctions (a fitted patch usually meets its neighbors near-tangentially) may have no analytic construction — both routes end at the mesh-boundary-chain machinery (\`repair_edge_curve_from_boundary\`, \`edge_curve_from_boundary_chain\`), which is surface-pair-agnostic and fits line, circle, AND a \`GeomAPI_PointsToBSpline\` curve through the chain vertices, keeping whichever deviates least.

550	- *Test models*: \`tests/nurbs/\` — 8 exact-reference STL/STEP pairs from \`gen-test-models\` (see tests/nurbs/README.md for the difficulty ladder and the strip-mesh rationale: ruled/extruded models ship full-length strips with NO interior vertices along the ruling, exactly what real CAD exporters emit).
551	
552	#### 2.4 Resolution & repair
553	
554	Turns 2.3's claims into a strict, connected, validated partition. All
555	operations are fit-validated and deterministic (fixed iteration order —
556	by region/hypothesis index, smallest region first for merges — bounded
557	rounds).
558	
559	**Claim resolution** — the boundary placement at tangent junctions: faces
560	claimed by multiple hypotheses (junction rows) go to the claimant whose
561	surface fits their vertices best, requiring a **2× margin** to prefer a
562	different side than the larger claimant (a true junction face fits both
563	sides equally — the margin prevents arbitrary flapping; residual ties
564	break to the larger claimant, then lower hypothesis index). Exact vertex
565	distances, no curvature involved.
566	
567	**Boundary relabel** (±1-row polish; port of the old
568	\`refine_boundary_assignments\`): after resolution, walk region-boundary
569	faces; move a face when an adjacent region's surface fits its vertices at
570	least 2× better; iterate to a fixpoint (≤ 10 rounds; boundaries only move
571	locally), then rebuild affected regions' vertex lists. Region *geometry*
572	is not refitted — only the membership map changes.
573	
574	**Merge**: absorb region S into an adjacent larger region T when every
575	vertex of S lies within \`--vertex-tolerance\` of T's fitted surface and
576	every centroid of S within \`--surface-tolerance\`; refit the union,
577	revalidate, keep only if valid. Eats junction-circle singletons (faces
578	whose vertices sit ON a tangent seam — genuinely ambiguous, claimable by
579	either side), chord-degenerate slivers (a single-facet-wide band of a
580	coarse cylinder validates as its own facet plane, but its vertices lie
581	exactly on the neighbor cylinder), and residual same-surface fragments.
582	This is the abandoned absorb pass's *tight* rule reborn with a principled
583	criterion — vertex tolerance, at which "on the same surface" is decisive;
584	never the chordal slop of the abandoned loose rule (0.4mm slop, 794
585	BRepCheck failures on planar-only 3DBenchy). B-spline surfaces are never
586	merge TARGETS for faces outside their fitted region: a fit vouches only
587	for its data (the island-dissolution guard in 2.3(e) is the fit-validated
588	way into a freeform patch).
589	
590	**Connectivity re-split + invariants** (hard assertions before stage 3):
591	resolution and relabeling can disconnect a region — re-split into
592	mesh-connected components (identical fitted geometry on two non-adjacent
593	regions is legal). Then assert: every mesh face belongs to exactly one
594	region (total coverage); every region is mesh-connected; every region's
595	surface validates the region's own vertices/centroids.
596	
597	(The old standalone "split repair" is gone: under-segmentation cannot
598	survive 2.3 — competition decomposes within smooth regions — and a region
599	nothing explains degrades to per-facet planes via 2.3(e). There is no
600	mechanism left that re-runs a curvature classifier at lowered thresholds;
601	that mechanism died with the classifier.)

604	
605	- Build \`Vec<SelectedSurface>\` — one per region, the **unchanged stage-3
606	  input contract**: \`surface_type\` (Planar, Cylindrical, Spherical, Conical,

But for a mixed region where competition succeeded on some faces and left freeform for others, throwing away the good analytic fits just to per-facet everything feels wasteful, even if a gathering pass could theoretically recover them.

158	    let mut seeds = region.faces.clone();

163	            }

165	        })

216	            // azimuthally around the tube; it only approaches κ1 near the

224	            };

> Now I'm thinking through the cleanest way to integrate step 6 with the compete.rs interface. The key design is that freeform operates on connected components of leftover faces within smooth regions, with small analytic islands (≤16 faces) provisionally dissolved. Components with fewer than 4 faces get converted to per-facet planes, and anything freeform can't handle at any grid density falls back to per-facet as well.
> 
> For the test models like bspline_hill and saddle, the whole region is typically one large smooth area. The ladder classification fails since these aren't plane/sphere/cone/torus, so competition runs and seeds grow small accidental analytic patches. The leftover blob ends up large, which currently triggers the LEFTOVER_BLOB_MAX discard path that converts everything to per-facet planes. The insight is to hand that large leftover blob to freeform instead of discarding it outright. Then I can run a deduce_bspline_surfaces-style pass over the per-facet result to gather components from single-face planar selections and small analytic patches.
> 
> The pragmatic approach is to add a freeform pass after competition that operates directly on the leftover structure, reusing the existing fit_component and build_region machinery. This new front-end would collect leftover components as connected face groups, run island dissolution against committed analytic hypotheses, call fit_component, and commit BSpline results or fall back to per-facet. The question is whether this pass should run post-hoc over the final classification result or integrate earlier in the pipeline. There's a tension with the LEFTOVER_BLOB_MAX threshold: if I discard whole regions per-facet and then re-gather, I risk losing analytic fits in mixed regions (freeform plus real analytic geometry), though the test models appear to be pure freeform anyway, so this might not be a practical concern.
> 
> But there's another wrinkle — running gathering after repair across the whole class would also pick up leftovers from other regions like the coarse-mesh fallback areas, and fitting those into a bspline could either fix a failing model or introduce a new failure, which is risky and needs testing.
> 
> Option 2 is to apply freeform directly where the leftovers are produced, before falling back to per-facet handling. This keeps the approach faithful to the design spec and naturally scopes freeform to just the region that failed the ladder, using that region's own competition results for island dissolution. The tradeoff is more new code and needing to construct the face selection locally, though the design spec suggests planar margins should land in the same smooth region anyway, so cross-region tangent merging shouldn't be an issue.
> 
> Now I'm thinking through whether a planar margin from a freeform patch actually stays within the same smooth region. Since the margin meets the patch tangentially with a smooth edge, it should be in the same region. The competition's plane rung might claim it as a committed analytic plane, and then island dissolution decides whether it rejoins the freeform patch. But island dissolution as currently described only handles small enclosed islands, so I need to check if that covers this case.

21	fn find(parent: &mut [usize], mut x: usize) -> usize {
22	    while parent[x] != x {
23	        parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]; // path halving
24	        x = parent[x];
25	    }
26	    x
27	}

29	/// Extract regions from the edge classification. Returns
30	/// \`(face_region, regions)\` where \`face_region[fi]\` is the region id of
31	/// face \`fi\`.
32	pub fn extract_regions(
33	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
34	    edge_classes: &EdgeClassification,
35	) -> (Vec<usize>, Vec<Region>) {
36	    let n = mesh.faces.len();
37	    let mut parent: Vec<usize> = (0..n).collect();
38	
39	    for fi in 0..n {
40	        let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
41	        for e in 0..vc {
42	            let ni = mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[e];
43	            if ni >= 0 && !edge_classes.is_boundary(fi, e) {
44	                let ra = find(&mut parent, fi);
45	                let rb = find(&mut parent, ni as usize);
46	                if ra != rb {
47	                    // Union by smaller root index keeps numbering stable.
48	                    parent[ra.max(rb)] = ra.min(rb);
49	                }
50	            }
51	        }
52	    }
53	
54	    let mut face_region = vec![usize::MAX; n];
55	    let mut region_of_root = vec![usize::MAX; n];
56	    let mut regions: Vec<Region> = Vec::new();
57	    for (fi, slot) in face_region.iter_mut().enumerate() {
58	        let root = find(&mut parent, fi);
59	        let id = if region_of_root[root] == usize::MAX {
60	            regions.push(Region::default());
61	            region_of_root[root] = regions.len() - 1;
62	            regions.len() - 1
63	        } else {
64	            region_of_root[root]
65	        };
66	        *slot = id;
67	        regions[id].faces.push(fi);
68	    }
69	
70	    for region in &mut regions {
71	        let mut vertices: Vec<usize> = region
72	            .faces
73	            .iter()
74	            .flat_map(|&fi| {
75	                let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
76	                mesh.faces[fi].vertex_indices[..vc].iter().copied()
77	            })
78	            .collect();
79	        vertices.sort_unstable();
80	        vertices.dedup();
81	        region.vertices = vertices;
82	    }
83	
84	    (face_region, regions)

694	fn choose_corners(
695	    lp: &[(usize, usize)],
696	    positions: &[[f64; 3]],
697	) -> Vec<usize> {
698	    let n = lp.len();
699	    // Cumulative chord length at each loop position.
700	    let mut cum = vec![0.0_f64; n + 1];
701	    for i in 0..n {
702	        let a = positions[lp[i].0];
703	        let b = positions[lp[(i + 1) % n].0];
704	        let d = ((a[0] - b[0]).powi(2) + (a[1] - b[1]).powi(2) + (a[2] - b[2]).powi(2)).sqrt();
705	        cum[i + 1] = cum[i] + d;
706	    }
707	    let total = cum[n];

709	    // Outside-surface transitions: vertex i sits between boundary edge i-1
710	    // and edge i; it is a corner candidate when their outside ids differ.
711	    let mut candidates: Vec<usize> = (0..n)

713	        .collect();

716	        return candidates;
717	    }
718	    if candidates.is_empty() {
719	        candidates.push(0);
720	    }

722	    // the quarter arc-length marks (from remaining candidates when there are
723	    // too many, from any loop vertex when there are too few).
724	    let anchor = candidates[0];
725	    let mut chosen = vec![anchor];
726	    let pool: Vec<usize> = if candidates.len() > 4 {
727	        candidates.clone()
728	    } else {
729	        (0..n).collect()
730	    };
731	    for k in 1..4 {
732	        let target = (cum[anchor] + total * k as f64 / 4.0) % total;
733	        let best = pool
734	            .iter()
735	            .copied()
736	            .filter(|i| !chosen.contains(i))
737	            .min_by(|&a, &b| {
738	                let da = arc_dist(cum[a], target, total);
739	                let db = arc_dist(cum[b], target, total);
740	                da.partial_cmp(&db).unwrap()

743	            chosen.push(i);
744	        }
745	    }

382	/// Connected components of a face set over shared mesh edges.
383	fn connected_components(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, faces: &[usize]) -> Vec<Vec<usize>> {
384	    let member: std::collections::HashSet<usize> = faces.iter().copied().collect();
385	    let mut seen: std::collections::HashSet<usize> = std::collections::HashSet::new();
386	    let mut components: Vec<Vec<usize>> = Vec::new();
387	    for &start in faces {
388	        if seen.contains(&start) {
389	            continue;
390	        }
391	        let mut comp = Vec::new();
392	        let mut stack = vec![start];
393	        seen.insert(start);
394	        while let Some(fi) = stack.pop() {
395	            comp.push(fi);
396	            let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
397	            for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
398	                if ni >= 0 {
399	                    let ni = ni as usize;
400	                    if member.contains(&ni) && seen.insert(ni) {
401	                        stack.push(ni);
402	                    }
403	                }
404	            }
405	        }
406	        comp.sort_unstable();
407	        components.push(comp);
408	    }
409	    components
410	}
