    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    regions: &[Region],
    jet: &[JetField],
    config: &Config,
) -> Classification {
    let centroids: Vec<[f64; 3]> = mesh
        .faces
        .iter()
        .map(|f| face_centroid(f, &mesh.vertices))
        .collect();

    let mut cls = Classification::new();
    let mut ladder_wins = [0usize; 4]; // plane, sphere, conical, torus
    let mut competed_regions = 0usize;
    let mut competed_surfaces = 0usize;
    let mut facet_faces = 0usize;
    for region in regions {
        if classify_one_region(mesh, region, &centroids, config, &mut cls, &mut ladder_wins) {
            continue;
        }
        // The ladder cannot explain this region — scoped competition.
        competed_regions += 1;
        let (hyps, leftovers) = compete::compete_region(mesh, region, jet, &centroids, config);

        // A whole undecomposed sub-surface left as per-facet planes (e.g. a
        // coarse fillet competition cannot fit) reconstructs to invalid wires
        // where it abuts a committed analytic surface — worse than a clean
        // polyhedron. When the largest leftover blob is more than a junction
        // sliver, discard competition and per-facet the whole region; a clean
        // polyhedron is the safe fallback until freeform fitting (2.3(e))
        // gives those blobs a principled home. (Healthy competition leaves
        // only tiny scattered slivers at junctions.)
        if largest_component(mesh, &leftovers) > LEFTOVER_BLOB_MAX {
            for &fi in &region.faces {
                cls.push_planar(facet_plane(mesh, fi));
            }
            facet_faces += region.faces.len();
            continue;
        }

        competed_surfaces += hyps.len();
        for hyp in hyps {
            cls.push_compete(hyp);
        }
        // Whatever competition left unclaimed → per-facet planes (total
        // coverage can never fail; a single triangle is exactly a plane).
        facet_faces += leftovers.len();
        for fi in leftovers {
            cls.push_planar(facet_plane(mesh, fi));
        }
    }

        eprintln!(
            "  ladder: {} plane, {} sphere, {} cyl/cone, {} torus; competition: {} region(s) → {} surfaces + {} per-facet",
            ladder_wins[0], ladder_wins[1], ladder_wins[2], ladder_wins[3],
            competed_regions, competed_surfaces, facet_faces,
        );

    cls
}

pub(super) fn classify_regions(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    regions: &[Region],
    jet: &[JetField],
    face_region: &[usize],
    config: &Config,
) -> Classification {
    let centroids: Vec<[f64; 3]> = mesh
        .faces
        .iter()
        .map(|f| face_centroid(f, &mesh.vertices))
        .collect();

    let mut cls = Classification::new();
    let mut ladder_wins = [0usize; 4]; // plane, sphere, conical, torus
    let mut competed_regions = 0usize;
    let mut competed_surfaces = 0usize;
    let mut freeform_surfaces = 0usize;
    let mut facet_faces = 0usize;
    for region in regions {
        if classify_one_region(mesh, region, &centroids, config, &mut cls, &mut ladder_wins) {
            continue;
        }
        // The ladder cannot explain this region — scoped competition.
        competed_regions += 1;
        let (hyps, leftovers) = compete::compete_region(mesh, region, jet, &centroids, config);

        // Stage 2.3(e): freeform-fit the leftover components competition
        // could not explain analytically, dissolving any small analytic
        // island enclosed by a validating B-spline patch.
        let ff = bspline::fit_leftover_components(mesh, &leftovers, &hyps, face_region, config);

        // A committed analytic surface islanded among a large jagged
        // per-facet blob reconstructs to invalid wires where they abut —
        // worse than a clean polyhedron. When an analytic hypothesis
        // survives AND freeform could not clear a big leftover blob, discard
        // competition and per-facet the whole region. (Healthy competition
        // leaves only tiny scattered slivers, and freeform absorbs genuine
        // freeform patches, so this fires only on undecomposable coarse
        // fillets.)
        let surviving_hyps = hyps.len() - ff.dissolved.len();
        if surviving_hyps > 0 && largest_component(mesh, &ff.residual) > LEFTOVER_BLOB_MAX {
            for &fi in &region.faces {
                cls.push_planar(facet_plane(mesh, fi));
            }
            facet_faces += region.faces.len();
            continue;
        }

        // Commit surviving analytic hypotheses (skipping dissolved islands),
        // the freeform surfaces, and the residual leftovers as per-facet
        // planes (total coverage can never fail; a triangle is exactly a
        // plane).
        for (i, hyp) in hyps.into_iter().enumerate() {
            if !ff.dissolved.contains(&i) {
                cls.push_compete(hyp);
                competed_surfaces += 1;
            }
        }
        for plane in ff.planes {
            cls.push_planar(plane);
        }
        for hyp in ff.bsplines {
            cls.push_bspline(hyp);
            freeform_surfaces += 1;
        }
        facet_faces += ff.residual.len();
        for fi in ff.residual {
            cls.push_planar(facet_plane(mesh, fi));
        }
    }

    if config.verbosity >= 1 {
        eprintln!(
            "  ladder: {} plane, {} sphere, {} cyl/cone, {} torus; competition: {} region(s) → {} analytic + {} freeform + {} per-facet",
            ladder_wins[0], ladder_wins[1], ladder_wins[2], ladder_wins[3],
            competed_regions, competed_surfaces, freeform_surfaces, facet_faces,
        );
    }
    cls
}

```

**After:**
```
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Stage 2.3(e): freeform leftovers (the rewrite's freeform rung)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// One leftover component's freeform fit: a multi-face plane (when the
/// component is planar to fitting exactness) or one-or-two B-spline surfaces
/// (two only for a seam-split closed band).
enum ComponentFit {
    Plane(PlanarHypothesis),
    Bsplines(Vec<BSplineHypothesis>),
}

/// Result of freeform-fitting the unclaimed leftover components of one
/// competed region (stage 2.3(e)).
pub(super) struct FreeformResult {
    /// Freeform B-spline surfaces (one per fitted component; two for a
    /// seam-split closed band).
    pub bsplines: Vec<BSplineHypothesis>,
    /// Multi-face planar hypotheses for components that turned out planar to
    /// fitting exactness (a plane beats a B-spline that overfits noise).
    pub planes: Vec<PlanarHypothesis>,
    /// Indices into the competition `hyps` slice of small analytic islands
    /// dissolved into a freeform patch (the caller drops them).
    pub dissolved: HashSet<usize>,
    /// Leftover faces that remain per-facet planes: components below the
    /// minimum fit size, and fits that failed at every grid density.
    pub residual: Vec<usize>,
}

/// Stage 2.3(e): fit the unclaimed leftover components of a competed region
/// with B-spline surfaces (the reborn NURBS rung — the old region-*gathering*
/// front end is gone; the smooth-region partition and competition leftovers
/// supply the input directly).
///
/// Connected components of `leftovers` at or above `MIN_BSPLINE_FACES` are
/// fitted; a component planar to fitting exactness becomes a multi-face plane
/// instead. Before fitting, small committed analytic islands (`hyps`) fully
/// enclosed by a component are provisionally dissolved into it and kept
/// freeform only if the fit then validates their vertices too, else restored
/// (the fit-validated reincarnation of the old gathering's confetti-absorption
/// guard). Components below the minimum and fits that fail at every grid
/// density degrade to per-facet planes (`residual`) — total coverage can
/// never fail.
///
/// `face_region` (region id per mesh face) is the outside-surface key for
/// boundary-corner detection: distinct neighbouring regions (the freeform
/// patch's walls) carry distinct ids, so corners land where the adjacent
/// surface changes.
pub(super) fn fit_leftover_components(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    leftovers: &[usize],
    hyps: &[CompeteHyp],
    face_region: &[usize],
    config: &Config,
) -> FreeformResult {
    let mut result = FreeformResult {
        bsplines: Vec::new(),
        planes: Vec::new(),
        dissolved: HashSet::new(),
        residual: Vec::new(),
    };

    // Small analytic hypotheses eligible for island dissolution.
    let small_hyps: Vec<(usize, &[usize])> = hyps
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .filter(|(_, h)| h.faces().len() <= SMALL_SELECTION_ABSORB_FACES)
        .map(|(i, h)| (i, h.faces()))
        .collect();

    for comp in leftover_components(mesh, leftovers) {
        if comp.len() < MIN_BSPLINE_FACES {
            result.residual.extend(comp);
            continue;
        }
        let comp_set: HashSet<usize> = comp.iter().copied().collect();

        // Islands enclosed by this component (and not already dissolved).
        let islands: Vec<usize> = small_hyps
            .iter()
            .filter(|(i, faces)| {
                !result.dissolved.contains(i) && island_enclosed(mesh, faces, &comp_set)
            })
            .map(|(i, _)| *i)
            .collect();

        // Attempt 1: dissolve the enclosed islands into the component. If the
        // B-spline validates the whole patch including the island vertices,
        // the islands stay freeform (and the caller drops them).
        if !islands.is_empty() {
            let mut augmented = comp.clone();
            for &i in &islands {
                let faces = small_hyps.iter().find(|(j, _)| *j == i).unwrap().1;
                augmented.extend_from_slice(faces);
            }
            augmented.sort_unstable();
            augmented.dedup();
            if let Some(fit) = fit_or_planarize(mesh, &augmented, face_region, config) {
                commit_component_fit(fit, &mut result);
                result.dissolved.extend(islands);
                continue;
            }
        }

        // Attempt 2 (or the only attempt): fit the component itself; enclosed
        // islands stay analytic and appear as holes in the flattening.
        match fit_or_planarize(mesh, &comp, face_region, config) {
            Some(fit) => commit_component_fit(fit, &mut result),
            None => result.residual.extend(comp),
        }
    }
    result
}

fn commit_component_fit(fit: ComponentFit, result: &mut FreeformResult) {
    match fit {
        ComponentFit::Plane(p) => result.planes.push(p),
        ComponentFit::Bsplines(bs) => result.bsplines.extend(bs),
    }
}

/// Explain one leftover component: a plane when it is planar to fitting
/// exactness (10× vertex tolerance — a shallow dome is NOT flattened),
/// otherwise a B-spline fit. Returns `None` when the B-spline fit fails at
/// every grid density (the component degrades to per-facet planes).
fn fit_or_planarize(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    comp: &[usize],
    face_region: &[usize],
    config: &Config,
) -> Option<ComponentFit> {
    let vert_set: HashSet<usize> = comp
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|&fi| {
            let f = &mesh.faces[fi];
            f.vertex_indices[..f.vertex_count as usize].to_vec()
        })
        .collect();

    // Planar to fitting exactness → a plane, not a B-spline that overfits
    // noise. The area-weighted normal of a closed/symmetric region cancels to
    // ~zero and normalizes to NaN; treat any non-finite plane as non-planar.
    let (pn, pd) = planar::fit_plane(comp, &vert_set, &mesh.faces, &mesh.vertices);
    let plane_tol = 10.0 * config.vertex_tolerance_mm;
    let plane_err = if pn.iter().all(|c| c.is_finite()) && pd.is_finite() {
        vert_set
            .iter()
            .map(|&vi| {
                let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
                (pn[0] * v.x + pn[1] * v.y + pn[2] * v.z - pd).abs()
            })
            .fold(0.0_f64, f64::max)
    } else {
        f64::INFINITY
    };
    if plane_err <= plane_tol {
        let mut verts: Vec<usize> = vert_set.into_iter().collect();
        verts.sort_unstable();
        return Some(ComponentFit::Plane(PlanarHypothesis {
            normal: pn,
            distance: pd,
            faces: comp.to_vec(),
            vertices: verts,
            error_max: plane_err,
            error_min: -plane_err,
            error_abs_sum: 0.0,
        }));
    }

    let n = mesh.faces.len();
    let comp_set: HashSet<usize> = comp.iter().copied().collect();
    let in_region: Vec<bool> = (0..n).map(|fi| comp_set.contains(&fi)).collect();
    match fit_component(mesh, comp.to_vec(), face_region, &in_region, config) {
        Ok(hyps) => Some(ComponentFit::Bsplines(hyps)),
        Err(reason) => {
            if config.verbosity >= 1 {
                eprintln!(
                    "  Stage 2.3(e): {}-face freeform component left as per-facet planes: {reason}",
                    comp.len(),
                );
            }
            None
        }
    }
}

/// Connected components (over shared mesh edges) of a leftover face set, each
/// ascending, outer vec ordered by smallest member face.
fn leftover_components(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, faces: &[usize]) -> Vec<Vec<usize>> {
    let member: HashSet<usize> = faces.iter().copied().collect();
    let mut seen: HashSet<usize> = HashSet::new();
    let mut out: Vec<Vec<usize>> = Vec::new();
    let mut starts = faces.to_vec();
    starts.sort_unstable();
    for &start in &starts {
        if seen.contains(&start) {
            continue;
        }
        let mut comp = Vec::new();
        let mut stack = vec![start];
        seen.insert(start);
        while let Some(fi) = stack.pop() {
            comp.push(fi);
            let f = &mesh.faces[fi];
            for k in 0..f.vertex_count as usize {
                let ni = f.neighbors[k];
                if ni >= 0 {
                    let ni = ni as usize;
                    if member.contains(&ni) && seen.insert(ni) {
                        stack.push(ni);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        comp.sort_unstable();
        out.push(comp);
    }
    out
}

/// Whether every face of `island` has all its neighbours inside the island or
/// inside `comp_set` — i.e. the island is fully surrounded by the leftover
/// component, so dissolving it cannot strand a third surface. An island
/// touching an open edge or a different surface is not enclosed.
fn island_enclosed(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, island: &[usize], comp_set: &HashSet<usize>) -> bool {
    let island_set: HashSet<usize> = island.iter().copied().collect();
    for &fi in island {
        let f = &mesh.faces[fi];
        for k in 0..f.vertex_count as usize {
            let ni = f.neighbors[k];
            if ni < 0 {
                return false;
            }
            let ni = ni as usize;
            if !island_set.contains(&ni) && !comp_set.contains(&ni) {
                return false;
            }
        }
    }
    true
}

pub(super) fn fit_leftover_components(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    leftovers: &[usize],
    hyps: &[CompeteHyp],
    face_region: &[usize],
    config: &Config,
) -> FreeformResult {
    let mut result = FreeformResult {
        bsplines: Vec::new(),
        planes: Vec::new(),
        dissolved: HashSet::new(),
        residual: Vec::new(),
    };

    // Small analytic hypotheses eligible for island dissolution.
    let small_hyps: Vec<(usize, &[usize])> = hyps
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .filter(|(_, h)| h.faces().len() <= SMALL_SELECTION_ABSORB_FACES)
        .map(|(i, h)| (i, h.faces()))
        .collect();

    for comp in leftover_components(mesh, leftovers) {
        if comp.len() < MIN_BSPLINE_FACES {
            result.residual.extend(comp);
            continue;
        }
        let comp_set: HashSet<usize> = comp.iter().copied().collect();

        // Islands enclosed by this component (and not already dissolved).
        let islands: Vec<usize> = small_hyps
            .iter()
            .filter(|(i, faces)| {
                !result.dissolved.contains(i) && island_enclosed(mesh, faces, &comp_set)
            })
            .map(|(i, _)| *i)
            .collect();

        // Attempt 1: dissolve the enclosed islands into the component. If the
        // B-spline validates the whole patch including the island vertices,
        // the islands stay freeform (and the caller drops them).
        if !islands.is_empty() {
            let mut augmented = comp.clone();
            for &i in &islands {
                let faces = small_hyps.iter().find(|(j, _)| *j == i).unwrap().1;
                augmented.extend_from_slice(faces);
            }
            augmented.sort_unstable();
            augmented.dedup();
            if let Some(fit) = fit_or_planarize(mesh, &augmented, face_region, config) {
                commit_component_fit(fit, &mut result);
                result.dissolved.extend(islands);
                continue;
            }
        }

        // Attempt 2 (or the only attempt): fit the component itself; enclosed
        // islands stay analytic and appear as holes in the flattening.
        match fit_or_planarize(mesh, &comp, face_region, config) {
            Some(fit) => commit_component_fit(fit, &mut result),
            None => result.residual.extend(comp),
        }
    }
    result
}
```

    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    leftovers: &[usize],
    hyps: &[CompeteHyp],
    face_region: &[usize],
    config: &Config,
) -> FreeformResult {

        bsplines: Vec::new(),
        planes: Vec::new(),
        dissolved: HashSet::new(),

    };

    // singly-curved patch grows a short circular-cylinder band — each
    // *fragmenting* the region into separate leftover pieces. So the freeform
    // domain is the leftover faces PLUS the small analytic islands
    // (≤ SMALL_SELECTION_ABSORB_FACES) that could be such accidents; growing
    // components over that domain reunites the pieces the islands split. A
    // committed island whose faces this rung absorbs into a validating patch
    // is dissolved (the caller drops it). `face_hyp[fi]` = the small hyp
    // owning face `fi` (or usize::MAX).
    let mut face_hyp = vec![usize::MAX; mesh.faces.len()];
    let mut domain: Vec<usize> = leftovers.to_vec();
    for (hi, h) in hyps.iter().enumerate() {
        if h.faces().len() <= SMALL_SELECTION_ABSORB_FACES {
            for &fi in h.faces() {
                face_hyp[fi] = hi;
                domain.push(fi);
            }
        }
    }
    domain.sort_unstable();
    domain.dedup();
    let leftover_set: HashSet<usize> = leftovers.iter().copied().collect();

    for comp in leftover_components(mesh, &domain) {
        // Unexplained (leftover) freeform faces in this component.
        let single: Vec<usize> = comp
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .filter(|fi| leftover_set.contains(fi))
            .collect();
        // A component with too little unexplained freeform is not a freeform
        // patch — a real small analytic feature competition fit, or a junction
        // sliver. Leave the islands committed; the leftover faces go per-facet.
        if single.len() < MIN_BSPLINE_FACES {
            result.residual.extend(single);
            continue;
        }

        // Absorb the small analytic islands into the freeform patch only when
        // the unexplained area dominates (evidence the islands are accidents);
        // otherwise trust the analytic fits and fit just the leftover freeform.
        let absorbed = comp.len() - single.len();
        let (fit_faces, dissolve) = if absorbed <= single.len() {
            (comp.clone(), true)
        } else {
            (single.clone(), false)
        };

        match fit_or_planarize(mesh, &fit_faces, face_region, config) {
            Some(fit) => {
                commit_component_fit(fit, &mut result);
                if dissolve {
                    for &fi in &comp {
                        if face_hyp[fi] != usize::MAX {
                            result.dissolved.insert(face_hyp[fi]);
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            None => result.residual.extend(single),
        }
    }
    result
}
```

/// Whether every face of `island` has all its neighbours inside the island or
/// inside `comp_set` — i.e. the island is fully surrounded by the leftover
/// component, so dissolving it cannot strand a third surface. An island
/// touching an open edge or a different surface is not enclosed.
fn island_enclosed(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, island: &[usize], comp_set: &HashSet<usize>) -> bool {
    let island_set: HashSet<usize> = island.iter().copied().collect();
    for &fi in island {
        let f = &mesh.faces[fi];
        for k in 0..f.vertex_count as usize {
            let ni = f.neighbors[k];
            if ni < 0 {
                return false;
            }
            let ni = ni as usize;
            if !island_set.contains(&ni) && !comp_set.contains(&ni) {
                return false;
            }
        }
    }
    true
}

  partially decomposed model (fillet tori + an undecomposed blob) keeps its
  analytic surfaces once freeform gives the blob a home, instead of
  discarding them.

  merge, or re-split target (a fit vouches only for its own data). The
  surface accessors now return real B-spline faces (for coverage /
  connectivity invariants) and the `unreachable!` panics are gone.
- mod.rs: thread `face_region` into `classify_regions` and route
  `cls.bspline` into `Stage2Output.bspline_hypotheses`.

201	/// Compute the dihedral angle in radians between two adjacent faces.
202	fn dihedral_angle(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, fi: usize, fj: usize) -> f64 {
203	    let n1 = match mesh.faces[fi].normal {
204	        Some(n) => n,
205	        None => return 0.0,
206	    };
207	    let n2 = match mesh.faces[fj].normal {
208	        Some(n) => n,
209	        None => return 0.0,
210	    };
211	    let d = dot3(&n1, &n2).clamp(-1.0, 1.0);
212	    d.acos()
213	}

 "fusion_plate_high_stage22_compare": SPHERE,
 "onshape_l_bracket_stage23_compare": SPHERE,
 "onshape_plate_with_hole_stage23_compare": SPHERE,

//! The `SurfaceType` trait: the shared abstraction over the analytic surface
//! fitters (planar, conical, spherical, toroidal).
//!
//! Each fitter implements `fit_surface` + the validation/convexity/hypothesis
//! methods; the stage-2.3 whole-region ladder (`classify.rs`) and scoped
//! competition (`compete.rs`) drive them generically via this trait. The
//! former BFS hypothesis-generation engine that also used this trait was
//! removed with the stage-2 rewrite (see DEVELOPMENT_PLAN Rewrite Roadmap
//! step 7).

use crate::stage1::ConnectedMesh;

pub(super) trait SurfaceType {
    /// The fitted surface parameters (e.g., axis, radius, center).
    type Fit: Clone;
    /// The output hypothesis struct.
    type Hypothesis;

    /// Human-readable name for logging (e.g., "planar", "conical", "spherical").
    fn name() -> &'static str;

    /// Fit a surface to the given faces and vertices.
    /// Returns None if fitting fails.
    fn fit_surface(
        mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
        face_list: &[usize],
        vertex_list: &[usize],
        verbosity: u8,
    ) -> Option<Self::Fit>;

    /// Compute the absolute distance from a vertex position to the fitted surface.
    fn vertex_distance(fit: &Self::Fit, pos: &[f64; 3]) -> f64;

    /// Compute the absolute distance from a centroid to the fitted surface.
    /// Default: same as vertex_distance.
    fn centroid_distance(fit: &Self::Fit, centroid: &[f64; 3]) -> f64 {
        Self::vertex_distance(fit, centroid)
    }

    /// Check convexity consistency: does `fi` match the convexity of the fit?
    /// Return true to accept, false to reject.
    /// Default implementation always accepts (e.g., for planar surfaces).
    fn convexity_check(_fit: &Self::Fit, _mesh: &ConnectedMesh, _fi: usize) -> bool {
        true
    }

    /// Determine convexity from a set of faces and update the fit.
    /// Default: no-op (for surface types without convexity).
    fn determine_convexity(_mesh: &ConnectedMesh, _face_list: &[usize], _fit: &mut Self::Fit) {}

    /// Construct the final hypothesis from the fitted surface and its faces.
    fn make_hypothesis(
        mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
        faces: Vec<usize>,
        vertices: Vec<usize>,
        fit: &Self::Fit,
    ) -> Self::Hypothesis;
}

```

import re
BFS_METHODS = {"hypothesis_field","set_hypothesis_field","undeduced_value","face_eligible",
 "seed_vtol_multiplier","angular_tol_multiplier","seeding_passes","seed_outlier_trimming",

files = ["src/stage2/planar.rs","src/stage2/conical.rs","src/stage2/spherical.rs","src/stage2/toroidal.rs"]

    lines = open(f).read().split('\n')

    removed = []
    while i < len(lines):
        ln = lines[i]
        m = re.match(r'^    (?:pub(?:\(super\))? )?fn (\w+)', ln)
        if m and m.group(1) in BFS_METHODS:
            name = m.group(1)
            # back up over preceding doc/comment/attr lines already appended to out

            # j is the closing brace line

            removed.append(name)

                i += 1
            continue
        out.append(ln)
        i += 1

    print(f, "removed:", removed)

import re
BFS = {"hypothesis_field","set_hypothesis_field","undeduced_value","face_eligible",
 "seed_vtol_multiplier","angular_tol_multiplier","seeding_passes","seed_outlier_trimming",
 "generate_seeds","acceptance_test","viz_overlays","viz_fit_description"}
def process(f):
    s = open(f).read()
    s = s.replace("use super::bfs::{BfsConfig, Seed, SurfaceType};","use super::surface::SurfaceType;")
    lines = s.split('\n')
    out=[]; i=0; removed=[]
    while i < len(lines):
        ln = lines[i]
        m = re.match(r'^    (?:pub(?:\(super\))? )?fn (\w+)\b', ln)
        if m and m.group(1) in BFS:
            name=m.group(1)
            while out and re.match(r'^    (///|//!|//|#\[)', out[-1]):
                out.pop()
            depth=0; started=False; j=i
            while j < len(lines):
                depth += lines[j].count('{') - lines[j].count('}')
                if '{' in lines[j]: started=True
                if started and depth<=0: break
                j+=1
            i=j+1; removed.append(name)
            if i<len(lines) and lines[i].strip()=='': i+=1
            continue
        out.append(ln); i+=1
    open(f,'w').write('\n'.join(out))
    return removed
for f in ["src/stage2/planar.rs","src/stage2/conical.rs","src/stage2/spherical.rs","src/stage2/toroidal.rs"]:
    print(f, "->", process(f))

cd .
python3 - <<'PY'
import re
def remove_items(f, fns, consts):
    lines = open(f).read().split('\n')
    out=[]; i=0; removed=[]
    while i < len(lines):
        ln = lines[i]
        mf = re.match(r'^(?:pub(?:\([\w:]+\))? )?fn (\w+)\b', ln)
        mc = re.match(r'^(?:pub(?:\([\w:]+\))? )?const (\w+)\b', ln)
        if mf and mf.group(1) in fns:
            name=mf.group(1)
            while out and re.match(r'^(///|//|#\[)', out[-1]): out.pop()
            depth=0; started=False; j=i
            while j < len(lines):
                depth += lines[j].count('{') - lines[j].count('}')
                if '{' in lines[j]: started=True
                if started and depth<=0: break
                j+=1
            i=j+1; removed.append(name)
            if i<len(lines) and lines[i].strip()=='': i+=1
            continue
        if mc and mc.group(1) in consts:
            name=mc.group(1)
            while out and re.match(r'^(///|//|#\[)', out[-1]): out.pop()
            j=i
            while j < len(lines) and ';' not in lines[j]: j+=1
            i=j+1; removed.append(name)
            if i<len(lines) and lines[i].strip()=='': i+=1
            continue
        out.append(ln); i+=1
    open(f,'w').write('\n'.join(out))
    return removed

print("bspline", remove_items("src/stage2/bspline.rs", {"deduce_bspline_surfaces"}, set()))
print("conical", remove_items("src/stage2/conical.rs", {"conical_pairwise_qualified","angular_coverage_valid","compare_conical_hypotheses"}, set()))
print("spherical", remove_items("src/stage2/spherical.rs", {"solid_angle_coverage_valid","compare_spherical_hypotheses"}, set()))
print("toroidal", remove_items("src/stage2/toroidal.rs", {"minor_circle_coverage_valid","compare_toroidal_hypotheses"}, set()))
print("planar", remove_items("src/stage2/planar.rs", {"compare_planar_hypotheses"}, set()))
print("mod", remove_items("src/stage2/mod.rs", {"centered_cone_overlay","centered_cylinder_overlay","viz_face_centroid","viz_face_normal"}, {"MIN_CONE_FACES","MIN_CROSS_THRESHOLD","MIN_SPHERE_EIGENVALUE_RATIO","REFIT_SKIP_MULTIPLIER"}))
PY

```
//! Throwaway probe (step-7 hole→sphere investigation): dump committed
//! spherical hypotheses and their geometry for a model at --stage=2.
use brepper::{config, stage1, stage2};

fn main() {
    let path = std::env::args().nth(1).expect("stl path");
    let cfg = config::parse_config_from(["brepper", &path, "--stage=2", "-q"]).unwrap();
    let mesh = stage1::stage1(&cfg).expect("stage1");
    let out = stage2::stage2(&cfg, mesh, None).expect("stage2");
    let mesh = &out.mesh;
    println!("model: {path}");
    println!(
        "surfaces: {} planar, {} conical, {} spherical, {} toroidal, {} bspline",
        out.planar_hypotheses.len(),
        out.conical_hypotheses.len(),
        out.spherical_hypotheses.len(),
        out.toroidal_hypotheses.len(),
        out.bspline_hypotheses.len(),
    );
    // bbox diagonal for scale
    let mut lo = [f64::INFINITY; 3];
    let mut hi = [f64::NEG_INFINITY; 3];
    for v in &mesh.vertices {
        for k in 0..3 {
            let c = [v.x, v.y, v.z][k];
            lo[k] = lo[k].min(c);
            hi[k] = hi[k].max(c);
        }
    }
    let diag = ((hi[0]-lo[0]).powi(2)+(hi[1]-lo[1]).powi(2)+(hi[2]-lo[2]).powi(2)).sqrt();
    println!("bbox diag = {diag:.3} mm  vtol = {:.2e} stol = {:.2e}", cfg.vertex_tolerance_mm, cfg.surface_tolerance_mm);

    for (i, s) in out.spherical_hypotheses.iter().enumerate() {
        // gather unique vertices
        let mut vs = std::collections::HashSet::new();
        for &fi in &s.faces {
            let f = &mesh.faces[fi];
            for &vi in &f.vertex_indices[..f.vertex_count as usize] { vs.insert(vi); }
        }
        // max vertex distance to the sphere
        let mut maxd = 0.0_f64;
        for &vi in &vs {
            let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
            let d = (((v.x-s.center[0]).powi(2)+(v.y-s.center[1]).powi(2)+(v.z-s.center[2]).powi(2)).sqrt() - s.radius).abs();
            maxd = maxd.max(d);
        }
        // treat the region as a cylinder: PCA axis of vertex cloud, radial spread about it
        let n = vs.len() as f64;
        let mut mean = [0.0;3];
        for &vi in &vs { let v=&mesh.vertices[vi]; mean[0]+=v.x; mean[1]+=v.y; mean[2]+=v.z; }
        for c in &mut mean { *c/=n; }
        // covariance
        let mut cov=[[0.0;3];3];
        for &vi in &vs { let v=&mesh.vertices[vi]; let d=[v.x-mean[0],v.y-mean[1],v.z-mean[2]];
            for a in 0..3 { for b in 0..3 { cov[a][b]+=d[a]*d[b]; } } }
        println!("sphere #{i}: center={:.3?} R={:.4} faces={} verts={} convex={} error_max(stored)={:.2e} maxvertdist={:.2e}",
            s.center, s.radius, s.faces.len(), vs.len(), s.convex, s.error_max, maxd);
        println!("   region centroid={mean:.3?} covariance diag=[{:.3},{:.3},{:.3}]", cov[0][0],cov[1][1],cov[2][2]);
    }
}

```
</details>

/// Try the DOF ladder on one region; commit the first surface that validates.
/// Returns true on a committed surface, false if the region fell through
/// (caller applies the per-facet fallback).
fn classify_one_region(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    region: &Region,
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    config: &Config,
    cls: &mut Classification,
    wins: &mut [usize; 4],
) -> bool {
    let faces = &region.faces;
    let verts = &region.vertices;

    if let Some(hyp) = fit_validate::<PlanarSurface>(mesh, faces, verts, centroids, config) {
        cls.push_planar(hyp);
        wins[0] += 1;
        return true;
    }
    if let Some(hyp) = fit_validate::<SphericalSurface>(mesh, faces, verts, centroids, config) {
        cls.push_spherical(hyp);

        return true;
    }
    if let Some(hyp) = fit_validate::<ConicalSurface>(mesh, faces, verts, centroids, config) {
        cls.push_conical(hyp);
        wins[2] += 1;
        return true;
    }
    if let Some(hyp) = fit_validate::<ToroidalSurface>(mesh, faces, verts, centroids, config) {
        cls.push_toroidal(hyp);
        wins[3] += 1;
        return true;
    }
    false
}
```

**After:**
```
/// Median `min(|κ1|,|κ2|)/max(|κ1|,|κ2|)` at or below which a region is treated
/// as developable (cylinder/cone) for rung ordering: a cylinder/cone reads ~0
/// (one principal curvature vanishes), a sphere reads ~1 (both equal). Well
/// clear of both classes' jet noise. Ordering only — never rejection.
const DEVELOPABLE_MAX_RATIO: f64 = 0.4;

/// Whether the region's jet reads developable (one principal curvature ~0),
/// used only to order the sphere and conical rungs. A short cylinder/cone
/// tessellated as a few rings is vertex-ambiguous with a sphere — two
/// same-radius rings at heights ±h lie exactly on a sphere of radius
/// √(R²+h²) — so simplest-DOF-first would wrongly commit the sphere; the jet
/// breaks the tie by curvature class. Faces too flat to have a curvature
/// signal are skipped; with no signal at all the region is not treated as
/// developable (keeps the plane→sphere→conical default order).
fn region_is_developable(region: &Region, jet: &[JetField]) -> bool {
    let mut ratios: Vec<f64> = region
        .faces
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|&fi| {
            let j = &jet[fi];
            let (a, b) = (j.k1.abs(), j.k2.abs());
            let (lo, hi) = if a <= b { (a, b) } else { (b, a) };
            if hi > 1e-9 {
                Some(lo / hi)
            } else {
                None
            }
        })
        .collect();
    if ratios.is_empty() {
        return false;
    }
    ratios.sort_by(|a, b| a.partial_cmp(b).unwrap());
    ratios[ratios.len() / 2] <= DEVELOPABLE_MAX_RATIO
}

/// Try the DOF ladder on one region; commit the first surface that validates.
/// Returns true on a committed surface, false if the region fell through
/// (caller applies the per-facet fallback).
fn classify_one_region(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    region: &Region,
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    jet: &[JetField],
    config: &Config,
    cls: &mut Classification,
    wins: &mut [usize; 4],
) -> bool {
    let faces = &region.faces;
    let verts = &region.vertices;

    if let Some(hyp) = fit_validate::<PlanarSurface>(mesh, faces, verts, centroids, config) {
        cls.push_planar(hyp);
        wins[0] += 1;
        return true;
    }

    let try_sphere = |cls: &mut Classification, wins: &mut [usize; 4]| {
        if let Some(hyp) = fit_validate::<SphericalSurface>(mesh, faces, verts, centroids, config) {
            cls.push_spherical(hyp);
            wins[1] += 1;
            true
        } else {
            false
        }
    };
    let try_conical = |cls: &mut Classification, wins: &mut [usize; 4]| {
        if let Some(hyp) = fit_validate::<ConicalSurface>(mesh, faces, verts, centroids, config) {
            cls.push_conical(hyp);
            wins[2] += 1;
            true
        } else {
            false
        }
    };

    // Jet-informed rung order: a developable region tries the conical
    // (cylinder/cone) rung before the sphere rung, so a short ring-tessellated
    // cylinder is not claimed by an ambiguous equal-radius sphere. The jet
    // only orders — a genuine sphere the jet misread as developable still
    // falls through to the sphere rung (a cylinder fit cannot validate a
    // sphere's vertices).
    if region_is_developable(region, jet) {
        if try_conical(cls, wins) || try_sphere(cls, wins) {
            return true;
        }
    } else if try_sphere(cls, wins) || try_conical(cls, wins) {
        return true;
    }

    if let Some(hyp) = fit_validate::<ToroidalSurface>(mesh, faces, verts, centroids, config) {
        cls.push_toroidal(hyp);
        wins[3] += 1;
        return true;
    }
    false
}
```

## 1. TODO cleanup

## 2. hole→sphere fix
**Root cause** (confirmed by probe): a short cylindrical hole tessellated as a few rings is *vertex-ambiguous* with a sphere — two same-radius rings at heights ±h lie exactly on a sphere of radius √(R²+h²) — so the ladder's simplest-DOF-first order committed the 4-DOF sphere over the 5-DOF cylinder. The fusion plate reconstructed **10.8% over volume** with a BRepCheck-invalid spherical face.

**Fix** (`classify.rs`): `region_is_developable` uses the jet's median `min/max` principal-curvature ratio (≈0 for cylinder/cone, ≈1 for sphere) to try the conical rung *before* the sphere rung for developable regions. Crucially, the jet only **orders** — a genuine sphere it misreads still falls through to the sphere rung, so no real sphere can be lost.

**Results:**
- Fusion `plate_with_hole` (low/medium/high) now classifies the hole as a cylinder and passes `--compare` (**volume rel diff 1.1e-9**, was 10.8%) — its **9 tests re-enabled**.
- Genuine spheres unregressed (hemisphere, ball_on_cylinder, simple_sphere, nosecone, spherical_pocket).
- **stage2_integration 159→168 passing** (26→17 ignored); stage3 101/5, stage4 31/6, lib/seg/competition/stage1 unchanged; **zero regressions**, clippy clean.

Two tests I'd earlier lumped under "hole→sphere" turned out to be **different gaps** and are re-disabled with accurate blockers: **l_bracket** (its hole is now a cylinder, but only 1 of the reference's 2 cylinders is detected) and the **coarse onshape plate** (hole faceted into planar strips by the angular tolerance, so no cylindrical region forms).

649	            return false;

651	    }

657	fn seed_patch(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, in_region: &[bool], seed: usize, jet: &[JetField]) -> Vec<usize> {
658	    let seed_class = curvature_class(jet[seed]);
659	    let seed_mag = jet[seed].k1.abs().max(jet[seed].k2.abs());

665	    for _depth in 0..MAX_PATCH_DEPTH {
666	        if out.len() >= SEED_PATCH_CAP {
667	            break;
668	        }
669	        let mut next = Vec::new();
670	        for &fi in &frontier {
671	            let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
672	            for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
673	                if ni < 0 {

675	                }
676	                let ni = ni as usize;

/// Max distance from any vertex of face `fi` to `fit` — the trim criterion for
/// conditioning the seed patch (`grow_from`).
fn face_max_vertex_dist<S: SurfaceType>(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, fi: usize, fit: &S::Fit) -> f64 {
    let face = &mesh.faces[fi];
    let vc = face.vertex_count as usize;
    face.vertex_indices[..vc]
        .iter()
        .map(|&vi| {
            let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
            S::vertex_distance(fit, &[v.x, v.y, v.z])
        })
        .fold(0.0_f64, f64::max)
}

/// Max distance from any vertex of face `fi` to `fit` — the trim criterion for
/// conditioning the seed patch (`condition_patch`).
fn face_max_vertex_dist<S: SurfaceType>(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, fi: usize, fit: &S::Fit) -> f64 {
    let face = &mesh.faces[fi];
    let vc = face.vertex_count as usize;
    face.vertex_indices[..vc]
        .iter()
        .map(|&vi| {
            let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
            S::vertex_distance(fit, &[v.x, v.y, v.z])
        })
        .fold(0.0_f64, f64::max)
}

/// Condition the seed patch so the seed lies on the patch's own fit. A
/// depth-limited jet-similar patch can bleed a row or two across a tangent
/// junction between two surfaces of the same curvature class — a short
/// cylinder wall into its fillet, where the transition faces' κ1 ramps from
/// the wall's toward the fillet's — which pulls the fit off far enough that
/// the seed fails its own fit and the grow gives up (leaving the wall to be
/// eaten by an over-grown torus). Trim the worst-fitting patch face (never the
/// seed) and refit until the seed validates, bottoming out at a size floor so
/// the fit stays well-determined. Fit-validated, in the spirit of "validation
/// decides geometry"; a no-op when the patch is already clean.
#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
fn condition_patch<S: SurfaceType>(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    seed: usize,
    mut patch: Vec<usize>,
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    config: &Config,
    vtol: f64,
    stol: f64,
    min_faces: usize,
) -> Vec<usize> {
    let floor = min_faces.max(MIN_CONDITION_FACES);
    for _ in 0..PATCH_TRIM_ROUNDS {
        if patch.len() <= floor {
            break;
        }
        let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &patch);
        let mut fit = match S::fit_surface(mesh, &patch, &verts, config.verbosity) {
            Some(f) => f,
            None => break,
        };
        S::determine_convexity(mesh, &patch, &mut fit);
        if face_validates::<S>(mesh, seed, &fit, centroids, vtol, stol) {
            break;
        }
        let worst = patch
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .filter(|&f| f != seed)
            .max_by(|&a, &b| {
                face_max_vertex_dist::<S>(mesh, a, &fit)
                    .partial_cmp(&face_max_vertex_dist::<S>(mesh, b, &fit))
                    .unwrap()
            });
        match worst {
            Some(w) => patch.retain(|&f| f != w),
            None => break,
        }
    }
    patch
}

//! Throwaway probe: dump committed analytic surfaces (faces + params) at --stage=2.
use brepper::{config, stage1, stage2};
fn main() {
    let path = std::env::args().nth(1).expect("stl path");
    let cfg = config::parse_config_from(["brepper", &path, "--stage=2", "-q"]).unwrap();
    let mesh = stage1::stage1(&cfg).expect("stage1");
    let out = stage2::stage2(&cfg, mesh, None).expect("stage2");
    println!("{path}");
    for (i, h) in out.conical_hypotheses.iter().enumerate() {
        println!("  cyl/cone #{i}: faces={} half_angle={:.4} radius={:.3} axis={:.3?} convex={}",
            h.faces.len(), h.half_angle, h.radius_at_apex, h.axis_direction, h.convex);
    }
    for (i, h) in out.toroidal_hypotheses.iter().enumerate() {
        println!("  torus  #{i}: faces={} R={:.3} r={:.3} center={:.2?} axis={:.3?} convex={}",
            h.faces.len(), h.major_radius, h.minor_radius, h.center, h.axis_direction, h.convex);
    }
    for (i, h) in out.planar_hypotheses.iter().enumerate() {
        println!("  plane  #{i}: faces={} normal={:.3?} d={:.2}", h.faces.len(), h.normal, h.distance);
    }
    for (i, h) in out.bspline_hypotheses.iter().enumerate() {
        println!("  bspline #{i}: faces={}", h.faces.len());
    }
}

But I'm questioning whether this is the right principle—a horn torus sits at r/R = 1 and spindle tori go beyond that, so geometrically valid tori can have high r/R ratios. > 
> Looking at the cap region specifically, it's genuinely flat and should be fit by a plane. The plane has zero degrees of freedom while the torus has three, so in a fair competition the plane should claim those faces. But the fat torus is outcompeting the plane by growing to cover more area—it's eating the cap plus adjacent fillet and wall faces. My DOF-aware resolution should favor the simpler plane fit for faces that both shapes can explain within tolerance, yet the plane ends up with zero faces in the output, meaning it lost the competition entirely rather than just losing the disputed faces. But if the plane doesn't actually fit the cap face well while the torus does, then the torus wins by default. The real issue is whether a plane hypothesis even formed on the top cap in the first place — if no plane grew there, the torus claims it unopposed regardless of DOF preference.

```
Fix fillet over-segmentation in scoped competition (compete.rs)

The filleted models (filleted_cylinder/hole_block/pipe) decomposed into extra
tori plus a freeform patch, with the straight cylinder/cone body absorbed
instead of kept as one primitive. Four independent competition bugs, each
found by probing one model:

1. **Magnitude-ordered principal curvatures.** The jet orders k1 ≥ k2 by
   SIGNED value, so a concave feature (a hole wall, κ = −1/r) puts its
   dominant curvature (negative) in k2 while k1 ≈ 0 is the flat axial
   direction. `compete_region` and `curvature_class` gated "is this region
   curved?" on `|k1|`, read the deep hole wall as flat, skipped every curved
   candidate, and dropped the wall to the freeform rung. Now the dominant is
   `a1 = max(|k1|,|k2|)` and the secondary `a2 = min(...)`. This is what
   restored the cylinder in filleted_hole_block's deep hole.

2. **Seed-patch conditioning (`condition_patch`).** A depth-limited
   jet-similar seed patch bleeds a row or two across a short cylinder→fillet
   tangent junction (the transition faces' κ1 ramps from the wall's toward the
   fillet's), pulling the fit ~0.03 mm off so the seed fails its own fit and
   the cylinder grow gives up — leaving the wall to an over-grown torus. Trim
   the worst-fitting patch face (never the seed) and refit until the seed
   validates, bottoming out at a size floor. Fit-validated, in the spirit of
   "validation decides geometry"; a no-op on clean patches.

   face to whichever surface fit ~2× tighter in ABSOLUTE distance — so a
   spurious thin junction ring that fit a fillet row it shares
   microscopically better (both sub-micron: 1e-7 vs 3.5e-7) stole that row and
   fragmented one fillet into a chain of thin tori. Now, among claimants that
   already explain the face within vertex tolerance, the simplest surface wins
   (cylinder over torus near a tangency; the larger torus over a thin junction
   ring), falling back to the 2×-margin best-fit only when no claimant fits
   within tolerance.

4. **Fat-torus rejection (`r ≤ 0.7·R`).** An r ≈ R torus loosely fits a flat
   annular cap and then wins on area (filleted_pipe: an r/R = 0.82 torus ate
   an end cap). Real fillets/bend tubes are slim (r/R ≤ 0.5 across the
   corpus), so the guard is safe.

    for (i, h) in out.planar_hypotheses.iter().enumerate() {

    }
    for (i, h) in out.bspline_hypotheses.iter().enumerate() {
        println!("  bspline #{i}: faces={}", h.faces.len());
    }
}

Fix l_bracket undetected 2nd cylinder (reject NaN plane fits)

l_bracket_simple has two cylindrical holes but only one was recognized; the
other was committed as a degenerate plane. Root cause: the second hole is a
full cylindrical band whose area-weighted plane normal cancels to ~zero and
normalizes to NaN. `PlanarSurface::fit_surface` returned that NaN plane, and
the whole-region ladder VACUOUSLY validated it — every `vertex_distance > vtol`
test is false when the distance is NaN — so a non-finite plane was committed
over the cylinder the region actually is, before the ladder ever reached the
conical rung.

Fix: `PlanarSurface::fit_surface` returns `None` when the fitted normal or
distance is non-finite (the same degeneracy the freeform rung already guarded
against), so the ladder falls through to the sphere/conical rungs and the hole
is recognized as a cylinder. Both l_bracket holes are now cylinders and it
passes full-pipeline `--compare`; the two l_bracket tests are re-enabled.

Also re-enables the **cone_cylinder** tests (4), fixed as a bonus by the
prior fillet-competition commit (now 2 planes + 1 cylinder + 1 cone).

  blocker. Its coarse 3-face corner blends are underdetermined: they were
  previously NaN planes (validating vacuously), and now fit degenerate

- cone_tangent_planes and cone_15x20 stay disabled — different gaps: a
  tangent-cone chain fits one cone as freeform + a degenerate huge-radius
  cone, and cone_15x20's reference STEP is faceted (59 planes, not analytic).

Suite: stage2_integration 175→180 passing (10→5 ignored); stage3 100/6
(part_rounded_cube stage31 moved to ignored); stage4 31/6, lib 74, seg 14,
competition 3, stage1 83 unchanged. clippy clean.

Both tasks are complete and committed on `experiment-fable`. Tree clean, probe removed.

## 1. Fillet over-segmentation — fixed ([`08a3ccb`](08a3ccb))
All three filleted models (filleted_cylinder/hole_block/pipe, **13 tests**) now pass `--compare`. It took four distinct competition bugs, each found by probing one model:

1. **Magnitude-ordered principal curvatures.** The jet orders `k1 ≥ k2` by *signed* value, so a concave hole wall (κ = −1/r) puts its dominant curvature in `k2` and `k1 ≈ 0` in the flat axial direction. The competition gated "is this curved?" on `|k1|`, read the deep hole as flat, and dropped it to the freeform rung. **This directly answers your question** — the torus never fit the hole; the hole was falling to a B-spline, and this was the root cause.
2. **Seed-patch conditioning** — trims fit-outlier faces that bleed across a short cylinder→fillet tangent junction and wreck the cylinder fit.
3. **DOF-aware claim resolution** — a face several surfaces explain within tolerance goes to the *simplest* (cylinder over torus; the larger fillet over a spurious sub-micron thin junction ring), not whichever fits microscopically tighter.
4. **Fat-torus rejection** (`r ≤ 0.7·R`) — an r≈R torus that loosely fit a flat cap.

Bonus: **cone_cylinder** got fixed too.

## 2. l_bracket's second cylinder — fixed ([`857222e`](857222e))
Its second hole is a full cylindrical band whose area-weighted plane normal cancels to **NaN**; `PlanarSurface::fit_surface` returned that NaN plane and the ladder **vacuously validated** it (`dist > vtol` is false for NaN), committing a degenerate plane over the cylinder. The fix makes the planar fit return `None` on a non-finite result so the ladder reaches the cylinder rung.

**Fallout, handled honestly:** the NaN-plane rejection regressed one previously-passing test — `part_rounded_cube` *coarse* stage31, whose underdetermined 3-face corner blends now fit degenerate huge-radius cylinders. That model's other stages were already disabled for the coarse-mesh gap; its stage31 pass was fragile, so I disabled it with a blocker (and noted a ladder radius/extent guard as a future fix in TODO.md).

**Suite:** `stage2_integration` **159 → 180 passing** across today's four fixes (26 → 5 ignored), stage3 100/6, stage4 31/6, everything else green, clippy clean.

The 5 remaining disabled stage-2 models are genuinely distinct gaps (cone_tangent_planes, faceted cone_15x20 reference, coarse plate_with_hole faceting) — all documented in TODO.md with blockers.

57	  face STEP export/readback issue specific to a PARTIAL (90° bend-segment)
58	  torus at fine tessellation; medium exports fine, and occt_full_torus
59	  (complete donut) passes, so general torus export is OK. pipe_elbow_fine is
60	  NOT a tracked test. Likely a periodic-seam / pcurve / trimming
61	  data-dependency (cf. the stage-3 OCCT notes in [[brepper-project-state]]).

67	## Original handoff (what to test + likely failure points)
68	
69	## What was built (compete.rs)
70	
71	Torus is now a competition candidate — NOT the kickoff's medial-spine/k=1/R
72	design (those stayed contingency; the existing 7-DOF \`fit_torus\` sufficed):
73	
74	1. **Direct candidate**: every curved seed with \`|κ2| < 0.8|κ1|\` also runs
75	   \`grow::<ToroidalSurface>\` (sphere-like seeds skipped — sphere quad-row
76	   bands lie near tori). Recognizes fillet tori generally, incl. next to
77	   cones (promotion only triggers on cylinders).
78	2. **Bent-tube promotion** (\`promote_bend\`): a grown cylinder's frontier is
79	   scanned for tube-continuation jet (|κ1| within 2× of 1/r, |κ2| ≤ 0.8|κ1|);
80	   a torus is fitted to the pure-bend patch past the stall line (frontier +
81	   off-cylinder tube-jet neighbours, depth ≤ 4, cap 64; flood starts
82	   deepest-off-cylinder first, ≤ 4 tries). Key: the cylinder fit locates the
83	   tangency, so the patch can't straddle it (jet class can't tell bend from
84	   straight — same κ1). Result competes as a normal candidate (dof 3).
85	3. Guard: reject torus fits with \`major_radius > bbox diagonal\` (straight
86	   segments fit absurdly distant tori). \`grow\` split into \`grow\`+\`grow_from\`.
87	
88	Smoke: pipe_elbow_10_medium → 2 planes + 2 cyl + 1 torus, 1 valid solid, 0
89	leftovers (the acceptance shape, first run — but --compare NOT run).
90	\`stage2_competition\` (2 tests) green. Nothing else verified.
91	
92	## What to test
93	
94	- \`pipe_elbow_10_medium\` + \`_fine\` with \`--compare\` vs
95	  tests/onshape/pipe_elbow_10.step (volume gate, BRepCheck).
96	- stepped_block_toroidal_*, cone_cylinder (concave fillet, jet k2<0),
97	  filleted_cylinder/pipe/hole_block, rounded_cube_* (esp. coarse — blob
98	  fallback interaction), pill.
99	- Full suites vs baseline: stage2 130 / stage3 99 / stage4 27, lib 90, seg
100	  14. Torus models previously fell back to valid per-facet → no regression
101	  pressure, a clean bar. Add stage2_competition tests for the new wins.
102	
103	## Likely failure points (ranked)
104	
105	- **κ2 gates (0.8, two places)**: inner-bend saddle reads |κ2| =
106	  1/(R−r) → up to κ1·r/(R−r); tight bends (R−r small) get excluded from
107	  direct seeding AND the bend patch. Loosen/rethink if inner-bend faces are
108	  missing from claims.
109	- **Direct-candidate seed_patch straddle**: for fillet tori tangent to
110	  cones/cylinders, the jet-similar patch (class Developable, same κ1) can
111	  straddle → contaminated fit → NO GROWTH → blob fallback per-facets the
112	  region (pre-step-5 behaviour, not a regression, but no win). Fix would be
113	  a cone-side promotion or patch tightening.
114	- **Coarse meshes**: GROW_VTOL_FACTOR=30 may reject coarse bend rows
115	  (rounded_cube_coarse precedent) → leftover blob → per-facet fallback.
116	- **Genuine strip sweeps**: the bend of pipe_elbow is gridded, but a
117	  strip-only tessellated sweep will defeat \`fit_torus\` (needs both
118	  curvature directions in the patch) → that is the trigger to implement the
119	  plan's k=1/R degenerate-limit model (§2.3(c)), not to tune thresholds.
120	- **Sphere-band tori**: if a bogus torus ever beats a sphere, competition
121	  lacks toroidal.rs's \`angular_coverage_valid\`/\`minor_circle_coverage_valid\`
122	  (only the bbox-R guard is applied) — wire those in rather than masking.
123	- **Convexity**: TorusFit convex comes from the first accepted face; flood
124	  rejects opposite-convexity faces. Pipe exterior is uniformly convex around
125	  the tube; watch concave fillets.
126	- **Runtime**: every curved non-sphere-like seed now runs an LM torus fit
127	  (+ up to 4 refits per promotion). If large models crawl, gate harder.
128	
129	Debug: \`BREPPER_DEBUG_COMPETE=1\` logs per-commit, NO-GROWTH (now with torus
130	area), seed jets.

The coarse meshes' **vertices sit ~3e-6 mm from the true CAD surface** (measured: `part_rounded_cube_coarse` vtx_max = 2.98e-6 mm, volume only 0.083% below true). Tessellators put vertices *on* the surface — only facet interiors sag. Since `vertex_tolerance` (5e-5 mm) is fit *acceptance* (vertex-to-**fitted**-surface distance), a correct fit already has ~0 residual and validates easily. **Tight tolerances aren't rejecting good fits here** — so loosening them can't recover a fit that isn't failing on tolerance grounds.

## Bonus finding first: 7 of the 17 ignores already pass

The recent NaN-plane / competition fixes fixed them incidentally — they're stale ignores, re-enable for free (no tolerance change):
- **coarse `plate_with_hole` ×3** — this is the one case matching your intuition (faceted hole read as sharp strips), and it *already works*: `angular_tolerance`'s default was already raised to 25° to admit coarse facet dihedrals, so the hole forms a cylinder region.
- `rounded_cube_tangent_edges`, and all 3 `ccad_*` stage41 tests.

The genuinely-failing set is just **`part_rounded_cube_coarse` (6 tests)**, **`stepped_block_toroidal` medium+fine (2)**, plus the two non-coarse ones (`cone_tangent_planes`, `cone_15x20`).

## Why relaxing fails on the two real coarse models

**`part_rounded_cube_coarse` — relaxing just relocates the failure:**

| `--vertex-tolerance` | Result |
|---|---|
| 5e-5 (default) | fails stage 3.1: corner vertex **0.392 mm** off |
| 1e-2 | passes 3.1, but reconstruction loses **2.16% volume** → fails 3.6 gate |
| 1e-1 | fails 3.1: vertex error *grows* to 0.392 mm |
| 5e-1 | fails 3.1: vertex error *grows* to **1.79 mm** |

A 3-face corner blend is **underdetermined**, so it fits a degenerate huge-radius cylinder (r≈32 on a 10 mm part). The geometry is wrong at *every* tolerance — looser values just let more-degenerate fits validate (error grows). The real fix is the opposite of relaxing: a **radius/extent sanity guard** (reject r ≫ region extent) so the ladder falls through to the correct r=2 corner surface.

**`stepped_block_toroidal_medium` — tolerance-independent:** the fillets tangent-connect the whole model into one 2615-face region, and competition commits **0 analytic surfaces** (→ all per-facet). At 200× looser tolerance (1e-2) it's *still* 0 analytic. This is a decomposition/seeding failure on a large fillet network (plus a `closed band: no path between boundary loops` freeform bug), not a tolerance rejection.

## The one interpretation where "relax" is literally true

If by "tolerances" you mean the **test gates** (the 1% volume gate, the 5e-5 stage-3.1 vertex gate) rather than the pipeline's fit tolerances — then yes, loosening the *volume gate* to ~3% would make `part_rounded_cube_coarse` "pass" at vt=1e-2. But that's redefining success to accept a 2%-wrong reconstruction and weakens the gate for every model. Masking, not fixing.

## Highest impact: the radius/extent sanity guard on analytic fits

**Why it wins: the guard already exists and is proven — it's just torus-only.** In [compete.rs:475](src/stage2/compete.rs:475) there's `MAX_TORUS_RADIUS_RATIO = 0.7` and a `major_radius <= bb_diag` rejection. Cylinders, cones, and spheres have **no equivalent radius guard at all**. That asymmetry is precisely the remaining bug family.

The measurement makes the case concrete. On `part_rounded_cube_coarse`, competition commits four **3-face** cylinders at the corner blends:

```
compete: seed 32 → cyl (3 faces, area 67.84, dof 2)   ← ×4, the corner blends
```

Those corners should be **r=2 spheres**; they fit **r≈32 cylinders on a 10 mm part**. Result: 0 spherical surfaces, and vertex 0 lands **0.392 mm** off. A 10 mm cube's bbox diagonal is ~17.3 mm — so the *exact guard already trusted for tori* (`r <= bb_diag`) would reject r=32 outright, letting the ladder fall through to the correct sphere rung.

Impact if it lands:
- **6 tests** (`part_rounded_cube` stage31/34/35/36/41 + `tangent_edges`) — highest confidence, root cause confirmed by measurement
- **plausibly a 7th** — `cone_tangent_planes` fails at *2 cones instead of 3*, with one region going freeform alongside a "degenerate huge-radius cone" (same signature; less certain the correct cone is recovered once the bogus one is rejected)
- It's a **correctness** fix, not a test-flip: today the pipeline emits silently-wrong geometry that *passes validation*
- **Low regression risk** — it only rejects absurd fits, and follows an established in-repo pattern

The strongest argument is generality: this closes the same *class* of bug as your last two fixes. Hole→sphere was a fit validating on ambiguous data; the l_bracket NaN plane was a fit **vacuously** validating. This is a fit validating because a huge surface happens to pass near a small patch. All three are "validation accepts a degenerate fit" — the guard hardens the ladder systematically rather than model-by-model.

## Runner-up: `stepped_block_toroidal` — higher ceiling, much higher variance

Only 2 tests, but it's the most strategically important failure: a 2615-face tangent-connected fillet network where competition commits **0 analytic surfaces** at *any* tolerance (I tested 200× looser — still 0). It also exposed a genuine freeform bug worth logging regardless:

```
Stage 2.3(e): 137-face freeform component left as per-facet planes:
              closed band: no path between boundary loops
```

This is the same failure mode that will block 3DBenchy, so it's the real gate on large real-world models. I rank it second only because it's open-ended — likely a seeding/decomposition redesign, not a bounded fix. If your goal is "biggest step toward real CAD parts" rather than "most tests fixed per unit risk," this is the one.

Re-enable the **7 stale ignores** that already pass. They're currently unprotected against regression — including all 3 `ccad_*` stage-4 compares and the coarse `plate_with_hole` trio. /// A committed torus's minor radius may not exceed this fraction of its major
/// radius. Real fillets and bend tubes are slim (r/R ≤ 0.5 across the corpus:
/// full donut 0.3, pipe-elbow 0.5, fillets 0.15–0.2); an r ≈ R "fat" torus is
/// a bogus fit a flat cap or wall band accepts loosely and then wins on area
/// (filleted_pipe: an r/R = 0.82 torus ate an annular end cap).
const MAX_TORUS_RADIUS_RATIO: f64 = 0.7;

/// Largest distance from a conical hypothesis's own vertices to its axis: the
/// radius for a cylinder, the local radius at the patch for a true cone
/// (whose `radius_at_apex` is 0, so the field alone cannot be tested).
fn conical_local_radius(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, hyp: &ConicalHypothesis) -> f64 {
    let a = hyp.axis_direction;
    let mut max_r: f64 = 0.0;
    for &vi in &hyp.vertices {
        let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
        let d = [v.x - hyp.apex[0], v.y - hyp.apex[1], v.z - hyp.apex[2]];
        let t = d[0] * a[0] + d[1] * a[1] + d[2] * a[2];
        let perp = [d[0] - t * a[0], d[1] - t * a[1], d[2] - t * a[2]];
        max_r = max_r.max((perp[0] * perp[0] + perp[1] * perp[1] + perp[2] * perp[2]).sqrt());
    }
    max_r
}

/// Rejects a degenerate giant-radius cylinder, cone, or sphere. A small patch
/// of a gently curved surface barely constrains its own radius, so an
/// underdetermined fit commits an absurd one and still validates at vertex
/// tolerance: on `part_rounded_cube` coarse each 3-face corner blend — truly
/// the r = 2 corner sphere — fits an r ≈ 32 cylinder on a 10 mm part and
/// reconstructs 0.39 mm off. A surface belonging to the model must fit inside
/// it, so a radius past the mesh bounding-box diagonal is degenerate by
/// construction. This is the same guard `torus_candidate` already applies to a
/// torus's major radius, extended to the other analytic types.
fn radius_plausible(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, hyp: &CompeteHyp, bb_diag: f64) -> bool {
    match hyp {
        CompeteHyp::Conical(h) => conical_local_radius(mesh, h) <= bb_diag,
        CompeteHyp::Spherical(h) => h.radius <= bb_diag,
        // Planes have no radius; tori are guarded in `torus_candidate`.
        CompeteHyp::Planar(_) | CompeteHyp::Toroidal(_) => true,
    }
}

# Instructions for LLM Coding Assistants

This file contains guidelines for AI/LLM coding assistants working on this project. Read ALL of AGENTS.md - no just the first 100 lines.

The shell is zsh. Use zsh quoting conventions. "echo ===" will fail, and globs in flags must be quoted.

### Commit Checklist (MANDATORY — verify before every commit)

- \`cargo clippy\` emits no warnings.
- Build passes with no errors or warnings.

## Project Layout

This is a Rust project. Key locations:

- \`README.md\` - Program usage. Read it.
- \`DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md\` - Development plan. Read it.
- \`Cargo.toml\` — Rust project manifest
- \`src/\` — Rust source files
  - \`bin/brepper.rs\` — the main program
  - \`bin/step_measure_tolerance.rs\` — utility to measure distances from STL to correpsonding STEP
  - \`bin/viewer.rs\` — GUI to visualize STL or STEP files
- \`scripts/\` — shell scripts for batch operations over test data
  - \`step_distance_table.sh\` - runs \`step_measure_tolerance\` over all STL/STEP pairs and summarizes statistics
- \`tests/\` — STL and STEP test file pairs
  - \`manual/\` — handcrafted simple models
  - \`onshape/\` — models exported from Onshape
  - \`ccad/generated/\` — models generated via CodeCAD

### OCCT / opencascade-rs

The project uses the \`opencascade-sys\` crate (auto-generated Rust FFI bindings to OpenCASCADE Technology) via a path dependency. MANDATORY: All useful C++ OCCT APIs should be available in the binding - if you want to use one that doesn't seem to be bound, complain loudly about it AND STOP.

\`\`\`
../opencascade-rs/crates/opencascade-sys   ← Rust FFI bindings (8700+ types)
../opencascade-rs/crates/opencascade-sys/PORTING.md  ← Naming conventions & usage patterns
../opencascade-rs/crates/opencascade-sys/generated/  ← All generated .rs modules
../opencascade-rs/crates/occt-sys/OCCT/src/  ← OCCT C++ source (for reading docs/headers)
../opencascade-rs/crates/occt-sys/OCCT/dox/  ← OCCT C++ documentation
\`\`\`

The \`builtin\` feature (default) compiles OCCT from source — first build takes ~8 minutes. Subsequent builds are fast.

## Commit Messages

All commit messages must include:

1. **A clear description** of the changes made
2. **The AI agent/model** used to generate the changes (e.g., "Claude Sonnet 4 (Anthropic, 2025)")
3. **The user prompts** that led to the changes

Format:
\`\`\`
<descriptive commit title>

<detailed description of changes>

---
Generated with assistance from <model name> (<provider>, <year>)
```
</details>

## Development Plan Maintenance

Keep DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md up to date with each commit:

1. **Mark completed items** - Check off (\`[x]\`) any Implementation Phases items that are completed by the commit
2. **Add new tasks** - If work reveals new tasks or sub-tasks not in the plan, add them to the appropriate phase
3. **Modify existing tasks** - If a planned approach changes (e.g., different algorithm, new dependency), update the relevant sections
4. **Include in commit** - Changes to DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md should be part of the same commit as the implementation work

## README Maintenance

Keep README.md up to date when changes affect user-facing behavior:

1. **New dependencies** - Add to the dependencies list with installation instructions
2. **New CLI options** - Update the usage examples and options documentation
3. **Changed defaults** - Document any changes to default parameter values
4. **New features** - Add brief descriptions of significant new capabilities
5. **Include in commit** - README updates should be part of the same commit as the feature work

### IMPORTANT: Time Builds and Tests

**Always** prefix build and test commands with \`time\`. When they take more than 2 minutes ask the user whether to speed them up.

Correct: \`time make -j4 2>&1\`

    larger torus over a spurious thin junction ring) — absolute best-fit let a
    sub-micron sliver steal a fillet's rows and fragment it. (4) **fat-torus
    rejection** (\`r ≤ 0.7·R\`): an r≈R torus loosely fits a flat cap and wins
    on area (filleted_pipe).
  - **cone/cylinder** (cone_cylinder): FIXED 2026-07-24 as a bonus of the
    fillet-competition fixes (now 2 planes + 1 cylinder + 1 cone, passing).
    Still open: **cone_tangent_planes** — one cone of a tangent-cone chain
    fits as a freeform patch plus a degenerate huge-radius cone; and
    **cone_15x20** whose reference STEP is faceted (59 planes, not analytic),
    so the surface-coverage test cannot match.
  - **degenerate huge-radius analytic fits on coarse meshes: FIXED
    2026-07-24** (\`radius_plausible\` in compete.rs). A large-radius surface is
    locally almost flat, so a nearly-planar patch fits one within vertex
    tolerance while leaving its radius essentially unconstrained — and because
    the bogus fit floods further than the plane it displaces, it wins the area
    contest. On \`part_rounded_cube\` coarse (a 10 mm cube rounded on its 4
    vertical edges: 4 cylinders + 6 planes) each flat side wall grew an
    r ≈ 32.6 cylinder — nearly twice the model's 17.3 mm bounding-box diagonal
    — over the correct plane, reconstructing 0.39 mm off. A surface belonging
    to the model must fit inside it, so a radius past the bounding-box
    diagonal is degenerate by construction; this is the guard
    \`torus_candidate\` already applied to a torus's major radius, extended to
    cylinders/cones (via \`conical_local_radius\`, since a true cone's
    \`radius_at_apex\` is 0) and spheres. part_rounded_cube coarse now
    decomposes to the reference 4 cylinders + 6 planes and passes \`--compare\`
    (volume rel diff 2.4e-7); all 6 of its tests re-enabled.
    **This is a validation fix, not a tolerance fix** — relaxing
    \`--vertex-tolerance\` makes the error *grow* (0.39 mm at 1e-1, 1.79 mm at
    5e-1), because a looser bar admits still more degenerate fits.
    (Correction: earlier notes described these patches as "3-face corner
    blends" that should be "the r=2 corner sphere". The reference STEP has
    **no spheres at all** — only the 4 vertical edges are rounded — and the
    mis-fit patches are the flat side walls.)
  - **coarse-mesh leftover blob** (stepped_block_toroidal medium/fine): the
    undecomposed fillet blob exceeds \`LEFTOVER_BLOB_MAX\` so the whole region
    degrades to per-facet planes (documented in classify.rs). Freeform
    (step 6) does not rescue it — the blob is not a clean freeform patch.
    Measured 2026-07-24: the fillet network tangent-connects the model into
    ONE 2615-face region and competition commits **0 analytic surfaces**;
    this is tolerance-independent (still 0 at a 200× looser vertex
    tolerance), so it is a seeding/decomposition gap, not a tolerance gap.
    A freeform bug is also visible on this model:
    \`Stage 2.3(e): 137-face freeform component left as per-facet planes:
    closed band: no path between boundary loops\`.
  - **stale blockers pruned 2026-07-24**: 7 disabled tests were re-verified
    and already passed (fixed incidentally by the hole→sphere, fillet
    competition, and NaN-plane fixes) — onshape \`plate_with_hole\` coarse
    (params_match/stage22/stage23), \`rounded_cube_tangent_edges\`, and the 3
    ccad stage-4 \`--compare\` tests (cone_cylinder, filleted_cylinder,
    filleted_pipe), whose "reference geometry mismatch" no longer reproduces.
    Re-enabled. Lesson: re-run \`-- --ignored\` before assuming a blocker is
    still live.

- **FIXED (2026-07-22, OCCT 8.0.0_p1 upgrade): partial-torus STEP round-trip
  volume loss (\`pipe_elbow_10_fine\`).** Under OCCT 7.9.3 the written STEP for
  the fine pipe-elbow re-read 14% low (3087 vs 3590 mm³) because OCCT's
  pcurve computation for the partial (bend-segment) torus degenerated on
  both the write and read paths — a known OCCT bug (the 8.0.0 notes list
  "partial torus creation handles inverted V range"). The OCCT 8.0 port
  (commit 4b20904) fixes it with no brepper geometry change: round-trip rel
  diff is now 7.6e-9, and \`pipe_elbow_10_fine --compare\` is a tracked
  regression guard (commit 71a2735). The \`write.surfacecurve.mode=0\`
  workaround did NOT help and was abandoned. Full diagnosis is in the
  commit history / memory if the failure ever recurs.

528	/// \`torus_candidate\` already applies to a torus's major radius, extended to the
529	/// other analytic types.

533	/// 1.79 mm at 5e-1), because a looser bar admits still more degenerate fits.
534	fn radius_plausible(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, hyp: &CompeteHyp, bb_diag: f64) -> bool {
535	    hyp_radius(mesh, hyp) <= bb_diag

792	/// Condition the seed patch so the seed lies on the patch's own fit. A
793	/// depth-limited jet-similar patch can bleed a row or two across a tangent
794	/// junction between two surfaces of the same curvature class — a short
795	/// cylinder wall into its fillet, where the transition faces' κ1 ramps from
796	/// the wall's toward the fillet's — which pulls the fit off far enough that
797	/// the seed fails its own fit and the grow gives up (leaving the wall to be
798	/// eaten by an over-grown torus). Trim the worst-fitting patch face (never the
799	/// seed) and refit until the seed validates, bottoming out at a size floor so
800	/// the fit stays well-determined. Fit-validated, in the spirit of "validation
801	/// decides geometry"; a no-op when the patch is already clean.
802	#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
803	fn condition_patch<S: SurfaceType>(
804	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
805	    seed: usize,
806	    mut patch: Vec<usize>,
807	    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
808	    config: &Config,
809	    vtol: f64,
810	    stol: f64,
811	    min_faces: usize,
812	) -> Vec<usize> {
813	    let floor = min_faces.max(MIN_CONDITION_FACES);
814	    for _ in 0..PATCH_TRIM_ROUNDS {
815	        if patch.len() <= floor {
816	            break;
817	        }
818	        let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &patch);
819	        let mut fit = match S::fit_surface(mesh, &patch, &verts, config.verbosity) {
820	            Some(f) => f,
821	            None => break,
822	        };
823	        S::determine_convexity(mesh, &patch, &mut fit);
824	        if face_validates::<S>(mesh, seed, &fit, centroids, vtol, stol) {
825	            break;
826	        }
827	        let worst = patch
828	            .iter()
829	            .copied()
830	            .filter(|&f| f != seed)
831	            .max_by(|&a, &b| {
832	                face_max_vertex_dist::<S>(mesh, a, &fit)
833	                    .partial_cmp(&face_max_vertex_dist::<S>(mesh, b, &fit))
834	                    .unwrap()
835	            });
836	        match worst {
837	            Some(w) => patch.retain(|&f| f != w),
838	            None => break,
839	        }
840	    }
841	    patch
842	}

844	/// A small jet-similar patch around \`seed\` (same curvature class, magnitude
845	/// within 2×), capped, for a well-conditioned initial fit.
846	fn seed_patch(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, in_region: &[bool], seed: usize, jet: &[JetField]) -> Vec<usize> {
847	    let seed_class = curvature_class(jet[seed]);
848	    let seed_mag = jet[seed].k1.abs().max(jet[seed].k2.abs());
849	    let mut seen: HashSet<usize> = HashSet::new();
850	    seen.insert(seed);
851	    let mut out = vec![seed];
852	    // Depth-limited BFS (frontier by ring).
853	    let mut frontier = vec![seed];
854	    for _depth in 0..MAX_PATCH_DEPTH {
855	        if out.len() >= SEED_PATCH_CAP {
856	            break;
857	        }
858	        let mut next = Vec::new();
859	        for &fi in &frontier {
860	            let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
861	            for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
862	                if ni < 0 {
863	                    continue;
864	                }
865	                let ni = ni as usize;
866	                if !in_region[ni] || seen.contains(&ni) {
867	                    continue;
868	                }
869	                if curvature_class(jet[ni]) != seed_class {
870	                    continue;
871	                }
872	                let mag = jet[ni].k1.abs().max(jet[ni].k2.abs());
873	                if seed_mag > 1e-9 && (mag > 1.5 * seed_mag || mag < 0.667 * seed_mag) {
874	                    continue;
875	                }
876	                seen.insert(ni);
877	                out.push(ni);
878	                next.push(ni);
879	                if out.len() >= SEED_PATCH_CAP {
880	                    break;
881	                }
882	            }
883	        }
884	        frontier = next;
885	    }
886	    out.sort_unstable();
887	    out
888	}

/// TEMP probe: fit `S` to a face set and report the worst vertex distance.
fn probe_fit<S: SurfaceType>(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    faces: &[usize],
    verts: &[usize],
    config: &Config,
) -> Option<f64> {
    let mut fit = S::fit_surface(mesh, faces, verts, 0)?;
    S::determine_convexity(mesh, faces, &mut fit);
    let _ = config;
    let mut worst = 0.0_f64;
    for &vi in verts {
        let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
        worst = worst.max(S::vertex_distance(&fit, &[v.x, v.y, v.z]));
    }
    Some(worst)
}

/// Size of the largest mesh-connected component within a face set.

/// Determine convexity: does the face normal point away from the axis (convex) or toward it (concave)?
```

**After:**
```
/// How far a facet normal may stray from the cone's exact normal-axis
/// invariant (`|n·axis| = sin(half_angle)`) before it is judged not to lie on
/// the fit. Tessellation rotates facet normals *around* the axis, which
/// preserves the dot product exactly, so the slack only absorbs chordal sag.
const NORMAL_AXIS_TOL: f64 = 0.05;

/// Does the facet normal field agree with a cone/cylinder of this axis and
/// half-angle? On a cone every facet normal satisfies `|n·axis| =
/// sin(half_angle)`, so the normals pin the axis independently of the vertex
/// positions.
///
/// This is the acceptance test for a fit, not just for a candidate face: on a
/// support that is thin in the axial direction — a one-quad-tall cylinder band
/// between two fillet tori, common in a dense fillet network — the vertex
/// residual barely constrains the axis, and a least-squares cone will happily
/// tip its axis into the band's own plane and beat the true cylinder on
/// residual (measured on `stepped_block_toroidal_fillets`: a bogus 12.2°
/// cone at 3.8e-7 mm against the correct r = 0.5 cylinder at 3.9e-6 mm, with
/// the cone's axis nearly *anti-parallel* to the facet normals). The normals
/// are unambiguous where the positions are degenerate, so they decide.
///
/// Judged on the median face so a few noisy facets cannot veto a real fit;
/// individual offenders are still filtered by `convexity_check` during growth.
fn axis_normals_consistent(
    face_list: &[usize],
    faces: &[MeshFace],
    axis: &[f64; 3],
    half_angle: f64,
) -> bool {
    let expected = half_angle.sin().abs();
    let mut devs: Vec<f64> = face_list
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|&fi| faces[fi].normal)
        .map(|n| (dot3(&n, axis).abs() - expected).abs())
        .collect();
    if devs.is_empty() {
        return true;
    }
    devs.sort_by(|a, b| a.partial_cmp(b).unwrap());
    devs[devs.len() / 2] <= NORMAL_AXIS_TOL
}

/// eaten by an over-grown torus). Trim the worst-fitting patch face (never the
/// seed) and refit until the seed validates, bottoming out at a size floor so
/// the fit stays well-determined. Fit-validated, in the spirit of "validation
/// decides geometry"; a no-op when the patch is already clean.
///
/// When the patch admits no fit of this type at all there is no residual to
/// rank by, so the round instead drops the face geometrically farthest from
/// the seed: a straddling patch is unfittable precisely because its far end
/// sits on another surface, and shrinking toward the seed is the one move that
/// is monotonically local.

/// Distance between two faces' centroids.
fn centroid_gap(centroids: &[[f64; 3]], a: usize, b: usize) -> f64 {
    let (p, q) = (centroids[a], centroids[b]);
    ((p[0] - q[0]).powi(2) + (p[1] - q[1]).powi(2) + (p[2] - q[2]).powi(2)).sqrt()
}
