161	I've read the seeding loop (\`compete.rs\`), the ladder (\`classify.rs\`), the \`SurfaceType\` fitters, the merge machinery, and confirmed nothing like recursive subdivision appears in the refuted-ideas list. Here's my assessment.
162	
163	## Short verdict: yes, it has real merit — and it's less foreign to the codebase than it sounds
164	
165	Your idea is best understood as: **make the existing ladder recursive instead of falling back to per-face seeding**. The root of your recursion already exists. \`fit_validate\` (classify.rs:371) does precisely your steps 1–2: fit on a stride subsample of vertices (capped at 3000 faces), validate against *all* vertices, and on a near-miss fold the worst offenders into the fit set and refit (\`REFIT_ADD\`/\`MAX_REFIT\`). What's missing is your step 3: today, when that fails, \`classify_regions\` gives up and hands the region to \`compete_region\`, which re-attempts "fit a small patch → validate by flooding" once per face. That's the 103 s. Your proposal replaces that brute-force fallback with recursion.
166	
167	## One correction to the diagnosis, from the code
168	
169	"Good seeds require an interior face" is right, but the *why* is largely measured already — it's in the TODO's step-5 notes:
170	
171	- Seeds aren't single faces today; each grows a blind ≤32-face BFS patch (\`seed_patch\`). Setting \`SEED_PATCH_CAP=1\` was measured: stepped_block fine collapses to 24,872 per-facet surfaces. A single facet pins a plane (3 DOF) but not a free 5-DOF cylinder fit — so the blind neighbourhood exists to bootstrap *parameters*, and it fails because its contamination lives in the fit parameters even though the flood re-validates faces.
172	- The seed *order* is already jet-interior-first (\`neighbor_jet_mismatch\` ascending), and the interior-skip means that once good surfaces commit, the faces left seeding are *exactly the junction-adjacent margins* — the worst possible seeds, whose patches straddle junctions. That's the "323 NO GROWTH seeds" and much of the runtime.
173	
174	So the failure isn't that interior seeds are unexplored — it's that the scheme must guess where the interior is, per face, with a blind patch. Your recursion never has to guess: **the hierarchy finds homogeneous supports by construction**. A node straddling a junction fails validation and splits; a node inside one surface validates. 183	## Your crux question: subdivide vs. give up

185	I'd argue the distinction mostly **dissolves** if you set the policy up right. Two observations:

187	- **Subdividing too often only costs time** (bounded, logarithmic). 188	- **Don't gate the split decision on residual magnitude.** The project's history is littered with non-monotonic residual-threshold responses (the \`acceptance_tol\` removal, the facet-scaled-growth refutation). \`REFIT_GIVE_UP\` survives only as a give-up-on-augmenting test, and under recursion its role is just "fall through to the next rung, then split".

190	So: per node, run the DOF ladder (jet-ordered, as now). If a rung validates → commit. Else split. At the size floor → per-facet plane or the freeform handoff. That's "jet as prior, not gate", consistent with the codebase's philosophy, and its unreliability on coarse meshes costs only time.

The merge test already exists — it's exactly \`merge_regions\`' "refit the union and revalidate" (repair.rs:459+). Note this also handles over-splitting within one surface for free.

228	## Why the arithmetic is better than "one face = plane, two = cylinder"
229	
230	Facet **normals** are exact in this pipeline (facets are exactly planar; the jet is what's unreliable — normals aren't the jet). And there's a lovely geometric fact the codebase already half-knows: the chord of a circular arc has its normal pointing exactly radially at the arc midpoint. So for a cylinder tessellated in arc-step quads, **every facet normal is an exact radial direction**, and for two facets at different arc positions:
231	
232	**axis = n₁ × n₂** — exact, regardless of how coarse the arc steps are.
233	
234	Then the circle fit in the perpendicular plane uses *vertices*, which lie on the true surface to ~1e-6 (your earlier point, and the B-prime measurements). Compare the measured alternative in the TODO breadcrumbs: the jet reads κ₁ = 0.023 / 0.162 / 2.2 across one exact r=0.5 arc on medium — the jet is worthless there, but n₁×n₂ is exact at any tessellation density. This is the "cheap, DOF-reducing bootstrap" the step-5 breadcrumbs were hunting for, and it's self-derived rather than borrowed — the per-seed borrowed-axis fragmentation failure (75→100 surfaces, measured twice) doesn't apply, because the axis comes from the patch's own validated members.
235	
236	The same normal-line reasoning gives closed-form initializers up the ladder:
237	
238	- **Sphere, 2 faces**: normal lines concur at the center (nearly — skew by chordal sag; take the common-perpendicular midpoint).
239	- **Torus, 4 faces** — and this is the one the TODO calls "the open case, 7 DOF with no equally cheap constraint": a torus normal line lies in the meridian plane, i.e. *the normal line and the axis are coplanar*. Two lines (p,d) are coplanar iff (p₂−p₁)·(d₁×d₂) = 0; each facet gives one such equation in the axis (4 DOF: direction 2 + position 2), so four faces determine the axis in closed form, then R and r fall out of the normal-line geometry. That initializer didn't exist when the breadcrumbs were written, as far as I can see in the tree.

243	The change is smaller than the subdivision idea and slots into one place: replace \`seed_patch\` + \`condition_patch\` (compete.rs:1027–1180) with an **earn-your-patch** grow:
244	
245	1. BFS from the seed; maintain current type + fit (closed-form only — no LM during patch construction).
246	2. Per frontier face: does it validate against the current fit at vtol (the existing \`face_validates\`)?
247	   - Yes → admit, refit cheaply.
248	   - No → try **promotion**: refit the accepted set + candidate at the next type; if *all* accepted faces validate under the promoted fit, promote and admit.
249	   - No type validates → the face is across a seam. Exclude it. That's the boundary found, not a fit failure.
250	3. Hand the patch + type + parameters to \`grow_from\` unchanged — first LM polish happens there, flood extends to true extent, \`resolve_claims\` arbitrates, exactly as today.

252	The property you wanted is now structural: **every patch member was admitted by validation against a fit of already-admitted members**, so the patch can never straddle a junction. The blind patch's failure mode — contamination living on in the fit *parameters* — has no way to happen. And note what this does to seed quality: a margin seed's first ring includes faces across the junction, which fail admission and get excluded, so growth proceeds into the interior. The 323 NO GROWTH seeds mostly become productive; seed ordering (\`neighbor_jet_mismatch\`) stops mattering.

254	**What retires:** \`SEED_PATCH_CAP\`, \`MAX_PATCH_DEPTH\`, \`PATCH_RADII\`, \`PATCH_TRIM_ROUNDS\`, \`MIN_CONDITION_FACES\`, all of \`condition_patch\` (the patch is clean by construction — no trimming needed), and probably \`MAX_TORUS_STARTS\` (multiple flood starts exist because the fit patch was unreliable). 258	**1. The answer is to grow both branches; the false branch self-prunes within 1–2 faces, because the next face at a different height is off the sphere by ≈ Δ²/2R ≈ 6e-4 mm ≫ vtol. Validation at vtol is sharp relative to tessellation steps, so false candidates die young and branching stays cheap. 289	Yes — and the facet-space version of your idea is a well-mapped piece of mathematics. But its value hinges entirely on one question: **what feeds the edge map**. Let me take the pieces in order.
290	
291	## The translation to facet-space is direct (and cheap)
292	
293	Your image-processing pipeline has exact named analogs on the dual graph (faces = nodes, adjacency = edges):
294	
295	- **"Blur the edge data and find points far from edges"** = the **distance transform** (grassfire transform). On a graph it's multi-source Dijkstra from edge faces, weighted by centroid gaps — which, note, is in *millimetres*, not hops. That matters here: \`PATCH_RADII\` exists precisely because hop counts lie on graded meshes (three hops walk ~18 mm along a fillet chain swept with 6 mm facets). A geodesic distance field has no such problem, and it's parameter-free — no blur radius, no iteration count, no λ.
296	- **"Local maxima far from edges"** = maxima of the distance field, i.e. the **medial axis** in facet-space. (Small sign correction to your description: if you blur the edge map itself, maxima sit *at* edges — you want maxima of distance-to-edge, equivalently minima of diffused edginess. Same object.)
297	- **"Seeds at the maxima"** = farthest-first / maximin seeding (Gonzalez's k-center traversal). It has a real guarantee: each successive seed maximizes distance from all boundaries and all previous seeds, so the sequence is provably spread — a much better answer than \`neighbor_jet_mismatch\`, which is a noisy jet-based *proxy* for exactly this quantity.
298	
299	So as a seed-ordering field: sound, standard, and a strict improvement on what \`compete_region\` does today.
300	
301	## The catch: the edge map is the hard part, and one source of it is measured dead
302	
303	Three possible sources, in order of trustworthiness:
304	
305	**1. Sharp edges — exact and free, but blind to the junctions that matter.** Stage 2.2 already detects sharp edges, and regions are connected components over non-sharp edges (\`regions.rs\`). A distance field from region boundaries is computable in one Dijkstra pass. But regions are *defined* as tangent-connected interiors — the tangent junctions you actually want distance from are invisible to this source. On stepped_block, one 26122-face region contains all 71 surfaces; distance-from-sharp-boundary tells you nothing about where the fillets are.
306	
307	**2. Curvature-based tangent-edge detection — measured dead, do not re-derive.** This is the 2026-07-20 pivot in TODO: no threshold separates real junctions from real curvature gradients. And there's a geometric reason it's worse than "noisy": at a tangent junction between a fillet and a plane, the fillet's arc steps *approach* the plane's slope, so the dihedral **dips** toward zero exactly at the seam. The junction is locally the *smoothest* place on the mesh — an anti-edge. Every local geometric field (jet, dihedral, curvature-step) inherits some version of this, which is why detection-as-gate kept failing.
308	
309	**3. Validation-failure frontiers — exact, and you already own the machine that produces them.** From the incremental-grow idea: when the earn-your-patch grow excludes a face, that face is across a seam. The excluded frontier *is* the tangent junction row, discovered as a side effect of fitting, with no threshold anywhere. This is the only tangent-edge map in the system that's exact.
310	
311	## The synthesis: distance field with feedback, not precomputation
312	
313	Putting those together, the right construction isn't "detect edges → distance transform → seed", it's a loop:
314	
315	1. Initialize distance sources = sharp boundaries (exact, free).
316	2. Seed at the **max-distance unexplained face** (farthest-first).
317	3. Grow with the earn-your-patch mechanism; commit the flood.
318	4. Mark the grow's *failure frontier* as new distance sources; update the field (incremental multi-source Dijkstra — cheap).
319	5. Repeat until nothing is unexplained.
320	
321	This replaces the jet-mismatch ordering with a geometric ordering, and every iteration's seed is maximally far from everything known to contaminate a fit — sharp edges, plus tangent seams discovered by previous grows. No detector, no threshold, no new tuned constants.
322	
323	**And it yields a principled answer to TODO item 2's actual question** ("how much of the 26122-face seed sweep does useful work"). The useful-work criterion: a seed can only claim new territory if its conditioning ball contains an *unclaimed* face. So maintain distance-to-nearest-unclaimed-face; skip any seed whose conditioning radius is smaller than that distance. That's a strict generalization of today's \`interior_of_claims\` (which checks only the radius-1 neighbourhood — compete.rs:420) to the true conditioning radius, and unlike a heuristic cap it's *sound*: a ball fully inside one committed surface can only refit that surface. On stepped_block fine, after the first few medial seeds commit the big surfaces, the unclaimed set collapses to junction zones, and the sweep collapses from 26K candidate seeds to the few hundred faces adjacent to leftovers. That's the runtime lever item 2 wants, derived rather than tuned.
324	
325	**Bonus use — identifiability.** A face's distance value caps the support its patch can gather, which caps the DOF its fit can determine: the degenerate free-radius tori (the ones \`MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG\` exists to reject) are born at faces whose reachable support is a handful of faces. Distance-from-boundary gives a per-seed "max supportable DOF" prior — it can cap the promotion ladder from the incremental-grow idea (don't promote to torus where the ball can only reach 7 faces), attacking the degeneracy at seed time rather than at commit time.
326

329	- **Idea 2 changed this idea's job.** Once patches are earned face-by-face under validation, seed interiority matters much less for *correctness* — a margin seed's first ring excludes the cross-junction faces and grows inward. 330	- **Any field computed before fitting is a prior; the only exact field comes from fitting.** If someone proposes feeding this with a jet/dihedral edge map, that's the refuted detector returning in a hat.
331	- **The full watershed reading is a bigger, different bet.** If you treat a continuous edginess field as topography and let basins flood until they meet, the watershed lines *are* the partition — no seeds at all. 335	Distance/grassfire transform (Borgefors), Blum's medial axis, marker-controlled watershed (Beucher & Vincent) — the marker version is the relevant one, and your "known-interior seeds" *are* the markers; farthest-first traversal (Gonzalez 1985); and your "blur then climb to maxima" is literally **mean-shift** mode-finding, whose mesh-segmentation cousins exist. 357	## The thesis in one paragraph
358	
359	The measured fragility of brepper concentrates in exactly one place: **stage 2.3(b)'s seeding**, and the pile of ~34 constants that exist because tangent seams are invisible to local geometry. Everything upstream (stage 1, sharp-edge detection → regions, the DOF ladder, \`fit_validate\`, the validation primitives) and everything downstream (claim arbitration, stage 3 assembly, the \`--compare\` harness) is principled and load-bearing. So this plan does **not** rewrite the pipeline. It replaces the blind-patch seeding mechanism with fits that are *earned under validation* rather than *grabbed and repaired*, makes seed exploration distance-guided so its cost scales with boundary-zone size rather than region size, deletes whatever is then measured inert on an expanded corpus, and quarantines the two genuine research problems (freeform fit conditioning; analytic-vs-B-spline model selection) behind explicit measurement gates. A partition-level rewrite (recursive subdivision / watershed) is held in reserve and only started with the user, with data, if the earlier phases leave the goals unmet.

369	3. **No new tolerance-like or threshold-like constants without explicit user sign-off.** Numeric-conditioning guards (determinant floors, minimum sin(dihedral) before normalizing a cross product) are not thresholds; say so in their doc comments when adding them.

393	## Phase 1 — Earned patches (the core rework)
394	
395	**Goal:** replace the blind seed patch with a patch *grown face-by-face under validation*, promoting surface type as accumulated DOF allow. A patch that can never straddle a junction by construction removes the root cause the step-5 notes document — the contamination that lives in fit *parameters*.
396	
397	**Build:**
398	1. **Closed-form initializers from exact facet normals** (LM is only for polish, in the existing \`grow_from\`):
399	   - Plane: one face (exact).
400	   - Cylinder: axis = n₁ × n₂ from two faces with non-parallel normals + \`fit_circle_for_axis\` (exists). Guard: only normalize the cross product above a numerical-conditioning floor; otherwise keep growing as plane until a better pair arrives.
401	   - Sphere: normal-line intersection from two faces (common-perpendicular midpoint).
402	   - Conical: existing normal-covariance machinery — sound now because the patch is clean.
403	   - Torus: derive the 4-face normal-line-coplanarity system (a torus's normal lines lie in the meridian planes, hence are coplanar with the axis). **Time-box this.** Unit-test on synthetic tori to ~1e-9 before integrating. If the derivation or conditioning doesn't pan out, *skip it* — direct torus seeding stays as today (\`torus_candidate\`), and Phase 1 is not blocked.
404	2. **The earn loop:** BFS from the seed; admit a frontier face iff it validates the current fit at \`vtol\`; on failure, attempt **promotion** in ladder order (plane → conical/sphere, jet-ordered as today → torus), refitting the accepted set + candidate and requiring *all* accepted faces to validate; if nothing validates, the face is across a seam — exclude it. **Branch** on genuine ambiguity (e.g., the 2-face cylinder/sphere trap): false branches should self-prune within a couple of faces because validation at \`vtol\` is sharp relative to tessellation steps.
405	3. **Cylinder→torus promotion via fit drift.** A bend is locally a valid cylinder, so validation never triggers promotion. The signal: along a straight cylinder successive refits are stationary; along a bend the fitted axis *precesses systematically*. Test drift as *sign-consistency* of successive axis deltas, not magnitude — if it needs a magnitude constant, **stop and ask**. Success here is what later allows deleting \`promote_bend\`; if it doesn't work, keep \`promote_bend\` and move on.
406	4. Hand patch + type + parameters to the **unchanged** \`grow_from\` flood/refit/commit/\`resolve_claims\` path. Commit semantics deliberately do not change: every guard (\`MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG\`, torus-ratio, \`MIN_*_FACES\`) keeps its exact meaning.
407	
408	**Delete (after ablation):** \`seed_patch\` jet filtering, \`condition_patch\`, \`SEED_PATCH_CAP\`, \`MAX_PATCH_DEPTH\`, \`PATCH_RADII\`, \`PATCH_TRIM_ROUNDS\`, \`MIN_CONDITION_FACES\`.
409	
410	**Assumption checks, in order, before building further:**
411	- *Axis-initializer quality across provenances.* On Parasolid quad strips, cylinder chord normals are exactly radial → n₁×n₂ exact. On OCCT Delaunay interiors this is *not* guaranteed. Measure axis error against reference cylinders across the Phase-0 corpus. If median error exceeds ~1° on some provenance, the initializer degrades to "covariance-axis over the earned patch" for that case — still clean, still not blind. **If even that underperforms the blind patch on any provenance, stop and ask** — the core premise needs re-examination.
412	- *Branch lifetime.* Instrument: branches should die within ~2 faces. If they persist, validation isn't as sharp as believed — stop and ask before the cost model changes.
413	- *NO GROWTH count* on the corpus should collapse toward zero.
414	
415	**Acceptance:** probe breakdowns equal-or-better on all models (stepped_block fine ≥ today's 75-surface state, medium not worse); suite green; constant count down by the deleted family.
416	
417	**Explicitly NOT fixed by this phase — do not chase them here:** the 4 surplus surfaces on fine (boundary precision), medium's gap, hill_with_hole's junk torus (model selection), runtime (Phase 2).

421	## Phase 2 — Seed exploration: ordering and bounded cost
422	
423	**Goal:** the 103 s question ("how much of the 26,122-face sweep does useful work") gets a *derived* answer: only seeds whose reachable ball contains an unclaimed face can do useful work.
424	
425	**Build, profile first:**
426	1. **Profile the runtime** (patch construction vs. LM fits vs. floods vs. claim resolution). Apply the cheapest fix that addresses the measured distribution; do not build the full machinery below if the profile says the cost is elsewhere. Report the profile to the user regardless.
427	2. **Distance field:** geodesic distance-to-region-boundary per face (multi-source Dijkstra, centroid-gap weights — millimetres, not hops; graded meshes make hop counts lie). Seed order: **farthest-first**, replacing \`neighbor_jet_mismatch\`.
428	3. **Duplicate abort:** a seed claimed by surface S whose minimal-patch ball lies entirely within S can only refit S — skip it (topological rule, strict generalization of \`interior_of_claims\`, no numeric tolerance).
429	4. **Frontier feedback (only if the profile says ordering still matters):** grow-failure frontiers (faces excluded by Phase-1 earns) become new distance sources for subsequent ordering. This is the exact tangent-edge map, discovered by fitting, never detected.

## The Robustness Rework (2026-07-29)

**This section is the rationale behind the phased plan in TODO.md.** TODO.md
carries the step-by-step instructions; this section records why each phase is
shaped the way it is, the design detail for the two new mechanisms (earned
patches, distance-guided exploration), the corpus strategy, what was considered
and deliberately not adopted, and the measurements preserved from the TODO
items the plan retired. It synthesizes two parallel design sessions held
2026-07-29 (one logged at `agent-logs/2026-07-29_14-59_nothinking.md`) plus the
measured record above.

### Goal and thesis

The goal changed: **maximum robustness and minimum fragility over all plausible
CAD-derived meshes**, not score on the current corpus. Fragility is
operationalized as two headline numbers: the stage-2 tuned-constant count
(34 at plan time; `grep -h "^const \|^pub(crate) const \|^pub(super) const "
src/stage2/*.rs | wc -l`) and the **cliff count** — the number of constants
whose ±2× perturbation collapses any model (four unrelated knobs once each
flipped stepped_block medium from 83 surfaces to full per-facet collapse).

The measured fragility concentrates in three structural debts, and the plan
retires them in dependency order:

1. **Evaluation is anecdotal.** 14 hand-watched models, Onshape/Parasolid-heavy;
   three NURBS models rotted silently because nothing watched them. You cannot
   claim generality you cannot measure → Phase 0 builds the instrument first.
2. **Two of three tolerances are guesses.** `--surface-tolerance` defaults to
   0.4 mm against a measured true sag of ~9e-4 mm (~400× too loose), making
   centroid validation nearly vacuous; `--angular-tolerance` is a stand-in for
   a discarded exporter setting. Both are measurable from the mesh itself
   → Phases 0 (diagnostics) and 3 (regime flip).
3. **One component — blind-patch seeding — forces most of the guard pile.**
   `seed_patch`/`condition_patch` fit an unvalidated 32-face BFS neighbourhood;
   the contamination lives on in the fit parameters, producing both the 323
   NO-GROWTH seeds and plausible-but-wrong fits. Roughly two-thirds of stage
   2's constants exist because tangent seams are invisible to it → Phases 1–2
   replace the mechanism, Phase 4 deletes what that makes inert.

Everything else measured principled — stage 1, sharp-edge regions, the DOF
ladder, `fit_validate`, `face_validates`, flood, `resolve_claims`,
relabel+refit, the locus machinery, stage 3 topological assembly, the
`--compare` gates — **is deliberately not touched**.

### Phase 1 design: earned patches (replaces the blind patch)

Replace grab-then-repair with **grow-under-validation**: BFS from the seed,
admitting a frontier face only if it validates against the current fit at
vertex tolerance; when a face fails, attempt **promotion** up the ladder
(plane → cylinder/cone or sphere → torus), refitting accepted+candidate and
requiring *every already-accepted face* to still validate; if no type
validates, the face is across a seam — exclude it and record it as a
**frontier face** (Phase 2 consumes these). The patch can never straddle a
junction by construction, which is the exact property the blind patch lacks.
Commit semantics do not change: the earned (type, params, patch) goes to the
unchanged `grow_from` flood/refit path, and every existing commit gate
(`MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG`, torus ratio, `MIN_*_FACES`, `resolve_claims`) keeps
its meaning.

What makes promotion workable at tiny support — where a free least-squares fit
is hopeless (sagitta arithmetic: over a 7.5° arc on r = 0.5 the sag is
~0.001 mm against a 2e-5 mm quantum, so a free radius is ~2% ≈ 200× vtol
wrong) — is that **facet normals are exact** and give closed-form,
DOF-reducing initializers:

- **Cylinder — axis = n₁ × n₂.** A planar facet spanning two rulings of a
  cylinder has its normal exactly perpendicular to the axis, at any coarseness,
  so two facets with non-parallel normals give the axis exactly on
  strip/quad-tessellated surfaces. Radius+origin then come from
  `fit_circle_for_axis` (cylindrical.rs), measured well-conditioned on short
  arcs (r = 0.99998 / 0.99999 / 0.50008 from 65°/60°/40° arcs). **Provenance
  caveat:** a general Delaunay triangle's normal is *not* exactly
  perpendicular to the axis; measure axis error per provenance (Phase 0's OCCT
  meshes), and degrade to the normal-covariance axis over the earned patch
  where needed — still clean, still not blind.
- **Sphere — concurrent normal lines.** For any planar facet inscribed in a
  sphere, the line through the facet's **circumcenter** along its normal
  passes exactly through the sphere centre (equidistance). Two facets → centre
  at the near-intersection (common-perpendicular midpoint), radius = distance.
- **Cone** — the existing normal-covariance axis (`smallest_eigenvector_3x3`)
  over the earned patch, guarded by `axis_normals_consistent`, both existing.
- **Torus — meridian coplanarity, the "open case" closed.** Every torus
  normal line lies in the meridian plane through its point, which contains
  the axis — so each facet contributes one coplanarity constraint
  `(pᵢ − a) · (nᵢ × d) = 0` on the axis (point a, direction d; 4 DOF; the
  system is bilinear — solve by alternation or pairwise elimination). Four
  facets pin the axis; then (R, r) is a 2-D circle fit in (ρ, z) profile
  coordinates — `fit_circle_2d` already exists (toroidal.rs). **Caveats:**
  rank-deficient by construction on sphere data (any axis through the centre
  satisfies it) and consistent-but-degenerate on cylinder data, so ladder
  order and a conditioning floor must precede it; grid-aligned quads give
  near-exact meridian normals, Delaunay triangles do not. **Time-boxed**: unit
  test to ~1e-9 on synthetic tori before integrating; if conditioning does not
  pan out, skip it — direct torus seeding stays as today and Phase 1 is not
  blocked.

Two behaviours need more than validation failure:

- **Ambiguity → branch, don't choose.** Two same-height faces of a cylinder
  validate as a sphere centred on the axis (the hole→sphere trap at patch
  scale). Grow both branches; the false one should die within a face or two
  (the next face at a different height is off the sphere by ≈ Δ²/2R ≫ vtol).
  Instrument branch lifetime; persistent branches mean validation is less
  sharp than believed — stop and ask.
- **Bent tube → drift-triggered promotion.** A bend is locally a valid
  cylinder (sag of the bend over a 2 mm patch at R = 14 is ~3.6e-5 mm), so
  admission never fails and promotion never triggers on residual. The signal
  is **systematic fit drift**: along a straight tube successive refits are
  stationary; along a bend the fitted axis precesses with a consistent sign as
  support accumulates. Test drift as sign-consistency of successive axis
  deltas, *not* magnitude (a magnitude bar would be a new tuned constant —
  stop and ask if one seems needed). Success retires `promote_bend` and the
  `BEND_*` constants; failure keeps them, and that is fine.

**Deleted when this lands (after ablation evidence):** `condition_patch`
entirely, `seed_patch`'s jet filtering, `SEED_PATCH_CAP`, `MAX_PATCH_DEPTH`,
`PATCH_RADII`, `PATCH_TRIM_ROUNDS`, `MIN_CONDITION_FACES`, likely
`MAX_TORUS_STARTS` (multiple flood starts exist because the fit patch was
unreliable).

### Phase 2 design: distance-guided exploration

The 26122-face seed sweep costs 103 s on stepped_block fine and its
useful-work fraction is unknown (profile first — do not build this phase's
machinery if the profile says the cost is in fits or floods rather than the
sweep). The principled orderings and bounds, all derived rather than tuned:

- **Distance field**: per-face geodesic distance to the region boundary
  (multi-source Dijkstra over the dual graph, **centroid-gap weights in
  millimetres, not hops** — hop counts lie on graded meshes, which is what
  `PATCH_RADII` existed to patch). Seed **farthest-first** (Gonzalez maximin),
  replacing `neighbor_jet_mismatch` — the jet-based proxy for exactly this
  quantity.
- **Feedback, not detection**: tangent junctions cannot be *detected* (the
  measured-dead pivot; a tangent junction is locally the *smoothest* place on
  the mesh — an anti-edge), but they are *discovered exactly* by Phase 1's
  excluded frontier faces. Add discovered frontiers as new distance sources
  incrementally. The only trustworthy edge map is the one the fits produce.
- **Duplicate abort**: a seed whose reachable ball lies entirely inside one
  committed surface can only refit that surface — skip it. Topological, a
  strict generalization of `interior_of_claims`, no numeric tolerance.
- **Acceptance discipline**: ordering must not change results. Bit-identical
  probe output, or every diff explained; order-dependence is itself the
  fragility being removed — stop and surface it.

### Phase 0 design: the corpus and the instrument

Three provenance sources, cheapest first, all scored against reference STEPs:

1. **OCCT re-mesh of existing references** (automated, free ground truth).
   `gen_test_models` already drives `BRepMesh` with deflection/angle settings
   (`write_tessellated_stl`); add a mode that loads any reference STEP and
   emits STL variants at several settings, plus **off-origin variants**
   (translate the shape ~1 m before both STL and STEP output) so the float32
   quantum question becomes testable. This adds constrained-Delaunay
   provenance to a strip-heavy corpus.
2. **Fusion 360 re-export** (user batch job): import reference STEPs, export
   STL at low/medium/high. Different tessellator, same ground truth.
3. **Wild STEP+STL pairs** (most representative, most care): harvest models
   published with both a STEP/F3D and an STL (Thingiverse API / Printables /
   GrabCAD, scripted or via a browser session). **Pair-verification gate**:
   run stage 1 `--compare`; a pair counts as ground truth only if mesh
   vertices lie on the STEP surfaces to within a few quanta — otherwise
   quarantine as crash-test-only (the STL may be a different revision,
   decimated, or repaired). Record the verification *rate*: it is itself the
   first field measurement of the provenance premise ("vertices lie on the
   true surface") in the wild. Keep licensing clean: store source URL,
   author, license, and hash in a manifest; do not commit files whose license
   does not permit redistribution (gitignore the external corpus, commit the
   manifest).

The instrument: a one-command sweep harness (per-model rows: per-type surface
breakdown, `--compare` distances, volume error, runtime, exit status;
machine-readable; saved baselines + diff mode) and a **fragility meter** that
perturbs/ablates each stage-2 constant and reports which models change.

### Tolerance sequencing (Phases 0 and 3)

Estimators are built and *reported* in Phase 0 (they double as the
provenance-violation detector: estimator disagreement or a missing dihedral
gap means a decimated/remeshed/faceted-by-construction input — warn now,
degrade gracefully in Phase 6). The **default flip is deferred to Phase 3**,
after the seeding rework stabilizes: a 400× change to `stol` moves behaviour
everywhere (`REFIT_GIVE_UP` is 8×stol; merge gates and `face_validates` use
it), and debugging it concurrently with new seeding would confound both. The
earn loop admits on *vertex* tolerance, so Phase 1 is essentially independent
of the stol regime. Ablation (Phase 4) runs after the flip so deletions are
judged under the final regime.

### Considered and not adopted (with reasons)

- **Recursive subdivision / split-and-merge as the architecture.** Strong
  asymptotics (the tree visits only boundary-containing paths) and its merge
  half already exists (`fit_validate` as union-revalidation), but: fixed
  geometric cuts do not respect seams (boundaries are mesh-edge chains;
  strip-shaped surfaces stay contaminated at every level until cells are
  smaller than the strip), and identifiability *inverts* — a sub-node of a
  real torus legitimately sweeps 5° and fits garbage parameters that validate
  locally, so every sweep guard would need to become "defer, don't reject"
  until merge time, a rework of commit semantics. Phases 1–2 deliver most of
  its benefit at a fraction of the risk. **Held in reserve**; do not start
  without Phase 1–4 measurements in hand and user sign-off.
- **Precomputed junction-evidence field for seeding** (dihedral
  second-difference, diffused; or any jet/dihedral edge map). Any field
  computed *before* fitting is a detector prior — the refuted detector
  returning in a hat. Superseded by the exact, threshold-free fit-derived
  frontier field of Phase 2. (For the record, the raw idea also had a real
  basis: within a tessellated surface the dihedral field is locally
  consistent and *steps* at junctions — but the OCCT-Delaunay and
  coarse-mesh cases erode it, and nothing needs it once frontiers exist.)
- **The "bridge" formulation of type promotion** (grow under an
  exactly-determined uncommittable fit until the new DOF identify). Correct
  shape, but its fragile middle regime — junction faces soaking into
  exactly-determined fits — is mostly obviated by the closed-form
  initializers, which pin the new DOF geometrically at 2–4 faces instead of
  waiting for least-squares identifiability. The earn loop keeps the bridge's
  two sound rules: full-support revalidation on every accretion, and
  identifiability-gated *commits*.
- **VSA (the old item C)** as a planned phase. Earned patches + the existing
  relabel/refit fixpoint already implement the alternation locally, and the
  known-working machinery it would replace (`resolve_claims`, relabel, merge)
  is exactly what a big rewrite puts at risk. Reserve, same gate as
  subdivision. The pending `snap_boundaries` keep/delete decision folds into
  Phase 4 with fresh ablation data (it is the per-face assignment criterion a
  future VSA would need, and the locus diagnostic depends on the module).
- **Retuning anything to close the last corpus gaps first** (stepped fine's 4
  surplus surfaces, medium's ~13). Deliberately deferred: they are boundary-
  and identifiability-residue that Phases 1–4 either fix or isolate, and
  chasing them now re-enters the one-model-at-a-time loop that produced the
  fragility.

### Preserved measurements from retired TODO items

(Everything here is measured; do not re-derive. Sources: 2026-07-26..29
sessions.)

- **Sagitta bound**: no local patch determines a free surface of revolution —
  7.5° arc on r = 0.5 → sag ~0.001 mm vs 2e-5 mm quantum → r ~2% (≈200×
  vtol) wrong. Only DOF reduction helps at small support.
- **Blind-patch facts**: `SEED_PATCH_CAP = 1` collapses stepped_block fine to
  24872 surfaces (the blind patch was the free path's only bootstrap);
  0 of 200 sampled flat seeds produced a patch that stayed on the flat
  (median 50% fillet contamination); 72 of 75 flat components are under the
  32-face cap; a 3232 mm² plane is 12 faces.
- **Borrowed axes**: per-seed borrowed-axis candidates fragment surfaces
  (75 → 100, cylinders 38 → 63, measured twice); (d2) works *only* because it
  selects largest validated area globally before committing. Any borrowed-axis
  use outside (d2) must keep that global selection.
- **Jet reliability**: fine meshes good (κ₁ = 2.005 vs true 2.0); coarse
  garbage (κ₁ = 0.023 / 0.162 / 2.2 across one exact r = 0.5 arc on medium).
  Facet long-edge direction is right ~65% on strips (up to 76° off) —
  corroborating only, never load-bearing.
- **Identifiability, not residual**: impostor cylinders/tori sweep 2.8–6.7°
  vs real surfaces ≥ 64.8°; spurious exactly-determined tori fit at
  0.52/0.72/0.87 quanta vs genuine mean 0.39 / max 0.56 — overlapping, so no
  residual or coverage test rejects them. `candidate_sweep` is vacuous for
  spheres and true cones — a normal-spread identifiability test for those is
  still missing (Phase 5c territory).
- **Exact-normal component exploration** (partial, superseded as a detection
  path): connected components over near-zero-dihedral edges give 342
  components ≥ 10 mm² where the reference has 16 planes, threshold-insensitive
  from 0.001° to 0.2°; top ~16 sum to 14301 mm² vs expected 13783. The
  unexplained tail was suspected large-radius fillets with sub-threshold
  steps. Do not resume as detection; frontier feedback replaces it.
- **hill_with_hole residue**: one junk torus — 17 faces (one over
  `SMALL_SELECTION_ABSORB_FACES = 16`), R = 3.5101 r = 2.3882 (r/R = 0.680,
  just under the 0.7 cap), area 1.533 mm² = **0.095%** of its freeform patch —
  vs `cone_tangent_planes`' real cones at large fractions (1081/163 mm²).
  Relative area is the one untried candidacy quantity. With the decomposition
  forced correct to 7 surfaces it then fails stage 4.1 volume at 6.96e-2
  relative — a separate freeform-accuracy/export issue.
- **Freeform fit failures**: `bspline_blister`'s 926-face component rejected
  by the §2.7 pole-bound check ("control points 2749.5 mm outside the data
  bounding box"), saddle's three components likewise; the check is right, the
  fit conditioning is the bug; nothing recovers, regions fall to per-facet.
  When they do decompose, 4 and 3 invalid micro-sliver faces remain (ignored
  test).
- **Sag truth values** for estimator validation: stage-1 `--compare` centroid
  max ≈ 8.9e-4 mm (stepped fine), 9.5e-4 mm (rounded_cube fine); Onshape
  angular settings 12.5°/6.25°/2.5°; Onshape-coarse worst sag 0.026 mm,
  Fusion-low 0.038 mm.
- **cone_15x20**: its reference STEP is itself faceted (59 planes, not
  analytic) — a corpus-data defect, not a pipeline bug; regenerate or mark
  unusable in Phase 0.

### Map from the retired TODO to the new plan

- Runtime bound (old item 2) → Phase 2 (profile first).
- stepped fine surplus / medium gap (old item 3) → Phase 1 acceptance targets,
  then Phase 4/5 residue.
- NURBS corpus blockers → Phase 5a (blister/saddle fit), Phase 5c

- B-prime (quantum) → Phase 0 clamp+report, Phase 5b unit-of-quality.
- B (tolerance estimation) → Phase 0 diagnostics + Phase 3 flip.
- C (VSA) and recursive subdivision → Reserve.
- Step 5 (delete the blind patch) → Phase 1 (earned patches are the missing

- snap_boundaries decision → Phase 4 with fresh ablation data.
- Faceted-by-construction / OpenSCAD → Phase 6.
- 3DBenchy, nosecone coverage, stage-1-only audit → Phase 0.
- Radius-refinement (old "robust rather than tuned" item 3) → Phase 4

# Brepper TODO — the Robustness Rework (plan set 2026-07-29)

This file is the **step-by-step execution plan**. Work the phases in order;
within a phase, work the numbered steps in order unless a step is marked
**[parallel-ok]**. The rationale, design detail, corpus strategy, and the
choices deliberately not made live in DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md under **"The
Robustness Rework (2026-07-29)"** — read that section AND "Rewriting stage
2.3(b): the blind patch is the root cause" before starting any phase.
Completed work is recorded in DONE.md. When you finish a step, annotate it
here in place (`**DONE <date>**` plus a one-line result with the key numbers),
matching the project's existing convention.

**Goal.** Maximum robustness and minimum fragility over all plausible
CAD-derived meshes — not score on the current corpus. Fragility is
operationalized: the stage-2 tuned-constant count (**34** at plan time) and
the **cliff count** (constants whose ±2× perturbation collapses any model).
Report both in every commit message that moves either.

## Execution rules — apply to every commit

1. **Invariants after every commit**: every mesh face in exactly one surface
   (`assert_invariants`); committed supports are flood/validation outputs at
   `vtol`/`stol`, never hand-adjusted; build clean; `cargo clippy` clean;
   suite green (`cargo test --release --no-fail-fast`, ~2.5 min) or newly
   `#[ignore]`d only with a precise blocker string.
2. **Measurement protocol**: save a `tmp/probe.sh` baseline before each phase;
   diff **per-type breakdowns** (plane/cyl/cone/sphere/torus/bspline), never
   surface counts alone (a 3-torus regression once hid behind an unchanged
   total of 71). The full suite is the decider. Once Phase 0 lands, the sweep
   harness joins the protocol.
3. **No new tolerance-like or threshold-like constant without user sign-off.**
   Numeric-conditioning floors (determinant floors, minimum |n₁×n₂| before
   normalizing) are not thresholds — say so in their doc comments when adding.
4. **Nothing is deleted without ablation evidence**: disable → probe → suite
   (→ harness) → delete, recording in DEVELOPMENT_PLAN what it was for and
   what superseded it.
5. **Stop and ask the user**, with measurements written down, when:
   - a step's listed assumption check fails;
   - results become **ordering-dependent** (ordering changes output);
   - you are about to implement a freeform-candidacy or model-selection rule

   - a detector seems to need "just one threshold";
   - a guard proposed for deletion still fires anywhere;

6. **Dead ends — do not re-derive** (details in DEVELOPMENT_PLAN):
   curvature/dihedral tangent-seam *detection* (dead twice; a tangent junction
   is locally the smoothest place on the mesh); acceptance-tolerance scaling
   with mesh quantum (chaotic, no plateau); complexity pricing among nested
   analytic types; clustering/snapping fitted radii; per-seed borrowed-axis
   commits without global selection (fragments surfaces, measured twice);
   face-size-ratio boundary tests (anti-correlated); count/fraction-based
   freeform candidacy rules (four dead); retuning flood/conditioning floors

**Diagnostics toolbox**: `tmp/probe.sh` (14-model per-type breakdown);
`dump_regions <model> jetdump` (per-face k1/k2/area/adjacency/normal);

(per-seed compete log); `src/bin/step_measure_tolerance.rs`.

## Phase 1 — Earned patches (the core rework)

Replace the blind seed patch with a patch **grown face-by-face under
validation**, promoting the surface type as the accumulated support allows.
Full design + math in DEVELOPMENT_PLAN ("The Robustness Rework", Phase 1
design). Commit semantics deliberately unchanged: earned (type, params,
patch) hands off to the existing `grow_from` flood/refit path, and every
commit gate (`MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG`, torus ratio, `MIN_*_FACES`,
`resolve_claims`) keeps its exact meaning.

- **1.1 Closed-form initializers, unit-tested first** (synthetic strips/tori;
  the corpus's exactness precedents — r = 0.99998-style — make ~1e-9
  assertions appropriate):
  - Cylinder: axis = n₁ × n₂ from two admitted faces with non-parallel
    normals (exact on strip/quad tessellation), then `fit_circle_for_axis`
    (cylindrical.rs — exists, measured well-conditioned on 40–65° arcs).
    Guard with a numeric conditioning floor on |n₁×n₂|, documented as
    validity-not-threshold.
  - Sphere: normal lines anchored at facet **circumcenters** (exact through
    the centre for inscribed facets); centre = common-perpendicular midpoint
    of two lines; radius = mean distance.
  - Cone: existing normal-covariance axis over the earned patch
    (`smallest_eigenvector_3x3`) + `axis_normals_consistent`.
  - Torus (**time-boxed — skip without blocking the phase if conditioning
    fails**): axis from the meridian-coplanarity system
    `(pᵢ − a)·(nᵢ × d) = 0` over ≥4 faces (bilinear; solve by alternation or
    pairwise elimination; rank-deficient on sphere/cylinder data by
    construction — ladder order and a conditioning floor must precede it);
    then (R, r) via the existing `fit_circle_2d` profile fit (toroidal.rs).
- **1.2 The earn loop.** Replace `seed_patch` + `condition_patch` inside
  `grow` (compete.rs): BFS from the seed; admit a frontier face iff it
  validates the current fit at vtol (`face_validates`); on failure attempt
  **promotion** in ladder order (plane → cylinder/cone or sphere → torus),
  refitting accepted+candidate and requiring **all already-accepted faces**
  to validate under the promoted fit; if nothing validates, the face is
  across a seam — exclude it and **record it as a frontier face** (Phase 2
  consumes these). **Branch on ambiguity** (e.g. two same-height cylinder
  faces validating as a sphere): grow both; false branches should self-prune
  within ~2 faces. Hand each surviving (type, patch, params) to the unchanged
  `grow_from`. Add counters (behind verbosity/env): NO-GROWTH count, branches
  spawned / died-within-2, promotions attempted/accepted, frontier faces.
- **1.3 Drift-triggered cylinder→torus promotion** (time-boxed). A bend is
  locally a valid cylinder, so admission never fails; the signal is
  **sign-consistent precession** of the fitted axis across successive refits
  as support accumulates — not a magnitude test (if a magnitude constant
  seems needed, stop and ask). If it works, `promote_bend` + `BEND_*` become
  Phase-4 deletion candidates; if not, keep them and move on.
- **1.4 Validate.**
  - *Initializer accuracy per provenance*: measure cylinder-axis error vs
    references across Parasolid strips AND the Phase-0 OCCT Delaunay meshes.
    If median error exceeds ~1° on a provenance, degrade that provenance to
    the covariance axis over the earned patch (still clean, still not blind).
    **Stop and ask** if even that underperforms the blind patch anywhere.
  - *Branch lifetime*: if branches persist past ~2 faces, validation is less
    sharp than believed — stop and ask before the cost model changes.
  - *NO-GROWTH count* (baseline 323 on stepped_block fine) should collapse
    toward zero.
  - *Acceptance*: probe per-type breakdowns equal-or-better corpus-wide;
    stepped_block fine ≥ today's 75-surface state; **stepped_block medium and
    part_rounded_cube coarse not worse** (the identifiability stress cases —
    the one place the blind patch did irreplaceable work); suite green;
    harness ≥ baseline.
- **1.5 Delete after ablation** (rule 4): `condition_patch`, `seed_patch`'s
  jet filtering, `SEED_PATCH_CAP`, `MAX_PATCH_DEPTH`, `PATCH_RADII`,
  `PATCH_TRIM_ROUNDS`, `MIN_CONDITION_FACES`; likely `MAX_TORUS_STARTS`.
  Report the constant count.

**Explicitly NOT fixed by this phase — do not chase here**: stepped fine's 4
surplus surfaces, medium's remaining gap, hill_with_hole's junk torus
(Phase 5c), runtime (Phase 2).

---

## Phase 2 — Distance-guided exploration and the runtime bound

- **2.1 Profile first.** Instrument the stepped_block fine run (103 s
  baseline): time in earn/patch construction vs LM fits vs floods vs
  `resolve_claims`. Report the split to the user. **Only build 2.2–2.4 if the
  seed sweep dominates**; otherwise apply the cheapest fix the profile names.
- **2.2 Distance field + farthest-first seeding.** Per-face geodesic distance
  to the region boundary (multi-source Dijkstra over face adjacency,
  **centroid-gap weights in mm, not hops** — hop counts lie on graded
  meshes). Order seeds farthest-first, replacing `neighbor_jet_mismatch`.
- **2.3 Duplicate abort.** Skip a seed whose reachable ball lies entirely
  inside one committed surface (it can only refit that surface) — the
  topological generalization of `interior_of_claims`; no numeric tolerance.
- **2.4 Frontier feedback** (only if the profile still warrants): add Phase
  1's excluded frontier faces as new distance sources incrementally — the
  exact tangent-junction map, discovered by fitting, never detected.
- **Acceptance**: results bit-identical to Phase 1's output, or every diff
  explained (**ordering-dependence = stop and surface it**); stepped fine
  runtime well under 103 s; record the number.

---

## Phase 3 — Flip the tolerance regime to measured values

Deferred until seeding is stable so the two changes are not debugged
concurrently (the earn loop admits on *vertex* tolerance, so Phase 1 did not
depend on this).

- **3.1** Add the fit-based sag estimator (per-facet centroid distance to its
  own committed fit on unambiguous regions — possible now that commits are
  trustworthy) and cross-check both estimators against reference truth across
  the full Phase-0 corpus including OCCT/Fusion/external pairs. **Stop and
  ask** on >5× disagreement anywhere.
- **3.2** Flip the `--surface-tolerance` default from 0.4 mm to the estimate
  (high quantile + safety margin — **never a median**; exporters also bind
  angular/min-width constraints, so legitimate facets sit above the median).
  Audit every dependent before flipping: `REFIT_GIVE_UP` (8×stol), merge's
  centroid gate, `face_validates`. Full harness sweep before/after; every
  regression explained or the flip reverted. The flag remains a user
  override; effective value = estimator unless overridden.
- **3.3** Angular tolerance from the dihedral gap where a clean gap exists;
  fall back to the current default otherwise, and *report which path was
  taken*. **Stop and ask** if no clean gap on more than 2 corpus models.
- **3.4** Document in README: recentring before export improves precision
  (quantum grows with |p|); decimated/repaired meshes violate the provenance
  premise and are detected, not silently mangled.

---

## Phase 4 — Ablation harvest and consolidation

- **4.1** Re-baseline the sweep harness and fragility meter under the new
  seeding + tolerance regime.
- **4.2** One candidate at a time, the standard protocol (disable → probe →
  suite → harness → delete-or-keep), in this order: `promote_bend` + `BEND_*`
  (if 1.3 landed); `rescue_with_neighbour_axes` (d2) and
  `rescue_leftover_components` (d) — earned patches may end the "never handed
  a clean face set" problem they exist for; `MAX_TORUS_STARTS`;
  `MAX_GROW_ROUNDS`; `MERGE_MAX_SMALL`; `SMALL_SELECTION_ABSORB_FACES`;
  `MIN_CYLINDER/SPHERE/TORUS_FACES`; then the degeneracy guards
  (`MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG`, `MAX_TORUS_RADIUS_RATIO`) — **expect these to still
  fire; firing means keep, not tune**. Finally ask whether the jet is needed
  beyond `region_is_developable` rung ordering.
- **4.3** `snap_boundaries` keep/delete: re-run its ablation and bring the
  numbers to the user (it is inert today but is the per-face assignment
  criterion a future VSA needs, and `dump_regions locus` shares the module —
  this is the user's call, flagged since 2026-07-28).
- **4.4** Radius-cloud diagnostic: fitted radii on stepped_block should
  tighten (was 2.9996/2.9997/3.0004, 1.0009/1.0018) now that supports are
  clean. If clouds persist, the supports still disagree — investigate that;
  never cluster, never snap to round numbers (recorded decisions).
- **4.5** Report the headline pair (constant count from 34; cliff count) in
  the phase-closing commit.

---

## Phase 5 — The research problems (each behind a measurement gate)

- **5a. Freeform fit conditioning. [parallel-ok — independent of Phases 1–4]**
  `bspline_blister`'s 926-face component fails the §2.7 pole-bound check
  ("control points 2749.5 mm outside the data bounding box"), saddle's three
  components likewise; nothing recovers and the regions fall to per-facet.
  The check is correct — fix the conditioning (Floater parameterization /
  knot placement / domain), do NOT loosen the check. Acceptance: both models
  decompose and pass their `--compare` blockers; then re-examine their
  ignored invalid-face tests (4 and 3 micro-sliver faces).
- **5b. Quantum as the unit of fit quality.** Report committed-fit residuals
  in quanta as a diagnostic (genuine ≤ ~1 q across a 7× quantum range;
  spurious ~80 q). Any use as a commit criterion is a user decision made on
  corpus measurements — bring numbers, not a patch.
- **5c. Analytic-vs-freeform model selection** (hill_with_hole's junk torus;
  the strip-vs-B-spline residue). **Hard gate**: before implementing
  anything, measure the relative-area separation across the whole corpus +
  harness (the junk torus is 0.095% of its patch; `cone_tangent_planes`'
  real cones are large fractions — and that model plus the ellipticals are
  what killed four prior rules; re-check them specifically). Bring the
  distribution to the user; only then choose a mechanism. Also add a test
  pinning `cone_tangent_planes`' currently *accidental* pass (its freeform
  rung fails as ill-conditioned; if 5a makes freeform stronger, this model is
  the canary). Afterwards: hill_with_hole's downstream stage-4.1 volume miss
  (6.96e-2 when the decomposition is right) is a separate freeform-accuracy/
  export bug — diagnose once candidacy is fixed.

---

## Phase 6 — Real-world hardening

- **6.1 Graceful degradation.** When the Phase-0 provenance detector fires
  (decimated/remeshed/faceted-by-construction input): warn precisely, run
  best-effort (freeform + per-facet), report what the data could support,
  never crash, never emit silent garbage. Exercise it on the quarantined
  external models and 3DBenchy.
- **6.2 Runtime scaling.** Measure on 100k–1M-face meshes from the external
  corpus; set and document a budget; profile-driven fixes only.
- **6.3 OpenSCAD / faceted-by-construction policy.** Generate two corpus
  models (low/high `$fn`), then implement the policy as an explicit, reported
  decision (flag or auto-detect-and-announce) per DEVELOPMENT_PLAN "Mesh
  provenance" — the prism-vs-cylinder ambiguity is genuine and cannot be
  measured away.
- **6.4** Promote backlog items as models demand (OBJ/PLY input, boundary
  crack stitching, IGES export).

---

## Reserve — partition-level architecture (user sign-off required)

If, **as measured by the harness**, Phases 1–4 leave seeding quality or sweep
cost unacceptable, the remaining lever is replacing the per-face sweep with a
partition: recursive split-and-merge (earned-patch fits at nodes,
union-revalidate merges via `fit_validate`, identifiability guards becoming
"defer, don't reject" until merge time) and/or VSA-style global alternation.
Both are deliberately reserved: they rewrite known-working machinery
(`resolve_claims`, relabel, merge) and their known hard parts (cut lines vs
seams; inverted identifiability) are documented in DEVELOPMENT_PLAN
("Considered and not adopted"). **Do not start without bringing Phase 1–4
measurements to the user.**

The parallel session sidesteps that: a strip facet's normal is *exactly* perpendicular to a cylinder's axis, so **axis = n₁×n₂ from two faces**; sphere centers via circumcenter-anchored normal-line concurrence (exact for inscribed facets); and a 4-face torus axis from meridian-plane coplanarity — closing what the breadcrumbs called "the open case," assembled from existing parts (`fit_circle_for_axis`, `fit_circle_2d`). 2. **Fit-derived distance field with feedback** instead of my dihedral-diffusion seed ordering. Its critique was correct: any field computed *before* fitting is the refuted detector in a hat. 3. **Profile-first discipline** on the runtime work — don't build the distance machinery if the 103 s turns out to live in fits or floods.

1666	## The Robustness Rework (2026-07-29)
1667	
1668	**This section is the rationale behind the phased plan in TODO.md.** TODO.md
1669	carries the step-by-step instructions; this section records why each phase is
1670	shaped the way it is, the design detail for the two new mechanisms (earned
1671	patches, distance-guided exploration), the corpus strategy, what was considered
1672	and deliberately not adopted, and the measurements preserved from the TODO
1673	items the plan retired. It synthesizes two parallel design sessions held
1674	2026-07-29 (one logged at \`agent-logs/2026-07-29_14-59_nothinking.md\`) plus the
1675	measured record above.
1676	
1677	### Goal and thesis
1678	
1679	The goal changed: **maximum robustness and minimum fragility over all plausible
1680	CAD-derived meshes**, not score on the current corpus. Fragility is
1681	operationalized as two headline numbers: the stage-2 tuned-constant count
1682	(34 at plan time; \`grep -h "^const \|^pub(crate) const \|^pub(super) const "
1683	src/stage2/*.rs | wc -l\`) and the **cliff count** — the number of constants
1684	whose ±2× perturbation collapses any model (four unrelated knobs once each
1685	flipped stepped_block medium from 83 surfaces to full per-facet collapse).
1686	
1687	The measured fragility concentrates in three structural debts, and the plan
1688	retires them in dependency order:
1689	
1690	1. **Evaluation is anecdotal.** 14 hand-watched models, Onshape/Parasolid-heavy;
1691	   three NURBS models rotted silently because nothing watched them. You cannot
1692	   claim generality you cannot measure → Phase 0 builds the instrument first.
1693	2. **Two of three tolerances are guesses.** \`--surface-tolerance\` defaults to
1694	   0.4 mm against a measured true sag of ~9e-4 mm (~400× too loose), making
1695	   centroid validation nearly vacuous; \`--angular-tolerance\` is a stand-in for
1696	   a discarded exporter setting. Both are measurable from the mesh itself
1697	   → Phases 0 (diagnostics) and 3 (regime flip).
1698	3. **One component — blind-patch seeding — forces most of the guard pile.**
1699	   \`seed_patch\`/\`condition_patch\` fit an unvalidated 32-face BFS neighbourhood;
1700	   the contamination lives on in the fit parameters, producing both the 323
1701	   NO-GROWTH seeds and plausible-but-wrong fits. Roughly two-thirds of stage
1702	   2's constants exist because tangent seams are invisible to it → Phases 1–2
1703	   replace the mechanism, Phase 4 deletes what that makes inert.
1704	
1705	Everything else measured principled — stage 1, sharp-edge regions, the DOF
1706	ladder, \`fit_validate\`, \`face_validates\`, flood, \`resolve_claims\`,
1707	relabel+refit, the locus machinery, stage 3 topological assembly, the
1708	\`--compare\` gates — **is deliberately not touched**.
1709	
1710	### Phase 1 design: earned patches (replaces the blind patch)
1711	
1712	Replace grab-then-repair with **grow-under-validation**: BFS from the seed,
1713	admitting a frontier face only if it validates against the current fit at
1714	vertex tolerance; when a face fails, attempt **promotion** up the ladder
1715	(plane → cylinder/cone or sphere → torus), refitting accepted+candidate and
1716	requiring *every already-accepted face* to still validate; if no type
1717	validates, the face is across a seam — exclude it and record it as a
1718	**frontier face** (Phase 2 consumes these). The patch can never straddle a
1719	junction by construction, which is the exact property the blind patch lacks.
1720	Commit semantics do not change: the earned (type, params, patch) goes to the
1721	unchanged \`grow_from\` flood/refit path, and every existing commit gate
1722	(\`MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG\`, torus ratio, \`MIN_*_FACES\`, \`resolve_claims\`) keeps
1723	its meaning.
1724	
1725	What makes promotion workable at tiny support — where a free least-squares fit
1726	is hopeless (sagitta arithmetic: over a 7.5° arc on r = 0.5 the sag is
1727	~0.001 mm against a 2e-5 mm quantum, so a free radius is ~2% ≈ 200× vtol
1728	wrong) — is that **facet normals are exact** and give closed-form,
1729	DOF-reducing initializers:
1730	
1731	- **Cylinder — axis = n₁ × n₂.** A planar facet spanning two rulings of a
1732	  cylinder has its normal exactly perpendicular to the axis, at any coarseness,
1733	  so two facets with non-parallel normals give the axis exactly on
1734	  strip/quad-tessellated surfaces. Radius+origin then come from
1735	  \`fit_circle_for_axis\` (cylindrical.rs), measured well-conditioned on short
1736	  arcs (r = 0.99998 / 0.99999 / 0.50008 from 65°/60°/40° arcs). **Provenance
1737	  caveat:** a general Delaunay triangle's normal is *not* exactly
1738	  perpendicular to the axis; measure axis error per provenance (Phase 0's OCCT
1739	  meshes), and degrade to the normal-covariance axis over the earned patch
1740	  where needed — still clean, still not blind.
1741	- **Sphere — concurrent normal lines.** For any planar facet inscribed in a
1742	  sphere, the line through the facet's **circumcenter** along its normal
1743	  passes exactly through the sphere centre (equidistance). Two facets → centre
1744	  at the near-intersection (common-perpendicular midpoint), radius = distance.
1745	- **Cone** — the existing normal-covariance axis (\`smallest_eigenvector_3x3\`)
1746	  over the earned patch, guarded by \`axis_normals_consistent\`, both existing.
1747	- **Torus — meridian coplanarity, the "open case" closed.** Every torus
1748	  normal line lies in the meridian plane through its point, which contains
1749	  the axis — so each facet contributes one coplanarity constraint
1750	  \`(pᵢ − a) · (nᵢ × d) = 0\` on the axis (point a, direction d; 4 DOF; the
1751	  system is bilinear — solve by alternation or pairwise elimination). Four
1752	  facets pin the axis; then (R, r) is a 2-D circle fit in (ρ, z) profile
1753	  coordinates — \`fit_circle_2d\` already exists (toroidal.rs). **Caveats:**
1754	  rank-deficient by construction on sphere data (any axis through the centre
1755	  satisfies it) and consistent-but-degenerate on cylinder data, so ladder
1756	  order and a conditioning floor must precede it; grid-aligned quads give
1757	  near-exact meridian normals, Delaunay triangles do not. **Time-boxed**: unit
1758	  test to ~1e-9 on synthetic tori before integrating; if conditioning does not
1759	  pan out, skip it — direct torus seeding stays as today and Phase 1 is not
1760	  blocked.
1761	
1762	Two behaviours need more than validation failure:
1763	
1764	- **Ambiguity → branch, don't choose.** Two same-height faces of a cylinder
1765	  validate as a sphere centred on the axis (the hole→sphere trap at patch
1766	  scale). Grow both branches; the false one should die within a face or two
1767	  (the next face at a different height is off the sphere by ≈ Δ²/2R ≫ vtol).
1768	  Instrument branch lifetime; persistent branches mean validation is less
1769	  sharp than believed — stop and ask.
1770	- **Bent tube → drift-triggered promotion.** A bend is locally a valid
1771	  cylinder (sag of the bend over a 2 mm patch at R = 14 is ~3.6e-5 mm), so
1772	  admission never fails and promotion never triggers on residual. The signal
1773	  is **systematic fit drift**: along a straight tube successive refits are
1774	  stationary; along a bend the fitted axis precesses with a consistent sign as
1775	  support accumulates. Test drift as sign-consistency of successive axis
1776	  deltas, *not* magnitude (a magnitude bar would be a new tuned constant —
1777	  stop and ask if one seems needed). Success retires \`promote_bend\` and the
1778	  \`BEND_*\` constants; failure keeps them, and that is fine.
1779	
1780	**Deleted when this lands (after ablation evidence):** \`condition_patch\`
1781	entirely, \`seed_patch\`'s jet filtering, \`SEED_PATCH_CAP\`, \`MAX_PATCH_DEPTH\`,
1782	\`PATCH_RADII\`, \`PATCH_TRIM_ROUNDS\`, \`MIN_CONDITION_FACES\`, likely
1783	\`MAX_TORUS_STARTS\` (multiple flood starts exist because the fit patch was
1784	unreliable).
1785	
1786	### Phase 2 design: distance-guided exploration
1787	
1788	The 26122-face seed sweep costs 103 s on stepped_block fine and its
1789	useful-work fraction is unknown (profile first — do not build this phase's
1790	machinery if the profile says the cost is in fits or floods rather than the
1791	sweep). The principled orderings and bounds, all derived rather than tuned:
1792	
1793	- **Distance field**: per-face geodesic distance to the region boundary
1794	  (multi-source Dijkstra over the dual graph, **centroid-gap weights in
1795	  millimetres, not hops** — hop counts lie on graded meshes, which is what
1796	  \`PATCH_RADII\` existed to patch). Seed **farthest-first** (Gonzalez maximin),
1797	  replacing \`neighbor_jet_mismatch\` — the jet-based proxy for exactly this
1798	  quantity.
1799	- **Feedback, not detection**: tangent junctions cannot be *detected* (the
1800	  measured-dead pivot; a tangent junction is locally the *smoothest* place on
1801	  the mesh — an anti-edge), but they are *discovered exactly* by Phase 1's
1802	  excluded frontier faces. Add discovered frontiers as new distance sources
1803	  incrementally. The only trustworthy edge map is the one the fits produce.
1804	- **Duplicate abort**: a seed whose reachable ball lies entirely inside one
1805	  committed surface can only refit that surface — skip it. Topological, a
1806	  strict generalization of \`interior_of_claims\`, no numeric tolerance.
1807	- **Acceptance discipline**: ordering must not change results. Bit-identical
1808	  probe output, or every diff explained; order-dependence is itself the
1809	  fragility being removed — stop and surface it.
1810	
1811	### Phase 0 design: the corpus and the instrument
1812	
1813	Three provenance sources, cheapest first, all scored against reference STEPs:
1814	
1815	1. **OCCT re-mesh of existing references** (automated, free ground truth).
1816	   \`gen_test_models\` already drives \`BRepMesh\` with deflection/angle settings
1817	   (\`write_tessellated_stl\`); add a mode that loads any reference STEP and
1818	   emits STL variants at several settings, plus **off-origin variants**
1819	   (translate the shape ~1 m before both STL and STEP output) so the float32
1820	   quantum question becomes testable. This adds constrained-Delaunay
1821	   provenance to a strip-heavy corpus.
1822	2. **Fusion 360 re-export** (user batch job): import reference STEPs, export
1823	   STL at low/medium/high. Different tessellator, same ground truth.
1824	3. **Wild STEP+STL pairs** (most representative, most care): harvest models
1825	   published with both a STEP/F3D and an STL (Thingiverse API / Printables /
1826	   GrabCAD, scripted or via a browser session). **Pair-verification gate**:
1827	   run stage 1 \`--compare\`; a pair counts as ground truth only if mesh
1828	   vertices lie on the STEP surfaces to within a few quanta — otherwise
1829	   quarantine as crash-test-only (the STL may be a different revision,
1830	   decimated, or repaired). Record the verification *rate*: it is itself the
1831	   first field measurement of the provenance premise ("vertices lie on the
1832	   true surface") in the wild. Keep licensing clean: store source URL,
1833	   author, license, and hash in a manifest; do not commit files whose license
1834	   does not permit redistribution (gitignore the external corpus, commit the
1835	   manifest).
1836	
1837	The instrument: a one-command sweep harness (per-model rows: per-type surface
1838	breakdown, \`--compare\` distances, volume error, runtime, exit status;
1839	machine-readable; saved baselines + diff mode) and a **fragility meter** that
1840	perturbs/ablates each stage-2 constant and reports which models change.
1841	
1842	### Tolerance sequencing (Phases 0 and 3)
1843	
1844	Estimators are built and *reported* in Phase 0 (they double as the
1845	provenance-violation detector: estimator disagreement or a missing dihedral
1846	gap means a decimated/remeshed/faceted-by-construction input — warn now,
1847	degrade gracefully in Phase 6). The **default flip is deferred to Phase 3**,
1848	after the seeding rework stabilizes: a 400× change to \`stol\` moves behaviour
1849	everywhere (\`REFIT_GIVE_UP\` is 8×stol; merge gates and \`face_validates\` use
1850	it), and debugging it concurrently with new seeding would confound both. The
1851	earn loop admits on *vertex* tolerance, so Phase 1 is essentially independent
1852	of the stol regime. Ablation (Phase 4) runs after the flip so deletions are
1853	judged under the final regime.
1854	
1855	### Considered and not adopted (with reasons)
1856	
1857	- **Recursive subdivision / split-and-merge as the architecture.** Strong
1858	  asymptotics (the tree visits only boundary-containing paths) and its merge
1859	  half already exists (\`fit_validate\` as union-revalidation), but: fixed
1860	  geometric cuts do not respect seams (boundaries are mesh-edge chains;
1861	  strip-shaped surfaces stay contaminated at every level until cells are
1862	  smaller than the strip), and identifiability *inverts* — a sub-node of a
1863	  real torus legitimately sweeps 5° and fits garbage parameters that validate
1864	  locally, so every sweep guard would need to become "defer, don't reject"
1865	  until merge time, a rework of commit semantics. Phases 1–2 deliver most of
1866	  its benefit at a fraction of the risk. **Held in reserve**; do not start
1867	  without Phase 1–4 measurements in hand and user sign-off.
1868	- **Precomputed junction-evidence field for seeding** (dihedral
1869	  second-difference, diffused; or any jet/dihedral edge map). Any field
1870	  computed *before* fitting is a detector prior — the refuted detector
1871	  returning in a hat. Superseded by the exact, threshold-free fit-derived
1872	  frontier field of Phase 2. (For the record, the raw idea also had a real
1873	  basis: within a tessellated surface the dihedral field is locally
1874	  consistent and *steps* at junctions — but the OCCT-Delaunay and
1875	  coarse-mesh cases erode it, and nothing needs it once frontiers exist.)
1876	- **The "bridge" formulation of type promotion** (grow under an
1877	  exactly-determined uncommittable fit until the new DOF identify). Correct
1878	  shape, but its fragile middle regime — junction faces soaking into
1879	  exactly-determined fits — is mostly obviated by the closed-form
1880	  initializers, which pin the new DOF geometrically at 2–4 faces instead of
1881	  waiting for least-squares identifiability. The earn loop keeps the bridge's
1882	  two sound rules: full-support revalidation on every accretion, and
1883	  identifiability-gated *commits*.
1884	- **VSA (the old item C)** as a planned phase. Earned patches + the existing
1885	  relabel/refit fixpoint already implement the alternation locally, and the
1886	  known-working machinery it would replace (\`resolve_claims\`, relabel, merge)
1887	  is exactly what a big rewrite puts at risk. Reserve, same gate as
1888	  subdivision. The pending \`snap_boundaries\` keep/delete decision folds into

1890	  future VSA would need, and the locus diagnostic depends on the module).
1891	- **Retuning anything to close the last corpus gaps first** (stepped fine's 4
1892	  surplus surfaces, medium's ~13). Deliberately deferred: they are boundary-
1893	  and identifiability-residue that Phases 1–4 either fix or isolate, and
1894	  chasing them now re-enters the one-model-at-a-time loop that produced the
1895	  fragility.

#!/bin/zsh
# Per-model surface-type breakdown: the acceptance corpus for stage-2 guards.
for m in \
  onshape/stepped_block_toroidal_fillets_fine onshape/stepped_block_toroidal_fillets_medium \
  onshape/rounded_cube_10_r2_fine onshape/part_rounded_cube_10_r2_coarse \
  onshape/pipe_elbow_10_medium onshape/nosecone_medium \
  onshape/pill_fine onshape/chamfered_cube_10_c1_medium \
  ccad/generated/cone_cylinder ccad/generated/filleted_cylinder ccad/generated/filleted_pipe \
  nurbs/bspline_wave nurbs/elliptical_arch nurbs/elliptical_cylinder ; do
  b=$(./target/release/dump_regions tests/$m.stl surfaces 2>/dev/null \
      | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i=="plane")p++; else if($i=="cyl")c++; else if($i=="cone")k++;
              else if($i=="sphere")s++; else if($i=="torus")t++; else if($i=="bspline")b++}
             END{printf "%d/%d/%d/%d/%d/%d", p+0,c+0,k+0,s+0,t+0,b+0}')
  printf "%-17s %s\n" "$(basename $m | cut -c1-17)" "$b"
done

use brepper::{config, stage1, stage2, stage3, stage4};

fn manifest_dir() -> String {
    env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR").to_string()
}

fn config_for_output(stl_path: &str, output_path: &str) -> config::Config {
    config::parse_config_from(["brepper", stl_path, "-o", output_path, "-q"]).unwrap()
}

fn config_for_compare(stl_path: &str, output_path: &str, step_path: &str) -> config::Config {
    let mut config = config::parse_config_from([
        "brepper", stl_path, "-o", output_path, "--compare", step_path, "-q",
    ])
    .unwrap();
    config.load_compare_step().unwrap();
    config
}

fn run_stage4(config: &config::Config) {
    let mesh = stage1::stage1(config).expect("stage1 should pass");
    let surfaces = stage2::stage2(config, mesh, None).expect("stage2 should pass");
    let brep = stage3::stage3(config, surfaces, None).expect("stage3 should pass");
    stage4::stage4(config, brep).expect("stage4 should pass");
}

// --- Basic STEP output tests ---

fn cube_step_output() {
    let dir = manifest_dir();
    let stl = format!("{dir}/tests/ccad/generated/cube.stl");
    let out = format!("{dir}/tmp/test_cube_output.step");
    let config = config_for_output(&stl, &out);
    run_stage4(&config);
    assert!(std::path::Path::new(&out).exists());
}

    Before this the eight NURBS models had stage-2 selection tests and

    regresses them is visible rather than silent.

    correct 7 are all present and exact; the surplus is a single junk torus
    of 17 faces, R=3.5101 r=2.3882, area 1.533 mm2, carved out of the

    SMALL_SELECTION_ABSORB_FACES = 16, and its r/R of 0.680 sits just under
    MAX_TORUS_RADIUS_RATIO = 0.7.

    quantity not among the four count-based candidacy rules already measured
    wrong, and one that diverges from count by orders of magnitude on a strip
    mesh. The junk torus is 0.095% of its freeform patch's area while
    cone_tangent_planes' real cones, which broke every previous rule, are a
    large fraction of theirs. TODO says to measure that separation across the
    corpus first, and to re-check cone_tangent_planes and the elliptical
    models specifically.
    
    Suite 513 passing / 9 ignored.

+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// NURBS corpus: end-to-end --compare
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+//
+// Added 2026-07-28. Before this the NURBS models had stage-2 *selection* tests
+// and nothing end to end, which is how three of the eight came to be silently

+
+macro_rules! nurbs_compare {
+    ($name:ident, $model:literal) => {

+                &format!("{dir}/tests/nurbs/{}.stl", $model),

+            run_stage4(&config);

+    };
+    ($name:ident, $model:literal, ignore = $why:literal) => {
+        #[test]

+            let config = config_for_compare(

+                &format!("{dir}/tmp/test_nurbs_{}.step", $model),
+                &format!("{dir}/tests/nurbs/{}.step", $model),

+        }

472	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
473	// NURBS corpus: end-to-end --compare
474	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
475	//
476	// Added 2026-07-28. Before this the NURBS models had stage-2 *selection* tests
477	// and nothing end to end, which is how three of the eight came to be silently
478	// broken: \`bspline_blister\` and \`bspline_saddle\` had collapsed to all-per-facet
479	// polyhedra and \`hill_with_hole\` was being shredded into 47 surfaces against a
480	// reference 7, all unnoticed because only stage 1 was checked. Every model has
481	// a reference STEP sitting next to it, so there was never a reason not to.
482	
483	macro_rules! nurbs_compare {
484	    ($name:ident, $model:literal) => {
485	        #[test]
486	        fn $name() {
487	            let dir = manifest_dir();
488	            let config = config_for_compare(
489	                &format!("{dir}/tests/nurbs/{}.stl", $model),
490	                &format!("{dir}/tmp/test_nurbs_{}.step", $model),
491	                &format!("{dir}/tests/nurbs/{}.step", $model),

  laststage=$(grep -oE '^(Stage|  Compare) [0-9.]+' $log | tail -1)

  printf "%-38s rc=%-3s %-14s last=%-16s %s %s\n" "$name" "$rc" "$surf" "$laststage" "$v41" "$err"
done

/// Build a compound containing all solids.
fn build_solid_compound(solids: &[OwnedPtr<topo_ds::Solid>]) -> OwnedPtr<topo_ds::Compound> {
    let builder = topo_ds::Builder::new();
    let mut compound = topo_ds::Compound::new();
    builder.make_compound(&mut compound);
    for solid in solids {
        builder.add(compound.as_shape_mut(), solid.as_shape());
    }
    compound
}

/// Compare the (already re-read) written STEP against the reference STEP
/// shape. \`output_shape\`/\`output_vol\` come from \`verify_output\`, which read
/// the file once for both the round-trip self-check and this comparison.
fn compare_output_to_step(
    output_shape: &topo_ds::Shape,
    output_vol: f64,
    config: &Config,
) -> Result<(), Stage4CompareError> {
    let compare_shape = config.compare_shape.as_ref().unwrap();

    // Compare volumes
    let ref_vol = compute_volume(compare_shape);
    let rel_diff = if ref_vol > 0.0 {
        (output_vol - ref_vol).abs() / ref_vol
    } else {
        0.0
    };

    if !config.quiet {
        eprintln!(
            "  Compare 4.1: output volume {output_vol:.6} mm\u{00b3} vs STEP {ref_vol:.6} mm\u{00b3} (rel diff {rel_diff:.2e})",
        );
    }

    if rel_diff > 0.01 {
        eprintln!(
            "  Compare 4.1: ERROR volume differs by {rel_diff:.2e} (>1%)",
        );
        return Err(Stage4CompareError::Volume { rel_diff });
    }

    // Compute BRepExtrema distance between output and reference
    let progress = message::ProgressRange::new();
    let dist_calc = b_rep_extrema::DistShapeShape::new_shape2_extflag_extalgo_progressrange(
        output_shape,
        compare_shape,
        0,
        extrema::ExtAlgo::Grad,
        &progress,
    );
    if dist_calc.is_done() && dist_calc.nb_solution() > 0 {
        let dist = dist_calc.value();
        if !config.quiet {
            eprintln!("  Compare 4.1: output distance to STEP = {dist:.6e} mm");
        }
        if dist > config.surface_tolerance_mm {
            return Err(Stage4CompareError::Distance {
                max_distance: dist,
                tolerance: config.surface_tolerance_mm,
            });
        }
    }

    Ok(())
}

fn compute_volume(shape: &topo_ds::Shape) -> f64 {
    let mut gprops = g_prop::GProps::new();
    b_rep_g_prop::volume_properties_shape_gprops_bool3(
        shape,
        &mut gprops,
        true, false, false,
    );
    gprops.mass().abs()
}
