705	- **1.1 Closed-form initializers, unit-tested first** **DONE 2026-07-31** —
706	  \`src/stage2/initialize.rs\`, 8 unit tests, not yet wired in (1.2 consumes it).
707	  All four are **exact on synthetic data**, far inside this step's ~1e-9 bar:
708	  cylinder axis 1e-14 / radius 1e-9 / position 1e-9 at r = 0.5, 7 and 40;
709	  sphere centre and radius 1e-9; cone axis 2.8e-14–1.9e-12, half-angle
710	  1.5e-12°–1.0e-10°, apex 3e-14–5e-13 mm across 10°–75°; torus axis 1e-9,
711	  centre 1e-6, radii 1e-6 at r/R = 0.25, 0.033 and 0.75.
712	  **Four things the step's own design had wrong, each measured:**
713	  1. **The bilinear meridian system is LINEAR in Plücker coordinates**, so no
714	     alternation or pairwise elimination is needed. With the line's moment
715	     \`m = a × d\`, \`(pᵢ − a)·(nᵢ × d) = qᵢ·d + nᵢ·m\` where \`qᵢ = pᵢ × nᵢ\` — one
716	     linear equation per facet in six unknowns. Geometrically it is just "every
717	     normal line of a surface of revolution meets the axis". It does need
718	     normalizing first (shift to the patch centroid, divide by its extent), or
719	     the length-carrying \`q\` block and the dimensionless \`n\` block differ by
720	     orders of magnitude and the null space drowns in the scale mismatch.
721	  2. **The cone cannot use that solve at all**, because a real cone
722	     tessellation is a *single ring*: a cone is ruled, one row of quads spans
723	     its whole height, every facet centroid sits at the same axial position,
724	     and their normal lines then all meet the axis at the **same point** — so
725	     any line through that point solves the system. Pinned by a test.
726	  3. **The cone cannot use the normal-covariance axis this step named either.**
727	     Over a full revolution the normal covariance has eigenvalues \`cos²α/2\`
728	     twice and \`sin²α\` once, so the axis is the smallest eigenvector only while
729	     **α < 35.26°** — a 90° countersink is 45° and the corpus's own
730	     \`cone_15x20\` is 36.87°. Over a partial arc it degrades further; measured,
731	     it fails most of a 5 half-angle × 3 arc grid. What works is exact and
732	     needs no arc: **every facet plane of a cone contains the apex** (a tangent
733	     plane along a ruling contains that ruling, and rulings meet at the apex —
734	     including the chord plane of a strip quad), so \`nᵢ·A = nᵢ·pᵢ\` pins the
735	     apex from three independent normals, and the direction and half-angle then
736	     come from the vertex directions about it.
737	  4. **A facet normal does not give the half-angle exactly.** A strip quad's
738	     chord plane leans off the tangent plane by
739	     \`n·d = sin α·cos(Δθ/2)/√(1 − sin²α sin²(Δθ/2))\`, an \`O(Δθ²/8)\` bias —
740	     predicted 1.5e-3 relative at Δθ = 0.11 rad and measured 9.985° against
741	     10.000°, the same 1.5e-3. Taking the angle from **vertices**, which lie
742	     exactly on the surface, is exact instead.
743	  **The rank test cannot do model selection, and does not try.** It was
744	  tempting to make it sharp enough to tell a torus from a sphere, since the
745	  meridian system is rank-deficient by construction on sphere data. Measured,
746	  that separation is not there: the degenerate sphere patch reads \`l1/l5\` =
747	  2.06e-6 against 9.2e-4 for the hardest genuine torus (R = 4, r = 3) — a
748	  factor of 450 with only data-dependence in between, which is rule 5's
749	  "detector needs just one threshold" trap. The floor is therefore purely
750	  numerical (1e-12 relative) and **structure does the discriminating for free**:
751	  a sphere's (ρ, z) profile is a circle centred on the axis, so its fitted major
752	  radius is ~0 and the \`minor < major\` check rejects it. That is what the step
753	  meant by "ladder order and a conditioning floor must precede it".
754	  **Selection is part of the algorithm**, per 1.0: \`select_axis_pair\` takes the

837	  spawned / died-within-2, promotions attempted/accepted, frontier faces.
838	  **From 1.0, two selection rules for the initializer, both free:**
839	  (a) *Pair the angularly MOST DISTANT admitted facets, not the newest
840	  neighbour.* The axis error is \`perpendicularity / |n₁ × n₂|\`, and adjacent
841	  facets put \`|n₁ × n₂|\` at sin(angular step) — 0.043 on a fine mesh, a ~23×
842	  amplification, worse the finer the mesh.
843	  (b) *Initialize only from RULING-ALIGNED facets.* A facet's normal is
844	  perpendicular to the axis iff two of its vertices share a ruling; **25.6% of
845	  corpus cylinder facets straddle three or more** and carry all of the
846	  perpendicularity error (aligned worst 0.0006°, straddling worst 1.0528°).
847	  The test needs no ground truth — given the candidate axis, compute the minimum
848	  angular gap between a facet's vertices — so the loop can *select* rather than
849	  hope. Quads are a 23× proxy (2.7% straddle vs 62.3% of triangles) but not a
850	  guarantee, so use the real test.
851	- **1.3 Drift-triggered cylinder→torus promotion** (time-boxed). A bend is
852	  locally a valid cylinder, so admission never fails; the signal is
853	  **sign-consistent precession** of the fitted axis across successive refits
854	  as support accumulates — not a magnitude test (if a magnitude constant
855	  seems needed, stop and ask). If it works, \`promote_bend\` + \`BEND_*\` become
856	  Phase-4 deletion candidates; if not, keep them and move on.
857	- **1.4 Validate.**
858	  - *Initializer accuracy per provenance*: **the instrument is 1.0's
859	    \`--reference-report\`, and the baseline it already produced is above.**
860	    Re-run it on the earned patches and compare against those numbers. The
861	    provenance fallback this step was written to trigger is **not needed** —
862	    OCCT Delaunay reads 0.0000° — so what to watch instead is the
863	    *conditioning* of the pairs the earn loop actually chooses: the error is
864	    \`perpendicularity / |n₁ × n₂|\`, so a loop that pairs neighbours inherits a
865	    ~23× amplification that has nothing to do with provenance. **Stop and ask**
866	    if the earned initializer underperforms the blind patch anywhere.
867	  - *Branch lifetime*: if branches persist past ~2 faces, validation is less
868	    sharp than believed — stop and ask before the cost model changes.
869	  - *NO-GROWTH count* (baseline 323 on stepped_block fine) should collapse
870	    toward zero.
871	  - *Acceptance*: probe per-type breakdowns equal-or-better corpus-wide;
872	    stepped_block fine ≥ today's 75-surface state; **stepped_block medium and
873	    part_rounded_cube coarse not worse** (the identifiability stress cases —
874	    the one place the blind patch did irreplaceable work); suite green;
875	    harness ≥ baseline.
876	- **1.5 Delete after ablation** (rule 4): \`condition_patch\`, \`seed_patch\`'s
877	  jet filtering, \`SEED_PATCH_CAP\`, \`MAX_PATCH_DEPTH\`, \`PATCH_RADII\`,
878	  \`PATCH_TRIM_ROUNDS\`, \`MIN_CONDITION_FACES\`; likely \`MAX_TORUS_STARTS\`.
879	  Report the constant count.

881	**Explicitly NOT fixed by this phase — do not chase here**: stepped fine's 4

887	## Phase 2 — Distance-guided exploration and the runtime bound
888	
889	- **2.1 Profile first.** Instrument the stepped_block fine run (103 s
890	  baseline): time in earn/patch construction vs LM fits vs floods vs
891	  \`resolve_claims\`. Report the split to the user. **Only build 2.2–2.4 if the
892	  seed sweep dominates**; otherwise apply the cheapest fix the profile names.
893	- **2.2 Distance field + farthest-first seeding.** Per-face geodesic distance
894	  to the region boundary (multi-source Dijkstra over face adjacency,
895	  **centroid-gap weights in mm, not hops** — hop counts lie on graded
896	  meshes). Order seeds farthest-first, replacing \`neighbor_jet_mismatch\`.
897	- **2.3 Duplicate abort.** Skip a seed whose reachable ball lies entirely
898	  inside one committed surface (it can only refit that surface) — the
899	  topological generalization of \`interior_of_claims\`; no numeric tolerance.
900	- **2.4 Frontier feedback** (only if the profile still warrants): add Phase
901	  1's excluded frontier faces as new distance sources incrementally — the
902	  exact tangent-junction map, discovered by fitting, never detected.
903	- **Acceptance**: results bit-identical to Phase 1's output, or every diff
904	  explained (**ordering-dependence = stop and surface it**); stepped fine
905	  runtime well under 103 s; record the number.

908	
909	## Phase 3 — Flip the tolerance regime to measured values
910	
911	Deferred until seeding is stable so the two changes are not debugged
912	concurrently (the earn loop admits on *vertex* tolerance, so Phase 1 did not
913	depend on this).
914	
915	- **3.1** Add the fit-based sag estimator (per-facet centroid distance to its
916	  own committed fit on unambiguous regions — possible now that commits are
917	  trustworthy) and cross-check both estimators against reference truth across
918	  the full Phase-0 corpus including OCCT/Fusion/external pairs. **Stop and
919	  ask** on >5× disagreement anywhere.
920	- **3.2** Flip the \`--surface-tolerance\` default from 0.4 mm to the estimate
921	  (high quantile + safety margin — **never a median**; exporters also bind
922	  angular/min-width constraints, so legitimate facets sit above the median).
923	  **Consider a PER-FACE tolerance instead of a global one** (user's proposal,
924	  2026-07-30). Measured in DEVELOPMENT_PLAN "What a tessellator actually
925	  bounds": achieved sag is \`min(chordal bound, R·(1−cos θ/2))\`, so it varies by
926	  an order of magnitude *within one model* — 0.08 of the requested deflection on
927	  a 2 mm fillet against 1.0 on a 12.5 mm sphere. Any single global value is
928	  therefore simultaneously too loose on small features and too tight on large
929	  ones. The local sag is already computable per face from the mesh alone
930	  (\`estimate.rs\`: \`θ·h/8\` from the facet's own dihedral and size), so
931	  \`tol(face) = max(f32 position bound, margin × local sag)\` needs no new
932	  measurement machinery — 0.6 supplies the floor, 0.7 the estimate.
933	  **Note the quantity is sag, not angle**: a 30° turn across a 0.05 mm facet is
934	  a tiny sag and across a 5 mm facet a large one, so the tolerance must scale
935	  with \`θ × h\`, not with θ.
936	  **This is NOT the 2026-07-27 self-calibrating tolerance that was removed.**
937	  That one scaled the bar by *each fit's own median residual* — self-referential,
938	  so a degenerate fit on a small patch loosened its own bar, and the recorded
939	  post-mortem is "the statistic measured the wrong thing". A mesh-derived local
940	  sag is independent of the fit being judged, which is the whole difference.
941	  Still needs the full Phase 3 treatment before landing: audit every dependent
942	  (\`REFIT_GIVE_UP\` is 8×stol, merge's centroid gate, \`face_validates\`), and
943	  check against the fragility meter, since four of the nine cliffs are
944	  seed-conditioning constants that a changed bar could move.
945	  **The dependent audit is DONE** (2026-07-30): all 29 uses read and classified
946	  in DEVELOPMENT_PLAN "Phase 3.2 dependent audit". Six purposes, three different
947	  length scales, and \`h/sag = 8/θ\` — so one constant provably cannot serve the
948	  two dominant uses. One use looks like a live bug rather than a tuning question:
949	  the §2.7 freeform fits are held to \`stol/8\` when their input is mesh vertices
950	  accurate to ~1e-6 mm. Full harness sweep before/after; every
951	  regression explained or the flip reverted. The flag remains a user
952	  override; effective value = estimator unless overridden.
953	- **3.3** Angular tolerance from the dihedral gap where a clean gap exists;
954	  fall back to the current default otherwise, and *report which path was
955	  taken*. **Stop and ask** if no clean gap on more than 2 corpus models.
956	- **3.4** Document in README: recentring before export improves precision
957	  (quantum grows with |p|); decimated/repaired meshes violate the provenance
958	  premise and are detected, not silently mangled.

413	parameters, refit triggers — and **never decides membership or
414	boundaries**; vertex-tolerance fit validation decides all geometry. Every
415	jet error therefore converts to wasted or saved time, never to wrong
416	output.
417	
418	**Precision note**: Mesh vertex positions, normals, and all fitted-surface
419	parameters use double-precision (\`f64\`) throughout.
420	
421	#### 2.1 Sharp edges + jet curvature prior
422	
423	Two products, both deterministic, both cheap (O(N·ring), single pass —
424	the classification fixpoint is gone; nothing iterates on classification
425	anymore).
426	
427	**(a) Sharp-edge classification — the only *decision* this stage makes.**
428	A manifold edge is BOUNDARY when its dihedral angle exceeds
429	\`--angular-tolerance\`; everything else is INTERIOR. The default 25° stays
430	above the tessellator's maximum dihedral step on smooth surfaces (coarse
431	fillets step ~24°/row). This rule is measured-exact on the corpus: every
432	sharp-edged analytic model segments perfectly by it alone (cube 6,
433	block_with_hole 7, pipe 4, two_holes 8, spherical_pocket 7,
434	chamfered_cube 26, cone_15x20 2, simple_cone 3 — one pass, no knobs
435	beyond the user-facing tolerance). The fit-free *curvature-jump* rule
436	that used to accompany it is retired (evidence in the Retrospective's
437	Resolution; autopsy in Abandoned Approaches): tangent junctions are found
438	by stage 2.3's fit competition instead.
439	
440	**(b) The jet curvature prior — data for 2.3, never a decision.** Each
441	face carries the differential summary of an **anchored osculating jet**
442	(Cazals & Pouget SGP 2005 — the standard robust curvature estimator for
443	irregular meshes): a quadratic height field \`z = Q(u,w)\` fitted to vertex
444	*positions* over a PCA tangent frame of the face's own + 1-ring vertex
445	neighborhood. Three properties make it robust to how CAD models are
446	actually triangulated (each was forced by a measured corpus failure):
447	
448	- **It uses vertex positions** — exact f32 mesh data — not normals. A long
449	  skinny strip/sliver triangle's plane is a chord whose normal can sit
450	  several degrees off the true tangent, so normal-based estimators inherit
451	  that error; positions are ground truth. The fit is tessellation-layout
452	  agnostic (aspect-ratio slivers, staggered rows, pole fans, strip meshes).
453	- **The tangent frame comes from a PCA of own + 1-ring vertices, not the
454	  facet normal** — the smallest-variance direction of the neighborhood IS
455	  the local normal and stays accurate on strips. Own vertices dominate the
456	  frame (weight \`OWN_WEIGHT\`).
457	- **The face's own vertices anchor the fit** (weight \`OWN_WEIGHT = 50\`).
458	  Tessellators never straddle a B-rep boundary with a triangle, so a face's
459	  own corners always lie on its own surface. There is **no outlier
460	  rejection** (rejection forces arbitrary one-side reads that vary face to
461	  face — measured); sharp-crease neighbors are excluded from the point set,
462	  and tangent-junction mixing is allowed — junction rows read intermediate
463	  values, which is fine because no decision ever keys on them.
464	
465	*Estimator history, for context:* per-edge κ = θ/d failed on irregular
466	tessellation (the centroid distance doesn't measure arc length in the
467	rotation direction — the 65:1 sliver fillet of rounded_cube_10_r2_fine
468	read ~100× low and fragmented ~50×). The neighbor-normal tensor fixed
469	strips and slivers but deadlocked on balanced-mix junction rings
470	(stepped_block's blend zones). The jet subsumes both — as a *measurement*;
471	as a junction *detector* the whole family is dead (see Resolution).
472	
473	**Per-face prior contents** (\`JetField\`, on \`Segmentation\`):
474	- \`(κ1, κ2)\` — signed principal curvatures (jet Hessian eigenvalues;
475	  positive convex). Few-% accurate on region interiors; contaminated on
476	  junction rows (by design — the anchor mixes).
477	- Principal directions — the Hessian's eigenvectors lifted to 3D in the
478	  PCA frame. The κ≈0 direction is a cylinder/cone ruling; the κ1
479	  direction wraps a tube.
480	- The PCA normal, and the **medial point** \`centroid + n̂/κ1\` (defined when
481	  \`|κ1|\` clears the noise floor) — a curvature-center / tube-center
482	  estimate feeding torus initialization and bent-tube promotion.
483	
484	**Type signatures the prior predicts** (used ONLY to order and prune work
485	in 2.3): plane (0,0); cylinder (κ,0), κ locally constant; cone (κ,0), κ
486	drifting along the ruling; sphere (κ,κ); torus (κ1 constant around the
487	tube, κ2 varying, sign change past the inner equator); anything else →
488	freeform-ish.
489	
490	Output: \`EdgeClassification\` (sharp classes + counts) and \`JetField\`,
491	both on \`Segmentation\`, consumed by 2.3 and by diagnostics/viz.
492	
493	#### 2.2 Smooth-region extraction
494	
495	Connected components of the face graph over INTERIOR (non-sharp) edges
496	(union-find; deterministic numbering by smallest member face index). A
497	**smooth region** is a maximal set of faces reachable without crossing a
498	sharp edge. On sharp-edged models it IS the final segmentation; on models
499	with tangency it is a *chain of tangentially-joined surfaces* that 2.3
500	decomposes — e.g. the capsule is ONE smooth region (both caps tangent to
501	the wall), a rounded cube's entire outer shell is ONE smooth region, the
502	nosecone is TWO (the cone+sphere tangent chain; the base disk), and the
503	pipe elbow's tube surface is ONE (torus bend tangent to both straight
504	pipes).
505	
506	Output (in \`Stage2Output.segmentation\`):
507	- \`face_region: Vec<usize>\` — exactly one region per face (total coverage
508	  by construction).
509	- \`regions: Vec<Region>\` — member faces + member vertices.
510	
511	Regions are connected by construction. There is no minimum size: a single
512	facet is a valid region.
513	
514	**Diagnostics** (report-only at this stage): with \`--compare\`, sample
515	midpoints of sharp BOUNDARY edges and check distance to the nearest
516	reference STEP *edge* (within \`--surface-tolerance\`); report region counts
517	vs reference face counts. Smooth-region counts are NOT expected to match
518	reference face counts on tangent models — that match is 2.3/2.4's job.
519	
520	#### 2.3 Per-region surface discovery
521	
522	Decompose each smooth region into its true surfaces. Two mechanisms, in
523	order; both decide membership exclusively by fit validation.
524	
525	**Validation (used everywhere, decisive by Design Principle #1):**
526	- Every claimed vertex within \`--vertex-tolerance\` of the surface.
527	- Every claimed face centroid within \`--surface-tolerance\` (chordal
528	  sagitta ≈ h²/8R stays well inside for real tessellations).
529	- Orientation coherence: every face normal agrees in sign with the surface
530	  normal at its centroid — this determines the hypothesis \`convex\` flag and
531	  replaces the old per-face BFS convexity checks.
532	- Numeric-validity guards retained from the fitters (fit-domain
533	  constraints, not selection heuristics): cone half-angle in [2°, 85°],
534	  torus \`0 < r ≤ R\`, sphere radius ≤ 1000× bounding-box diagonal.
535	- **Sub-tolerance features**: when the fitted curvature radius is below
536	  \`--surface-tolerance\` (3DBenchy has r=0.2mm cylinders against the 0.4mm
537	  default), centroid checks are vacuous at that scale; validate by vertex
538	  tolerance alone and mark the region (stage 3's chain validation shares
539	  the blind spot — see TODO, face-5841 family).
540	
541	**(a) Whole-region ladder.** Try to explain the ENTIRE region with one
542	surface, ascending DOF; the first fit that validates wins. Simplest-first
543	resolves degeneracy (any plane also lies on an infinite-radius cylinder; a
544	single facet is exactly a plane) without coverage heuristics.
545	
546	| Rung | Surface | DOF | Fit (see SURFACE_FITTING.md) |
547	|------|---------|-----|------------------------------|
548	| 1 | Plane | 3 | Area-weighted normal average |
549	| 2 | Sphere | 4 | Algebraic LSQ + Gauss-Newton |
550	| 3 | Cylinder | 5 | Normal-covariance axis + 2D circle fit + LM |
551	| 4 | Cone | 6 | Two-path (pointed/truncated) + LM; the existing code fits cylinder and cone together and this rung keeps that dual-fit internally, preferring the cylinder when both validate |
552	| 5 | Torus | 7 | Medial-axis tube-center + SOR axis + LM |
553	
554	The **jet signature orders and prunes the rungs** (a (κ,κ) region tries
555	sphere first; (0,0) tries plane; a failed prediction falls through to the
556	remaining rungs — a misprediction costs one cheap failed fit, never a
557	wrong region). Fits see the whole region — maximal support, which keeps
558	the strip problem dead for any region that IS one surface. For large
559	regions, fit on a deterministic vertex subsample, validate against all
560	vertices, refit augmented with the worst offenders on a near-miss
561	(bounded retries). Most regions of most models end here.
562	
563	**(b) Scoped fit competition** — for regions the ladder cannot explain
564	(tangent chains). Seed-first multi-type competition, run INSIDE the smooth
565	region; the sharp boundary cordons the arena, so competition cost is
566	bounded and cross-region accidents are impossible.
567	
568	- **Seeds**: faces not yet claimed by any committed hypothesis, in
569	  jet-interior-first order (faces whose (κ1,κ2) best match their
570	  neighbors' — the descendant of curvature-guided seed ordering;
571	  misordering costs only time). Claimed faces never seed.
572	- **Per seed**: run the surface types' fit-and-expand from that same seed
573	  (jet-pruned rung set, as in (a)) and commit the hypothesis with the
574	  **largest validated area** (simplest-DOF tiebreak — a plane ties an
575	  infinite-radius cylinder).
576	- **Growth is two phases, and only the second is validated.** *This is the
577	  as-built shape and it differs from the original design; the difference
578	  matters, so it is spelled out here rather than left to the roadmap notes.*
579	  1. **Conditioning patch** (\`seed_patch\` → \`condition_patch\`): an
580	     **unvalidated** depth-limited BFS neighbourhood of the seed —
581	     \`MAX_PATCH_DEPTH\` 3 hops, \`SEED_PATCH_CAP\` 32 faces — optionally
582	     filtered by *jet similarity* (same coarse curvature class; magnitude
583	     within 1.5×; within \`PATCH_RADII\` = 4 curvature radii of the seed).
584	     The initial fit is a least-squares fit to that patch. \`condition_patch\`
585	     then trims fit-outlier faces until the seed validates against its own
586	     patch's fit, bottoming out at a size floor.
587	  2. **Flood**: BFS from the seed accepting a face only when the current fit
588	     validates it (vertex tolerance + centroid tolerance + orientation
589	     coherence), refitting to a fixpoint.
590	- *Why not the original design.* §2.3(b) first specified that initial
591	  parameters come **analytically from the jet at the seed face** — r ≈ 1/κ1,
592	  sphere centre ≈ centroid − n̂/κ1, ruling/axis from the κ≈0 principal
593	  direction, torus tube centres from medial points. That was abandoned
594	  because the jet's *magnitude* is not trustworthy at the scale of a small
595	  fillet: adjacent facets of one exact r = 0.5 arc read κ1 = 0.023, 0.162 and
596	  2.2, i.e. radii of 43 mm, 6 mm and 0.45 mm for the same feature, so
597	  "r ≈ 1/κ1" would be wrong by 100×. Fitting a neighbourhood is robust to
598	  that — but it introduces a failure the original design could not have,
599	  since there is no patch to straddle when the parameters come from one
600	  face. See "Why stepped_block_toroidal is hard" above: on a mesh whose
601	  facet sizes vary 2000:1 the patch cannot stay on its own surface, and the
602	  jet filter that is supposed to keep it there classifies only 0.17% of that
603	  model's faces as flat.
604	- **Ordering**: jet-informed candidate ordering grows the clean core first,
605	  so refits run from well-conditioned support and junction rows arrive last,
606	  when the model is already determined.
607	- **Claims**: expansion may grow through faces claimed by earlier
608	  hypotheses — junction-row faces whose vertices genuinely lie on two
609	  surfaces end up claimed by both, which is the true ambiguity; 2.4
610	  resolves multi-claims by best fit.
611	- **Soundness** (the sub-region lemma, under exactness): an accidental fit
612	  is by definition supported on a *sub-region*; the true surface fitted
613	  from an interior seed expands — with vertex tolerance as the arbiter —
614	  to its entire true extent. When all types compete from the SAME seed,
615	  largest-validated-area selects the true surface. Cross-surface leakage
616	  is bounded to genuine junction rows: two distinct analytic surfaces
617	  agreeing to vertex tolerance over an extended patch would be
618	  near-identical. (The abandoned BFS pipeline compared hypotheses born
619	  from *different* seeds at *different* times — that is why commit order
620	  mattered there and does not matter here.)
621	
622	**(c) Growth & model promotion — the degenerate-limit growth model.**
623	Strip-tessellated curved sweeps (the pipe-elbow bend; extrusions) defeat
624	seed-local fits: a cylinder fit claims one strip and stalls, because the
625	neighboring strip sits ~R·Δφ²/2 off the fit — hundreds to thousands of
626	times vertex tolerance. The cure is growing with a model family whose
627	degenerate cases are *regular interior points* of the parameter space:
628	
629	- Parameterize the bent tube by a point on the spine, spine direction,
630	  tube radius \`r\`, spine **curvature** \`k = 1/R\`, and a bending-plane
631	  azimuth — \`k = 0\` IS the cylinder, no infinity anywhere (the
632	  Pratt/Taubin move that makes lines a regular case of circles).
633	- **Promotion trigger — jet-informed, not blanket**: when growth stalls,
634	  read the stalled frontier's jet. Tube-continuation signature (κ1 ≈ the
635	  claimed tube's 1/r, small nonzero κ2) → attempt the promotion refit,
636	  seeding \`k\` from a circle/line fit through the **medial points** of the
637	  claimed support. Incompatible signature ((0,0) plane, (κ,κ) sphere) →
638	  stop; don't spend the refit. This replaces both the old 10×
639	  \`REFIT_SKIP_MULTIPLIER\` window (far too tight for strips) and blanket
640	  chordal-proximity refitting (too expensive).
641	- **Regularization**: while support spans one strip, \`k\` is
642	  unidentifiable — ridge toward \`k = 0\`, relaxing as support grows.
643	  Exactness bounds the over-flexibility risk: flexibility cannot absorb
644	  faces of a genuinely different surface, because vertex tolerance
645	  remains the acceptance bar.
646	- Once enough arc is claimed, hand off to the full torus fitter and
647	  validate normally. **Model reduction at commit**: collapse \`k ≈ 0\`
648	  (spine deviation from straight < vertex tolerance over the claimed
649	  extent) back to a cylinder.
650	- Scope guard: a bent-tube-only generalization could lock onto a sphere's
651	  latitude band and stall (the dual pathology). The sphere rung competing
652	  from the same seed covers spheres; if band-locking is ever observed
653	  *winning* a commit, the answer is widening the promotion family (the
654	  SOR-profile / Dupin-cyclide direction in SURFACE_FITTING.md), never a
655	  mask.
656	
657	**(d) Model-conditioned jet bands** (effort gates only). With a hypothesis
658	in hand, the model PREDICTS each candidate face's (κ1,κ2) — *including
659	gradients*: a fitted cone predicts (cos α/ρ(h), 0) with ρ varying along
660	the axis, so the gradient class that broke the fit-free classifier is a
661	non-issue against a model. Generous bands (≈[⅓×, 3×] of predicted — jet
662	interiors are few-% accurate, junction rows off by up to ~half) may skip
663	hopeless refit attempts and order candidates. NEVER to reject a face that
664	vertex-validates. (This is the old pipeline's one genuinely effective
665	consistency heuristic — the |n·axis| = sin α normal-axis check — reborn
666	in curvature space with a model to condition on.)
667	
668	**Identifiability is not model selection.** Two different questions get
669	conflated when a fit looks wrong. *Model selection* asks which of several
670	candidates explains the data best, and is answered by comparing residuals and
671	coverage. *Identifiability* asks whether the data pins a parameter at all — and
672	a fit with an unpinned parameter is not a slightly-worse explanation but a free
673	variable that happened to land somewhere, which no comparison between candidates
674	can detect. The degenerate tori on \`stepped_block_toroidal\` are the case in
675	point: they report R = 20…114 mm on 0.5 mm fillets, and on their own support
676	they genuinely fit *better* than the cylinder they displace, so every
677	residual-based or coverage-based rule prefers them. What is wrong with them is
678	that their support sweeps 3–7° about the axis, which cannot determine a major
679	radius. \`MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG\` states exactly that and nothing else.
680	
681	Keep the three kinds of guard distinct when adding one, because they have
682	different justifications and different evidence:
683	
684	- *Identifiability* — the data does not determine this parameter
685	  (\`MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG\`, \`axis_normals_consistent\`).
686	- *Validity* — this surface cannot be represented or exported sanely
687	  (\`MIN/MAX_HALF_ANGLE_DEG\` bounding a cone away from a cylinder and a plane,
688	  \`MAX_TORUS_RADIUS_RATIO\` keeping a torus off its self-intersecting limit,
689	  rejecting non-finite fits).
690	- *Model selection* — which candidate wins. This is the only one that should be
691	  a comparison, and it is the one that most often gets written as a threshold
692	  when it should not be.
693	
694	### Rewriting stage 2.3(b): the blind patch is the root cause

1772

1774	admitting a frontier face only if it validates against the current fit at

1842	entirely, \`seed_patch\`'s jet filtering, \`SEED_PATCH_CAP\`, \`MAX_PATCH_DEPTH\`,
1843	\`PATCH_RADII\`, \`PATCH_TRIM_ROUNDS\`, \`MIN_CONDITION_FACES\`, likely

1847	### Reference labeling, and what it settled (Phase 1.0, 2026-07-30)
1848	
1849	\`src/reference.rs\` (\`--reference-report\`) labels every mesh face with the
1850	reference face it came from and scores the mesh against that ground truth.
1851	Step-by-step numbers are in TODO.md 1.0; what belongs here is why it exists,
1852	why it is nearly free, and the four results that change later phases.
1853	
1854	**It is a read-back, not a new computation.** Stage 1's \`--compare\` already runs
1855	\`BRepExtrema_DistShapeShape\` from every mesh face centroid to a compound of the
1856	reference's faces. That call already determines which reference face won and at
1857	what (u,v); \`min_distance_to_shape\` was returning only the distance and dropping
1858	both. \`SupportOnShape2\` hands the winner back, so ground-truth labeling of the
1859	entire mesh costs one accessor call per face that was already being computed.
1860	The alternative that was on the table — a standalone probe — would have cost far
1861	more than that and measured the wrong object: it reads raw STL triangles, where
1862	the pipeline's mesh has been repaired and quad-fused, which is why
1863	\`step_measure_tolerance\` needed a \`--quad\` flag bolted on. **The general lesson
1864	is that a measurement belongs where the computation already happens**, and the
1865	same investigation found the cost of ignoring it: \`step_measure_tolerance\` still
1866	measures against the reference *solid*, so it silently reports exactly 0 for any
1867	deviation over OCCT's hard-coded 1 µm classifier tolerance (\`aTolerance = 0.001\`
1868	in \`BRepExtrema_DistShapeShape\`'s \`SolidTreatment\`) and is correct below it —
1869	exact where the answer does not matter, zero where it does. That is the same
1870	"never measure a distance against a solid" defect fixed in the pipeline on
1871	2026-07-29, in the one place the fix did not reach. It also refines that entry:
1872	the old stage-1 centroid check was not vacuous on all convex geometry, only
1873	above 1 µm, which is exactly why correct models looked right and nobody noticed.
1874	
1875	**1. The closed-form axis error is \`perpendicularity error / |n₁ × n₂|\`.**
1876	Verified to 0.1% on \`pipe_elbow_10\` Parasolid medium: a perpendicularity max of
1877	0.0280° over a conditioning p50 of 0.0271 predicts 1.033°, and the measured
1878	error is 1.0342°, identical across all 348 pairs. One relation explains every
1879	cylinder outlier in the sweep, and it separates two causes that a raw error
1880	number confounds — normals that are not perpendicular, and perfect normals
1881	amplified by an ill-conditioned cross product.
1882	
1883	**2. The Delaunay caveat did not reproduce, and the reason is architectural.**
1884	The Phase 1 design warned that "a general Delaunay triangle's normal is not
1885	exactly perpendicular to the axis" and told 1.4 to degrade that provenance to a
1886	covariance axis. Measured, OCCT's re-meshes read perpendicularity p50 = p95 =
1887	**0.0000°** and axis error **0.0000°** at every density on five of six models.
1888	The reason is already recorded under "Mesh provenance and the seam assumption":
1889	OCCT's Delaunay is *constrained* by the pre-discretized face boundaries, so a
1890	cylinder's triangles still span two rulings and their normals are still exactly
1891	perpendicular. The provenance fallback is not needed. The single genuine
1892	non-perpendicular case corpus-wide is \`l_bracket_simple\` Fusion medium
1893	(perpendicularity p50 0.2740°), a small hole carrying 96 facets over 75 mm².
1894	
1895	**3. Adjacent facets are the worst possible pairing, and finer meshes are
1896	worse.** \`|n₁ × n₂|\` for an adjacent pair is \`sin(angular step)\` — measured p50
1897	0.0432 on stepped_block fine, which is sin(2.48°) and independently recovers
1898	Onshape's 2.5° setting. So the amplification in (1) is ~23× on a fine mesh and
1899	grows as the mesh refines. This inverts the natural assumption that a denser
1900	mesh gives a better closed-form fit, and it is a design constraint on Phase 1.2
1901	rather than a property of any exporter: **pair the seed with the angularly most
1902	distant admitted facet**, where the factor is 1 and the axis error falls to the
1903	perpendicularity error itself (under 0.032° everywhere in the corpus). A 90°
1904	reading, which is the max on three rows, is the fully degenerate pair of two
1905	facets on one ruling strip — no information rather than a wrong answer.
1906	
1907	**4. The torus initializer should not be skipped.** Phase 1.1 time-boxes it on
1908	the suspicion that the meridian-coplanarity system is too ill-conditioned to
1909	solve. Its residual — the quantity the solve drives to zero — measures p50
1910	**2.354e-5 mm** over 23 863 torus facets on stepped_block fine, which is the
1911	mesh's own float32 quantum. The constraint is satisfied to the limit of what the
1912	mesh can express.
1913	
1914	**The seam assumption now has a direct measurement, and it holds.** Phase 0.5b
1915	measured only half of Design Principle #2 — that mesh *vertices* lie on the
1916	reference surfaces. The other half, that a *facet* never straddles a face
1917	boundary, is what the earned patch depends on and had never been measured.
1918	Labeling gives it for free: 51 of 157 483 facets across 79 meshes disagree about
1919	their own label across their own interior, **0.032%**. The number is an estimate
1920	rather than a bound in either direction — it over-reports where a neighbouring
1921	face curves back within reach of a sample point, and under-reports a straddle
1922	confined to a facet's rim, since the samples cover the middle of a facet — but
1923	both error terms are bounded by something this small, so the conclusion survives
1924	the imprecision even though the count does not. The only recurring cluster is
1925	exactly 12 facets on \`stepped_block_toroidal\` under OCCT coarse/medium and
1926	Fusion medium/fine, absent under Parasolid and under OCCT fine; consistent with
1927	coarse facets spanning that model's known narrow flat regions, and not chased.
1928	
1929	**Segmentation scoring closes the over-segmentation hole**, which this document
1930	recorded as needing its own step. Two area-weighted, threshold-free numbers from
1931	the same labels: \`ref coverage\` = \`Σ_R max_S area(R,S) / Σ area\` is 1.0 when no
1932	reference face was split across several of our surfaces, and \`surf purity\` =
1933	\`Σ_S max_R area(S,R) / Σ area\` is 1.0 when none of our surfaces spans several
1934	reference faces. They separate the two failure directions that "over-segmented"
1935	was being used for loosely. On the case that motivated it — \`rand_filleted_box_0\`,
1936	9 surfaces against a reference 26, passing every existing gate at 6.7e-3
1937	relative volume — they read **1.0000 and 0.2201**, correctly diagnosing merging
1938	rather than splitting, where a correct model reads 1.0000/1.0000. This satisfies
1939	the standing rule about metrics: asked what it returns for a grossly wrong
1940	input, it returns something unmistakably different from a right one.
1941	
1942	**Freeform reference faces, and the property that actually governs facet-normal
1943	exactness.** The normal report initially covered only analytic reference faces,
1944	which is 32–66% of a NURBS model's area — the rest was announced as unmeasured
1945	by the \`analytic area\` figure but not scored. Extending it needed only the
1946	footpoint (u,v) that \`ParOnFaceS2\` already reports from the same distance query,
1947	plus \`GeomLProp_SLProps\` (which arrived in the bindings on 2026-07-30).
1948	\`SLProps\` is used rather than a raw \`D1U × D1V\` because it answers
1949	\`IsNormalDefined\`, and a B-spline face has poles and seams where the normal
1950	genuinely does not exist; those facets are excluded rather than scored as an
1951	error of some size. Over the 8-model NURBS corpus every freeform facet evaluated
1952	and none landed on a pole.
1953	
1954	The result is not the obvious one. Freeform facet normals are 2–3 orders of
1955	magnitude less exact than analytic ones — \`bspline_terrain\` p50 0.9396°,
1956	\`hill_with_hole\` 0.9014°, against 0.0000° for planes — but that comparison is
1957	confounded, because the corpus's freeform models are ~100× coarser per facet.
1958	Ruledness separates them better: **\`bspline_wave\`'s *extrusion* faces read p50
1959	0.0507° at 16.7 mm² per facet, while \`bspline_terrain\`'s B-spline faces read
1960	0.9396° at 0.53 mm² per facet — the 30× coarser surface is 19× more exact.**
1961	
1962	**But ruledness is necessary, not sufficient — the real condition is that the
1963	tessellation be ruling-ALIGNED.** (Raised by the user, then measured; an earlier
1964	version of this section claimed ruledness governs, which is wrong.) The exact
1965	statement: a facet on a cylinder has its normal perpendicular to the axis **iff
1966	two of its vertices share a ruling**. Parametrize the cylinder and project the
1967	vertices along the axis; they land on a circle, the facet's plane is parallel to
1968	the axis iff those projections are collinear, and three points on a circle are
1969	collinear only when two coincide. A tessellator that lays triangles *across* the
1970	ruling family therefore produces skewed normals on a geometrically perfect
1971	cylinder.
1972	
1973	Measured over the 12 cylinder-bearing models, 12 275 cylinder facets: facets
1974	with an edge on a ruling are perpendicular to a worst case of **0.0006°**, while
1975	the **25.6%** that straddle three or more rulings reach **1.0528°**. Every
1976	non-zero perpendicularity in the corpus comes from a straddling facet, so
1977	alignment is the whole story — though straddling is necessary rather than
1978	sufficient for a *large* error, since the tilt grows with a facet's angular
1979	spread and shrinks with its axial one. That also explains the extrusion number
1980	above: 0.0507° rather than 0.0000° is itself evidence that those facets are not
1981	aligned, because alignment would force exactness.
1982	
1983	Where alignment comes from: quad fusion is a **23× discriminator but not a
1984	guarantee** — 2.7% of fused quads straddle against 62.3% of triangles (a
1985	coplanar quad on a cylinder *usually* spans two rulings, but four points on an
1986	elliptical section are coplanar too). Simple geometry gets alignment for free —
1987	a plain cylinder under OCCT is 120 quads / 0 triangles, 100% aligned, which is
1988	the real reason result (2)'s OCCT re-meshes read 0.0000°, sharper than "the
1989	rulings survive as face boundaries". Straddling concentrates where a tessellator
1990	cannot lay a clean strip: \`stepped_block_toroidal\` straddles 49–53% at every
1991	OCCT density, and its narrow flat regions between fillets are exactly its known
1992	pathology.
1993	
1994	This is *better* news for Phase 1.2 than the aggregate suggested, because the
1995	test needs no ground truth. Given a candidate axis, the minimum angular gap
1996	between a facet's vertices says whether that facet's normal can be trusted, so
1997	the earn loop can **select** the facets it initializes from rather than hoping.
1998	With the amplification law, the rule becomes: pair two **ruling-aligned** facets
1999	that are **angularly distant**. For Phase 5's freeform work the consequence is
2000	unchanged — facet normals cannot be assumed reliable on a doubly-curved patch at
2001	any density, since there are no rulings to align to.
2002	
2003	**A numerical fact worth not rediscovering.** An angle assertion near 0° cannot
2004	be tightened past about 1e-6°, because it goes through \`acos\`, which near an
2005	argument of 1 turns a 1e-16 rounding error into ~1.5e-8 rad. Assert on
2006	\`|â × b̂|\` instead, which is linear in the error and resolves to machine epsilon.
2007	Measured, not theorized: an exactly-constructed strip cylinder failed a 1e-9°
2008	perpendicularity assertion at one sample out of sixteen, and the same property
2009	passes at 1e-15 in cross-product form. The reported angles in \`reference.rs\` are
2010	printed to four decimals of a degree, far above that floor, so the report is
2011	unaffected — but do not read exactness below ~1e-6° out of a number from \`acos\`.
2012	
2013	### Phase 1.1 as built: what the closed-form initializers actually needed
2014	
2015	All four initializers are exact on synthetic data (numbers in TODO.md 1.1), but
2016	three of the four constructions the Phase 1 design named turned out to be wrong,
2017	and the reasons generalize past this step.
2018	
2019	**The bilinear system was an artefact of the coordinates.** The design records
2020	the torus axis constraint \`(pᵢ − a)·(nᵢ × d) = 0\` as bilinear in the axis point
2021	and direction, to be solved "by alternation or pairwise elimination". Writing the
2022	axis as a *line* rather than a point-plus-direction removes the bilinearity
2023	outright: with the moment \`m = a × d\`, the constraint becomes \`qᵢ·d + nᵢ·m = 0\`
2024	where \`qᵢ = pᵢ × nᵢ\` — one linear equation per facet in six unknowns, solved as a
2025	null space with no iteration and no starting guess. The identity underneath is
2026	"every normal line of a surface of revolution meets the axis". The one caveat is

2026	"every normal line of a surface of revolution meets the axis". The one caveat is
2027	scaling: the \`q\` block carries length units and the \`n\` block does not, so the
2028	system must be normalized to the patch's own centroid and extent first or the
2029	null space is lost in the scale mismatch rather than in the data.
2030	
2031	**A cone is not a surface of revolution as far as this solve is concerned.** The
2032	same normal-line construction is *rank-deficient on a single ring of cone
2033	facets*, and a single ring is exactly what a real cone tessellation is: a cone is
2034	ruled, so one row of quads spans its entire height, every facet centroid sits at
2035	the same axial position, and their normal lines then all meet the axis at the
2036	same point. Any line through that point satisfies the system. On a torus the
2037	meeting point slides with the tube angle, which is why the identical solve is
2038	well posed there. The lesson is that "surface of revolution" is not the property
2039	that makes the solve work — *variation in where the normal lines cross the axis*
2040	is.
2041	
2042	**The normal-covariance cone axis has a regime the plan did not account for.**
2043	A cone's normals lie on a cone of the same half-angle about the axis, so over a
2044	full revolution the covariance has eigenvalues \`cos²α/2\` (twice) and \`sin²α\`
2045	(once), and the axis is the smallest eigenvector only while **α < 35.26°**. That
2046	is not exotic: a 90° countersink is 45°, and the corpus's own \`cone_15x20\` is
2047	36.87°. Over the partial arc an earned patch actually has, the perpendicular
2048	spread is not isotropic either and it degrades before that. What replaces it is
2049	both exact and arc-free: **every facet plane of a cone contains the apex**,
2050	because a tangent plane along a ruling contains that ruling and all rulings meet
2051	at the apex — and this holds for the chord plane of a strip quad too, since two
2052	rulings still meet there. So \`nᵢ·A = nᵢ·pᵢ\` pins the apex from three independent
2053	normals, whatever the tessellation, and direction and half-angle follow from the
2054	vertex directions about it.
2055	
2056	**Facet normals are exact for directions and biased for angles.** The
2057	perpendicularity result from Phase 1.0 says a ruling-aligned facet normal is
2058	*exactly* perpendicular to the axis. It does not say the normal equals the
2059	tangent-plane normal: a strip quad's chord plane leans off it by
2060	\`n·d = sin α·cos(Δθ/2)/√(1 − sin²α sin²(Δθ/2))\`, an \`O(Δθ²/8)\` bias. Predicted
2061	1.5e-3 relative at Δθ = 0.11 rad, and the half-angle measured 9.985° against a
2062	true 10.000° — the same 1.5e-3. Vertices carry no such bias because they lie on
2063	the surface exactly, so wherever a quantity can be taken from vertices rather
2064	than from normals, it should be.
2065	
2066	**The conditioning floor is not a model selector, and the attempt to make it one
2067	was the familiar trap.** The meridian system is rank-deficient by construction on
2068	sphere data, so it was tempting to threshold the spectrum tightly enough to
2069	reject a sphere. Measured, the separation is not available: the degenerate sphere
2070	patch reads \`l1/l5\` = 2.06e-6 and the hardest genuine torus (R = 4, r = 3) reads
2071	9.2e-4, a factor of 450 with nothing but data-dependence between them — TODO
2072	rule 5's "detector needs just one threshold" reached from yet another direction.
2073	The floor stayed purely numerical, and *structure* does the discrimination for
2074	free: a sphere's (ρ, z) profile is a circle centred on the axis, so its fitted
2075	major radius comes out ~0 and the \`minor < major\` check rejects it outright. This
2076	is what the design meant by "ladder order and a conditioning floor must precede
2077	it" — type discrimination belongs to the ladder and to validation, never to a
2078	conditioning guard.

2080	### Phase 1.2 as attempted: why the blind patch is load-bearing
2081	
2082	Phase 1.2 was to replace \`seed_patch\` + \`condition_patch\` with a patch grown
2083	under validation. It was implemented, measured over five rounds, and **not
2084	landed** (branch \`phase-1.2-earn-loop-attempt\`). Step-by-step numbers are in
2085	TODO.md 1.2. What belongs here is the shape of the result, because it revises
2086	the phase thesis rather than merely reporting a bug.
2087	
2088	**The thesis.** "Replace grab-then-repair with grow-under-validation … The patch
2089	can never straddle a junction by construction, which is the exact property the
2090	blind patch lacks." The closed-form initializers were what made this look
2091	possible: fit exactly from a handful of facets, so validation can gate growth
2092	from the first face.
2093	
2094	**What happened.** Each round removed one piece of the blind machinery and
2095	measured the consequence; each consequence was a mechanism the previous round
2096	had not predicted.
2097	
2098	1. *Validated-only growth starves.* A cone cannot be fitted from the two facets
2099	   a validated loop has when it must first decide, so it never grows. The blind
2100	   patch was solving a real chicken-and-egg: a fit needs support, and support
2101	   needs a fit.
2102	2. *Breadth-first collection is actively wrong on a developable.* A cone's
2103	   tangent plane is **constant along a ruling**, so a plane fitted to one facet
2104	   explains its neighbours up that ruling to ~5e-7 mm — well inside \`vtol\`. BFS
2105	   therefore walks the ruling, accepting coplanar facet after coplanar facet,
2106	   and produces a flat strip whose centred normal covariance is rank 0. No
2107	   curved surface can be initialized from it, ever. The loop was systematically
2108	   collecting the faces carrying no curvature information and rejecting the ones
2109	   that carried it.
2110	3. *Spread-first collection straddles junctions.* Fixing (2) by preferring the
2111	   candidate that most increases \`|n₁ × n₂|\` inverts the failure: "most
2112	   different normal" is a fair description of *a face on the neighbouring
2113	   surface*. Measured, it split every fillet of \`rounded_cube_offset_occt_medium\`
2114	   (12 cylinders → 24) and invented two spheres on
2115	   \`cone_tangent_planes_occt_medium\`. **Two different questions had been
2116	   conflated**: which faces to *collect* wants similarity, which faces to
2117	   *initialize from* wants spread. The blind patch had the first right and the
2118	   second wrong; the earn loop had the second right and the first backwards.
2119	4. *Curvature similarity is not sufficient either.* It is the right signal —
2120	   curvature distinguishes surfaces, normal direction does not — but on a
2121	   rounded cube the fillet radius **equals** the corner-sphere radius, so it
2122	   does not separate them.
2123	5. *Validation must trim, not filter.* Clearing a patch when the seed fails its
2124	   own fit cost everything: **747 of 762** earn calls returned a bare seed.
2125	   Dropping the farthest face and refitting — \`condition_patch\`'s reasoning,
2126	   that an unfittable collection is unfittable *because* its far end is on
2127	   another surface — recovered it.
2128	
2129	**The result.** The best-performing form is: collect jet-similar, walk the DOF
2130	ladder, keep the connected component the fit explains, trimming toward the seed
2131	when the seed fails. That is \`seed_patch\` + \`condition_patch\` with a ladder
2132	choice added. **The design converged back onto what it set out to replace**, and
2133	the honest reading is that the blind patch and its conditioning are doing
2134	necessary work rather than papering over a defect.
2135	
2136	Two consequences outlive the step:
2137	
2138	- **Phase 1.5's deletion list is not supported.** \`seed_patch\`,
2139	  \`condition_patch\`, \`PATCH_TRIM_ROUNDS\` and \`MIN_CONDITION_FACES\` are
2140	  load-bearing. The four fragility cliffs among them are the price of the
2141	  fit/support chicken-and-egg, not of arbitrary tuning, and deleting them on
2142	  Phase 1's authority alone would regress the corpus.
2143	- **Closed-form initializers seed least squares; they do not replace it.** The
2144	  half-angle read from facet normals inherits the \`O(Δθ²/8)\` chord-plane bias —
2145	  0.93% at a 15.65° step, ~200× \`vtol\`. Only quantities read from *vertices*
2146	  reach the validation bar, because vertices lie on the surface exactly and
2147	  facet planes do not. The cone worked only once the closed form was used to
2148	  seed \`ConicalSurface::fit_surface\` rather than to stand in for it. This is the
2149	  same lesson as Phase 1.1's "take angles from vertices, not normals", arriving
2150	  with a price attached.
2151	
2152	**What did work**, and is worth carrying into any redesign: for plane, cylinder,
2153	sphere and torus the earned patch reproduced the existing decomposition
2154	byte-identically; and **planes must keep the blind patch outright**, because an
2155	earned plane patch is by construction "the faces that validate a plane", so a
2156	single-facet plane always succeeds, is committed, and starves the 2.3(e)
2157	B-spline fallback of the coherent leftover region it needs (the NURBS models
2158	collapsed to 94/51/83 per-facet planes with no B-spline at all).

2160	### Phase 2 design: distance-guided exploration
2161	
2162	The 26122-face seed sweep costs 103 s on stepped_block fine and its
2163	useful-work fraction is unknown (profile first — do not build this phase's
2164	machinery if the profile says the cost is in fits or floods rather than the
2165	sweep). The principled orderings and bounds, all derived rather than tuned:
2166	
2167	- **Distance field**: per-face geodesic distance to the region boundary
2168	  (multi-source Dijkstra over the dual graph, **centroid-gap weights in
2169	  millimetres, not hops** — hop counts lie on graded meshes, which is what
2170	  \`PATCH_RADII\` existed to patch). Seed **farthest-first** (Gonzalez maximin),
2171	  replacing \`neighbor_jet_mismatch\` — the jet-based proxy for exactly this
2172	  quantity.
2173	- **Feedback, not detection**: tangent junctions cannot be *detected* (the
2174	  measured-dead pivot; a tangent junction is locally the *smoothest* place on
2175	  the mesh — an anti-edge), but they are *discovered exactly* by Phase 1's
2176	  excluded frontier faces. Add discovered frontiers as new distance sources
2177	  incrementally. The only trustworthy edge map is the one the fits produce.
2178	- **Duplicate abort**: a seed whose reachable ball lies entirely inside one
2179	  committed surface can only refit that surface — skip it. Topological, a
2180	  strict generalization of \`interior_of_claims\`, no numeric tolerance.
2181	- **Acceptance discipline**: ordering must not change results. Bit-identical
2182	  probe output, or every diff explained; order-dependence is itself the
2183	  fragility being removed — stop and surface it.

2185	### Phase 0 design: the corpus and the instrument
2186	
2187	Three provenance sources, cheapest first, all scored against reference STEPs:
2188	
2189	1. **OCCT re-mesh of existing references** (automated, free ground truth).
2190	   \`gen_test_models\` already drives \`BRepMesh\` with deflection/angle settings
2191	   (\`write_tessellated_stl\`); add a mode that loads any reference STEP and
2192	   emits STL variants at several settings, plus **off-origin variants**
2193	   (translate the shape ~1 m before both STL and STEP output) so the float32
2194	   quantum question becomes testable. This adds constrained-Delaunay
2195	   provenance to a strip-heavy corpus.
2196	2. **Fusion 360 re-export** (user batch job): import reference STEPs, export
2197	   STL at low/medium/high. Different tessellator, same ground truth.
2198	3. **Wild STEP+STL pairs** (most representative, most care): harvest models
2199	   published with both a STEP/F3D and an STL (Thingiverse API / Printables /
2200	   GrabCAD, scripted or via a browser session). **Pair-verification gate**:
2201	   run stage 1 \`--compare\`; a pair counts as ground truth only if mesh
2202	   vertices lie on the STEP surfaces to within a few quanta — otherwise
2203	   quarantine as crash-test-only (the STL may be a different revision,
2204	   decimated, or repaired). Record the verification *rate*: it is itself the
2205	   first field measurement of the provenance premise ("vertices lie on the
2206	   true surface") in the wild. Keep licensing clean: store source URL,
2207	   author, license, and hash in a manifest; do not commit files whose license
2208	   does not permit redistribution (gitignore the external corpus, commit the
2209	   manifest).
2210	
2211	The instrument: a one-command sweep harness (per-model rows: per-type surface
2212	breakdown, \`--compare\` distances, volume error, runtime, exit status;
2213	machine-readable; saved baselines + diff mode) and a **fragility meter** that
2214	perturbs/ablates each stage-2 constant and reports which models change.

2217

220	/// Decompose a tangent-chain region. Returns the committed analytic
221	/// hypotheses (a strict partition after claim resolution) plus the leftover
222	/// faces no hypothesis explained.
223	pub(super) fn compete_region(
224	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
225	    region: &Region,
226	    jet: &[JetField],
227	    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
228	    config: &Config,
229	) -> (Vec<CompeteHyp>, Vec<usize>) {
230	    let n = mesh.faces.len();
231	    let debug = config.verbosity >= 3 || std::env::var("BREPPER_DEBUG_COMPETE").is_ok();
232	    let mut in_region = vec![false; n];
233	    for &fi in &region.faces {
234	        in_region[fi] = true;
235	    }
236	
237	    // Region curvature scale: a face reads "flat" when its principal
238	    // curvature radius exceeds a couple of region diameters.
239	    let extent = region_extent(mesh, region);
240	    let flat_eps = if extent > 0.0 { 1.0 / (2.0 * extent) } else { 1e-6 };
241	
242	    // Seed order: jet-interior-first (ascending curvature mismatch with
243	    // region neighbors), ties by face index for determinism.
244	    let mut seeds = region.faces.clone();
245	    let score: Vec<f64> = (0..n)
246	        .map(|fi| {
247	            if !in_region[fi] {
248	                return f64::INFINITY;
249	            }
250	            neighbor_jet_mismatch(mesh, fi, jet, &in_region)
251	        })
252	        .collect();
253	    seeds.sort_by(|&a, &b| {
254	        score[a]
255	            .partial_cmp(&score[b])
256	            .unwrap()
257	            .then_with(|| a.cmp(&b))
258	    });
259	
260	    // Every region face seeds exactly once — \`seeds\` is a permutation of them,
261	    // which is what terminates the loop. Committing a hypothesis does NOT
262	    // remove the faces it grew into from the seed pool.
263	    //
264	    // Growing into a face is a hypothesis, not a conclusion. The committed
265	    // face set is always a \`flood\` output, so every member validates — but
266	    // against a fit whose parameters came from an unvalidated seed
267	    // neighbourhood, so "validated" does not mean "the right surface". Letting
268	    // those faces seed too means a wrong hypothesis can be out-competed by a
269	    // right one grown from a face it had swallowed; \`resolve_claims\` already
270	    // exists to arbitrate the multi-claims that produces.
271	    //
272	    // It also makes the long-standing claim that seed misordering "costs only
273	    // time" actually true: previously an early bad hypothesis consumed faces a
274	    // later, better seed needed.
275	    let mut committed: Vec<CompeteHyp> = Vec::new();
276	    let mut claim_lists: Vec<Vec<usize>> = vec![Vec::new(); n]; // face -> committed idxs
277	    let mut claimed = vec![false; n];
278	
279	    for &seed in &seeds {
280	        // Skip only faces in the INTERIOR of what is already explained: every
281	        // neighbour claimed too. Seeding there cannot produce a competitor —
282	        // a fit grown from the middle of a validated surface refits that same
283	        // surface — so it is pure cost. Faces at the margin still seed.
284	        if claimed[seed] && interior_of_claims(mesh, seed, &claimed) {
285	            continue;
286	        }
287	        let jf = jet[seed];
288	        // Dominant / secondary principal-curvature MAGNITUDES. The jet orders
289	        // k1 ≥ k2 by signed value, so for a concave feature (a hole wall,
290	        // κ = −1/r) the dominant curvature is negative and lands in k2 —
291	        // taking |k1| as the dominant would read the wall's flat axial
292	        // direction and treat the hole as planar. Order by magnitude instead.
293	        let a1 = jf.k1.abs().max(jf.k2.abs());
294	        let a2 = jf.k1.abs().min(jf.k2.abs());
295	
296	        // Grow the jet-pruned candidate types; keep the largest validated
297	        // area (simplest-DOF tiebreak).
298	        let mut best: Option<(CompeteHyp, f64, u8)> = None; // (hyp, area, dof)
299	        let consider = |hyp_area: Option<(CompeteHyp, f64)>, dof: u8, best: &mut Option<(CompeteHyp, f64, u8)>| {
300	            if let Some((h, area)) = hyp_area {
301	                let sweep = candidate_sweep(mesh, &h);
302	                if sweep < MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG.to_radians() {
303	                    if debug {
304	                        eprintln!(
305	                            "    compete: seed {seed} rejected {} sweeping only {:.1}\u{00b0} about its axis — radius undetermined ({} faces, area {area:.2})",
306	                            h.kind_name(),
307	                            sweep.to_degrees(),
308	                            h.faces().len(),
309	                        );
310	                    }
311	                    return;
312	                }
313	                let better = match best {
314	                    None => true,
315	                    Some((_, ba, bd)) => area > *ba + 1e-9 || ((area - *ba).abs() <= 1e-9 && dof < *bd),
316	                };
317	                if better {
318	                    *best = Some((h, area, dof));
319	                }
320	            }
321	        };
322	
323	        // Plane is always a candidate (cheap; catches misread flats).
324	        let plane = grow::<PlanarSurface>(mesh, &in_region, seed, jet, centroids, config, 1);
325	        let mut cone_area = None;
326	        let mut sphere_area = None;
327	        let mut torus_area = None;
328	        if a1 >= flat_eps {
329	            // Curved: a developable (cylinder/cone) is always plausible.
330	            let cone = grow::<ConicalSurface>(mesh, &in_region, seed, jet, centroids, config, MIN_CYLINDER_FACES);
331	            cone_area = cone.as_ref().map(|(_, a, f)| (*a, f.len()));
332	
333	            // Toroidal candidate: a direct grow from this seed (fillet tori,
334	            // bend tubes), skipped when the seed reads sphere-like — every
335	            // adjacent quad-row band of a sphere lies near some torus, so a
336	            // (κ,κ) seed's torus is at best a bogus band that loses to the
337	            // sphere anyway. A torus seed reads |κ2| < |κ1| (κ2 varies
338	            // azimuthally around the tube; it only approaches κ1 near the
339	            // degenerate R≈r hole of a donut — a whole-region ladder case,
340	            // not a competition case).
341	            let mut torus = if a2 < 0.8 * a1 {
342	                let patch = seed_patch(mesh, &in_region, seed, jet);
343	                torus_candidate(mesh, &in_region, &patch, &[seed], centroids, config)
344	            } else {
345	                None
346	            };
347	            // Bent-tube promotion: a cylinder that stalled against
348	            // tube-continuation faces is the developable prefix of a bent
349	            // tube; grow a torus from the pure-bend patch past the stall.
350	            if let Some((cyl, _, cyl_faces)) = cone.as_ref() {
351	                if cyl.is_cylinder() {
352	                    let promoted =
353	                        promote_bend(mesh, &in_region, cyl, cyl_faces, jet, centroids, config);
354	                    if let Some(p) = promoted {
355	                        if torus.as_ref().is_none_or(|(_, a, _)| p.1 > *a) {
356	                            torus = Some(p);
357	                        }
358	                    }
359	                }
360	            }
361	            torus_area = torus.as_ref().map(|(_, a, f)| (*a, f.len()));
362	
363	            consider(cone.map(|(h, a, _)| (CompeteHyp::Conical(h), a)), 2, &mut best);
364	            // Curved in both directions → also try a sphere.
365	            if a2 >= 0.3 * a1 {
366	                let sphere = grow::<SphericalSurface>(mesh, &in_region, seed, jet, centroids, config, MIN_SPHERE_FACES);
367	                sphere_area = sphere.as_ref().map(|(_, a, f)| (*a, f.len()));
368	                consider(sphere.map(|(h, a, _)| (CompeteHyp::Spherical(h), a)), 1, &mut best);
369	            }
370	            consider(torus.map(|(h, a, _)| (CompeteHyp::Toroidal(h), a)), 3, &mut best);
371	        }
372	        let plane_area = plane.as_ref().map(|(_, a, f)| (*a, f.len()));
373	        consider(plane.map(|(h, a, _)| (CompeteHyp::Planar(h), a)), 0, &mut best);
374	
375	        if debug && best.is_none() {
376	            eprintln!(
377	                "    compete: seed {seed} jet=({:.3},{:.3}) class {:?} → NO GROWTH (plane {plane_area:?} cone {cone_area:?} sphere {sphere_area:?} torus {torus_area:?})",
378	                jf.k1, jf.k2, curvature_class(jf),
379	            );
380	        }
381	
382	        if let Some((hyp, area, dof)) = best {
383	            if debug {
384	                eprintln!(
385	                    "    compete: seed {seed} → {} ({} faces, area {area:.2}, dof {dof}, sweep {:.1}\u{00b0})",
386	                    hyp.kind_name(),
387	                    hyp.faces().len(),
388	                    match &hyp {
389	                        CompeteHyp::Toroidal(t) => torus_sweep(mesh, t).to_degrees(),
390	                        CompeteHyp::Conical(c) => conical_sweep(mesh, c).to_degrees(),
391	                        _ => 0.0,
392	                    }
393	                );
394	            }
395	            let idx = committed.len();
396	            for &f in hyp.faces() {
397	                claim_lists[f].push(idx);
398	                claimed[f] = true;
399	            }
400	            committed.push(hyp);
401	        }
402	        // A seed that grows nothing analytic costs only its own turn.
403	    }
404	
405	    resolve_claims(
406	        mesh,
407	        &region.faces,
408	        &mut committed,
409	        &claim_lists,
410	        config.vertex_tolerance_mm,
411	        config,
412	    )
413	}

415	/// Resolve multi-claimed faces to their best-fitting claimant (2× margin to
416	/// leave the larger claimant), rebuild each hypothesis's face/vertex lists,
417	/// drop hypotheses that lost all faces, and collect unclaimed leftovers.
418	/// Is every neighbour of \`fi\` claimed too? Such a face is interior to the
419	/// explained set and cannot seed anything new.
420	fn interior_of_claims(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, fi: usize, claimed: &[bool]) -> bool {
421	    let face = &mesh.faces[fi];
422	    let vc = face.vertex_count as usize;
423	    face.neighbors[..vc]
424	        .iter()
425	        .all(|&ni| ni < 0 || claimed[ni as usize])
426	}

434	/// direction recovers r = 0.99998 / 0.99999 / 0.50008 against true 1.0 / 1.0 /
435	/// 0.5, with residuals five to ten times *under* vertex tolerance. With the
436	/// axis fixed the fit is a 3-DOF circle in the perpendicular plane, which is
437	/// well conditioned on a short arc — so growth can start from the seed facet
