I read DEVELOPMENT_PLAN, README, TODO and your new Invariants section, built the measuring instrument, and ran it over the corpus. Nothing in the invariants or the algorithm was changed.

## Verdict on the new material

**The framing is right and worth building on.** "Define near-invariants first, then make the algorithm satisfy them" is the correct move for this codebase, and two of your five headings turn out to be *provable* rather than merely empirical — which is better than you hoped. But the section as written has one truncated sentence, one self-contradictory definition, and three specifics that measurement refutes outright. It is not workable as-is; it is workable after edits I can enumerate precisely.

## What I built

- **`--invariant-report`** (`src/stage2/invariants.rs`, ~1400 lines) — runs after stage 2.2, needs `--compare`. It reuses `reference::label_faces`, which already labels every mesh facet with its ground-truth reference face for free, so each proposed invariant is scored against the reference's *own exact* surface parameters.
- **`tools/invariants.sh`** — harness over `sweep.sh`'s model/reference pairing; **`tools/inv_analyze.py`** — aggregator.
- One production refactor: extracted `compete_from_seed` verbatim out of `compete_region` so the harness drives the *real* competition rather than a reimplementation. Suite **595 passed / 0 failed**, clippy clean, `rounded_cube_10_r2_fine` still 26 = 6/12/8.

Coverage: **147 models, 2303 reference faces, 10 128 seed runs, 179 414 candidate seed chains**; a deep pass with the full four-type competition per seed over 103 models / 7630 seeds.

Instrument sanity check: it independently reproduced Phase 1.0's recorded **1.0342°** adjacent-pair cylinder-axis error on `pipe_elbow_10` medium.

---

## Findings

### 1. Fitting Requirement — satisfiable, but the probes are wrong (fixably)

Your three per-type probe rules collapse into **one** rule with a proof behind it. For a facet with vertices on the surface, the deviation is a quadratic vanishing at the vertices, so in barycentrics `e = −Σλᵢλⱼ·qᵢⱼ`. The max over the facet is therefore between the largest **edge-midpoint** value and 4/3 of it, exactly, to second order. Measured over 895 non-degenerate faces:

| probe | p95 ratio to true facet max | max |
|---|---|---|
| boundary edge midpoints (as written) | 1.742 | 1.999 |
| edge midpoints **+ quad diagonals** | **1.012** | **1.497** |
| facet centroid | 1.384 | 2.239 |

The centroid's 2.239 matches the derived worst case of 9/4 to three digits, and on a saddle the centroid can read exactly zero where the facet is off by the full sag. **The centroid is not a bound on anything.** The boundary-only version fails at exactly 2.0 on quad-tessellated spheres because a parallelogram's diagonal midpoint *is* its centre, where the sag is 2× the side midpoints'.

So: edge midpoints of a *triangulation* (boundary edges plus fused-quad diagonals), times 4/3, is a rigorous whole-facet bound at ~1.5 distance evaluations per triangle. That answers both of your TODOs — including the NURBS one — with one rule instead of three.

**Vertex tolerance.** On verified synthetic ground truth the invariant holds at p95 ≈ 1.5 float32 quanta, max ≈ 5. But two true cylinders on `stepped_block_toroidal_fillets_fine` sit at **8.8 and 8.5 quanta = 7.7e-5 mm, over the 5e-5 default vtol**. The requirement is *unsatisfiable* there today — no algorithm can recover those two surfaces.

**Surface tolerance.** True facet sag over the corpus spans p50 2.2e-6 to max 0.325 mm — five orders of magnitude — against a single 0.4 mm default with 1.23× margin at the worst point. This is your Phase 3.2 per-face-tolerance argument arriving from the invariant side.

### 2. "All facet relative angles within angle tolerance" — refuted as a membership rule

**856 of 1073 reference faces have an interior dihedral ≥ their smallest boundary dihedral.** Worst: `nosecone_medium`'s sphere, 17.58° inside vs 0.021° across the tangency — 822×. No threshold separates those.

Worse, it is already doing damage as a *partition* rule: stage 2.1's own classifier calls **350 edges sharp strictly inside 68 true reference surfaces**, cutting them before any fitting. `filleted_pipe` gets 11 sharp edges inside each of its two big tori (interior dihedral 31.4°); stage 2.4's repair silently sews them back. That is precisely the heuristic-on-heuristic you want gone. The largest cluster is Fusion's coarse preset — **30° normal deviation against a 25° default angular tolerance**, so every coarse Fusion cylinder is cut into 12 pieces.

### 3. Surface Identification — your proposed tie-break points the wrong way

The TODO asks how to choose when a cone also fits a cylinder. Measured, on the true support of each reference face:

| true type | a wrong type also validates at vtol |
|---|---|
| cylinder | sphere on **496 of 652**; torus on 307 |
| cone | sphere on 64 of 91; torus on 32 |
| plane | sphere on 322 of 1261; cyl/cone on 126 |

And the residuals are indistinguishable — both sit at ~0.2–0.5 quanta. The decisive number:

> **On 393 of 397 true cylinders (99%), the impostor sphere fits the cylinder's own facets *better* than the cylinder does** (median 0.555× the residual, p95 0.991).

So "the cylindrical fit should fit much more precisely" is not merely a weak signal — it is systematically **inverted**. `simple_cylinder` shows why cleanly: its 32-quad band has vertices on exactly two circles, which lie exactly on a sphere; residual 2.07e-7 mm, machine precision. This is identifiability, not model selection, and it is the same wall your DEVELOPMENT_PLAN already documents under `MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG`.

### 4. Surface Seed Independence — badly false today

Running the production `grow` from seeds spread across each true surface:

| type | faces | seeds | grew | recovered truth | faces where all seeds agreed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| plane | 326 | 2569 | 93.1% | 91.5% | 284/326 (87%) |
| sphere | 139 | 1112 | 70.7% | 64.5% | 21/139 (15%) |
| torus | 129 | 1030 | 68.3% | 18.3% | **2/129 (2%)** |
| cylinder | 612 | 4785 | 56.7% | 48.3% | 133/612 (22%) |
| cone | 79 | 632 | 28.2% | 24.8% | 8/79 (10%) |
| **all** | **1285** | **10128** | **66.8%** | **56.5%** | **448/1285 (34.9%)** |

Failure *direction* differs by type and matches the recorded history: cones **never leak** and starve (0% leak, 11% stop-short — the Phase 1.2 chicken-and-egg); tori and spheres both leak and starve (~40–53% each). Seam-split reference faces account for almost none of it (union scoring moves 56.5% → 58.3%).

Restricting to **interior** seeds (every mesh neighbour in the same reference face) helps a lot — grew 66.8% → 87.5%, agreeing faces 34.9% → 63.8% — but **74% of reference faces have no interior facet at all** (median 29 facets; strip-tessellated cylinders are one quad row, so every facet touches a cap). An interiority precondition would be vacuous where it is most needed.

At the **type** level the picture is much better. Full competition per seed: 91.9% of faces had every seed agree on one winning type, and conditional on producing a winner — cyl 95%, plane 98%, sphere 90%, torus 96%, cone 85% correct. **The type is nearly seed-independent; the extent is not.**

### 5. Growth Independence — provable, and confirmed

`flood` is defined as the connected component of `{faces validating a fixed fit}` containing the seed, returned sorted. That is a set, so it is order-independent by construction. Re-running every flood with the neighbour iteration reversed: **0 differences in 18 429 seeds.**

The real order dependence is the *refit fixpoint* `F ← flood(fit(F))`. Starting it from the whole true face set instead of the seed patch reproduces the truth on only 83.0%, and **648 of 1285 faces disagree between the oracle start and the seed starts**. So state this heading as a theorem about `flood` and put the empirical burden on the fixpoint.

### 6. Seed Requirements — the stated cylinder/cone rule is unusable as written

Enumerating every ≤4-facet chain inside each developable reference face:

- 14.2% have exactly 6 distinct vertices.
- **74.5% of those have some four coplanar** — a fused quad is coplanar by construction, so read literally, *"no more than three of which are coplanar" rejects three-quarters of the valid seeds*, including the best ones.
- Only 4.4% are wholly coplanar (the degeneracy you're actually aiming at), **and excluding them does not lower the worst axis error at all** — 90° either way.
- Axis error from a rule-conforming chain: p50 0.0000° but **p95 21.8°, max 90°**. For cones the per-face median is **46°**, and 76 of 87 cone faces have a conforming chain more than 1° wrong. (Phase 1.1 already recorded why: a real cone tessellation is a single ring, and every normal line meets the axis at the same point.)
- The same initializer over the **whole face with Phase 1.1's pair selection**: p95 **0.10°**, max 3.07° on synthetic ground truth. ~200× better.

Counting vertices is the wrong shape of condition. What makes a seed good is having enough facets to *select* a ruling-aligned, angularly-distant pair from.

### 7. Textual defects

- "Surfaces can be discovered by growing a set of seed facets to the set of contiguous facets that satisfy " — sentence truncated.
- "A **non-contiguous** facet chain is a set of facets where each facet shares a single edge with **any** other facet" — self-contradictory; that definition is *contiguous*, and "any" should be "some". Also "non-contiuous" typo twice.
- "Fitted cylinder must not have such a large radius as to be effectively planar. (TBD!)" is a new tuned threshold, which TODO rule 5 says needs sign-off — and the ladder's simplest-DOF-first rule already answers it without one.

---

## Recommendations (not implemented)

1. **Collapse the three fitting rules into one**: all vertices ≤ vtol; all edge midpoints of a facet *triangulation* (boundary edges + fused-quad diagonals) ≤ ¾·stol. Drop facet centroids entirely — they are not a bound. This covers NURBS too and answers both TODOs.
2. **State tolerances in the units the data has**: vertex bar in float32 position bounds (~2 quanta p95, ~5 max), surface bar as a multiple of the facet's own local sag. A global 5e-5 makes two true `stepped_block` cylinders unrecoverable by construction.
3. **Demote the angular condition** from a membership/partition rule to a post-hoc consistency check, and require the angular tolerance to exceed the exporter's own angular setting (Fusion Low is 30° > the 25° default). Today 68 true surfaces are cut and repaired back.
4. **Rewrite the seed rule as a selection over a pool, not a minimal set.** Delete the coplanarity clause (it rejects 74.5% of good seeds and catches none of the bad). Keep a rank/conditioning condition instead — Phase 1.1's `select_axis_pair` already is it.
5. **Add an identifiability precondition to Surface Identification**, and record in the section that the residual-magnitude tie-break is measured-dead (99% inverted). The discriminator has to stay structural: ladder order plus `MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG`-style tests.
6. **Restate Seed Independence declaratively, as a property of the output.** Call `(T, θ, F)` *admissible* iff `F` is mesh-connected, `θ = fit_T(F)`, every facet of `F` validates `θ`, and no facet adjacent to `F` does. That is checkable in O(|F|) on every run, it makes Growth Independence a corollary rather than an experiment, and it converts an unbounded for-all-over-seeds into a finite check. Seed independence then becomes "the admissible set is small and the algorithm finds all of it".
7. **Add the two missing invariants**: the partition invariant (every facet in exactly one surface — `assert_invariants` enforces it, but the section doesn't state it), and a *boundary* invariant, since every current statement is per-surface and the junction rows are where the difficulty actually lives.

## Caveats on the measurement

Ground truth is the `--compare` reference, and roughly a third of the wild `external/` pairs are recorded as not-ground-truth — the vertex-invariant tails (1313 quanta) come from there; the synthetic split is in the report. `cone_15x20.step` is a faceted 59-plane reference, and its rows show up as degenerate 1-facet "planes". Freeform reference faces are unmeasured (no closed-form distance). Seeds are sampled 8–12 per face, not exhaustive. And the seed-independence numbers describe *today's* blind-patch `grow` — they are a baseline, not a bound on what's achievable.

Full output: `tmp/inv-report-broad.txt`, `tmp/inv-report-deep.txt`, raw TSVs in `tmp/inv-{broad,deep}.tsv`. Nothing is committed — the working tree has the tool plus your two doc edits.

fn chains_with_six_vertices(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    faces: &[usize],
    member: &HashSet<usize>,
    cap: usize,
) -> (Vec<Vec<usize>>, usize) {
    let mut out: Vec<Vec<usize>> = Vec::new();
    let mut considered = 0usize;
    for &start in faces {
        if out.len() >= cap {
            break;
        }
        // Depth-first enumeration of simple paths from \`start\`.
        let mut stack: Vec<Vec<usize>> = vec![vec![start]];
        while let Some(path) = stack.pop() {
            if out.len() >= cap {
                break;
            }
            if path.len() >= 2 {
                considered += 1;
                if vertices_of(mesh, &path).len() == 6 {
                    let mut p = path.clone();
                    p.sort_unstable();
                    out.push(p);
                }
            }
            if path.len() >= MAX_CHAIN {
                continue;
            }
            let last = *path.last().unwrap();
            let vc = mesh.faces[last].vertex_count as usize;
            for &ni in &mesh.faces[last].neighbors[..vc] {
                if ni < 0 {
                    continue;
                }
                let nj = ni as usize;
                if !member.contains(&nj) || path.contains(&nj) {
                    continue;
                }
                let mut next = path.clone();
                next.push(nj);
                stack.push(next);
            }
        }
    }
    out.sort();
    out.dedup();
    (out, considered)
}
```
</details>

pub(crate) fn min_ruling_gap_rad(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    fi: usize,
    axis_pos: [f64; 3],
    axis_dir: [f64; 3],
) -> Option<f64> {
    let mut d = axis_dir;
    if normalize3(&mut d) == 0.0 {
        return None;
    }
    let (u, v) = perpendicular_basis(&d);

    let face = &mesh.faces[fi];
    let n = face.vertex_count as usize;
    if n < 3 {
        return None;
    }
    let mut thetas = Vec::with_capacity(n);
    for k in 0..n {
        let vtx = &mesh.vertices[face.vertex_indices[k]];
        let w = [
            vtx.x - axis_pos[0],
            vtx.y - axis_pos[1],
            vtx.z - axis_pos[2],
        ];
        let axial = dot3(&w, &d);
        let radial = [
            w[0] - axial * d[0],
            w[1] - axial * d[1],
            w[2] - axial * d[2],
        ];
        thetas.push(dot3(&radial, &v).atan2(dot3(&radial, &u)));
    }

    let mut min_gap = f64::MAX;
    for i in 0..n {
        for j in (i + 1)..n {
            let mut delta = (thetas[i] - thetas[j]).abs();
            if delta > std::f64::consts::PI {
                delta = std::f64::consts::TAU - delta;
            }
            min_gap = min_gap.min(delta);
        }
    }
    Some(min_gap)
}

/// \`|n_i × n_j|\` — how well-conditioned the pair is as an axis source, and
/// exactly the denominator in the amplification law.
fn pair_conditioning(a: &[f64; 3], b: &[f64; 3]) -> f64 {
    let c = cross3(a, b);
    (c[0] * c[0] + c[1] * c[1] + c[2] * c[2]).sqrt()
}

/// The most angularly distant pair of facet normals in \`faces\`.
fn widest_normal_pair(faces: &[usize], mesh: &ConnectedMesh) -> Option<(usize, usize, f64)> {
    let mut best: Option<(usize, usize, f64)> = None;
    for (a, &fi) in faces.iter().enumerate() {
        let Some(ni) = mesh.faces[fi].normal else {
            continue;
        };
        for &fj in &faces[a + 1..] {
            let Some(nj) = mesh.faces[fj].normal else {
                continue;
            };
            let k = pair_conditioning(&ni, &nj);
            if best.is_none_or(|(_, _, bk)| k > bk) {
                best = Some((fi, fj, k));
            }
        }
    }
    best
}

/// Pick the pair of facets to take an axis from: ruling-aligned, and as
/// angularly distant as the patch allows.
///
/// Two passes, because alignment is defined relative to an axis we do not have
/// yet. The first pass gives a provisional axis good enough to *classify*
/// facets — misjudging alignment needs an axis error of order the angular step,
/// far beyond what pass one produces — and the second pass re-picks among the
/// facets that survive. If too few survive, the provisional pair stands: a
/// worse-conditioned axis is still better than no axis, and validation
/// downstream is what decides whether the fit lives.
///
/// Returns the pair and the axis direction it implies.
fn select_axis_pair(faces: &[usize], mesh: &ConnectedMesh) -> Option<(usize, usize, [f64; 3])> {
    let axis_of = |fi: usize, fj: usize| -> Option<[f64; 3]> {
        let (ni, nj) = (mesh.faces[fi].normal?, mesh.faces[fj].normal?);
        let mut axis = cross3(&ni, &nj);
        if normalize3(&mut axis) < MIN_CROSS_NORM {
            return None;
        }
        Some(axis)
    };

    let (pi, pj, _) = widest_normal_pair(faces, mesh)?;
    let provisional = axis_of(pi, pj)?;

    // Any point on the provisional axis will do to measure ruling gaps: the
    // gap is an angle about the axis direction, and shifting the reference
    // point along or across the axis moves every vertex's θ together.
    let anchor = face_centroid(&mesh.faces[pi], &mesh.vertices);
    let aligned: Vec<usize> = faces
        .iter()
        .copied()
        .filter(|&fi| {
            min_ruling_gap_rad(mesh, fi, anchor, provisional)
                .is_some_and(|gap| gap < RULING_SAME_RAD)
        })
        .collect();

    if aligned.len() >= 2 {
        if let Some((ai, aj, _)) = widest_normal_pair(&aligned, mesh) {
            if let Some(axis) = axis_of(ai, aj) {
                return Some((ai, aj, axis));
            }
        }
    }
    Some((pi, pj, provisional))
}

/// Every distinct vertex index used by \`faces\`.
fn patch_vertices(faces: &[usize], mesh: &ConnectedMesh) -> Vec<usize> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for &fi in faces {
        let f = &mesh.faces[fi];
        for k in 0..f.vertex_count as usize {
            let vi = f.vertex_indices[k];

fn sym4_eigenvalues(m0: &[[f64; 4]; 4]) -> [f64; 4] {
    let mut a = *m0;

                let t = theta.signum() / (theta.abs() + (theta * theta + 1.0).sqrt());
                let c = 1.0 / (t * t + 1.0).sqrt();
                let s = t * c;

                    b[q][k] = s * a[p][k] + c * a[q][k];

                a = d;

        }

    let mut e = [a[0][0], a[1][1], a[2][2], a[3][3]];

/// The **dual** (plane-coordinate) view of a developable seed.
///
/// Every facet plane of a cone contains the apex (Phase 1.1), and every facet
/// plane of a cylinder is parallel to the axis — the same statement in
/// homogeneous coordinates. Writing facet `i`'s plane as the 4-vector
/// `(nᵢ, −nᵢ·pᵢ)`, a cone with apex `A` makes every plane orthogonal to
/// `(A, 1)` and a cylinder with axis direction `u` makes every plane orthogonal
/// to `(u, 0)`. So for ANY developable of revolution the facet planes span a
/// 3-dimensional subspace of ℝ⁴, and the apex-or-axis **is the null vector** —
/// with `w₄ ≠ 0` reading as a cone at `w₁₂₃/w₄` and `w₄ = 0` as a cylinder
/// along `w₁₂₃`, continuously, no infinity in between.
///
/// That makes the two singular-value ratios below the natural statement of what
/// a seed has to satisfy, in place of counting vertices:
///
/// - `sigma4` (smallest / largest) — how *developable* the patch is. Non-zero
///   means the facets do not lie on any common cone or cylinder.
/// - `sigma3` (second-smallest / largest) — whether the patch **identifies**
///   one. Zero means the null space is 2-dimensional, i.e. the apex is a free
///   point on a line and a cylinder is indistinguishable from a one-parameter
///   family of cones. A triangle fan around a shared vertex on a cylinder is
///   exactly this case, and so is a patch confined to a single ruling.
///
/// Coordinates are shifted to the patch centroid and scaled by its extent
/// first: the `n` block is dimensionless and the `−n·p` block carries length,
/// so without normalization the spectrum measures the choice of origin rather
/// than the data (the same trap Phase 1.1 hit with the torus Plücker system).
fn plane_spectrum(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, faces: &[usize]) -> Option<(f64, f64)> {
    if faces.len() < 3 {
        return None;
    }
    let mut c = [0.0_f64; 3];
    let mut cnt = 0.0_f64;
    for &fi in faces {
        let q = face_centroid(&mesh.faces[fi], &mesh.vertices);
        for k in 0..3 {
            c[k] += q[k];
        }
        cnt += 1.0;
    }
    for k in 0..3 {
        c[k] /= cnt;
    }
    let mut extent = 0.0_f64;
    for &fi in faces {
        for p in facet_points(mesh, fi) {
            extent = extent.max(norm(sub(p, c)));
        }
    }
    if extent <= 0.0 {
        return None;
    }
    let mut g = [[0.0_f64; 4]; 4];
    for &fi in faces {
        let n = facet_normal(mesh, fi);
        let p = face_centroid(&mesh.faces[fi], &mesh.vertices);
        let pt = [
            (p[0] - c[0]) / extent,
            (p[1] - c[1]) / extent,
            (p[2] - c[2]) / extent,
        ];
        let v = [n[0], n[1], n[2], -dot(n, pt)];
        for i in 0..4 {
            for j in 0..4 {
                g[i][j] += v[i] * v[j];
            }
        }
    }
    let e = sym4_eigenvalues(&g);
    if e[3] <= 0.0 {
        return None;
    }
    // Singular values are sqrt of the Gram's eigenvalues.
    Some((
        (e[0].max(0.0) / e[3]).sqrt(),
        (e[1].max(0.0) / e[3]).sqrt(),
    ))
}

/// Do all the facets of `chain` share one common vertex? (The case the
/// Invariants section's coplanarity clause was reaching for.)
fn shares_common_vertex(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, chain: &[usize]) -> bool {
    let mut common: Option<HashSet<usize>> = None;
    for &fi in chain {
        let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
        let set: HashSet<usize> = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_indices[..vc].iter().copied().collect();
        common = Some(match common {
            None => set,
            Some(c) => c.intersection(&set).copied().collect(),
        });
        if common.as_ref().is_some_and(|c| c.is_empty()) {
            return false;
        }
    }
    common.is_some_and(|c| !c.is_empty())
}

/// Enumerate facet **chains** (paths in the dual graph, the section's'''

Your seed requirements are written **per type** — a cylinder seed, a cone seed, a sphere seed. fn patch_size_probe(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    faces: &[usize],
    truth_axis: ([f64; 3], [f64; 3]),
    is_cone: bool,
    model: &str,
    ref_idx: usize,
    kind: &str,
) {
    const SIZES: [usize; 10] = [2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 64];
    const STARTS: usize = 8;
    let member: HashSet<usize> = faces.iter().copied().collect();
    let (_, want_dir) = truth_axis;
    let want = unit(want_dir);
    let ang = |d: [f64; 3]| -> f64 {
        let d = unit(d);
        let c = [
            d[1] * want[2] - d[2] * want[1],
            d[2] * want[0] - d[0] * want[2],
            d[0] * want[1] - d[1] * want[0],
        ];
        norm(c).clamp(0.0, 1.0).asin().to_degrees()
    };
    let stride = (faces.len() / STARTS).max(1);
    for &start in faces.iter().step_by(stride).take(STARTS) {
        // One BFS from the start, recording the axis error each time the
        // accumulated patch reaches the next size on the ladder.
        let mut patch = vec![start];
        let mut seen: HashSet<usize> = HashSet::from([start]);
        let mut frontier = vec![start];
        let mut next_size = 0usize;
        while next_size < SIZES.len() {
            while next_size < SIZES.len() && patch.len() >= SIZES[next_size] {
                let target = SIZES[next_size];
                let sub: Vec<usize> = patch[..target.min(patch.len())].to_vec();
                let got = if is_cone {
                    super::initialize::cone(&sub, mesh, 5e-5)
                } else {
                    super::initialize::cylinder(&sub, mesh)
                };
                if let Some(
                    super::initialize::Initial::Cylinder { axis_dir, .. }
                    | super::initialize::Initial::Cone { axis_dir, .. },
                ) = got
                {
                    println!(
                        "PATCHSIZE\t{model}\t{ref_idx}\t{kind}\t{target}\t{:.6}",
                        ang(axis_dir)
                    );
                }
                next_size += 1;
            }
            // Expand one ring.
            let mut ring = Vec::new();
            for &fi in &frontier {
                let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
                for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
                    if ni < 0 {
                        continue;
                    }
                    let nj = ni as usize;
                    if member.contains(&nj) && seen.insert(nj) {
                        patch.push(nj);
                        ring.push(nj);
                    }
                }
            }
            if ring.is_empty() {
                break;
            }
            frontier = ring;
        }
    }
}

## The three objects

| object | what it is | where |
|---|---|---|
| **seed** | one facet index | `compete.rs`: `seeds = region.faces.clone()`, `for &seed in &seeds` |
| **fit patch** | ≤32 facets, ≤3 hops, grown from that one facet | `seed_patch` → `condition_patch`; this is what least-squares actually sees |
| **support** | whatever the flood validated | `flood` output, refit to a fixpoint |

Your Invariants section uses "seed" for the middle one under *Surface Seed Requirements* ("a facet chain including exactly 6 vertices") and for the first under *Sphere* ("all facets sharing an edge with **the seed facet**") and *Seed Independence* ("the seed consists of facets which are members of the surface" — ambiguous, but the quantifier only makes sense over sets).

Mapping my findings onto that:

- **S (34.9% of surfaces gave one answer) and G (0 of 18 429 order differences)** — quantified over **single starting facets**. These bear on *Seed Independence*.
- **E (the detector table, the 45.6° cone number)** — quantified over **facet sets**, where the 2–4 facet chain *was* the entire fit support. These bear on *Seed Requirements*.

My admissibility clauses last message were written as if those were one object. They belong to the fit patch.

## The gap, now filled

I had measured 2–4 facets and the whole face, and nothing between — while the pipeline fits 32. Paired (the same 67 cylinder / 46 cone reference faces at every rung), closed-form axis error against the number of facets the fit sees:

| facets | cyl p50 | cyl p95 | cyl >1° | cone p50 | cone p95 | cone >1° |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 0.0000 | 4.115 | 17.3% | 45.74 | 90.00 | 100% |
| 4 | 0.0000 | 1.483 | 7.5% | 34.31 | 77.69 | 92% |
| 8 | 0.0000 | 1.305 | 8.0% | 9.46 | 73.32 | 78% |
| **16** | 0.0000 | **0.471** | **2.8%** | 1.30 | 46.05 | 55% |
| 24 | 0.0000 | 0.545 | 3.5% | 0.404 | 4.69 | 19.6% |
| 32 | 0.0000 | 1.100 | 7.1% | 0.194 | 1.57 | 10.3% |
| **64** | 0.0000 | 1.077 | 5.2% | **0.034** | **0.289** | **0%** |

Three things fall out.

**A cylinder's median is exact at every size** — support buys tail reliability, not accuracy. **A cone's median is the answer itself**: 45.7° at 2 facets is the degenerate reading, i.e. no information, and it takes ~24 facets to get under a degree and 64 to be clean.

**And the cylinder curve is not monotone.** p95 bottoms at 16 facets (0.471°, 2.8% over a degree) and *degrades* to 1.100° / 7.1% at 32. This is the paired comparison on fixed faces, so it is not a population artefact. I have not measured the mechanism, but the obvious suspect is `select_axis_pair`'s first pass: `widest_normal_pair` runs over the whole patch *before* alignment is known, and on a larger patch the widest pair is likelier to include one of the 25.6% straddling facets, poisoning the provisional axis that the alignment test then depends on.

**So there is no single right size**, which is the strongest argument yet against legislating one. `SEED_PATCH_CAP = 32` sits past the cylinder optimum and well short of the cone's — and it is one of Phase 0.4's nine fragility cliffs. new = r'''// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The clean grow operator, and its basin of attraction
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Refit-and-reflood rounds before the clean operator gives up.
const MAX_CLEAN_ROUNDS: usize = 12;

/// What happened when a seed SET was grown under the clean operator.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
enum Basin {
    /// Converged to exactly the reference face. The seed is in the basin.
    Exact,
    /// Converged to a strict subset — the fit stalled inside its own surface.
    Short,
    /// Converged to a strict superset — the fit leaked past the true boundary.
    Leak,
    /// Converged to something that is neither.
    Other,
    /// No fit of this type exists on the seed set (or on some later support).
    NoFit,
    /// The fit of the seed set does not validate any facet of the seed set.
    SeedRejected,
    /// Still moving at the round cap.
    NoConverge,
}

impl Basin {
    fn code(self) -> u8 {
        match self {
            Basin::Exact => 0,
            Basin::Short => 1,
            Basin::Leak => 2,
            Basin::Other => 3,
            Basin::NoFit => 4,
            Basin::SeedRejected => 5,
            Basin::NoConverge => 6,
        }
    }
}

/// **The clean operator.** `F₀ = S`; `F_{k+1}` = the union of the validated
/// components containing the seed set, under a fresh least-squares fit of
/// `F_k`; iterate to a fixpoint.
///
/// No `seed_patch`, no `condition_patch`, no trimming, no jet — the seed set is
/// the entire initial fit support and validation is the only thing that decides
/// membership. This is the baseline the Invariants section is trying to
/// establish, so the question "which seed sets are valid" becomes "which seed
/// sets lie in the basin of attraction of their own surface", which is what
/// this measures.
///
/// Growth is confined to the smooth region, as the pipeline does: the sharp
/// partition is the one thing measured exact, so leaving it in place isolates
/// the seeding question from the partitioning one.
fn grow_clean<S: SurfaceType>(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    in_region: &[bool],
    seed: &[usize],
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    config: &Config,
) -> (Basin, Vec<usize>, usize, bool) {
    let vtol = config.vertex_tolerance_mm;
    let stol = config.surface_tolerance_mm;
    let mut cur: Vec<usize> = seed.to_vec();
    cur.sort_unstable();
    let mut self_ok = false;
    for round in 0..MAX_CLEAN_ROUNDS {
        let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &cur);
        let Some(mut fit) = S::fit_surface(mesh, &cur, &verts, 0) else {
            return (Basin::NoFit, cur, round, self_ok);
        };
        S::determine_convexity(mesh, &cur, &mut fit);
        if round == 0 {
            // Does the seed set's own fit explain the whole seed set? A
            // ground-truth-free predicate, so it could gate admission in
            // production.
            self_ok = seed
                .iter()
                .all(|&fi| compete::face_validates::<S>(mesh, fi, &fit, centroids, vtol, stol));
        }
        let mut next: HashSet<usize> = HashSet::new();
        for &st in seed {
            if next.contains(&st) {
                continue;
            }
            let comp = compete::flood::<S>(mesh, in_region, st, &fit, centroids, vtol, stol);
            next.extend(comp);
        }
        if next.is_empty() {
            return (Basin::SeedRejected, cur, round, self_ok);
        }
        let mut nv: Vec<usize> = next.into_iter().collect();
        nv.sort_unstable();
        if nv == cur {
            return (Basin::Exact, cur, round, self_ok); // caller re-classifies
        }
        cur = nv;
    }
    (Basin::NoConverge, cur, MAX_CLEAN_ROUNDS, self_ok)
}

/// Classify a converged result against the reference face.
fn classify(result: &[usize], truth: &HashSet<usize>) -> Basin {
    let inside = result.iter().filter(|f| truth.contains(f)).count();
    if inside == result.len() && result.len() == truth.len() {
        Basin::Exact
    } else if inside == result.len() {
        Basin::Short
    } else if inside == truth.len() {
        Basin::Leak
    } else {
        Basin::Other
    }
}

/// How large does a fit support have to be before it determines a developable?'''
assert s.count(anchor)==1
s=s.replace(anchor,new,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
print('ok')

anchor = "/// How large does a fit support have to be before it determines a developable?"
new = r'''/// Sample seed SETS inside one reference face and report, for each, whether the
/// clean operator grows it to exactly that face.
///
/// Three shapes, because the answer may depend on more than size:
/// - `ball`   — a BFS neighbourhood of `k` facets, the compact seed.
/// - `split`  — two BFS balls of `k/2` at the two most distant starts, which is
///              the well-conditioned shape for an axis (Phase 1.0's
///              "angularly most distant pair") and is *disconnected*.
/// - `strip`  — `k` facets taken in index order from one start, which on a
///              strip tessellation walks the ruling (Phase 1.2's measured
///              rank-0 failure).
#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
fn basin_probe<S: SurfaceType>(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    in_region: &[bool],
    faces: &[usize],
    truth: &HashSet<usize>,
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    config: &Config,
    truth_axis: Option<([f64; 3], [f64; 3])>,
    model: &str,
    ref_idx: usize,
    kind: &str,
) {
    const SIZES: [usize; 8] = [2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24];
    const STARTS: usize = 5;
    let member: HashSet<usize> = faces.iter().copied().collect();
    let ball = |start: usize, k: usize| -> Vec<usize> {
        let mut out = vec![start];
        let mut seen: HashSet<usize> = HashSet::from([start]);
        let mut frontier = vec![start];
        while out.len() < k && !frontier.is_empty() {
            let mut ring = Vec::new();
            for &fi in &frontier {
                let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
                for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
                    if ni < 0 || out.len() >= k {
                        continue;
                    }
                    let nj = ni as usize;
                    if member.contains(&nj) && seen.insert(nj) {
                        out.push(nj);
                        ring.push(nj);
                    }
                }
            }
            if ring.is_empty() {
                break;
            }
            frontier = ring;
        }
        out.sort_unstable();
        out
    };
    // Geometric spread of a seed set about the true axis, for the analysis.
    let spread = |set: &[usize]| -> (f64, f64) {
        let Some((tpos, tdir0)) = truth_axis else {
            return (f64::NAN, f64::NAN);
        };
        let tdir = unit(tdir0);
        let (bu, bv) = super::perpendicular_basis(&tdir);
        let mut angles: Vec<f64> = Vec::new();
        let (mut zmin, mut zmax, mut rmax) = (f64::INFINITY, f64::NEG_INFINITY, 0.0_f64);
        for &fi in set {
            for p in facet_points(mesh, fi) {
                let w = sub(p, tpos);
                let z = dot(w, tdir);
                let rad = sub(w, [tdir[0] * z, tdir[1] * z, tdir[2] * z]);
                let (x, y) = (dot(rad, bu), dot(rad, bv));
                let rr = x.hypot(y);
                if rr > 1e-12 {
                    angles.push(y.atan2(x));
                }
                zmin = zmin.min(z);
                zmax = zmax.max(z);
                rmax = rmax.max(rr);
            }
        }
        if angles.len() < 2 || rmax <= 0.0 {
            return (0.0, 0.0);
        }
        angles.sort_by(|a, b| a.partial_cmp(b).unwrap());
        let mut gap = angles[0] + std::f64::consts::TAU - angles[angles.len() - 1];
        for w in angles.windows(2) {
            gap = gap.max(w[1] - w[0]);
        }
        (
            (std::f64::consts::TAU - gap).max(0.0).to_degrees(),
            (zmax - zmin) / rmax,
        )
    };

    let stride = (faces.len() / STARTS).max(1);
    let starts: Vec<usize> = faces.iter().copied().step_by(stride).take(STARTS).collect();
    let far = *faces.last().unwrap();
    for &start in &starts {
        for &k in &SIZES {
            if k > faces.len() {
                continue;
            }
            let mut cases: Vec<(&str, Vec<usize>)> = vec![("ball", ball(start, k))];
            if k >= 4 {
                let mut sp = ball(start, k / 2);
                sp.extend(ball(far, k - k / 2));
                sp.sort_unstable();
                sp.dedup();
                cases.push(("split", sp));
            }
            {
                let i0 = faces.iter().position(|&f| f == start).unwrap_or(0);
                let strip: Vec<usize> =
                    faces.iter().cycle().skip(i0).take(k).copied().collect();
                let mut st = strip;
                st.sort_unstable();
                st.dedup();
                cases.push(("strip", st));
            }
            for (shape, set) in cases {
                if set.len() < 2 {
                    continue;
                }
                let connected = is_connected(mesh, &set);
                let (sweep, axial) = spread(&set);
                let (mut verdict, result, rounds, self_ok) =
                    grow_clean::<S>(mesh, in_region, &set, centroids, config);
                if verdict == Basin::Exact {
                    verdict = classify(&result, truth);
                }
                let inside = result.iter().filter(|f| truth.contains(f)).count();
                let jacc = if result.is_empty() && truth.is_empty() {
                    1.0
                } else {
                    inside as f64 / (result.len() + truth.len() - inside).max(1) as f64
                };
                println!(
                    "BASIN\t{model}\t{ref_idx}\t{kind}\t{}\t{shape}\t{}\t{}\t{}\t{}\t{}\t\
                     {sweep:.3}\t{axial:.5}\t{jacc:.4}\t{}",
                    faces.len(),
                    set.len(),
                    u8::from(connected),
                    u8::from(self_ok),
                    verdict.code(),
                    rounds,
                    result.len(),
                );
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Is a facet set connected through the mesh's face adjacency?
fn is_connected(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, set: &[usize]) -> bool {
    if set.is_empty() {
        return true;
    }
    let member: HashSet<usize> = set.iter().copied().collect();
    let mut seen: HashSet<usize> = HashSet::from([set[0]]);
    let mut stack = vec![set[0]];
    while let Some(fi) = stack.pop() {
        let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
        for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
            if ni < 0 {
                continue;
            }
            let nj = ni as usize;
            if member.contains(&nj) && seen.insert(nj) {
                stack.push(nj);
            }
        }
    }
    seen.len() == set.len()
}

/// How large does a fit support have to be before it determines a developable?'''

Here's the answer to the design question, measured rather than argued. I built the clean operator you describe — `F₀ = S`, `F_{k+1}` = validated component(s) containing S under a fresh least-squares fit of `F_k`, iterate to fixpoint — with no `seed_patch`, no `condition_patch`, no trimming, no jet. Then I grew **87 510 seed sets over 897 reference faces / 107 models**: 8 sizes × 3 shapes × 5 start positions per face, every seed set drawn entirely from inside one true surface.

## The definition that works

> **A set S of facets is a valid seed for type T iff `fit_T(S)` exists and every facet of S validates that fit at vertex tolerance.**

That's it. Nothing about connectivity, vertex counts, coplanarity, or fit accuracy.

| | seed sets | grew to exactly the surface |
|---|---|---|
| fails the predicate | 5 046 | **0.4%** |
| passes it | 82 464 | **84.6%** |

The failures below the line are 64% "the fit doesn't explain its own seed" and 30% "no fit exists" — i.e. the predicate catches exactly the two ways a seed can be hopeless, and nothing else.

What makes it the right shape rather than one more heuristic: it is **the fixpoint condition itself, evaluated at round 0**. The property you want at the end — `F = flood(fit(F))` — applied at the start is `S ⊆ flood(fit(S))`. Admission and termination become one predicate at two scales, and it introduces no new constant (it reuses `vtol`/`stol`).

Adding a size floor of 8 facets, per reference face — *every* admissible seed set converging to the same, correct answer:

| type | faces | all seeds exact | all seeds agree |
|---|---|---|---|
| plane | 145 | **100.0%** | 100.0% |
| cylinder | 379 | **92.3%** | 94.5% |
| sphere | 139 | **91.4%** | 92.8% |
| cone | 41 | 61.0% | 70.7% |
| torus | 125 | **16.8%** | 61.6% |

For comparison, the current pipeline (single seed facet + `seed_patch` + `condition_patch`) gives full seed-agreement on **34.9%** of surfaces. So the clean baseline is not a regression to be defended — for planes, cylinders and spheres it is substantially better than what exists.

## Your instincts confirmed

- **A bad fit really is good enough.** Cylinders: 74.9% at |S| = 2, **91.5% at |S| = 3**, plateau ~95% by 12. A 3-facet seed with a 1° axis error still converges, because the refit fixes it. The seed does not need to be accurate, only *determining*.
- **Connectivity is not required.** Connected 79.6%, disconnected 80.1%. The best-performing shape was `split` — two BFS balls at the two most distant points of the surface (82.3%, only 25% connected) — which is also the well-conditioned shape for an axis. That's a real design freedom worth writing into the definition explicitly, since "chain" implies otherwise.
- **Shape barely matters**: ball 78.4%, split 82.3%, strip 79.3%. Including the ruling-walking `strip`, which was fatal in Phase 1.2 — because there it fed a *one-shot* fit, and here the refit loop recovers.

## Two walls no seed definition can move

**1. Tori leak, and they leak seed-independently.** 45.6% of all torus seed sets converge to the surface *plus a collar*: overshoot p50 **1.04×**, p95 1.12, max 1.20. And 62% of torus faces have every admissible seed landing within 2% of the *same* answer. So growth is already seed-independent there — it simply does not stop at the true boundary. Past a tangent junction the neighbour's facets are within `vtol` of the torus because tangency means second-order agreement. **This is a boundary problem, not a seeding problem**, and no definition of "valid seed set" reaches it.

**2. Cones cannot be seeded small.** At the sizes sampled, 21% SeedRejected + 14% NoFit. The support-size curve says a cone's axis needs 24–64 facets to get under a degree, against ~16 for a cylinder. A cone should be reached by promotion from a validated cylinder, not seeded locally.

## What I'd change in the invariant's wording

Keep the definition above, and **change the target of the growth invariant** from "covers the surface exactly" to:

> **Growth invariant.** For every valid seed set S ⊆ F, the fixpoint of grow-with-refit **contains F**, and overshoots only into facets that a neighbouring surface explains strictly better.

Measured, "all admissible seeds cover the truth" reads 100 / 95.3 / 92.8 / 63.4 / **60.8%** for plane / cylinder / sphere / cone / torus, against "exactly" at 100 / 92.3 / 91.4 / 61.0 / **16.8%**. The entire torus gap is the collar.

That formulation is achievable, it preserves seed independence, and it puts the boundary decision where the information actually is — a *comparison between two surfaces*, not a threshold inside one. Which means the clean baseline should eliminate `seed_patch` and `condition_patch` (the measurements support that) but **keep multi-claiming and `resolve_claims`** (the measurements say the collar is unavoidable without them).

## Caveats

Growth stayed confined to the smooth region — I kept the sharp partition, since it's the one thing measured exact, so this isolates seeding from partitioning. The surface *type* was given by ground truth; type discovery is a separate question and my earlier numbers say residual can't answer it. Cone n = 41 faces is thin. Sampling is 5 starts × 8 sizes × 3 shapes per face, not exhaustive. And I haven't re-run the suite since these diagnostic additions — all of it sits behind `--invariant-report` and `BREPPER_INV_BASIN=1`, but it's unverified.

Per seed set it's **98.4%** at a floor of 16. For scale: exact-match at floor 8 was 80.6% of faces, and the *current* pipeline's single-facet seed independence was 34.9%. Allowing overshoot is what turns this from "mostly works" into an invariant worth stating.

Note the curve plateaus at 16 — going to 24 buys 0.4 points. That's the size floor, and it's a plateau rather than a knee you have to tune onto.

## The second clause holds identically

| type | overshoot lands in an **adjacent** reference face | neighbour explains it **strictly better** |
|---|---|---|
| cylinder | 100.0% | 100.0% |
| cone | 100.0% | 100.0% |

| plane | no overshoot at all | — |

Every overshoot facet in the corpus is in a face adjacent to the one that grew, and every one that can be measured is closer to its true owner's surface than to the fit that claimed it. So `resolve_claims` is handed exactly the information your invariant promises it — the boundary decision is a comparison between two surfaces, and the comparison always points the right way.

(The sphere row is a real gap, not a pass: sphere overshoots land on freeform neighbours, which have no closed-form distance, so I couldn't score them. 145 plane faces never overshot at all.)

## How much collar resolution has to absorb

Median |result| / |truth| is **1.000** for plane, cylinder, cone and sphere. Only tori carry a real collar: median **1.019**, p95 **1.117**, max 1.20. So the work is bounded at roughly a 2% median / 12% tail overgrowth on fillets, and nothing anywhere else.

## What's left

At floor 16 the residual is **cones (83.8%)** and **tori (83.2%)**. Cones mostly fail as `NoFit` — the fitter declines the support entirely, consistent with the earlier support-size curve saying a cone's axis needs 24–64 facets. Tori fail as `SeedRejected` and `Short`.

Stalls — the one failure mode that genuinely breaks the invariant — are only **1.70%** of admissible seeds at floor 8, and they are mostly a seed property rather than a face property: 60 faces have *some* seeds stall while others succeed, against only 7 where every seed stalls. Almost all of them are `stepped_block_toroidal`, the corpus's known narrow-flat-region pathology. When a seed does stall it stalls badly (median shortfall 47% of the face), so this is a distinct failure to detect, not a near-miss to tolerate.

And one finding worth building into the definition: **spread seeds beat compact ones.** Stall rate by shape — `split` (two distant balls, mostly disconnected) 1.02%, `ball` 1.48%, `strip` 2.56%; by connectivity — disconnected 0.67%, connected 2.46%. So not only is connectivity not required, requiring it would make the invariant *worse*.

## Suggested wording

> **Valid seed set.** A set S of facets is a valid seed for surface type T iff `fit_T(S)` exists, every facet of S validates it at vertex tolerance, and |S| ≥ 16. S need not be connected, and a spread seed is preferred to a compact one.
>
> **Growth invariant.** For every valid seed set S contained in a surface F, grow-with-refit converges to a set that **contains F**, and every facet it adds beyond F belongs to a reference-adjacent surface that explains that facet strictly better.

Measured: 95.0% of reference faces satisfy the first part for *every* admissible seed; the second part holds on 100% of overshoot facets.

## Caveats

Growth stayed inside the smooth region (sharp partition retained). Surface *type* was given by ground truth — type discovery is a separate question, and my earlier measurement says residual magnitude cannot answer it. Sphere overshoot is unscored against the second clause. Cone n = 41 faces is thin. Sampling was 5 starts × 8 sizes × 3 shapes per face — 87 510 grows over 897 faces / 107 models — not exhaustive. 87	### Reference scoring (\`--reference-report\`)
88	
89	With a \`--compare\` reference, brepper can label every mesh face with the
90	reference face it came from — recovered from the distance computation the
91	compare already performs — and then score three things against that ground
92	truth. All of it is diagnostics: nothing downstream reads it.
93	
94	At **stage 1**, properties of the mesh alone (so they are still measurable on
95	models where stage 2 fails):
96	
97	- **Facet-normal exactness** per reference surface type: the angle between the
98	  mesh facet normal and the true surface normal. Analytic faces use a closed
99	  form; B-spline, Bezier, revolution, extrusion and offset faces are evaluated
100	  through OCCT at the footpoint, and facets at a pole or seam — where the normal
101	  does not exist — are excluded rather than scored.
102	- **Closed-form initializer error**: the cylinder axis from \`n₁ × n₂\`, the
103	  sphere centre from circumcenter normal lines, and the torus
104	  meridian-coplanarity residual, each against the reference's own parameters,
105	  reported with the conditioning that governs them.
106	- **The seam assumption**: how often a facet's own interior disagrees about
107	  which reference face it belongs to.
108	
109	At the end of **stage 2**, our decomposition against the reference's:
110	
111	- **\`ref coverage\`** — 1.0 when no reference face was split across several of
112	  our surfaces (no over-segmentation).
113	- **\`surface purity\`** — 1.0 when none of our surfaces spans several reference
114	  faces (no merging).
115	
116	Both are area-weighted and threshold-free. They catch what the distance and
117	volume gates cannot: a 9-surface decomposition of a 26-surface part passes every
118	existing gate but scores \`surface purity 0.2201\`.

120	### Invariant scoring (\`--invariant-report\`)
121	
122	Scores the clauses of DEVELOPMENT_PLAN's **Invariants** section against the same
123	ground truth. Also diagnostics only, and it runs after **stage 2.2** rather than at
124	the end of stage 2, so it still works on models whose decomposition crashes or
125	times out. One TSV row per reference face on stdout, a per-model summary on stderr.
126	
127	\`\`\`bash
128	./target/release/brepper input.stl --compare reference.step --stage 2.2 --invariant-report -v
129	\`\`\`
130	
131	Five families, one per clause:
132	
133	- **F — is the fitting requirement satisfiable?** With the reference's *own* exact
134	  parameters, how far off it the facets' vertices, edge midpoints, quad diagonals,
135	  centroids and interiors actually land. This asks whether a clause can be met at
136	  all before asking whether the algorithm meets it, and it is what showed that
137	  facet centroids are not a bound on the whole facet while edge midpoints are.
138	- **A — can an angular tolerance separate adjacent surfaces?** The largest dihedral
139	  *inside* a reference face against the smallest *across* its boundary, plus the
140	  count of edges stage 2.1 calls sharp strictly inside a true surface.
141	- **I — does a wrong surface type also explain a true support?** All four analytic
142	  types fitted to each reference face's own facets, with residuals in float32
143	  quanta.
144	- **S — seed independence.** Growth run from many seeds inside one true surface:
145	  how many recover it, how many distinct answers come back, and whether a failure
146	  leaked past the true boundary or stopped short of it.
147	- **G — growth independence.** The flood re-run with the neighbour iteration
148	  reversed, and the refit fixpoint restarted from the whole true face set.

185	reference face, \`Q\` quit. The status line names the seed shape, how far the seed
186	sits from its own fit, and the diagnosis — which validation clause refused what,
187	since \`face_validates\` is a conjunction of vertex distance, centroid distance and
188	orientation coherence and naming only the first is misleading.
189	
190	\`BREPPER_VIZ_SEEDS_TEXT=1\` prints the same diagnoses with no window, which is what
191	the corpus catalogues are built from.
192	
193	See [DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md](DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md) for full documentation.
194	
195	### Tolerance Settings
196	
197	#### Surface Tolerance
198	
199	This is how far the surface of a mesh triangle is allowed to deviate from the surface it is approximating.
200	
201	Onshape calls this "Chordal tolerance (mm)", and the preset values are:
202	- Coarse: 0.24 mm
203	- Medium: 0.12 mm
204	- Fine: 0.06 mm
205	
206	Fusion 360 calls this "Surface Deviation", and the preset values seem to vary based on model size:
207	- Low: 1x
208	- Medium: 2.5x
209	- High: 8x
210	
211	#### Angular Tolerance
212	
213	This is the maximum angle between adjacent triangle faces that approximate a smooth surface.
214	
215	Onshape calls this "Angular deviation (deg)", and the present values are:
216	- Coarse: 12.5 deg
217	- Medium: 6.25 deg
218	- Fine: 2.5 deg
219	
220	Fusion 360 calls this "Normal Deviation", and the preset values are:
221	- Low: 30.0
222	- Medium: 15.0
223	- High: 10.0
224	In theory "Normal Deviation" should be the maximum angular error of the face relative to the surface normal, but in practice it seems to result in the given maximum angular deviation.
225	
226	### OCCT-Generated Test Models
227	
228	Models in \`tests/occt/\` and \`tests/nurbs/\` are generated directly via OCCT by
229	the \`gen-test-models\` binary (\`./scripts/generate_occt_models.sh\`) — used for
230	models that ccad cannot express. \`tests/occt/\` holds analytic models such as
231	\`hollow_cube\` (a solid with a fully enclosed internal void, for multi-shell
232	solid support). \`tests/nurbs/\` holds freeform models (exact B-spline patches,
233	conic/B-spline extrusions) exercising the stage 2.7 NURBS fallback; all 8
234	pass full \`--compare\` — see \`tests/nurbs/README.md\`. The generated STL/STEP pairs are committed.
235	
236	### Generating Test Models
237	
238	Some tests use models generated via [CodeCAD](https://codecad.xyz/). The generated STL/STEP files are committed to the repo, so CodeCAD is not required to run tests.
239	
240	To add or modify these models:
241	1. Install CodeCAD
242	2. Edit files in \`tests/ccad/parts/\` — see \`tests/ccad/README.md\` for primitive conventions and placement rules
243	3. Run \`./tests/ccad/generate_models.sh\`
244	
245	**Important:** \`box(w,d,h)\` places a corner at the origin, not centered. Use \`center_xyz()\` to center. Each part file includes analytical surface area and volume in its header comments.
246	
247	### Interactive Debugging Visualization
248	
249	Use \`--viz-stages\` to open a 3D window and step through BFS hypothesis deduction interactively.
250	Use \`--viz-stages-level\` to control how often the visualization pauses:
251	- Level 1 (default): Pauses at each committed hypothesis
252	- Level 2: Also pauses at each accepted seed before BFS expansion
253	- Level 3: Also pauses at each face accepted during BFS expansion
254	
255	\`\`\`bash
256	# Visualize planar and cylindrical hypothesis stages (committed hypotheses only)
257	brepper input.stl --viz-stages=2.1,2.2
258	
259	# Visualize with seed-level detail
260	brepper input.stl --viz-stages=2.2 --viz-stages-level=2
261	
262	# Visualize all stage 2 hypothesis types with STEP comparison overlay
263	brepper input.stl --compare reference.step --viz-stages=2.1,2.2,2.3
264	\`\`\`
265	
266	At each BFS step, the window shows the STL mesh with highlighted faces: seed faces in green, previously accepted faces in blue, the just-accepted face in dark blue, and BFS queue frontier edges in red. Cylindrical and spherical hypotheses also display translucent geometry overlays. When \`--compare\` is provided, the STEP surface is shown at 35% opacity for reference.
267	
268	| Action | Control |
269	|--------|:--------|
270	| Next step | \`Space\` |
271	| Skip to next seed/hypothesis | \`Shift+Space\` |
272	| Skip to face seed | \`Click\` on a face |
273	| Quit visualization | \`Q\` |
274	
275	Supported stages: \`2.1\` (sharp edges + jet prior), \`2.2\` (smooth regions), \`3.3\` (edge curves), \`3.4\` (faces), \`3.5\` (shells), \`3.6\` (solids). (The old per-type BFS viz stages are retired with the stage-2 rewrite.)
276	
277	\`--viz-seeds\` opens the same window on a different question — how seed sets grow rather than how the pipeline proceeds — and is documented under [Seed-growth visualization](#seed-growth-visualization---viz-seeds) above.
278	
279	
280	## Viewer
281	
282	\`viewer\` is an interactive 3D viewer for STL and STEP files.
283	
284	\`\`\`
285	USAGE:
286	    viewer [OPTIONS] <file>...
287	
288	ARGUMENTS:
289	    <file>...   One or more STL or STEP files to view (detected by extension)
290	
291	OPTIONS:
292	    --deflection <value>          Linear deflection for STEP tessellation (default: 0.1)
293	    --angular-deflection <value>  Angular deflection for STEP tessellation in degrees (default: 28.6)
294	\`\`\`
295	
296	Multiple files can be loaded simultaneously; each is rendered in a distinct color.
297	
298	### Examples
299	
300	\`\`\`bash
301	# View a single STEP file
302	./target/release/viewer part.step
303	
304	# View a STEP and an STL side by side
305	./target/release/viewer reference.step output.stl
306	
307	# Finer tessellation for curved surfaces
308	./target/release/viewer part.step --deflection 0.01 --angular-deflection 5.7
309	\`\`\`
310	
311	### Controls
312	
313	| Action | Control |
314	|--------|:--------|
315	| Rotate (around model center) | Left-click + drag |
316	| Pan | Right-click + drag |
317	| Zoom (at cursor) | Scroll wheel |
318	| Quit | \`q\` or \`Esc\` |
319	| Toggle perspective/orthographic | \`p\` |
320	| Toggle wireframe edges | \`e\` |
321	| Toggle soft (mesh) edges | \`Shift+E\` |
322	| Toggle solid faces | \`s\` |
323	| Toggle hidden-edge removal | \`h\` |
324	
325	Rendering uses PBR shading with ambient and two directional lights. Sharp feature edges (boundary edges and edges where the dihedral angle exceeds ~45°) are drawn as a solid wireframe overlay. Softer mesh edges (dihedral angle below ~45°) are drawn at 50% opacity and can be toggled independently with \`Shift+E\`. Zooming targets the point under the mouse cursor.
326	
327	### Running Tests
328	
329	\`\`\`bash
330	# Run all tests (unit + integration)
331	cargo test
332	
333	# Run only integration tests
334	cargo test --test stage1_integration
335	\`\`\`
336	
337	Integration tests in \`tests/stage1_integration.rs\` verify that:
338	- All STL files in \`tests/manual/\`, \`tests/onshape/\`, \`tests/ccad/generated/\`, and \`tests/fusion/\` pass stage 1 mesh validation and coplanar triangle fusion
339	- All STL/STEP pairs pass \`--compare\` surface distance checks (after fusion)
340	- Bad files in \`tests/bad/\` fail with expected error types (degenerate faces, non-manifold edges, inconsistent winding, compare failures)
341	
342	Integration tests in \`tests/stage2_integration.rs\` verify that:
343	- Planar hypothesis deduction produces correct counts for known planar models (cube=6, wedge=6, chamfered cube=26)
344	- Cylindrical hypothesis deduction produces correct counts and properties (simple_cylinder=1 convex, block_with_hole=1 concave, pipe=2, two_holes=2 concave)
345	- Spherical hypothesis deduction produces correct counts and properties (simple_sphere=1 convex r=10, hemisphere=1 convex r=10, spherical_pocket=1 concave r=8, ball_on_cylinder=1 sphere+1 cylinder)
346	- Surface selection (stage 2.6) produces correct surface type counts for known models (block_with_hole=6 planar+1 cylindrical, pipe=2 planar+2 cylindrical, ball_on_cylinder=1 planar+1 cylindrical+1 spherical, hemisphere=1 planar+1 spherical, simple_sphere=1 spherical, cone_15x20=1 planar+1 conical, simple_cone=2 planar+1 conical)
347	- All STL/STEP pairs pass \`--compare\` validation at stages 2.1, 2.2, 2.3, and 2.6
348	- Deduced cylinder parameters (axis direction, axis position, radius) match STEP cylinder parameters for all cylindrical test models
349	- Deduced sphere parameters (center, radius) match STEP sphere parameters for all spherical test models
350	- Angular tolerance enforcement prevents spurious cylindrical/spherical hypotheses on planar-only models (e.g., cube faces meet at 90°, exceeding the 25° default)
351	Integration tests in \`tests/stage3_integration.rs\` verify that:
352	- Adjacency graph topology (faces, edges, vertices) is correct for known models (cube=6F/12E/8V, cylinder=3F/2E/0V, sphere=1F/0E/0V, etc.)
353	- Euler's formula V-E+F=2 holds for genus-0 models
354	- Edge validity, adjacency symmetry, and edge-face consistency are maintained
355	- All STL/STEP pairs pass \`--compare\` validation at stage 3.1, verifying that reconstructed edge boundary vertices lie on STEP edges and BRep vertices coincide with STEP vertices
356	- Tangency detection (stage 3.2) correctly identifies no tangent edges for models composed of planar, cylindrical, and spherical surfaces meeting at angles > 2°
357	- Edge curve computation (stage 3.3) produces 3D curves for all edges via surface-surface intersection, verified across all test models (cube, cylinder, hemisphere, ball_on_cylinder, block_with_hole, chamfered_cube, spherical_pocket)
358	- Face creation (stage 3.4) successfully creates OCCT \`TopoDS_Face\` objects for all test models via shared-edge topological assembly: every edge is one \`TopoDS_Edge\` shared by both adjacent faces, with per-face pcurves, seam edges, and degenerate pole edges built uniformly for all surface types. All STL/STEP pairs pass \`--compare\` validation at stage 3.4
359	- Shell construction (stage 3.5) assembles faces into shells directly from the shared-edge topology (closed by construction; no sewing) and produces correctly oriented shells. All STL/STEP pairs pass \`--compare\` validation
360	- Solid construction (stage 3.6) creates solids from shells via \`ShapeFix_Solid::SolidFromShell\`. Volume comparison against STEP reference and \`BRepExtrema_DistShapeShape\` distance checks pass for all test models
361	Integration tests in \`tests/stage4_integration.rs\` verify that:
362	- STEP output files are written successfully for cube, cylinder, and sphere models
363	- All STL/STEP pairs pass \`--compare\` validation at stage 4.1, verifying volume agreement and \`BRepExtrema_DistShapeShape\` distance between written output and reference STEP

1	# STL to STEP Conversion Utility - Development Plan
2	
3	## Project Overview
4	
5	**brepper** (B-Rep from Mesh) - A utility to convert triangulated STL meshes from CAD exports into parametric STEP files with fitted analytic and freeform surfaces.
6	
7	## Design Principles
8	
9	The stage 2 architecture was rewritten twice: from the fit-driven BFS
10	hypothesis pipeline to partition-then-classify (2026-07-17), and then —
11	after the fit-free curvature-jump classifier was measured to be
12	unsalvageable (2026-07-20, see the Stage-2 Retrospective's Resolution) —
13	to the current **sharp-partition + scoped fit competition** design. These
14	principles drive it; retired mechanisms and the reasons they died are in
15	[Abandoned Approaches](#abandoned-approaches).
16	
17	1. **Exactness is the superpower.** Mesh vertices lie on the true CAD
18	   surfaces within numerical epsilon. A candidate surface either validates
19	   every claimed vertex within \`--vertex-tolerance\` or the claim is wrong —
20	   validation is decisive, not statistical. We are not solving the
21	   fit-primitives-in-noisy-scans problem the literature (RANSAC lineage)
22	   addresses.
23	2. **The answer's boundaries are already in the mesh.** CAD tessellators emit
24	   seam edges along B-rep face boundaries — *including tangent junctions*
25	   (verified 2026-07-17 on the nosecone cone–sphere tangency: 0 of 1572 STL
26	   triangles straddle the tangency ring; 104 vertices lie exactly on it). So
27	   the true segmentation is a partition of the mesh face graph whose region
28	   boundaries are a subset of mesh edges, and every region is connected.
29	   This is architectural rather than lucky, and it is worth knowing why,
30	   because the whole pipeline rests on it — see **Mesh provenance and the seam
31	   assumption** below.
32	3. **Partition by what is certain; decompose the rest by fit competition.**
33	   Sharp dihedral edges are exact and cheap — they partition the mesh into
34	   smooth regions with no calibration (measured: every sharp-edged corpus
35	   model segments perfectly by them alone). Tangent junctions inside a
36	   smooth region are NOT reliably detectable fit-free (measured: no
37	   threshold on local curvature differences separates real junctions from
38	   real curvature gradients — the classes overlap in that statistic), so
39	   they are found by fit competition: surfaces fitted from seeds compete on
40	   validated area, and the exact vertex test places the boundary.
41	4. **Curvature allocates effort; fitting decides geometry.** The per-face
42	   jet curvature field orders seeds, prunes and orders fit attempts, seeds
43	   initial parameters, and gates expensive refits — and never decides
44	   membership or boundaries. Every curvature error converts to wasted or
45	   saved time, never to wrong output.
46	5. **Repair by validation, locally.** Remaining mistakes surface as
47	   validation failures and are repaired by local fit-validated operations —
48	   resolve multi-claimed junction rows to the better-fitting side, merge
49	   fragments a neighbor's surface explains, relabel ±1-row boundary error.
50	   No global fix-up passes with chordal slop.
51	6. **Invariants are enforced, not assumed.** Before stage 3: every mesh face
52	   belongs to exactly one region; every region is mesh-connected; every
53	   region's surface validates its own faces; results are deterministic.
54	   (The abandoned pipeline's greedy selection violated connectivity —
55	   3DBenchy face 5841 reached stage 3.4 claiming three disconnected mesh
56	   regions.) These are the *coverage* invariants and they are asserted every
57	   run; the **Invariants** section below states the per-surface and per-seed
58	   ones, which are measured rather than asserted, and says how well each holds.
59	
60	## Assumptions
61	
62	- Assumes the vertices of the mesh lie precisely on the CAD surfaces, modulo numerical error/stability.
63	- Assumes transitions between shapes always have a seam — verified to hold
64	  even for tangent transitions (see Design Principles #2 and **Mesh
65	  provenance** below). This holds for every B-rep CAD tessellator; it does
66	  *not* carry information for mesh-native sources such as OpenSCAD, which are
67	  a known, deliberately unhandled gap.
68	- Assumes manifold mesh (each edge shared by exactly 2 faces).
69	- Assumes consistent face orientation (all normals point outward).
70	
71	Fails noisily if any of the assumptions are violated, after stage 1.2's
72	repair pass has fixed what can be fixed without moving a vertex
73	(\`--strict-mesh\` disables repair).
74	
75	### Mesh provenance and the seam assumption
76	
77	Design Principle #2 — that a B-rep face boundary is always a chain of mesh
78	edges, tangent or not — is load-bearing for the entire pipeline, so this
79	records why it holds and where it stops holding. (Researched 2026-07-28.)
80	
81	**Why it holds: every B-rep faceter is edge-first.** They all discretize each
82	edge *once*, shared by both adjacent faces, and then fill each face's
83	parametric domain out to those fixed boundary polylines. This is not a
84	stylistic choice a vendor might change — it is how watertightness is
85	guaranteed. OCCT states it outright: "At the first step all edges from a face
86	are discretized… At the second step, the faces are tessellated", with "edges
87	tessellation data … used to form contours of target faces and passed as input
88	to the triangulation algorithm" and "each face is processed separately". ACIS
89	is documented as "maintaining the edge consistency between adjacent faces";
90	Parasolid's vertex-matching machinery exists so that neighbouring face meshes
91	meet exactly. A tangent edge is an edge in the *topology*, so it is discretized
92	like any other and no triangle can straddle it.
93	
94	**What the likely sources are.** For models destined for STL and print-sharing
95	sites:
96	
97	| Tool | Kernel | Faceter |
98	|------|--------|---------|
99	| Fusion 360, Inventor | ShapeManager (Autodesk's ACIS fork) | quad-tree gridding |
100	| SolidWorks, Onshape, Solid Edge, Shapr3D, Plasticity | Parasolid | per-face, vendor |
101	| FreeCAD | Open CASCADE | **Delaunay** (Watson) in UV space |
102	| Rhino | own | regular quad grid + recursive subdivision |
103	| Tinkercad, SketchUp, Blender, OpenSCAD | none — mesh/CSG native | n/a |
104	
105	Note the corpus is Onshape-heavy (Parasolid) plus CodeCAD, so it is *not*
106	representative of the faceter mix in the wild.
107	
108	**Delaunay does occur, and the assumption survives it.** FreeCAD — the
109	fastest-growing free option, and the same mesher brepper itself uses — meshes
110	with OCCT's \`BRepMesh\`, which is genuinely Delaunay. But it is a *constrained*
111	Delaunay whose constraints are the pre-discretized face boundaries, so seams
112	are preserved exactly as elsewhere. What differs between faceters is the
113	*interior* pattern: grid-based faceters (ACIS, Rhino, Parasolid) leave a
114	strongly structured, anisotropic mesh, Delaunay much less so. The practical
115	consequence is that **boundary preservation is dependable across all of them,
116	while sampling density and anisotropy are corroborating evidence only** — worth
117	remembering if the tessellation layout is ever used as a signal (it is not
118	today; stage 2 uses only dihedral angle and the curvature jet).
119	
120	**OpenSCAD and other mesh-native sources: a known gap, not handled.** These
121	have no B-rep at any stage — \`cylinder()\` is a prism and \`sphere()\` a
122	polyhedron from the moment they are created, with CSG run on polyhedra (CGAL,
123	or the newer Manifold backend). Consequences:
124	
125	- *The seam assumption holds trivially and uselessly.* Every facet is planar,
126	  so no triangle can span an orientation change — a stronger guarantee than any
127	  B-rep faceter gives. But **every** edge is a facet boundary, so nothing
128	  distinguishes an intended face boundary from a discretization step. The seam
129	  carries no information; only the curvature jump does (a constant dihedral
130	  through a fillet, dropping to 0° on the flat it meets).
131	- *There are no tangencies.* What was meant as a C¹ junction becomes a finite
132	  dihedral of one discretization step. OpenSCAD's fragment rule is
133	  \`n = ceil(max(min(360/$fa, r*2*PI/$fs), 5))\` with defaults \`$fa = 12\`,
134	  \`$fs = 2\`, so \`n\` caps at 30 and *every* curve carries a dihedral of at least
135	  12°.
136	- *Our \`--angular-tolerance\` of 25° is therefore the arbiter*, with a sharp
137	  crossover: \`$fn ≥ 15\` — or, on defaults, radius ≳ 4.5 mm, where
138	  \`ceil(πr) ≥ 15\` — reads as smooth and gets an analytic fit, while \`$fn ≤ 14\`
139	  reads as sharp and stays a prism. A \`$fn = 6\` hex nut correctly stays
140	  hexagonal; the near-ubiquitous \`$fn = 100\` reads as smooth.
141	- *Where a fit is attempted it will succeed easily.* OpenSCAD **inscribes** its
142	  polygons — the reason holes print undersized — so a prism's vertices lie
143	  exactly on the ideal cylinder of radius r, and vertex validation passes at
144	  ~zero residual. The binding check is the centroid one against
145	  \`--surface-tolerance\`: the sagitta is \`r(1 − cos(180/n))\`, which is 0.11 mm
146	  for r = 20, n = 30 (passes 0.4) but 0.55 mm for r = 100, n = 30 (fails, so
147	  the surface degrades to per-facet planes). Large-radius curves at default
148	  resolution are thus the expected failure mode.
149	- *The ambiguity is genuine, not a defect.* A 15-gon prism and a coarsely
150	  tessellated cylinder are the same mesh; nothing in it says which the designer
151	  meant. \`--angular-tolerance\` decides, which makes it a policy dial here
152	  rather than a measurement.
153	
154	We are not addressing this yet. When we do, the likely shape is a flag marking
155	the input as faceted-by-construction, or auto-detection — see TODO.md. Two
156	signals look promising for detection: an OpenSCAD revolution has a *constant*
157	dihedral of exactly 360/n around the whole curve (a B-rep tessellation's steps
158	vary and its density changes at seams), and its vertices sit exactly on the
159	circumscribed circle rather than straddling the true surface.
160	
161	## Invariants
162	
163	The point of these is consistency: the surfaces recovered from a mesh should be a
164	function of the mesh, not of facet ordering, seed choice, or traversal order.
165	They are stated as near-invariants because they are asked of a float32 mesh, so
166	"holds" means "holds to a bound derived from the mesh's own precision".
167	
168	**All of them have now been measured** against \`--compare\` ground truth over 147
169	models and 2303 reference faces (\`--invariant-report\`, see below). Every clause
170	carries its measured status. Where a clause was refuted the refutation is kept
171	rather than deleted, because several of the refuted forms are the obvious ones and
172	will otherwise be re-derived.
173	
174	### Surface Fitting Requirement
175	
176	One rule for every analytic type and for NURBS, replacing the per-type variants
177	this section used to carry:
178	
179	* **All vertices within \`--vertex-tolerance\` of the surface.**
180	* **All edge midpoints within ¾ · \`--surface-tolerance\`** — the edges of a
181	  *triangulation* of the facet, which for a fused quad means its two diagonals as
182	  well as its four sides.
183	* **No two adjacent facets of one surface separated by more than
184	  \`--angular-tolerance\`** — as a post-hoc consistency check only, never as a
185	  membership rule. See Surface Identification.
186	
187	**Why edge midpoints, and why the ¾.** Write the facet's deviation from the
188	surface as a height function vanishing at the vertices. To second order it is a
189	quadratic, and in barycentric coordinates
190	\`e(λ) = −Σ_{i<j} λᵢλⱼ · (pᵢ−pⱼ)ᵀH(pᵢ−pⱼ)\`. At the midpoint of edge \`ij\` that is
191	\`|qᵢⱼ|/8\`; maximised over the simplex it is at most \`max|q|/6\`. So
192	
193	> **max over the facet ∈ [M, (4/3)·M]**, where \`M\` is the largest edge-midpoint
194	> deviation.
195	
196	Checking edge midpoints and allowing ¾ of the tolerance is therefore a *bound* on
197	the whole facet, not a proxy for it — which answers the two TODOs this section
198	used to carry about sampling facet interiors, including for NURBS. Cost is about
199	1.5 evaluations per triangle, since each interior mesh edge is shared.
200	
201	Measured over 895 non-degenerate reference faces, ratio of the true whole-facet
202	maximum to each candidate probe:
203	
204	| probe | p95 | max | over 4/3 |
205	|---|---|---|---|
206	| boundary edge midpoints only | 1.742 | 1.999 | 63 of 895 |
207	| **edge midpoints + quad diagonals** | **1.012** | **1.497** | **1 of 895** |
208	| facet centroid | 1.384 | 2.239 | — |
209	
210	**Facet centroids are not a bound and are dropped.** The measured worst case,
211	2.239, matches the derived 9/4 for a needle triangle to three digits; and where
212	the curvature is indefinite (a saddle, a torus's inner equator) the centroid can
213	read *exactly zero* while the facet is off by the full sag. 23 corpus faces read
214	under a quarter of their edge-midpoint maximum. The single face that exceeds 4/3
215	with diagonals included is a 16-facet "plane" on a wild-corpus model that is
216	probably not planar.
217	
218	**The vertex clause holds at the mesh's own precision, not at a fixed number.**
219	On verified synthetic ground truth: plane p95 0.64 quanta, cylinder 1.22, cone
220	1.22, sphere 1.49, torus 1.45; worst case ~5 quanta. But two true cylinders on
221	\`stepped_block_toroidal_fillets_fine\` sit at 8.8 and 8.5 quanta = 7.7e-5 mm,
222	**outside the 5e-5 default**, so at today's tolerance the requirement is
223	unsatisfiable on those two surfaces and no algorithm can recover them. State the
224	bar in float32 position bounds (Phase 0.6 supplies the bound).
225	
226	**\`--surface-tolerance\` is barely non-binding.** The true worst facet sag over the
227	corpus is 0.325 mm against the 0.4 mm default — 1.23× margin — while the p50 is
228	2.2e-6 mm. Five orders of magnitude of spread under one constant; see Phase 3.2
229	for the per-face alternative.
230	
```
