```
fn resolve_claims(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    region_faces: &[usize],
    committed: &mut Vec<CompeteHyp>,
    claim_lists: &[Vec<usize>],
    vtol: f64,
    config: &CompeteConfig,
) -> (Vec<CompeteHyp>, Vec<usize>) {
    let hyp_area: Vec<f64> = committed
        .iter()
        .map(|h| h.faces().iter().map(|&fi| face_area(&mesh.faces[fi], &mesh.vertices)).sum())
        .collect();

    let mut assigned: Vec<Vec<usize>> = vec![Vec::new(); committed.len()];
    let mut leftovers: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();

    for &fi in region_faces {
        let claimants = &claim_lists[fi];
        if claimants.is_empty() {
            leftovers.push(fi);
            continue;
        }
        if claimants.len() == 1 {
            assigned[claimants[0]].push(fi);
            continue;
        }
        let dist = |ci: usize| max_vertex_dist(mesh, &committed[ci], fi);
        // Among claimants that ALREADY explain the face within vertex
        // tolerance, prefer the simplest surface (lowest DOF), then largest
        // area, then lowest index: a face on both a cylinder and a torus near
        // their tangency is the cylinder's; a face on a real fillet and a
        // spurious thin junction torus (both sub-micron) is the larger
        // fillet's. Comparing absolute best-fit here instead would let a tiny
        // tighter sliver steal it and fragment one surface into a chain.
        let within: Vec<usize> = claimants.iter().copied().filter(|&ci| dist(ci) <= vtol).collect();
        let winner = if !within.is_empty() {
            *within
                .iter()
                .min_by(|&&a, &&b| {
                    committed[a]
                        .dof_rank()
                        .cmp(&committed[b].dof_rank())
                        .then_with(|| hyp_area[b].partial_cmp(&hyp_area[a]).unwrap())
                        .then_with(|| a.cmp(&b))
                })
                .unwrap()
        } else {
            // No claimant fits within tolerance — best-fit, with a 2× margin
            // to leave the larger-area claimant (a true junction face fits
            // both sides equally; the margin prevents flapping).
            let mut order: Vec<usize> = claimants.clone();
            order.sort_by(|&a, &b| {
                hyp_area[b].partial_cmp(&hyp_area[a]).unwrap().then_with(|| a.cmp(&b))
            });
            let mut winner = order[0];
            let mut winner_d = dist(winner);
            for &ci in &order[1..] {
                let d = dist(ci);
                if d * 2.0 < winner_d {
                    winner = ci;
                    winner_d = d;
                }
            }
            winner
        };
        assigned[winner].push(fi);
    }

    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for (ci, mut hyp) in committed.drain(..).enumerate() {
        let faces = std::mem::take(&mut assigned[ci]);
        if faces.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &faces);
        hyp.set_faces(faces, verts);
        // The fit was computed on the support the flood grew, which included
        // every face this hypothesis could reach — junction rows it has now
        // lost to a better claimant among them. Those rows are exactly the ones
        // that pull a fit off true, so a hypothesis that has just been trimmed
        // is carrying the error of faces it no longer owns. Refit on what it
        // actually kept. (Measured on rounded_cube fine, whose r = 2 edge
        // fillets read 1.9976–1.9984 with no vertex closer than 5e-4 mm to
        // their own surface, against a mesh whose vertices are 1.9e-6 mm from
        // the true CAD surfaces; refitting takes them to 2.0000.)
        refit_in_place(mesh, &mut hyp, config);
        out.push(hyp);
    }
    (out, leftovers)
}


/// Refit a committed hypothesis to its current face set, keeping the existing
/// fit if the fitter cannot produce one.
fn refit_in_place(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, hyp: &mut CompeteHyp, config: &CompeteConfig) {
    let faces = hyp.faces().to_vec();
    let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &faces);
    let v = config.verbosity;
    match hyp {
        CompeteHyp::Planar(h) => {
            if let Some(fit) = super::surface::cached_fit::<PlanarSurface>(mesh, &faces, &verts, v) {
                *h = PlanarSurface::make_hypothesis(mesh, faces, verts, &fit);
            }
        }
        CompeteHyp::Conical(h) => {
            if let Some(mut fit) = super::surface::cached_fit::<ConicalSurface>(mesh, &faces, &verts, v) {
                ConicalSurface::determine_convexity(mesh, &faces, &mut fit);
                *h = ConicalSurface::make_hypothesis(mesh, faces, verts, &fit);
            }
        }
        CompeteHyp::Spherical(h) => {
            if let Some(mut fit) = super::surface::cached_fit::<SphericalSurface>(mesh, &faces, &verts, v) {
                SphericalSurface::determine_convexity(mesh, &faces, &mut fit);
                *h = SphericalSurface::make_hypothesis(mesh, faces, verts, &fit);
            }
        }
        CompeteHyp::Toroidal(h) => {
            if let Some(mut fit) = super::surface::cached_fit::<ToroidalSurface>(mesh, &faces, &verts, v) {
                ToroidalSurface::determine_convexity(mesh, &faces, &mut fit);
                *h = ToroidalSurface::make_hypothesis(mesh, faces, verts, &fit);
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Max distance from face \`fi\`'s vertices to a committed hypothesis.
fn max_vertex_dist(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, hyp: &CompeteHyp, fi: usize) -> f64 {
    let face = &mesh.faces[fi];
    let vc = face.vertex_count as usize;
    face.vertex_indices[..vc]
        .iter()
        .map(|&vi| {
            let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
            let p = [v.x, v.y, v.z];
            match hyp {
                CompeteHyp::Planar(h) => {
                    (h.normal[0] * p[0] + h.normal[1] * p[1] + h.normal[2] * p[2] - h.distance).abs()
                }
                CompeteHyp::Conical(h) => {
                    if h.is_cylinder() {
                        super::cylindrical::vertex_to_cylinder_distance(
                            v, &h.apex, &h.axis_direction, h.radius_at_apex,
                        )
                        .abs()
                    } else {
                        super::conical::vertex_to_cone_distance(v, &h.apex, &h.axis_direction, h.half_angle)
                            .abs()
                    }
                }
                CompeteHyp::Spherical(h) => {
                    super::spherical::vertex_to_sphere_distance(v, &h.center, h.radius).abs()
                }
                CompeteHyp::Toroidal(h) => super::toroidal::vertex_to_torus_distance(
                    v,
                    &h.center,
                    &h.axis_direction,
                    h.major_radius,
                    h.minor_radius,
                )
                .abs(),
            }
        })
        .fold(0.0_f64, f64::max)
}
```

```
### The measured starting point

On \`simple_cone\` (true half-angle 9.4623°, apex at (0,0,60)), a two-quad seed
whose six vertices lie in two rings of three spanning 31.3° of arc:

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| reference parameters' residual on those six vertices | 4.1e-7 mm = 0.01× vtol = 0.40 quanta |
| \`fit_cone\`'s half-angle | **2.54°** |
| \`axis_normals_consistent\` on that fit | correctly refuses it |
### Option C — two circles from the ring structure

Two ruling-aligned quads give six vertices in two rings of three, one per rim.
Three points in space determine a unique circle, so each rim yields a centre, a
radius and a normal; the line through the two centres is the axis and the two
radii at two heights give the half-angle by similar triangles. Exact, vertices
only, non-iterative, and it works from **2 facets**.

Measured on the seed above: axis **0.0002°** off, half-angle **0.0001°** off,
the two radii recovered to 0.1–0.2× vtol, against a mesh error of 4.1e-7 mm.
Conditioning is comfortable rather than marginal — the rings span 31.3°, and the
sensitivity \`2ε/α²\` gives a radius uncertainty of 1.1e-5 mm, under a quarter of
vtol.

**Cost and weakness.** Needs the ruling structure the other options do not: two
rings with ≥3 points each, i.e. ruling-aligned facets. Phase 1.0 measured 25.6%
of corpus cylinder facets straddling three or more rulings, so this cannot be the
only route. Ring identification needs no provisional axis — the shared edge
between two quads in a strip *is* a ruling, so its endpoints are one per ring and
walking the strip labels the rest combinatorially.

**Built 2026-10-15 as \`initialize::cone_from_rings\`; measured; not wired.** Two
departures from the design above, and the reason it stays unwired.

- *Rims are found, not labelled.* "A shared edge is a ruling" holds only for
  quads in one band; in a triangle strip the shared edges alternate between
  rulings and diagonals. Instead every split of the seed's vertices into two
  groups of ≥3 is tried — at most \`2^(n−1)\`, with \`n\` capped at 10 by a work
  bound that decides nothing — each scored by the largest distance of any vertex
  from the cone the split implies. The true split scores at the mesh's own
  precision and a wrong one misses by a wide margin. Unit-tested exact to 1e-9 at
  10°–84°, from **two quads or four triangles** alike.
- *Taper, not apex.* The profile is \`ρ = r₁ + t·h\`, so a split reading \`t = 0\`
  is a cylinder at a regular point rather than an apex at infinity (and is left
  to the caller's own cylinder route).

**Why it is not wired: two coaxial circles always lie on a cone.** A single band
of *any* surface of revolution has its vertices on two coaxial circles, so this
route finds an **exact** cone on a band of a torus fillet just as it does on a
real cone. Wired into \`fit_surface\` it committed a 17-face, 360° impostor cone on
\`filleted_pipe\` and broke that model. Nothing at band level separates the two —
not the residual, and not the facet normals either, because a facet's plane is
fixed by vertices that lie on both surfaces. This is the Invariants section's
"two circles lie exactly on a sphere" with the sphere replaced by a cone, and it
belongs to the same family of answers: discrimination has to come from beyond
the band (the torus continues smoothly into the next band; the cone's band ends
at its rims), i.e. from competition or branching, not from a better fit.

### Considered and rejected

- **Solving the 6-DOF system from exactly six points.** Exactly determined, so
  finitely many right circular cones pass through them — but a polynomial system
  with multiple roots and no least-squares character. It is also the configuration
  where a *second exact cone* was measured: on one \`simple_cone\` seed the fitter
  returned half-angle 72.85° with its apex 10.8 patch-extents away, explaining the
  six vertices to 6.7e-16 mm, i.e. better than the true cone manages against a
  float32 mesh. Six points genuinely admit more than one cone; Option C escapes
  that only because the ring structure supplies information beyond the six
  positions.
- **Reordering \`compute_truncated_cone_axis\` to try the exact normal-difference
  method before the apex→centroid guess.** Tried, and much worse — see the DO-NOT
  note on that function. Differencing near-identical normals destroys the signal.
- **Orthogonal-distance geometric fitting** (Lukács et al.; Ahn, *Least Squares
  Orthogonal Distance Fitting of Curves and Surfaces*, Springer LNCS 3151). This
  is the right *refinement* and is essentially what the existing LM already does.
  It does not address initialization, which is where every measured failure is.

### Sources

- Andrews, J.; Séquin, C. H. *Type-Constrained Direct Fitting of Quadric
  Surfaces.* Computer-Aided Design & Applications 10(a), 2013.
- Andrews, J.; Séquin, C. H. *Generalized, basis-independent kinematic surface

- Lukács, G.; Martin, R.; Marshall, D. *Faithful Least-Squares Fitting of Spheres,

- Petitjean, S. *A survey of methods for recovering quadrics in triangle meshes.*

- Pottmann, H.; Lee, I.-K.; Randrup, T. *Reconstruction of kinematic surfaces from
  scattered data.* 1998.
- Taubin, G. / Pratt, V. — direct algebraic surface fitting, the source of the
  generalized-eigenvalue form used in Options A and B.

## Nested fitting: a rank ladder instead of a type ladder (surveyed 2026-08-06)

The question this section answers: **could one fitter, run on a growing patch,
return "the simplest surface that explains what I have so far" — plane, then
cylinder, then cone, then sphere, then torus — with the type an *output* rather
than a precondition?** Asked because that is the missing piece of Phase 1.2. The
earn loop died on a chicken-and-egg — "a cone cannot be fitted from the two
facets a validated loop has when it must first decide, so it never grows" — and
a fitter that never has to decide first does not have that problem.

This is a survey with the option set, the costs, and the two families that are
*not* the answer. **The rank-ladder claim has since been measured** — see "The
rank ladder measured" below, which demotes it from backbone to complement: it is
decisive for sphere and plane and structurally blind to the cylinder. Read the
derivation first; the verdict depends on it.
```

```
extra_flags() {
    case "$1" in
        *rounded_cube_10_r2_coarse*) echo "--angular-tolerance 20" ;;
        *) echo "" ;;
    esac
}

# Every STL under tests/ except:
#   bad/         inputs that must FAIL; the suite pins their exact errors
#   *.ascii.stl  duplicate geometry, pinned by a reader test instead
model_list() {
    find tests -name '*.stl' \
        -not -path 'tests/bad/*' \
        -not -name '*.ascii.stl' \
    | sort \
    | { [ -n "$FILTER" ] && grep -E "$FILTER" || cat; }
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# One model
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

run_one() {
    local stl="$1"
    local model="${stl#tests/}"; model="${model%.stl}"
    local step flags log outstep start end secs rc
    step=$(find_step "$stl")
    flags=$(extra_flags "$stl")
    log=$(mktemp); outstep="$log.step"

    start=$(date +%s.%N)
    if [ -n "$step" ]; then
        timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$BREPPER" "$stl" -o "$outstep" --compare "$step" -v $flags \
            >"$log" 2>&1
    else
        timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$BREPPER" "$stl" -o "$outstep" -v $flags >"$log" 2>&1
    fi
    rc=$?
    end=$(date +%s.%N)
    secs=$(awk "BEGIN{printf \"%.2f\", $end - $start}")

    local status=ok
    [ $rc -eq 0 ] || status=fail
    [ $rc -eq 124 ] && status=timeout

    # "Stage 2 types: 2 plane, 2 cyl, 0 cone, 0 sphere, 4 torus, 0 bspline (8 total)"
    local types
    types=$(grep -m1 '^Stage 2 types:' "$log" \
        | sed -E 's/^Stage 2 types: ([0-9]+) plane, ([0-9]+) cyl, ([0-9]+) cone, ([0-9]+) sphere, ([0-9]+) torus, ([0-9]+) bspline \(([0-9]+) total\)/\7\t\1\t\2\t\3\t\4\t\5\t\6/')
    [ -n "$types" ] || types=$(printf -- '-\t-\t-\t-\t-\t-\t-')

    local edge vol note
    edge=$(grep -m1 'Compare 3.1: edge boundary max dist' "$log" \
        | sed -E 's/.*max dist ([0-9.e+-]+) mm.*/\1/')
    [ -n "$edge" ] || edge=-
    vol=$(grep -m1 'Compare 4.1: output volume' "$log" \
        | sed -E 's/.*rel diff ([0-9.e+-]+)\).*/\1/')
    [ -n "$vol" ] || vol=-
    note=""
    if [ "$status" != ok ]; then
        note=$(grep -m1 -iE '^Error|panicked at' "$log" | tr '\t' ' ' | cut -c1-160)
        [ "$status" = timeout ] && note="timed out after ${TIMEOUT}s"
    fi

    # $types is itself seven tab-separated fields, so this is one row of the
    # 14 documented columns.
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
        "$model" "$status" "$([ -n "$step" ] && echo step || echo none)" \
        "$types" "$edge" "$vol" "$secs" "$note"
    # Progress on stderr: rows are sorted at the end, so without this a
    # ten-minute sweep looks like a hang.
    printf '  %-8s %6ss  %s\n' "$status" "$secs" "$model" >&2
    rm -f "$log" "$outstep"
}
```

```
pub(super) fn compete_from_seed(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    in_region: &[bool],
    seed: usize,
    jet: &[JetField],
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    config: &CompeteConfig,
    flat_eps: f64,
    debug: bool,
) -> Option<(CompeteHyp, f64, u8)> {
    {
        let jf = jet[seed];
        // Dominant / secondary principal-curvature MAGNITUDES. The jet orders
        // k1 ≥ k2 by signed value, so for a concave feature (a hole wall,
        // κ = −1/r) the dominant curvature is negative and lands in k2 —
        // taking |k1| as the dominant would read the wall's flat axial
        // direction and treat the hole as planar. Order by magnitude instead.
        let a1 = jf.k1.abs().max(jf.k2.abs());
        let a2 = jf.k1.abs().min(jf.k2.abs());

        // Grow the jet-pruned candidate types; keep the largest validated
        // area (simplest-DOF tiebreak).
        let mut best: Option<(CompeteHyp, f64, u8)> = None; // (hyp, area, dof)
        let consider = |hyp_area: Option<(CompeteHyp, f64)>, dof: u8, best: &mut Option<(CompeteHyp, f64, u8)>| {
            if let Some((h, area)) = hyp_area {
                let sweep = candidate_sweep(mesh, &h);
                if sweep < MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG.to_radians() {
                    if debug {
                        eprintln!(
                            "    compete: seed {seed} rejected {} sweeping only {:.1}\u{00b0} about its axis — radius undetermined ({} faces, area {area:.2})",
                            h.kind_name(),
                            sweep.to_degrees(),
                            h.faces().len(),
                        );
                    }
                    return;
                }
                let better = match best {
                    None => true,
                    Some((_, ba, bd)) => area > *ba + 1e-9 || ((area - *ba).abs() <= 1e-9 && dof < *bd),
                };
                if better {
                    *best = Some((h, area, dof));
                }
            }
        };

        // Plane is always a candidate (cheap; catches misread flats).
        let plane = grow::<PlanarSurface>(mesh, in_region, seed, jet, centroids, config, 1);
```

```
/// Refit a committed hypothesis to its current face set, keeping the existing

```

**After:**
```
/// Committed hypotheses that are redundant: every one of their faces is also
/// claimed, and explained within `vtol`, by a single other claimant of strictly
/// larger area. Returns `(dropped, container)` per hypothesis.
///
/// Per-face resolution alone cannot see this. It hands a face several claimants
/// explain to the lowest-DOF one, which is right at a tangency — a face on both
/// a cylinder and its fillet torus is the cylinder's — but wrong when the
/// simpler claimant is merely a *piece* of the more complex one: a cone fitted
/// to one facet band of a torus is exact on that band (two coaxial circles
/// always lie on a cone, SURFACE_FITTING.md "Option C"), and it would carve the
/// band out of the fillet. A cylinder is never wholly inside its fillet, so the
/// tangency rule is untouched; an impostor confined to a band of a larger
/// surface always is.
fn contained_hypotheses(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    committed: &[CompeteHyp],
    claim_lists: &[Vec<usize>],
    hyp_area: &[f64],
    vtol: f64,
) -> Vec<(bool, usize)> {
    (0..committed.len())
        .map(|ci| {
            let faces = committed[ci].faces();
            let Some(&first) = faces.first() else { return (false, ci) };
            claim_lists[first]
                .iter()
                .copied()
                .filter(|&cj| cj != ci && hyp_area[cj] > hyp_area[ci])
                .find(|&cj| {
                    faces.iter().all(|&fi| {
                        claim_lists[fi].contains(&cj) && max_vertex_dist(mesh, &committed[cj], fi) <= vtol
                    })
                })
                .map_or((false, ci), |cj| (true, cj))
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Refit a committed hypothesis to its current face set, keeping the existing
/// fit if the fitter cannot produce one.
```

```
columns names the guard that refused it.

### Seed-growth visualization (\`--viz-seeds\`)

Opens the 3D window and walks **anchor facets**, stopping on each one for which
*every* conforming seed set fails to grow to its surface. Requires \`--compare\`.

\`\`\`bash
./target/release/brepper tests/ccad/generated/simple_cone.stl   --compare tests/ccad/generated/simple_cone.step --stage 2.2   --viz-seeds --viz-seed-spec-only --viz-seed-samples 12 -v
\`\`\`

| colour | meaning |
|--------|---------|
| white | the anchor facet |
| green | the rest of the seed set |
| blue | correctly covered |
| red | overshoot — grown past the true boundary |
| orange | true facets that **blocked** further growth |
| yellow | true facets missed for some other reason |

Controls are the same as \`--viz-stages\`: \`Space\` next seed set, \`Shift+Space\` next
reference face, \`Q\` quit. The status line names the seed shape, how far the seed
sits from its own fit, and the diagnosis — which validation clause refused what,
since \`face_validates\` is a conjunction of vertex distance, centroid distance and
orientation coherence and naming only the first is misleading.

\`BREPPER_VIZ_SEEDS_TEXT=1\` prints the same diagnoses with no window, which is what
the corpus catalogues are built from.

See [DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md](DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md) for full documentation.

### Tolerance Settings

#### Surface Tolerance

This is how far the surface of a mesh triangle is allowed to deviate from the surface it is approximating.

Onshape calls this "Chordal tolerance (mm)", and the preset values are:
- Coarse: 0.24 mm
- Medium: 0.12 mm
- Fine: 0.06 mm
```

```
**The cone is the type where identification currently fails**, and the cause is
the fitter rather than the information. On \`simple_cone\`, a two-quad seed whose six
vertices determine the cone to **0.0001°** (two rings of three spanning 31.3°;
circumcircle radii to 0.1–0.2× vtol) produces a \`fit_cone\` half-angle of **2.54°**
against a true 9.4623°. \`axis_normals_consistent\` correctly refuses that, and the
fallback cylinder then misses its own seed vertices by 222.7× vtol. Of the cone
rung's refusals, 42% are the axis-normal check, 27% a half-angle outside
[2°, 85°], 12% an apex 429–2128 mm from a 41 mm model. The guards are right; the
initialization is not. Options are catalogued in SURFACE_FITTING.md, "Cone
initialization".

*Update 2026-10-15.* One initialization defect turned out to be structural and is
fixed: the fitter's axis came from the uncentred normal covariance, which cannot
fit a cone wider than ~35° at all, and the centred-normal seed now backs it up
(gated — see SURFACE_FITTING.md for why the gate matters). Cone facets with a
working seed set on the three models above: \`simple_cone\` 4/12 → **8/12**,
\`cone_cylinder\` 7/12 → **12/12**, \`nosecone\` 10/12 → **12/12**. Option C (two
rims) takes \`simple_cone\` to 12/12 as well, but it is exact on a single band of
*any* surface of revolution and so manufactures impostor cones on torus bands;
it is built and not wired.

**One genuinely non-identifiable case exists** and is worth knowing: on one
\`simple_cone\` seed the fitter returned a half-angle 72.85° cone with its apex 10.8
patch-extents away that explains the six vertices to 6.7e-16 mm — *better* than
the true cone manages against a float32 mesh. Six points admit more than one right
circular cone. It is the exception (8 of 9 cone failures are convergence, not
identifiability), but it bounds what any optimizer can be asked to do.

Because a NURBS surface can have sub-surfaces that fit other types (a cylindrical
strip around an ellipsoid's equator), NURBS identification is left out of these
  allowed to grow, and the cone does not hold — for a reason that is a fitter
  defect rather than an invariant that needs weakening.

Still open:

- **Whether the sharp partition belongs in the growth invariant at all.** Growth
  confined to a smooth region cannot cover a surface the partition has cut, and
  stage 2.1 cuts 68 true surfaces on 350 edges (see 2.1(a)). Unconfined growth
  covers those but runs across tangent junctions instead. Neither bound is right
  as stated.
- **A cone seed rule that works**, which needs the fitter fixed first. *Partly
  done 2026-10-15*: the wide-cone half of the fitter defect is fixed (above). The
  two-facet half is not — Option C solves it exactly but is exact on a single
  band of every surface of revolution, so it needs a discrimination mechanism
  beyond the band before it can be wired.
- **NURBS**, deliberately excluded above.

## Dependencies

| Library | Purpose | Version |
|---------|---------|---------|

- **1.1 Closed-form initializers, unit-tested first** **DONE 2026-07-31** —
  \`src/stage2/initialize.rs\`, 8 unit tests. **Wiring update 2026-08-06: the TORUS
  initializer is now consumed**, as a second candidate inside
  \`ToroidalSurface::fit_surface\`, LM-refined and selected against the geometric
  fit on residual. The cylinder, sphere and cone ones remain unconsumed.
  **Wiring update 2026-10-15:** the torus candidate is now **gated** — consulted
  only when the geometric fit misses \`RESCUE_ERR_THRESHOLD\`, accepted only if it
  meets it — which keeps the filleted seed wins (24/24, 24/24, 48/48 anchors) and
  returns stepped_block fine to 76. The **cone**'s centred taper seed is now
  consumed too (\`initialize::cone_taper_seed\`, same gate), fixing wide cones; and
  Option C (\`initialize::cone_from_rings\`) is built and deliberately unwired
  because two coaxial circles always lie on a cone, which makes it an impostor
  generator on torus bands.
  What forced it was a separate defect in \`fit_torus_inner\`: it picked the **25th
  percentile** of adjacent-pair normal-line radius estimates to separate tube from
  azimuthal readings, which is a statistic on a sample of four and on a small
  vertex star lands in the wrong population — producing an axis a quarter-turn off
  with the data on the fitted torus's inner equator (\`filleted_hole_block\`:
  R 20.7 / r 18.7 against a true 9 / 2, 193× vtol, where the reference's own
  parameters fit the same 16 vertices to 2.1 float32 quanta and the sum-squared
  residual at the truth was 1.4e7× smaller). Replaced by a candidate sweep selected
  on residual; no tolerance added. Together the two changes take the fraction of
  torus facets with a workable seed set from 25/54/90% to **100/100/100%** on
  \`filleted_hole_block\`, \`filleted_cylinder\`, \`filleted_pipe\`. **Cost:**
  \`stepped_block\` fine 75 → 127 surfaces, medium loses a torus, and
```

```
#[test]
fn competition_nosecone_cone_sphere_base() {
    // The nosecone's cone+sphere tangent chain is one region; the base disk
    // is a separate sharp-bounded plane. Competition + the ladder together
    // yield cone + sphere + base = 3 surfaces (the reference's 3 faces).
    let out = run("tests/onshape/nosecone_medium.stl");
    let [planar, _, cones, spheres, _, _] = selected_counts(&out);
    assert_eq!(spheres, 1, "1 nose sphere");
    assert_eq!(cones, 1, "1 body cone");
    assert_eq!(planar, 1, "1 base plane");
    assert_eq!(out.selected_surfaces.len(), 3, "cone + sphere + base");
    assert_total_coverage(&out);
}

#[test]
fn competition_stepped_block_fillet_network_stays_analytic() {
    // A dense fillet network — 37 cylinders + 18 tori + 16 planes in the
    // reference — tangent-connects the whole model into ONE 26122-face region,
    // so every surface has to come out of competition.
    //
    // This model used to collapse entirely to per-facet planes: one r = 0.5
    // fillet band, a single quad tall between two corner tori, left the axis so
    // weakly constrained that a bogus 12° cone beat the true cylinder on
    // residual, and the leftover blob that left behind tripped classify.rs's
    // whole-region discard. Then it decomposed but over-fitted: near-cylindrical
    // tori ate perimeter fillets and near-planar cylinders ate wall strips,
    // each winning on area as a super-model of the surface it displaced
    // (see \`MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG\`).
    //
    // The decomposition now matches the reference exactly, surface for surface,
    // and \`onshape_stepped_block_toroidal_fine_stage41_compare\` checks the
    // geometry that comes out of it.
    let out = run("tests/onshape/stepped_block_toroidal_fillets_fine.stl");
    let [planar, cylinders, cones, spheres, tori, bsplines] = selected_counts(&out);
    assert_eq!(tori, 18, "the reference's 18 corner-blend tori");
    assert_eq!(cylinders, 37, "the reference's 37 fillet cylinders");
    assert_eq!(planar, 16, "the reference's 16 planes");
    assert_eq!((cones, spheres, bsplines), (0, 0, 0), "no cones, spheres or freeform");
    assert_eq!(out.selected_surfaces.len(), 71, "the reference's 71 surfaces");
    assert_total_coverage(&out);
}

/// Every tangent junction must end up on the mesh-edge chain the two fitted
/// surfaces' junction geometry picks out (stage 2.4 boundary snap,
/// \`locus.rs\`). This is the property snap exists to establish, and it is
/// stronger than a surface count: a boundary one tessellation row off leaves
/// the counts intact and shows up only here (and, much later, as a stage-3
/// \`--compare\` edge distance).
///
/// The second number is how many adjacent pairs have a junction geometry
/// \`locus.rs\` does not implement — cone-plane ruling tangency, non-coaxial
/// pairs other than the cylinder-to-torus tube junction, point tangencies.
/// Every corpus model here reaches zero of both; a rise in the second is a new
/// junction type the module should learn, and stage 2.4 reports it by name.
#[test]
fn boundaries_sit_on_their_junctions() {
    for model in [
        "tests/onshape/stepped_block_toroidal_fillets_fine.stl",
        "tests/onshape/stepped_block_toroidal_fillets_medium.stl",
        "tests/onshape/rounded_cube_10_r2_fine.stl",
        "tests/onshape/pipe_elbow_10_medium.stl",
        "tests/onshape/pill_fine.stl",
        "tests/ccad/generated/filleted_cylinder.stl",
        "tests/ccad/generated/filleted_pipe.stl",
    ] {
        let (out, config) = run_with_config(model);
        let (unhandled, wrong_side) = stage2::locus_summary(&out, &config);
        assert_eq!(
            wrong_side, 0,
            "{model}: {wrong_side} face(s) sit on the wrong side of a tangent junction",
        );
        assert_eq!(
            unhandled, 0,
            "{model}: {unhandled} pair(s) with a tangent junction locus.rs cannot build",
        );
    }
}

/// Every selected surface at full precision, in selection order: the
/// fingerprint two stage-2 runs must agree on bit for bit.
fn fingerprint(out: &stage2::Stage2Output) -> Vec<String> {
    out.selected_surfaces
        .iter()
        .map(|s| match s {
            stage2::SelectedSurface::Planar(i) => format!("{:?}", out.planar_hypotheses[*i]),
            stage2::SelectedSurface::Conical(i) => format!("{:?}", out.conical_hypotheses[*i]),
            stage2::SelectedSurface::Spherical(i) => format!("{:?}", out.spherical_hypotheses[*i]),
            stage2::SelectedSurface::Toroidal(i) => format!("{:?}", out.toroidal_hypotheses[*i]),
            stage2::SelectedSurface::BSpline(i) => {
                let b = &out.bspline_hypotheses[*i];
                format!("bspline {:?} {:?} {:?}", b.faces, b.error_max, b.centroid_error_max)
            }
        })
        .collect()
```
```
}

#[test]
fn filleted_pipe_surface_selection() {
    let stl = format!("{}/tests/ccad/generated/filleted_pipe.stl", manifest_dir());
    let config = config_for_stl_stage26(&stl);
    let output = run_stage2(&config);

    let torus_count = output.selected_surfaces.iter()
        .filter(|s| matches!(s, stage2::SelectedSurface::Toroidal(_)))
        .count();
    let cyl_count = output.selected_surfaces.iter()
        .filter(|s| is_selected_cylinder(s, &output))
        .count();
    assert!(torus_count >= 4, "filleted_pipe should have at least 4 toroidal surfaces, got {}", torus_count);
    assert!(cyl_count >= 2, "filleted_pipe should have at least 2 cylindrical surfaces, got {}", cyl_count);
}
```

```
/// Most vertices [\`cone_from_rings\`] will split, which bounds its work at
/// \`2^(n-1)\` partitions — 256 at the cap, the size of a four-quad chain plus
/// slack. It decides nothing about the surface; a larger support simply goes
/// to the centred-normal route, which needs breadth and has it.
const RING_SPLIT_MAX_VERTICES: usize = 10;

/// A cone from the **two rings** of a single-band strip — SURFACE_FITTING.md's
/// cone initialization Option C. Returns \`(apex, axis_dir, half_angle)\` with the
/// axis oriented from the apex toward the support.
///
/// A CAD tessellator lays a cone as one band of facets spanning its whole
/// height, so every vertex of a small seed sits on one of two circles, one per
/// rim. Three points determine a circle, so each rim gives a centre and a
/// radius; the line through the centres is the axis and the two radii at two
/// heights give the taper by similar triangles. Vertices only — no facet
/// normal, so none of the \`O(Δθ²/8)\` chord-plane lean — and it works from **two
/// facets**, where every normal-based route is rank-deficient (two normals pin
/// nothing about a cone).
///
/// **Which vertex belongs to which rim is found, not assumed.** The documented
/// design labels rims combinatorially by treating a shared quad edge as a
/// ruling, which holds only for quads in one band; a triangle strip's shared
/// edges alternate between rulings and diagonals. Instead every split of the
/// vertices into two groups of at least three is tried, each scored by the
/// largest distance of any vertex from the cone the split implies. On the true
/// split that is the mesh's own precision; a wrong split makes two circles whose
/// centre line is not their common normal, and misses by a large margin. The
/// winner is a seed for least squares, never the answer.
///
/// The taper \`t = dρ/dh\` is used throughout rather than the apex, for the reason
/// [\`cone_tapered\`] gives: \`t = 0\` is a cylinder, a regular point rather than an
/// apex at infinity. A split that reads as a cylinder returns \`None\` — the
/// caller fits cylinders by its own route — and so does any support too large or
/// too small to split.
pub(crate) fn cone_from_rings(
    faces: &[usize],
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
) -> Option<([f64; 3], [f64; 3], f64)> {
    let verts = patch_vertices(faces, mesh);
    let n = verts.len();
    if !(6..=RING_SPLIT_MAX_VERTICES).contains(&n) {
        return None;
    }
    let pts: Vec<[f64; 3]> = verts
        .iter()
        .map(|&vi| {
            let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
            [v.x, v.y, v.z]
        })
        .collect();

    /// The best split so far: its score, and the profile it implies.
    struct Split {
        score: f64,
        c1: [f64; 3],
        d: [f64; 3],
        r1: f64,
        taper: f64,
    }
    let mut best: Option<Split> = None;
```

```
+/// Committed hypotheses that are redundant: every one of their faces is also
+/// claimed, and explained within \`vtol\`, by a single other claimant of strictly
+/// larger area. Returns \`(dropped, container)\` per hypothesis.
+///
+/// Per-face resolution alone cannot see this. It hands a face several claimants
+/// explain to the lowest-DOF one, which is right at a tangency — a face on both
+/// a cylinder and its fillet torus is the cylinder's — but wrong when the
+/// simpler claimant is merely a *piece* of the more complex one: a cone fitted
+/// to one facet band of a torus is exact on that band (two coaxial circles
+/// always lie on a cone, SURFACE_FITTING.md "Option C"), and it would carve the
+/// band out of the fillet. A cylinder is never wholly inside its fillet, so the
+/// tangency rule is untouched; an impostor confined to a band of a larger
+/// surface always is.
+fn contained_hypotheses(
+    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
+    committed: &[CompeteHyp],
+    claim_lists: &[Vec<usize>],
+    hyp_area: &[f64],
+    vtol: f64,
+) -> Vec<(bool, usize)> {
+    (0..committed.len())
+        .map(|ci| {
+            let faces = committed[ci].faces();
+            let Some(&first) = faces.first() else { return (false, ci) };
+            claim_lists[first]

+                .copied()
+                .filter(|&cj| cj != ci && hyp_area[cj] > hyp_area[ci])
+                .find(|&cj| {
+                    faces.iter().all(|&fi| {
+                        claim_lists[fi].contains(&cj) && max_vertex_dist(mesh, &committed[cj], fi) <= vtol
+                    })
+                })
+                .map_or((false, ci), |cj| (true, cj))
+        })
+        .collect()
+}
```

```
## Cone initialization: the options (surveyed 2026-08-06; status 2026-10-15)

The cone is the worst-initialized surface in the pipeline, and unlike the torus
its problem is not a single fixable defect. This section records what fails, what
the literature says is and is not possible, and the routes that were open.

> **Status 2026-10-15.** Two things changed, and they are different kinds of
> change.
>
> **A defect was found and fixed: the fitter could not fit wide cones at all.**
> \`fit_cone\`'s primary path takes the axis as the smallest eigenvector of the
> **uncentred** normal covariance — the form "Centring matters" below records as
> wrong above a 35.26° half-angle — and its normal-line rescue degenerates on a
> wide cone too, because every normal lies near the axis. The centred form was
> built in Phase 1.1 (\`initialize::cone_tapered\`) and never reached the fitter.
> On \`cone_tangent_planes_occt_fine\` this refused a 73.0° and an 84.3° cone **on
> their entire true support** (503 and 504 facets); a torus then claimed their
> territory and stage 3 failed — the \`remesh_cone_tangent_fine\` test failure that
> had been attributed to the 2026-08-06 torus change. \`ConicalSurface::fit_surface\`
> now consults the centred-normal seed, LM-refined, when the existing routes do
> not explain the support to \`RESCUE_ERR_THRESHOLD\` — **and accepts it only if it
> does**. The second half matters: ungated, it regressed every \`stepped_block\`
> variant (+30–55 planes) and broke \`rounded_cube_10_r2_occt_medium\`, because on a
> conditioning patch straddling a junction the centred cone out-fit the true
> cylinder on residual and then grew nothing. That is the torus lesson
> ("residual on the current support does not predict how a fit will grow") a
> second time; requiring the route to *explain* the support rather than merely
> beat the primary removed all of it.
>
```

```markdown
# Option C + containment rule — experiment result (2026-10-16)

Verdict: ACCEPTED. Rule + Option C wired; no ok→fail across 193 models.

Rule (`compete::contained_hypotheses`, called at the top of `resolve_claims`):
drop a committed hypothesis when every one of its faces is also claimed, and
explained within vtol, by a single other claimant of strictly larger area.
No new constant, order-independent (computed over the full committed set), never
creates leftovers (container claims every face; area strictly increases).

Sweeps (tools/sweep.sh, jobs 8, baseline = HEAD 55fe0c4: 115 ok / 73 fail / 5 timeout):
- rule alone: 0 status changes; 1 model changed — VoronUsers__12mm_strip_mini_mount
  61→56 (fail→fail, same 2.63 mm edge error; drops two 4-face cones inside two
  tiny tori; reference = 8 planes + 5 cyl).
- Option C alone: 1 ok→fail (filleted_pipe 8→9, +1 cone), plus the 3 below.
- rule + Option C: 0 status changes; 3 changed, all fail→fail and toward the reference:
  - led_cover_drag_chain_termination: cone 2→4 (ref has 4), cyl 24→22 (ref 14)
  - nurbs/hill_with_hole: spurious torus gone, types now exactly ref (5 plane,
    1 cyl, 1 bspline); passes 3.1 (1.0e-8 mm), now fails at 3.6 (boundary
    deviation 10.9 mm) — new first-failure point, not chased.
  - 12mm_strip_mini_mount: 61→58
- filleted_pipe end to end with rule+OptC: 8 surfaces, two 17-face ring cones
  dropped (one per top fillet torus), vol rel 9.52e-8 (unchanged from HEAD).
- --viz-seeds (12 anchors): simple_cone 8→12/12, cone_cylinder 12/12, nosecone 12/12.
- Suite: 493 passed / 0 failed / 32 ignored.
```

```
//! Integration tests for stage 2.3(b) scoped fit competition: tangent-chain
//! regions the whole-region ladder cannot explain must decompose into their
//! true analytic surfaces (vertex-tolerance validated, not just counted).
//!
//! These run the full stage-2 pipeline (default stage) and assert the typed
//! hypothesis counts on the headline acceptance models, including the
//! stage-2.3(c) bent-tube promotion win (pipe elbow → torus + 2 cylinders).

use brepper::config;
use brepper::{stage1, stage2};

fn manifest_dir() -> String {
    env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR").to_string()
}

fn run(stl_rel: &str) -> stage2::Stage2Output {
    run_with_config(stl_rel).0
}

fn run_with_config(stl_rel: &str) -> (stage2::Stage2Output, config::Config) {
    let stl = format!("{}/{stl_rel}", manifest_dir());
    let config = config::parse_config_from(["brepper", &stl, "-q"]).unwrap();
    let mesh = stage1::stage1(&config).expect("stage1");
    let out = stage2::stage2(&config, mesh, None).expect("stage2");
    (out, config)
}

/// Count selected surfaces by type: (planar, cylinder, cone, spherical,
/// toroidal, bspline). Per project policy, assertions are on stage 2.6
/// *selected* surfaces — the hypothesis vectors also carry entries that repair
/// emptied out.
fn selected_counts(out: &stage2::Stage2Output) -> [usize; 6] {
    let mut n = [0usize; 6];
    for s in &out.selected_surfaces {
        match s {
            stage2::SelectedSurface::Planar(_) => n[0] += 1,
            stage2::SelectedSurface::Conical(i) => {
                if out.conical_hypotheses[*i].is_cylinder() {
                    n[1] += 1
                } else {
                    n[2] += 1
                }
            }
            stage2::SelectedSurface::Spherical(_) => n[3] += 1,
            stage2::SelectedSurface::Toroidal(_) => n[4] += 1,
            stage2::SelectedSurface::BSpline(_) => n[5] += 1,
        }
    }
    n
}

/// Every mesh face is covered by exactly one selected surface.
fn assert_total_coverage(out: &stage2::Stage2Output) {
    let n = out.mesh.faces.len();
    let mut count = vec![0u32; n];
    for s in &out.selected_surfaces {
        let faces = match s {
            stage2::SelectedSurface::Planar(i) => &out.planar_hypotheses[*i].faces,
            stage2::SelectedSurface::Conical(i) => &out.conical_hypotheses[*i].faces,
            stage2::SelectedSurface::Spherical(i) => &out.spherical_hypotheses[*i].faces,
            stage2::SelectedSurface::Toroidal(i) => &out.toroidal_hypotheses[*i].faces,
            stage2::SelectedSurface::BSpline(i) => &out.bspline_hypotheses[*i].faces,
        };
        for &fi in faces {
            count[fi] += 1;
        }
    }
    assert!(count.iter().all(|&c| c == 1), "every face covered exactly once");
}

#[test]
fn competition_rounded_cube_shell_decomposes_6_12_8() {
    // The rounded-cube outer shell is one smooth region (a tangent chain);
    // competition must split it into 6 planes + 12 fillet cylinders + 8
    // corner spheres — the reference's 26 analytic faces.
    let out = run("tests/onshape/rounded_cube_10_r2_fine.stl");
    let [planar, cylinders, cones, spheres, tori, _] = selected_counts(&out);
    assert_eq!(spheres, 8, "8 corner spheres");
    assert_eq!(cylinders, 12, "12 edge-fillet cylinders");
    assert_eq!((cones, tori), (0, 0), "no cones or tori");
    assert_eq!(planar, 6, "6 face planes");
    assert_eq!(out.selected_surfaces.len(), 26, "26 analytic surfaces total");
    assert_total_coverage(&out);
}

#[test]
fn competition_pipe_elbow_torus_two_cylinders() {
    // The pipe elbow is one smooth tangent chain: two straight tube segments
    // joined by a 90° bend, capped by two end disks. Stage 2.3(c) bent-tube
    // promotion must recognize the bend as a torus, so competition + the
    // ladder yield 1 torus + 2 cylinders + 2 base planes = 5 surfaces (the
    // reference's 5 analytic faces), with no strip machinery and no
    // per-facet leftovers.
    let out = run("tests/onshape/pipe_elbow_10_medium.stl");
    let [planar, cylinders, cones, _, tori, _] = selected_counts(&out);
    assert_eq!(tori, 1, "1 bend torus");
    assert_eq!(cylinders, 2, "2 straight tube cylinders");
    assert_eq!(cones, 0, "no cones");
    assert_eq!(planar, 2, "2 end-cap planes");
    assert_eq!(out.selected_surfaces.len(), 5, "torus + 2 cyl + 2 planes");
    assert_total_coverage(&out);
}

#[test]
fn competition_nosecone_cone_sphere_base() {
    // The nosecone's cone+sphere tangent chain is one region; the base disk
    // is a separate sharp-bounded plane. Competition + the ladder together
    // yield cone + sphere + base = 3 surfaces (the reference's 3 faces).
    let out = run("tests/onshape/nosecone_medium.stl");
    let [planar, _, cones, spheres, _, _] = selected_counts(&out);
    assert_eq!(spheres, 1, "1 nose sphere");
    assert_eq!(cones, 1, "1 body cone");
    assert_eq!(planar, 1, "1 base plane");
    assert_eq!(out.selected_surfaces.len(), 3, "cone + sphere + base");
    assert_total_coverage(&out);
}

#[test]
#[ignore = "stepped_block_toroidal fine regressed 71 -> 138 surfaces when the self-calibrating acceptance tolerance was removed (2026-07-28). The tolerance was NOT doing its stated job -- it was masking a seed-conditioning defect: 323 seeds produce NO GROWTH, including FLAT seeds failing to grow a PLANE, which cannot be a tolerance problem since a wall's vertices sit at ~1e-15. The cause is condition_patch giving up at MIN_CONDITION_FACES without checking whether the seed validates, on a model whose flat regions are narrow strips between fillets so a 32-face BFS patch always straddles. THE CONSTANT CANNOT BE RETUNED: measured, the conical conditioning floor at 2 gives stepped_block 75 surfaces (cylinders and tori exactly right at 37/18) but hands filleted_pipe a spurious 18-face cone; at 6 filleted_pipe is correct and stepped_block is 136; at 4 both are wrong. It is a lever, not a bound -- same pathology as the tolerance it was hiding behind. Needs the seed-patch mechanism reworked so a patch cannot straddle, not a new value. See DEVELOPMENT_PLAN."]
fn competition_stepped_block_fillet_network_stays_analytic() {
    // A dense fillet network — 37 cylinders + 18 tori + 16 planes in the
    // reference — tangent-connects the whole model into ONE 26122-face region,
    // so every surface has to come out of competition.
    //
    // This model used to collapse entirely to per-facet planes: one r = 0.5
    // fillet band, a single quad tall between two corner tori, left the axis so
    // weakly constrained that a bogus 12° cone beat the true cylinder on
    // residual, and the leftover blob that left behind tripped classify.rs's
    // whole-region discard. Then it decomposed but over-fitted: near-cylindrical
    // tori ate perimeter fillets and near-planar cylinders ate wall strips,
    // each winning on area as a super-model of the surface it displaced
    // (see \`MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG\`).
    //
    // The decomposition now matches the reference exactly, surface for surface,
    // and \`onshape_stepped_block_toroidal_fine_stage41_compare\` checks the
    // geometry that comes out of it.
    let out = run("tests/onshape/stepped_block_toroidal_fillets_fine.stl");
    let [planar, cylinders, cones, spheres, tori, bsplines] = selected_counts(&out);
    assert_eq!(tori, 18, "the reference's 18 corner-blend tori");
    assert_eq!(cylinders, 37, "the reference's 37 fillet cylinders");
    assert_eq!(planar, 16, "the reference's 16 planes");
    assert_eq!((cones, spheres, bsplines), (0, 0, 0), "no cones, spheres or freeform");
    assert_eq!(out.selected_surfaces.len(), 71, "the reference's 71 surfaces");
    assert_total_coverage(&out);
}

/// Every tangent junction must end up on the mesh-edge chain the two fitted
/// surfaces' junction geometry picks out (stage 2.4 boundary snap,
/// \`locus.rs\`). This is the property snap exists to establish, and it is
/// stronger than a surface count: a boundary one tessellation row off leaves
/// the counts intact and shows up only here (and, much later, as a stage-3
/// \`--compare\` edge distance).
///
/// The second number is how many adjacent pairs have a junction geometry
/// \`locus.rs\` does not implement — cone-plane ruling tangency, non-coaxial
/// pairs other than the cylinder-to-torus tube junction, point tangencies.
/// Every corpus model here reaches zero of both; a rise in the second is a new
/// junction type the module should learn, and stage 2.4 reports it by name.
#[test]
#[ignore = "stepped_block_toroidal fine regressed 71 -> 138 surfaces when the self-calibrating acceptance tolerance was removed (2026-07-28). The tolerance was NOT doing its stated job -- it was masking a seed-conditioning defect: 323 seeds produce NO GROWTH, including FLAT seeds failing to grow a PLANE, which cannot be a tolerance problem since a wall's vertices sit at ~1e-15. The cause is condition_patch giving up at MIN_CONDITION_FACES without checking whether the seed validates, on a model whose flat regions are narrow strips between fillets so a 32-face BFS patch always straddles. THE CONSTANT CANNOT BE RETUNED: measured, the conical conditioning floor at 2 gives stepped_block 75 surfaces (cylinders and tori exactly right at 37/18) but hands filleted_pipe a spurious 18-face cone; at 6 filleted_pipe is correct and stepped_block is 136; at 4 both are wrong. It is a lever, not a bound -- same pathology as the tolerance it was hiding behind. Needs the seed-patch mechanism reworked so a patch cannot straddle, not a new value. See DEVELOPMENT_PLAN."]
fn boundaries_sit_on_their_junctions() {
    for model in [
        "tests/onshape/stepped_block_toroidal_fillets_fine.stl",
        "tests/onshape/stepped_block_toroidal_fillets_medium.stl",
        "tests/onshape/rounded_cube_10_r2_fine.stl",
        "tests/onshape/pipe_elbow_10_medium.stl",
        "tests/onshape/pill_fine.stl",
        "tests/ccad/generated/filleted_cylinder.stl",
        "tests/ccad/generated/filleted_pipe.stl",
    ] {
        let (out, config) = run_with_config(model);
        let (unhandled, wrong_side) = stage2::locus_summary(&out, &config);
        assert_eq!(
            wrong_side, 0,
            "{model}: {wrong_side} face(s) sit on the wrong side of a tangent junction",
        );
        assert_eq!(
            unhandled, 0,
            "{model}: {unhandled} pair(s) with a tangent junction locus.rs cannot build",
        );
    }
}

/// Every selected surface at full precision, in selection order: the
/// fingerprint two stage-2 runs must agree on bit for bit.
fn fingerprint(out: &stage2::Stage2Output) -> Vec<String> {
    out.selected_surfaces
        .iter()
        .map(|s| match s {
            stage2::SelectedSurface::Planar(i) => format!("{:?}", out.planar_hypotheses[*i]),
            stage2::SelectedSurface::Conical(i) => format!("{:?}", out.conical_hypotheses[*i]),
            stage2::SelectedSurface::Spherical(i) => format!("{:?}", out.spherical_hypotheses[*i]),
            stage2::SelectedSurface::Toroidal(i) => format!("{:?}", out.toroidal_hypotheses[*i]),
            stage2::SelectedSurface::BSpline(i) => {
                let b = &out.bspline_hypotheses[*i];
                format!("bspline {:?} {:?} {:?}", b.faces, b.error_max, b.centroid_error_max)
            }
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Competition evaluates seeds speculatively on worker threads and applies
/// the results in seed order, so the thread count must not change a single
/// bit of stage 2's output — and the output must not depend on hash-set
/// iteration order, which differs between \`HashSet\` instances even within one
/// process. This model showed run-to-run differences in its
/// fitted parameters' last bits before 2026-10-16 (a plane offset summed in
/// \`HashSet\` order; candidate axes collected in it), so a reintroduced
/// order dependence is likely to show up here too.
#[test]
fn competition_is_thread_count_independent() {
    // One small model: it exhibited the run-to-run difference, and the test
    // must stay cheap — it runs stage 2 three times.
    let model = "tests/ccad/generated/cone_cylinder.stl";
    let stl = format!("{}/{model}", manifest_dir());
    let run_with = |threads: &str| {
        let config =
            config::parse_config_from(["brepper", &stl, "--stage=2", "-q", threads]).unwrap();
        let mesh = stage1::stage1(&config).expect("stage1 should pass");
        fingerprint(&stage2::stage2(&config, mesh, None).expect("stage2 should pass"))
    };
    let serial = run_with("--threads=1");
    assert!(!serial.is_empty(), "{model}: no surfaces");
    assert_eq!(run_with("--threads=1"), serial, "{model}: two serial runs differ");
    assert_eq!(run_with("--threads=4"), serial, "{model}: 4 threads differ from 1");
}
```

```
            vertex_tolerance_mm: c.vertex_tolerance_mm,
            surface_tolerance_mm: c.surface_tolerance_mm,

/// Max faces in the jet-similar seed patch used to condition the initial fit.
const SEED_PATCH_CAP: usize = 32;

/// Max trim rounds when conditioning a seed patch (one worst face per round).
const PATCH_TRIM_ROUNDS: usize = 16;

/// Floor on the patch size while conditioning — below this an analytic fit is
/// under-determined and trimming would chase noise.
const MIN_CONDITION_FACES: usize = 6;

/// Max BFS depth of the seed patch. Kept shallow so the patch stays local to
/// the seed and does not bleed across a tangent junction between two surfaces
/// of the same curvature class (e.g. a cone meeting a cylinder, where the
/// curvature is continuous across the seam) — a straddling patch fits neither
/// surface. An interior seed's shallow neighbourhood is on one surface, which
/// is all the initial fit needs; the flood then grows it to the true extent.
const MAX_PATCH_DEPTH: usize = 3;

/// Seed-patch radius bound, measured in radii of curvature of the seed's own
/// jet. \`MAX_PATCH_DEPTH\` bounds the patch in *hops*, which stops bounding it
----
/// Max distance from any vertex of face \`fi\` to \`fit\` — the trim criterion for
/// conditioning the seed patch (\`condition_patch\`).
fn face_max_vertex_dist<S: SurfaceType>(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, fi: usize, fit: &S::Fit) -> f64 {
    let face = &mesh.faces[fi];
    let vc = face.vertex_count as usize;
    face.vertex_indices[..vc]
        .iter()
        .map(|&vi| {
            let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
            S::vertex_distance(fit, &[v.x, v.y, v.z])
        })
        .fold(0.0_f64, f64::max)
}

/// Condition the seed patch so the seed lies on the patch's own fit. A
/// depth-limited jet-similar patch can bleed a row or two across a tangent
/// junction between two surfaces of the same curvature class — a short
/// cylinder wall into its fillet, where the transition faces' κ1 ramps from
/// the wall's toward the fillet's — which pulls the fit off far enough that
/// the seed fails its own fit and the grow gives up (leaving the wall to be
/// eaten by an over-grown torus). Trim the worst-fitting patch face (never the
/// seed) and refit until the seed validates, bottoming out at a size floor so
/// the fit stays well-determined. Fit-validated, in the spirit of "validation
/// decides geometry"; a no-op when the patch is already clean.
///
/// When the patch admits no fit of this type at all there is no residual to
/// rank by, so the round instead drops the face geometrically farthest from
/// the seed: a straddling patch is unfittable precisely because its far end
/// sits on another surface, and shrinking toward the seed is the one move that
/// is monotonically local.
#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
fn condition_patch<S: SurfaceType>(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    seed: usize,
    mut patch: Vec<usize>,
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    config: &CompeteConfig,
    vtol: f64,
    stol: f64,
    min_faces: usize,
) -> Vec<usize> {
    let floor = min_faces.max(MIN_CONDITION_FACES);
    for _ in 0..PATCH_TRIM_ROUNDS {
        if patch.len() <= floor {
            break;
        }
        let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &patch);
        let mut fit = match super::surface::cached_fit::<S>(mesh, &patch, &verts, config.verbosity) {
            Some(f) => f,
            None => {
                // No fit to rank by — shrink toward the seed instead.
                let far = patch
                    .iter()
                    .copied()
                    .filter(|&f| f != seed)
                    .max_by(|&a, &b| {
                        centroid_gap(centroids, seed, a)
                            .partial_cmp(&centroid_gap(centroids, seed, b))
                            .unwrap()
                    });
                match far {
                    Some(f) => {
                        patch.retain(|&p| p != f);
                        continue;
                    }
                    None => break,
                }
            }
        };
        S::determine_convexity(mesh, &patch, &mut fit);
        if face_validates::<S>(mesh, seed, &fit, centroids, vtol, stol) {
            break;
        }
        let worst = patch
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .filter(|&f| f != seed)
            .max_by(|&a, &b| {
                face_max_vertex_dist::<S>(mesh, a, &fit)
                    .partial_cmp(&face_max_vertex_dist::<S>(mesh, b, &fit))
                    .unwrap()
            });
        match worst {
            Some(w) => patch.retain(|&f| f != w),
            None => break,
        }
    }
    patch
}

/// Distance between two faces' centroids.
fn centroid_gap(centroids: &[[f64; 3]], a: usize, b: usize) -> f64 {
    let (p, q) = (centroids[a], centroids[b]);
    ((p[0] - q[0]).powi(2) + (p[1] - q[1]).powi(2) + (p[2] - q[2]).powi(2)).sqrt()
}
```

```
/// jet-similar seed patch, then flood-accept every region face the fit
/// validates and refit on the grown support, to a fixpoint. Returns the
/// hypothesis, its validated area, and its face list.
pub(super) fn grow<S: SurfaceType>(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    in_region: &[bool],
    seed: usize,
    jet: &[JetField],
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    config: &CompeteConfig,
    min_faces: usize,
) -> Option<(S::Hypothesis, f64, Vec<usize>)> {
    let patch = seed_patch(mesh, in_region, seed, jet);
    grow_from::<S>(mesh, in_region, seed, patch, centroids, config, min_faces)
}
```

```
stepped_block_toroidal fine gives 138 surfaces at 1×, 90 at 2×, 134 at 5×, 113 at 12× and
the exact 71 at 30×. A bound behaves monotonically with a plateau. A lever does
this. The constant was not buying tolerance, it was choosing which accidental
fit won a contested support.

*What removing it bought.* \`bspline_blister\` goes from 968 surfaces (959 of them
per-facet) to **7** against a reference of 6 — the spurious analytic patches
competition was carving out of it were what had prevented the freeform fit from
taking the region at all. \`hill_with_hole\` goes from 47 to **8** against a
reference of 7. Both had been broken and unwatched.

*What it exposed, and what is now blocked on it.* stepped_block_toroidal fine regresses
71 → 138, through **323 seeds that produce no growth** — including *flat* seeds
failing to grow a *plane*, which cannot be a tolerance problem, since a wall's
vertices sit at ~1e-15. The cause is \`condition_patch\`: it trims a straddling
seed patch until the seed validates but gives up at \`MIN_CONDITION_FACES\`
*without checking whether it succeeded*, and stepped_block's flat regions are
narrow strips between fillets, so a 32-face BFS patch always straddles and
cannot be trimmed to a clean one. The loose bar hid this by validating the
contaminated fit anyway.

**That floor cannot simply be retuned, and this is measured.** At a conical
conditioning floor of 2, stepped_block_toroidal fine recovers to 75 surfaces with its
cylinders and tori exactly right (37 and 18) — but \`filleted_pipe\` acquires a
spurious 18-face 5.6° cone that fits at 6e-7. At 6, filleted_pipe is correct and
stepped_block is 136. At 4, both are wrong. Making the floor per-type via a
\`SurfaceType::CONDITION_FLOOR\` associated constant does not help either, because
the conflict is within a single type (conical). It is the same pathology as the
tolerance it was hiding behind: a lever, not a bound.

**So the next step is not a value.** The seed patch must not straddle in the
first place — \`seed_patch\` grows a depth-limited BFS neighbourhood and hands
\`condition_patch\` the job of repairing it afterwards, which is the wrong shape.
Three stepped_block tests carry this as their blocker.

**Snap shared boundaries to the junction, not to a residual comparison.**
Nothing in stage 2 reasoned about where a boundary *should* be — it fell out of
flood plus claim resolution, and every remaining \`--compare\` failure has been a
boundary sitting a tessellation row off. The seam assumption says the correct
boundary already exists in the mesh as a chain of edges, so this is selection
from a guaranteed-nonempty set rather than a search. \`locus.rs\` supplies the
criterion and \`snap_boundaries\` (repair.rs) applies it.

*Use the minimum-distance locus, not the intersection.* At a tangent junction
the surfaces graze rather than cross, and their intersection is catastrophically
ill-conditioned: a plane offset by δ from the torus it should graze meets it in
a circle displaced by √(2rδ), which is how a 4.7e-4 mm plane-fit error became
the recorded 4.4e-2 mm edge error. The locus of minimum distance — the set of
points where the two normal fields agree — has no such amplification, and the
reason is worth remembering: displacing the plane along its own normal leaves
the tangency circle exactly where it was, so the locus does not depend on the
----
*exactly* perpendicular to the axis. It does not say the normal equals the
tangent-plane normal: a strip quad's chord plane leans off it by
\`n·d = sin α·cos(Δθ/2)/√(1 − sin²α sin²(Δθ/2))\`, an \`O(Δθ²/8)\` bias. Predicted
1.5e-3 relative at Δθ = 0.11 rad, and the half-angle measured 9.985° against a
true 10.000° — the same 1.5e-3. Vertices carry no such bias because they lie on
the surface exactly, so wherever a quantity can be taken from vertices rather
than from normals, it should be.

**The conditioning floor is not a model selector, and the attempt to make it one
was the familiar trap.** The meridian system is rank-deficient by construction on
sphere data, so it was tempting to threshold the spectrum tightly enough to
reject a sphere. Measured, the separation is not available: the degenerate sphere
patch reads \`l1/l5\` = 2.06e-6 and the hardest genuine torus (R = 4, r = 3) reads
9.2e-4, a factor of 450 with nothing but data-dependence between them — TODO
rule 5's "detector needs just one threshold" reached from yet another direction.
The floor stayed purely numerical, and *structure* does the discrimination for
free: a sphere's (ρ, z) profile is a circle centred on the axis, so its fitted
major radius comes out ~0 and the \`minor < major\` check rejects it outright. This
is what the design meant by "ladder order and a conditioning floor must precede
it" — type discrimination belongs to the ladder and to validation, never to a
conditioning guard.

### The torus fitter's percentile, and what wiring the closed form in cost (2026-08-06)

Two changes to \`toroidal.rs\`, found by asking \`--viz-seeds\` why a vertex star of a
fillet fails its own fit. Both are live.

**1. The 25th percentile was the defect.** \`fit_torus_inner\` estimates the minor
radius from normal-line intersections of adjacent facet pairs, which mix two
populations — tube curvature (≈ r) and azimuthal curvature (≈ R ± r) — and it
separated them by taking the 25th percentile, on the correct reasoning that tube
readings are the smaller ones. On a large patch that works. On a 4–9 facet vertex
star there are only a handful of pairs, so if one is a tube pair the percentile is
an *azimuthal* reading, and every later step compounds it: the tube centres are
placed at \`v + r·n\` with the wrong r, so they lie on a circle in the wrong plane,
\`fit_circle_3d\` fits that circle, and LM refines into a basin whose axis is a
-----
>   by its slowest test.
> - Rule 6's dead-end list has grown; four of the new entries are cone- and
>   torus-seeding ideas that look obviously right.

**Goal.** Maximum robustness and minimum fragility over all plausible
CAD-derived meshes — not score on the current corpus. Fragility is
operationalized: the stage-2 tuned-constant count (**34** at plan time) and
the **cliff count** (constants whose ±2× perturbation collapses any model).
Report both in every commit message that moves either.

---

## Execution rules — apply to every commit

1. **Invariants after every commit**: every mesh face in exactly one surface
   (\`assert_invariants\`); committed supports are flood/validation outputs at
   \`vtol\`/\`stol\`, never hand-adjusted; build clean; \`cargo clippy\` clean;
   suite green (\`cargo test --release --no-fail-fast\`, ~3 min) or newly
   \`#[ignore]\`d only with a precise blocker string.
2. **Measurement protocol**: save a \`tools/sweep.sh --baseline\` before each
   phase (and \`tools/probe.sh\` for a fast look);
   diff **per-type breakdowns** (plane/cyl/cone/sphere/torus/bspline), never
   surface counts alone (a 3-torus regression once hid behind an unchanged
   total of 71 — and measured again in Phase 0.3, the \`--compare\` gates pass a
   9-surface decomposition of a 26-surface part, so counts are the only thing
   that catches over-segmentation). The full suite is the decider.
3. **No new tolerance-like or threshold-like constant without user sign-off.**
   Numeric-conditioning floors (determinant floors, minimum |n₁×n₂| before
   normalizing) are not thresholds — say so in their doc comments when adding.
4. **Nothing is deleted without ablation evidence**: disable → probe → suite
   (→ harness) → delete, recording in DEVELOPMENT_PLAN what it was for and
   what superseded it.
5. **Stop and ask the user**, with measurements written down, when:
   - a step's listed assumption check fails;
   - results become **ordering-dependent** (ordering changes output);
   - you are about to implement a freeform-candidacy or model-selection rule
     (five have failed; none lands unmeasured);
   - a detector seems to need "just one threshold";
   - a guard proposed for deletion still fires anywhere;
   - you want to start anything in the **Reserve** section.
6. **Dead ends — do not re-derive** (details in DEVELOPMENT_PLAN):
   curvature/dihedral tangent-seam *detection* (dead twice; a tangent junction
   is locally the smoothest place on the mesh); acceptance-tolerance scaling
   with mesh quantum (chaotic, no plateau); complexity pricing among nested
   analytic types; clustering/snapping fitted radii; per-seed borrowed-axis
   commits without global selection (fragments surfaces, measured twice);
   face-size-ratio boundary tests (anti-correlated); count/fraction-based
   freeform candidacy rules (four dead); retuning flood/conditioning floors
   (non-monotonic everywhere); **collecting a fit patch by normal spread**
   (straddles tangent junctions — fillets split 12→24, spurious spheres) and
   **validated-only patch growth** (starves cones: a fit needs support and
   support needs a fit) — both measured in 1.2, both look obviously right.
   Added 2026-08-06 from the invariants rework, all measured, all obvious-looking:
   **cylinder-then-cone promotion** (a cylinder fitted to cone data grows by
   *nothing* — 0 promotions on 36 cone anchors — because a cone has no straight
   stretch, unlike the bend \`promote_bend\` exploits); **plane-then-cone promotion**
   (the plane rung reached 0 facets on every round); **undirected support
   enlargement** (takes \`simple_cone\` to 12/12 and regresses \`cone_cylinder\` 7→6
   and \`nosecone\` 10→8 by growing 3.5× past the true face across a tangency);
   **the dual plane-rank identifiability test** (σ₃ catches 12% of bad seeds while
   rejecting 83% of good ones — anti-correlated); **reordering
```

```
#!/bin/bash
# The sweep harness (Phase 0.3): every corpus model through the full pipeline
# with --compare, one machine-readable row per model, with baseline save/diff.
#
# This is the instrument the Robustness Rework is measured with. It replaces
# eyeballing tools/probe.sh output on 14 hand-picked models. See TODO.md
# ("Measurement protocol") and DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md ("The Robustness Rework").
#
# Usage:
#   tools/sweep.sh [--out FILE] [--jobs N] [--filter REGEX] [--timeout SECS]
#   tools/sweep.sh --baseline [FILE]   run, then save the result as the baseline
#   tools/sweep.sh --diff [FILE]       run, then diff against the baseline
#   tools/sweep.sh --diff-only A B     diff two existing result files
#   tools/sweep.sh --list              print the model/reference pairing and exit
#
# Defaults: --out tmp/sweep.tsv, --jobs 8, --timeout 300, baseline
# tmp/sweep-baseline.tsv (tmp/ is gitignored, so baselines stay local).
#
# Output is TSV with a '#'-comment header. Columns:
#   model    path under tests/, without the .stl extension
#   status   ok | fail | timeout
#   ref      step (compared against a reference) | none (crash-test only)
#   n        total surfaces in the final selection
#   plane cyl cone sphere torus bspline    per-type breakdown
#   edge_mm  stage 3.1 max edge-boundary distance to the reference
#   vol_rel  stage 4.1 output-volume relative error
#   secs     wall time
#   note     first error line, or empty
#
# RUNTIME CAVEAT: with --jobs > 1 the secs column is inflated by contention.
# Use --jobs 1 for any runtime measurement (Phase 2). The header records the
# job count so a diff cannot silently compare the two.

set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

# Overridable so tools/fragility.sh can sweep a stashed perturbed binary.
BREPPER=${BREPPER:-./target/release/brepper}
OUT=tmp/sweep.tsv
JOBS=8
FILTER=""
# 300 s is above every corpus model's runtime (worst: bspline_hill ~285 s) and
# below 3DBenchy's, which does not finish — the one row that is meant to read
# \`timeout\` until Phase 6.2 addresses runtime on real-world meshes.
TIMEOUT=300
BASELINE=tmp/sweep-baseline.tsv
MODE=run

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model/reference pairing
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Rules, in order. Anything that falls through runs without --compare and is
# reported as ref=none, which is correct for crash-test-only inputs but is
# also how a new model with a perfectly good reference could go unmeasured —
# so \`--list\` prints the pairing for review.

find_step() {
    local stl="$1"
    local dir base stripped
    dir=$(dirname "$stl")
    base=$(basename "$stl" .stl)

    # A sources.tsv in the STL's own directory, keyed by full stem, wins over
    # every rule below. Generated corpora write one (tests/fusion_reexport/), so
    # a re-tessellation is paired with the reference it actually came from
    # instead of a stem search, which is ambiguous — plate_with_hole_100x50.step
    # exists under two directories — and resolves in filesystem order.
    if [ -f "$dir/sources.tsv" ]; then
        local recorded
        recorded=$(awk -F'\t' -v m="$base" '$1 == m { print $2; exit }' "$dir/sources.tsv")
        [ -n "$recorded" ] && { echo "$recorded"; return; }
    fi

    # tests/remesh: <model>_offset_occt_<density> pairs with the translated
    # reference written next to it; <model>_occt_<density> with the original
    # reference in another directory, which tests/remesh/sources.tsv records
    # (keyed by model rather than by stem, hence its own rule).
    if [[ "$base" == *_offset_occt_* ]]; then
        local off="${base%_occt_*}"
```

```
# than 1% and above a picometre floor. Runtime is compared ONLY when both runs
# used --jobs 1: under parallelism the contention noise is larger than any
# regression worth reporting (measured: the same model, same binary, 27.8 s vs
# 63.3 s across two jobs=8 runs).

diff_results() {
    local old="$1" new="$2"
    [ -f "$old" ] || { echo "no baseline at $old" >&2; return 2; }
    local oj nj
    oj=$(grep -m1 '^# jobs' "$old" | awk '{print $3}')
    nj=$(grep -m1 '^# jobs' "$new" | awk '{print $3}')
    awk -v OLD="$old" -v serial="$([ "$oj" = 1 ] && [ "$nj" = 1 ] && echo 1 || echo 0)" '
        function num(x) { return (x == "-" ? -1 : x + 0) }
        # A measurement moved if one side is missing or they differ by >1%.
        #
        # NOISE is 1e-9 mm: an exact fit reports an edge distance around 1e-15 mm
        # — cancellation noise in a machine-epsilon quantity — and comparing two
        # of those RELATIVELY flags every run. A picometre is nine orders below
        # the f32 quantum of any real mesh, so below it, zero and 1.8e-15 are
        # the same measurement.
        function moved(a, b,   x, y) {
            x = num(a); y = num(b)
            if ((x < 0) != (y < 0)) return 1
            if (x < 0) return 0
            if (x < 1e-9 && y < 1e-9) return 0
            return (y > x * 1.01 || y < x * 0.99)
        }
        BEGIN {
            FS = OFS = "\t"
            split("model status ref n plane cyl cone sphere torus bspline " \
                  "edge_mm vol_rel secs note", name, " ")
            while ((getline line < OLD) > 0) {
                if (line ~ /^#/) continue
                split(line, f, FS)
                base[f[1]] = line
            }
        }
        /^#/ { next }
        {
            key = $1
            if (!(key in base)) { printf "NEW      %s (%s, n=%s)\n", key, $2, $4; changed++; next }
            split(base[key], b, FS)
            seen[key] = 1
            msg = ""
            # Status and the integer counts are identities: any change matters.
            for (i = 2; i <= 10; i++)
                if (b[i] != $i) msg = msg sprintf(" %s %s->%s", name[i], b[i], $i)
            for (i = 11; i <= 12; i++)
                if (moved(b[i], $i)) msg = msg sprintf(" %s %s->%s", name[i], b[i], $i)
            # Runtime: only meaningful serially, and only large moves.
            if (serial && num(b[13]) > 0.5 && \
                (num($13) > num(b[13]) * 1.5 || num($13) < num(b[13]) / 1.5))
                msg = msg sprintf(" secs %s->%s", b[13], $13)
            if (msg != "") { printf "CHANGED  %s:%s\n", key, msg; changed++ }
        }
        END {
            for (key in base)
                if (!(key in seen)) {
                    split(base[key], b, FS)
                    printf "GONE     %s (was %s)\n", key, b[2]
                    changed++
                }
            if (changed == 0) print "no changes vs baseline"
            else printf "%d model(s) changed\n", changed
        }
    ' "$new"
```

```
/// band out of the fillet. A cylinder is never wholly inside its fillet — it
/// continues past the junction rows the torus can reach — so the tangency rule
/// is untouched; an impostor confined to one band is wholly inside the surface
/// once that surface grows across the band from a seed of its own.
///
/// Computed over the whole committed set at once, so it does not depend on the
/// order hypotheses were committed in; and it adds no constant — the bar is the
/// vertex tolerance per-face resolution already uses.
fn contained_hypotheses(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    committed: &[CompeteHyp],
    claim_lists: &[Vec<usize>],
    hyp_area: &[f64],
    vtol: f64,
) -> Vec<(bool, usize)> {
    (0..committed.len())
        .map(|ci| {
            let faces = committed[ci].faces();
            let Some(&first) = faces.first() else { return (false, ci) };
            claim_lists[first]
                .iter()
                .copied()
                .filter(|&cj| cj != ci && hyp_area[cj] > hyp_area[ci])
                .find(|&cj| {
                    faces.iter().all(|&fi| {
                        claim_lists[fi].contains(&cj) && max_vertex_dist(mesh, &committed[cj], fi) <= vtol
                    })
                })
                .map_or((false, ci), |cj| (true, cj))
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Refit a committed hypothesis to its current face set, keeping the existing
/// fit if the fitter cannot produce one.
fn refit_in_place(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, hyp: &mut CompeteHyp, config: &CompeteConfig) {
    let faces = hyp.faces().to_vec();
    let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &faces);
    let v = config.verbosity;
    match hyp {
        CompeteHyp::Planar(h) => {
            if let Some(fit) = super::surface::cached_fit::<PlanarSurface>(mesh, &faces, &verts, v) {
                *h = PlanarSurface::make_hypothesis(mesh, faces, verts, &fit);
            }
        }
        CompeteHyp::Conical(h) => {
            if let Some(mut fit) = super::surface::cached_fit::<ConicalSurface>(mesh, &faces, &verts, v) {
                ConicalSurface::determine_convexity(mesh, &faces, &mut fit);
                *h = ConicalSurface::make_hypothesis(mesh, faces, verts, &fit);
            }
        }
        CompeteHyp::Spherical(h) => {
            if let Some(mut fit) = super::surface::cached_fit::<SphericalSurface>(mesh, &faces, &verts, v) {
                SphericalSurface::determine_convexity(mesh, &faces, &mut fit);
                *h = SphericalSurface::make_hypothesis(mesh, faces, verts, &fit);
            }
        }
        CompeteHyp::Toroidal(h) => {
            if let Some(mut fit) = super::surface::cached_fit::<ToroidalSurface>(mesh, &faces, &verts, v) {
                ToroidalSurface::determine_convexity(mesh, &faces, &mut fit);
                *h = ToroidalSurface::make_hypothesis(mesh, faces, verts, &fit);
            }
        }
    }
}
```
</details>
