```
>   for invariants work** — those numbers pin the design being replaced — and
>   still applies to any change made *to* the existing pipeline, as this one was.
>   The suite took ~26 min by 2026-10-15; it is **~3 min** since 2026-10-16
>   (one test binary, deduplicated model runs, three bit-identical pipeline
>   speed-ups, and competition parallelized with bit-identical output —
>   DEVELOPMENT_PLAN, "Suite runtime"). It is now bound by total CPU work, not
>   by its slowest test.
> - Rule 6's dead-end list has grown; four of the new entries are cone- and
>   torus-seeding ideas that look obviously right.

**Goal.** Maximum robustness and minimum fragility over all plausible
CAD-derived meshes — not score on the current corpus. Fragility is
operationalized: the stage-2 tuned-constant count (**34** at plan time) and
the **cliff count** (constants whose ±2× perturbation collapses any model).
Report both in every commit message that moves either.

---

## Execution rules — apply to every commit

1. **Invariants after every commit**: every mesh face in exactly one surface
   (\`assert_invariants\`); committed supports are flood/validation outputs at
   \`vtol\`/\`stol\`, never hand-adjusted; build clean; \`cargo clippy\` clean;
   suite green (\`cargo test --release --no-fail-fast\`, ~3 min) or newly
   \`#[ignore]\`d only with a precise blocker string.
2. **Measurement protocol**: save a \`tools/sweep.sh --baseline\` before each
   phase (and \`tools/probe.sh\` for a fast look);
   diff **per-type breakdowns** (plane/cyl/cone/sphere/torus/bspline), never
   surface counts alone (a 3-torus regression once hid behind an unchanged
   total of 71 — and measured again in Phase 0.3, the \`--compare\` gates pass a
   9-surface decomposition of a 26-surface part, so counts are the only thing
   that catches over-segmentation). The full suite is the decider.
3. **No new tolerance-like or threshold-like constant without user sign-off.**
   Numeric-conditioning floors (determinant floors, minimum |n₁×n₂| before
   normalizing) are not thresholds — say so in their doc comments when adding.
4. **Nothing is deleted without ablation evidence**: disable → probe → suite
   (→ harness) → delete, recording in DEVELOPMENT_PLAN what it was for and
   what superseded it.
5. **Stop and ask the user**, with measurements written down, when:
   - a step's listed assumption check fails;
   - results become **ordering-dependent** (ordering changes output);
   - you are about to implement a freeform-candidacy or model-selection rule
     (five have failed; none lands unmeasured);
   - a detector seems to need "just one threshold";
   - a guard proposed for deletion still fires anywhere;
   - you want to start anything in the **Reserve** section.
6. **Dead ends — do not re-derive** (details in DEVELOPMENT_PLAN):
   curvature/dihedral tangent-seam *detection* (dead twice; a tangent junction
   is locally the smoothest place on the mesh); acceptance-tolerance scaling
   with mesh quantum (chaotic, no plateau); complexity pricing among nested
   analytic types; clustering/snapping fitted radii; per-seed borrowed-axis
   commits without global selection (fragments surfaces, measured twice);
   face-size-ratio boundary tests (anti-correlated); count/fraction-based
   freeform candidacy rules (four dead); retuning flood/conditioning floors
   (non-monotonic everywhere); **collecting a fit patch by normal spread**
   (straddles tangent junctions — fillets split 12→24, spurious spheres) and
   **validated-only patch growth** (starves cones: a fit needs support and
   support needs a fit) — both measured in 1.2, both look obviously right.
   Added 2026-08-06 from the invariants rework, all measured, all obvious-looking:
   **cylinder-then-cone promotion** (a cylinder fitted to cone data grows by
   *nothing* — 0 promotions on 36 cone anchors — because a cone has no straight
   stretch, unlike the bend \`promote_bend\` exploits); **plane-then-cone promotion**

   comparison as a seed-quality signal** (a strictly better-conditioned candidate
   selected on residual made \`stepped_block\` fine 75→127 surfaces: residual on the
   current support does not predict how a fit will grow).
```

```
#!/bin/bash
# The sweep harness (Phase 0.3): every corpus model through the full pipeline
# with --compare, one machine-readable row per model, with baseline save/diff.
#
# This is the instrument the Robustness Rework is measured with. It replaces
# eyeballing tools/probe.sh output on 14 hand-picked models. See TODO.md
# ("Measurement protocol") and DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md ("The Robustness Rework").
#
# Usage:
#   tools/sweep.sh [--out FILE] [--jobs N] [--filter REGEX] [--timeout SECS]
#   tools/sweep.sh --baseline [FILE]   run, then save the result as the baseline
#   tools/sweep.sh --diff [FILE]       run, then diff against the baseline
#   tools/sweep.sh --diff-only A B     diff two existing result files
#   tools/sweep.sh --list              print the model/reference pairing and exit
#
# Defaults: --out tmp/sweep.tsv, --jobs 8, --timeout 300, baseline
# tmp/sweep-baseline.tsv (tmp/ is gitignored, so baselines stay local).
#
# Output is TSV with a '#'-comment header. Columns:
#   model    path under tests/, without the .stl extension
#   status   ok | fail | timeout
#   ref      step (compared against a reference) | none (crash-test only)
#   n        total surfaces in the final selection
#   plane cyl cone sphere torus bspline    per-type breakdown
#   edge_mm  stage 3.1 max edge-boundary distance to the reference
#   vol_rel  stage 4.1 output-volume relative error
#   secs     wall time
#   note     first error line, or empty
#
# RUNTIME CAVEAT: with --jobs > 1 the secs column is inflated by contention.
# Use --jobs 1 for any runtime measurement (Phase 2). The header records the
# job count so a diff cannot silently compare the two.

set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

# Overridable so tools/fragility.sh can sweep a stashed perturbed binary.
BREPPER=${BREPPER:-./target/release/brepper}
OUT=tmp/sweep.tsv
JOBS=8
FILTER=""
# 300 s is above every corpus model's runtime (worst: bspline_hill ~285 s) and
# below 3DBenchy's, which does not finish — the one row that is meant to read
# \`timeout\` until Phase 6.2 addresses runtime on real-world meshes.
TIMEOUT=300
BASELINE=tmp/sweep-baseline.tsv
MODE=run

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model/reference pairing
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Rules, in order. Anything that falls through runs without --compare and is
# reported as ref=none, which is correct for crash-test-only inputs but is
# also how a new model with a perfectly good reference could go unmeasured —
# so \`--list\` prints the pairing for review.

find_step() {
    local stl="$1"
    local dir base stripped
    dir=$(dirname "$stl")
    base=$(basename "$stl" .stl)

    # A sources.tsv in the STL's own directory, keyed by full stem, wins over
    # every rule below. Generated corpora write one (tests/fusion_reexport/), so
    # a re-tessellation is paired with the reference it actually came from
    # instead of a stem search, which is ambiguous — plate_with_hole_100x50.step
    # exists under two directories — and resolves in filesystem order.
    if [ -f "$dir/sources.tsv" ]; then
        local recorded
        recorded=$(awk -F'\t' -v m="$base" '$1 == m { print $2; exit }' "$dir/sources.tsv")
        [ -n "$recorded" ] && { echo "$recorded"; return; }
    fi

    # tests/remesh: <model>_offset_occt_<density> pairs with the translated
    # reference written next to it; <model>_occt_<density> with the original
    # reference in another directory, which tests/remesh/sources.tsv records
    # (keyed by model rather than by stem, hence its own rule).
    if [[ "$base" == *_offset_occt_* ]]; then
        local off="${base%_occt_*}"
     680
```

```
#!/bin/bash
# The pair-verification gate (Phase 0.5c): does a mesh actually lie on the
# reference surfaces it claims as ground truth?
#
# A STEP+STL pair is only ground truth if the mesh was tessellated from that
# exact geometry. A pair can fail for many reasons — a different revision, a
# decimated or repaired mesh, a healed or reparameterized import, a units or
# placement error — and every one of them silently poisons a --compare result.
# Run this on any newly acquired corpus before trusting it.
#
# Usage:
#   tools/verify_pairs.sh <dir> [--jobs N]
#
# <dir> must contain a sources.tsv mapping each STL stem to its reference STEP,
# the same manifest tools/sweep.sh reads.
#
# Two outcomes per file:
#   VERIFIED   the mesh's VERTICES lie on the reference surfaces
#   QUARANTINE they do not. Keep for crash-testing, never as truth.
#
# The verdict is taken on the vertex distance p95, NOT the max, and the two are
# reported side by side with their ratio (TAIL). A wild mesh can be exact to the
# file format across almost all of its vertices and carry a thin tail of strays
# from repair, decimation, or a simplified small feature; a max-based verdict
# throws the whole pair away for those few. Measured on the ToolChanger ducts,
# the densest meshes in tests/external at 64-71 facets per 90 degrees of arc:
# vertex p95 6.9e-6 mm, BELOW their own 9.3e-6 mm float32 position bound, with a
# max of 4.3e-4. Those are exact tessellations of their STEP, and the max-based
# gate rejected both.
#
# A large TAIL is therefore not a pass/fail signal by itself, it is a description:
# TAIL near 1 means a uniform offset (wrong frame, wrong revision, an offset
# variant), TAIL in the hundreds means a few bad vertices on an otherwise exact
# mesh. Read it with SAG: a max below the mesh's own chord error is inside the
# mesh's own approximation of the surface.
#
# The gate is defined on vertices, per the plan: "the pair counts as ground truth
# only if mesh vertices lie on the STEP surfaces within a few quanta". Stage 1
# also gates facet CENTROID distance against --surface-tolerance, which measures
# something else entirely — the tessellation's sag — and a legitimately coarse
# mesh fails it while being perfect ground truth. Measured: four Fusion exports
# requested at 0.5 mm chordal deviation have centroid sags of 0.51-0.83 mm, over
# the 0.4 mm default, with vertex distances of 1.8e-7 to 5.4e-6 mm. Those are
# impeccable pairs from a coarse tessellation, not bad provenance.
#
# So the centroid gate is disabled here and the sag REPORTED instead. Note what
# it implies for Phase 3: brepper's default --surface-tolerance rejects any mesh
# exported at a chordal deviation above ~0.4 mm, which is an ordinary setting.
#
# This script briefly carried a third state, CONTAINED, for a pass reporting a
# distance of exactly zero — the signature of a mesh lying wholly inside its
# reference, which is how a corpus written 1000x too small once scored 15/15.
# That was a workaround for a bug in stage 1, which measured against the
# reference SOLID rather than its faces and so answered "is this point inside?".
# Stage 1 now measures against a face compound and reports the true distance
# (12.4875 mm for that corpus), so the heuristic is redundant and is gone. See
# src/compare.rs.
#
# The stage-1 summary's float32 position bound is reported alongside, because it
# reveals coordinate scale directly: the metres-scale sphere read 5.7e-10 mm
```

```
176	### Surface Fitting Requirement
177	
178	One rule for every analytic type and for NURBS, replacing the per-type variants
179	this section used to carry:
180	
181	* **All vertices within \`--vertex-tolerance\` of the surface.**
182	* **All edge midpoints within ¾ · \`--surface-tolerance\`** — the edges of a
183	  *triangulation* of the facet, which for a fused quad means its two diagonals as
184	  well as its four sides.
185	* **No two adjacent facets of one surface separated by more than
186	  \`--angular-tolerance\`** — as a post-hoc consistency check only, never as a
187	  membership rule. See Surface Identification.
188	
189	**Why edge midpoints, and why the ¾.** Write the facet's deviation from the
190	surface as a height function vanishing at the vertices. To second order it is a
191	quadratic, and in barycentric coordinates
192	\`e(λ) = −Σ_{i<j} λᵢλⱼ · (pᵢ−pⱼ)ᵀH(pᵢ−pⱼ)\`. At the midpoint of edge \`ij\` that is
193	\`|qᵢⱼ|/8\`; maximised over the simplex it is at most \`max|q|/6\`. So
194	
195	> **max over the facet ∈ [M, (4/3)·M]**, where \`M\` is the largest edge-midpoint
196	> deviation.
197	
198	Checking edge midpoints and allowing ¾ of the tolerance is therefore a *bound* on
199	the whole facet, not a proxy for it — which answers the two TODOs this section
200	used to carry about sampling facet interiors, including for NURBS. Cost is about
201	1.5 evaluations per triangle, since each interior mesh edge is shared.
202	
203	Measured over 895 non-degenerate reference faces, ratio of the true whole-facet
204	maximum to each candidate probe:
205	
206	| probe | p95 | max | over 4/3 |
207	|---|---|---|---|
208	| boundary edge midpoints only | 1.742 | 1.999 | 63 of 895 |
209	| **edge midpoints + quad diagonals** | **1.012** | **1.497** | **1 of 895** |
210	| facet centroid | 1.384 | 2.239 | — |
211	
212	**Facet centroids are not a bound and are dropped.** The measured worst case,
213	2.239, matches the derived 9/4 for a needle triangle to three digits; and where
214	the curvature is indefinite (a saddle, a torus's inner equator) the centroid can
215	read *exactly zero* while the facet is off by the full sag. 23 corpus faces read
216	under a quarter of their edge-midpoint maximum. The single face that exceeds 4/3
217	with diagonals included is a 16-facet "plane" on a wild-corpus model that is
218	probably not planar.
219	
220	**The vertex clause holds at the mesh's own precision, not at a fixed number.**
221	On verified synthetic ground truth: plane p95 0.64 quanta, cylinder 1.22, cone
222	1.22, sphere 1.49, torus 1.45; worst case ~5 quanta. But two true cylinders on
223	\`stepped_block_toroidal_fillets_fine\` sit at 8.8 and 8.5 quanta = 7.7e-5 mm,
224	**outside the 5e-5 default**, so at today's tolerance the requirement is
225	unsatisfiable on those two surfaces and no algorithm can recover them. State the
226	bar in float32 position bounds (Phase 0.6 supplies the bound).
227	
228	**\`--surface-tolerance\` is barely non-binding.** The true worst facet sag over the
229	corpus is 0.325 mm against the 0.4 mm default — 1.23× margin — while the p50 is
230	2.2e-6 mm. Five orders of magnitude of spread under one constant; see Phase 3.2
231	for the per-face alternative.
232	
233	### Surface Seed Requirements
234	
235	A surface is discovered by growing a **seed set** — a set of facets that is the
236	entire initial fit support — under validation, refitting as it grows. There is no
237	separate unvalidated "patch": the seed set is what the first fit sees.
238	
239	A **facet chain** is a set of facets forming a path in the dual graph: each facet
240	shares an edge with the next, and each has at most two neighbours within the set.
241	(This section previously called it a "non-contiguous facet chain", which
242	contradicted its own definition — a set whose members share edges is contiguous.)
243	
244	* **Plane:** any facet of the surface. *Measured: 99.9% of plane facets have a
245	  working seed; 98.7% of plane faces have one for every facet.*
246	* **Cylinder:** a facet chain of at most 4 facets with **exactly 6 distinct
247	  vertices**. Measured, exactly three shapes reach 6 — two quads, four triangles,
248	  or two triangles and a quad — and the rule works: **94.1%** of cylinder facets
249	  have a working seed. Two quads on a cylinder give 6 vertices against 5 DOF, so
250	  there is one redundant constraint, which is what pins the right root.
251	* **Cone:** the same chain, or three triangular facets sharing one vertex (the
252	  candidate apex). The apex alternative earns its place — it is the *least*
253	  working rule for 21% of cone facets, cases the chain cannot reach. But the cone
254	  is the weak type: **49.4%** of cone facets have a working seed under these
255	  rules, and 22% have none at any support size up to 48 facets. The cause is the
256	  fitter, not the rule — see Surface Identification.
257	* **Sphere:** the seed facet plus every facet sharing an edge with it (and the
258	  same ring taken about each of its neighbours). *Measured: **100.0%** of sphere
259	  facets and **100.0%** of sphere faces. This rule is exactly right as written.*
260	* **Torus:** the closed ring of facets about one vertex — its **vertex star** —
261	  grown outward while the seed set's own fit does not yet validate the whole seed
262	  set. Typically 4–12 facets, occasionally up to 32.
263	* **NURBS:** fallback for the connected leftovers nothing analytic explains.
264	
265	**Why a torus needs a star rather than a chain.** A torus's normal lines cross the
266	axis at a point that *slides with the tube angle*, so a seed confined to one tube
267	angle cannot pin the axis — and two quads along the major direction is exactly
268	that, which is why a 6-vertex chain is under-determined for a torus. A vertex
269	star wraps a grid node, so it spans both parametric directions by construction.
270	Measured, the least support that works per torus facet: bare star 40%, the union
271	of the anchor's own vertex stars a further 25%, and the rest need 8–48 facets,
272	with 0.8% never working. Requiring the ring to **close** matters: complete stars
273	win 40% of facets, boundary-cut ones 4%.
274	
275	**The "no more than three coplanar" clause is deleted.** It was aimed at a real
276	degeneracy — a fan of facets sharing a vertex, which on a cylinder leaves the apex
277	free along a line — but as a detector it is useless and as a filter it is
278	destructive. Measured over 27 984 six-vertex chains: it rejects **85.3%** of the
279	chains that produce a good axis while catching only 39.8% of those that produce a
280	bad one. Worse, a fused quad is coplanar *by construction* — that is why it was
281	fused — so the clause rejects, by definition, every seed containing one: 99.7% of
282	2-quad chains and 92.4% of 2-triangle-plus-quad chains. And four vertices spanning
283	two rulings of a cylinder lie on two parallel lines, hence in a plane, so it also
284	bites the ruling-aligned triangle strips that Phase 1.0 measured as the *good*
285	ones. Excluding only the wholly-coplanar chains changes the worst axis error not
286	at all (90° either way).
287	
288	**The "not effectively planar" clause is deleted.** A large-radius cylinder that
289	validates every vertex is a valid explanation of the data; preferring the plane is
290	a matter of ladder order, which stage 2.3 already has (simplest DOF first), not of
291	a radius threshold.
292	
293	**Seed admissibility, replacing the combinatorial clauses.** A seed set is valid
294	for type T iff:
295	
296	1. \`fit_T(seed)\` exists, and
297	2. every facet of the seed set validates that fit at vertex tolerance.
298	
299	Nothing about connectivity, vertex counts, or coplanarity. Measured over 87 510
300	seed sets: seeds failing this grow to the right surface **0.4%** of the time;
301	seeds passing it, **84.6%**. It is the fixpoint condition of growth itself,
302	evaluated at round 0 — \`S ⊆ flood(fit(S))\` is the round-0 case of
303	\`F = flood(fit(F))\` — so admission and termination are one predicate at two
304	scales, and it introduces no new constant.
305	
306	**Seed sets need not be connected**, and requiring it would make things worse:
307	measured, disconnected seeds stall on 0.67% of attempts against 2.46% for
308	connected ones, and the best-performing shape was two small balls at the two most
309	distant points of the surface — which is also the well-conditioned shape for an
310	axis (Phase 1.0's amplification law). The chain rules above are stated as chains
311	because that is what the corpus supplies, not because connectivity is required.
312	
313	### Surface Identification
314	
315	For every analytic surface in the reference, growth from some admissible seed
316	finds that surface — **subject to an identifiability precondition**, which is the
317	part this section previously left out.
318	
319	**A wrong type frequently explains a true support exactly, and the residual does
320	not discriminate.** Measured on the true facet set of each reference face:
321	
322	| true type | a wrong type also validates at vtol |
323	|---|---|
324	| cylinder | sphere on **496 of 652**; torus on 307 |
325	| cone | sphere on 64 of 91; torus on 32 |
326	| plane | sphere on 322 of 1261; cyl/cone on 126 |
327	
328	The impostor residuals sit at 0.2–0.5 float32 quanta — the same order as the
329	correct type's. **The tie-break this section used to propose is refuted, and
330	points the wrong way:** on **393 of 397** true cylinders the impostor sphere fits
331	the cylinder's own facets *better* than the cylinder does, median 0.555× the
332	residual. \`simple_cylinder\` shows why in one line: its 32-quad band has vertices
333	on exactly two circles, and two circles lie exactly on a sphere — residual
334	2.07e-7 mm, machine precision. This is identifiability, not model selection, and
335	the distinction is the one already drawn in stage 2.3.
336	
337	So type discrimination stays structural: ladder order (simplest DOF first),
338	largest validated area, and identifiability guards such as
339	\`MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG\`. Never a comparison of residuals between types.
340	
341	**The cone is the type where identification currently fails**, and the cause is
342	the fitter rather than the information. On \`simple_cone\`, a two-quad seed whose six
343	vertices determine the cone to **0.0001°** (two rings of three spanning 31.3°;
344	circumcircle radii to 0.1–0.2× vtol) produces a \`fit_cone\` half-angle of **2.54°**
345	against a true 9.4623°. \`axis_normals_consistent\` correctly refuses that, and the
346	fallback cylinder then misses its own seed vertices by 222.7× vtol. Of the cone
347	rung's refusals, 42% are the axis-normal check, 27% a half-angle outside
348	[2°, 85°], 12% an apex 429–2128 mm from a 41 mm model. The guards are right; the
349	initialization is not. Options are catalogued in SURFACE_FITTING.md, "Cone
350	initialization".
351	
352	*Update 2026-10-15.* One initialization defect turned out to be structural and is
353	fixed: the fitter's axis came from the uncentred normal covariance, which cannot
354	fit a cone wider than ~35° at all, and the centred-normal seed now backs it up
355	(gated — see SURFACE_FITTING.md for why the gate matters). Cone facets with a
356	working seed set on the three models above: \`simple_cone\` 4/12 → **8/12**,
357	\`cone_cylinder\` 7/12 → **12/12**, \`nosecone\` 10/12 → **12/12**. Option C (two
358	rims) takes \`simple_cone\` to 12/12 as well, but it is exact on a single band of
359	*any* surface of revolution and so manufactures impostor cones on torus bands.
360	*Update 2026-10-16:* it is wired, because the impostor turned out to be
361	rejectable one level up — the true torus, grown from another seed, claims the
362	whole band, and claim resolution now drops a hypothesis wholly inside a larger
363	claimant (SURFACE_FITTING.md, "Option C", with the sweep numbers: no ok→fail,
364	three failing models moved toward their references).
365	
366	**One genuinely non-identifiable case exists** and is worth knowing: on one
367	\`simple_cone\` seed the fitter returned a half-angle 72.85° cone with its apex 10.8
368	patch-extents away that explains the six vertices to 6.7e-16 mm — *better* than
369	the true cone manages against a float32 mesh. Six points admit more than one right
370	circular cone. It is the exception (8 of 9 cone failures are convergence, not
371	identifiability), but it bounds what any optimizer can be asked to do.
372	
373	Because a NURBS surface can have sub-surfaces that fit other types (a cylindrical
374	strip around an ellipsoid's equator), NURBS identification is left out of these
375	invariants.
376	
377	### Surface Seed Independence
378	
379	Stated existentially, which is the right quantifier for an algorithm that gets to
380	*choose* its seeds:
381	
382	> **For every facet of a surface there is at least one admissible seed set
383	> containing that facet whose growth covers the surface.**
384	
385	Not "every admissible seed set works" — that is a much stronger claim and it is
386	false (34.9% of surfaces under the current seeding, 80.6% under the clean
387	operator). Measured with the section's own seed rules, growth limited only by
388	validation:
389	
390	| type | facets with a working seed | faces where every facet has one |
391	|---|---|---|
392	| sphere | **100.0%** | **100.0%** |
393	| plane | 99.9% | 98.7% |
394	| cylinder | 94.1% | 86.4% |
395	| cone | 49.4% | 26.8% |
396	| torus (star only) | 65.4% | 22.4% |
397	| torus (star, grown) | **99.2%** | **99.2%** |
398	| **all** | **89.7%** | |
399	
400	*Update 2026-10-15, after the wide-cone fix* (SURFACE_FITTING.md, "Cone
401	initialization"). The per-facet catalogue above has not been re-run, but the
402	\`--invariant-report\` S family has, over the same 79 cone reference faces and 940
403	seeds: seeds that grow **28.1% → 76.4%**, seeds that recover the true face set
404	**24.8% → 71.1%**, faces whose seeds all agree **8 → 17 of 79** (interior seeds:
405	56.4% → 92.8% exact, 10 → 19 of 24 faces). Across all types, 57.3% → 60.2% of
406	seeds recover the true set, and reference faces not explained at \`vtol\` by a fit
407	of their own type fall **71 → 31**, the cone's own-type residual p95 from 19 926
408	float32 quanta to 1.97.
409	
410	### Growth Independence
411	
412	Two halves, and only the second is empirical.
413	
414	**The flood is order-independent by construction.** Given a fixed fit, the grown
415	set is *defined* as the connected component of \`{facets validating the fit}\`
416	containing the seed — a set, not a traversal. Confirmed at **0 differences over
417	18 429 seeds** with the neighbour iteration reversed. This half is a theorem and
418	should be stated as one.
419	
420	**The refit fixpoint is start-dependent.** Growth is the iteration
421	\`F ← flood(fit(F))\`, which is neither monotone nor a contraction. Starting it from
422	the whole true face set instead of a seed reproduces the truth on 83.0% of faces,
423	and 648 of 1285 faces disagree between the two starts. Where the invariant needs
424	defending, this is where.
425	
426	### Coverage and boundary invariants
427	
428	Two invariants the earlier version of this section omitted, both of which the
429	per-surface clauses above permit violating:
430	
431	* **Partition.** Every mesh facet belongs to exactly one committed surface, and
432	  every surface is mesh-connected. Already enforced by \`assert_invariants\` in
433	  stage 2.4, and stated here because the per-surface clauses do not imply it.
434	* **Boundary.** Growth may **overshoot** — cover the surface and a collar beyond
435	  it — and every overshoot facet must belong to an adjacent surface that explains
436	  it strictly better. Measured, this holds identically: **100%** of overshoot
437	  facets land in a reference-adjacent face and **100%** of the scorable ones are
438	  closer to their true owner than to the fit that claimed them. Overshoot is
439	  small everywhere except fillet tori (median |result|/|truth| 1.000 for plane,
440	  cylinder, cone and sphere; torus median 1.019, p95 1.117).
441	
442	  This is why the growth invariant must be stated as *covers*, not *equals*.
443	  Scored per reference face over admissible seeds, requiring equality reads
444	  **80.6%** and requiring coverage **88.9%** — and the torus is essentially the
445	  whole difference, 16.8% against 60.8%. The boundary decision then belongs to a
446	  comparison between two surfaces, which is what \`resolve_claims\` already is, and
447	  it is handed exactly the information the clause promises.
448	
449	### Measuring these (\`--invariant-report\`, \`--viz-seeds\`)
450	
451	\`src/stage2/invariants.rs\`, diagnostics only — nothing downstream reads it. Runs
452	after stage 2.2, where the jet and the smooth regions exist and the mesh is still
453	untouched, so it works on models whose decomposition crashes or times out.
454	
455	- \`--invariant-report --compare ref.step\` scores the five families above, one TSV
456	  row per reference face on stdout plus a per-model summary on stderr.
457	  \`tools/invariants.sh\` sweeps the corpus (sharing \`sweep.sh\`'s model/reference
458	  pairing so the two instruments cover the same models); \`tools/inv_analyze.py\`
459	  aggregates.
460	- \`--viz-seeds\` walks anchor facets interactively and stops on those where *every*
461	  conforming seed set fails: seed green, covered blue, overshoot red, the true
462	  facets that blocked growth orange, missed yellow, anchor white. The status line
463	  names the failing clause.
464	- Env-gated probes: \`BREPPER_INV_FITDUMP=1\` prints the reference's own parameters
465	  beside the fitted ones for any seed that fails admission, with a
466	  NOT-IDENTIFIABLE / CONVERGENCE verdict from their sum-squared residuals;
467	  \`BREPPER_INV_BASIN=1\` sweeps the clean operator's basin of attraction;
468	  \`BREPPER_INV_PATCHSIZE=1\` measures fit accuracy against support size;
469	  \`BREPPER_INV_KINEMATIC=1\` (family K, \`tools/invariants.sh --kinematic\`) scores
470	  the kinematic rank ladder — see SURFACE_FITTING.md, "Nested fitting: a rank
471	  ladder instead of a type ladder". Its result bears directly on the cone and
472	  torus rows of the table above: the ladder reads a torus's axis structure on
473	  **81.5%** of readings and a cone's on 28.6%, and is structurally blind to the
474	  **cylinder** (4.5% of faces), because a cylinder is tessellated as a single
475	  row of quads and one axial band has a plane's rank at any circumferential
476	  extent. \`BREPPER_INV_JUNCTION=1\` (family J, \`--junction\`) races the rank
477	  against vertex validation across tangent junctions: over 490 races the rank
478	  never fired first, and validation fires with one or two foreign facets in the
479	  patch, so there is no room for an earlier detector. \`BREPPER_INV_REFDUMP=1\` and
480	  \`BREPPER_INV_FITVERBOSE=N\` print reference parameters and name the guard that
481	  refused a true support.
482	
483	**One reporting trap worth recording.** \`face_validates\` is a conjunction of
484	*three* tests — vertex distance, centroid distance, orientation coherence — and a
485	diagnosis naming only the first is actively misleading: 7% of seeds refused by
486	their own fit pass the vertex test and die on centroid or orientation. Every
487	verdict names its clause for that reason.
488	
489	### Open questions
490	
491	Answered by measurement:
492	
493	- *Do we need quad fusion?* Not for the invariants to hold, but it matters for
494	  conditioning: quad fusion is a 23× discriminator for ruling alignment (2.7% of
495	  fused quads straddle against 62.3% of triangles), and the edge-midpoint bound
496	  needs a quad's diagonals to be sound.
497	- *How do we test these without exponential search?* Seed independence is
498	  existential and per-facet, so the space is \`facets × conforming seeds per
499	  facet\` — polynomial, and sampled deterministically at a fixed stride. Growth
500	  independence needs no search at all for the flood half (it is a theorem) and
501	  randomised round-orders for the rest.
502	- *How well do they hold at finite precision?* The tables above. The short answer
503	  is that plane, cylinder and sphere hold well, the torus holds once its seed is
504	  allowed to grow, and the cone does not hold — for a reason that is a fitter
505	  defect rather than an invariant that needs weakening.
506	
507	Still open:
508	
509	- **Whether the sharp partition belongs in the growth invariant at all.** Growth
510	  confined to a smooth region cannot cover a surface the partition has cut, and
511	  stage 2.1 cuts 68 true surfaces on 350 edges (see 2.1(a)). Unconfined growth
512	  covers those but runs across tangent junctions instead. Neither bound is right
513	  as stated.
514	- **A cone seed rule that works**, which needs the fitter fixed first. *Partly
515	  done 2026-10-15*: the wide-cone half of the fitter defect is fixed (above).
516	  *Done 2026-10-16*: the two-facet half — Option C solves it exactly but is exact
517	  on a single band of every surface of revolution, and the discrimination beyond
518	  the band is now \`compete::contained_hypotheses\` (a hypothesis every face of
519	  which a larger claimant also claims and explains within vtol is dropped).
520	  Cone seed coverage is 12/12 on \`simple_cone\`, \`cone_cylinder\` and \`nosecone\`.
521	- **NURBS**, deliberately excluded above.
522	
523	## Dependencies
524	
525	| Library | Purpose | Version |
```

```
/// Minimum number of mesh faces required to accept a cylindrical hypothesis.
/// Any real CAD tessellation of a cylinder produces at least 3 facets around
/// the circumference; this rejects spurious 2-face fits (e.g. adjacent torus
/// facets that locally approximate a cylinder).
pub(crate) const MIN_CYLINDER_FACES: usize = 3;

/// Minimum number of mesh faces required to accept a spherical hypothesis.
/// Sphere fitting has 4 degrees of freedom (cx, cy, cz, r), so at least 4
/// non-degenerate faces are needed for a well-determined fit. This also rejects
/// spurious fits from small patches that are consistent with many surface types.
pub(crate) const MIN_SPHERE_FACES: usize = 4;

/// Minimum number of mesh faces required to accept a toroidal hypothesis.
/// A torus has 7 degrees of freedom (center xyz, axis direction 2, R, r),
/// so at least 7 faces are needed for a well-determined fit.
pub(crate) const MIN_TORUS_FACES: usize = 7;

/// Maximum sphere radius as a multiple of the mesh bounding-box diagonal.
/// With solid-angle coverage validation and surface-tolerance validation during
/// BFS, this no longer needs to be tight — those checks prevent pathological
/// growth. A large value serves as a numerical guardrail against degenerate fits.
pub(crate) const MAX_SPHERE_RADIUS_FACTOR: f64 = 1000.0;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A planar surface hypothesis fitted to a set of mesh faces.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct PlanarHypothesis {
    /// Unit normal vector pointing outward from the shell/solid.
    pub normal: [f64; 3],
    /// Signed distance from origin to plane along the normal.
    pub distance: f64,
    /// Set of mesh face indices that fit this hypothesis.
    pub faces: Vec<usize>,
    /// Set of mesh vertex indices on this plane.
    pub vertices: Vec<usize>,
    /// Maximum (positive) distance from any vertex to the plane.
    pub error_max: f64,
    /// Minimum (most negative) distance from any vertex to the plane.
    pub error_min: f64,
    /// Sum of absolute vertex-to-plane distances.
    pub error_abs_sum: f64,
}

/// A cylindrical or conical surface hypothesis fitted to a set of mesh faces.
/// Cylinders are represented as cones with half_angle == 0.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ConicalHypothesis {
    /// The apex of the cone, or a point on the axis for cylinders.
    pub apex: [f64; 3],
    /// Unit direction vector along the cone/cylinder axis.
    pub axis_direction: [f64; 3],
    /// Half-angle of the cone in radians (0 for cylinders).
    pub half_angle: f64,
    /// Cylinder radius (when half_angle == 0). 0 for true cones.
    pub radius_at_apex: f64,
    /// Whether the surface normal points away from the axis (convex=true) or toward it (concave=false).
    pub convex: bool,
    /// Set of mesh face indices that fit this hypothesis.
    pub faces: Vec<usize>,
    /// Set of mesh vertex indices on this surface.
    pub vertices: Vec<usize>,
    /// Maximum absolute distance from any vertex to the surface.
    pub error_max: f64,
    /// Maximum absolute distance from any face centroid to the surface.
    pub centroid_error_max: f64,
    /// Sum of absolute vertex-to-surface distances.
    pub error_abs_sum: f64,
}

impl ConicalHypothesis {
    /// Returns true if this hypothesis represents a cylinder (half_angle ≈ 0).
    pub fn is_cylinder(&self) -> bool {
        self.half_angle < 1e-4
    }
}
```

```
//! Stage 4: Output
//!
//! 4.1: Write constructed objects to a STEP file.

use crate::config::Config;
use crate::stage3::Stage3Output;
use opencascade_sys::{
    b_rep_g_prop, g_prop,
    topo_ds, OwnedPtr,
};
use std::error::Error;
use std::fmt::{Display, Formatter};
use std::time::Instant;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Errors
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum Stage4Error {
    MissingOutputPath,
    TransferFailed(String),
    WriteFailed(String),
    Compare(Stage4CompareError),
}

impl Display for Stage4Error {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Stage4Error::MissingOutputPath => write!(f, "no output STEP file path specified (-o)"),
            Stage4Error::TransferFailed(msg) => write!(f, "stage 4.1 STEP transfer failed: {msg}"),
            Stage4Error::WriteFailed(msg) => write!(f, "stage 4.1 STEP write failed: {msg}"),
            Stage4Error::Compare(e) => write!(f, "stage 4.1 compare: {e}"),
        }
    }
}

impl Error for Stage4Error {}

impl From<Stage4CompareError> for Stage4Error {
    fn from(e: Stage4CompareError) -> Self {
        Stage4Error::Compare(e)
    }
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum Stage4CompareError {
    /// The written STEP file could not be read back for validation.
    RoundTrip { path: String, error: String },
    /// The output's volume differs from the reference beyond 1% relative.
    Volume { rel_diff: f64 },
    /// The output shape is farther from the reference than --surface-tolerance.
    Distance { max_distance: f64, tolerance: f64 },
}

impl Display for Stage4CompareError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Stage4CompareError::RoundTrip { path, error } => {
                write!(f, "failed to re-read written STEP file {path}: {error}")
            }
            Stage4CompareError::Volume { rel_diff } => {
                write!(
                    f,
                    "output volume differs from STEP by {rel_diff:.2e} relative (tolerance 1e-2)"
                )
            }
            Stage4CompareError::Distance { max_distance, tolerance } => {
                write!(
                    f,
                    "output STEP distance {max_distance:.6e} exceeds tolerance {tolerance:.6e}"
                )
            }
        }
    }
}
```

```
/// Compute maximum distance between STL mesh vertices/centroids and STEP model surfaces,
/// and maximum angular deviation between adjacent STL faces on the same STEP surface.
///
/// Reads an STL file to extract vertex positions and triangle centroids, reads a
/// STEP file to extract surfaces, and computes the minimum distance from each
/// point to any STEP surface. Also builds triangle adjacency and maps each
/// triangle to its nearest STEP surface, then measures the dihedral angle
/// between adjacent triangles sharing the same STEP surface.
///
/// Units: all distances are in mm. OCCT's STEPControl_Reader converts STEP
/// file units (typically meters for Onshape exports) to mm internally.
/// STL files have no unit metadata; coordinates are assumed to be in mm.
use brepper::stage1::{self, VertexWeldOptions};
use opencascade_sys::{
    b_rep, b_rep_builder_api, b_rep_extrema, b_rep_g_prop, extrema, g_prop, gp, message, rw_stl,
    step_control, top_abs, top_exp, topo_ds,
};
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::env;
use std::process;

fn main() {
    let args: Vec<String> = env::args().collect();

    // Parse --quad flag
    let mut positional = Vec::new();
    let mut use_quad = false;
    for arg in &args[1..] {
        if arg == "--quad" {
            use_quad = true;
        } else {
            positional.push(arg.as_str());
        }
    }
    if positional.len() != 2 {
        eprintln!("Usage: {} [--quad] <input.stl> <input.step>", args[0]);
        process::exit(1);
    }
    let stl_path = positional[0];
    let step_path = positional[1];

    // Read STL → Poly_Triangulation
    if !std::path::Path::new(stl_path).exists() {
        eprintln!("Error: STL file not found: {stl_path}");
        process::exit(1);
```

```bash
#!/bin/zsh
# Reference-free evaluation: run brepper on every corpus STL WITHOUT --compare,
# then measure the output STEP against the input STL (not against a reference).
# This answers the product question: "given only an STL, do we produce a usable
# STEP, how fast, and how faithful is it to the mesh?"
#
# Usage: tmp/eval_noref.sh [jobs] [timeout_secs]
# Output: tmp/eval/noref.tsv
#   model status secs tris faces vtx_max ctr_max vol_rel note
set -u
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
JOBS=${1:-6}
TMO=${2:-120}
OUT=tmp/eval
mkdir -p $OUT/out $OUT/rows
rm -f $OUT/rows/*.tsv

run_one() {
    local stl="$1" tmo="$2" out="$3"
    local rel="${stl#tests/}"; rel="${rel%.stl}"
    local key="${rel//\//__}"
    local step="$out/out/$key.step"
    rm -f "$step"
    local t0=$(perl -MTime::HiRes=time -e 'print time')
    local err
    err=$(timeout "$tmo" ./target/release/brepper "$stl" -o "$step" -v 2>&1)
    local rc=$?
    local t1=$(perl -MTime::HiRes=time -e 'print time')
    local secs=$(printf '%.2f' $((t1 - t0)))
    local status=ok note=""
    if [ $rc -eq 124 ]; then status=timeout
    elif [ $rc -ne 0 ] || [ ! -s "$step" ]; then
        status=fail
        note=$(print -r -- "$err" | grep -m1 -i 'error\|panick' | cut -c1-200 | tr '\t' ' ')
    fi
    local tris=- faces=- vmax=- cmax=- volrel=-
    if [ $status = ok ]; then
        local m
        m=$(timeout 300 ./target/release/step-measure-tolerance "$stl" "$step" 2>&1)
        tris=$(print -r -- "$m" | sed -n 's/^STL: .* nodes, \([0-9]*\) triangles/\1/p')
        faces=$(print -r -- "$m" | sed -n 's/^STEP: \([0-9]*\) faces/\1/p')
        local last=$(print -r -- "$m" | tail -1)
        vmax=$(print -r -- "$last" | cut -f1)
        cmax=$(print -r -- "$last" | cut -f3)
        local sv=$(print -r -- "$last" | cut -f9) mv=$(print -r -- "$last" | cut -f11)
        volrel=$(awk -v a="$sv" -v b="$mv" 'BEGIN{ if (b+0==0) print "-"; else printf "%.3e", (a-b)/b }')
    fi
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$rel" $status $secs "$tris" "$faces" "$vmax" "$cmax" "$volrel" "$note" > "$out/rows/$key.tsv"
}

typeset -a stls
stls=(tests/{external,downloaded,onshape,fusion,fusion_reexport,remesh,ccad/generated,nurbs,random,occt,manual}/*.stl(N))
print "models: ${#stls}" >&2
for stl in $stls; do
    while (( $(jobs -r | wc -l) >= JOBS )); do sleep 0.2; done
    run_one "$stl" "$TMO" "$OUT" &
done
wait
{ printf 'model\tstatus\tsecs\ttris\tfaces\tvtx_max\tctr_max\tvol_rel\tnote\n'; cat $OUT/rows/*.tsv | sort; } > $OUT/noref.tsv
print "wrote $OUT/noref.tsv" >&2

```

```bash
#!/bin/zsh
# Post-process tmp/eval/noref.tsv: for each model, face-type histogram and
# BRepCheck validity of OUR output, next to the reference STEP's histogram.
# Output: tmp/eval/post.tsv
#   model status secs tris vtx_max vol_rel valid out_faces out_types ref_faces ref_types
set -u
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
OUT=tmp/eval
typeset -A REF
tools/sweep.sh --list 2>/dev/null | while read -r line; do
    stl="${line%%.stl *}"
    step="${line##* }"
    [[ "$line" == *.stl\ * ]] || continue
    [[ "$step" == tests/* ]] && REF[$stl]="$step"
done

hist() {  # step-faces output -> "n valid plane:cyl:cone:sphere:torus:other"
    awk '
      /^face / { t=$3; if (t=="plane") p++; else if (t=="cylinder") c++; else if (t=="cone") k++; else if (t=="sphere") s++; else if (t=="torus") o++; else x++; n++ }
      /BRepCheck valid=/ { v=$0; sub(/.*valid=/,"",v) }
      END { printf "%d\t%s\t%d:%d:%d:%d:%d:%d", n, (v==""?"?":v), p,c,k,s,o,x }'
}

{
printf 'model\tstatus\tsecs\ttris\tvtx_max\tvol_rel\tvalid\tout_faces\tout_p:cy:co:s:t:x\tref_faces\tref_p:cy:co:s:t:x\n'
tail -n +2 $OUT/noref.tsv | while IFS=$'\t' read -r model st secs tris faces vmax cmax volrel note; do
    key="${model//\//__}"
    o="-\t-\t-"; r="-\t-\t-"
    if [ "$st" = ok ]; then
        o=$(timeout 300 ./target/release/step-faces "$OUT/out/$key.step" 2>/dev/null | hist)
    fi
    ref="${REF[$model]:-}"
    if [ -n "$ref" ] && [ -f "$ref" ]; then
        r=$(timeout 300 ./target/release/step-faces "$ref" 2>/dev/null | hist)
    fi
    of=$(print -r -- "$o" | cut -f1); ov=$(print -r -- "$o" | cut -f2); ot=$(print -r -- "$o" | cut -f3)
    rf=$(print -r -- "$r" | cut -f1); rt=$(print -r -- "$r" | cut -f3)
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$model" "$st" "$secs" "$tris" "$vmax" "$volrel" "$ov" "$of" "$ot" "$rf" "$rt"
done
} > $OUT/post.tsv
print "wrote $OUT/post.tsv" >&2
```

```
//! Stage 2.3(b): scoped fit competition.
//!
//! For a smooth region the whole-region ladder (2.3(a)) cannot explain — a
//! tangent chain like the rounded-cube shell (6 planes, 12 fillet cylinders,
//! 8 corner spheres) or the nosecone's cone+sphere — decompose it by
//! seed-first multi-type competition run INSIDE the region. The sharp
//! boundary cordons the arena, so competition cost is bounded and
//! cross-region accidents are impossible.
//!
//! - **Seeds**: every region face seeds exactly once, in jet-interior-first
//!   order (faces whose (κ1,κ2) best match their neighbors' seed before
//!   junction rows). Committing a hypothesis does NOT retire the faces it grew
//!   into — growing into a face is a hypothesis, not a conclusion, and a face
//!   swallowed by a wrong surface must still be able to seed the right one
//!   (\`resolve_claims\` arbitrates the resulting multi-claims). Only faces in
//!   the *interior* of the explained set are skipped, since a fit grown from
//!   the middle of a validated surface merely refits that surface.
//! - **Per seed**: grow each candidate surface type (jet-pruned) from a
//!   small jet-similar seed patch — fit, flood-accept every region face the
//!   fit validates, refit on the grown support, to a fixpoint — and commit
//!   the hypothesis with the **largest validated area** (simplest-DOF
//!   tiebreak). The jet only orders and prunes; vertex-tolerance validation
//!   decides every face.
//! - **Claims**: a flood may grow through faces already claimed by an
//!   earlier hypothesis (junction rows that genuinely lie on two surfaces),
//!   so a face can be claimed by several hypotheses. \`resolve_claims\` first
//!   drops any hypothesis wholly inside a larger claimant (every face also
//!   claimed and explained within vtol by it — a band impostor, not a
//!   surface), then assigns each contested face to the claimant that fits its
//!   vertices best (2× margin to leave the larger claimant).
//! - **Toroidal candidates (stage 2.3(c))**: a torus competes like any other
//!   type — grown directly from curved seeds (fillet tori, bend tubes), and
//!   additionally *promoted* from a cylinder whose flood stalled against
//!   faces whose jet continues the tube (κ1 ≈ the tube's 1/r, |κ2| well
//!   below κ1 — a bent tube's signature). The promotion seeds its fit from
//!   the pure-bend patch just past the stall line: the cylinder fit itself
//!   locates the tangency, so the patch cannot straddle it the way a
//!   jet-class patch can (bend and straight tube share κ1).
//!
//! **Soundness** (the sub-region lemma, under exactness): an accidental fit
//! is supported on a *sub-region*; the true surface fitted from an interior
//! seed floods — vertex tolerance the arbiter — to its entire true extent,
//! and largest-validated-area then selects it over the accidental one.
//!
//! Faces no hypothesis claims are returned as leftovers; the caller degrades
//! them to per-facet planes (freeform fitting is stage 2.3(e), a later step).

use std::collections::HashSet;

use crate::config::Config;
use crate::stage1::ConnectedMesh;

use super::surface::SurfaceType;
use super::conical::{ConeFit, ConicalSurface};
use super::edges::JetField;
use super::planar::PlanarSurface;
use super::regions::Region;
use super::spherical::{bounding_box_diagonal, SphericalSurface};
use super::toroidal::ToroidalSurface;
use super::{
    face_area, ConicalHypothesis, PlanarHypothesis, SphericalHypothesis, ToroidalHypothesis,
    MIN_CYLINDER_FACES, MIN_SPHERE_FACES, MIN_TORUS_FACES,
};

/// The settings competition reads, as a plain \`Sync\` value.
///
/// \`Config\` carries the \`--compare\` reference shape, an OCCT handle, so it
/// cannot be shared across threads — and competition, which \`compete_region\`
/// runs on several, never reads it. The field names match \`Config\`'s so the code
/// below reads exactly as it did when it took \`&Config\`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct CompeteConfig {
    pub vertex_tolerance_mm: f64,
    pub surface_tolerance_mm: f64,
    pub verbosity: u8,
    /// \`--threads\`; \`None\` = all cores.
    pub threads: Option<usize>,
}

impl From<&Config> for CompeteConfig {
    fn from(c: &Config) -> Self {
        CompeteConfig {
            vertex_tolerance_mm: c.vertex_tolerance_mm,
            surface_tolerance_mm: c.surface_tolerance_mm,
            verbosity: c.verbosity,
            threads: c.threads,
        }
    }
}

/// Max faces in the jet-similar seed patch used to condition the initial fit.
const SEED_PATCH_CAP: usize = 32;

/// Max trim rounds when conditioning a seed patch (one worst face per round).
const PATCH_TRIM_ROUNDS: usize = 16;

/// Floor on the patch size while conditioning — below this an analytic fit is
/// under-determined and trimming would chase noise.
const MIN_CONDITION_FACES: usize = 6;

/// Max BFS depth of the seed patch. Kept shallow so the patch stays local to
/// the seed and does not bleed across a tangent junction between two surfaces
/// of the same curvature class (e.g. a cone meeting a cylinder, where the
/// curvature is continuous across the seam) — a straddling patch fits neither
/// surface. An interior seed's shallow neighbourhood is on one surface, which
/// is all the initial fit needs; the flood then grows it to the true extent.
const MAX_PATCH_DEPTH: usize = 3;

/// Seed-patch radius bound, measured in radii of curvature of the seed's own
/// jet. \`MAX_PATCH_DEPTH\` bounds the patch in *hops*, which stops bounding it
```

```
3096	  works because a bend genuinely *is* locally a cylinder (sag ~3.6e-5 mm over a
```

```
fn assert_invariants(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, cls: &Classification) {
    let n = mesh.faces.len();

    // Total coverage: every face in exactly one selected surface.
    let mut count = vec![0u32; n];
    for si in 0..cls.selected.len() {
        for &fi in surface_faces(cls, si) {
            count[fi] += 1;
        }
    }
    for (fi, &c) in count.iter().enumerate() {
        assert_eq!(c, 1, "stage 2.4 invariant: face {fi} covered {c} times, expected 1");
    }

    // Connectivity: each surface's faces form one mesh-connected component.
    for si in 0..cls.selected.len() {
        let faces = surface_faces(cls, si);
        if faces.len() < 2 {
            continue;
        }
        let comps = connected_components(mesh, faces);
        assert_eq!(
            comps.len(),
            1,
            "stage 2.4 invariant: surface {si} has {} disconnected components",
            comps.len()
        );
    }
}
```

```
## Phase 6 — Real-world hardening

- **6.1 Graceful degradation.** When the Phase-0 provenance detector fires
  (decimated/remeshed/faceted-by-construction input): warn precisely, run
  best-effort (freeform + per-facet), report what the data could support,
  never crash, never emit silent garbage. Exercise it on the quarantined
  external models and 3DBenchy.
- **6.2 Runtime scaling.** Measure on 100k–1M-face meshes from the external
  corpus; set and document a budget; profile-driven fixes only.
- **6.3 OpenSCAD / faceted-by-construction policy.** Generate two corpus
  models (low/high \`$fn\`), then implement the policy as an explicit, reported
  decision (flag or auto-detect-and-announce) per DEVELOPMENT_PLAN "Mesh
  provenance" — the prism-vs-cylinder ambiguity is genuine and cannot be
  measured away.
- **6.4** Promote backlog items as models demand (OBJ/PLY input, boundary
  crack stitching, IGES export).

---

## Reserve — partition-level architecture (user sign-off required)

If, **as measured by the harness**, Phases 1–4 leave seeding quality or sweep
cost unacceptable, the remaining lever is replacing the per-face sweep with a
partition: recursive split-and-merge (earned-patch fits at nodes,
union-revalidate merges via \`fit_validate\`, identifiability guards becoming
"defer, don't reject" until merge time) and/or VSA-style global alternation.
Both are deliberately reserved: they rewrite known-working machinery
(\`resolve_claims\`, relabel, merge) and their known hard parts (cut lines vs
seams; inverted identifiability) are documented in DEVELOPMENT_PLAN
("Considered and not adopted"). **Do not start without bringing Phase 1–4
measurements to the user.**

---
```

```
pub fn stage2(
    config: &Config,
    mesh: ConnectedMesh,
    viz: Option<&crate::viz::VizSender>,
) -> Result<Stage2Output, Stage2Error> {
    // --- Stage 2.1(a): sharp-edge classification (fit-free) ---
    let t = Instant::now();
    let edge_classes = edges::classify_edges(&mesh, config.angular_tolerance_rad);
    if config.verbosity >= 1 {
        let total = edge_classes.sharp_count + edge_classes.interior_count;
        eprintln!(
            "Stage 2.1(a) ({:.3}s): Sharp-edge classification: {} manifold edges — {} sharp, {} interior",
            t.elapsed().as_secs_f64(),
            total,
            edge_classes.sharp_count,
            edge_classes.interior_count,
        );
    }
    // --- Stage 2.1(b): osculating-jet curvature prior ---
    let t = Instant::now();
    let jet = edges::compute_jet_field(&mesh, &edge_classes);
    if config.verbosity >= 1 {
        eprintln!(
            "Stage 2.1(b) ({:.3}s): Jet curvature prior: {} faces summarized",
            t.elapsed().as_secs_f64(),
            jet.len(),
        );
    }
    let mut segmentation = Segmentation {
        edge_classes,
        jet,
        face_region: Vec::new(),
        regions: Vec::new(),
    };
    if config.viz_active(2, 1) {
        if let Some(vs) = viz {
            let overlay = segmentation_edges_overlay(&mesh, &segmentation.edge_classes);
            if matches!(vs.show_and_wait(overlay), VizAction::Quit) {
                return Ok(segmentation_only_output(mesh, segmentation));
            }
        }
    }
    if !config.stage.at_least(2, 2) {
        return Ok(segmentation_only_output(mesh, segmentation));
    }

    // --- Stage 2.2: region extraction ---
    let t = Instant::now();
    let (face_region, region_list) =
        regions::extract_regions(&mesh, &segmentation.edge_classes);
    if config.verbosity >= 1 {
        let single = region_list.iter().filter(|r| r.faces.len() == 1).count();
        let largest = region_list.iter().map(|r| r.faces.len()).max().unwrap_or(0);
        eprintln!(
            "Stage 2.2 ({:.3}s): Region extraction: {} regions over {} faces ({} single-face, largest {} faces)",
            t.elapsed().as_secs_f64(),
            region_list.len(),
            mesh.faces.len(),
            single,
            largest,
        );
        if config.verbosity >= 2 {
            for (i, r) in region_list.iter().enumerate() {
                if r.faces.len() > 1 {
                    eprintln!(
                        "  Region {}: {} faces, {} vertices (first face {})",
                        i,
                        r.faces.len(),
                        r.vertices.len(),
                        r.faces[0],
                    );
                }
            }
        }
    }
    segmentation.face_region = face_region;
    segmentation.regions = region_list;
    if config.viz_active(2, 2) {
```

## 🤖 Assistant
<!-- msg_011CgwaFGHYkQRzU2y3aTYY3 -->

## Verdict

The core ideas are sound, but the project optimised the wrong target. It reproduces reference B-reps to 5e-5 mm on small clean parts and mostly cannot convert a real part. I'd keep the foundations, restructure the pipeline around "never fail, degrade gracefully", and rewrite the surface-discovery loop. I would not start over.

## What I measured

I ran the existing reference sweep, then every corpus STL with **no** reference (120 s limit), checking each output against its input mesh.

| | Synthetic / own exports (138) | Real-world (56) |
|---|---|---|
| Valid solid, faithful to mesh | 106 | **13** |
| …and face types match the original | 92 | 5 |
| Exit 0 but invalid solid | 6 | 6 |
| Hard failure | 7 | 14 |
| Timeout | 1 | 22 |

"Faithful" means mesh vertices within 1e-3 mm of the output and volume within 2%. That threshold wrongly flags some of the 18 remaining synthetic models, which are coarse meshes with a correct result. Test suite and clippy are green (3.4 min).

Why real parts fail:

- **Freeform surfaces stall classification (22 timeouts).** Every facet in a smooth region seeds a fit of every surface type. A 3,500-triangle button with one spline surface does not finish in 150 s; 3DBenchy's hull is a single 139k-facet region.
- **Stage 3 is all-or-nothing (10 failures).** One face with an unsupported loop/seam/pole layout aborts the whole model, so more faces means more ways to fail.
- **Non-manifold meshes are rejected outright (4 failures).**
- **No self-check.** Without a reference STEP, an invalid or zero-volume result exits 0.
- **Chamfers become spheres.** In 4 of the 12 "good" real parts with a reference, every cone came out as a sphere band. A single row of quads between two circles fits a sphere exactly, and the sphere wins as the simpler type. The reference comparison passes these.
- **"Exact vertices" is only ~95% true.** On verified real pairs, p95 vertex error is at float precision, but the tail reaches 2e-4 to 5e-3 mm against a tolerance of 5e-5 that is treated as decisive.

## Why it stalled

- **The yardstick was wrong.** Success meant matching the original CAD file at every stage, which pulled months of work into float-precision questions on 12-facet cones.
- **Real-world hardening was scheduled last** ("Phase 6").
- **Since late July most commits measure or document rather than build.** Stage 2 has 76 tuned constants; the docs are ~530 KB that `AGENTS.md` tells every agent to read in full.

## Path forward

1. **Replace the yardstick.** Use a reference-free scoreboard over the real-world set: valid solid, fidelity to the input mesh, runtime, share of area that is analytic, and type agreement where a reference exists. Always self-check the output and fail loudly. A prototype is in `tmp/eval_noref.sh`, `tmp/eval_post.sh` and `tmp/eval_summary.py`; results are in `tmp/eval/post.tsv`.
2. **Make the pipeline total.** Add "faceted" as a first-class surface type. Any region that can't be classified in budget, or any face stage 3 can't build, is demoted to planar facets and its neighbours rebuilt. Repair non-manifold edges and turn invariant panics into repairs. Target: 56/56 real parts produce a valid, faithful solid; quality then becomes a number to raise.
3. **Rewrite surface discovery (stage 2.3/2.4, ~6k lines).** Keep the sharp-edge partition and the fitters. Replace per-facet seeding with budgeted sampled seeds, deduplicated candidates, and early "this is freeform" exit.
4. **Fix quality by real-world frequency.**
   - Cone versus sphere: use facet evidence, not only vertices. Ruling edges lie on a cone but not on the impostor sphere; this is an untested hypothesis.
   - Stray vertices: validation should tolerate the tail rather than fragment on it.
   - Missing cylinders: `dock_to_rhxs` recovers 7 of 12.
   - Splines swallowing planes and fillets: a rounded cube comes out as 8 spheres plus one spline.
5. **Shrink the docs.** Archive the plan/TODO/learnings and write a ~200-line design doc with a short dead-ends list. Retire the ~5k lines of invariant instrumentation once the scoreboard exists.

Keep stage 1, the fitters, stage 3's shared-edge assembly (it needs isolation, not replacement), and the corpus.

## 🤖 Assistant
<!-- msg_011CgwaPNCi4bBGcLfpVjeBW -->

That late background job (vertex distance of each real-world mesh to its reference STEP) finished, and it softens one of my findings rather than changing the recommendation.

Of the 53 real-world pairs, 36 produced a measurement within the 120 s limit (17 did not):

- **21 have every vertex within the 5e-5 mm tolerance**, so on those the "exact vertices" premise holds fully.
- **4 are genuine pairs with a stray tail** (worst vertex 3e-4 to 6e-3 mm).
- **11 are more than 0.01 mm off**, which means the STL and STEP are not the same geometry (different revision or frame), so they say nothing about exactness.

So "only ~95% true" overstated it: I had generalised from a few of the tail cases. A fairer statement is that exactness holds on most real meshes, and a minority carry a stray-vertex tail that the all-vertices-must-pass rule can't absorb. Tolerating the tail still belongs in step 4, but it is a lower-frequency problem than the timeouts, the all-or-nothing stage 3, and the chamfer-to-sphere confusion.

Separately, those 11 mismatched pairs (plus however many of the 17 unmeasured ones) shouldn't be used as ground truth in the new scoreboard; they are still fine as reference-free inputs.

Five models have a true stray tail, and two more have a thicker one. I re-measured all twelve real-world pairs that narrowly miss the 5e-5 mm tolerance, this time with percentiles, because my earlier list of four was partly wrong.

**True stray tail** (at least 95% of vertices within tolerance, a few far outside):

| Model | Vertices | p50 (mm) | p95 (mm) | Max (mm) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ToolChanger__blower_fan_duct` | 2,889 | 1.9e-6 | 7.0e-6 | 4.3e-4 |
| `ToolChanger__blower_fan_duct_(m)` | 2,957 | 1.9e-6 | 6.8e-6 | 3.4e-4 |
| `ToolChanger__dock_brace` | 4,329 | 2.5e-6 | 2.1e-5 | 4.6e-3 |
| `ToolChanger__docking_station` | 8,330 | 3.8e-7 | 1.9e-6 | 1.8e-4 |
| `ToolChanger__docking_station_(m)` | 8,372 | 5.2e-7 | 2.3e-6 | 1.8e-4 |

**Thicker tail** (median is exact, but more than 5% of vertices are outside tolerance):

| Model | Vertices | p50 (mm) | p95 (mm) | Max (mm) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `NucDeck__left_side_grip` | 7,759 | 6.4e-6 | 1.5e-4 | 9.8e-4 |
| `White-Knight__1-belt_stepper_direct_drive_mount2_for_e3d_v2` | 4,824 | 2.7e-6 | 1.5e-3 | 5.7e-3 |

**Not a tail** — the median vertex is already outside tolerance, so the whole mesh is offset from its reference:

- `NucDeck__trigger_button_left` and `NucDeck__trigger_button_right` (p50 about 6.2e-5)
- `ToolChanger__blower_fan_holder_arm` (p50 7.6e-5, p95 ≈ max)
- `ToolChanger__dock_brace_(m)` (p50 9.8e-3)
- `White-Knight__1-direct_drive_hotend_carriage_v10` (p50 7.6e-4)

Four of these five are paired with a rigidly re-framed (`_aligned`) reference, so alignment error is a likely cause, but I haven't confirmed it.

This corrects my previous message: of the four I named there, `trigger_button_right` and `blower_fan_holder_arm` are whole-mesh offsets, not tails. That job also missed several of the models above because it timed out on them.

I haven't checked where on each mesh the stray vertices sit (for example, whether they cluster on face boundaries). The full table is in `tmp/eval/tail.tsv`, produced by `tmp/eval_tail.sh`.

```
732	// Reference alignment (Phase 0.5b)
733	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
734	//
735	// \`gen_test_models align <dir>\` writes \`<stem>_aligned.step\` beside any
736	// \`<stem>.stl\` + \`<stem>.step\` pair whose two files describe the same part in
737	// different coordinate frames.
738	//
739	// Wild pairs need this. Measured over 18 STEP+STL pairs harvested from
740	// open-source hardware repos, half were published in different frames: the STL
741	// positioned for printing, the STEP left in design coordinates. Nine differ by a
742	// pure translation (up to 112 mm) and three by a 90 degree axis swap, which is
743	// Z-up versus Y-up. Those are the same object, and refusing to compare them
744	// measures the exporter's habits rather than the geometry.
745	//
746	// THE TRANSFORM IS DERIVED, NEVER FITTED. Translation comes from bounding-box
747	// centres and rotation is chosen from the 24 axis-aligned rotations by which one
748	// makes the *unsorted* extents match. Nothing here minimizes the vertex distance
749	// that the verification gate then measures, so the gate keeps its power to fail:
750	// a genuine pair collapses to ~1e-7 mm (measured: a NucDeck button went from
751	// 6.52 mm to 4.58e-7 after a (-0.5, 0, -6.5) translation), and a mismatched pair
752	// does not collapse under any of the 24. A free six-degree-of-freedom best fit
753	// would instead quietly minimize the very number being used as evidence.
754	//
755	// A pair whose extents match under no rotation is left alone: those are revision
756	// drift or genuinely different parts, and that is a finding to report rather
757	// than a transform to search for.
758	
759	/// Bounding box of a shape as (min, max).
760	///
761	/// The shape is meshed first, and that is not optional. \`BRepBndLib::Add\`'s
762	/// \`useTriangulation\` flag means "use a triangulation IF THE FACE HAS ONE"; a
763	/// shape just read from STEP has none, so OCCT falls back to bounds derived from
764	/// surface poles, which for B-spline and other curved faces enclose the control
765	/// hull rather than the surface. Measured on \`OrcaCube v2.step\`, a 30 mm cube:
766	/// the pole-based box reads 34.8 x 56.0 x 30.9, overestimating one axis by
767	/// 4.8 mm. Comparing that against an exact mesh bounding box — which is what
768	/// alignment does — turns a padded reference into a phantom size difference and
769	/// a wrong translation.
770	///
771	/// The deflection scales with the part, because a fixed absolute one does not
772	/// work: 1e-4 mm is wasted precision on a 10 mm button and takes minutes on a
773	/// 4.8 MB, 200 mm enclosure. The pole-based box is used only to size the part —
774	/// it is an overestimate, which is exactly the safe direction for choosing a
775	/// deflection — and the real box is then taken from the triangulation. The
776	/// target is a bounding box an order of magnitude tighter than the noise floor
777	/// this feeds (\`NOISE_SHIFT_MM\`), which is all the accuracy a centre-derived
778	/// translation can use.
779	fn shape_bounds(shape: &topo_ds::Shape) -> ([f64; 3], [f64; 3]) {
780	    let mut rough = bnd::Box::new();
781	    b_rep_bnd_lib::add_shape_box_bool(shape, &mut rough, true);
782	    let diag = if rough.is_void() {
783	        1.0
784	    } else {
785	        let d = [
786	            rough.get_x_max() - rough.get_x_min(),
787	            rough.get_y_max() - rough.get_y_min(),
788	            rough.get_z_max() - rough.get_z_min(),
789	        ];
790	        (d[0] * d[0] + d[1] * d[1] + d[2] * d[2]).sqrt()
791	    };
792	    let deflection = (diag * 5.0e-6).clamp(1.0e-4, 5.0e-3);
793	
794	    let _mesh = b_rep_mesh::IncrementalMesh::new_shape_real_bool_real_bool(
795	        shape, deflection, false, 0.1, false,
796	    );
797	    let mut bbox = bnd::Box::new();
798	    b_rep_bnd_lib::add_shape_box_bool(shape, &mut bbox, true);
799	    (
800	        [bbox.get_x_min(), bbox.get_y_min(), bbox.get_z_min()],
801	        [bbox.get_x_max(), bbox.get_y_max(), bbox.get_z_max()],
802	    )
803	}
804	
805	/// The 24 axis-aligned rotations: signed permutations of the axes with
806	/// determinant +1 (the proper rotations of a cube).
807	fn axis_rotations() -> Vec<[[f64; 3]; 3]> {
808	    let mut out = Vec::new();
809	    for perm in [[0, 1, 2], [0, 2, 1], [1, 0, 2], [1, 2, 0], [2, 0, 1], [2, 1, 0]] {
810	        for signs in 0..8 {
811	            let s = [
812	                if signs & 1 != 0 { -1.0 } else { 1.0 },
813	                if signs & 2 != 0 { -1.0 } else { 1.0 },
814	                if signs & 4 != 0 { -1.0 } else { 1.0 },
815	            ];
816	            let mut m = [[0.0_f64; 3]; 3];
817	            for r in 0..3 {
818	                m[r][perm[r]] = s[r];
819	            }
820	            let det = m[0][0] * (m[1][1] * m[2][2] - m[1][2] * m[2][1])
821	                - m[0][1] * (m[1][0] * m[2][2] - m[1][2] * m[2][0])
822	                + m[0][2] * (m[1][0] * m[2][1] - m[1][1] * m[2][0]);
823	            if det > 0.5 {
824	                out.push(m);
825	            }
826	        }
827	    }
828	    out
829	}
830	
831	fn align_corpus(dir: &str) {
832	    let mut aligned = 0;
833	    let mut untouched = Vec::new();
834	    let mut entries: Vec<_> = std::fs::read_dir(dir)
835	        .expect("cannot read alignment directory")
836	        .filter_map(|e| e.ok())
837	        .map(|e| e.path())
838	        .filter(|p| p.extension().is_some_and(|e| e.eq_ignore_ascii_case("stl")))
839	        .collect();
840	    entries.sort();
841	
842	    for stl_path in entries {
843	        let stem = stl_path.file_stem().unwrap().to_string_lossy().to_string();
844	        let step_path = format!("{dir}/{stem}.step");
845	        if !std::path::Path::new(&step_path).exists() {
846	            continue;
847	        }
848	        // brepper's reader, so ASCII and binary are both handled -- several of
849	        // these files begin with the text "solid" yet are binary.
850	        let mesh = match brepper::stage1::read_connected_mesh_from_stl(
851	            &stl_path.to_string_lossy(),
852	            brepper::stage1::VertexWeldOptions::default(),
853	        ) {
854	            Ok(m) => m,
855	            Err(e) => {
856	                untouched.push(format!("{stem}: STL unreadable ({e})"));
857	                continue;
858	            }
859	        };
860	        if mesh.vertices.is_empty() {
861	            continue;
862	        }
863	        let mut lo = [f64::MAX; 3];
864	        let mut hi = [f64::MIN; 3];
865	        for v in &mesh.vertices {
866	            for (i, c) in [v.x, v.y, v.z].into_iter().enumerate() {
867	                lo[i] = lo[i].min(c);
868	                hi[i] = hi[i].max(c);
869	            }
870	        }
871	        let mesh_size = [hi[0] - lo[0], hi[1] - lo[1], hi[2] - lo[2]];
872	        let mesh_centre = [
873	            (hi[0] + lo[0]) / 2.0,
874	            (hi[1] + lo[1]) / 2.0,
875	            (hi[2] + lo[2]) / 2.0,
876	        ];
877	
878	        let shape = match read_step_file(&step_path) {
879	            Ok(s) => s,
880	            Err(e) => {
881	                untouched.push(format!("{stem}: STEP unreadable ({e})"));
882	                continue;
883	            }
884	        };
885	        let (slo, shi) = shape_bounds(&shape);
886	        let step_size = [shi[0] - slo[0], shi[1] - slo[1], shi[2] - slo[2]];
887	        let step_centre = [
888	            (shi[0] + slo[0]) / 2.0,
889	            (shi[1] + slo[1]) / 2.0,
890	            (shi[2] + slo[2]) / 2.0,
891	        ];
892	        let scale = mesh_size.iter().fold(0.0_f64, |a, &b| a.max(b)).max(1e-9);
893	
894	        // The first rotation whose permuted extents match; extents alone decide,
895	        // never the distance the gate will measure.
896	        let chosen = axis_rotations().into_iter().find(|m| {
897	            (0..3).all(|r| {
898	                let rotated: f64 = (0..3).map(|c| m[r][c] * step_size[c]).sum::<f64>().abs();
899	                (rotated - mesh_size[r]).abs() / scale < 0.02
900	            })
901	        });
902	        let Some(m) = chosen else {
903	            untouched.push(format!(
904	                "{stem}: extents {:.1}x{:.1}x{:.1} vs {:.1}x{:.1}x{:.1} match under no rotation",
905	                mesh_size[0], mesh_size[1], mesh_size[2],
906	                step_size[0], step_size[1], step_size[2]
907	            ));
908	            continue;
909	        };
910	        let rotated_centre: Vec<f64> = (0..3)
911	            .map(|r| (0..3).map(|c| m[r][c] * step_centre[c]).sum())
912	            .collect();
913	        let t = [
914	            mesh_centre[0] - rotated_centre[0],
915	            mesh_centre[1] - rotated_centre[1],
916	            mesh_centre[2] - rotated_centre[2],
917	        ];
918	        let identity = m[0][0] == 1.0 && m[1][1] == 1.0 && m[2][2] == 1.0;
919	        let shift = (t[0] * t[0] + t[1] * t[1] + t[2] * t[2]).sqrt();
920	        // A translation this small is not evidence of displacement. Both centres
921	        // come from bounding boxes, and a tessellated mesh's box is inset from
922	        // the true solid by up to the sag — asymmetrically, so the centre
923	        // inherits an error of that order (~1e-2 mm on these meshes). Applying
924	        // it makes an already-framed pair WORSE: measured on the ToolChanger
925	        // ducts, whose vertex p95 went 6.9e-6 -> 4.4e-4 mm when a ~4e-4 mm
926	        // "correction" was applied to a pair that was already exact.
927	        //
928	        // The cut is safe rather than tuned: across the corpus the shifts are
929	        // bimodal with a 3000x empty gap — noise at 5e-4 and 2e-3 mm, real
930	        // displacements at 6.5 mm and above — so any cut inside the gap gives
931	        // the same answer. The skipped magnitude is printed, so a future corpus
932	        // landing IN the gap shows up instead of being silently decided.
933	        const NOISE_SHIFT_MM: f64 = 1.0e-2;
934	        if identity && shift < NOISE_SHIFT_MM {
935	            println!("  {stem}: already aligned (bbox centres differ by {shift:.3e} mm, below the {NOISE_SHIFT_MM:.0e} mm noise floor)");
936	            continue;
937	        }
938	
939	        let mut trsf = gp::Trsf::new();
940	        trsf.set_values(
941	            m[0][0], m[0][1], m[0][2], t[0],
942	            m[1][0], m[1][1], m[1][2], t[1],
943	            m[2][0], m[2][1], m[2][2], t[2],
944	        );
945	        let mut xform = b_rep_builder_api::Transform::new_shape_trsf_bool(&shape, &trsf, true);
946	        let moved = xform.as_modify_shape_mut().shape();
947	        write_step(moved, dir, &format!("{stem}_aligned"));
948	        println!(
949	            "  {stem}: {} translate ({:.3}, {:.3}, {:.3})",
950	            if identity { "aligned by".to_string() } else { format!("rotation {m:?} +") },
951	            t[0], t[1], t[2]
952	        );
953	        aligned += 1;
954	    }
955	
956	    println!("\naligned {aligned}; left alone {}:", untouched.len());
957	    for u in &untouched {
958	        println!("  {u}");
959	    }
960	}
961	
962	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
963	// Randomized variants (Phase 0.3)
964	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
965	//
966	// \`gen_test_models random [<out_dir>] [<per_family>] [<seed>]\` writes a seeded
967	// population of parameterized models: STL + STEP pair each, at a tessellation
968	// density that is also drawn.
969	//
970	// Why random: fourteen hand-watched models can be satisfied by machinery that
971	// happens to suit their particular radii and fillet sizes. A seeded population
972	// cannot be memorized — the parameters land where no constant was ever tuned.
973	// The families deliberately sweep the quantities the tuned constants care
974	// about: fillet radius against face size, torus r/R across the whole range up
```
