```
//! Geometric comparison against a reference STEP — and the trap that made three
//! of these gates read zero for every input, right and wrong alike.
//!
//! # Never measure a distance against a solid
//!
//! \`BRepExtrema_DistShapeShape\` computes the **minimum** distance between two
//! shapes, and it reports **zero whenever one lies inside the other**. Point
//! against a solid therefore answers "is it inside?", not "how far is it from
//! the surface?", and shape against shape answers "do they overlap?", not "do
//! they agree?". Both are useless as accuracy gates, and neither announces
//! itself: a wrong answer and a perfect one both print \`0.000000e0\`.
//!
//! Measured 2026-07-29, all three found at once:
//!
//! * stage 1's vertex check passed a mesh written 1000× too small — a 25 mm
//!   sphere spanning 0.025 mm sat wholly inside its own reference and reported
//!   a distance of exactly 0. Its centroid check was worse than useless: an
//!   inscribed tessellation puts every facet centroid *inside* the solid, which
//!   is precisely the sag the check exists to measure, so it read 0 on convex
//!   geometry everywhere. One of the two recorded sag truth values was 4.3×
//!   understated as a result.
//! * stage 3.4 sampled a point per face against the reference solid, same trap.
//! * stages 3.6 and 4.1 compared our solid to the reference solid and gated on
//!   the result. Two solids that overlap at all are at distance zero, so those
//!   gates never fired. Measured on a decomposition with 9 surfaces against a
//!   reference 26 and *no planes at all*: both printed \`0.000000e0\`, exactly as
//!   for a perfect model.
//!
//! # What to use instead
//!
//! * A point against a boundary: [\`face_compound\`], then the point-distance
//!   helpers in [\`crate::stage1\`]. A compound of faces has no inside.
//! * Two shapes against each other: [\`boundary_deviation\`]. Note that swapping
//!   in face compounds is **not** sufficient here — the minimum distance
//!   between two boundaries that touch anywhere is still zero. It samples the
//!   reference's surface and measures each point to ours, which is also the one
//!   direction nothing else checks.
//!
//! If you add a comparison, ask what your metric returns for a *grossly* wrong
//! input. If that is indistinguishable from a right one, the metric is wrong.

use opencascade_sys::{b_rep, b_rep_mesh, top_abs, top_exp, top_loc, topo_ds, OwnedPtr};

/// A compound of every face of \`shape\` — the correct target for a
/// point-to-boundary distance.
///
/// A solid is not: see the module docs. Stage 3 builds edge and vertex
/// compounds for its own compares for the same reason.
pub fn face_compound(shape: &topo_ds::Shape) -> OwnedPtr<topo_ds::Compound> {
    let builder = topo_ds::Builder::new();
    let mut compound = topo_ds::Compound::new();
    builder.make_compound(&mut compound);
    let mut explorer = top_exp::Explorer::new_shape_shapeenum2(
        shape,
        top_abs::ShapeEnum::Face,
        top_abs::ShapeEnum::Shape,
    );
    while explorer.more() {
        builder.add(compound.as_shape_mut(), explorer.value());
        explorer.next();
    }
    compound
}

/// Triangulation deflection used by [\`boundary_deviation\`], as a fraction of
/// the tolerance being tested against.
///
/// The deviation is sampled at triangulation nodes, so its resolution is the
/// deflection it meshes at. A tenth of the tolerance keeps the discretization
/// an order below the quantity being gated. This is a numerical-accuracy choice
/// for a diagnostic, not a tuned threshold: it trades runtime for resolution and
/// changes no decision except by making the measurement sharper. It also tracks
/// \`--surface-tolerance\`, so tightening that in Phase 3 sharpens this for free.
const DEVIATION_MESH_FRACTION: f64 = 0.1;

/// Sample points: every triangulation node of every face of \`shape\`.
///
/// The shape must already be meshed. Node coordinates are in the face's local
/// frame, so the face location has to be applied — see \`viz.rs\`, which reads
/// triangulations the same way.
fn triangulation_nodes(shape: &topo_ds::Shape) -> Vec<[f64; 3]> {
    let mut points = Vec::new();
    let mut explorer = top_exp::Explorer::new_shape_shapeenum2(
        shape,
        top_abs::ShapeEnum::Face,
        top_abs::ShapeEnum::Shape,
    );
    while explorer.more() {
        let face = topo_ds::face_shape(explorer.value());
        let mut location = top_loc::Location::new();
        let tri_handle = b_rep::Tool::triangulation(face, &mut location, 0);
        if tri_handle.is_null() {
            explorer.next();
            continue;
        }
        let tri = tri_handle.get();
        let has_location = !location.is_identity();
        for i in 1..=tri.nb_nodes() {
            let node = tri.node(i);
            let (mut x, mut y, mut z) = (node.x(), node.y(), node.z());
            if has_location {
                location
                    .transformation()
                    .transforms_real3(&mut x, &mut y, &mut z);
            }
            points.push([x, y, z]);
        }
        explorer.next();
    }
    points
}

/// How far the reference's boundary strays from ours: the maximum distance from
/// any point on the reference surface to our nearest surface.
///
/// This is the direction nothing else in the pipeline measures. Stage 1 and
/// stage 3.4 both go ours-to-reference, which cannot notice a reference feature
/// we failed to reproduce — our points can all sit perfectly on the reference
/// while whole regions of the reference have nothing of ours near them. Running
/// it the other way catches exactly that.
///
/// Built from sampled points against a face compound rather than from
/// \`DistShapeShape\` on the two shapes, for the reason in the module docs: a
/// minimum distance between overlapping shapes is zero, and between two
/// boundaries that touch anywhere it is also zero. \`BRepExtrema_ShapeProximity\`
/// was tried first and rejected — its "minimal thickness of a layer containing
/// both shapes" reported 13.2 mm for a hemisphere whose volume matched its
/// reference to 1.2e-7, so whatever it measures, it is not this.
///
/// Returns \`None\` if the reference cannot be sampled, which callers must treat
/// as "not measured" rather than as agreement.
pub fn boundary_deviation(
    ours: &topo_ds::Shape,
    reference: &topo_ds::Shape,
    tolerance: f64,
) -> Option<f64> {
    let deflection = (tolerance * DEVIATION_MESH_FRACTION).max(1.0e-6);
    let _mesh = b_rep_mesh::IncrementalMesh::new_shape_real_bool_real_bool(
        reference,
        deflection,
        false,
        0.5, // ~28.6 degrees, matching the corpus generator's tessellation angle
        false,
    );
    let samples = triangulation_nodes(reference);
    if samples.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    let ours_faces = face_compound(ours);
    let (max_dist, _) = crate::stage1::max_distance_to_shape(&samples, ours_faces.as_shape());
    Some(max_dist)
}
```

```
pub fn label_faces(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, model: &ReferenceModel) -> Vec<FaceLabel> {
    let n = mesh.faces.len();
    let unlabeled = FaceLabel {
        support: Support::None,
        distance: f64::MAX,
        uv: None,
        ambiguous: false,
    };
    if n == 0 || model.is_empty() {
        return vec![unlabeled; n];
    }

    let label_one = |fi: usize| -> FaceLabel {
        if mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count == 0 {
            return unlabeled;
        }
        let pts = sample_points(mesh, fi);
        let (distance, support, uv) = nearest(pts[0], model);
        let mut ambiguous = false;
        for &p in &pts[1..] {
            let (_, s, _) = nearest(p, model);
            if s != support {
                ambiguous = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        FaceLabel {
            support,
            distance,
            uv,
            ambiguous,
        }
    };

    let threads = std::thread::available_parallelism()
        .map(|p| p.get())
        .unwrap_or(1)
        .min(8)
        .min(n.div_ceil(16).max(1));
    if threads <= 1 {
        return (0..n).map(label_one).collect();
    }

    struct SharedModel(*const ReferenceModel);
    unsafe impl Send for SharedModel {}
    unsafe impl Sync for SharedModel {}
    let shared = SharedModel(model as *const _);

    let chunk = n.div_ceil(threads);
    let mut out = vec![unlabeled; n];
    std::thread::scope(|s| {
        for (ci, out_chunk) in out.chunks_mut(chunk).enumerate() {
            let shared = &shared;
            s.spawn(move || {
                let model = unsafe { &*shared.0 };
                let base = ci * chunk;
                for (k, slot) in out_chunk.iter_mut().enumerate() {
                    let fi = base + k;
                    if mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count == 0 {
                        continue;

                    let pts = sample_points(mesh, fi);
                    let (distance, support, uv) = nearest(pts[0], model);
                    let mut ambiguous = false;
                    for &p in &pts[1..] {
                        let (_, s, _) = nearest(p, model);
                        if s != support {
                            ambiguous = true;
                            break;
                        }
                    }
                    *slot = FaceLabel {
                        support,
                        distance,
                        uv,
                        ambiguous,
                    };
                }
            });
        }
    });
    out
}
```

```
impl Error for CompareError {}

/// Compute the minimum distance from a point to the bounded compare shape
/// using BRepExtrema_DistShapeShape, which respects face trimming boundaries.
///
/// Pass a compound of FACES, never a solid: \`DistShapeShape\` reports zero for a
/// point inside a solid, so a solid target silently turns this into a
/// containment test. See [\`crate::compare\`].
pub fn min_distance_to_shape(
    pt: &gp::Pnt,
    compare_shape: &opencascade_sys::topo_ds::Shape,
) -> f64 {
    let mut vertex = b_rep_builder_api::MakeVertex::new_pnt(pt);
    let vtx_shape = vertex.vertex();
    let progress = message::ProgressRange::new();
    let dist_calc = b_rep_extrema::DistShapeShape::new_shape2_extflag_extalgo_progressrange(
        vtx_shape.as_shape(),
        compare_shape,
        0, // F (unused/obsolete)
        extrema::ExtAlgo::Grad,
        &progress,
    );
    if dist_calc.is_done() && dist_calc.nb_solution() > 0 {
        dist_calc.value()
    } else {
        f64::MAX
    }
}

/// Compute the minimum distance from each point to the bounded compare shape,
/// in parallel across threads. Returns one distance per input point.
///
/// Safety: \`BRepExtrema_DistShapeShape\`, \`BRepBuilderAPI_MakeVertex\`, and the
/// \`gp\` value types have no global mutable state and do not mutate the target
/// shape (verified in the OCCT C++ source — see LEARNINGS.md "OCCT Thread
/// Safety"), so sharing a read-only \`&Shape\` across threads is sound.
pub fn distances_to_shape(
    points: &[[f64; 3]],
    shape: &opencascade_sys::topo_ds::Shape,
) -> Vec<f64> {
    let n = points.len();
    let threads = std::thread::available_parallelism()
        .map(|p| p.get())
        .unwrap_or(1)
        .min(8)
        .min(n.div_ceil(16).max(1));
    if threads <= 1 {
        return points
            .iter()
            .map(|p| {
                let pt = gp::Pnt::new_real3(p[0], p[1], p[2]);
                min_distance_to_shape(&pt, shape)
            })
            .collect();
    }

    struct SharedShape(*const opencascade_sys::topo_ds::Shape);
    unsafe impl Send for SharedShape {}
    unsafe impl Sync for SharedShape {}
    let shared = SharedShape(shape as *const _);

    let chunk = n.div_ceil(threads);
    let mut out = vec![0.0_f64; n];
    std::thread::scope(|s| {
        for (pts_chunk, out_chunk) in points.chunks(chunk).zip(out.chunks_mut(chunk)) {
            let shared = &shared;
            s.spawn(move || {
                let shape = unsafe { &*shared.0 };
                for (p, o) in pts_chunk.iter().zip(out_chunk.iter_mut()) {
                    let pt = gp::Pnt::new_real3(p[0], p[1], p[2]);
                    *o = min_distance_to_shape(&pt, shape);
                }
            });
        }
    });
    out
}

/// Find the maximum of \`distances_to_shape\` over the points.
/// Returns (max_distance, index_of_max); (0.0, 0) for empty input.
pub fn max_distance_to_shape(
fn nearest(pt: [f64; 3], model: &ReferenceModel) -> (f64, Support, Option<(f64, f64)>) {
    let p = gp::Pnt::new_real3(pt[0], pt[1], pt[2]);
    let mut vertex = b_rep_builder_api::MakeVertex::new_pnt(&p);
    let vtx_shape = vertex.vertex();
    let progress = message::ProgressRange::new();
    let dist = b_rep_extrema::DistShapeShape::new_shape2_extflag_extalgo_progressrange(
        vtx_shape.as_shape(),
        model.shape(),
        0, // F (unused/obsolete)
        extrema::ExtAlgo::Grad,
        &progress,
    );
    if !dist.is_done() || dist.nb_solution() < 1 {
        return (f64::MAX, Support::None, None);
    }
    let support = match dist.support_type_shape2(1) {
        b_rep_extrema::SupportType::Isinface => {
            let shape = dist.support_on_shape2(1);
            match model.support_index(&shape) {
                Some(i) => Support::Face(i),
                None => Support::None,
            }
        }
        // The closest point on the reference lies on an edge or a vertex of it,
        // so the sample is off the end of any single face's trimmed domain.
        _ => Support::Seam,
    };
    // The footpoint's parameters on the winning face, for the freeform normals
    // that cannot be evaluated from the sample point. Only meaningful when the
    // support is a face.
    let uv = match support {
        Support::Face(_) => {
            let (mut u, mut v) = (0.0_f64, 0.0_f64);
            dist.par_on_face_s2(1, &mut u, &mut v);
            Some((u, v))
        }
        _ => None,
    };
    (dist.value(), support, uv)
}
//! Generates test models that cannot be produced via ccad, using OCCT
//! directly. The STL/STEP pairs are written to tests/occt/ and tests/nurbs/
//! and committed to the repo, so this tool only needs to be re-run when a
//! model changes.
//!
//! Usage: gen_test_models [<occt_dir>] [<nurbs_dir>]
//!        (defaults: tests/occt tests/nurbs)
//!
//! tests/occt/ models (analytic, exercise the existing pipeline):
//! - hollow_cube: 20 mm cube with a fully enclosed 10 mm cubic void at its
```

Your usage limit was reached partway through this, so the provenance half is done and the alignment fix is not.

**Done: CAD provenance.** Yes, the files say where they came from. I read each STEP header and each STL's 80-byte header and wrote the result to [tests/external/README.md](tests/external/README.md):

| Repo | Exporter |
|---|---|
| NucDeck (8), ToolChanger (10 of 11) | SolidWorks 2021 |
| Open-Task-Light (10), VoronUsers strip mounts and snap-ins (5), ToolChanger `hemera_bowden_bracket`, OpenBot `front_light_spacer`, `OrcaCube v2` | Fusion 360, confirmed in both STEP and STL |
| White-Knight (9), VoronUsers chain anchors (4) | Fusion 360 STEP; only one of these STLs carries a Fusion signature, the rest have no signature |
| OpenBot joints (3) | Siemens NX 9 STEP; STL header blank |
| VoronUsers `10x11_befenybay_chain_top_anchor` | CATIA V5 STEP; STL unsigned |
| VoronUsers `2020-wago_221-412_tray-5x2` | unknown (blank originating system) |
| `3DBenchy` | FreeCAD / Open CASCADE STEP |

So the real-world set is SolidWorks and Fusion 360 plus a few NX and one CATIA part; nothing is from Onshape or Rhino. Where the STL has no signature, the STL exporter is inferred from the STEP and may differ.

**Diagnosed but not fixed: alignment.** The existing aligner (`gen_test_models align`) translates by the difference of bounding-box centres and tries only the 24 axis-aligned rotations. A mesh's bounding box is inset by up to its chord error, so the translation is only good to about 1e-4 to 1e-2 mm, which is why the five "whole mesh offset" pairs miss the 5e-5 tolerance. The earlier agent avoided fitting a transform on purpose, to keep the check honest.

**What's left:**
- Add a rigid refinement after the derived transform: least-squares fit of mesh vertices to the reference surfaces, translation first and full rotation only if needed.
- Regenerate the `_aligned.step` files and re-measure p50/p95/max for every pair.
- Sort the 11 pairs that are more than 0.01 mm off into "same part, different frame" and "different revision".
- The five true stray-tail models won't reach "all vertices within tolerance" by alignment alone, since their bulk is already exact; I'd expect them to keep a few stray vertices.

The README also records the measured distances and this plan. Nothing is committed.

```
/// The reference model: a face compound to measure against, plus one
/// [\`RefSurface\`] per face **in compound-explorer order**.
///
/// The order matters: [\`ReferenceModel::support_index\`] recovers a face index
/// by walking the same compound with the same explorer, so the two orders are
/// the same by construction rather than by assumption.
pub struct ReferenceModel {
    compound: OwnedPtr<topo_ds::Compound>,
    /// Face → index, for turning a \`SupportOnShape2\` result back into a
    /// [\`Self::surfaces\`] subscript in O(1).
    ///
    /// This is OCCT's \`TopTools_IndexedMapOfShape\`. That name is a *deprecated
    /// typedef* in OCCT 8.0 and does not appear in the bindings; the canonical
    /// type does, spelled out as its template instantiation. \`ShapeMapHasher\`
    /// is the variant whose equality is \`TopoDS_Shape::IsSame\`, which is the
    /// comparison this needs.
    face_index: OwnedPtr<n_collection::IndexedMap_TopoDS_Shape_TopTools_ShapeMapHasher>,
    /// The underlying geometry of each face, for the freeform types that have
    /// no closed-form normal. \`BRep_Tool::Surface(F)\` applies the face's
    /// location, so these are in world coordinates and share the (u,v)
    /// parameterization that \`ParOnFaceS2\` reports.
    ///
    /// Only read by [\`Self::normal_at_uv\`], which runs single-threaded in
    /// [\`report\`]; labeling never touches these, which is what keeps the
    /// \`unsafe impl Sync\` on the sharing wrapper in [\`label_faces\`] honest.
    geometry: Vec<OwnedPtr<geom::Handle_Geom_Surface>>,
    pub surfaces: Vec<RefSurface>,
}

impl ReferenceModel {
    /// Build the ground truth from a \`--compare\` shape.
    pub fn load(shape: &topo_ds::Shape) -> Self {
        let compound = crate::compare::face_compound(shape);
        let mut surfaces = Vec::new();
        let mut face_index =
            n_collection::IndexedMap_TopoDS_Shape_TopTools_ShapeMapHasher::new();
        let mut explorer = top_exp::Explorer::new_shape_shapeenum2(
            compound.as_shape(),
            top_abs::ShapeEnum::Face,
            top_abs::ShapeEnum::Shape,
        );
        let mut geometry = Vec::new();
        while explorer.more() {
            let face = topo_ds::face_shape(explorer.value());
            surfaces.push(read_surface(face));
            geometry.push(b_rep::Tool::surface_face(face));
            face_index.add(explorer.value());
            explorer.next();
        }
        Self {
            compound,
            face_index,
            geometry,
            surfaces,
        }
    }

    /// The exact unit surface normal of reference face \`i\` at parameters
    /// \`(u, v)\`, unoriented — the freeform counterpart of
    /// [\`RefSurface::normal_at\`].
    ///
    /// Uses \`GeomLProp_SLProps\`, which reports \`IsNormalDefined\` rather than
    /// silently returning a zero-length \`D1U × D1V\`. That matters here: a
    /// B-spline reference face has poles and seams where the normal genuinely
    /// does not exist, and those must be dropped from the statistics rather
    /// than counted as an error of some size.
    ///
    /// \`RESOLUTION\` is the linear tolerance below which SLProps calls a
    /// derivative vector null. It is a numeric-conditioning floor, not a
    /// threshold: it decides only whether a quantity exists, never whether a
    /// fit is good.
    pub fn normal_at_uv(&self, i: usize, u: f64, v: f64) -> Option<[f64; 3]> {
        const RESOLUTION: f64 = 1.0e-12;
        let surface = self.geometry.get(i)?;
        let mut props =
            geom_l_prop::SLProps::new_handlegeomsurface_real2_int_real(surface, u, v, 1, RESOLUTION);
        if !props.is_normal_defined() {
            return None;
        }
        let n = props.normal();
        unit([n.x(), n.y(), n.z()])
    }

    /// The compound of reference faces — the correct distance target. Never
    /// measure against the solid: see [\`crate::compare\`].
    pub fn shape(&self) -> &topo_ds::Shape {
        self.compound.as_shape()
    }

    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.surfaces.len()
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.surfaces.is_empty()
    }

//! - hill_with_hole: bspline_hill minus an off-center vertical cylinder.
//!   Freeform × analytic interaction: inner loop on the B-spline face,
//!   cylinder∩B-spline edge curves, tessellated (irregular) mesh.
//! - elliptical_cylinder: full elliptical prism — a closed periodic
//!   freeform wall (stretch case: needs a periodic B-spline face + seam).

use brepper::read_step_file;
use opencascade_sys::{
    b_rep_algo_api, b_rep_bnd_lib, b_rep_check, b_rep_fillet_api, b_rep_g_prop, b_rep_mesh,
    b_rep_prim_api, bnd,
    b_rep_builder_api, b_rep_tools, ch_fi3d, g_prop, geom, gp, message, stl_api,
    n_collection, top_abs, top_exp, topo_ds, OwnedPtr,
};
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::f64::consts::PI;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Shared helpers
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn write_step(shape: &topo_ds::Shape, dir: &str, name: &str) {
    let step_path = format!("{dir}/{name}.step");
    brepper::write_step_file(shape, &step_path).expect("failed to write STEP");
    println!("wrote {step_path}");
}

/// Tessellate a shape and write its STL (used for occt/ models and for
/// nurbs models whose mesh should look like a real CAD export).
fn write_tessellated_stl(shape: &topo_ds::Shape, dir: &str, name: &str, deflection: f64, angle_deg: f64) {
    let _mesh = b_rep_mesh::IncrementalMesh::new_shape_real_bool_real_bool(
        shape, deflection, false, angle_deg.to_radians(), false,
    );
    let stl_path = format!("{dir}/{name}.stl");
    let mut writer = stl_api::Writer::new();
    *writer.ascii_mode() = false;
    let progress = message::ProgressRange::new();
    if !writer.write_shape_charptr_progressrange(shape, &stl_path, &progress) {
        panic!("failed to write {stl_path}");
    }
    println!("wrote {stl_path}");
}

fn write_pair(shape: &topo_ds::Shape, dir: &str, name: &str) {
    write_tessellated_stl(shape, dir, name, 0.1, 28.6);
    write_step(shape, dir, name);
}
```

```bash
# Volume, area, bbox extents of a binary/ASCII STL (numpy-free).
import struct, sys
def read(path):
    b=open(path,'rb').read()
    n=struct.unpack_from('<I',b,80)[0] if len(b)>=84 else 0
    if 84+50*n==len(b):
        tris=[]
        for i in range(n):
            f=struct.unpack_from('<12f',b,84+50*i)
            tris.append((f[3:6],f[6:9],f[9:12]))
        return tris
    import re
    v=[tuple(map(float,m.groups())) for m in re.finditer(rb'vertex\s+(\S+)\s+(\S+)\s+(\S+)',b)]
    return [tuple(v[i:i+3]) for i in range(0,len(v),3)]
def props(path):
    tris=read(path); vol=0.0; area=0.0
    lo=[1e300]*3; hi=[-1e300]*3
    for a,b,c in tris:
        for p in (a,b,c):
            for k in range(3):
                lo[k]=min(lo[k],p[k]); hi[k]=max(hi[k],p[k])
        ux,uy,uz=b[0]-a[0],b[1]-a[1],b[2]-a[2]; vx,vy,vz=c[0]-a[0],c[1]-a[1],c[2]-a[2]
        cx,cy,cz=uy*vz-uz*vy,uz*vx-ux*vz,ux*vy-uy*vx
        area+=0.5*(cx*cx+cy*cy+cz*cz)**0.5
        vol+=(a[0]*(b[1]*c[2]-b[2]*c[1])-a[1]*(b[0]*c[2]-b[2]*c[0])+a[2]*(b[0]*c[1]-b[1]*c[0]))/6
    return vol,area,[hi[k]-lo[k] for k in range(3)]
if __name__=='__main__':
    v,a,e=props(sys.argv[1]); print("%.4f\t%.4f\t%.3f x %.3f x %.3f"%(v,a,*e))
EOF
```

```bash
/// A point's closest approach to the reference boundary: where it landed and,
/// when that is the interior of a face, the surface normal there.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct Footpoint {
    pub distance: f64,
    /// The closest point on the reference.
    pub point: [f64; 3],
    /// Unit surface normal at `point`, unoriented. `None` when the closest
    /// point is on an edge or vertex of the reference (no single face owns it)
    /// or at a pole/seam where the normal does not exist.
    pub normal: Option<[f64; 3]>,
}

/// The footpoint of every point on the reference. `None` where OCCT found no
/// solution.
///
/// This is what a point-to-surface registration needs (`gen_test_models
/// align`): the residual along the *surface* normal, which stays well defined
/// as the distance goes to zero, where the direction of `point - footpoint`
/// does not.
///
/// The distance queries run in parallel, exactly as in [`label_faces`]; the
/// normals are evaluated afterwards on the calling thread, because
/// [`ReferenceModel::normal_at_uv`] reads the geometry handles that the
/// labeling threads must not touch.
pub fn footpoints(points: &[[f64; 3]], model: &ReferenceModel) -> Vec<Option<Footpoint>> {
    type Raw = (f64, Support, Option<(f64, f64)>, [f64; 3]);
    let n = points.len();
    if n == 0 || model.is_empty() {
        return vec![None; n];
    }
    let threads = std::thread::available_parallelism()
        .map(|p| p.get())
        .unwrap_or(1)
        .min(8)
        .min(n.div_ceil(16).max(1));
    let mut raw: Vec<Raw> = vec![(f64::MAX, Support::None, None, [0.0; 3]); n];
    if threads <= 1 {
        for (slot, &p) in raw.iter_mut().zip(points) {
            *slot = nearest_with_point(p, model);
        }
    } else {
        struct SharedModel(*const ReferenceModel);
        unsafe impl Send for SharedModel {}
        unsafe impl Sync for SharedModel {}
        let shared = SharedModel(model as *const _);
        let chunk = n.div_ceil(threads);
        std::thread::scope(|s| {
            for (pts_chunk, out_chunk) in points.chunks(chunk).zip(raw.chunks_mut(chunk)) {
                let shared = &shared;
                s.spawn(move || {
                    let model = unsafe { &*shared.0 };
                    for (p, slot) in pts_chunk.iter().zip(out_chunk.iter_mut()) {
                        *slot = nearest_with_point(*p, model);
                    }
                });
            }
        });
    }
    raw.into_iter()
        .map(|(distance, support, uv, point)| {
            if distance == f64::MAX {
                return None;
            }
            let normal = match (support, uv) {
                (Support::Face(i), Some((u, v))) => model.normal_at_uv(i, u, v),
                _ => None,
            };
            Some(Footpoint { distance, point, normal })
        })
        .collect()
}
''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
```

```bash
new='''/// Exact mass properties of the solid bounded by the given faces of a closed
/// oriented mesh, by summing signed tetrahedra against the origin.
fn mesh_mass_props(mesh: &brepper::stage1::ConnectedMesh, faces: &[usize]) -> MassProps {
    let mut vol = 0.0_f64;
    let mut m1 = Vector3::zeros();
    let mut m2 = Matrix3::zeros();
    for &fi in faces {
        let f = &mesh.faces[fi];
        let n = f.vertex_count as usize;
        let p = |k: usize| {
            let v = &mesh.vertices[f.vertex_indices[k]];
            Vector3::new(v.x, v.y, v.z)
        };
        for k in 1..n.saturating_sub(1) {
            let (a, b, c) = (p(0), p(k), p(k + 1));
            let v = a.dot(&b.cross(&c)) / 6.0;
            let s = a + b + c;
            vol += v;
            m1 += s * (v / 4.0);
            // Integral of x xT over the tetrahedron (0, a, b, c).
            m2 += (a * a.transpose() + b * b.transpose() + c * c.transpose() + s * s.transpose())
                * (v / 20.0);
        }
    }
    let centre = m1 / vol;
    MassProps { volume: vol, centre, cov: m2 / vol - centre * centre.transpose() }
}

/// One connected body of the mesh: its vertices and its mass properties.
struct MeshBody {
    points: Vec<[f64; 3]>,
    mass: MassProps,
}

/// Split a mesh into its vertex-connected bodies, largest volume first.
fn mesh_bodies(mesh: &brepper::stage1::ConnectedMesh) -> Vec<MeshBody> {
    let n = mesh.vertices.len();
    let mut parent: Vec<usize> = (0..n).collect();
    fn find(parent: &mut [usize], mut i: usize) -> usize {
        while parent[i] != i {
            parent[i] = parent[parent[i]];
            i = parent[i];
        }
        i
    }
    for f in &mesh.faces {
        let a = find(&mut parent, f.vertex_indices[0]);
        for k in 1..f.vertex_count as usize {
            let b = find(&mut parent, f.vertex_indices[k]);
            parent[b] = a;
        }
    }
    let mut faces_of: HashMap<usize, Vec<usize>> = HashMap::new();
    for (fi, f) in mesh.faces.iter().enumerate() {
        if f.vertex_count >= 3 {
            let root = find(&mut parent, f.vertex_indices[0]);
            faces_of.entry(root).or_default().push(fi);
        }
    }
    let mut points_of: HashMap<usize, Vec<[f64; 3]>> = HashMap::new();
    for (vi, v) in mesh.vertices.iter().enumerate() {
        let root = find(&mut parent, vi);
        points_of.entry(root).or_default().push([v.x, v.y, v.z]);
    }
    let mut bodies: Vec<MeshBody> = faces_of
        .into_iter()
        .map(|(root, faces)| MeshBody {
            points: points_of.remove(&root).unwrap_or_default(),
            mass: mesh_mass_props(mesh, &faces),
        })
        .collect();
    bodies.sort_by(|a, b| b.mass.volume.abs().total_cmp(&a.mass.volume.abs()));
    bodies
}

/// Each solid of a shape, wrapped in its own compound, largest volume first.
fn step_solids(shape: &topo_ds::Shape) -> Vec<OwnedPtr<topo_ds::Compound>> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut explorer = top_exp::Explorer::new_shape_shapeenum2(
        shape,
        top_abs::ShapeEnum::Solid,
        top_abs::ShapeEnum::Shape,
    );
    while explorer.more() {
        let builder = topo_ds::Builder::new();
        let mut compound = topo_ds::Compound::new();
        builder.make_compound(&mut compound);
        builder.add(compound.as_shape_mut(), explorer.value());
        out.push(compound);
        explorer.next();
    }
    out.sort_by(|a, b| {
        shape_volume(b.as_shape()).abs().total_cmp(&shape_volume(a.as_shape()).abs())
    });
    out
}

fit='''/// Fit one rigid body: the motion `T` that carries `shape` (the reference, as
/// published) onto the mesh points, and the name of the coarse candidate it
/// was refined from.
fn fit_body(points: &[[f64; 3]], mesh_mass: &MassProps, shape: &topo_ds::Shape) -> (Rigid, String) {
    let mut lo = [f64::MAX; 3];
    let mut hi = [f64::MIN; 3];
    for p in points {
        for i in 0..3 {
            lo[i] = lo[i].min(p[i]);
            hi[i] = hi[i].max(p[i]);
        }
    }
    let mesh_size = Vector3::new(hi[0] - lo[0], hi[1] - lo[1], hi[2] - lo[2]);
    let mesh_centre = Vector3::new(hi[0] + lo[0], hi[1] + lo[1], hi[2] + lo[2]) / 2.0;
    let diag = mesh_size.norm().max(1e-9);
    let model = brepper::reference::ReferenceModel::load(shape);

    // --- Step 1: the coarse frame, from derived candidates. ---
    // Candidates are (label, T) with T mapping the reference into the mesh
    // frame; they are scored through T's inverse so the reference shape is
    // never moved.
    let score_pts = subsample(points, 80);
    let raw_score = distance_stats(&score_pts, &Rigid::identity(), &model)[0];
    let mut best = ("identity".to_string(), Rigid::identity(), raw_score);
    // Within a thousandth of the part's size the refinement converges from
    // where it stands, and searching frames would only cost time.
    if raw_score > 1.0e-3 * diag {
        let mut candidates: Vec<(String, Rigid)> = Vec::new();
        let (slo, shi) = shape_bounds(shape);
        let step_size = Vector3::new(shi[0] - slo[0], shi[1] - slo[1], shi[2] - slo[2]);
        let step_centre = Vector3::new(shi[0] + slo[0], shi[1] + slo[1], shi[2] + slo[2]) / 2.0;
        let scale = mesh_size.max();
        for (k, m) in axis_rotations().into_iter().enumerate() {
            let r = Matrix3::from_fn(|i, j| m[i][j]);
            let rotated = (r * step_size).abs();
            if (0..3).all(|i| (rotated[i] - mesh_size[i]).abs() / scale < 0.02) {
                candidates.push((format!("bbox#{k}"), Rigid { r, t: mesh_centre - r * step_centre }));
            }
        }
        let step_mass = step_mass_props(shape);
        let em = principal_axes(&mesh_mass.cov);
        let es = principal_axes(&step_mass.cov);
        for signs in 0..8 {
            let s = Matrix3::from_diagonal(&Vector3::new(
                if signs & 1 != 0 { -1.0 } else { 1.0 },
                if signs & 2 != 0 { -1.0 } else { 1.0 },
                if signs & 4 != 0 { -1.0 } else { 1.0 },
            ));
            let r = em * s * es.transpose();
            if r.determinant() > 0.0 {
                candidates.push((
                    format!("inertia#{signs}"),
                    Rigid { r, t: mesh_mass.centre - r * step_mass.centre },
                ));
            }
        }
        // Score every candidate where it stands, then refine the best few on a
        // small sample before choosing: principal axes are only as good as the
        // solid's moments are distinct, and a candidate that starts a few
        // degrees out can still be the right one.
        let mut scored: Vec<(f64, String, Rigid)> = candidates
            .into_iter()
            .map(|(label, t)| (distance_stats(&score_pts, &t.inverse(), &model)[0], label, t))
            .collect();
        scored.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.total_cmp(&b.0));
        let trial_pts = subsample(points, 200);
        for (_, label, t) in scored.into_iter().take(6) {
            let m = refine_rigid(t.inverse(), &trial_pts, &model);
            let score = distance_stats(&score_pts, &m, &model)[0];
            if score < best.2 {
                best = (label, m.inverse(), score);
            }
        }
    }
    let (coarse, coarse_t, _) = best;

    // --- Step 2: rigid refinement. ---
    let fitted_m = refine_rigid(coarse_t.inverse(), &subsample(points, 800), &model);
    (fitted_m.inverse(), coarse)
}
```

<details>
<summary>Bash: Add a diagnostic that tests stray vertices against the reference's untrimmed surfaces, and build</summary>

```bash
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='src/bin/gen_test_models.rs'
s=open(p).read()
diag='''// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Stray-vertex diagnosis
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
//
// `gen_test_models strays <stl> <step>` asks, of each mesh vertex that is
// farther than the vertex tolerance from the reference's TRIMMED faces, how far
// it is from the reference's UNTRIMMED surfaces: the smallest and the
// second-smallest such distance.
//
// The distinction matters because brepper validates a vertex against a fitted,
// unbounded surface, while every reference measurement here is against faces
// bounded by their edges. A boundary vertex should lie on two surfaces, so:
//
// * second-smallest within tolerance: the vertex is on both of its surfaces and
//   only misses the reference's trimming — exact for brepper's purposes.
// * smallest within, second not: it lies on one surface and off its neighbour,
//   which is what a vertex sampled from an approximated edge curve looks like.
// * smallest not within: it is off every surface of the reference.
fn diagnose_strays(stl_path: &str, step_path: &str) {
    let mesh = brepper::stage1::read_connected_mesh_from_stl(
        stl_path,
        brepper::stage1::VertexWeldOptions::default(),
    )
    .expect("STL unreadable");
    let shape = read_step_file(step_path).expect("STEP unreadable");
    let model = brepper::reference::ReferenceModel::load(&shape);
    let points: Vec<[f64; 3]> = mesh.vertices.iter().map(|v| [v.x, v.y, v.z]).collect();
    let tol = 5.0e-5_f64.max(brepper::stage1::float32_position_bound_mm(&mesh));
    let feet = brepper::reference::footpoints(&points, &model);

    let mut surfaces = Vec::new();
    let mut explorer = top_exp::Explorer::new_shape_shapeenum2(
        &shape,
        top_abs::ShapeEnum::Face,
        top_abs::ShapeEnum::Shape,
    );
    while explorer.more() {
        surfaces.push(b_rep::Tool::surface_face(topo_ds::face_shape(explorer.value())));
        explorer.next();
    }

    let (mut strays, mut on_both, mut on_one, mut on_none) = (0usize, 0usize, 0usize, 0usize);
    let mut worst_second = 0.0_f64;
    for (p, fp) in points.iter().zip(&feet) {
        let Some(fp) = fp else { continue };
        if fp.distance <= tol {
            continue;
        }
        strays += 1;
        let pnt = gp::Pnt::new_real3(p[0], p[1], p[2]);
        let mut d: Vec<f64> = surfaces
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|s| {
                let proj = geom_api::ProjectPointOnSurf::new_pnt_handlegeomsurface_extalgo(
                    &pnt,
                    s,
                    extrema::ExtAlgo::Grad,
                );
                (proj.is_done() && proj.nb_points() > 0).then(|| proj.lower_distance())
            })
            .collect();
        d.sort_by(f64::total_cmp);
        let (d1, d2) = (d.first().copied().unwrap_or(f64::MAX), d.get(1).copied().unwrap_or(f64::MAX));
        if d2 <= tol {
            on_both += 1;
        } else if d1 <= tol {
            on_one += 1;
            worst_second = worst_second.max(d2);
        } else {
            on_none += 1;
        }
        if strays <= 12 {
            println!(
                "  vertex ({:.4}, {:.4}, {:.4}): trimmed {:.2e}, untrimmed nearest {:.2e}, second {:.2e}{}",
                p[0], p[1], p[2], fp.distance, d1, d2,
                if fp.normal.is_none() { "  [nearest an edge]" } else { "" },
            );
        }
    }
    println!(
        "{strays} of {} vertices beyond {tol:.1e} mm of the trimmed reference: {on_both} lie on two \\
         untrimmed surfaces, {on_one} on one only (second surface up to {worst_second:.2e} mm away), \\
         {on_none} on none",
        points.len(),
    );
}

'''
i=s.index('// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Randomized variants (Phase 0.3)')
s=s[:i]+diag+s[i:]
old='''    if args.first().map(String::as_str) == Some("random") {'''
new='''    if args.first().map(String::as_str) == Some("strays") {
        diagnose_strays(
            args.get(1).expect("usage: gen_test_models strays <stl> <step>"),
            args.get(2).expect("usage: gen_test_models strays <stl> <step>"),
        );
        return;
    }
    if args.first().map(String::as_str) == Some("random") {'''
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new)
old='''    b_rep_builder_api, b_rep_tools, ch_fi3d, g_prop, geom, gp, message, stl_api,'''
new='''    b_rep, b_rep_builder_api, b_rep_tools, ch_fi3d, extrema, g_prop, geom, geom_api, gp, message,
    stl_api,'''
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
cargo build --release 2>&1 | grep -E '^(warning|error)' -A 14 | head -50
```

<!-- msg_011CgwzVePmFdU6abDVUUrJQ -->

Alignment is fixed wherever it was the problem, but not every vertex ends up within tolerance: 26 of the 53 pairs are now fully exact, and the rest have causes alignment can't touch.

## What was wrong with the alignment

- **Translation only as good as the mesh's chord error.** The old aligner matched bounding-box centres, which left five genuine pairs 6e-5 to 1e-2 mm off.
- **Wrong rotation picked.** It took the first axis-aligned rotation whose box extents matched, and a box has the same extents after a 180° flip. Six White-Knight pairs sat 10–17 mm off for this reason.
- **Two-body parts.** The four VoronUsers chain anchors have their two bodies laid out for printing in the STL and assembled in the STEP, so no single motion aligns them (they were 200–300 mm off).

The aligner (`gen-test-models align`) now scores candidate frames by actual vertex distance, refines with a rigid least-squares fit, fits multi-body parts body by body, and leaves already-exact pairs untouched.

## Result over 53 pairs (tolerance 5e-5 mm)

| Verdict | Pairs | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| exact | 26 | every vertex within tolerance |
| tail | 11 | at least 95% within, a few vertices beyond |
| partial | 13 | median vertex within, more than 5% beyond |
| mismatch | 3 | median vertex beyond tolerance |

- Pairs with at least 95% of vertices in tolerance went from 30 to 37.
- Pairs whose median vertex is in tolerance went from about 32 to 50.
- The strict stage-1 reference check, which fails on the single worst vertex, passes 22 (was 21). That is the 26 exact pairs minus four meshes stage 1 rejects as non-manifold.
- The test suite passes (378 passed, 32 ignored) and clippy is clean.

## Why the rest aren't exact

- **Tail (11): mostly a measurement artifact.** The stray vertices sit on face boundaries, and the check measures against the reference's trimmed faces. I added `gen-test-models strays` to re-measure them against the untrimmed surfaces.
  - On the SolidWorks parts I checked (`ToolChanger__docking_station`, `ToolChanger__blower_fan_duct`), every stray lies on two surfaces to about 1e-6 mm.
  - On the Fusion chain anchor and the NucDeck trigger button, some strays are real: on one surface and up to 3e-3 mm off its neighbour.
- **Different revisions (5):** the two Open-Task-Light belt clips, and NucDeck's joystick ring, right side grip and back cover. Volumes differ by up to 27% or features are 0.2–0.85 mm off.
- **White-Knight (9): not good examples.** None is exact. Their STLs were moved or re-saved after export: fitted rotations come out at 89.9995° and 120.0461°, and one file has 86% of its coordinates rounded to 0.001 mm. I'd drop this repo as ground truth.
- **Two unexplained:** `NucDeck__left_side_grip` and `ToolChanger__dock_brace_(m)` are exact at the median with 6–16% of vertices up to about 2e-3 mm off.

Your examples are better than they looked: Open-Task-Light, OpenBot, most of VoronUsers and ToolChanger, and the NucDeck buttons are solid ground truth.

The aligner rewrote the gitignored `_aligned.step` files in `tests/external/` (old ones backed up in `tmp/eval/aligned_backup/`) and re-pointed `sources.tsv`. Nothing is committed.

The stage-1 check still fails the 11 tail pairs on their worst vertex. Judging boundary vertices against untrimmed surfaces would let the genuinely exact ones pass.

Files are in `tests/external`:
- README.md
- alignment.tsv

```
// Compare mesh against STEP surfaces
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct CompareError {
    pub vertex_max_distance: f64,
    pub vertex_max_index: usize,
    pub vertex_tolerance: f64,
    pub centroid_max_distance: f64,
    pub centroid_max_face_index: usize,
    pub centroid_tolerance: f64,
}

impl Display for CompareError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        let mut parts = Vec::new();
        if self.vertex_max_distance > self.vertex_tolerance {
            parts.push(format!(
                "vertex {} is {:.6e} mm from nearest STEP surface (tolerance: {:.6e} mm)",
                self.vertex_max_index, self.vertex_max_distance, self.vertex_tolerance
            ));
        }
        if self.centroid_max_distance > self.centroid_tolerance {
            parts.push(format!(
                "face {} centroid is {:.6e} mm from nearest STEP surface (tolerance: {:.6e} mm)",
                self.centroid_max_face_index, self.centroid_max_distance, self.centroid_tolerance
            ));
        }
        write!(f, "comparison failed: {}", parts.join("; "))
    }
}

impl Error for CompareError {}
            max_i = i;
        }
    }
    (max_d, max_i)
}

/// Check mesh vertices and face centroids against comparison STEP shape.
fn compare_mesh_to_step(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, config: &Config) -> Result<(), CompareError> {
    // Measure against the reference's FACES. Against the solid, every interior
    // point reads as distance zero — see the \`compare\` module docs.
    let faces = crate::compare::face_compound(config.compare_shape.as_ref().unwrap());
    let compare_shape = faces.as_shape();

    // Check all vertices. The distribution is kept, not just the max: a single
    // vertex off the surface is a repaired or decimated mesh, while a whole
    // population sitting at the same small offset is the exporter's own
    // fidelity. The two want different responses and the max alone cannot tell
    // them apart — measured on wild pairs in Phase 0.5b, where three SolidWorks
    // exports read 4e-4 mm at the max and 1e-5 at the median.
    let vertex_points: Vec<[f64; 3]> = mesh.vertices.iter().map(|v| [v.x, v.y, v.z]).collect();
    let vtx_dists = distances_to_shape(&vertex_points, compare_shape);
    let (mut vtx_max_dist, mut vtx_max_idx) = (0.0_f64, 0_usize);
    for (i, &d) in vtx_dists.iter().enumerate() {
        if d > vtx_max_dist {
            vtx_max_dist = d;
            vtx_max_idx = i;
        }
    }
    let vtx_quantiles = {
        let mut sorted = vtx_dists.clone();
        sorted.sort_by(f64::total_cmp);
        let at = |q: f64| sorted[(((sorted.len().max(1) - 1) as f64) * q).round() as usize];
        (at(0.50), at(0.95))
    };

    // Check all face centroids
    let centroid_points: Vec<[f64; 3]> = mesh
        .faces
        .iter()
        .map(|face| {
            let n = face.vertex_count as usize;
            let mut c = [0.0_f64; 3];
            for vi in 0..n {
                let v = &mesh.vertices[face.vertex_indices[vi]];
                c[0] += v.x;
                c[1] += v.y;
                c[2] += v.z;
            }
            let inv_n = 1.0 / n as f64;
            [c[0] * inv_n, c[1] * inv_n, c[2] * inv_n]
        })
        .collect();
    let (ctr_max_dist, ctr_max_face) = max_distance_to_shape(&centroid_points, compare_shape);

    if !config.quiet {
        eprintln!(
            "  Compare: vertex dist p50 {:.6e} / p95 {:.6e} / max {:.6e} mm, \
             centroid max dist {:.6e} mm",
            vtx_quantiles.0, vtx_quantiles.1, vtx_max_dist, ctr_max_dist
        );
    }

    let vtx_fail = vtx_max_dist > config.vertex_tolerance_mm;
    let ctr_fail = ctr_max_dist > config.surface_tolerance_mm;

    if vtx_fail || ctr_fail {
        return Err(CompareError {
            vertex_max_distance: vtx_max_dist,
            vertex_max_index: vtx_max_idx,
            vertex_tolerance: config.vertex_tolerance_mm,
            centroid_max_distance: ctr_max_dist,
            centroid_max_face_index: ctr_max_face,
            centroid_tolerance: config.surface_tolerance_mm,
        });
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

```bash
new='''    /// For a point that misses the reference's trimmed faces: where its closest
    /// point landed, and how far it is from the *untrimmed* surface of every
    /// face meeting there.
    ///
    /// A B-rep face is a surface cut down by its edges, and a point-to-face
    /// distance therefore measures two different things at once: how far the
    /// point is off the surface, and how far it is outside the trim. A mesh
    /// vertex on a face boundary can be exactly on both surfaces that meet
    /// there and still read 1e-4 mm, because the reference's edge — an explicit
    /// curve that a STEP file stores as an approximation of the true
    /// intersection — passes that far to one side of it. This separates the
    /// two. See [`BoundaryMiss::on_intersection`].
    ///
    /// Not thread-safe (it reads the geometry handles); call it for the few
    /// points that need it, not for every vertex.
    pub fn boundary_miss(&self, pt: [f64; 3]) -> Option<BoundaryMiss> {
        let p = gp::Pnt::new_real3(pt[0], pt[1], pt[2]);
        let mut vertex = b_rep_builder_api::MakeVertex::new_pnt(&p);
        let vtx_shape = vertex.vertex();
        let progress = message::ProgressRange::new();
        let dist = b_rep_extrema::DistShapeShape::new_shape2_extflag_extalgo_progressrange(
            vtx_shape.as_shape(),
            self.shape(),
            0, // F (unused/obsolete)
            extrema::ExtAlgo::Grad,
            &progress,
        );
        if !dist.is_done() || dist.nb_solution() < 1 {
            return None;
        }
        let support = dist.support_on_shape2(1);
        let (on_boundary, support_tolerance, sub_kind) = match dist.support_type_shape2(1) {
            b_rep_extrema::SupportType::Isinface => (false, 0.0, top_abs::ShapeEnum::Face),
            b_rep_extrema::SupportType::Isonedge => (
                true,
                b_rep::Tool::tolerance_edge(topo_ds::edge(&support)),
                top_abs::ShapeEnum::Edge,
            ),
            b_rep_extrema::SupportType::Isvertex => (
                true,
                b_rep::Tool::tolerance_vertex(topo_ds::vertex(&support)),
                top_abs::ShapeEnum::Vertex,
            ),
        };

        // Every face the support belongs to, in the same explorer order as
        // `self.geometry`.
        let mut surface_distances = Vec::new();
        let mut faces = top_exp::Explorer::new_shape_shapeenum2(
            self.shape(),
            top_abs::ShapeEnum::Face,
            top_abs::ShapeEnum::Shape,
        );
        let mut fi = 0usize;
        while faces.more() {
            let meets = if on_boundary {
                let mut subs = top_exp::Explorer::new_shape_shapeenum2(
                    faces.value(),
                    sub_kind,
                    top_abs::ShapeEnum::Shape,
                );
                let mut found = false;
                while subs.more() {
                    if subs.value().is_same(&support) {
                        found = true;
                        break;
                    }
                    subs.next();
                }
                found
            } else {
                faces.value().is_same(&support)
            };
            if meets {
                let proj = geom_api::ProjectPointOnSurf::new_pnt_handlegeomsurface_extalgo(
                    &p,
                    &self.geometry[fi],
                    extrema::ExtAlgo::Grad,
                );
                if proj.is_done() && proj.nb_points() > 0 {
                    surface_distances.push(proj.lower_distance());
                }
            }
            fi += 1;
            faces.next();
        }
        surface_distances.sort_by(f64::total_cmp);
        Some(BoundaryMiss {
            trimmed_distance: dist.value(),
            on_boundary,
            support_tolerance,
            surface_distances,
        })
    }

new='''/// What [`ReferenceModel::boundary_miss`] found for one point.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct BoundaryMiss {
    /// Distance to the reference's trimmed faces — the ordinary measurement.
    pub trimmed_distance: f64,
    /// The closest point is on an edge or vertex of the reference rather than
    /// in the interior of a face.
    pub on_boundary: bool,
    /// OCCT's own tolerance on that edge or vertex: how far the reader found
    /// the edge's curve to stray from the surfaces it bounds. Zero for a face.
    pub support_tolerance: f64,
    /// Distance to the untrimmed surface of each face meeting at the closest
    /// point, ascending. One entry for a face interior.
    pub surface_distances: Vec<f64>,
}

impl BoundaryMiss {
    /// The point lies, within `tolerance`, on at least two of the surfaces that
    /// meet where it landed — that is, on their intersection, which is where a
    /// tessellator puts a boundary vertex. Such a point is exact in the sense
    /// brepper relies on (it validates vertices against unbounded fitted
    /// surfaces); what it misses is only the reference's trim.
    pub fn on_intersection(&self, tolerance: f64) -> bool {
        self.on_boundary
            && self.surface_distances.len() >= 2
            && self.surface_distances[1] <= tolerance
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Labeling
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
'''
```

```bash
// boundary rule (`compare_mesh_to_step`), kept runnable so the rule can be
// re-checked on a new corpus.
fn diagnose_strays(stl_path: &str, step_path: &str) {
    let mesh = brepper::stage1::read_connected_mesh_from_stl(
        stl_path,
        brepper::stage1::VertexWeldOptions::default(),
```

<details>
<summary>Bash: Require two genuinely distinct surfaces for the excuse, rebuild, and retest</summary>

```bash
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='src/reference.rs'
s=open(p).read()
a=s.index('impl BoundaryMiss {')
b=s.index('// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Labeling')
new='''impl BoundaryMiss {
    /// The folded angle (0 to 90 degrees, in radians) between the best-conditioned
    /// pair of adjacent surfaces that the point lies on within `tolerance`.
    ///
    /// `None` unless there are two such surfaces whose normals genuinely differ.
    /// That last condition is structural, not a threshold: CAD kernels routinely
    /// split one surface into several faces (a cylinder into two halves), and
    /// two faces of the SAME surface do not make an intersection — a point on
    /// that surface lies on "both" wherever it is. The floor separates
    /// identical normals from different ones at the precision the normals are
    /// evaluated to, and is taken on the cross product because `acos` near 1
    /// turns a 1e-16 rounding error into a 1e-8 angle.
    fn intersection_angle(&self, tolerance: f64) -> Option<f64> {
        if !self.on_boundary {
            return None;
        }
        let on: Vec<[f64; 3]> = self
            .surface_distances
            .iter()
            .zip(&self.surface_normals)
            .filter(|(d, _)| **d <= tolerance)
            .filter_map(|(_, n)| *n)
            .collect();
        let mut best: Option<f64> = None;
        for i in 0..on.len() {
            for j in i + 1..on.len() {
                let s = norm(cross(on[i], on[j]));
                if s > 1.0e-9 {
                    let angle = s.atan2(dot(on[i], on[j]).abs());
                    best = Some(best.map_or(angle, |b: f64| b.max(angle)));
                }
            }
        }
        best
    }

    /// The point lies, within `tolerance`, on two distinct surfaces that meet
    /// where it landed — that is, on their intersection, which is where a
    /// tessellator puts a boundary vertex. Such a point is exact in the sense
    /// brepper relies on (it validates vertices against unbounded fitted
    /// surfaces); what it misses is only the reference's trim.
    pub fn on_intersection(&self, tolerance: f64) -> bool {
        self.intersection_angle(tolerance).is_some()
    }

    /// How far outside the trim a point on the intersection can legitimately
    /// sit, or `None` if it is not on one.
    ///
    /// Being on the intersection is not enough to excuse a point, because an
    /// intersection curve runs on past the end of its edge: lengthen a box by
    /// 1 mm and its four moved corners are still exactly on two of the old
    /// box's planes. So the miss also has to be no larger than the reference's
    /// own edge can explain.
    ///
    /// Locally the two surfaces are planes whose normals meet at an angle
    /// `theta`. The set of points within `e` of both is a rhombus about the
    /// intersection line reaching `e / sin(theta/2)` one way and
    /// `e / cos(theta/2)` the other. The reference's edge curve is within its
    /// `support_tolerance` of both surfaces and the vertex within `tolerance`
    /// of both, so the two can be at most
    ///
    /// `(support_tolerance + tolerance) / min(sin(theta/2), cos(theta/2))`
    ///
    /// apart. Every quantity is read from the reference or is the vertex
    /// tolerance already in force; nothing here is tuned. The amplification is
    /// real and matters: at a shallow junction a curve can hug both surfaces
    /// and still wander sideways, which is why a fixed multiple of the edge
    /// tolerance does not work (measured on `ToolChanger__dock_brace`: a vertex
    /// on both surfaces to 4e-7 mm sits 8.5e-4 mm from an edge of tolerance
    /// 3.7e-4). At a tangent junction the bound is correspondingly loose, and
    /// what limits the miss there is the requirement that the vertex be within
    /// `tolerance` of BOTH surfaces, which only holds close to the tangency.
    pub fn trim_allowance(&self, tolerance: f64) -> Option<f64> {
        // The angle is already folded into [0, 90] degrees, where the smaller
        // of sin and cos of the half-angle is the sine.
        let half = 0.5 * self.intersection_angle(tolerance)?;
        Some((self.support_tolerance + tolerance) / half.sin())
    }

    /// The point misses the trimmed reference only because of where the
    /// reference's edge runs: it is on the intersection of two adjacent
    /// surfaces and within [`Self::trim_allowance`] of the edge.
    pub fn excused(&self, tolerance: f64) -> bool {
        self.trim_allowance(tolerance).is_some_and(|a| self.trimmed_distance <= a)
    }
}

'''
s=s[:a]+new+s[b:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
```

```
#### 1.2 Mesh Validation
Traverse the faces of the mesh, collecting statistics, validating the geometry, and populating normals and neighbors.
- Collect stats into \`MeshValidationStats\` and optionally print: \`mesh_faces\`, \`mesh_vertices\`, \`mesh_edges_open\` (edges with only 1 incident face), \`mesh_edges_non_manifold\` (edges with >2 incident faces), \`mesh_edges_inconsistent_orientation\`, \`mesh_faces_degenerate\`, \`connected_shells\`, \`solids\`, \`voids_within_solids\`.
- Compute and populate mesh face normals using Newell's method (handles both triangles and quads with consistent winding).
- Compute mesh face neighbors based on shared mesh edges. For each edge (vertex pair), collect all face uses. For manifold edges (exactly 2 uses), set both faces as neighbors. Also check orientation consistency: properly oriented adjacent faces should traverse the shared edge in opposite directions.
- Count connected shells via BFS over a face adjacency graph. A shell is counted as a "solid" if all its edges are manifold (exactly 2 faces per edge).
- **Repair pass** (bypassed by \`--strict-mesh\`): drop duplicate-vertex and
  coincident faces, stitch T-junction slivers (splitting the long-edge
  neighbor at the interior vertex), unify winding per shell, and reorient
  inverted closed shells — everything fixable without moving a vertex.
- With the \`--compare\` flag: check that all vertices are within \`--vertex-tolerance\` of the STEP shape, and that all face centroids are within \`--surface-tolerance\`. Uses \`BRepExtrema_DistShapeShape\` for bounded distance (respects face trimming). Reports the worst vertex and worst centroid with their distances.

Validation checks, in priority order (first failure is reported):
1. **Degenerate faces**: faces with <3 vertices or zero-area normals.
2. **Non-manifold edges**: edges shared by >2 faces.
3. **Inconsistent orientation**: adjacent faces that traverse a shared edge in the same direction (indicating flipped normals within a shell).
4. **Inverted normals**: for each closed shell, compute the signed volume via the divergence theorem (sum of signed tetrahedra formed by each face and the origin: V = (1/6) Σ v0·(v1×v2)). A negative signed volume is legitimate for an internal void shell (normals point out of the material, i.e. into the cavity): such shells are accepted — and counted in \`voids_within_solids\` — when their bounding box is contained in some closed positive shell's box. Otherwise a negative volume means all face normals point inward (consistently inverted winding); this catches meshes where orientation is internally consistent (check 3 passes) but globally inverted.
5. **Self-intersections**: intentionally deferred to a later stage where richer geometric predicates are available and O(N²) triangle checks can be avoided.

    <input.stl>              Input STL file (binary or ASCII)

GENERAL OPTIONS:
    -o <step>, --output=<step>  Output STEP file
    --stl-units=<units>      Units used by the STL file (mm, cm, m, in, ft, um; default: mm)
    --step-units=<units>     Units to use in exported STEP file (default: mm)
    --compare=<step>         STEP file to compare to at each step
    --reference-report       Score the mesh and our segmentation against the --compare
                             reference: facet-normal exactness per surface type, closed-form
                             initializer error, the seam assumption, and over/under-segmentation.
                             Diagnostics only. Requires --compare.
```

## 🤖 Assistant
<!-- msg_011CgxEsnqWEnRij7kRrnNae -->

The gate fix was finished when the limit hit; only the write-up was outstanding. The stage-1 reference check now passes 26 of the 53 real-world pairs (was 22), and the four that changed are exactly the SolidWorks parts whose "stray" vertices were a measurement artifact.

## The rule

A vertex beyond `--vertex-tolerance` of the reference's trimmed faces is no longer counted against the pair when all three hold:

- **On a boundary:** its closest reference point is on an edge or vertex, not inside a face.
- **On both surfaces:** it is within tolerance of the untrimmed surfaces of at least two faces meeting there.
- **Within the edge's own accuracy:** its miss is no more than that edge's OCCT tolerance plus the vertex tolerance.

No new tuned constant is involved. When vertices are excused, stage 1.2 prints a second `Compare:` line saying how many and how far.

## Results

- **Now pass:** `ToolChanger__docking_station`, `…docking_station_(m)`, `…blower_fan_duct`, `…blower_fan_duct_(m)`. Every over-tolerance vertex (12 to 60 per part, up to 4.3e-4 mm) is excused.
- **Still fail, correctly:** the belt clips, which are a different revision 0.2 mm wider than their reference, have 0 vertices excused.
- **Still fail on genuinely stray vertices (7 pairs):** `ToolChanger__dock_brace`, the two NucDeck trigger buttons and the four Fusion chain anchors. About 1% of their vertices are on one surface and up to 4e-3 mm off its neighbour, or off in face interiors.
- **Totals in `alignment.tsv`:** 26 exact, 4 trim-only, 7 tail, 13 partial, 3 mismatch. The gate passes the 26 exact plus 4 trim-only, less four exact meshes that stage 1 rejects as non-manifold.
- **Checks:** 118 unit tests and 378 integration tests pass (32 ignored, as before); clippy is clean. Three of the unit tests are new and cover the excuse rule.

## One thing I tried and dropped

A looser third condition, scaling the allowance by the angle between the two surfaces, would excuse a few more real vertices at shallow junctions. It also excused two corners of the different-revision belt clip, because that file has one plane split into two faces whose normals differ by rounding. I kept the strict version and left a do-not-re-derive note on `BoundaryMiss::trim_allowance`.

## For the converter

The seven tail pairs matter beyond the test corpus: real Fusion and SolidWorks exports carry about 1% of vertices that are off a surface by around 1e-3 mm. The pipeline's rule that every claimed vertex must validate at 5e-5 mm has to tolerate that, which is step 4 of the path I proposed earlier.

Nothing is committed. The changes are in `src/stage1.rs`, `src/reference.rs`, `src/bin/gen_test_models.rs` (which also gains a `strays` diagnostic), the README, the development plan, the TODO, and `tests/external/` (README.md, alignment.tsv, sources.tsv).

```bash
while pgrep -f 'eval_dump.sh' >/dev/null; do sleep 10; done; ls tmp/eval/dump | wc -l; cat > tmp/stray_stats.py <<'EOF'
# Per-model summary of tmp/eval/dump/<stem>.tsv: how many vertices exceed the
# tolerance, by how much, and whether they are localized on the part.
import sys, glob, os, math
TOL=5e-5
def q(v,p): return v[min(len(v)-1,int(round((len(v)-1)*p)))]
print("stem\tverts\tover\tpct\tp50_over\tp95_over\tmax\tbbox_frac\tplateau")
for f in sorted(glob.glob('tmp/eval/dump/*.tsv')):
    pts=[]
    for l in open(f).read().split('\n')[1:]:
        if l: pts.append(tuple(map(float,l.split('\t'))))
    n=len(pts)
    lo=[min(p[k] for p in pts) for k in range(3)]; hi=[max(p[k] for p in pts) for k in range(3)]
    over=[p for p in pts if p[3]>TOL]
    if not over:
        print(os.path.basename(f)[:-4],n,0,sep='\t'); continue
    d=sorted(p[3] for p in over)
    # share of the part's bounding box (per axis, product) that the strays span
    frac=1.0
    for k in range(3):
        ext=hi[k]-lo[k]
        if ext>1e-9:
            frac*= (max(p[k] for p in over)-min(p[k] for p in over))/ext
    # plateau: share of strays within 5% of the most common magnitude (a discrete offset)
    top=d[-1]
    plateau=sum(1 for x in d if x>0.9*top)/len(d)
    print(os.path.basename(f)[:-4],n,len(over),"%.1f"%(100*len(over)/n),"%.1e"%q(d,0.5),"%.1e"%q(d,0.95),"%.1e"%top,"%.2f"%frac,"%.2f"%plateau,sep='\t')
EOF
python3 tmp/stray_stats.py | column -t -s$'\t' | cut -c1-170
```

Your suspicion holds for 7 of the 23 remaining pairs: the STEP and STL are different geometry. Another 6 are STLs that were modified after export, and 10 are genuine pairs with small deviations.

Tolerance is 5e-5 mm. "Over" counts vertices beyond it; "typical" is the median distance among those vertices.

## STEP and STL are different geometry (7)

The signature is vertices more than 0.01 mm off, confined to one feature, while the rest of the part is exact.

| Model | CAD | Over | Typical | Max | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Open-Task-Light__belt_clip` | Fusion 360 | 530 of 1394 (38%) | 0.20 mm | 0.20 mm | every stray exactly 0.200 mm off; volume +11% |
| `Open-Task-Light__carriage_belt_clip` | Fusion 360 | 530 of 1394 (38%) | 0.20 mm | 0.20 mm | same as above |
| `NucDeck__joystick_surround_ring` | SolidWorks 2021 | 145 of 1774 (8%) | 1.0 mm | 3.3 mm | volume +27%; STL committed six weeks after the STEP |
| `NucDeck__right_side_grip` | SolidWorks 2021 | 1336 of 7844 (17%) | 1.1e-4 mm | 0.85 mm | 72 vertices 0.44–0.85 mm off in one 35 × 11 mm patch |
| `White-Knight__1-direct_drive_extruder_mount_v9` | Fusion 360 STEP | 6251 of 7608 (82%) | 5.4e-4 mm | 0.24 mm | 615 vertices 0.01–0.24 mm off in a 10 × 13 × 13 mm region |
| `NucDeck__back_cover_7th_gen_intel_nuc` | SolidWorks 2021 | 1289 of 10333 (12%) | 1.2e-4 mm | 0.35 mm | 6 vertices up to 0.35 mm off in one 1 mm spot |
| `White-Knight__1-5i_case_front_knight_v14` | Fusion 360 STEP | 2857 of 13657 (21%) | 1.3e-4 mm | 0.10 mm | 30 vertices up to 0.10 mm off in one spot |

Only the joystick ring has upstream history showing which file is newer. For the others the two files landed in the same commits, so I can't say whether the STEP or the STL was the one edited.

## STL re-oriented after export (6, all White-Knight)

Upstream commit "Updated STL file orientation" rewrote these STLs two days after the STEPs were committed. Deviations are spread over the whole part rather than one feature. The STEPs are Fusion 360; the STLs carry no exporter signature.

| `…1-right_rear_idler_part_2_…_v3` | 1813 of 9888 (18%) | 1.0e-4 mm | 5.5e-3 mm |

The hotend carriage also has 86% of its coordinates rounded to 0.001 mm. The two White-Knight parts in the first table were in the same commit, so they have this spread as well as the local difference.

```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Harvest wild STEP+STL pairs from open-source hardware repos (Phase 0.5b).

The point of 0.5b is pairs WE DID NOT EXPORT. Our own corpora verify at 31/31
by construction, so they cannot measure whether the provenance premise — mesh
vertices lie on the true CAD surface — survives contact with the wild. A pair
published by a third party can fail for reasons we never see in-house: the STL
was decimated for printing, the mesh was repaired, or the CAD was updated and
the mesh never re-exported. Measuring how often that happens is the deliverable.

GitHub is used rather than a model-sharing site because open-source hardware
repos commit STEP and STL side by side, from one author and one revision, under
a licence that is explicit and machine-readable. \`gh\` supplies auth.

Discovery walks each repo's git tree in ONE API call rather than crawling
directories, then pairs by stem. Pairing rule is recorded per pair so a
surprising verification result can be audited:
  same-dir   both files in one directory (jig.step + jig.stl)
  sibling    stem matches across sibling directories (STEP/lock.step +
             STL/lock.stl), which is the other common layout
A stem that matches more than once in a repo is skipped rather than guessed.

Writes to tests/external/ (gitignored) plus a committed manifest recording URL,
repo, author, licence, path, size and sha256 for every file taken.
"""

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import math
import os
import re
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import urllib.parse
from collections import defaultdict

REPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
OUT_DIR = os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "tests", "external")
MANIFEST = os.path.join(OUT_DIR, "manifest.tsv")

# Unrelated projects, so no single CAD workflow dominates the sample. Found via
# \`gh search code --extension=step\` across several unrelated query terms.
CANDIDATE_REPOS = [
    "bit-bots/bitbots_3d_print",         # humanoid robotics (university team)
    "VoronDesign/VoronUsers",            # 3D printer mods, hundreds of authors
    "e3donline/ToolChanger",             # printer toolchanger (E3D, commercial)
    "ob-f/OpenBot",                      # robotics (Intel research)
    "NAK3DDesigns/White-Knight",         # printer design
    "OpenAstroTech/OpenAstroTracker",    # astronomy mount
    "Rat-Rig/V-core-3",                  # printer (commercial)
    "NikodemBartnik/IndyMill",           # CNC mill
    "dmcke5/NucDeck",                    # handheld console enclosure
    "stevenbennett/Open-Task-Light",     # lighting
]

# Licences whose terms permit redistributing the files, so a pair could be
# committed rather than only analysed locally. Anything else is fetched for
# local analysis only and flagged in the manifest.
REDISTRIBUTABLE = {
    "MIT", "Apache-2.0", "BSD-2-Clause", "BSD-3-Clause", "Unlicense", "CC0-1.0",
    "GPL-2.0", "GPL-3.0", "LGPL-2.1", "LGPL-3.0", "AGPL-3.0", "MPL-2.0",
    "CC-BY-4.0", "CC-BY-SA-4.0", "CERN-OHL-S-2.0", "CERN-OHL-W-2.0",
}

MAX_FILE_BYTES = 20 * 1024 * 1024


def gh_api(path, jq=None):
    cmd = ["gh", "api", path]
    if jq:
        cmd += ["--jq", jq]
    out = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if out.returncode != 0:
        return None
    return out.stdout


def repo_info(repo):
    raw = gh_api(f"repos/{repo}")
    if raw is None:
        return None
    d = json.loads(raw)
    return {
        "repo": repo,
        "owner": d["owner"]["login"],
        "license": (d.get("license") or {}).get("spdx_id") or "NONE",
        "branch": d["default_branch"],
        "stars": d["stargazers_count"],
    }


def find_pairs(repo, branch):
    """Every (step, stl) pair in the repo, by stem, with the rule that matched."""
    raw = gh_api(f"repos/{repo}/git/trees/{branch}?recursive=1")
    if raw is None:
        return []
    tree = json.loads(raw).get("tree", [])
    steps, stls = defaultdict(list), defaultdict(list)
    for node in tree:
        if node.get("type") != "blob":
            continue
        path = node["path"]
        stem, _, ext = path.rpartition("/")[2].rpartition(".")
        ext = ext.lower()
        key = stem.lower()
        if ext in ("step", "stp"):
            steps[key].append(node)
        elif ext == "stl":
            stls[key].append(node)

    pairs = []
    for stem in sorted(set(steps) & set(stls)):
        # Ambiguous stems are skipped, not guessed: two different parts both
        # called "base" would otherwise be paired across mods.
        if len(steps[stem]) != 1 or len(stls[stem]) != 1:
            continue
        step, stl = steps[stem][0], stls[stem][0]
        sdir, mdir = step["path"].rpartition("/")[0], stl["path"].rpartition("/")[0]
```
