    fn test_config() -> config::Config {
        config::parse_config_from(["brepper", "dummy.stl", "-q"]).unwrap()
    }

    /// A strip of 4 quads along x (z=0), 8 triangles, with the two vertices at
    /// x=3 raised `lift` in z: as if the edge between quads 2 and 3 were on an
    /// approximated edge curve, off the plane.
    fn lifted_strip(lift: f64) -> ConnectedMesh {
        let mut verts = Vec::new();
        for x in 0..=4 {
            let z = if x == 3 { lift } else { 0.0 };
            verts.push(MeshVertex::from_xyz(x as f64, 0.0, z));
            verts.push(MeshVertex::from_xyz(x as f64, 1.0, z));
        }
        let mut faces = Vec::new();
        for q in 0..4 {
            let (a, b, c, d) = (2 * q, 2 * q + 1, 2 * q + 2, 2 * q + 3);
            faces.push(tri(a, c, d));
            faces.push(tri(a, d, b));
        }
        let mut mesh = ConnectedMesh { vertices: verts, faces, stats: Default::default() };
        mesh.validate_and_populate_topology().expect("valid mesh");
        mesh
    }

    /// T = quads 0-1, S = quad 2, U = quad 3, all fitted as z=0.
    fn lifted_cls(n_faces: usize) -> Classification {
        Classification {
            planar: vec![
                planar(vec![0, 1, 2, 3], vec![0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]),
                planar(vec![4, 5], vec![4, 5, 6, 7]),
                planar(vec![6, 7], vec![6, 7, 8, 9]),
            ],
            conical: Vec::new(),
            spherical: Vec::new(),
            toroidal: Vec::new(),
            bspline: Vec::new(),
            selected: vec![
                SelectedSurface::Planar(0),
                SelectedSurface::Planar(1),
                SelectedSurface::Planar(2),
            ],
            joined: vec![false; n_faces],
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn boundary_merge_joins_a_sliver_whose_off_vertices_stay_on_an_edge() {
        // S's lifted vertices (5e-4 off T, within the 1e-3 boundary bound) are
        // shared with U, so they stay on an edge of S+T: S merges into T, and
        // its facets are marked joined. U's would then be inside T+U — every
        // facet around them on T or U — so U is refused.
        let mesh = lifted_strip(5e-4);
        let mut cls = lifted_cls(mesh.faces.len());
        let centroids: Vec<[f64; 3]> =
            mesh.faces.iter().map(|f| face_centroid(f, &mesh.vertices)).collect();
        let merged = merge_regions(&mesh, &mut cls, &centroids, &test_config());
        assert_eq!(merged, 1);
        assert_eq!(cls.planar[0].faces.len(), 6, "S joined T");
        assert!(cls.planar[1].faces.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(cls.planar[2].faces, vec![6, 7], "U kept: its lifted vertices would be inside");
        assert!(cls.is_joined(4) && cls.is_joined(5));
        assert!(!cls.is_joined(6) && !cls.is_joined(7));
        // T's fit came from its strict facets only: still z=0.
        assert!(cls.planar[0].distance.abs() < 1e-12);
    }

    #[test]
    fn boundary_merge_is_off_at_the_vertex_tolerance_and_past_the_bound() {
        let off = config::parse_config_from([
            "brepper", "dummy.stl", "-q", "--boundary-tolerance=5e-5",
        ])
        .unwrap();
        let mesh = lifted_strip(5e-4);
        let mut cls = lifted_cls(mesh.faces.len());
        let centroids: Vec<[f64; 3]> =
            mesh.faces.iter().map(|f| face_centroid(f, &mesh.vertices)).collect();
        assert_eq!(merge_regions(&mesh, &mut cls, &centroids, &off), 0);

        // 2e-3 off is past the default 1e-3 bound.
        let mesh = lifted_strip(2e-3);
        let mut cls = lifted_cls(mesh.faces.len());
        let centroids: Vec<[f64; 3]> =
            mesh.faces.iter().map(|f| face_centroid(f, &mesh.vertices)).collect();
        assert_eq!(merge_regions(&mesh, &mut cls, &centroids, &test_config()), 0);
    }

## 🤖 Assistant
<!-- msg_011ChHmz8v6VjZHeTrmUJZvh -->

The boundary join is built, and four of the six tolerant-edge parts now come out good. The full corpus run and the test suite are still going.

- **Fixed:** the three VoronUsers strip mounts (invalid before) and `drag_chain_link` (failed before) are now good. The mini strip mount went from 60 faces to 22 (its reference has 13).
- **Not fixed:** `drag_chain_termination_(base)` went from timeout to a stage-3.1 adjacency failure. `led_cover_drag_chain_termination` still fails on a different face, and `penultimate_link` still times out.

How it works:
- **Discovery is unchanged:** surfaces are still found at `--vertex-tolerance`.
- **Join:** a leftover facet next to a surface already found joins it if its vertices are within `--boundary-tolerance`. The default is 1e-3 mm, twice the worst miss measured.
- **Small surfaces:** stage 2.4's existing small-surface merge (at most 16 facets) now also takes a small surface whose facets are within the bound of a larger neighbour. It was needed because competition commits 3–8 facet cones along these edges before the join can claim them.
- **Edge rule:** a vertex more than the vertex tolerance off its surface must stay on an edge of that surface. Joined facets are never used to refit a surface.
- **Self-check:** it allows the looser bound only at vertices where two output faces meet.

Clippy is clean, and nothing is committed.

Two side findings:
- **The Mac is asleep:** it wakes for about 45 s every 15 minutes, which is why every long run took many times longer than normal.
- **Scoreboard runtimes:** they were wall-clock, so a 4.5 s run could show 895 s. I switched them to the same clock as the timeout, which stops during sleep.

I'll report the full scoreboard diff and the test results when they finish.

<!-- msg_011ChJCpdUwqjRsJmsHPPMFd -->

Amphetamine was working; a reboot won't help. The Mac slept because the lid was closed, and Amphetamine's keep-awake doesn't apply when the lid closes.

**What the power log shows:**
- Amphetamine's "Single-Use - System" hold was in force the whole night; it has now been running for 19 hours.
- The log records "Clamshell Sleep", which means lid closed, at 18:21 and 21:09 yesterday and again at 03:15.
- From then until morning the Mac woke for about 45 seconds every 15 minutes, which is why the runs crawled.
- The wake at 07:24 says "due to lid", which is you opening it.

**Why Amphetamine didn't stop it:** what it holds only prevents idle sleep, and macOS still sleeps on lid close. Your Amphetamine settings ask it to prevent closed-display sleep ("Allow Closed-Display Sleep" is 0). On a MacBook with no external display, that needs the separate free helper app, Amphetamine Enhancer, with its Closed-Display Mode option installed. Enhancer isn't in /Applications, and the system's `SleepDisabled` flag is 0.

**Your options:**
- Leave the lid open; the display can still turn off.
- Install Amphetamine Enhancer and turn on Closed-Display Mode.
- Connect an external display and power, which is what macOS needs to keep running with the lid shut.

**Where the boundary-tolerance work stands:**
- **Full scoreboard:** wild good went from 11 to 15 (the three strip mounts and `drag_chain_link`), invalid from 5 to 2, and fail from 5 to 3. Synthetic statuses are unchanged.
- **Tests:** all pass, 121 unit and 378 integration.

- **Docs and baseline:** TODO, README, DEVELOPMENT_PLAN and the scoreboard baseline are updated.
- **Nothing is committed.**

    // A vertex more than vertex tolerance off the surface must stay on that
    // surface's edge: that is the case the bound exists for (a vertex on an
    // approximated edge curve), and the only one the self-check allows. A
    // joined facet that would leave such a vertex inside the surface — every
    // facet around it on the same surface — goes back to the leftovers. Taking
    // a facet out only ever puts vertices on the edge, so one pass settles it.
    let vtol = config.vertex_tolerance_mm;
    for hi in 0..hyps.len() {
        let mut kept: Vec<usize> = Vec::with_capacity(added[hi].len());
        for &fi in &added[hi] {
            let f = &mesh.faces[fi];
            let inside = f.vertex_indices[..f.vertex_count as usize].iter().any(|&vi| {
                let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
                fits[hi].distance(&[v.x, v.y, v.z]) > vtol
                    && super::vertex_fan(mesh, fi, vi).iter().all(|&g| owner[g] == hi)
            });
            if inside {
                open[fi] = true;
                owner[fi] = usize::MAX;
            } else {
                kept.push(fi);
            }
        }
        added[hi] = kept;
    }
```

**After:**
```
    // A vertex more than vertex tolerance off the surface must be on a real
    // edge of it — the case the bound exists for, a vertex on an approximated
    // edge curve between two CAD faces. It is on one when a facet around it is
    // across a sharp edge (outside this region: neither a surface's nor a
    // leftover here) or belongs to another surface of at least two facets (one
    // facet is no evidence of a face: every triangle is exactly a plane). A
    // leftover facet does not count. Bordering only leftovers is what a
    // near-tangent blend looks like: measured on `ToolChanger__blower_fan_duct`,
    // counting leftovers let 244 blend facets join analytic surfaces, the
    // freeform patch they belonged to stopped fitting, and per-facet planes
    // went from 767 to 2039. A joined facet with an off vertex on no real edge
    // goes back to the leftovers; repeated until none does, since sending one
    // back can take away another's evidence.
    let vtol = config.vertex_tolerance_mm;
    loop {
        let size: Vec<usize> =
            (0..hyps.len()).map(|h| hyps[h].faces().len() + added[h].len()).collect();
        let mut evict: Vec<(usize, usize)> = Vec::new();
        for (hi, extra) in added.iter().enumerate() {
            for &fi in extra {
                let f = &mesh.faces[fi];
                let loose = f.vertex_indices[..f.vertex_count as usize].iter().any(|&vi| {
                    let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
                    fits[hi].distance(&[v.x, v.y, v.z]) > vtol
                        && !super::vertex_fan(mesh, fi, vi).iter().any(|&g| {
                            let o = owner[g];
                            (o == usize::MAX && !open[g]) || (o != usize::MAX && o != hi && size[o] >= 2)
                        })
                });
                if loose {
                    evict.push((fi, hi));
                }
            }
        }
        if evict.is_empty() {
            break;
        }
        for (fi, hi) in evict {
            open[fi] = true;
            owner[fi] = usize::MAX;
            added[hi].retain(|&g| g != fi);
        }
    }

        determine (at least `min_support`: 2 for a plane, the existing
        `MIN_*_FACES` otherwise). Only such a determined surface takes joined
        facets. A joined facet is flagged (`Classification::joined`) and is
        never used to refit a surface; refits and merge revalidation hold it
        to the boundary bound.

        surface take facets. On `ToolChanger__blower_fan_duct` that made
        stage 2 much worse: a one-facet competition "cylinder" took 69
        freeform facets, near-tangent blend facets joined analytic surfaces,

- **Only well-fitted surfaces can take extra facets.** A surface needs at least as many strictly validated facets as its type needs to be fitted at all: two for a plane, and the existing minimums for cylinders, spheres and tori. Competition had left a cylinder fitted to one facet, which took 69 facets of a freeform face.
